name: Abbots Langley and Kings Langley
intro: Taken together, Abbots Langley and Kings Langley have 18,203 residents in Hertfordshire, covered by the WD4 and WD5 postcode districts. Abbots Langley is a large, old village, recorded in the Domesday Book as Langelai, and economically it is closely linked to Watford, which is 7 km from the centre. It was once part of the Watford Rural District and has been in the Three Rivers district since 1974. Hemel Hempstead is the nearest town at 5.2 km, with Rickmansworth, Chorleywood and Bushey all around 8 km away and St Albans at 9.6 km. For a driver with an AdBlue warning, Bourne End Services on the A41 is the nearest listed service area, 7.4 km away in a straight line, and two motorway sites follow at 14.5 km and 14.9 km.
roadsText: Bourne End Services on the A41 is the nearest service area, 7.4 km from the centre in a straight line. London Gateway Services on the M1 is 14.5 km away and South Mimms Services on the A1(M) is 14.9 km. That gives drivers in WD4 and WD5 three options within 14.9 km: one on the A41 and two on motorways.

name: Aberdare
intro: In the Cynon Valley area of Rhondda Cynon Taf, Aberdare stands where the Rivers Dare and Cynon meet. It sits about 4 miles (6km) south-west of Merthyr Tydfil, 20 miles north-west of Cardiff and 22 miles east-north-east of Swansea, and had an estimated 39,550 residents in mid-2017. The town's postcode district is CF44. Its road list is made up of A-roads: the A465, A470, A4060, A4233, A4059, A4102 and A4054. Mountain Ash is about 4.7km away, Merthyr Tydfil 6.7km, Rhondda 7.7km and Tonypandy 9.8km, so a lot of local driving links one neighbouring town to the next. There is no motorway in the list, and the closest service areas are more than 20km off, which is worth bearing in mind if an AdBlue light comes on during a day of local work.
roadsText: Around Aberdare the listed roads are the A465, A470, A4060, A4233, A4059, A4102 and A4054. The nearest service areas are Sarn Park services on the M4 at about 21.5km, Cardiff West services, also on the M4, at 24.2km, and Glanusk services on the A40 at 27.6km. All three are some distance from CF44, so a driver with an AdBlue warning may be better off stopping safely first and working out the next step from there.

name: Aberdeen
intro: Third in size among Scotland's cities, Aberdeen is a port city in North East Scotland with 198,590 people in its main urban area in 2020 and 220,690 in the wider settlement. Its seaport is the largest in the north-east of Scotland, and the city has a long, sandy coastline. Postcode districts on the list include AB10, AB11, AB12, AB15, AB16, AB22, AB24 and AB25. For a van or diesel-car driver, the main point is distance: the nearest service area is 51.5 km away, so an AdBlue warning is best handled while still in or near the city. The A96, A92, A93, A944, A947, A956 and A9119 are among the recorded roads. Westhill is 10.1 km away, Stonehaven and Inverurie are both 21.6 km, and Ellon is 23.9 km, while Peterhead lies 43.8 km off.
roadsText: The A944, A9119, A96, A92, A93, A956 and A947 are the main roads recorded around Aberdeen. Service areas are a long way out: Stracathro Services on the A90 is 51.5 km away, Ashgrove Services on the A96 is 57.3 km and Forfar Services on the A90 is 75.1 km. Nearer the city, OpenStreetMap lists a station in Westhill (AB32 6TJ), 10.2 km away, as selling AdBlue at the pump. That data is incomplete, so other stations may also stock it.

name: Abergavenny
intro: Promoted as a "Gateway to Wales", Abergavenny is a market town in Monmouthshire around 7 miles (11 km) from the border with Herefordshire, at the point where the A40 trunk road meets the recently upgraded A465 Heads of the Valleys road. It grew from the Roman fort of Gobannium into a medieval walled town in the Welsh Marches, and stands where the Gavenny joins the River Usk. Mountains and hills surround it almost entirely, including the Blorenge, the Sugar Loaf and Skirrid Fawr, and the town gives access to the Black Mountains and the Brecon Beacons National Park. NP7 is the local postcode district. Nearby towns are spread out: Abertillery is 12.8 km away, Ebbw Vale 13.9 km, Pontypool 15.1 km and Monmouth 20.9 km. With the nearest listed services 15.4 km off on the A40, an AdBlue warning here is worth acting on early.
roadsText: Abergavenny sits where the A40 trunk road meets the A465 Heads of the Valleys road. The two nearest service areas are both on the A40: Monmouth A40 Services, 15.4 km away in a straight line, and Symonds Yat Services at 24.5 km. The nearest motorway stop listed is Magor Services on the M4, 29.4 km away. Distances by road will be longer, so a driver with an AdBlue warning should not count on a quick motorway stop from here.

name: Abertillery
intro: Once a major coal mining centre, Abertillery (Abertyleri) is a town and community in Blaenau Gwent County Borough, in the Ebbw Fach valley and the historic county of Monmouthshire. In the 1990s the area was returned to a greener environment using EU and other funding. The surrounding landscape borders the Brecon Beacons National Park and the Blaenavon World Heritage Site. The town is on the A467, 15 miles (24 km) north of the M4 and 5 miles (8 km) south of the A465 Heads of the Valleys trunk road, and about 25 miles (40 km) by road from Cardiff. NP13 is the postcode district. Ebbw Vale is 8.2 km away, Tredegar 8.8 km, Blackwood 8.9 km and Pontypool 9.2 km. With the M4 that far south, an AdBlue warning here means planning a stop rather than expecting services nearby.
roadsText: Abertillery is on the A467, 15 miles (24 km) north of the M4 and 5 miles (8 km) south of the A465. The nearest service areas are Cardiff Gate Services on the M4, 22.1 km away in a straight line, Monmouth A40 Services on the A40 at 22.6 km and Magor Services on the M4 at 26.6 km. Road distances will be longer than these straight-line figures.

name: Aberystwyth
intro: Near the confluence of the River Ystwyth and the Afon Rheidol, on Cardigan Bay on the west coast of Wales, Aberystwyth is the largest town in Ceredigion and a university and seaside town. Its name means the mouth of the Ystwyth. The 2021 population was 14,640, and the SY23 postcode district covers the town, which is divided into five areas: Aberystwyth Town, Llanbadarn Fawr, Waunfawr, Trefechan and Penparcau. Aberaeron, the county's other administrative centre, is 16 miles (26 km) away. Distance is the defining fact for drivers here. The nearest town on the list, Newtown, is 51.9 km away, and the nearest listed service area is 61.9 km away in a straight line, so it makes sense to deal with an AdBlue warning before setting off on a long run. One local forecourt is listed as selling AdBlue at the pump.
roadsText: Aberystwyth is a long way from any listed service area. The nearest is Glanusk Services on the A40, 61.9 km away in a straight line, followed by Pont Abraham Services on the M4 at 73.8 km and Moto Swansea West Services at 81.6 km. Closer to home, Tymawr Filling Station, a BP site in Aberystwyth (SY23 3EH) 5.7 km from the centre, is listed in OpenStreetMap as selling AdBlue at the pump. That data is incomplete.

name: Abingdon-on-Thames
intro: Commonly known simply as Abingdon, this historic market town stands on the River Thames in the Vale of White Horse district of Oxfordshire, and is the historic county town of Berkshire. Abingdon Abbey, founded around 676 AD, gave its name to the emerging town. By the 18th and 19th centuries the town sat on important routes for goods transport thanks to Abingdon Lock and the Wilts & Berks Canal. The town's railway station closed to passengers in 1963. The road list is long: the A34, A415, A420, A423, A338, A4074, A4142 and A4183 all appear, and the OX14 postcode district covers the town. Didcot is 7.7km away and Oxford 8.8km, with Wantage at 14.2km. For a diesel driver, that means plenty of A-road driving, with the nearest service area 13km away.
roadsText: The A34, A420, A423, A4142, A4183, A415, A4074 and A338 are the main roads listed around Abingdon-on-Thames. The nearest service areas are Peartree Services on the A44 (13km), Oxford Services on the M40 (14km) and Thame Services on the A418 (22.3km). A driver with an AdBlue warning therefore faces a run of at least 13km to reach a service area.

name: Accrington
intro: Locals commonly shorten the name to Accy. Accrington is the largest settlement in Hyndburn and the seat of the borough council, with a population of 35,456 at the 2011 census. It lies about 4 miles east of Blackburn and 6 miles west of Burnley, with Preston 13 miles to the west and Manchester 20 miles to the south, and the River Hyndburn runs through it in a culvert. The town was once a centre of the cotton and textile machinery industries and is known for its dense NORI building bricks. For drivers, the M65 is the only motorway listed among its roads, alongside A roads including the A679, A56 and A680. Oswaldtwistle is just 2.7 km away, and the town's postcode district is BB5. When an AdBlue warning appears, the two nearest service areas are both on the M65.
roadsText: The M65 is the motorway listed for Accrington, with A roads including the A679, A56, A678, A6068, A6119, A680 and A6185. Blackburn with Darwen Services on the M65 is 8.7 km away and Hollin Bank Service Station, also on the M65, is 12.5 km. The next nearest, Rivington Services on the M61, is 21.8 km off. Blackburn itself is 8.1 km away.

name: Addlestone
intro: The largest settlement in the Borough of Runnymede, and its administrative centre, Addlestone is a Surrey town about 18½ miles (30 kilometres) south-west of London. It has a population of 13,748 and spans the KT15 and KT16 postcode districts. Addlestone sits among a tight group of towns. Chertsey is just 2.4 km away and Weybridge 2.6 km, with New Haw, West Byfleet and Sheerwater at 3.3 km and Byfleet at 3.6 km, while Staines-upon-Thames and Walton-on-Thames are 5.8 km and 5.9 km off. If a van or diesel car shows an AdBlue warning, the nearest listed service area is Wisley Services on the A3, 8.8 km away in a straight line, and Cobham Services on the M25 is 9.4 km. Heston Services on the M4 is the third option at 14.5 km.
roadsText: Addlestone's closest listed service area is Wisley Services on the A3, 8.8 km away in a straight line. Cobham Services on the M25 is almost as near at 9.4 km, and Heston Services on the M4 is 14.5 km. All three figures are straight-line distances, so the drive to each will be longer, which is worth factoring in if an AdBlue warning is already lit.

name: Adwick le Street
intro: North-west of Doncaster, Adwick le Street is a village in the City of Doncaster that gives its name to the Adwick le Street & Carcroft ward. That ward also covers Carcroft, Woodlands and Highfields, which together had 16,518 residents at the 2021 census. Woodlands, a model village built for Brodsworth Colliery, is now the largest of these settlements. The Adwick le Street Urban District existed in the West Riding until 1974. The area uses the DN6 postcode district. Nearby, Scawthorpe and Cusworth is about 3.8 km away, Bentley 4.9 km, South Elmsall 6.4 km and Doncaster 8.7 km. For drivers dealing with an AdBlue warning, Barnsdale Bar Services on the A1 is the nearest listed service area, about 6.6 km away in a straight line, and a station in Doncaster listed as selling AdBlue at the pump is about 8.3 km away.
roadsText: Barnsdale Bar Services on the A1 is the closest service area, about 6.6 km from Adwick le Street in a straight line. Doncaster (North) Services on the M180 (13.4 km) and Ferrybridge Services on the M62 (14.6 km) come next. OpenStreetMap lists two stations as selling AdBlue at the pump: one in Doncaster (DN4 0TP), about 8.3 km away, and another in Pontefract (WF7 7HX), about 12.3 km away. The map data is incomplete, so others may exist.

name: Airdrie
intro: Sitting on a plateau about 130 m above sea level, Airdrie is a North Lanarkshire town 19 km east of Glasgow, with 35,846 residents in 2022. It began as a market town in the late 17th century and later grew with weaving, manufacturing, coal and iron. In the 21st century it is a regional centre for services and retail and a commuter settlement within the Central Belt. The M8 is on its road list, along with the A8, A73, A89, A723, A725, A775 and A8010. ML6 and ML5 are the postcode districts. Coatbridge is 3.9 km away, Bellshill 6.3 km and Cumbernauld 9.4 km, with Wishaw at 10.4 km. Three motorway service areas lie between 8.1 km and 13.2 km away, which gives drivers some choice if an AdBlue warning appears.
roadsText: The M8, A725, A8, A89, A73, A8010, A775 and A723 are the main roads recorded around Airdrie. Three service areas lie within 13.2 km: Bothwell Services on the M74 at 8.1 km, Hamilton Services on the M74 at 9.6 km and Heart of Scotland Services on the M8 at 13.2 km. The last of these sits on the M8, which also appears on Airdrie's own road list.

name: Aldershot
intro: Known as the Home of the British Army, Aldershot grew from a small village into a Victorian town on the strength of that connection. It sits on heathland in the extreme north-east corner of Hampshire, 31 miles south-west of London, within the Rushmoor district. The town is part of the Aldershot Urban Area, a loose conurbation of 243,344 people that also takes in Camberley and Farnborough. Postcode districts are GU11 and GU12. Neighbouring places are very close: Ash and Ash Vale is 2.3km away, Weybourne 2.9km, Farnborough 4.2km and Farnham 5.1km. The A331, A31, A323, A325, A3011, A3016, A327 and A287 are all listed, so local driving is largely on A roads across a built-up area, with the nearest motorway services 8.8km away at Fleet on the M3.
roadsText: Eight A roads are listed around Aldershot: the A331, A31, A323, A325, A3011, A3016, A327 and A287. The closest service area is Fleet Services on the M3, about 8.8km away. Liphook Services and Wisley Services, both on the A3, are 18.9km and 19.2km away. For most local journeys, the M3 stop at Fleet is the nearest roadside option if an AdBlue warning appears.

name: Aldridge
intro: Historically a village, and part of Staffordshire until 1974, Aldridge is now a town in the Metropolitan Borough of Walsall in the West Midlands. It is three miles (five kilometres) from Brownhills, five miles (eight kilometres) from Walsall, six miles (ten kilometres) from Sutton Coldfield and seven miles (eleven kilometres) from Lichfield. Two postcode districts cover the town, WS9 and WS4. Nearby places include Rushall and Shelfield at 2.1 km, Streetly at 3.7 km, Pelsall at 4.2 km and Bloxwich at 5 km. A van or diesel car with an AdBlue warning has motorway services within reach: the nearest listed is on the M6 Toll, 7.2 km away in a straight line, with another on the M6 at 9.8 km. OpenStreetMap also lists a station in Burntwood, 8.3 km off, as selling AdBlue at the pump.
roadsText: Norton Canes Services on the M6 Toll is the nearest service area to Aldridge, 7.2 km away in a straight line, followed by Hilton Park Services on the M6 at 9.8 km and The Trucker's Rest on the A5 at 12.6 km. OpenStreetMap lists a station in Burntwood (WS7 3XA), 8.3 km away, as selling AdBlue at the pump, and another in Warley at 13.4 km. An HGV-only site in Birmingham (B25 8DW) at 17.1 km is for lorries. These records are incomplete.

name: Alloa
intro: South of the Ochil Hills, on the north bank of the Forth where some say the river becomes the Firth of Forth, Alloa is the administrative centre of Clackmannanshire Council. It lies six miles (ten kilometres) east of Stirling and 13 miles (21 km) west of Dunfermline. The population was estimated at approximately 20,730 in 2016. Its port stopped operating in 1970, and the local economy now centres on retail and leisure. Tullibody, its north-western neighbour, is about half the size of Alloa, with Lornshill between the two. Postcode district FK10 covers the town. Larbert is about 10 km away in a straight line, Falkirk 12.7 km and Grangemouth 13 km. For a van or diesel car with an AdBlue warning, the nearest service area is on the M9, about 9.1 km away, with another on the A9 at around 14 km.
roadsText: Stirling Services on the M9 is the closest service area to Alloa, about 9.1 km away in a straight line. Balhaldie Services on the A9 is about 14 km away and Kinross Services on the M90 about 24.3 km. From the FK10 district, those are the three nearest service areas, and the road distance to each will be longer than the straight-line figure.

name: Alsager
intro: To the north-west of Stoke-on-Trent and east of Crewe, Alsager is a town and civil parish in Cheshire East. At the 2021 census the parish had 13,389 residents and the built-up area 15,505. The parish is bordered by Betchton to the north, Church Lawton to the north-east and east, Kidsgrove to the south-east, Audley Rural to the south, Barthomley to the south-west, Haslington to the west and Hassall to the north-west. The ST7 postcode district covers the town. Kidsgrove is the nearest neighbouring town at about 3.9 km, followed by Sandbach at 7 km, Biddulph at 8.7 km and Newcastle-under-Lyme at 9 km. For a driver with an AdBlue warning, Alsager is close to the M6, with Crewe Services only about 3.9 km away.
roadsText: Crewe Services on the M6 is the nearest service area to Alsager, about 3.9 km away, with Sandbach Services, also on the M6, at around 5.5 km. Keele Services on the M6 is roughly 11.4 km off. OpenStreetMap has a station in Newcastle-under-Lyme, about 13.8 km away, listed as selling AdBlue at the pump. OpenStreetMap's records are incomplete, so other stations may stock it.

name: Alton
intro: Recorded in the 11th-century Domesday Book as having the most valuable market in England, Alton is a market town and civil parish in East Hampshire, near the source of the northern branch of the River Wey. It sits on the A31, 16 miles from Winchester, and had 17,880 residents at the 2021 census. The town is covered by the GU34 postcode district. The nearest towns are all some distance off: Farnham is 13.9 km away in a straight line and Basingstoke 15.4 km, with Weybourne, Fleet and Petersfield between 15.6 and 16.7 km. For a van or diesel car with an AdBlue warning, the nearest listed service area is Liphook Services on the A3, 13.3 km away in a straight line, with Petersfield Services on the A3 and Fleet Services on the M3 both under 18 km.
roadsText: Alton is on the A31. The nearest listed service areas are Liphook Services on the A3 at 13.3 km, Petersfield Services, also on the A3, at 16.2 km, and Fleet Services on the M3 at 17.7 km. All are straight-line distances from the town centre, so the drive to any of them will be longer.

name: Altrincham
intro: Altrincham has held a market since the right was granted in 1290, and the market continues today. The town lies south of the River Mersey, 8 miles south-west of Manchester, 3 miles south-west of Sale and 10 miles east of Warrington. Historically in Cheshire, it became part of Greater Manchester in 1974, and its built-up area had 49,680 people in 2021. The town has good transport links to Manchester, Sale, Stretford and Stockport. Postcode districts WA14, WA15, M23 and M33 are listed, so addresses carry both WA and M prefixes. The M56 and M60 are on the road list, along with the A56, A560, A538, A556, A5103 and A555. Sale is 3.5 km away, Hale 4.8 km and Wythenshawe 4.9 km, with Urmston, Stretford and Irlam all within 7.3 km. Three service areas on the M6 are about 10 to 11 km away.
roadsText: Altrincham's main roads include the M56 and M60, plus the A56, A560, A538, A556, A5103 and A555. Three M6 service areas are close together: Tabley Hill at 10.4 km, Knutsford at 11 km and Lymm at 11.1 km. Stations listed as selling AdBlue at the pump in OpenStreetMap include one in Warrington's WA3 (12.2 km), one in Manchester's M25 postcode district (16.4 km) and one about 19.3 km away. Others may not be mapped.

name: Amersham
intro: Two distinct areas make up Amersham, a market town in the Chiltern Hills of Buckinghamshire. Old Amersham sits in the valley of the River Misbourne, while Amersham-on-the-Hill grew up in the early 20th century around Amersham station. The town is part of the London commuter belt, 27 miles (43 km) north-west of central London, 15 miles (24 km) south-east of Aylesbury and 9 miles (14 km) north-east of High Wycombe. It is covered by the HP6 and HP7 postcode districts and has a population of 17,377. For a driver dealing with an AdBlue warning, the nearest listed service area is Bourne End Services on the A41, 8.7 km away in a straight line, with Beaconsfield Services on the M40 at 10 km. Chesham is the closest neighbouring town at 4.3 km, followed by Chorleywood (7.2 km), Hazlemere (7.4 km) and Beaconsfield (8.4 km).
roadsText: Bourne End Services on the A41 is the closest service area to Amersham, 8.7 km away in a straight line. Beaconsfield Services on the M40 is at 10 km, and London Gateway Services on the M1 is much further at 23.8 km. Actual driving distances will be longer than these straight-line figures, so allow for that if an AdBlue warning is already showing.

name: Amesbury
intro: Stonehenge lies within the parish of Amesbury, a Wiltshire town that is claimed to be the oldest occupied settlement in Great Britain, first settled around 8820 BC. The parish also includes the hamlets of Ratfyn and West Amesbury and part of the Boscombe Down military airfield. The town has a population of 12,676 and falls in the SP4 postcode district. Salisbury is the nearest neighbouring town at 9.8 km, with Tidworth at 10.4 km and Andover at 20.3 km, while Romsey and Devizes are 26.5 km and 26.8 km away. All three of the listed service areas near Amesbury are on the A303, the nearest 16.5 km away in a straight line, so for a van or diesel car with an AdBlue warning that is the road to think about first.
roadsText: Every service area listed near Amesbury is on the A303. Weyhill Services is the closest at 16.5 km in a straight line, followed by The Buck Services at 24.1 km and Barton Stacey Services at 26.3 km. Distances by road will be longer, so allow for that if an AdBlue message appears while driving in the SP4 area.

name: Andover
intro: Running right alongside the A303 trunk road, Andover is a Test Valley town on the River Anton, a major tributary of the Test, at the eastern end of Salisbury Plain. It lies 18 miles west of Basingstoke, 14 miles from Winchester and 35 miles north of Southampton, and the town has a population of 48,484, with postcode districts SP10 and SP11. The town developed as a centre for grain milling and wool processing, and took on a significant Armed Forces presence in the 20th century. For drivers, the A303 is the main reference point, with the A3057, A3093, A343 and A342 also listed. Neighbouring towns are relatively spread out: Tidworth is 13.8km away, Winchester 20km and Amesbury 20.3km, with Newbury at 23.8km. Trips beyond the town often mean longer runs on trunk and A roads.
roadsText: Andover's listed main roads are the A303, A3057, A3093, A343 and A342. All three of the nearest service areas are on the A303: Weyhill Services (4.1km), The Buck Services (5.2km) and Barton Stacey Services (7.7km). For a driver on the trunk road with an AdBlue warning, that means three places to pull in, the furthest of them 7.7km from town.

name: Antrim
intro: The county town of County Antrim lies on the banks of the Six Mile Water, on the north-east shore of Lough Neagh and about 23 km northwest of Belfast. Antrim is a historic market town with 25,606 residents at the 2021 census, and since 2015 it has been part of Antrim and Newtownabbey Borough Council. The BT41 postcode district covers it. Two motorways appear on the local road list, the M2 and the M22, alongside the A6, A26, A57 and A522, so motorway driving is close at hand. Ballyclare is 14.1 km away and Ballymena 16.8 km, with Newtownabbey at 20.5 km and Belfast at 22.7 km. Knowing the nearest services and AdBlue pumps helps when a dashboard warning appears partway through a journey, especially as the closest station listed as selling AdBlue at the pump is in Newtownabbey.
roadsText: Main roads recorded around Antrim are the M22, M2, A6, A26, A57 and A522. Temple Patrick Services Northbound on the M2 is the nearest service area, 12.7 km away. Lisburn Services on the M1 is 25.2 km away and Glenshane Tourist Services on the A6 is 35.7 km. OpenStreetMap lists a station in Newtownabbey (BT36 4GX), 15.5 km away, as selling AdBlue at the pump. That map data is incomplete, so other sites may sell it too.

name: Arbroath
intro: The largest town in Angus, Arbroath is a historic coastal town and former royal burgh on the North Sea coast, with 23,481 residents in 2022. It lies some 16 miles (26 km) east-northeast of Dundee and 45 miles (72 km) south-southwest of Aberdeen. The town's story began with the founding of Arbroath Abbey in 1178, and it grew through flax, jute and engineering during the Industrial Revolution; a new harbour followed in 1839, and by the 20th century it was one of Scotland's larger fishing ports. Postcode district DD11 covers the town. Carnoustie is the closest neighbour at about 10.5 km in a straight line, with Montrose at 18.7 km and Forfar at 20.2 km. For an AdBlue warning, the two nearest service areas are both on the A90, about 21.6 km and 23.3 km away.
roadsText: No motorway service area is close to Arbroath. The two nearest stops are both on the A90: Forfar Services, about 21.6 km away in a straight line, and Stracathro Services, about 23.3 km away. The next is Kinross Services on the M90, about 65.5 km away, so for most drivers in the DD11 district the A90 is the road to aim for.

name: Ardrossan
intro: The main mainland terminal for ferry services to the Isle of Arran, Ardrossan is a town on the North Ayrshire coast, on the east shore of the Firth of Clyde. It has a population of 10,670 and forms the 'Three Towns' conurbation with Saltcoats and Stevenston; Saltcoats is just 1.6 km from the centre. The town is also home to the Ardrossan Wind Farm. Its addresses use the KA22 and KA21 postcode districts. Kilwinning (6.4 km) and Irvine (10.2 km) are the next nearest towns, with Troon, Largs and Kilmarnock between 14.9 and 20.1 km away. For anyone driving to or from the ferry with an AdBlue warning showing, distance is the issue: the nearest listed motorway service areas are about 50 km away in a straight line, and the road journey to them is longer still.
roadsText: Ardrossan's nearest listed service areas are all on the M74, about 50 km away in a straight line: Bothwell Services at 50.1 km, Hamilton Services at 50.7 km and the M74 Truck Stop at 57.4 km. Drivers heading for or coming off the Arran ferry should allow for that distance, since the road journey to any of them will be longer than the straight-line figure.

name: Armadale
intro: West Lothian's Armadale lies in the Central Belt of Scotland, west of Bathgate and east of Blackridge, and was once known as Barbauchlaw. It is a former mining town that was also known for brick manufacturing, and today it is primarily residential, built around a central Mains Street with parks, green spaces and nature reserves, many of them on former mines and industrial land. About 12,720 people live in the town, which sits in the EH48 postcode district. Whitburn (3.7 km) and Bathgate (3.9 km) are the closest neighbouring towns, with Linlithgow at 10.7 km and Livingston at 10.9 km. For a driver with an AdBlue warning light, the useful fact is that Heart of Scotland Services on the M8 is only 5.2 km from the town centre in a straight line, which puts a motorway services stop within easy reach.
roadsText: Heart of Scotland Services on the M8 is the closest listed service area to Armadale, 5.2 km away in a straight line. Beyond that, Hamilton Services on the M74 is 24.2 km away and Stirling Services on the M9 is 24.4 km away. The M8 site is by far the nearest option, and actual driving distances to all three will be longer than these straight-line figures.

name: Armagh
intro: Classed by the Northern Ireland Statistics and Research Agency as a medium-sized town, Armagh was given city status in 1994 and Lord Mayoralty status in 2012. It is the county town of County Armagh and the ecclesiastical capital of Ireland, with two cathedrals and a reputation for Georgian architecture. The 2021 Census recorded 16,310 people, and the city sits in the BT61 postcode district. For drivers, the picture is one of moderate distances to neighbouring towns: Dungannon is about 18.3 km away, Craigavon 21.1 km, Banbridge 24.8 km and Newry 28.7 km, with Cookstown at 33 km and Lisburn at 45.2 km. Cohannon Services on the M1, around 16.8 km away, is the closest service area for a van or diesel car with an AdBlue warning, and the next is much further out at 47.1 km.
roadsText: Cohannon Services on the M1 is the closest service area to Armagh, about 16.8 km away in a straight line. After that the distances grow quickly: Lisburn Services, also on the M1, is about 47.1 km away and Glenshane Tourist Services on the A6 about 55.3 km. For most drivers in the BT61 district, Cohannon on the M1 is the realistic stop.

name: Armthorpe
intro: Described as a large suburban village, Armthorpe is a civil parish in the City of Doncaster, South Yorkshire, and was historically within the West Riding. Its population of 12,630 had risen to 14,457 by the 2011 census. The village uses the DN3 postcode district and sits close to several neighbours: Kirk Sandall and Edenthorpe is about 2.9 km away, Doncaster 4.6 km, Dunscroft and Hatfield 4.8 km and Bentley 6.6 km, with New Rossington and Rossington about 7.7 km off. For a van or diesel car with an AdBlue warning, services are within reasonable reach. Doncaster (North) Services on the M180 is the nearest listed service area, about 7.2 km in a straight line, and a station in Doncaster listed as selling AdBlue at the pump is about 9.1 km away.
roadsText: Doncaster (North) Services on the M180 is the closest service area to Armthorpe, roughly 7.2 km in a straight line. Barnsdale Bar Services on the A1 (15.9 km) and Blyth Services on the A1(M) (16.6 km) are next. OpenStreetMap lists a station in Doncaster (DN4 0TP), about 9.1 km away, as selling AdBlue at the pump. That list is not complete, so other stations may also sell it.

name: Arnold
intro: Gedling Borough Council is headquartered in Arnold, a market town just north-east of Nottingham's city boundary and part of the Greater Nottingham conurbation. The built-up area had 40,010 residents at the 2021 census, and areas within the town include Daybrook, Woodthorpe, Redhill, Warren Hill, Killisick and Dorket Head. Postcode districts are NG3, NG4 and NG5. Main roads include the A60, A610, A611 and A614, along with the A6002, A6130, A6211 and A6514. Carlton is about 4.3 km away and Nottingham around 5.3 km, with Hucknall at 6.8 km and West Bridgford at 8.2 km. Although Arnold is joined to the conurbation, the nearest service area is still about 6.7 km away, so a driver with an AdBlue warning should know which way to head.
roadsText: Arnold's main roads are the A60, A610, A611, A614, A6002, A6130, A6211 and A6514. The nearest service areas are Trent Bridge Services on the A6011, about 6.7 km away, Pierrepont on the A52 at 7.8 km and Trowell Services on the M1 at 10.6 km. A Tesco station about 15 km away is listed in OpenStreetMap as selling AdBlue at the pump; that list is incomplete.

name: Ascot
intro: Best known as the home of Ascot Racecourse and the Royal Ascot meeting, Ascot is a Berkshire town in the Royal Borough of Windsor and Maidenhead, 25 miles west of London. It is made up of three areas, Ascot itself, North Ascot and South Ascot, and lies in the civil parish of Sunninghill and Ascot. Around 24,003 people live in the area, which uses the SL5 postcode district. In straight-line terms, Bracknell is 6.8 km away, Egham 7.2 km and Windsor 8.3 km, with Camberley and Crowthorne both under 10 km and Chertsey at 10.2 km. The main roads listed around the town are the M3, A322, A330, A329, A30 and A332, so the M3 is close by for a van or diesel car, though the nearest listed service area is 16.9 km away on the A3.
roadsText: Main roads listed around Ascot are the M3, A322, A330, A329, A30 and A332. The nearest listed service areas are Wisley Services on the A3 at 16.9 km, Fleet Services on the M3 at 18.1 km and Cobham Services on the M25 at 20.5 km, all measured in a straight line from the town centre. Expect the drive to any of them to be longer.

name: Ash and Ash Vale
intro: In the far west of the borough of Guildford, Ash is a Surrey village and civil parish on the eastern side of the River Blackwater. This page covers it together with Ash Vale, an area of about 24,284 people in the GU12 postcode district. Ash has direct roads to Aldershot, Farnham and Guildford, and a station on the Reading to Guildford and Gatwick line. Aldershot is only 2.3 km away, with Farnborough and Weybourne both 5 km off, Farnham at 6.8 km and Frimley at 7.2 km. The main roads listed around the area are the A331, A31, A323, A324, A3011, A325, A327 and A3016, all of them A roads, with no motorway among those listed. For a van or diesel car with an AdBlue warning, the nearest listed service area is Fleet Services on the M3, 10.6 km away in a straight line.
roadsText: Eight main roads are listed around Ash and Ash Vale: the A331, A31, A323, A324, A3011, A325, A327 and A3016. The nearest listed service areas are Fleet Services on the M3 at 10.6 km, Wisley Services on the A3 at 16.9 km and Liphook Services, also on the A3, at 19.8 km. All distances are measured in a straight line from the centre, so road journeys will be longer.

name: Ashby-de-la-Zouch
intro: Commonly shortened to Ashby, Ashby-de-la-Zouch is a market town in North West Leicestershire, near the borders with Derbyshire and Staffordshire, with 16,491 residents at the 2021 census. It lies at the heart of the National Forest and on the A42 between Tamworth and Nottingham. The parish includes the hamlets of Shellbrook to the west and Boundary to the north-west, and the postcode district is LE65. Swadlincote, Burton upon Trent, Melbourne and Coalville are all within 10 miles, and Derby is 12 miles due north. By straight-line distance, Swadlincote is 7 km away, Coalville 7.3 km and Whitwick 7.8 km. If a van or diesel car shows an AdBlue warning, a station in Swadlincote, 8.4 km away, is listed as selling AdBlue at the pump.
roadsText: Ashby sits on the A42 between Tamworth and Nottingham. The nearest service areas are Moto Donington Park Services on the M1 at 13.6 km, ExtraMSA Derby with Burton Services on the A50 at 14.4 km and Welcome Break Derby South Services on the A50 at 15 km. A station in Swadlincote (DE12 8AA), 8.4 km away, is listed on OpenStreetMap as selling AdBlue at the pump. That data is incomplete, so other stations may also sell it.

name: Ashford
intro: Ashford lies on the River Great Stour at the southern, scarp edge of the North Downs, about 61 miles (98 km) by road south-east of central London and 15 miles (24 km) north-west of Folkestone. A market town since the Middle Ages, it grew as a rail hub at the centre of five railway lines and had a population of 83,213 at the 2021 census. Postcode districts are TN23 and TN24. The M20 is the motorway listed for the area, with the A28, A2070, A20 and A251 among the other main roads. The nearest towns are some distance away: Hythe is 16 km, Folkestone and Faversham are both 19.1 km and Canterbury 20.9 km. Helpfully for anyone with an AdBlue warning, a truckstop is listed just 2.9 km from the town.
roadsText: The M20, A28, A2070, A20, A2042, A292 and A251 are the main roads listed for Ashford. Ashford International Truckstop on the A2070 is the nearest listed service area, 2.9 km away, with Folkestone Services on the M20 at 12.9 km and Maidstone Services, also on the M20, at 22.8 km. A station at New Romney (TN28 8AZ), 17.8 km away, is listed as selling AdBlue at the pump in OpenStreetMap; that list is incomplete.

name: Ashford
intro: Heathrow Airport is just 2.5 miles north of Ashford, a town in the Borough of Spelthorne about 14 miles west of central London. Historically part of Middlesex, it has been in Surrey since 1965, and its name comes from a ford of the River Ash, a distributary of the River Colne. The town had 27,382 residents in 2011 and is covered by the TW15 postcode district. Ashford Common, a more residential ward, includes part of Queen Mary Reservoir, and green spaces such as Bedfont Lakes and Shortwood Common surround the town. Neighbouring places are close: Stanwell is 2 km away, Staines-upon-Thames 2.8 km and Sunbury-on-Thames 4.8 km, with Chertsey, Egham and Weybridge all under 7 km. For a driver with an AdBlue warning, the nearest listed service area is Heston Services on the M4, 7.9 km away in a straight line.
roadsText: The nearest listed service area to Ashford is Heston Services on the M4, 7.9 km away in a straight line. Next come Cobham Services on the M25 at 15 km and Wisley Services on the A3 at 15.8 km. Road distances will be longer than these straight-line figures, so it is worth planning a stop before an AdBlue warning becomes urgent.

name: Ashington
intro: Ashington lies 15 miles north of Newcastle upon Tyne, west of the A189, with the River Wansbeck forming its southern border. Once a centre of the coal mining industry, it is a town and civil parish in Northumberland that had 27,864 residents at the 2011 Census. Its postcode districts are NE63, NE64 and NE62. Bedlington (5.4 km) and Blyth (6.6 km) are the nearest towns, with Morpeth at 8.6 km and Cramlington at 10.2 km; Killingworth and Whitley Bay are both more than 15 km away. The listed roads are the A189, A1068, A196, A197, A1147 and A193, all A-roads, and the nearest service area in the data is 13.3 km away. For a van with an AdBlue warning, that distance is worth bearing in mind before a longer run.
roadsText: The main roads listed around Ashington are the A189, A1068, A196, A197, A1147 and A193. The nearest service area is Seaton Burn Services on the A19, 13.3 km away; after that, Washington Services on the A1(M) is 32 km and Easington Services on the A19 is 43.5 km. A station in Newcastle upon Tyne, 15.5 km away, is listed as selling AdBlue at the pump in OpenStreetMap, but its coverage is incomplete.

name: Ashtead
intro: On the single-carriageway A24 between Epsom and Leatherhead, its closest neighbours, Ashtead is a Mole Valley village in Surrey. It lies about 16 miles (26 kilometres) south of central London, on the northern slopes of the North Downs, and the Metropolitan Green Belt encircles it. Residential growth followed the opening of the railway line between Epsom and Leatherhead in 1859 and continued into the 20th century, peaking in the 1930s. Ashtead has a population of 14,830 and is covered by the KT21 postcode district. Leatherhead is 2.6 km away and Epsom 3.3 km, with Tadworth and Epsom Downs, Ewell, Great Bookham and Fetcham, and Cobham all between 5.1 km and 6.3 km. If an AdBlue warning appears, the nearest listed service area is Cobham Services on the M25, 7.3 km away in a straight line, with Wisley Services on the A3 at 13.1 km.
roadsText: The A24 passes through Ashtead as a single-carriageway road between Epsom and Leatherhead. For services, Cobham Services on the M25 is the nearest listed option at 7.3 km in a straight line, followed by Wisley Services on the A3 at 13.1 km and Heston Services on the M4 at 20.8 km. The road distance to each will be longer than these figures.

name: Ashton-in-Makerfield
intro: Locks and hinges have long been made in Ashton-in-Makerfield, a market town in the borough of Wigan, 4 miles south of Wigan, with 26,380 residents at the 2021 census. Historically part of Lancashire, it once formed a chapelry with neighbouring Haydock until the two were split in 1845, and it sits on the Lancashire Coalfield, where it was a coal mining district. WN4 is its postcode district. Haydock is 3.3 km away, Newton-le-Willows 4.5 km and Golborne 4.6 km, so the town is part of a close cluster of places. The M6 and M58 are both listed among the roads nearby, with the A49, A58 and A580. If an AdBlue warning appears, two Warrington stations, 9.3 km and 11 km away, are listed on OpenStreetMap as selling AdBlue at the pump.
roadsText: Listed roads around Ashton-in-Makerfield are the M6 and M58, plus the A49, A58, A580, A577, A5062 and A599. Burtonwood Services on the M62 is 8.4 km away, Rivington Services on the M61 12.6 km and Earlsfield Services on the M57 14.4 km. OpenStreetMap lists two Warrington sites (WA5 3TP at 9.3 km and WA3 6RW at 11 km) and a third station, 18.1 km away, as selling AdBlue at the pump. Other stations may be unmapped.

name: Ashton-under-Lyne
intro: Also known simply as Ashton, Ashton-under-Lyne is a market town in the Metropolitan Borough of Tameside, on the north bank of the River Tame in the foothills of the Pennines, 6 miles east of Manchester. It had 48,604 people at the 2021 census. The cotton trade arrived in 1769 and transformed the town, which was replanned on a grid. Its postcode districts carry three prefixes: OL6, OL7 and OL8, SK15 and SK16, and M43. Six towns are within 5 km, with Dukinfield at 2.4 km, Audenshaw and Stalybridge at 3.5 km, Droylsden at 4.1 km, Failsworth at 4.5 km and Mossley at 4.6 km, so a local trip can pass through several of them. The M60 and M67 are on the road list, together with the A6043, A627, A670, A6140, A635 and A6017.
roadsText: Ashton's main roads include the M60 and M67, with the A6043, A627, A670, A6140, A635 and A6017. Birch Services on the M62 is the nearest service area at 12.2 km; Knutsford and Tabley Hill, both on the M6, are 29.8 km away. A station just 4.3 km away and one in Manchester's M25 postcode district at 13.8 km are listed as selling AdBlue at the pump in OpenStreetMap. Those listings are not exhaustive.

name: Atherton
intro: Coal mining and nail manufacture were part of Atherton from the 14th century, and the town was a key part of the Manchester Coalfield during the Industrial Revolution. Its last deep coal mine closed in 1966 and its last cotton mill in 1999. Today Atherton, historically in Lancashire, is the third-largest retail centre in the Borough of Wigan, and some significant manufacturing remains. It lies 5 miles south of Bolton, 7 miles east of Wigan and 10 miles north-west of Manchester. Its postcode districts are M46, M29, BL5 and WN7. Tyldesley is just 2.6 km away, Westhoughton 3 km and Leigh 4.2 km. The M61 is the motorway listed nearby; if an AdBlue warning comes on, Rivington Services on the M61 is 9.9 km away.
roadsText: Atherton's listed roads are the M61 plus the A579, A577, A6, A58, A580, A673 and A5082. Rivington Services on the M61 is the nearest service area at 9.9 km, with Burtonwood Services on the M62 at 15.8 km and Birch Services on the M62 at 17.5 km. Stations listed on OpenStreetMap as selling AdBlue at the pump include sites in Warrington (WA3 6RW at 12.3 km and WA5 3TP at 17.4 km) and Manchester (M25 3AJ at 13.1 km). The map is incomplete.

name: Attleborough
intro: Lying on the A11 between Norwich and Thetford, Attleborough is a Breckland market town whose population has grown from 9,702 in 2001 to 11,232 in 2021. The parish covers 21.9 square kilometres, and the town is in the NR17 postcode district. Its railway station has main line services to both Norwich and Cambridge. For a van or diesel car with an AdBlue warning, the A11 is the road to know: Thickthorn Services on the A11 is the nearest listed service area, 17 km away in a straight line, and the next is more than 40 km away. Wymondham is the closest town at 9.3 km, followed by Watton at 14.2 km and Dereham at 18.9 km, with Thetford, Norwich and Taverham and Drayton all between 21.5 km and 23 km.
roadsText: Attleborough lies on the A11, and Thickthorn Services on that road is the closest service area, 17 km from the centre in a straight line. Beacon Hill Services on the A140 is 40.8 km away and Freebridge Park on the A47 is 49.9 km. With the other two so far off, the A11 site is the realistic services stop from NR17.

name: Audenshaw
intro: East of Gorton and 4.9 miles (7.9 km) east of Manchester city centre, Audenshaw is a town in Tameside, Greater Manchester. It was historically part of Lancashire and had 11,419 residents in 2011. Audenshaw expanded as a textile centre during the Industrial Revolution and the Victorian era, with hat-making, cotton-spinning, calico-printing and silk-weaving, and it joined the Metropolitan Borough of Tameside in 1974. Postcode districts M43, M34 and OL7 cover parts of the town. The neighbours are close: Droylsden is about 1.8 km away, Denton 2.6 km and Dukinfield 2.9 km, with Ashton-under-Lyne at 3.5 km. Reddish and Failsworth are both within about 4 km. For a driver with an AdBlue warning, the nearest motorway service area is Birch Services on the M62, about 12.5 km off.
roadsText: Birch Services on the M62 is the closest service area to Audenshaw, about 12.5 km away. Knutsford Services and Tabley Hill Service Station, both on the M6, are each around 26.3 km off. OpenStreetMap has a site roughly 5.1 km away listed as selling AdBlue at the pump, plus a station under Manchester at about 12.7 km. Its records are incomplete, so other stations may also sell it.

name: Aylesbury
intro: Midway between High Wycombe and Milton Keynes, Aylesbury is the county town of Buckinghamshire. Its urban area had a population of 87,950 in 2021, and the town is set to keep growing, with a housing target of 16,000 new homes by 2033. Postcode districts are HP19, HP20, HP21 and HP22. The main roads listed for the area are A roads, including the A41, A413 and A418, and no motorway appears among them. The closest neighbouring towns are a little way off: Tring is 10.1 km away, Thame 13.9 km and Leighton Buzzard 15.6 km. Drivers caught by an AdBlue warning should note that the nearest listed service area is 13.4 km out on the A418, with the next two more than 20 km away, so it helps to know the options before setting off.
roadsText: Six A roads are listed for Aylesbury: the A413, A41, A418, A4010, A4157 and A4156. Thame Services on the A418 is the nearest listed service area, 13.4 km away. Bourne End Services on the A41 is 20.5 km and Oxford Services on the M40 is 21.7 km. The first two both sit on roads that also appear in Aylesbury's own road list, the A418 and the A41.

name: Ayr
intro: On Scotland's southwest coast, Ayr is the administrative centre of South Ayrshire Council and the historic county town of Ayrshire. A former royal burgh, it had 46,182 people in 2022, making it the second largest town in Ayrshire. It is contiguous with the smaller town of Prestwick to the north, and the suburb of Alloway lies towards the south of the town. The KA7 and KA8 postcode districts cover it. Main roads recorded here are the A77, A70, A713, A79 and A719. Prestwick is 4.1 km away and Troon 10.7 km, with Irvine at 18.6 km and Kilmarnock at 18.8 km. Distance is the defining feature for drivers: the nearest service areas are all on the M74, at least 50.4 km off, so an AdBlue warning needs dealing with closer to home.
roadsText: The A77, A70, A713, A79 and A719 are the main roads recorded around Ayr. Motorway services are a long way from the town: the M74 Truck Stop is 50.4 km away, Hamilton Services on the M74 is 51.9 km and Cairn Lodge, also on the M74, is 52 km. With nothing nearer on this list, plan ahead if a warning appears before a long run.

name: Bacup
intro: In the South Pennines close to Lancashire's boundaries with West Yorkshire and Greater Manchester, Bacup is a Rossendale town in the Rossendale Valley and the upper Irwell Valley. It is 4 miles (6.4 km) east of Rawtenstall, 6 miles (9.7 km) north of Rochdale and 7 miles (11 km) south of Burnley, and it had 13,323 residents at the 2011 Census. The town grew up as a mill town around the bridge over the River Irwell and the north-south and east-west crossroad at its centre. The OL13 postcode district covers Bacup. Todmorden is about 6.6 km away, Haslingden 8.3 km and Littleborough 8.7 km. For a van or diesel car with an AdBlue warning, the main point is distance: the closest motorway service area is about 14.5 km off.
roadsText: Birch Services on the M62 is the nearest service area to Bacup, about 14.5 km away. Hollin Bank Service Station on the M65 is around 15 km off, and Blackburn with Darwen Services, also on the M65, about 18.4 km. OpenStreetMap has a station under Manchester, roughly 18.6 km away, listed as selling AdBlue at the pump. OpenStreetMap is not a complete record, so nearer stations may also stock it.

name: Baglan
intro: Named after Saint Baglan, this village adjoins Port Talbot and is a community and ward in Neath Port Talbot county borough. It sits on the side of a steep hill, with Mynydd-y-Gaer to the north and Mynydd Dinas to the east, and the moors and Baglan Bay to the south-west. The population rose from 6,654 in 2001 to 6,819 in 2011. Baglan railway station is on the South Wales Main Line, with trains to Cardiff and Swansea. The village falls in the SA11 postcode district. Neath is 3.6 km away and Port Talbot 4.7 km, with Swansea at 7.8 km, Maesteg at 11.6 km and Pyle at 14.7 km. The nearest listed service area for a driver with an AdBlue warning is on the M4, 13.3 km away in a straight line.
roadsText: The nearest service areas to Baglan are all on the M4. Swansea West Services is 13.3 km away in a straight line, Sarn Park Services 19.8 km and Pont Abraham Services 21.3 km. Road distances will be longer than these figures. None is especially close, so if an AdBlue warning appears around Baglan it is better to plan where to stop than to rely on reaching a service area.

name: Baildon
intro: Continuous with Shipley and Bradford as one urban area, Baildon is a town and civil parish in the Bradford Metropolitan Borough, 3 miles (5 km) north of Bradford city centre and within the historic boundaries of the West Riding. It is part of the West Yorkshire Built-up Area, with Shipley to the south and Saltaire to the west. The Baildon ward had 15,360 residents at the 2011 census. Postcodes here fall in BD17 and BD18. Shipley is about 1.9 km away, Bingley 3.6 km, Guiseley 5.2 km, Bradford 6.1 km and Yeadon 7.4 km. Motorway services are a fair distance off, though. The nearest listed, Hartshead Moor Services on the M62, is about 15 km away in a straight line, which is worth bearing in mind if an AdBlue warning comes on.
roadsText: The nearest service areas to Baildon, measured in a straight line, are Hartshead Moor Services on the M62 at about 15 km, Skelton Lake Service Station on the M1 at 21.6 km and Wetherby Services on the A1(M) at 28.8 km. None of the three is especially close, and real road distances will be longer than these figures.

name: Balderton
intro: Balderton is one of the largest villages in Nottinghamshire and now adjoins Newark-on-Trent, which lies to its north-west and is only 2.7 km away. The village is split between the historic village in the south-east and New Balderton, and the parish had 9,917 residents at the 2021 census. The postcode district is NG24. Beyond Newark, the next towns are some distance off: Bingham is 16.4 km away, Grantham 18.7 km and North Hykeham 19.4 km. For drivers, the A1 is right on the doorstep: Welcome Break Newark on the A1 is just 0.8 km from Balderton, and a second service area on the A46 is 4.5 km away. If a van or diesel car shows an AdBlue warning, there is somewhere to stop very close by.
roadsText: Welcome Break Newark on the A1 is under a kilometre from Balderton, at 0.8 km. Newark Services on the A46 is 4.5 km away and North Muskham, also on the A1, is 8.5 km away. With three service areas inside 9 km across the A1 and A46, there are several places nearby to stop if a warning comes on.

name: Baldock
intro: The River Ivel rises from springs in Baldock, a historic market town in the North Hertfordshire district of Hertfordshire. It lies 53 km north of London and 23 km north-north-west of Hertford, the county town, and had a population of 10,615 in 2021. Baldock's postcode district is SG7. Several neighbouring towns are very close: Letchworth is only 2.7 km away to the south-west, Stotfold 4.5 km and Hitchin 6.9 km, with Stevenage, to the south, 8.5 km off. Biggleswade is 11.7 km away and Royston, to the north-east, 13.4 km. Driving from Baldock often means short runs between these towns, and the A1(M) is right on hand too, with Baldock services on that road just 3.3 km from the town. A van or diesel car here can switch between local errands and motorway miles with very little in between.
roadsText: Baldock services on the A1(M) is the nearest place to stop, 3.3 km from the town, which makes it handy if a warning light comes on at the start of a longer journey. Beyond that, the next service areas are much further away: Toddington on the M1 is 22 km off, and Bedford services on the A421 is 23.9 km.

name: Ballyclare
intro: About 13 miles (21 km) north-north-west of Belfast, Ballyclare is a market town on the Six Mile Water in County Antrim, with 10,850 residents at the 2021 census. It probably began as a crossing point of the river, and its broad main street dates from the 17th century, with the Market Square and Town Hall at the centre. Two local roads, the Mill Road and the Green Road, take their names from a paper mill and a linen bleach green that have been closed for some time. Today the town is a local service centre with a significant dormitory role in relation to Belfast. The BT39 postcode district covers it. Newtownabbey is about 11.7 km away, Carrickfergus 13 km and Antrim 14.1 km. For an AdBlue warning, there is a service area on the M2 only about 6.4 km away.
roadsText: Temple Patrick Services Northbound on the M2 is the nearest service area to Ballyclare, about 6.4 km away in a straight line. Lisburn Services on the M1 is about 25 km away and Glenshane Tourist Services on the A6 about 47.4 km. OpenStreetMap lists a station in Newtownabbey (BT36 4GX), about 8.9 km away, as selling AdBlue at the pump. That source is incomplete, so treat it as one known option rather than a full list.

name: Ballymena
intro: Built on the Braid River, Ballymena is a County Antrim town about 45 km northwest of Belfast and part of the Borough of Mid and East Antrim. Its 2021 census population of 31,205 made it the seventh largest town in Northern Ireland. The villages around it include Cullybackey, Ahoghill, Broughshane and Kells-Connor, and the town itself is covered by the BT42 and BT43 postcode districts. The M2 is the motorway on the local road list, with the A26, A36, A42, A43 and A523 also recorded. Antrim is the nearest of the listed towns at 16.8 km, followed by Ballyclare (21.7 km), Ballymoney (27.5 km) and Larne (29.5 km). The nearest service area is 25.1 km away, which is worth bearing in mind if an AdBlue warning comes on.
roadsText: Roads recorded around Ballymena are the M2, A26, A36, A523, A42 and A43. The nearest service area is Temple Patrick Services Northbound on the M2, 25.1 km away. Glenshane Tourist Services on the A6 is 28.5 km away and Lisburn Services on the M1 is 41.5 km. With no service area any closer, it pays to act on an AdBlue warning before setting out on a longer run rather than relying on finding a stop on the way.

name: Ballymoney
intro: Established by Scottish settlers in the early 17th century, Ballymoney is a market town and civil parish in County Antrim, within the Causeway Coast and Glens Borough Council area. The parish spreads across the historic baronies of Dunluce Upper and Kilconway in County Antrim and into the barony of North East Liberties of Coleraine in County Londonderry. It had 11,048 residents at the 2021 census. The town hosts the Ballymoney Show, one of the oldest agricultural shows in Northern Ireland, founded in 1902. Its postcode district is BT53. Coleraine is about 12.1 km away, but Ballymena and Limavady are roughly 28 km off, and Antrim, Ballyclare and Cookstown are between 43.7 km and 49.9 km. The closest service area for a driver with an AdBlue warning is about 28.3 km away on the A6.
roadsText: Glenshane Tourist Services on the A6 is the nearest service area to Ballymoney, about 28.3 km away in a straight line. Temple Patrick Services Northbound on the M2 is about 52.4 km away and Cohannon Services on the M1 about 64.1 km. Distances by road will be longer, so it is sensible to know the route from the BT53 district before setting off with a warning showing.

name: Bamber Bridge
intro: Bamber Bridge is a large village rather than a town, set in the borough of South Ribble, Lancashire, 3 miles south-east of Preston. Its name, from Old English, probably means tree-trunk bridge, and people who live here are often known locally as Briggers. The PR5 and PR1 postcode districts cover the area. For drivers, its position is the useful part: the M6, M65 and M61 are all listed among the roads around Bamber Bridge, along with the A6, A582, A59, A5085 and A583. Neighbouring towns are close as well, with Penwortham 4.1 km away, Leyland 4.4 km and Preston 5 km. If an AdBlue warning comes on, the three nearest service areas are between 11.1 km and 15.8 km away and are listed below.
roadsText: The M6, M65 and M61 are listed around Bamber Bridge, with the A6, A582, A59, A5085 and A583 also listed. For a stop with facilities, Charnock Richard Services on the M6 is 11.1 km away, Blackburn with Darwen Services on the M65 is 12.8 km and Rivington Services on the M61 is 15.8 km. Preston is 5 km away.

name: Banbridge
intro: Banbridge grew up as a coaching stop on the road from Belfast to Dublin, and it still lies on the A1 road beside the River Bann. The town takes its name from a bridge built over the Bann in 1712 and later thrived on Irish linen. Since 2015 it has been part of Armagh City, Banbridge and Craigavon Borough Council, and it had 17,400 residents in 2021. The main street is unusual: it climbs a steep hill before levelling out, and an underpass was built in 1834 because horses hauling heavy loads struggled to reach the top. The underpass is officially named Downshire Bridge but often called The Cut. Its postcode district is BT32. Craigavon is about 12.7 km away and Newry 19.4 km, with Armagh and Lisburn both around 25 km off. The nearest service areas to Banbridge are both on the M1.
roadsText: Banbridge lies on the A1 road. The nearest service areas are Lisburn Services on the M1, about 26.6 km away in a straight line, and Cohannon Services, also on the M1, at about 29.5 km. Temple Patrick Services Northbound on the M2 is about 42 km away. All three are a fair distance from the town, so a driver with an AdBlue warning should not count on reaching one quickly.

name: Banbury
intro: Serving north Oxfordshire and the southern parts of Warwickshire and Northamptonshire, a predominantly rural area, Banbury is a historic market town on the River Cherwell and a significant commercial and retail centre. The parish had 54,335 residents at the 2021 Census. Banbury is 22 miles (35 km) north-north-west of Oxford and 37 miles (60 km) south-east of Birmingham. Postcode districts are OX16 and OX17. The M40 is listed alongside the A422, A423, A361 and A4260. Towns around it are spread out: Brackley is the nearest at 13.4 km, with Bicester 22.1 km away and Towcester and Daventry both 25.2 km. The nearest listed service area is 15.8 km away on the M40, which is worth knowing before an AdBlue warning catches you out on a rural run.
roadsText: For Banbury, the main roads listed are the M40, A422, A423, A361 and A4260. Two of the three nearest listed service areas are on the M40: Cherwell Valley Services at 15.8 km and Warwick Services at 20.7 km. Towcester Services on the A43 is 24 km away. None is in the town itself, so it helps to know which way you are heading when an AdBlue warning comes on.

name: Bangor
intro: On the southern side of Belfast Lough, Bangor is a seaside city in County Down with 64,596 residents at the 2021 census. It was granted city status in 2022, becoming Northern Ireland's sixth city, and sits within the Belfast metropolitan area, 22 km east of Belfast city centre. The A2 and the Belfast to Bangor railway line link it to Belfast. Tourism is important to the local economy, particularly in the summer months. The city covers the BT19 and BT20 postcode districts and falls within Ards and North Down. Newtownards is the closest of the listed towns at 7.8 km, with Holywood at 10.4 km and Newtownabbey at 15.5 km. With the nearest motorway services more than 20 km away, it helps to know where the closer AdBlue pumps are before a dashboard warning turns into a problem.
roadsText: The A2, A21 and A48 are the main roads recorded around Bangor. No motorway service area is close by: the nearest is Temple Patrick Services Northbound on the M2 at 22.8 km, then Lisburn Services on the M1 at 26.3 km and Cohannon Services on the M1 at 66.2 km. OpenStreetMap lists a station in Bangor (BT19 1AA), 1.9 km away, as selling AdBlue at the pump, and another at BT6 0LT, 18.1 km away. The map data is incomplete, so there may be other options.

name: Bangor
intro: Two bridges, the Britannia and the Menai Suspension, link Bangor to the Isle of Anglesey. The cathedral city in Gwynedd was historically part of Caernarfonshire, had a built-up area population of 16,990 at the 2021 census and is home to Bangor University. Its postcode districts include LL57 and LL59. Other towns are some distance away: Conwy is about 22.5km off, Llandudno 23.5km and Colwyn Bay 27.8km, with Holyhead at 34km. Many journeys are either short trips around the city or longer runs to the next town or across to Anglesey. Those gaps between towns are long for a van or diesel car, though one service area is about 2.9km from the city.
roadsText: The closest service area to Bangor is Bangor services on the A5, about 2.9km from the city. Further out, Orme View services and Parc Cybi are both on the A55, at about 17.3km and 33.1km. OpenStreetMap lists a forecourt at Penmaenmawr (LL34 6UN), roughly 17.4km away, as selling AdBlue at the pump, though that data is incomplete and other sites may stock it.

name: Barking and Dagenham
intro: Barking, Chadwell Heath and Dagenham are the three main towns of the London Borough of Barking and Dagenham, an Outer London borough in East London. It was created in 1965 as the London Borough of Barking and took its current name in 1980. The south of the borough lies within the London Riverside section of the Thames Gateway, an area designated as a national priority for urban regeneration. The borough had 187,000 residents at the 2011 census. The A13 and A406 are among the main roads listed, along with the A12, A117, A123, A1020, A1153 and A1400, and postcode districts include RM6, RM8, RM9, RM10, IG3 and IG11. Redbridge is 5.9km away, Newham 6.4km and Havering 7.3km. A diesel van with an AdBlue warning here may be on one of those main roads or just over the boundary in a neighbouring borough.
roadsText: The A13 leads the road list for Barking and Dagenham, which also takes in the A123, A406, A1020, A12, A117, A1400 and A1153. Thurrock Services on the M25 is the closest listed service area at 11.4km, then Orsett Cock Services on the A13 at 19.1km and Tollgate Services on the A2 at 21.4km. A station just 3.4km away is listed as selling AdBlue at the pump on OpenStreetMap, as is one at Catford (14.2km). The map does not cover every station.

name: Barnet
intro: Hendon, Finchley, Golders Green, Friern Barnet, Chipping Barnet, Whetstone and Edgware are the major urban settlements of the London Borough of Barnet, a suburban borough in north London. It also has village settlements such as Totteridge and Arkley, and rural areas that form part of the Green Belt. The borough covers 86.74 square kilometres and had 405,050 inhabitants in 2024. It borders Hertsmere in Hertfordshire to the north, Camden and Haringey to the south-east, Enfield to the east, and Harrow and Brent to the west of the ancient Watling Street, now the A5. Main roads listed are the M1, A1, A41, A406, A1100, A598, A5000 and A504. For a van or diesel car showing an AdBlue warning, London Gateway Services on the M1 is just 4.4 km away. Borehamwood is 6.7 km away and Brent 7.8 km. Postcode districts listed include N2, N3, N12, N20, NW4, NW7 and EN5.
roadsText: The M1, A1, A41 and A406 are listed for Barnet, with the A1100, A598, A5000 and A504. London Gateway Services on the M1 is 4.4 km away and South Mimms Services on the A1(M) is 8.2 km away, so two motorway service areas are within easy reach of the borough. Heston Services on the M4 is 18.9 km off.

name: Barnham
intro: Eastergate and Barnham merged on 1 April 2019 to form the civil parish of Barnham and Eastergate. Barnham itself is a village and Anglican parish in the Arun district of West Sussex, centred north of Bognor Regis, and it falls in the PO22 postcode district. Bognor Regis is 5.9 km away, Wick 7.5 km, Littlehampton 8.6 km and Chichester 9 km, with Rustington at 12 km and Selsey at 15.4 km. Should an AdBlue warning appear, Barnham is unusually well placed for one service area: Fontwell Services on the A27 is just 1.8 km away in a straight line. Beyond that, the next listed options are both more than 27 km off, so the A27 site is the one that matters for drivers here.
roadsText: Fontwell Services on the A27 is the nearest listed service area to Barnham, only 1.8 km away in a straight line. The next two are far further off: Buck Barn on the A24 at 27.3 km and Farlington Services, also on the A27, at 27.6 km. For a driver in PO22, the A27 carries two of the three sites. Actual driving distances will be longer.

name: Barnoldswick
intro: A market town and civil parish in the Borough of Pendle, Barnoldswick is in Lancashire but lies within the boundaries of the historic West Riding of Yorkshire. The civil parish has a population of 10,752, and the town falls in the BB18 postcode district. Leeds is 30 miles (48 km) away and Lancaster 40 miles (64 km). Closer by, Skipton is to the east, Clitheroe to the west, Burnley to the south and Keighley to the east-south-east. Colne is the nearest neighbour at about 6.8 km in a straight line, with Nelson at 9.3 km and Brierfield at 10.9 km, while Skipton, Burnley and Clitheroe are between 11.8 km and 14.5 km away. If an AdBlue warning comes on, the closest motorway service area is around 10.2 km off on the M65, and the next two are 29.9 km and 36.8 km away.
roadsText: Hollin Bank Service Station on the M65 is the nearest service area to Barnoldswick, about 10.2 km away in a straight line. Beyond that the options thin out: Blackburn with Darwen Services, further along the M65, is about 29.9 km away, and the Hartshead Moor service area on the M62 is about 36.8 km. Road distances from the BB18 district will be longer than these figures.

name: Barnsley
intro: Along the M1 corridor, with Leeds and Wakefield to the north and Sheffield to the south, Barnsley is the main settlement of its metropolitan borough and the fourth largest in South Yorkshire. The town had 71,599 residents at the 2021 census. Doncaster lies to the east and Huddersfield to the north-west, while Manchester is reached west across the Peak District on the A628, one of the main roads listed around the town. That spread of routes, from motorway to an A road across the Peak District, covers very different kinds of driving for a van or diesel car with an AdBlue warning. Postcode districts are S70, S71 and S75. Neighbouring places sit close in: Royston and Cudworth and Shafton are both 4.5 km away as the crow flies, Darton 4.6 km and Wombwell 5.8 km. Linen, coal mining, glass making and textiles were among the town's former industries.
roadsText: The M1 heads the list of main roads around Barnsley, which also includes the A61, A635, A633, A628, A6133, A637 and A6195. Woolley Edge services on the M1 is the nearest service area, 8.7 km away as the crow flies, with Barnsdale Bar on the A1 at 16.9 km and Whitwood on the M62 at 17.6 km. OpenStreetMap lists a station with a Pontefract address, 12.9 km away, as selling AdBlue at the pump. It is not a complete record.

name: Barnstaple
intro: At the River Taw's lowest crossing point before the Bristol Channel, Barnstaple is a town and civil parish in the North Devon district, with a population of 31,271. From the 14th century it was licensed to export wool, and after its harbour silted up other trades developed, such as shipbuilding, foundries and sawmills. A Victorian market building with a high glass and timber roof still survives. The EX31 and EX32 postcode districts cover the town. Distance is the defining feature of driving here: Bideford is 12.7 km away, but the next nearest towns are much further, with Minehead at 42.7 km, Tiverton at 44.4 km and Exeter at 55.3 km. The nearest motorway services are 52.2 km away, so a van or diesel car with an AdBlue warning can face a long drive before reaching a motorway stop.
roadsText: Barnstaple's main roads are the A39, A361, A377 and A3125. Roundswell Service Area on the A39 is close by at 2.5 km. After that, the nearest motorway services are a long way off: Tiverton services on the M5 is 52.2 km away and Cullompton services on the M5 is 52.7 km. It makes sense to deal with any warning before setting off on a long run.

name: Barrhead
intro: Thirteen kilometres (8 mi) south-west of Glasgow city centre, Barrhead is an East Renfrewshire town on the edge of the Fereneze Braes. Its population at the 2011 census was 17,268, and it uses the G78 postcode district. Several neighbouring towns are close. Newton Mearns is about 4.6 km away in a straight line and Paisley 4.8 km, with Giffnock at 6.1 km, Renfrew at 8.2 km and Johnstone at 8.5 km. Glasgow itself is about 10.2 km off by the same measure. Drivers with an AdBlue warning will find the nearest motorway service areas both on the M74, about 20.6 km and 22.3 km away, while a station in Glasgow about 9.1 km away is listed as selling AdBlue at the pump. Road distances to any of these will be longer than the straight-line figures given here.
roadsText: The three nearest service areas to Barrhead are all on the M74: Bothwell Services at about 20.6 km in a straight line, Hamilton Services at about 22.3 km and the M74 Truck Stop at about 35.5 km. A station in Glasgow (G11 6DN), about 9.1 km away, is listed in OpenStreetMap as selling AdBlue at the pump. OpenStreetMap data is incomplete, so it is not a full list.

name: Barrow-in-Furness
intro: At the tip of the Furness peninsula, Barrow-in-Furness has water on three sides: Morecambe Bay to the east, the Duddon Estuary to the west and the Irish Sea to the south. That geography matters for anyone driving with an AdBlue warning. The main roads listed are the A590, A595 and A5087, and the nearest service areas in the data are on the M6, more than 32 km away. Ulverston is the closest town at 12.1 km, while Heysham, Morecambe, Fleetwood, Lancaster and Cleveleys are all at least 23.4 km off. Barrow lies 24 miles south-west of Kendal and 18 miles west of Lancaster. In 2021 its population was 55,489, making it the second-largest urban area in Cumbria after Carlisle. Postcode districts LA13 and LA14 cover the town, and its docks are now the Royal Port of Barrow.
roadsText: Barrow's main roads are the A590, A595 and A5087. Every service area in the data is on the M6 and a long way off: Burton-in-Kendal Services at 32.7 km, Lancaster Services at 35 km and Killington Lake Services at 44.2 km. For a van or diesel car with a low AdBlue warning, it is worth planning around those distances before leaving LA13 or LA14.

name: Barry
intro: The development of Barry Docks, which in 1913 was the largest coal port in the world, saw Barry grow significantly from the 1880s. Today it is a coastal town in the Vale of Glamorgan, on the north coast of the Bristol Channel about 14 km south-south-west of Cardiff, with 56,605 people at the 2021 census. It is also a seaside resort with several beaches and the Barry Island Pleasure Park, and it has absorbed its larger neighbouring villages of Cadoxton and Barry Island. The CF62 and CF63 postcode districts cover the town. Penarth is 6.7 km away and Cardiff 11.4 km, while Church Village and Caerphilly are further out at 17.7 km and 19 km. With no motorway among the main roads near the town, a diesel van or car here relies on A roads for local trips, and the nearest motorway services are 11.5 km away on the M4.
roadsText: Barry's main roads are the A4055, A4050, A4226 and A4231. The nearest service area is Cardiff West on the M4, 11.5 km away, followed by Cardiff Gate on the M4 at 17.3 km and Sarn Park on the M4 at 25.8 km. All three are on the M4, so reaching any of them means a drive out of town first.

name: Barton-upon-Humber
intro: At the southern end of the Humber Bridge, on the south bank of the Humber Estuary, Barton-upon-Humber (or simply Barton) is a town and civil parish in North Lincolnshire, within the ceremonial county of Lincolnshire. It is 6 miles (10 km) south-west of Kingston upon Hull and 31 miles (50 km) north-north-east of Lincoln, the county town, with Scunthorpe to the south-west and Grimsby to the south-east. The population was 11,066 at the 2011 Census, and the DN18 postcode district covers the town. Hessle is the nearest neighbouring town at 4.5 km, with Willerby and Anlaby at 7.5 km and Brough at 8.8 km. A driver with an AdBlue warning should be aware that the nearest listed service area, Ulceby Truckstop on the A160, is 12.4 km away, and the next is 38 km off.
roadsText: Ulceby Truckstop on the A160 is the nearest service area to Barton-upon-Humber, 12.4 km away in a straight line. After that the gap is large: Doncaster (North) Services on the M180 is 38 km away and Showground Services on the A15 is 44.4 km. Road distances will be longer than these figures, so drivers in DN18 should factor that in if an AdBlue warning appears.

name: Basildon
intro: Twenty-seven miles (43 km) east of Central London, Basildon lies 11 miles (18 km) south of Chelmsford and 10 miles (16 km) west of Southend-on-Sea. The main part of the town sits between the A127 to the north and the A13 to the south, two dual carriageways linking London to Southend, so a van or diesel car with an AdBlue warning in the main part of town has a dual carriageway to the north and another to the south. Basildon was a small village until the mid-20th century, and in 1949 it was designated a new town to accommodate London overspill. The designated area took in the existing villages of Pitsea, Laindon and Vange, and the town was then built out with new residential and industrial areas and a new town centre. The wider borough also includes Billericay and Wickford. Postcode districts for the area include SS13, SS14, SS15, SS16 and SS17, along with SS12, CM11 and CM12. Stanford-le-Hope is 5.8 km away and Canvey Island 11.1 km.
roadsText: The A127 and A13 are the main roads here, with the A176, A1235, A1321, A129, A132 and A128 also listed for the town. The nearest service area is Orsett Cock Services on the A13, 7.3 km away. Thurrock Services on the M25 is 14.5 km off, and Tollgate Services on the A2 is 17.9 km away.

name: Basingstoke
intro: The largest settlement in Hampshire without city status, Basingstoke sits in a valley at the source of the River Loddon, on the western edge of the North Downs. It remained a small market town until the early 1960s and expanded in the mid-1960s after an agreement between London County Council and Hampshire County Council; the 2021 estimate put the population at 107,642. Basingstoke is 22 miles (35 km) south of Reading and 30 miles (48 km) north-east of Southampton. Its postcode districts are RG21 to RG25. The M3 is the motorway listed for the town, with the A339, A33, A340 and A30 among the other main roads. The nearest towns are not especially close, with Tadley 10.8 km away and Alton 15.4 km, and the nearest listed service area is 11.9 km out, so it helps to know the options when an AdBlue warning appears.
roadsText: The M3 is the only motorway among Basingstoke's listed main roads, alongside the A339, A33, A3010, A340 and A30. Popham Services on the A303 is the nearest listed service area, 11.9 km away, with Fleet Services on the M3 at 17.4 km and Reading Services on the M4 at 18.3 km. The Swallowfield By-pass station (RG7 1LZ), 16.8 km away, is listed as selling AdBlue at the pump in OpenStreetMap, though that data is incomplete.

name: Bath
intro: Set in the valley of the River Avon, 18 km south-east of Bristol and 156 km west of London, Bath is the largest city and urban settlement in Somerset. Named after its Roman-built baths, it became a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1987 and was later listed as one of the Great Spa Towns of Europe. Its Georgian architecture, built from Bath stone, includes the Royal Crescent and the Circus. The BA1 and BA2 postcode districts cover the city, which has a population of 94,080. There is no motorway among the main roads listed for the city; the A4, A36 and A46 head that list instead. Neighbouring towns include Keynsham at 9.7 km, Trowbridge at 13.2 km, Corsham at 13.3 km and Midsomer Norton at 13.5 km, so a working day in a diesel van can easily take in several of them as well as the city itself.
roadsText: The main roads near Bath are the A4, A36, A46, A367, A3039, A3604, A3062 and A431. The nearest service areas are all at least 20.3 km away: Leigh Delamere on the M4 at 20.3 km, Warminster on the A350 at 21.6 km, and Chippenham Pit Stop on the M4 at 23 km. That distance is worth bearing in mind before setting off on a longer run with a warning light showing.

name: Bathgate
intro: Adjacent to the M8 and 8 km west of Livingston, Bathgate is a West Lothian town with a number of villages falling under its umbrella, among them Blackburn, Whitburn, Stoneyburn, Armadale, Torphichen and Fauldhouse. It lies 3 km south of Cairnpapple Hill, and by the Victorian era it had grown into an industrial and mining centre linked to the coal and shale oil industries. The EH48 postcode district covers the town, with a listed population of 23,600. Being right beside the M8 means motorway access is close, and the A89, A705, A706, A779, A800, A801 and A7066 are also recorded. Armadale is 3.9 km away and Whitburn 5 km, with Livingston at 7.1 km and Linlithgow at 8.8 km. The nearest service area is under 9 km away.
roadsText: Main roads recorded around Bathgate are the M8, A89, A800, A7066, A779, A801, A706 and A705. Heart of Scotland Services on the M8 is the nearest service area at 8.6 km. After that, the distances jump: Dreghorn Services on the A720 is 25.2 km away and Stirling Services on the M9 is 26.6 km. If a warning appears, the M8 services are the closest option on this list.

name: Batley
intro: South-west of Leeds, north-west of Wakefield and Dewsbury, south-east of Bradford and north-east of Huddersfield, Batley sits in the Heavy Woollen District of West Yorkshire among a tightly packed group of towns. It is a market town in Kirklees with a population of 48,730 at the 2011 census. Heckmondwike is only 2.3 km away as the crow flies, Dewsbury 3.8 km, Morley 3.9 km and Liversedge 4.3 km, so a short journey can easily take you into another town. Three motorways, the M62, M621 and M1, appear among the main roads around Batley, together with A roads such as the A62, A638 and A653. If the AdBlue light comes on, that motorway access is useful, because the nearest service area is 7 km away. Postcode districts are WF13, WF16 and WF17.
