roadsText: The M62, M621 and M1 are all listed among Batley's main roads, as are the A638, A62, A650, A653 and A644. The closest service area is Hartshead Moor on the M62, 7 km away as the crow flies; Woolley Edge on the M1 is 12.4 km and Skelton Lake Service Station on the M1 is 12.6 km. OpenStreetMap lists a station with a Leeds address, 12.7 km away, as selling AdBlue at the pump. That list is incomplete.

name: Beaconsfield
intro: With a motorway service area bearing its name close by, Beaconsfield is well placed for a driver who needs to stop. The market town and civil parish lies in Buckinghamshire, 24 miles (39 kilometres) north-west of central London and 16 miles (26 kilometres) south-east of Aylesbury, next to the Chiltern Hills Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty. Its Old Town high street has Georgian, neo-Georgian and Tudor revival architecture. Beaconsfield has a population of 14,142 and its postcode district is HP9. If an AdBlue warning appears, Beaconsfield Services on the M40 is the nearest listed service area, 2.5 km away in a straight line. Flackwell Heath and Wooburn Green (3.8 km), Hazlemere (6.2 km), Chalfont St Peter (6.3 km) and High Wycombe (6.9 km) are the closest neighbouring places.
roadsText: Beaconsfield Services on the M40 is 2.5 km from the town in a straight line, by far the closest listed service area. The next two are a long way further: Bourne End Services on the A41 at 17 km and Heston Services on the M4 at 22.2 km. Road distances will be longer than these straight-line figures, so the M40 site is the practical first stop.

name: Bearsden
intro: Along the north-western fringe of Greater Glasgow, approximately ten kilometres from the city centre, Bearsden is an East Dunbartonshire town of 28,470 people (2020). It began in the 17th century as the kirkton of the parish of New Kilpatrick and developed into a suburb of the city after a railway connection to Glasgow was built in 1863. The Roman Antonine Wall runs through the town. The recorded main roads are all A roads: the A81, A82, A739, A807, A808, A809, A810 and A879. Postcode districts G61 and G62 are joined by G13, G15 and G23 on the list. Milngavie is just 2.6 km away, Clydebank 4.8 km and Renfrew 6.3 km. The nearest motorway service area is 20.6 km away, so the stations listed as selling AdBlue at the pump are the closer options to know about.
roadsText: The A809, A808, A81, A810, A739, A82, A807 and A879 are the main roads recorded around Bearsden. Motorway services are some way off: Bothwell Services on the M74 at 20.6 km, Hamilton Services on the M74 at 23.7 km and Stirling Services on the M9 at 30.9 km. Closer in, OpenStreetMap lists a station in Glasgow (5.9 km) and another site 14.8 km away as selling AdBlue at the pump. That data is incomplete.

name: Bebington
intro: Ask where Bebington starts and ends and the answer depends on the definition. The original villages are Lower Bebington and Higher Bebington, but some definitions take in Port Sunlight, New Ferry, Spital and Storeton, and the former Municipal Borough also included Bromborough, Eastham, Raby, Thornton Hough and Brimstage. The town lies 5 miles south of Liverpool, close to the River Mersey on the eastern side of the Wirral Peninsula, with Birkenhead and Wallasey to the north-north-west and Heswall to the west-south-west. Its built-up area had 57,600 people. Postcode districts CH42, CH62 and CH63 are listed. The M53 and A41 lead the road list, with the A552, A561, A5227, A550, A562 and A5137. Birkenhead is 6.2 km away, Neston 6.4 km and Heswall 6.7 km. The nearest service areas in the data are all more than 15 km away.
roadsText: Bebington's main roads are the M53 and A41, with the A552, A561, A5227, A550, A562 and A5137. The nearest service areas are Earlsfield Services on the M57 at 15.1 km, Chester Services on the M56 at 15.3 km and Chester West Services on the A55 at 17.4 km. The nearest site OpenStreetMap has listed as selling AdBlue at the pump, in Liverpool L5 (9.9 km), is marked HGV-only, and its records are incomplete.

name: Bedford
intro: Founded at a ford on the River Great Ouse, Bedford is the county town of Bedfordshire and the seat of the Borough of Bedford. The market town had an urban area population of 167,446 at the 2021 census, and it has deep roots: borough status came in 1166, it has been represented in Parliament since 1265, and Bedford Castle was built by Henry I before being destroyed in 1224. The town is also known for its large population of Italian descent. For a driver with an AdBlue warning light, the useful facts are the roads and neighbours. The A6, A421 and A428 all reach the town, and Kempston is only 3.6 km away. Sandy is 11.4 km off, Flitwick 15.2 km, Biggleswade 15.4 km and St Neots 16.1 km, with Rushden at 19.1 km. Bedford's postcode districts are MK40, MK41 and MK42.
roadsText: Main roads listed are the A6, A421, A428, A4280, A600, A5140, A5141 and A603. Bedford Services on the A421 is close by, 3.9 km from the town. On the M1, Crawley Crossing Truck Stop is 16.3 km away and Newport Pagnell Services is 20.8 km away, giving two motorway options further out.

name: Bedlington
intro: In south-east Northumberland, roughly 16 km north-east of Newcastle and Newcastle Airport, Bedlington is an ancient market town in the civil parish of West Bedlington. The 2011 census gave it a population of 18,470. St Cuthbert's Church, parts of which date back to the 11th century, stands at the heart of the original sandstone conservation town centre, and the main street is Front Street. The town is roughly 10 minutes from the A1, and other towns sit close around it: Blyth to the east is 4.7 km away, Cramlington to the south 5.1 km, Ashington to the north-east 5.4 km and Morpeth to the north-west 7.1 km. For a diesel van or car, that means a lot of short runs between neighbouring towns, starting from the NE22 postcode district, with the A1 a short drive away for longer trips.
roadsText: Bedlington is roughly 10 minutes from the A1. The closest service area is Seaton Burn on the A19, 7.9 km away; beyond that, Washington services on the A1(M) is 27.3 km and Easington on the A19 39.7 km, so the stops are spread out. A station in Newcastle upon Tyne, 10.4 km away, is listed in OpenStreetMap as selling AdBlue at the pump. That data is incomplete.

name: Bedworth
intro: With Coventry to the south and Nuneaton to the north, Bedworth is a market town in the Warwickshire borough of Nuneaton and Bedworth. Locally the name is pronounced 'Beduth'. The 2021 census counted 31,090 residents, and the postcode district is CV12. What matters most to a driver dealing with an AdBlue warning is how close the motorway network is. Two motorways, the M6 and the M69, appear among the main roads around the town, with the A444, A4600, A46 and A4254 also listed, and Corley services on the M6 is just 4 km away in a straight line. Both are close: Nuneaton is 6.1 km away in a straight line and Coventry 7.3 km. Hinckley, at 10.7 km, is the next nearest town, followed by Kenilworth at 15.4 km and Earl Shilton at 15.9 km.
roadsText: Two motorways, the M6 and M69, are among the main roads around Bedworth, along with the A444, A4600, A46 and A4254. Corley on the M6 is the closest service area, 4 km away in a straight line; Rugby services, also on the M6, is 17.6 km away and Tamworth services on the M42 is 18.1 km. OpenStreetMap lists one station 5.8 km from the town as selling AdBlue at the pump, but that dataset is patchy and will miss others.

name: Beeston
intro: Three miles (4.8 km) south-west of Nottingham city centre, Beeston is a town in the Borough of Broxtowe with a population of 52,359. The University of Nottingham's main campus lies to its north-east, while the River Trent and the village of Attenborough, with its wetlands, lie to the south. The postcode district is NG9. Main roads include the M1, A52, A453, A6005, A6007 and A6514, so the motorway is part of the local picture. The town is closely surrounded by neighbours: Stapleford is about 2.5 km away, Clifton 4.2 km, Long Eaton 5 km and Nottingham itself 6.1 km, with Ilkeston at 6.8 km. For a driver with an AdBlue warning, that means a motorway service area and several neighbouring towns are all within a short distance, with Trowell Services on the M1 under 5 km out.
roadsText: Main roads around Beeston include the M1, A52, A453, A6002, A6005, A6007, A6464 and A6514. Trowell Services on the M1 is the nearest service area, about 4.8 km away. Trent Bridge Services on the A6011 is around 6.7 km out, and Pierrepont on the A52 about 10.6 km.

name: Belfast
intro: As the capital, largest city and main port of Northern Ireland, Belfast stands on the banks of the river Lagan and reaches the open sea through Belfast Lough and the North Channel. The city recorded a population of 345,418 in 2021, and 704,406 across the wider Belfast area. When it was granted city status in 1888, Belfast was the world's largest centre of linen manufacture, and by the 1900s its shipyards were building up to a quarter of all United Kingdom tonnage. For drivers today, the city has four motorways listed, the M1, M2, M3 and M5, along with the A2, A12, A20 and A24. Postcode districts covering the city include BT1, BT2, BT7 and BT12, and Castlereagh (3.7 km), Newtownabbey (7.1 km) and Holywood (8 km) are close by. If an AdBlue warning comes on, a filling station in BT6, 3.2 km away, is listed on OpenStreetMap as selling AdBlue at the pump.
roadsText: Belfast's listed roads include the M1, M2, M3 and M5, plus the A20, A24, A2 and A12. Lisburn Services on the M1 is 9.4 km away and the northbound services at Temple Patrick on the M2 are 12.4 km; Cohannon Services on the M1 is much further at 48.5 km. OpenStreetMap lists stations at BT6 0LT (3.2 km), Newtownabbey BT36 4GX (9.1 km) and Bangor BT19 1AA (16.4 km) as selling AdBlue at the pump. It is not a complete list.

name: Bellshill
intro: Ten miles (sixteen kilometres) south-east of Glasgow city centre and 37 mi (60 km) west of Edinburgh, Bellshill is a North Lanarkshire town of about 20,650 people, counting the villages of Orbiston and Mossend. It now forms part of a continuous suburban settlement anchored by Motherwell, with a total population of around 125,000. Distances to the neighbours are short: Motherwell is 2 mi (3 km) to the south, Hamilton 3 mi (5 km) to the south-west, Viewpark 1½ mi (2.5 km) to the west, Holytown 2 mi (3 km) to the east and Coatbridge 3 mi (5 km) to the north. Postcode district ML4 covers the town. Airdrie is about 6.3 km away in a straight line. For a driver with an AdBlue warning, two service areas on the M74 are only about 2.6 km and 3.4 km away.
roadsText: Bothwell Services on the M74 is about 2.6 km from Bellshill in a straight line, and Hamilton Services, on the same motorway, about 3.4 km. The third nearest, Heart of Scotland Services on the M8, is about 17.2 km away. OpenStreetMap lists a station in Glasgow (G11 6DN), about 19.1 km away, as selling AdBlue at the pump, but its AdBlue records are incomplete.

name: Belper
intro: One of the first mill towns of the early Industrial Revolution, Belper is now part of the Derwent Valley Mills World Heritage Site. The town and civil parish lies on the River Derwent about 7 miles north of Derby, in the Amber Valley district, and also includes the village of Milford and the hamlets of Bargate, Blackbrook and Makeney. The parish had 21,440 residents at the 2021 census. Its postcode district is DE56. Ripley is the closest neighbouring town at 5.5 km, with Somercotes and Swanwick and Heanor both 8.7 km away and Derby itself 12.6 km. Belper is some distance from the motorway: the two nearest service areas, both on the M1, are more than 15 km away. That is worth knowing if a van or diesel car shows an AdBlue warning here.
roadsText: The nearest service areas to Belper are Trowell Services on the M1, 15.5 km away, and Tibshelf Services, also on the M1, at 15.7 km. Welcome Break Derby South Services on the A50 is 18.9 km from the town. With all three more than 15 km off, a stop needs a little planning if a warning comes on while you are driving around the Derwent valley.

name: Bentley
intro: A former mining village on the River Don, Bentley is now a suburb two miles north of Doncaster city centre. Its colliery closed in December 1993 and is now Bentley Community Woodland. The Bentley built-up area subdivision had 12,048 residents, and the wider ward, which includes Arksey, Shaftholme, Toll Bar and part of Scawthorpe, had 18,195 at the 2021 census. The area takes in West End, New Village and Rostholme, and postcodes fall in DN5 and DN1. Bentley and nearby Toll Bar were badly affected by floods in June 2007. Scawthorpe and Cusworth is about 1.7 km away and Doncaster 3.8 km. For an AdBlue warning, a station in Doncaster listed as selling AdBlue at the pump is about 4.5 km away, and Barnsdale Bar Services on the A1 is about 11.5 km in a straight line.
roadsText: From Bentley, the nearest service areas in a straight line are Barnsdale Bar Services on the A1 (11.5 km), Doncaster (North) Services on the M180 (12 km) and Blyth Services on the A1(M) (17.7 km). OpenStreetMap lists a station in Doncaster (DN4 0TP), about 4.5 km away, and another in Pontefract (WF7 7HX), about 17.1 km away, as selling AdBlue at the pump. The listing is not complete.

name: Berkhamsted
intro: In the Bulbourne Valley, 26 miles (42 km) north-west of London, Berkhamsted is a Hertfordshire market town with 21,245 residents at the 2021 census. Together with the adjoining village of Northchurch it is surrounded by countryside and the Chiltern Hills, an Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty. The town is in the borough of Dacorum, which is based in neighbouring Hemel Hempstead, and it has a long history, from a first mention in 970 AD to the ruins of its Norman castle. The HP4 postcode district covers the town. If an AdBlue warning comes on, Bourne End Services on the A41 is the nearest listed service area, 3.7 km from the centre. Chesham is 5.8 km away, Tring 7.3 km and Hemel Hempstead 7.5 km, with Amersham at 9.6 km.
roadsText: Bourne End Services on the A41 is close to Berkhamsted, 3.7 km from the town centre in a straight line. The next nearest are motorway sites: Beaconsfield Services on the M40 at 19.6 km and Toddington Services on the M1 at 21.2 km. From HP4, the A41 site is by far the nearest of the three.

name: Berwick-upon-Tweed
intro: England's northernmost town, Berwick-upon-Tweed lies at the mouth of the River Tweed on the east coast of Northumberland, just 4 km south of the border with Scotland. It is 90 km south-east of Edinburgh and 105 km north of Newcastle upon Tyne. The civil parish, formed in 2008, brings together Berwick, Spittal and Tweedmouth, and the town is covered by the TD15 postcode district. For more than 400 years the area was fought over in border wars between England and Scotland. Its position still shapes driving today: the nearest neighbouring towns are all across the border in Scotland, with Dunbar 40.9 km away, Galashiels 52.6 km, Haddington 52.7 km and Hawick 61.5 km. A diesel van or car based here covers long distances between places, and all three of the nearest service areas are on the A1.
roadsText: Berwick-upon-Tweed's nearest service areas are all on the A1, and all a long way off. Adderstone is 26.1 km away, while MacMerry is 58.2 km and Musselburgh 67.9 km. With gaps like that, an AdBlue warning on a longer journey may leave a good distance to cover before the next stop, so it is worth keeping an eye on the dashboard before setting out.

name: Beverley
intro: The county town of the East Riding of Yorkshire, Beverley lies 8 miles (13 km) north-west of Hull city centre. Its built-up area had 30,930 residents at the 2021 census, and the smaller civil parish 18,014. It was founded in the seventh century by John of Beverley and later grew into a significant wool-trading town. Beverley Minster, the North Bar gatehouse, the Westwood common and Beverley Racecourse are among its landmarks. For anyone driving with an AdBlue warning, the more relevant facts are the roads and the distances. The main roads listed are the A1035, A164, A1079 and A1174, none of them a motorway, and the nearest service area is more than 26 km away. Cottingham is 6.5 km away on a direct line and Kingston upon Hull 10.7 km. The postcode district is HU17.
roadsText: Main roads around Beverley are the A1035, A164, A1079 and A1174. The town is a long way from a motorway service area. On a direct line, Ulceby Truckstop on the A160 is 26.3 km away, Doncaster North services on the M180 is 46.4 km and Bilbrough Top Service Area on the A64 is 50.2 km. Road distances will be greater than these figures.

name: Bexhill-on-Sea
intro: Along the Sussex coast between Hastings and Eastbourne, Bexhill-on-Sea (often shortened to Bexhill) is a seaside town and civil parish in the Rother district of East Sussex. The 2021 census recorded 43,754 residents, and the town is covered by the TN39 and TN40 postcode districts. No motorway appears in the road list. Instead, the A259 is joined by the A269, A271, A2036, A2690 and A2691. Hastings is 8.7km away and Eastbourne 13.1km, with Hailsham at 13.5km and Polegate at 14.5km. Further afield, Seaford is 24.7km and Uckfield 28km. For a van or diesel car with an AdBlue warning, the key point is distance: the nearest service area is 15km away and the next two are 43.8km and 44.4km out.
roadsText: Main roads listed around Bexhill-on-Sea are the A259, A2690, A269, A2691, A2036 and A271. The nearest service area is Polegate Services on the A22, about 15km away. Beyond that, Pyecombe Services on the A23 is 43.8km and Ashford International Truckstop on the A2070 is 44.4km. With roadside services this spread out, it pays to deal with an AdBlue warning before setting off on a longer trip.

name: Bexley
intro: Within the Thames Gateway, an area designated as a national priority for urban regeneration, the London Borough of Bexley is a south-east London borough that forms part of Outer London. Its main settlements are Sidcup, Erith, Bexleyheath, Belvedere, Crayford, Welling and Old Bexley, and it has 248,287 residents. Main roads listed include the A2, A13, A206, A207, A220, A221, A223 and A2041, and postcode districts include DA5, DA6, DA7, DA8, DA16, DA17, DA18 and SE2. Dartford is only 6.6km away, Greenwich 7km and Swanley 8km, so neighbouring places are close at hand. For a driver with an AdBlue warning, the closest listed service area, Thurrock Services on the M25, is 9km away.
roadsText: Bexley's main roads include the A2, A13, A220, A221, A207, A206, A2041 and A223. Thurrock Services on the M25 is 9km away, Tollgate Services on the A2 15.9km and Orsett Cock Services on the A13 18km. In OpenStreetMap, which is incomplete, a station 9.7km away and one at Catford, 11.1km away, are listed as selling AdBlue at the pump.

name: Bicester
intro: Eleven miles north-east of Oxford, Bicester is a market town and civil parish in the Cherwell district of Oxfordshire, home to 37,748 people, and its postcode district is OX26. The town's transport links go back a long way: it sits at the intersection of two Roman roads. Today the A41 runs through Bicester, connecting it to Aylesbury, the M40 and the A34, and the A4421 and A4095 complete the main road list. The town grew significantly in the 20th century because of its military role, with RAF Bicester established in 1917 and a major ordnance depot built in 1942. Kidlington is 12.6km away, Brackley 14.8km and Oxford 17.4km, so trips out of town usually mean the A41, A34 or M40 rather than short local hops.
roadsText: Main roads listed around Bicester are the M40, A41, A34, A4421 and A4095. Cherwell Valley Services on the M40 is the nearest service area at 6.4km. Peartree Services on the A44 is 14.6km away and Oxford Services on the M40 is 18.3km. With the A41 linking the town to the M40, Cherwell Valley is the closer of the two M40 service areas to town.

name: Biddulph
intro: Close to the Staffordshire and Cheshire county border, Biddulph is a town and civil parish in the Staffordshire Moorlands district, 9 miles (14 km) north of Stoke-on-Trent and 5 miles (8 km) south-east of Congleton. The parish had 19,892 people in 2011, and the town is in the ST8 postcode district. Kidsgrove is 5.5 km away, with Alsager at 8.7 km, Leek at 9.2 km, Newcastle-under-Lyme at 11.1 km and Sandbach at 13.5 km. For a driver dealing with an AdBlue warning, the M6 is the motorway to know: all three of the nearest listed service areas are on it, between 11.5 km and 14.9 km away in a straight line. OpenStreetMap also lists a station in Newcastle-under-Lyme as selling AdBlue at the pump.
roadsText: All three of the nearest service areas to Biddulph are on the M6: Sandbach Services, 11.5 km away in a straight line, Crewe Services at 12 km and Swift Services at 14.9 km. A station in Newcastle-under-Lyme (ST5 4DH), the same 14.9 km away, is listed in OpenStreetMap as selling AdBlue at the pump. That data is incomplete, so nearer stations may also sell AdBlue.

name: Bideford
intro: A historic port town on the estuary of the River Torridge, Bideford is the main town of the Torridge district in north Devon, with a population of 19,493. It is covered by the EX39 postcode district. For drivers, what stands out is distance. Barnstaple, 12.7 km away, is the only neighbouring town close by; the next ones listed, Tiverton, Tavistock, Minehead and Exeter, are all more than 52 km off. Service areas follow the same pattern. Roundswell Service Area on the A39 is 10.3 km away in a straight line, but the next two options, both on the M5, are around 60 km off. With an AdBlue warning on a van or diesel car, that makes the A39 site the realistic stop, and longer trips out of EX39 are worth planning around it.
roadsText: Roundswell Service Area on the A39 is the nearest listed service area to Bideford, 10.3 km away in a straight line. The next two are both on the M5 and much further: Cullompton Services at 60.5 km and Tiverton Services at 61.1 km. For a driver in EX39 with an AdBlue warning, the A39 site is the only listed option within a short drive, and road distances will be longer than these figures.

name: Biggleswade
intro: Biggleswade's population grew by 36% between the 2011 and 2021 censuses, reaching 22,541. The market town lies on the River Ivel in Central Bedfordshire, 11 miles (18 km) south-east of Bedford, and is covered by the SG18 postcode district. The Great North Road ran through the town until a new route around it was completed in 1961, and the town centre is now a conservation area. For a van or diesel car with an AdBlue warning, the nearest listed service area is Baldock Services on the A1(M), 8.5 km away in a straight line. Sandy, at 6.5 km, is the closest neighbouring town, with Stotfold at 7.8 km and Baldock and Letchworth at 11.7 km and 11.8 km. Hitchin and Bedford are around 15 km away.
roadsText: Baldock Services on the A1(M) is the closest service area to Biggleswade, 8.5 km from the town centre in a straight line. Bedford Services on the A421 is 15.6 km away, and Caxton Gibbet Services on the A428 is 19 km. That makes the A1(M) site the first one to aim for from SG18 if an AdBlue message appears.

name: Billericay
intro: Founded in the 13th century by the Abbot of West Ham, in his Manor of Great Burstead, Billericay is a historic market town and civil parish in the Borough of Basildon. It lies 23 miles (37 km) east of the City of London, and its built-up area had 34,075 people at the 2021 census. In 1620 four local people sailed on the Mayflower, and many local businesses and organisations still use that name. When a dashboard AdBlue message appears, the roads matter more: the A127 and A12 are both listed, along with the A129, A176, A1235 and A1023. Basildon is 6.5 km away, Wickford 6.7 km and Brentwood 8.6 km, while Stanford-le-Hope, Rayleigh, and Thundersley and South Benfleet are all between 12.2 and 12.6 km off. Postcode districts are CM11 and CM12.
roadsText: Listed roads are the A127, A12, A129, A176, A1235 and A1023. Orsett Cock Services on the A13 is 13.2 km away, Boreham Services on the A131 15.5 km and Thurrock Services on the M25 18.5 km. Lorry pumps in Chelmsford (CM2 5PY), 15.5 km away, are listed on OpenStreetMap as selling AdBlue at the pump, but they are marked HGV-only and the OpenStreetMap data is incomplete.

name: Billingham
intro: Since Anglo-Saxon times there has been a settlement at Billingham, now a town and civil parish in County Durham on the north side of the River Tees. It is governed as part of the Borough of Stockton-on-Tees and had 33,927 residents at the 2021 census. A post-Second World War town centre was built north of the old village centre, and the town is home to the Billingham Manufacturing Plant, a major producer of chemicals for agriculture. Main roads listed include the A19, A66, A689, A172, A139, A1027, A1032 and A1046, and postcode districts include TS1, TS2, TS20 and TS23. Stockton-on-Tees is 4.6km away, Thornaby-on-Tees 5.3km and Middlesbrough 6.6km. All three listed stops are 6.7km or less away, with Wolviston Services on the A689 the closest at 4km, so a driver with an AdBlue warning here is not far from somewhere to pull in.
roadsText: Billingham's main roads include the A19, A66, A689, A172, A1046, A1027, A139 and A1032. Wolviston Services on the A689 is just 4km away, southbound services on the A19 6.6km and Teesside Truck Stop on the A66 6.7km. A station near Durham (DH6 3LJ), 18km away, is listed as selling AdBlue at the pump in OpenStreetMap, which does not record every outlet.

name: Bilston
intro: Four kilometres south east of Wolverhampton city centre, Bilston is a Black Country market town inside the City of Wolverhampton, historically part of Staffordshire and close to the borders of Sandwell and Walsall. It is a former coal and iron mining district that later became a centre for steel production, and the 2021 Census put its population at 34,639. Local driving here is a matter of short hops between closely spaced towns: Darlaston is 2.8 km away in a straight line, Tipton 3.1 km, Coseley 3.4 km, Willenhall 3.8 km and Wednesbury 4 km. A short journey can easily cross a borough boundary, and the postcode districts around the town reflect that spread, taking in WV14, WV13, WV2, WV1, WS10 and DY4. If an AdBlue warning comes on, the M6 is the one motorway among the main roads nearby, alongside A roads such as the A41, A463 and A4123.
roadsText: The M6 is the motorway among the main roads around Bilston, alongside the A463, A41, A4444, A454, A4123, A461 and A4150. In a straight line, the nearest service areas are Hilton Park on the M6 (9 km), The Trucker's Rest on the A5 (13.1 km) and Norton Canes on the M6 Toll (13.3 km). OpenStreetMap lists a station with a Warley address (7 km) and one with a Burntwood address (15.9 km) as selling AdBlue at the pump; treat that as a starting point, as its records are incomplete.

name: Bingham
intro: Eleven miles east of Nottingham, Bingham is a market town in the Rushcliffe borough of Nottinghamshire. Newark-on-Trent is 14 miles to the north-east and Grantham 16 miles to the east. The town has grown steadily, from 8,655 people in 2001 to 9,131 in 2011 and 10,080 at the 2021 census, and its postcode district is NG13. Carlton, 8.3 km away, is the closest neighbouring town, with West Bridgford 11.7 km off and Arnold 12.2 km. Nottingham itself is 14.9 km away. For a van or diesel car with an AdBlue warning, the nearest service area is Pierrepont on the A52, 8.3 km from the town, and the next two options are both just over 12 km away.
roadsText: Pierrepont on the A52 is the nearest service area to Bingham, 8.3 km away. Trent Bridge Services on the A6011 and Welcome Break Hickling on the A606 are both 12.3 km from the town. The three sites sit on different roads, the A52, the A6011 and the A606, so the best stop depends on which way you are travelling.

name: Bingley
intro: Bingley is a market town and civil parish in the City of Bradford metropolitan borough of West Yorkshire, sited on the River Aire and the Leeds and Liverpool Canal. The 2021 Census counted 18,040 residents, and the postcode district is BD16. What a driver needs to know is how it connects to the places around it. Baildon is 3.6 km away measured directly, Shipley 4.8 km and Keighley 5.7 km, while Bradford, Guiseley and Ilkley all lie around 8 km off, so a local run from Bingley can take in several towns within a short distance. Motorway service areas are further away: the nearest, on the M62, is 16.5 km from the town, so with an AdBlue warning showing it makes sense to plan ahead rather than hope for a stop nearby.
roadsText: The nearest service area to Bingley is Hartshead Moor on the M62, 16.5 km away measured directly. The next two are much further: Skelton Lake Service Station on the M1 at 25.1 km and Hollin Bank Service Station on the M65 at 26.3 km. Those are straight-line distances, so the drive will be longer, which is worth factoring in when an AdBlue warning appears.

name: Birkenhead
intro: Opposite Liverpool on the west bank of the River Mersey, Birkenhead is an industrial port town on the Wirral Peninsula. It lay within the historic county of Cheshire and became part of Merseyside in 1974, and its built-up area had 109,835 people at the 2021 census. The Mersey Railway linked Birkenhead and Liverpool through the first railway tunnel beneath a tidal estuary. Much of the former dockland is now being built on with offices and housing as part of the Wirral Waters development. The M53 is the only motorway on the road list, joined by the A552, A5227, A5139, A554, A41, A5036 and A5052. Postcode districts CH41 to CH46 are all listed, along with CH49 and CH61. Wallasey is 3.6 km away, Heswall and Bebington 6.2 km and West Kirby 7.5 km. The closest service areas in the data are more than 16 km away.
roadsText: Birkenhead's main roads are the M53, A552, A5227, A5139, A554, A41, A5036 and A5052. The nearest service areas are Earlsfield Services on the M57 at 16.1 km, Old Meadow Services on the M58 at 17.4 km and Singing Kettle Services on the A55 at 20.5 km. In OpenStreetMap, a station at Old Meadow (17.4 km) is listed as selling AdBlue at the pump; a nearer site in Liverpool L5 is marked HGV-only. The map data is incomplete.

name: Birmingham
intro: England's largest local authority district by population, Birmingham had about 1.2 million people in the city proper in 2025 and sits at the centre of the West Midlands region. With Wolverhampton, Walsall, West Bromwich, Dudley and Solihull it forms the West Midlands conurbation, and Sutton Coldfield falls within the city limits to the north and north-east. Postcode districts covered here include B2, B4, B5, B7, B8, B9, B10 and B12. The road list mixes motorway and city routes: the M6, A38(M), A4540, A45, A34, A38, A5127 and A4167. Smethwick, Solihull, Sutton Coldfield, West Bromwich and Oldbury are all between about 7.6km and 10.6km from the centre. In practice that means dense urban driving across a large built-up area, often with motorway access on the same trip. The nearest motorway services are 12km or more from the centre, so a warning picked up in the city is not always close to a service area.
roadsText: Around the city, the listed roads take in the M6, A38(M), A4540, A45, A34, A38, A5127 and A4167. For a motorway stop, Frankley services on the M5 is about 12km from the centre, Hopwood Park services on the M42 14.2km and Tamworth services, also on the M42, 20.5km. OpenStreetMap lists an HGV-only refuelling site in B25, 2.6km away, and a forecourt in Warley, 12km away, as selling AdBlue at the pump. Its records are incomplete.

name: Birstall
intro: Charnwood's largest village, Birstall sits 3 miles north of Leicester city centre and is part of the wider Leicester Urban Area. The area has a population of 14,317 and is covered by the LE4 postcode district. For drivers, Birstall is closely tied to its neighbours, with Syston 3.9 km away, Mountsorrel 4.7 km and Leicester itself 5.6 km. Leicester Forest East and Kirby Muxloe is 9.1 km off, Oadby 9.7 km and Wigston 10.8 km. The standout fact for anyone with a van or diesel car is how close the roadside services are: ExtraMSA Leicester Services on the A6 is about 1 km from Birstall, so if an AdBlue warning appears nearby, there is somewhere to pull in almost on the doorstep.
roadsText: ExtraMSA Leicester Services on the A6 is about 1 km from Birstall, making it the closest stop by a wide margin. Leicester Forest East Services on the M1 is 8.8 km away and Six Hills Services Northbound on the A46 is 9.1 km away. With all three within 9.1 km, there are options on the A6, the M1 and the A46.

name: Birtley
intro: Joined to Chester-le-Street across the county boundary with County Durham, Birtley is a town in the Metropolitan Borough of Gateshead, Tyne and Wear, lying to the south of Gateshead itself. It has a population of 13,840 and falls within the DH3 postcode district. With neighbouring towns so close, plenty of local driving here is short: Washington is 4.1 km away, Gateshead 4.6 km and Chester-le-Street 4.8 km, with Shiney Row and Penshaw at 7 km, Stanley at 8.2 km and Whickham at 8.3 km. Birtley is also very close to the A1(M). Washington services on that road is only 1.7 km from the town, so a van or diesel car can switch from local streets to motorway driving almost straight away, and an AdBlue warning could appear on either.
roadsText: Washington services on the A1(M) is just 1.7 km from Birtley, close enough to be the natural first stop if a warning light comes on. The other nearby service areas are both on the A19 and much further away, Easington at 17.6 km and Seaton Burn at 18.9 km. A station in Newcastle upon Tyne, 15.7 km away, is listed in OpenStreetMap as selling AdBlue at the pump; that data is incomplete.

name: Bishop Auckland
intro: Where the River Wear meets the River Gaunless, Bishop Auckland is a market town and civil parish in County Durham, 19 km north-west of Darlington and the same distance south-west of Durham. The first part of its name reflects the Bishops of Durham, whose hunting lodge here became their main residence and the forerunner of Auckland Castle. The town grew quickly with coal mining during the Industrial Revolution, and after that industry declined, manufacturing became its largest sector. The 2021 census recorded 23,354 people, and the town is covered by the DL14 postcode district. Newton Aycliffe is 8 km away and Spennymoor 9 km, while Darlington and Durham are both a little over 16 km. The town is a short drive from the A1(M) rather than right beside it, with three service areas on that road between 11 km and 14 km away.
roadsText: All three of the nearest service areas to Bishop Auckland are on the A1(M). Forest Park is 11 km from the town, Bradbury 11.9 km and Durham services 14 km. Any of them can serve as a stopping point if a warning light comes on during a run onto the motorway, but none is in the town itself, so on local journeys the nearest services are some way off.

name: Bishop's Cleeve
intro: Cleeve Hill, the highest point in the Cotswolds, rises above Bishop's Cleeve, a large village in the Borough of Tewkesbury, Gloucestershire. It has grown quickly, from 10,612 people in 2011 to 14,068 at the 2021 Census, and is covered by the GL52 postcode district. Cheltenham is the nearest town at 5.7 km, with Tewkesbury at 7.5 km, Churchdown at 11 km and Brockworth at 12.9 km. Gloucester is 15 km away and Evesham 17.5 km, while Oxford is 44 miles (71 km) off. With an AdBlue warning on a van or diesel car, the M5 is the main route to services. The nearest listed service area is Strensham Services, 14.2 km away in a straight line, with Gloucester Services, also on the M5, at 18 km.
roadsText: Both of the nearest listed service areas to Bishop's Cleeve are on the M5: Strensham Services at 14.2 km in a straight line and Gloucester Services at 18 km. Ross Spur Services on the M50 is further at 34.7 km. With nothing listed closer than 14.2 km, drivers in GL52 will usually need a run onto the M5 to reach services, and road distances will be longer than these figures.

name: Bishop's Stortford
intro: Right on the Essex border, Bishop's Stortford is a market town and civil parish in East Hertfordshire, 11 miles (18 km) east-north-east of the county town of Hertford and 28 miles (45 km) north-north-east of Charing Cross. The M11 passes to the east of the town, and Stansted Airport lies immediately east of the motorway. The town grew up around a ford on the River Stort and has been a market town since medieval times. At the 2021 census the built-up area had 40,915 people. The railway station is on the West Anglia Main Line from London Liverpool Street to Cambridge and Stansted Airport. Roads listed for the town are the M11, A120, A1250, A1060 and A1184, and a motorway service area is only 2.3 km away. Sawbridgeworth is 6.6 km away, Harlow 11.7 km and Great Dunmow 13.3 km. The postcode district is CM23.
roadsText: The M11, A120, A1250, A1060 and A1184 are the listed roads. Birchanger Green Services on the M11 is just 2.3 km away, while Boreham Services on the A131 (27.6 km) and Four Went Ways Services on the A11 (28.9 km) are much further. A station in the town (CM23 3LA), about 1 km away, is listed on OpenStreetMap as selling AdBlue at the pump. OpenStreetMap's AdBlue data is incomplete, so there may be others.

name: Bishopbriggs
intro: Approximately 4 miles (6 km) from Glasgow city centre, on the northern fringe of Greater Glasgow, Bishopbriggs is an East Dunbartonshire town that now works as a suburb and commuter town for Glasgow. It grew in the 19th century from a small village on the old road from Glasgow to Kirkintilloch and Stirling, taking in Auchinairn, Cadder, Jellyhill and Mavis Valley along the way. The population is approximately 23,500 and the postcode district is G64. Historically in Lanarkshire, it was an independent burgh from 1964 to 1975. Two motorways, the M80 and M8, appear among its main roads alongside the A803, A807 and A879. Kirkintilloch is about 5.9 km away in a straight line, Bearsden 7.4 km and Milngavie 7.8 km, so most neighbouring places are within 8 km.
roadsText: Main roads listed for Bishopbriggs are the M80, M8, A803, A807, A879, A80, A804 and A81. The nearest service areas are Bothwell Services on the M74, about 14.2 km away in a straight line, Hamilton Services on the M74 at 17.5 km and Stirling Services on the M9 at 26.2 km. A station in Glasgow (G11 6DN), about 7.4 km away, is listed in OpenStreetMap as selling AdBlue at the pump. Coverage of AdBlue in OpenStreetMap is incomplete.

name: Blaby and Whetstone
intro: Old Norse is the likely source of Blaby's name, meaning the farmstead of a man named Blár. The large village lies about five miles south of Leicester city centre in the Blaby District and is part of the Leicester Urban Area. This page covers it together with Whetstone; the combined area has a population of 14,072 and sits in the LE8 postcode district. Neighbouring places are close: Enderby and Narborough is just 3 km away, Wigston 4.2 km, Leicester Forest East and Kirby Muxloe 7 km, and both Oadby and Leicester 7.3 km. The M1 is near too, as Leicester Forest East Services is 6 km from the area, which gives a nearby stop if an AdBlue warning appears on a van or diesel car.
roadsText: Leicester Forest East Services on the M1 is the nearest service area to Blaby and Whetstone, 6 km away. ExtraMSA Leicester Services on the A6 is 13.8 km off and Rugby Services on the M6 is 18.4 km away. Leicester Forest East is much the closest of the three, so it is the stop to remember if a warning comes on nearby.

name: Blackburn
intro: North of the West Pennine Moors, on the southern edge of the Ribble Valley, Blackburn lies 8 miles east of Preston and 21 miles north-north-west of Manchester. It is the administrative centre of Blackburn with Darwen, a unitary authority it shares with the town of Darwen, 5.6 km away. At the 2021 census the town had 124,983 people, making it the second-largest town in Lancashire after Blackpool. It is a former mill town. The M65 is the motorway on the road list, with the A6078, A666, A6077, A677, A678, A6119 and A59 making up the rest. Postcode districts BB1, BB2, BB3 and BB6 cover the area. Oswaldtwistle (5.5 km), Great Harwood (6.8 km) and Accrington (8.1 km) are close by, with Haslingden and Bamber Bridge both around 12 km off. The nearest service area is only 3.7 km away.
roadsText: Blackburn's listed roads are the M65, A6078, A666, A6077, A677, A678, A6119 and A59. The closest service area is Blackburn with Darwen Services on the M65, just 3.7 km away. Rivington Services on the M61 is 17.3 km off and Charnock Richard Services on the M6 is 18.7 km, so for most drivers in BB1 to BB3 and BB6 the M65 services will be the first stop.

name: Blackpool
intro: Blackpool lies on the Irish Sea coast of the Fylde peninsula, about 14 miles west of Preston and 27 miles north of Liverpool. It grew from a hamlet into a resort once sea bathing became fashionable, and the opening of a railway station in 1846 brought visitors in larger numbers. The coastal position shapes driving here. The M55 is the only motorway on the road list, and the nearest service areas in the data are all on the M6 or M58, at least 24.9 km away. The rest of the list is made up of the A583, A5073, A587, A5230, A5099, A584 and A586. Postcode districts FY1, FY2, FY3, FY4 and FY8 cover the town. Lytham St Anne's (5.3 km) and Poulton-le-Fylde (6.4 km) are the nearest towns, with Thornton (8.9 km), Cleveleys (9.6 km) and Fleetwood (12.9 km) also close.
roadsText: Blackpool's main roads are the M55 with the A583, A5073, A587, A5230, A5099, A584 and A586. Service areas are some distance away: Lancaster Services on the M6 is 24.9 km, Charnock Richard Services, also on the M6, 28.2 km, and Old Meadow Services on the M58 32.2 km. With the nearest listed services that far off, a low AdBlue warning is best dealt with before leaving town.

name: Blackwood
intro: Set on the Sirhowy River in the South Wales Valleys, Blackwood (Coed Duon) is a town, community and electoral ward administered as part of Caerphilly County Borough, within the historic county of Monmouthshire. The town houses a growing number of light industrial and high-tech firms. The NP12 postcode district covers it. Ystrad Mynach is 3.5 km away, with Risca at 7.6 km, Abertillery at 8.9 km and Caerphilly at 10.2 km, while Pontypridd and Cwmbrân are 11.5 km and 12 km away. The nearest listed service areas are all on the M4, the closest 15.1 km away in a straight line and the next at 19.2 km. That means a driver who gets an AdBlue warning around Blackwood has some distance to cover before reaching motorway services, and it is sensible to plan the stop rather than leave it late.
roadsText: The three nearest service areas to Blackwood are on the M4: Cardiff Gate Services, 15.1 km away in a straight line, Cardiff West Services at 19.2 km and Magor Services at 26.6 km. Road distances will be longer than these straight-line figures. With no service area close to the town, a van or diesel car showing an AdBlue warning is better dealt with promptly than driven on in the hope of a stop.

name: Blandford Forum
intro: Rebuilt after a major fire in 1731, Blandford Forum is a Dorset market town on the River Stour known for its Georgian architecture. It lies 13 miles (21 km) north-west of Poole and had 10,607 residents at the 2021 census, within the DT11 postcode district. The local economy is a mix of the service sector and light industry, and on the hills 2 miles (3 km) north-east of the town is Blandford Camp, a military base and home of the Royal Corps of Signals. Service areas are a long way off from here: the nearest listed one is 30.3 km away in a straight line, on the A31, so an AdBlue warning is better dealt with sooner than later. Corfe Mullen is the closest neighbouring town at 14.6 km, then Wimborne Minster at 15.2 km and Ferndown at 19.5 km.
roadsText: No listed service area is close to Blandford Forum. Picket Post Services on the A31 is the nearest at 30.3 km in a straight line, Rufus Stone, also on the A31, is 38 km away and Warminster Services on the A350 is 39.8 km. Two Shell sites are listed in OpenStreetMap as selling AdBlue at the pump: MFG Creekmoor in Poole (BH17 7FR) at 18.1 km and Gillingham Service Station at 20 km. That list is incomplete.

name: Blantyre
intro: Bounded by the River Clyde to the north, the Rotten Calder to the west, the Rotten Burn to the south and the Park Burn to the east, Blantyre is a South Lanarkshire town and civil parish of about 16,900 people. The Park Burn marks its boundary with the larger adjoining town of Hamilton, which is only about 3.5 km away. Blantyre is also known as the birthplace of the explorer David Livingstone. Postcode district G72 covers the town. Cambuslang is about 4.4 km away in a straight line, Viewpark 4.5 km, Bellshill 5.4 km, Motherwell 6.6 km and East Kilbride 6.8 km, so the town sits among a tight cluster of neighbouring towns. For an AdBlue warning, Blantyre is well placed: two M74 service areas are only about 3.1 km and 3.9 km away.
roadsText: Two M74 service areas are close to Blantyre: Bothwell Services, about 3.1 km away in a straight line, and Hamilton Services, about 3.9 km. The M74 Truck Stop, on the same motorway, is about 20.6 km away. The nearest station listed in OpenStreetMap as selling AdBlue at the pump is in Glasgow (G11 6DN), about 15.8 km away, though that coverage is incomplete.

name: Blaydon
intro: Together with neighbouring Winlaton, which it now runs into, Blaydon forms the town of Blaydon-on-Tyne in the Metropolitan Borough of Gateshead. Historically it was in County Durham, and between 1894 and 1974 the Blaydon urban district stretched 16 km inland from the Tyne along the River Derwent, taking in the mining communities of Chopwell and High Spen and villages such as Rowlands Gill and Winlaton Mill. The Blaydon and Winlaton ward had 13,896 residents in 2011, and the town is in the NE21 postcode district. Whickham is only 2.2 km away and Newcastle upon Tyne 5.9 km, with Gateshead at 8.2 km, Prudhoe at 9.2 km and Ponteland at 9.8 km. With neighbours this close, many trips in a van or diesel car are fairly short.
roadsText: Washington services on the A1(M) is 12.1 km from Blaydon and Seaton Burn on the A19 is 12.7 km, so the two nearest service areas are about equally far. Easington, also on the A19, is 28.1 km away. A station in Newcastle upon Tyne, 11.3 km from the town, is listed in OpenStreetMap as selling AdBlue at the pump; that list is incomplete, so other forecourts may also sell it.

name: Bletchley
intro: One of the constituent towns of Milton Keynes, Bletchley gives its name to a census built-up area covering the south-west of the city, home to 45,010 people in 2021. The West Coast Main Line railway divides that area between Bletchley and Fenny Stratford, which holds the commercial centre, and West Bletchley, which includes the old pre-railway village centre. Postcode districts here include MK1, MK2, MK3, MK4 and MK17. The A5, A421, A4146 and A509 are the main roads listed, and Milton Keynes itself is 5.2km away. Leighton Buzzard is 9.5km and Newport Pagnell 10km, with Flitwick at 16.5km and Buckingham at 17km. No motorway appears on the road list, and the nearest service areas are all on the M1, so a diesel driver here mostly uses A roads around the city.
roadsText: The A421, A5, A4146 and A509 are the main roads listed for Bletchley. Every one of the nearest service areas is on the M1: Crawley Crossing Truck Stop at 9.7km, Newport Pagnell Services at 10km and Toddington Services at 16.9km. For a van with an AdBlue warning, the M1 is where the closest roadside stops are.

name: Bloxwich
intro: Between Walsall, Cannock, Willenhall and Brownhills lies Bloxwich, a market town in the Metropolitan Borough of Walsall with a population of 51,891. Postcode districts listed for the town are WS1, WS2, WS3, WS4 and WV12. Four motorways appear on the local road list, the M6, M54, M5 and M6 Toll, along with the A34, A461, A4148 and A454. Neighbouring places are very close: Pelsall is about 2.8km away, Rushall and Shelfield 3km, Willenhall 3.7km and Walsall 4km. For a diesel van or car, Bloxwich combines short local trips with easy access to several motorways. Two motorway service areas are within 6.3km, so a planned stop is not far away if an AdBlue warning comes on during a longer run.
roadsText: Hilton Park services on the M6 is about 5.3km from Bloxwich and Norton Canes services on the M6 Toll 6.3km, with a truck stop on the A5 at 9km. The town's listed roads are the M6, M54, M5, M6 Toll, A34, A461, A4148 and A454. OpenStreetMap lists forecourts in Burntwood (about 8.7km) and Warley (about 12.1km), plus an HGV-only site in Birmingham (19.8km), as selling AdBlue at the pump. Its coverage is incomplete.

name: Blyth
intro: Southeast Northumberland's coast is home to Blyth, an industrial port town and civil parish south of the River Blyth, with 39,731 people at the 2021 census, up 6% from 37,347 in 2011. The port dates from the 12th century, although the modern town only began to develop in the early 18th century. Coal mining and shipbuilding helped it prosper, and while those industries have largely gone, the port still receives paper and pulp from Scandinavia. The town has been undergoing regeneration since the early 1990s. The A189 and A193 are among its main roads, along with the A190, A192, A1061, A1068, A1147 and A1171, and its postcode districts include NE24. Bedlington is 4.7km away, Cramlington 5.7km and Ashington 6.6km. Seaton Burn Services is 9.2km away, but the next listed services are 25.8km off, which is worth knowing if an AdBlue warning appears on a longer run.
roadsText: Eight main roads are listed for Blyth: the A189, A193, A1061, A1147, A192, A190, A1068 and A1171. Seaton Burn Services on the A19 is the nearest listed service area at 9.2km. After that the distances jump: Washington Services on the A1(M) is 25.8km away and Easington Services on the A19 36.9km. According to OpenStreetMap, whose records are incomplete, a station in Newcastle upon Tyne, 10.1km away, is listed as selling AdBlue at the pump.

name: Bo'ness
intro: Borrowstounness, usually shortened to Bo'ness, is a town, former burgh and seaport on the south bank of the Firth of Forth. Historically part of West Lothian, it now lies in the Falkirk council area, 17 miles (27 kilometres) north-west of Edinburgh and 6¾ miles (11 kilometres) east of Falkirk. The 2011 census counted 15,100 residents. Until the 20th century the town was a site of coal mining, saltmaking and pottery; the coal mine closed in 1982 and the waterfront is now mainly used for leisure, though an ironworks and a timberyard and sawmill remain beside the Forth. Postcode district EH51 covers the town. Linlithgow is about 3.8 km away in a straight line and Grangemouth 7.1 km, with Broxburn, Rosyth and Bathgate between 11.3 km and 12.5 km. For an AdBlue warning, the three nearest service areas are on the M8, M9 and M90, between about 18.8 km and 24.5 km away.
roadsText: Heart of Scotland Services on the M8 is the nearest service area to Bo'ness, about 18.8 km away in a straight line. Stirling Services on the M9 is about 21 km away and Kinross Services on the M90 about 24.5 km. Each sits on a different motorway, so the best choice from the EH51 district depends on which way a driver is already heading.

name: Bodmin
intro: South-west of Bodmin Moor, Bodmin is a Cornish town whose civil parish matches the town closely, so the area is mostly urban in character. It had 16,909 residents at the 2021 census and is covered by the PL31 postcode district. Bodmin became the county town of Cornwall in 1838, when the main courts moved there from Launceston, though it gradually lost its county town functions to Truro, with the county's main courthouse moving there in 1988. Around the parish are Cardinham, Lanhydrock, Lanivet and Helland. St Austell is the nearest town at 14.6 km and Liskeard 18 km, while Newquay is 25.1 km away. For a van or diesel car with an AdBlue warning, the nearest listed service area is Cornwall Services on the A30, 8.5 km away in a straight line.
roadsText: Cornwall Services on the A30 is the nearest listed service area to Bodmin, 8.5 km away in a straight line. The next options are a lot further: Saltash Services on the A388 at 34.3 km and Roundswell Service Area on the A39 at 79.8 km. For drivers in PL31 with an AdBlue warning, the A30 site is by some distance the closest stop.

name: Bognor Regis
intro: Known simply as Bognor to many, Bognor Regis is a town and seaside resort in the Arun district of West Sussex, 6 miles (10 km) south-east of Chichester and 16 miles (26 km) east of Portsmouth. The nearby villages of Felpham and Aldwick are now suburbs, along with North and South Bersted, and the built-up area had 63,855 people at the 2011 census. The town gained the Regis name by royal consent in 1929. Postcode districts are PO21 and PO22. The A259 and A29 are the only main roads listed, and neither is a motorway. Barnham is 5.9 km away, Chichester 8.2 km and Selsey 9.8 km. The nearest listed services for a driver with an AdBlue warning are at Fontwell, 7.5 km away on the A27.
roadsText: Only two main roads are listed for Bognor Regis: the A259 and the A29. The nearest listed service area is Fontwell Services on the A27, 7.5 km away. Beyond that the distances grow: Farlington Services, also on the A27, is 25.4 km and Petersfield Services on the A3 is 30.4 km. Fontwell is the realistic first stop for most drivers in the town.

name: Bolsover
intro: The administrative centre of its own district, Bolsover is a Derbyshire market town 18 miles from Sheffield, 26 miles from Nottingham and 27 miles from Derby. Its civil parish, Old Bolsover, takes in the town along with the New Bolsover model village, Hillstown, Carr Vale, Shuttlewood, Stanfree, Oxcroft and Whaley. The parish had 11,673 residents at the 2011 census, and the postcode district is S44. Staveley is 5.6 km away, Shirebrook 6.2 km and Brimington 7.3 km, with Chesterfield 9.6 km off. Two M1 service areas are within about 11 km, which matters if a van or diesel car shows an AdBlue warning.
roadsText: Welcome Break Woodall Services on the M1 is 9.4 km from Bolsover and Tibshelf Services, also on the M1, is 10.7 km away. Sheffield Service Area on the A6102 is further out at 17.7 km. A station 14.4 km from Bolsover is listed on OpenStreetMap as selling AdBlue at the pump. Because that dataset is incomplete, a nearer forecourt may sell AdBlue too.

name: Bolton
intro: In the foothills of the West Pennine Moors, Bolton sits between Manchester, Blackburn, Wigan, Bury and Salford. It is the administrative centre of a metropolitan borough of 296,169 people, with 184,073 living in the town itself. Bolton began as a small moorland settlement known as Bolton le Moors and grew into a mill town, and the towns and villages around it now make up the wider borough. The postcode districts listed are BL1, BL2, BL3, BL4, BL7 and M38. The M61 is the motorway on the road list, joined by the A666, A673, A58, A579, A6, A6027 and A6099. Farnworth (4.9 km) and Little Lever (5.1 km) are the closest neighbours, with Kearsley, Little Hulton, Horwich and Westhoughton all within 7.5 km. For a driver with an AdBlue warning, the nearest service area in the data is on the M61, 9.3 km away.
roadsText: Bolton's main roads are the M61, A666, A673, A58, A579, A6, A6027 and A6099. Rivington Services on the M61 is the nearest service area at 9.3 km, followed by Birch Services on the M62 at 13.6 km and Blackburn with Darwen Services on the M65 at 14.1 km. Stations in Manchester's M25 postcode district (11.2 km) and in Warrington's WA3 (19.9 km) are listed as selling AdBlue at the pump in OpenStreetMap; the list is not exhaustive.

name: Bonnyrigg
intro: Between the Rivers North Esk and South Esk, 13 km southeast of Edinburgh city centre, Bonnyrigg had an estimated 18,120 people in 2018, the highest of any town in Midlothian. The locality takes in the adjacent settlement of Lasswade, along with Polton village, the Poltonhall housing estate and modern development at Hopefield. EH19 and EH18 are the postcode districts. Mayfield is 3.6 km away and Dalkeith 3.7 km, with Penicuik at 8.1 km and Musselburgh at 8.3 km. For a driver dealing with an AdBlue warning, the useful detail is that two service areas, one on the A1 and one on the A720, are 6.7 km and 8.3 km from the town, so reaching a stop does not mean a long detour.
roadsText: The nearest service area to Bonnyrigg is Musselburgh Services on the A1, 6.7 km away. Dreghorn Services on the A720 is 8.3 km and MacMerry, also on the A1, is 16.6 km. With two stops within 8.3 km on different roads, drivers have a choice depending on which way they are heading.

name: Bootle
intro: Bootle lies close to the Irish Sea with Liverpool to the south, and that position shaped its growth. It expanded rapidly in the 1800s, first as a dormitory town for wealthy merchants and then as a centre of commerce and industry after the railway arrived and the docks expanded. Historically part of Lancashire, it is now in the Metropolitan Borough of Sefton and part of the Liverpool City Region. Large-scale renewal projects have begun to help regenerate the local economy. Seven postcode districts are listed: L4, L5, L9, L20, L21, L22 and L30. Litherland is just 2 km away and Crosby 4 km, with Wallasey at 6 km, Liverpool and Maghull at 7.1 km and Kirkby at 8.1 km. The M57 and M58 are both on the road list, with the A565, A5058, A5036, A59, A506 and A580.
roadsText: Bootle's main roads include the M57 and M58, plus the A565, A5058, A5036, A59, A506 and A580. Old Meadow Services on the M58 is 8.5 km away and Earlsfield Services on the M57 11.7 km, with Burtonwood Services on the M62 at 24.1 km. In OpenStreetMap, a station at Old Meadow (8.6 km) is listed as selling AdBlue at the pump. A site in L5, 2.9 km away, is also listed but marked HGV-only. The data is incomplete.

name: Borehamwood
intro: Twelve miles (19 km) from Charing Cross, Borehamwood, historically also written Boreham Wood, is a town in southern Hertfordshire within the London commuter belt. It is in the Hertsmere district, and its film and TV studios are commonly known as Elstree Studios. For a diesel driver, what stands out is the number of major roads listed nearby: the M1, M25, A1(M), A1 and A41, plus the A5135, A411 and A5183. Two motorway service areas are within 5 km of the town. Bushey is 5.8 km away, Barnet 6.7 km and Potters Bar 7.6 km, with Harrow at 8.7 km, Watford 9.1 km and St Albans 10.9 km. Postcode districts are WD6 and WD7. The population is 39,760.
roadsText: The M1, M25, A1(M), A1 and A41 are listed for Borehamwood, with the A5135, A411 and A5183. Two service areas are very close: London Gateway Services on the M1 at 3.1 km and South Mimms Services on the A1(M) at 4.8 km. Bourne End Services on the A41 is further away, at 19.8 km.

name: Boston
intro: An inland port as well as a market town, Boston lies in Lincolnshire to the south-east of Lincoln, east of Nottingham and north-east of Peterborough. The Haven flows about 5 miles (8 km) from the town to the Lincolnshire coast at The Wash, and the surrounding land is the flat country of Lincolnshire, across which St Botolph's Church can be seen from miles away. The town had 45,339 residents at the 2021 census and its postcode district is PE21. The nearest towns are some distance off: Spalding is about 23.5 km away, Sleaford 26.2 km, Skegness 29.6 km and Bourne 33 km. Main roads are the A16, A52, A1121, A1137 and A1138. Three service areas sit just over 10 km out, on the A16, A52 and A17, which gives a driver with an AdBlue warning a choice of directions.
roadsText: Boston's main roads are the A16, A52, A1121, A1137 and A1138. Three service areas lie a similar distance from town: Sutterton Services on the A16 at about 10.2 km, Bicker Bar Services on the A52 at 10.3 km and Sutterton Truck Stop on the A17 at 10.4 km.

name: Bourne
intro: Lincolnshire's South Kesteven district includes the market town of Bourne, which lies on the eastern slopes of the limestone Kesteven Uplands and the western edge of the Fens. It is 11 miles (18 km) north-east of Stamford, 12 miles (19 km) west of Spalding and 17 miles (27 km) north of Peterborough, and a 2019 estimate put its population at 16,780. The postcode district is PE10. Further afield, Grantham is about 23.8 km away, Sleaford 25.9 km and Oakham 26.2 km. That spread is reflected in the service areas: the nearest, on the A16 and A1, are between about 14.6 km and 16.3 km out. Closer to home, one station in Bourne is listed in OpenStreetMap as selling AdBlue at the pump, which may help if a warning appears locally.
roadsText: Bourne's nearest service areas are Lincs Gateway Services on the A16, about 14.6 km away, and Colsterworth Truck Stop and Colsterworth Services on the A1, at around 16.1 km and 16.3 km. Two stations are listed in OpenStreetMap as selling AdBlue at the pump: a BP in Bourne (PE10 0EN), about 4.7 km away, and BP Colsterworth Service Station at about 16.6 km. The data is incomplete.

name: Bournemouth
intro: A seven-mile stretch of golden sand runs along the coast at Bournemouth, the largest town in Dorset, which had a built-up population of 196,455 at the 2021 census. The coastal resort is in the Bournemouth, Christchurch and Poole unitary area and is a population centre within the South East Dorset conurbation, with its shoreline continuing west towards Sandbanks and Poole. The town attracts over five million visitors a year, and financial services now play a significant role in the local economy alongside tourism. Postcode districts include BH1, BH2, BH3, BH4, BH5, BH8, BH9 and BH10. Neighbouring towns are close: Poole is 5.8 km away, Ferndown 7.2 km and Christchurch 9.1 km, with West Moors, Wimborne Minster and Corfe Mullen all within 10.6 km. For a van or diesel car, many trips here are short runs between neighbouring towns, which is worth bearing in mind when the nearest service areas are some distance out.
roadsText: The main roads around Bournemouth are the A338, A35, A3049, A348, A347, A3060, A3040 and A341. Picket Post on the A31 is the nearest service area at 16.2 km, with Rufus Stone on the A31 at 25.4 km and West Wellow on the A36 at 33.7 km. A forecourt at Creekmoor in Poole (BH17 7FR), 8.5 km away, is listed as selling AdBlue at the pump in OpenStreetMap data. The map data is incomplete, so other stations may sell it too.

name: Brackley
intro: Where West Northamptonshire meets Oxfordshire and Buckinghamshire, Brackley is a market town of 16,195 people (2021) that grew up on the trade routes linking London, Birmingham, the Midlands, Cambridge and Oxford. Banbury is 9 miles to the west-north-west, Oxford 19 miles to the south-south-west and Northampton 22 miles to the north-east. The postcode district is NN13. No other town is especially close: Buckingham is 11.9 km away, Banbury 13.4 km, Bicester 14.8 km and Towcester 15.4 km, with Daventry 25.7 km off. The nearest motorway services are 9.8 km away on the M40. With that spacing, it helps to know the options before an AdBlue warning on a van or diesel car becomes urgent.
roadsText: Brackley's nearest service area is Moto Cherwell Valley Services on the M40, 9.8 km away. Towcester Services on the A43 is 14.5 km from the town and Jacks Hill Cafe & Truck Stop on the A5 is 16 km away. That puts stops on three different routes, the M40, the A43 and the A5, all within 16 km of Brackley.

name: Bracknell
intro: Declared a New Town in the 20th century, Bracknell grew rapidly and absorbed surrounding villages including Easthampstead, Ramslade and Old Bracknell. It is now the third largest town in Berkshire and the administrative centre of Bracknell Forest, lying 11 miles (18 km) east of Reading and 25 miles (40 km) west of central London. Postcode districts are RG12 and RG42. The road list includes the M4 and A329(M), along with the A322, A329 and A332. Neighbouring towns are close: Crowthorne is 4.6 km away, Wokingham 6.4 km, Ascot 6.8 km and Sandhurst 6.9 km. Even so, none of the listed service areas is in the town, with the nearest 14.3 km away on the M3, so a driver with an AdBlue warning is better off knowing the options in advance.
roadsText: The M4 and A329(M) are the motorways listed for Bracknell, with the A322, A329, A3095, A332, A330 and A321 making up the rest of the list. The nearest listed service area is Fleet Services on the M3, 14.3 km away, followed by Reading Services on the M4 at 19.4 km and Beaconsfield Services on the M40 at 22 km. The Swallowfield By-pass station (RG7 1LZ), 15.9 km away, is listed as selling AdBlue at the pump in OpenStreetMap, an incomplete source.

name: Bradford
intro: About 9 miles (14 km) west of Leeds, Bradford is the second-largest part of the West Yorkshire Built-up Area, with 352,317 people in the city itself at the 2021 census and 546,976 across the wider metropolitan borough. It grew in the 19th century as an international centre of textile manufacture, particularly wool, which earned it the nickname 'Wool City'. The one motorway among the main roads listed is the M606, alongside A roads such as the A647, A650 and A6177. Postcode districts include BD1, BD2, BD3, BD5, BD6, BD7, BD8 and BD9. Neighbouring towns are close: Shipley is 4.3 km away measured directly, Pudsey 5.9 km, Baildon 6.1 km and Bingley 8 km, so an AdBlue warning that shows up on a local run could come on in any of them as easily as in the city.
roadsText: The M606 is the motorway listed among Bradford's main roads, together with the A647, A650, A6177, A658, A6036, A6120 and A6181. The nearest service area is Hartshead Moor on the M62, 8.9 km away measured directly, followed by Skelton Lake Service Station on the M1 (19.3 km) and Woolley Edge on the M1 (23.7 km). OpenStreetMap lists a station with a Leeds address, 19.4 km away, as selling AdBlue at the pump. The map data behind that is incomplete.

name: Bradley Stoke
intro: Bounded by the M5 and M4 to the north and east, Bradley Stoke is the northernmost part of the Bristol built-up area, about 10 km north-north-east of the city centre. It was planned in the late 1970s, building began in 1987, and it became Europe's largest new town built with private investment. It is primarily a residential suburb, with fewer major employers than its neighbours Patchway to the west and Stoke Gifford to the south, and it forms part of the North Fringe of Bristol. The BS32 and BS34 postcode districts cover the town, which has a population of 25,194. Patchway is 2.1 km away, Stoke Gifford and Filton 2.6 km, and Frampton Cotterell and Winterbourne 4.5 km. For van and diesel-car drivers, motorways are right on the doorstep, with four of them listed among the roads nearby.
roadsText: Four motorways are listed around Bradley Stoke: the M4, M5, M32 and M48, along with the A4174, A38, A4017 and A4018. The nearest service area is Severn View on the M48, 9.5 km away, followed by Avon Lodge on the A4 at 10.2 km and Gordano on the M5 at 12.5 km.

name: Bradwell
intro: Immediately west of Great Yarmouth and Gorleston-on-Sea, Bradwell is a Norfolk village and civil parish that is largely indistinguishable from their built-up area. It has a population of 11,632 and falls in the Great Yarmouth district and the NR31 postcode district. Gorleston-on-Sea is 1.9 km from the centre and Great Yarmouth 3.1 km, with Lowestoft 11.9 km away and Norwich 29 km. North Walsham and Taverham and Drayton are both about 34 km off. For a driver whose van or diesel car shows an AdBlue warning, the key point is distance to services: the nearest listed service area, Thickthorn Services on the A11, is 32.2 km away in a straight line, and the next is more than 63 km away. Road distances will be longer again.
roadsText: Service areas are a long way from Bradwell. Thickthorn Services on the A11 is the nearest at 32.2 km in a straight line, followed by Beacon Hill Services on the A140 at 63.6 km and Sprougton Road Services on the A14 at 69.8 km. Road distances will be longer still, so drivers in NR31 should not count on a services stop being close.

name: Braintree
intro: Bypassed by the A120 and A131, Braintree is the largest settlement in Braintree District, with 43,190 people in its built-up area at the 2021 census. The district also covers an extensive surrounding area, so a Braintree District address may well be outside the town. The town has grown into its neighbouring settlements. The original parish lay on the River Brain, bounded to the north by Stane Street, the Roman road from Braughing to Colchester, with the parish of Bocking beyond it; the two were united in 1934 as Braintree and Bocking. Trains serve two stations in the town, at the end of the Braintree Branch Line from Witham. Halstead is 8.9 km away, Witham 10.3 km, Great Dunmow 13.7 km and Chelmsford 16.7 km, with Maldon and Sudbury a little further. The A1017 is also listed among the main roads. Postcode districts are CM7 and CM77.
roadsText: The A120 and A131 bypass the town, and the A1017 is also listed. Boreham Services on the A131 is 14.4 km away, Birchanger Green Services on the M11 24.7 km and Ardleigh South Services on the A120 29 km. Lorry pumps in Chelmsford (CM2 5PY), 14.4 km away, are listed on OpenStreetMap as selling AdBlue at the pump but are marked HGV-only. OpenStreetMap's AdBlue data is incomplete.

name: Bramhall
intro: Formerly a civil parish in Cheshire, Bramhall is now a large village in the Metropolitan Borough of Stockport, Greater Manchester. At the 2021 census its built-up area, as defined by the Office for National Statistics, had a population of 17,195. The SK7 postcode district covers the village. Cheadle Hulme is the nearest neighbour at about 2.1 km, with Hazel Grove at 3.1 km and Poynton at 3.4 km. Cheadle is around 4.1 km away and Stockport 5 km, while Wilmslow is about 6.2 km away. Six neighbouring towns and villages lie within about 6.2 km. The point to note if an AdBlue warning appears is that the nearest motorway service areas, both on the M6, are about 17.5 km and 18.1 km away.
roadsText: The nearest service areas to Bramhall are on the M6: Knutsford Services, about 17.5 km away, and Tabley Hill Service Station, about 18.1 km. Lymm Services, also on the M6, is around 22.7 km off. OpenStreetMap has a site roughly 17.1 km away listed as selling AdBlue at the pump. Its records are incomplete, so somewhere nearer may also sell it.

name: Bredbury and Woodley
intro: Between the valleys of the rivers Tame and Goyt, Bredbury sits on the lower southern slopes of Werneth Low, an outlier of the Pennines. The town is in the Metropolitan Borough of Stockport, 8 miles (12.9 km) south-east of Manchester, 2 miles (3.2 km) east of Stockport and 3 miles (4.8 km) south-west of Hyde. Together with Woodley it forms a built-up area that had 17,040 residents at the 2021 census. The SK6 postcode district covers it. Romiley is about 2.2 km away, Denton 3 km and Reddish 3.6 km, with Stockport, Hyde and Marple all between 3.7 km and 4.3 km. Six neighbouring places sit within 4.3 km of the town. For a van or diesel car with an AdBlue warning, the nearest motorway services are much further, at Birch on the M62, about 17.7 km away.
roadsText: The nearest service area to Bredbury and Woodley is Birch Services on the M62, about 17.7 km away. Knutsford Services and Tabley Hill Service Station, both on the M6, are around 23.7 km and 24 km off. OpenStreetMap has a site roughly 10.6 km away listed as selling AdBlue at the pump, and one under Manchester at about 17.2 km. Those records are incomplete, so nearer stations may also sell it.

name: Brent
intro: West and north-west London's Brent is an Outer London borough with an estimated 353,000 residents as of 2024. Its major districts are Kenton, Kilburn, Willesden, Wembley and Harlesden, with Stonebridge, Kingsbury, Kensal Green, Neasden and Queen's Park as sub-districts. Land use is a mixture of residential, industrial and commercial, including the Park Royal commercial estate, and the borough has an inner-city character in the east and a more suburban one in the west. For a diesel van, that can mean industrial land and residential streets on the same round, spread across the HA0, HA9, NW9 and NW10 postcode districts. The M1, A406, A40, A41 and A1 are among the main roads in and around Brent. Harrow is 6km away, Ealing 6.4km and Barnet 7.8km, so an AdBlue warning that starts on a Brent job can easily follow the vehicle over a borough boundary.
roadsText: The main road refs here are the M1, A406, A40, A41, A1, A598, A4089 and A479. London Gateway Services on the M1 is the nearest listed service area at 8.1km, followed by Heston Services on the M4 (11.2km) and South Mimms Services on the A1(M) (14.8km). Because the M1 is one of Brent's own main roads, London Gateway is the stop most within reach for a vehicle already on it.

name: Brentwood
intro: Just outside the M25 London Orbital Motorway, 20 miles (32 km) north-east of Charing Cross, Brentwood is part of the London commuter belt. Its suburbs include Shenfield, Warley, Brook Street and Hutton, and the Borough of Brentwood also covers surrounding rural areas, so not every Brentwood address is in the town itself. The High Street runs along a Roman road that became one of the main routes between London and East Anglia. Beyond the town centre, residential areas are surrounded by open countryside and woodland, some of it within a few hundred yards of the centre. The built-up area had 55,340 people at the 2021 census. The M25, A12 and A127 are the big roads listed for the town, with the A128, A1023 and A129 alongside them. Havering is 7.8 km away and Billericay 8.6 km. Postcode districts are CM13, CM14 and CM15.
roadsText: The M25, A12 and A127 are all listed for Brentwood, along with the A128, A1023 and A129. Orsett Cock Services on the A13 is 14.4 km away and Thurrock Services on the M25 is 14.9 km away, with Boreham Services on the A131 at 20.9 km. One station 17.7 km from the town is listed on OpenStreetMap as selling AdBlue at the pump, though OpenStreetMap's AdBlue data is incomplete.

name: Bridgend
intro: Pen-y-bont ar Ogwr, the Welsh name for Bridgend, means the end of the bridge on the Ogmore, and the town is named after the medieval bridge over the River Ogmore. It lies halfway between Cardiff and Swansea, 32 km from each, and the River Ewenny also flows through it. Bridgend has greatly expanded since the early 1980s, from 39,429 people in 2001 to 49,597 in 2021, and it lies within the Cardiff Capital Region. The CF31 and CF35 postcode districts cover the town. Sarn is 4.2 km away, Pyle 8.4 km and Porthcawl 9.3 km, with Tonyrefail at 12.2 km and Maesteg at 12.8 km. With the M4 among the main roads and a motorway service area just 2.9 km from the centre, diesel vans and cars here can move easily between local roads and the motorway.
roadsText: Bridgend's main roads include the M4, A4061, A473, A4063, A48, A4065, A4064 and A4106. Sarn Park services on the M4 is just 2.9 km from the town, so it is the obvious place to pull in. The next options are Cardiff West on the M4 at 17.8 km and Cardiff Gate on the M4 at 30.3 km.

name: Bridgnorth
intro: A bridge over the River Severn gives Bridgnorth its name, and the river divides this Shropshire market town and civil parish in two: High Town, the upper town on the west bank, and Low Town on the east bank. The population at the 2011 Census was 12,079, and the town is in the WV16 postcode district. It is some way from other towns: Wombourne is 15.1 km away, Telford 17.3 km, Kingswinford and Codsall both 18.5 km, Sedgley 19.9 km and Kidderminster 20.1 km. Distance to services matters here when an AdBlue warning comes on. The nearest listed service area is on the M54, 15.8 km off in a straight line, and the next two are more than 27 km away, so it is better to plan a stop than hope to find one.
roadsText: Service areas are not close to Bridgnorth. The nearest is Telford Services on the M54, 15.8 km away in a straight line. Beyond that, Hilton Park Services on the M6 is 27.4 km off and The Trucker's Rest on the A5 is 29 km. Road distances will be longer than these figures, so an AdBlue warning here is worth acting on before a longer trip.

name: Bridgwater
intro: Each November, Bridgwater hosts its annual carnival, the largest of the Somerset carnivals. The historic market town lies on the River Parrett at the edge of the Somerset Levels, and its built-up area had 47,860 people at the 2021 census. It was once the largest port in Somerset and later developed as an industrial centre, with brick and tile works, ship building and railway engineering. The Battle of Sedgemoor was fought nearby in 1685. The TA6 postcode district covers the town. Burnham-on-Sea is 13 km away and Taunton 13.6 km, with Street at 18.4 km and Weston-super-Mare at 24.7 km. The M5 is among the main roads close to the town, alongside the A39, A38 and A372, so many diesel journeys here combine local roads with motorway stretches.
roadsText: Bridgwater's main roads are the M5, A39, A38 and A372. Bridgwater services on the M5 is just 2.3 km from the town centre, which makes it the obvious place to stop. Sedgemoor services on the M5 is 17.1 km away and Taunton Deane services on the M5 is 19.2 km, giving three options along the same motorway.

name: Bridlington
intro: By the North Sea, on the Holderness part of the Yorkshire Coast, Bridlington is a seaside town in the East Riding of Yorkshire, about 28 miles (45 km) north of Hull and 34 miles (55 km) east of York. It is a sea-fishing port, known as the largest lobster port in Europe, and its main trade is summer tourism. Its population is put at 34,831. For a driver dealing with an AdBlue warning, the key point is distance. The nearest town is Driffield at 17.8 km on a direct line, Scarborough is 22.8 km away, and the three nearest service areas are all more than 52 km off. The main roads are the A165, A614 and A1038, with no motorway among them. The town is covered by the YO15 and YO16 postcode districts.
roadsText: The A165, A614 and A1038 are the main roads listed around Bridlington. Service areas are a long way off by any measure: Ulceby Truckstop on the A160 is 52.1 km away on a direct line, Bilbrough Top Service Area on the A64 is 67.4 km and Doncaster North services on the M180 is 75.8 km. An AdBlue warning here is best not left until a long journey.

name: Bridport
intro: Just 1½ miles (2.4 km) inland from the English Channel, near where the River Brit meets its tributary the Asker, Bridport is a Dorset market town with Saxon origins and a long history as a rope-making centre. At the 2021 census the built-up area had 12,295 residents, and the DT6 postcode district covers it. The town's boundary reaches the coast at West Bay, a small fishing harbour also known as Bridport Harbour. For a driver with an AdBlue warning, the key fact is distance: every listed service area is on the M5, and the closest is 38.5 km away in a straight line. Neighbouring towns are spread out too, with Chard at 21.3 km, Dorchester at 22.2 km, Weymouth at 23.9 km and Yeovil at 24.4 km.
roadsText: Bridport is a long way from any listed service area. The three nearest are all on the M5: RoadChef Taunton Deane Services at 38.5 km in a straight line, Moto Bridgwater Services at 44.6 km and ExtraMSA Cullompton Services at 46.4 km.
