Road distances will be longer still, so an AdBlue warning here is not something to leave until a services stop comes up.

name: Brierfield
intro: Between Burnley and Nelson in the Borough of Pendle, Brierfield is a Lancashire town and civil parish that had 8,193 residents at the 2011 census. Burnley lies 3 miles (4.8 km) to the south-west and Nelson just 1 mile (1.6 km) to the north-east, with Reedley the same short distance to the south-west. The parish adjoins Reedley Hallows, Old Laund Booth and Nelson, the Burnley parish of Briercliffe and the unparished part of Burnley, so it shares boundaries with neighbours on several sides. The BB9 postcode district covers it. Colne is about 5.4 km away and Padiham 6 km, with Barnoldswick and Clitheroe at 10.9 km and 11.9 km. For a driver dealing with an AdBlue warning, Brierfield has one clear advantage: a service station on the M65 is listed only about 0.7 km away.
roadsText: Brierfield is very close to a motorway stop: Hollin Bank Service Station on the M65 is about 0.7 km away. Further out, Blackburn with Darwen Services, also on the M65, is about 20.4 km away in a straight line, and Birch Services on the M62 is about 28.5 km. For drivers in the BB9 district, the M65 is the obvious road to a service area.

name: Brierley Hill
intro: Three miles (five kilometres) south of Dudley and one mile north of Stourbridge, Brierley Hill is a Black Country town in the Metropolitan Borough of Dudley, originally part of Staffordshire. It lies in a heavily industrialised area and is best known for glass and steel manufacturing; the Round Oak Steelworks site was redeveloped in the 1980s as the Merry Hill Shopping Centre, and since 2008 the town has been the Strategic Town Centre of Dudley Borough. Distances between places are short. Stourbridge is 3 km away on a direct line, Kingswinford 3.3 km, Cradley Heath 3.7 km, Dudley 3.8 km and Halesowen 4.2 km, so an AdBlue warning that appears on a local run could leave you in any of them. Postcode districts DY5, DY8, DY2, DY6 and B64 all touch the area. No motorway appears among the main local roads; the A461, A491, A449 and A4036 are among those listed.
roadsText: Every main road listed around Brierley Hill is an A road: the A461, A4036, A458, A491, A449, A456, A4123 and A4100. The nearest motorway service area is Frankley on the M5, 8.6 km away on a direct line, followed by Hopwood Park on the M42 (17 km) and Hilton Park on the M6 (19.2 km). OpenStreetMap lists a station with a Warley address (6.6 km) and another 14.4 km away as selling AdBlue at the pump, though the map records behind that are incomplete.

name: Brighouse
intro: Junction 25 of the M62 serves Brighouse, a Calderdale town on the River Calder 4 miles (6.4 km) east of Halifax. For a van or diesel car with an AdBlue warning, that motorway link is the headline: the M62 and M606 are both listed among the main roads, and Hartshead Moor services is only 2.9 km away in a straight line. The town also has a railway station and a mooring basin on the Calder and Hebble Navigation. Its name comes from a 'Bridge House' on or near the bridge over the Calder, and it began as a hamlet of nearby Rastrick. The 2001 census gave the Brighouse and Rastrick area a population of 32,360. Although local government links it with Halifax, Brighouse has an HD6 postcode, and the HX5 and HD2 districts also reach the area. Elland is 3.7 km away, Cleckheaton 5.1 km and Huddersfield 6.3 km.
roadsText: Main roads around Brighouse include the M62 and M606, together with the A644, A58, A629, A62, A6036 and A6026. Hartshead Moor services on the M62 is by far the closest service area, 2.9 km away in a straight line. The next two are both on the M1: Woolley Edge at 18.2 km and Skelton Lake Service Station at 22.1 km.

name: Brighton and Hove
intro: Two seaside resorts and several villages make up Brighton and Hove, a city and unitary authority that is ceremonially in East Sussex. Together with Worthing and Littlehampton, the two resorts form the second most-populous built-up area in South East England after South Hampshire, and the city itself has a population of around 277,096. Postcode districts across the city include BN1, BN2 and BN3, along with BN7, BN10, BN41, BN42 and BN45. The main roads listed for the area include the A23, A27, A259 and A270, so driving here ranges from city streets to the main routes in and out. Neighbouring towns are close: Lewes is 8.5 km away, Southwick 9 km and Peacehaven 9.4 km. When an AdBlue warning comes on, it helps that the nearest listed service area is 7.9 km away on the A23.
roadsText: Around Brighton and Hove, the main roads listed are the A23, A27, A270, A2010, A259, A2023 and A2038. The nearest listed service areas are on the A23: Pyecombe Services at 7.9 km and Ricebridge Services (Hickstead) at 15.2 km, with Buck Barn on the A24 at 23.4 km. A station about 1.3 km from the city centre is listed as selling AdBlue at the pump in OpenStreetMap; that data is incomplete, so others may stock it too.

name: Brimington
intro: With Staveley 2.3 km to the east and Chesterfield 3.2 km away, Brimington is a large village and civil parish in the Borough of Chesterfield, Derbyshire. The parish includes Brimington Common along the Calow Road and New Brimington, a late 19th-century extension towards the Staveley Iron Works, and Hollingwood is nearby. It had 8,788 residents at the 2011 census and is covered by two postcode districts, S43 and S41. Dronfield is 7 km away and Bolsover 7.3 km. The nearest motorway services are a little over 10 km away at Welcome Break Woodall Services on the M1, so for a van or diesel car with an AdBlue warning, it is worth planning a stop rather than hoping to reach one.
roadsText: The Calow Road runs through Brimington Common. Welcome Break Woodall Services on the M1 is the nearest service area to Brimington, 10.1 km away. Sheffield Service Area on the A6102 is 13.2 km off and Tibshelf Services, also on the M1, is 13.8 km away. All three are more than 10 km away, so a stop needs a little planning.

name: Bristol
intro: The most populous city in the South West, Bristol sits on the River Avon with Gloucestershire to the north, Somerset to the south and a short stretch of Bristol Channel coastline to the west. The city and county are almost entirely urbanised, with an estimated 494,399 people in 2024, and the wider urban area spills over into South Gloucestershire, Bath and North East Somerset and North Somerset. For a van or diesel-car driver, that means a lot of urban driving across postcode districts such as BS1, BS2, BS3, BS4, BS5, BS6, BS7 and BS8. Neighbouring areas are close by: Kingswood and Fishponds is 6.7 km away, Stoke Gifford 6.9 km, Filton 7 km and Keynsham 7.8 km, with Patchway and Bradley Stoke within 9.2 km. An AdBlue warning here is as likely to appear in city traffic as on the way out of town.
roadsText: Main roads around central Bristol include the M32, A38, A4044, A4, A370, A4032, A37 and A3029. The nearest service areas are Gordano on the M5, 8.7 km away, and Avon Lodge on the A4 at 9.1 km. Severn View on the M48 is further out at 17 km. All three sit outside the city centre, so they are most useful on a longer trip rather than a run across town.

name: Brixham
intro: One of England's largest remaining commercial fishing fleets is anchored in the natural harbour around which Brixham is built. The predominantly hilly coastal town, in the borough of Torbay in Devon, is one of the borough's three main centres, along with Paignton and Torquay. Historically the town was two communities: Fishtown by the harbour and Cowtown, one mile (1.6 km) inland around what is now St Mary's Square, on the road out of town to the south-west towards Kingswear. Brixham had 16,825 residents at the 2021 census and is covered by the TQ5 postcode district. Paignton is 5 km away and Torquay 10.9 km. Listed service areas are distant from here: for a van or diesel car with an AdBlue warning, the nearest is Exeter Services on the M5, 36.5 km away in a straight line.
roadsText: Exeter Services on the M5 is the nearest listed service area to Brixham, 36.5 km away in a straight line. Saltash Services on the A388 is 50.2 km off and Cullompton Services, also on the M5, is 53.5 km. With every listed option more than 36 km from TQ5, an AdBlue warning is better dealt with early than left until a long drive.

name: Broadstairs
intro: On the Isle of Thanet in east Kent, about 130 km east of London, Broadstairs is one of Thanet's seaside resorts, set between Margate and Ramsgate. Margate is 3.6 km away and Ramsgate 3 km, so the three towns sit close together and many local trips are short. The town spreads from Haine Road in the west to Kingsgate in the north and Dumpton in the south, and the civil parish of Broadstairs and St Peter's includes St Peter's itself. Postcode districts in the area are CT10, CT9 and CT11, and the population is 25,780. Beyond Thanet the distances open up: Deal is 16.7 km away, Herne Bay 19.3 km and Canterbury 25.6 km. That mix of short local journeys and longer runs out of Thanet is worth bearing in mind for anyone running a diesel van or car here.
roadsText: The main roads around Broadstairs are the A256, A299, A28, A255 and A254. The closest service area is Minster on the A299, 7.7 km away. After that the distances grow: Whitfield on the A2 is 25.2 km and Folkestone services on the M20 is 39.9 km. For a longer trip out of Thanet, Minster is the realistic place to stop before heading further.

name: Brockworth
intro: Brockworth's population rose from 7,387 in 2011 to 9,422 at the 2021 census. The village lies in the Borough of Tewkesbury on the old Roman road linking the City of Gloucester with Barnwood, 4 miles (6.4 km) south-east of central Gloucester and 11.5 miles (18.5 km) north of Stroud, and it is in the GL3 postcode district. It is known locally for the annual rolling of Double Gloucester cheese down Cooper's Hill, and during the Second World War the Gloster Aircraft Company built the Hawker Hurricane here. A driver with an AdBlue warning is well placed in Brockworth, because Westmorland Gloucester Services on the M5 is only 5.4 km away in a straight line. Gloucester is 4.4 km away, Churchdown 5.2 km and Cheltenham 7.7 km, with Stroud at 12.3 km.
roadsText: Westmorland Gloucester Services on the M5 is the nearest service area to Brockworth, just 5.4 km away in a straight line. The next two are also M5 sites but much further off: RoadChef Strensham Services at 23.9 km and Welcome Break Michaelwood Services at 28 km. For most drivers in GL3, the Gloucester services will be the practical first stop if an AdBlue warning comes on.

name: Bromley
intro: As the largest and southeasternmost borough in London, Bromley covers a lot of ground. It borders Surrey and Kent and was itself part of Kent until 1965. The borough takes its name from Bromley, its principal town, and its other districts include Penge, Hayes, West Wickham, Chislehurst, Beckenham and Orpington. At the 2021 census it had 329,991 residents. Because the borough is so large, a van covering it end to end can be a long way from home when an AdBlue warning appears. The main roads listed are the A21, A20, A232, A233, A222, A208, A2022 and A223, and postcode districts include BR1, BR2, BR4 and BR6. Lewisham is 8.8km away, Swanley 9km and Croydon 9.4km.
roadsText: The road list for Bromley covers the A21, A232, A20, A233, A222, A208, A2022 and A223. Clacket Lane Services on the M25 is the nearest listed service area at 12km, with Thurrock Services on the M25 at 20km and Tollgate Services on the A2 at 22.4km. In OpenStreetMap's incomplete data, a station at Catford (8.1km) and another 18.4km away are listed as selling AdBlue at the pump.

name: Bromsgrove
intro: The 2021 census counted 34,755 residents in Bromsgrove, the largest town and administrative centre of Bromsgrove District. It lies about 13 miles (21km) south-west of Birmingham city centre and 16 miles north-east of Worcester. It was a small market town in the Middle Ages, producing cloth, and became a major centre for nail making in the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries. Postcodes are B60 and B61. Two motorways, the M5 and M42, appear on the road list along with the A38, A448 and A491. Catshill is only about 3.4km away, with Redditch at 9.1km and Droitwich Spa 10.1km. Driving from here can mix short A-road trips with motorway runs on the M5 or M42. Hopwood Park services is about 8.3km away on the M42, the nearest stop if an AdBlue warning comes on.
roadsText: Both motorways on Bromsgrove's road list have service areas within reach: Hopwood Park on the M42 is about 8.3km away and Frankley on the M5 11.2km. Strensham services, also on the M5, is further at 30.6km. The other listed roads are the A38, A448 and A491. Forecourts at DY10 1JS (about 13.6km) and in Warley (about 19.4km) are listed on OpenStreetMap as selling AdBlue at the pump, and that data is incomplete.

name: Brough
intro: At the edge of the Yorkshire Wolds, Brough is a town in the East Riding of Yorkshire and part of the civil parish of Elloughton-cum-Brough, shared with the neighbouring village of Elloughton. The Yorkshire Wolds Way National Trail passes its eastern end. Brough had 13,331 residents at the 2021 census and uses the HU15 postcode district. Hessle is about 7 km away, Willerby and Anlaby 7.7 km and Barton-upon-Humber 8.8 km, with Cottingham, Kingston upon Hull and Beverley between 11.3 km and 15.5 km. Service areas are a long way off. For a driver with an AdBlue warning, the nearest listed is Ulceby Truckstop on the A160, about 21.2 km in a straight line, and the nearest motorway services, Doncaster (North) Services on the M180, is about 32.5 km away.
roadsText: Brough's nearest service area is Ulceby Truckstop on the A160, roughly 21.2 km in a straight line. Doncaster (North) Services on the M180 is about 32.5 km away and Bilbrough Top Service Area on the A64 about 46.2 km. None is close, so it is worth knowing which one you are aiming for before setting off with a warning showing.

name: Brownhills
intro: South of Cannock Chase and close to the large Chasewater reservoir, Brownhills is a historic market and industrial town in the Metropolitan Borough of Walsall, within the historic county boundaries of Staffordshire. It is 6 miles (9.7 km) north-east of Walsall, a similar distance south-west of Lichfield and 13 miles (20.9 km) north-north-west of Birmingham, and neighbours the villages of Pelsall and Walsall Wood. The town lies close to the route of the ancient Watling Street and grew around coal mining, especially after canal and railway links arrived in the mid-19th century; Ogley Hay, one of its districts, is recorded in the Domesday Book. WS8 is the postcode district. For an AdBlue warning, Brownhills is well placed, as the nearest listed service area, on the M6 Toll, is only 3.2 km away in a straight line.
roadsText: Norton Canes Services on the M6 Toll is the nearest service area to Brownhills, just 3.2 km away in a straight line. Hilton Park Services on the M6 is 8.4 km off and The Trucker's Rest on the A5 is 9.8 km. OpenStreetMap lists a station in Burntwood (WS7 3XA), 3.8 km away, as selling AdBlue at the pump, and another in Warley at 17.1 km. Those records are incomplete, so other local stations may sell it too.

name: Broxburn
intro: West Lothian's Broxburn lies 12 miles (19 km) from the West End of Edinburgh and 5 miles (8.0 km) from Edinburgh Airport, with Livingston 5 miles (8.0 km) to the south. The town now forms one built-up area with neighbouring Uphall, and Winchburgh sits just to the north. It grew in the Victorian era on the back of shale oil extraction and has kept growing since through new housing. Broxburn falls within the EH52 postcode district and has a population of around 15,970. Livingston is 4.9 km away, South Queensferry 8.1 km, Linlithgow 8.7 km and Bathgate 10.1 km, so neighbouring towns are close at hand. None of the service areas listed for Broxburn is on the doorstep, so a van or diesel car showing an AdBlue warning is worth sorting before a longer run.
roadsText: The closest service areas listed for Broxburn are Dreghorn Services on the A720, 16.3 km away, and Heart of Scotland Services on the M8 at 18.6 km. Musselburgh Services on the A1 is further out at 26.5 km. All six neighbouring towns listed for Broxburn, from Livingston at 4.9 km to Rosyth at 12.2 km, are nearer than any of these stops, which is worth bearing in mind if an AdBlue warning appears on a short local journey.

name: Buckhurst Hill
intro: Inside the M25 but just beyond the administrative boundary of Greater London, Buckhurst Hill is an Epping Forest District town 11 miles (18 km) north-east of Charing Cross. It borders the London Borough of Redbridge and grew after its railway station opened in 1856, on a line that now forms part of the Central line. The parish had 11,755 residents in 2021, and the IG9 and IG8 postcode districts cover the area. Chigwell is 2.9 km away and Loughton 3.4 km, with Redbridge, Waltham Forest and Waltham Abbey between 5.4 km and 7 km. For an AdBlue warning, the nearest listed service area is South Mimms Services on the A1(M) at 19.5 km in a straight line, while a station 9.6 km away is listed in OpenStreetMap as selling AdBlue at the pump.
roadsText: Buckhurst Hill lies inside the M25. The nearest service areas are South Mimms Services on the A1(M), 19.5 km away in a straight line, London Gateway Services on the M1 at 21.2 km and Thurrock Services on the M25 at 22 km. A station 9.6 km away is listed in OpenStreetMap as selling AdBlue at the pump. OpenStreetMap's AdBlue records are incomplete, so other forecourts may also sell it.

name: Buckingham
intro: Close to the borders with Northamptonshire and Oxfordshire, Buckingham is a market town in the north of Buckinghamshire. It was the county town from the 10th century until Aylesbury took over the role in the 18th. The civil parish had 14,294 residents at the 2021 census, and the MK18 postcode district covers the town. It lies approximately 12 miles (19 km) west of Milton Keynes, 19 miles (31 km) south-east of Banbury and 24 miles (39 km) north-east of Oxford, and the University of Buckingham is based here. This is a spread-out area for a driver: the nearest town, Brackley, is 11.9 km away, and Towcester, Milton Keynes and Bicester are all between 14.6 km and 15.9 km. If an AdBlue warning comes on, none of the listed service areas is close. The nearest, Towcester Services on the A43, is 14.6 km away in a straight line.
roadsText: Three service areas lie between 14.6 km and 16.4 km of Buckingham in a straight line, each on a different road. Towcester Services on the A43 is nearest at 14.6 km, Cherwell Valley Services on the M40 is 15.5 km away and Jacks Hill Cafe & Truck Stop on the A5 is 16.4 km. Road distances will be longer, so allow for that once an AdBlue warning shows.

name: Buckley
intro: Flintshire's second-largest town by population, Buckley (Bwcle) had 16,135 people in its community at the 2021 census. It lies two miles (3 km) from Mold in North East Wales and is contiguous with the villages of Ewloe, Alltami and Mynydd Isa. The town is on the A549, and the larger A55 passes nearby. The CH7 postcode district covers Buckley. Hawarden is 4.9 km away and Connah's Quay 5.9 km, while Flint is 9.2 km off, Chester 12.4 km, Neston 14.1 km and Wrexham 14.7 km. For a van or diesel car with an AdBlue warning, the most useful fact is how close the A55 is: the nearest listed service area is on that road, just 2.4 km away in a straight line. Two more, on the A5156 and the A483, are both within 16.2 km.
roadsText: Buckley is on the A549, with the A55 passing nearby. The nearest service area is Chester West Services on the A55, only 2.4 km away in a straight line. Further out are Holt Road Services on the A5156 at 14.7 km and Rhostyllen Services on the A483 at 16.2 km. Road distances will be longer than these straight-line figures, but Chester West is close enough to be a sensible place to pull in if an AdBlue warning appears.

name: Burgess Hill
intro: Just on the West Sussex side of the county border, Burgess Hill sits on the edge of the South Downs National Park, 10 miles north of Brighton and Hove. Part of its World's End district crosses into the Lewes district of East Sussex. At the 2011 Census it was the most populous parish in the Mid Sussex District, and the RH15 and BN6 postcode districts cover the area. Haywards Heath lies 5.5km to the north-east and Hassocks and Hurstpierpoint just 3.4km away, while Brighton and Hove is 13km off and Lewes 13.1km. The A23, A272, A273 and A2300 are the main roads listed. All three of the nearest service areas are on the A23, the closest of them just 4.4km away.
roadsText: Burgess Hill's listed main roads are the A272, A23, A273 and A2300. Every one of the three nearest service areas is on the A23: Ricebridge Services (Hickstead) at 4.4km, Pyecombe Services at 7.1km and Handcross at 12.1km. One station about 13.4km away is listed as selling AdBlue at the pump. OpenStreetMap's records are incomplete, so treat this as a partial picture.

name: Burnham-on-Sea
intro: Land reclamation and sea defences have dominated the history of Burnham-on-Sea, which lies at the mouth of the River Parrett on Bridgwater Bay, where the Somerset Levels meet the Bristol Channel. It grew from a small fishing village into a seaside resort from the late 18th century, and it now forms a continuous built-up area with the neighbouring market town of Highbridge, with which it shares a town council. At the 2021 census, Burnham-on-Sea had 16,320 residents. The town is covered by the TA8 postcode district. Weston-super-Mare is 11.7 km away and Bridgwater 13 km. The M5 is close by for a driver with an AdBlue warning: Sedgemoor Services is 5.8 km away in a straight line, and Bridgwater Services, also on the M5, is 15.2 km.
roadsText: All three of the nearest listed service areas to Burnham-on-Sea are on the M5: Sedgemoor Services at 5.8 km in a straight line, Bridgwater Services at 15.2 km and Taunton Deane Services at 31.4 km. A filling station at Lower Weare (BS26 2JE), 11 km away, is listed on OpenStreetMap as selling AdBlue at the pump. That data is incomplete, so other sites may sell it too.

name: Burnley
intro: Burnley stands where the River Calder meets the River Brun, 21 miles north of Manchester and 20 miles east of Preston. Countryside lies to the south and east of the town, with Padiham to the west and Brierfield to the north. It is the administrative centre of the Borough of Burnley and had 78,266 residents in 2021. During the Industrial Revolution it became one of Lancashire's most prominent mill towns. The town has strong economic links with Manchester and Leeds and with neighbouring towns along the M65 corridor, and the M65 is the motorway on the road list, with the A6114, A682, A679, A671, A646, A6068 and A56. Postcode districts BB10 and BB11 cover the town. Brierfield is 3.4 km away, Nelson and Padiham 5.1 km, Colne 8.3 km, Accrington 9.7 km and Rawtenstall 10.3 km. A service area sits just 4.1 km away on the M65.
roadsText: Burnley's main roads are the M65 with the A6114, A682, A679, A671, A646, A6068 and A56. Hollin Bank Service Station on the M65 is the nearest at 4.1 km, and Blackburn with Darwen Services, also on the M65, is 18.3 km away. The third, Birch Services on the M62, is 25.1 km off, so for drivers in BB10 and BB11 the M65 is the main route to a service area.

name: Burntwood
intro: Once a mining town, Burntwood grew in the nineteenth century around coal and is now one of the largest urbanised parishes in England, in the Lichfield District of Staffordshire. It lies about 4 miles (6 km) west of Lichfield and north east of Brownhills, and its population is given as 26,049. The town is made up of several areas, including Boney Hay, Chase Terrace, Chasetown, Gorstey Lea, Burntwood Green, and Summerfield and All Saints, so a driver giving a location may name one of these rather than Burntwood itself. Postcode districts are WS7 and WS8. For anyone with an AdBlue light showing, the standout fact is how close the M6 Toll is: Norton Canes services on it is only 3.4 km away as the crow flies. Brownhills is 3.8 km from the town, and Cannock and Pelsall are both 6.2 km away.
roadsText: The M6 Toll is the motorway among the main roads around Burntwood, which also include the A5195, A5, A452, A461, A51, A515 and A5192. Norton Canes services on the M6 Toll is 3.4 km away as the crow flies, The Trucker's Rest on the A5 is 9.5 km and Hilton Park on the M6 is 9.8 km. OpenStreetMap lists a station with a Burntwood address, 0.8 km from the centre, as selling AdBlue at the pump. Its data is incomplete, so it may not be the only one.

name: Burton Latimer
intro: Sitting between Kettering and Wellingborough, Burton Latimer is a North Northamptonshire town about 3.1 miles south-east of Kettering and 4.5 miles north of Wellingborough. Its population was 10,444 at the 2021 census and its postcode district is NN15. Kettering is 4.7 km away and Wellingborough 6.7 km, while Raunds is 9.7 km away, Rushden 10.2 km, Desborough 13 km and Corby 14.1 km. For a van or diesel car with an AdBlue warning, the nearest roadside stops are 10.3 km and 11.1 km away, one on the A14 and one on the A45. Neither is on the doorstep, so it is worth deciding where to stop before the warning becomes urgent.
roadsText: The nearest stops to Burton Latimer are Rothwell Truck Stop on the A14, 10.3 km away, and Thrapston Services on the A45, 11.1 km away. Welford Truck Stop, also on the A14, is much further at 24.1 km. With the two closest options on different roads, the A14 and the A45, it helps to know which direction you are heading before a warning light becomes urgent.

name: Burton upon Trent
intro: Close to the Derbyshire border, Burton upon Trent is a market town on the River Trent in East Staffordshire, known for its brewing. Its name is often shortened to Burton. It lies 11 miles (18km) south-west of Derby and had 76,270 residents at the 2021 census, and it grew up around Burton Abbey. Its postcode districts are DE13, DE14 and DE15. There is no motorway on the road list; the listed roads are the A5189, A5121, A511, A38, A444 and A514. Swadlincote is about 6.3km away, with Ashby-de-la-Zouch at 13.3km and Derby, Lichfield and Uttoxeter all between 17.2km and 18.5km. That means local driving is largely on A-roads, with longer runs to neighbouring towns and cities. The nearest service area is about 8.9km away on the A50.
roadsText: Burton's three nearest service areas are all on the A50: Derby with Burton services at about 8.9km, Uttoxeter services at 18.2km and Derby South services at 20.1km. Listed roads around the town are the A5189, A5121, A511, A38, A444 and A514. A forecourt at Swadlincote (DE12 8AA), about 14.4km away, is listed on OpenStreetMap as selling AdBlue at the pump. OpenStreetMap does not record every site, so others may stock it.

name: Bury
intro: Bury is a market town on the River Irwell, 5 miles east of Bolton, 6 miles south-west of Rochdale and 8 miles north-west of Manchester. Part of the historic county of Lancashire, it has been in Greater Manchester since 1974 and had 81,101 residents in 2021, with 193,846 across the wider borough. It emerged in the Industrial Revolution as a mill town manufacturing textiles, and is known for its open-air market. For a town of its size the road list is motorway-heavy: the M66, M62 and M60 all appear, alongside the A56, A58, A6053, A6184 and A665. Postcode districts BL8 and BL9 cover the town. Radcliffe (3.9 km), Heywood (4.6 km), Ramsbottom (4.9 km) and Whitefield (5.1 km) are the nearest places, with Little Lever at 6.1 km and Prestwich at 7.4 km. Birch Services is just 5.1 km away.
roadsText: Bury's main roads are the M66, M62 and M60, plus the A56, A58, A6053, A6184 and A665. Birch Services on the M62 is just 5.1 km away. Further out are Blackburn with Darwen Services on the M65 (17.9 km) and Rivington Services on the M61 (18.5 km). A station in Manchester's M25 postcode district, 6.4 km away, and another about 13 km off are listed as selling AdBlue at the pump in OpenStreetMap. It is not a complete record.

name: Bury St Edmunds
intro: Laid out on a grid pattern by Abbot Baldwin around 1080, when it was called Beodericsworth, Bury St Edmunds is a cathedral town, market town and civil parish in West Suffolk, known locally as Bury. It is the cultural and retail centre for West Suffolk, tourism is a major part of the economy, and it is also known for brewing, malting and sugar processing. The built-up area had 41,280 people at the 2021 census. Main roads listed are the A14, A143, A134, A1302 and A1101. Neighbouring towns are spread out, which is worth knowing with an AdBlue warning on: Thetford is 18.7 km away, Stowmarket 20.6 km, Newmarket 20.7 km, Sudbury 23.1 km, Haverhill 25.7 km and Soham 27.1 km. Postcode districts are IP32 and IP33.
roadsText: Main roads listed are the A14, A143, A134, A1302 and A1101. The nearest service area is Beacon Hill Services on the A140, 27.5 km away, followed by a service area on the A14 at 34 km and Four Went Ways Services on the A11 at 35.8 km. A station in Stowmarket (IP14 3QQ), 18.9 km away, is listed on OpenStreetMap as selling AdBlue at the pump; that source is incomplete.

name: Bushey
intro: Reaching 165 metres (541 ft) above sea level, Bushey Heath is a large neighbourhood on the south-east side of Bushey, on the boundary with the London Borough of Harrow. The town itself is in the Hertsmere borough of Hertfordshire and is the second most populated town there, with 28,416 people at the 2021 census, up from 25,328 in 2011. The M1 and M25 are the motorways listed for Bushey, along with the A41, A4008, A405, A411, A4125 and A4140. Watford is only 3.3 km away, Borehamwood 5.8 km and Harrow 6.5 km, with Rickmansworth 7.5 km, Abbots Langley and Kings Langley 8.2 km and Chorleywood 10.4 km. Postcode districts listed for Bushey are WD17, WD18, WD19, WD23 and WD24, so an address here may carry any of several WD codes.
roadsText: The M1 and M25 are listed for Bushey, with the A41, A4008, A405, A411, A4125 and A4140. London Gateway Services on the M1 is the nearest service area, 6.8 km away. South Mimms Services on the A1(M) is 10.2 km off, and Bourne End Services on the A41 is 15.4 km away.

name: Buxton
intro: At around 1,000 feet above sea level, Buxton is England's highest market town, a spa town in the High Peak borough of Derbyshire with 20,048 residents at the 2021 census. It lies on the edge of the Peak District National Park, close to Cheshire to the west and Staffordshire to the south, and its postcode district is SK17. For drivers, the defining fact is distance. The nearest towns listed are Macclesfield at 14.6 km, Poynton at 17.2 km and Leek at 18.6 km, and the closest motorway services are more than 30 km away on the M6. A van or diesel car that develops an AdBlue warning around Buxton could be a long way from a service area, so it is sensible to deal with a warning promptly rather than wait for a trip to a bigger town.
roadsText: The nearest service areas to Buxton are all on the M6 and all more than 30 km away: RoadChef Sandbach Services at 31 km, Knutsford Services at 32.9 km and Tabley Hill Service Station at 34.1 km. With that much distance to the nearest of them, it makes sense to plan around a warning light before setting off rather than counting on reaching a motorway stop.

name: Byfleet
intro: Medieval in origin, Byfleet is a village in the far east of the borough of Woking in Surrey, around 1.5 miles (2.4 km) east of West Byfleet, from which the M25 and the Wey Navigation separate it. Its winding main street, High Road, has old public houses, several timber-framed houses and other listed 16th and 17th century houses, and the former Brooklands motor racing circuit is just to the north. The village is served by Byfleet & New Haw railway station, has a population of 14,187 and falls in the KT13 postcode district. Weybridge is 3 km away and Addlestone 3.6 km, with New Haw, West Byfleet and Sheerwater at 4.1 km. For a driver with an AdBlue warning, two service areas are close by in a straight line: Cobham Services on the M25 at 5.8 km and Wisley Services on the A3 at 6.5 km.
roadsText: The M25 runs between Byfleet and West Byfleet. Cobham Services on that motorway is the nearest listed service area at 5.8 km in a straight line, and Wisley Services on the A3 is 6.5 km away. Heston Services on the M4 is further out at 16.2 km. Expect the driving distance to each to be longer than these figures.

name: Caerphilly
intro: CF83 is the postcode district for Caerphilly, the largest town in Caerphilly County Borough. It sits at the southern end of the Rhymney Valley, separated from the Cardiff suburbs of Lisvane and Rhiwbina by Caerphilly Mountain, and lies 7 miles (11km) north of Cardiff and 9.5 miles west of Newport. The 2011 census recorded 41,402 people in the town. The roads around it include the M4, A470, A468, A469, A4054 and A473. Church Village, Ystrad Mynach, Pontypridd and Risca all sit between 6.9km and 8.4km away. With Cardiff and several neighbouring towns this close, many trips are short, and two motorway service areas are within 9.5km. For a driver who gets an AdBlue warning, that means a planned stop is rarely far away.
roadsText: Two motorway stops sit close to Caerphilly, both on the M4: Cardiff Gate services at about 8km and Cardiff West services at 9.5km. Sarn Park services, also on the M4, is about 24.7km away. The listed roads around the town are the M4, A470, A468, A469, A4054 and A473. For CF83 drivers, the two Cardiff stops are the realistic options if an AdBlue warning appears and a stop is needed.

name: Calne
intro: Chippenham lies 6 mi (10 km) west of Calne and Bath 19 mi (31 km) to the west, while Marlborough is 13 mi (21 km) to the east and Swindon 16 mi (26 km) to the north-east. The town is on the A4 national route and on the River Marden, the only town on that river, at the north-western edge of the North Wessex Downs. It had 19,074 inhabitants at the 2021 Census and is covered by the SN11 postcode district. Devizes is 9.6 km away and Melksham 11.7 km, with Royal Wootton Bassett at 13.5 km. When an AdBlue warning comes up, the M4 is the nearest source of services: Chippenham Pit Stop is 11.7 km away in a straight line and Leigh Delamere Services 14.1 km, both on that motorway.
roadsText: Calne is on the A4. The two nearest listed service areas are both on the M4: Chippenham Pit Stop at 11.7 km in a straight line and Leigh Delamere Services at 14.1 km. The Swindon J15 truckstop on the A420 is 24 km away. A station in Swindon (SN5 8UY), 16.2 km off, is listed on OpenStreetMap as selling AdBlue at the pump; that data is incomplete, so other sites may sell it.

name: Camberley
intro: Close to where Surrey meets Hampshire and Berkshire, Camberley is a town in the Borough of Surrey Heath, 29 miles south-west of central London. It grew from two settlements: Yorktown, which grew up after the Royal Military College was built at Sandhurst in 1812, and Cambridge Town, laid out around the time the Staff College opened in 1862. The two are now contiguous, and the town took its current name in 1877. The A30 London Road was once the London-Basingstoke turnpike, opened in 1728. The M3, A331, A322, A325, A321, A3095 and A332 are also listed. The postcode districts are GU15, GU16 and GU19. Frimley is 2.4km away and Sandhurst 3.9km, so local driving spans closely spaced towns, with a motorway on the road list.
roadsText: The M3, A331, A322, A325, A30, A321, A3095 and A332 are the main roads listed around Camberley. Fleet Services on the M3 is the nearest service area at 10km, followed by Wisley Services on the A3 (17.4km) and Cobham Services on the M25 (22.6km). A station on the Swallowfield By-pass near Reading (RG7 1LZ), about 19km away, is listed as selling AdBlue at the pump; OpenStreetMap's list is not complete.

name: Camborne
intro: Once one of the most significant tin-mining areas in the world, Camborne is a Cornish town whose name, Kammbronn in Cornish, means 'crooked hill'. The town lies about 2 miles (3 km) inland, but its parish reaches the north coast at Hell's Mouth and Deadman's Cove, and it also includes a number of hamlets. The built-up area had 20,450 residents at the 2021 census, and the town is in the TR14 postcode district. Redruth is just 5.5 km away, Helston 12.7 km, Penryn 14 km and Truro 18.1 km, with Penzance at 20.6 km. For a driver with an AdBlue warning, services are distant: the nearest listed service area is Cornwall Services on the A30, 41.3 km away in a straight line, so a services stop is not a quick option from here.
roadsText: At 41.3 km in a straight line, Cornwall Services on the A30 is the nearest listed service area to Camborne. Saltash Services on the A388 is 78.6 km off, and Roundswell Service Area on the A39 is 127.3 km. With every listed option this far from TR14, an AdBlue warning is best dealt with promptly rather than left until a long drive.

name: Cambourne
intro: A planned development on the A428, Cambourne lies between Cambridge, 9 miles (14 km) to the east, and St Neots and Bedford to the west. It is made up of four areas, Great Cambourne, Lower Cambourne, Upper Cambourne and West Cambourne, and is the largest settlement in South Cambridgeshire, with 12,350 people at the 2021 census. The town sits close to Bourn Airfield and is covered by the CB23 postcode district. For anyone dealing with an AdBlue warning, Cambourne is well placed: Caxton Gibbet Services on the A428 is 2.6 km from the centre, Cambridge Services on the A14 is 7.2 km, and a station 3.6 km away is listed in OpenStreetMap as selling AdBlue at the pump. St Ives is 12.9 km away and St Neots 13.5 km.
roadsText: Cambourne sits on the A428, and Caxton Gibbet Services on that road is the nearest service area, 2.6 km away in a straight line. Cambridge Services on the A14 is 7.2 km off and Brampton Hut Services on the A141 is 17.8 km. OpenStreetMap lists a station 3.6 km away and another at CB3 0LQ, 10.9 km away, as selling AdBlue at the pump. That data is incomplete, so other forecourts may also stock it.

name: Cambridge
intro: Well known as the home of the University of Cambridge, the city is the county town of Cambridgeshire and lies on the River Cam, 55 miles (89 km) north of London. The City of Cambridge had 145,700 residents at the 2021 census, and the wider built-up area, which extends beyond the city council boundary, had 181,137. Postcode districts are CB1, CB2, CB3, CB4 and CB5. The M11 and A14 are among the main roads, along with the A10, A428, A603, A1134, A1303 and A1307. Neighbouring towns are spread out: Cambourne is about 14.1 km away, Newmarket 19.1 km, Soham 19.9 km and Royston 20.1 km. For a driver with an AdBlue warning, that means the nearest service areas, at 10.5 km and beyond, are often closer than the next town.
roadsText: Main roads around Cambridge include the M11, A10, A14, A428, A603, A1134, A1303 and A1307. The nearest service areas are Four Went Ways Services on the A11, about 10.5 km away, ExtraMSA Cambridge Services on the A14 at 12.3 km and Caxton Gibbet Services on the A428 at 16.5 km. Girton Service Station (CB3 0LQ), about 3.9 km away, and a BP at around 10.5 km are listed in OpenStreetMap as selling AdBlue at the pump; that list is incomplete.

name: Cambuslang
intro: Never having had a town hall, Cambuslang may be considered the largest village in Scotland, though it is a town of approximately 30,000 people on the south-eastern outskirts of Greater Glasgow. It lies just south of the River Clyde, about ten kilometres southeast of the centre of Glasgow, within South Lanarkshire, and borders Rutherglen to the west. Historically it was a large civil parish that took in the hamlets of Newton, Flemington, Westburn and Halfway. Most employment in the area now comes from the distribution or service industries. G72, G73 and G32 are the postcode districts. The road list includes the M74, M73, M8 and A8(M), with the A8, A89, A724 and A725. Rutherglen is 3.4 km away and Blantyre 4.4 km, with East Kilbride at 6.6 km, and a motorway service area is 5.8 km from the town.
roadsText: Main roads recorded around Cambuslang are the M74, M73, M8, A8(M), A89, A725, A8 and A724. Bothwell Services on the M74 is 5.8 km away and Hamilton Services on the M74 is 8.1 km, with the M74 Truck Stop at 24.8 km. OpenStreetMap lists a station in Glasgow (G11 6DN), 11.4 km away, as selling AdBlue at the pump. Treat that as a partial list, since the map data is incomplete.

name: Camden
intro: Camden Town Hall, on Euston Road, lies 2 mi (3.2 km) north of Charing Cross, which shows how central this Inner London borough is. Established on 1 April 1965 from the former metropolitan boroughs of Holborn, St Pancras and Hampstead, Camden shares parts of the West End with the City of Westminster in the south and also borders the City of London. Mixed-use districts such as Camden Town and Kentish Town sit in the centre, with residential areas around Hampstead Heath in the north. The borough had 210,136 residents in 2021. The M1 appears in its main road list alongside the A5, A41, A400, A503, A4200, A5205 and A4380, and postcode districts include NW1, NW3, NW5, NW6, NW8, N1C, N6 and N19. Because driving here ranges from West End streets to residential roads in the north, naming the district helps pin down where a vehicle with an AdBlue warning has stopped.
roadsText: Roads listed for Camden are the M1, A41, A5205, A400, A503, A4200, A5 and A4380. The nearest listed service areas are London Gateway Services on the M1 at 11.8km, South Mimms Services on the A1(M) at 16.1km and Heston Services on the M4 at 17.3km. A station at Catford (15.7km) and one 16.6km away are listed as selling AdBlue at the pump in OpenStreetMap, which does not record every forecourt.

name: Cannock
intro: Hednesford and the Cannock Chase Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty lie to the north of Cannock, a town in the Cannock Chase district of Staffordshire. To the south is the West Midlands conurbation, and the town itself lies on the M6, A34 and A5. Walsall, Burntwood, Stafford and Telford are not far off, and nor are Lichfield and Wolverhampton. Postcodes are WS11 and WS12. As well as the M6, the road list includes the M6 Toll, A460, A4601, A5190 and A5195. Great Wyrley and Cheslyn Hay is about 4.5km away, Burntwood 6.2km and Rugeley 8.3km. For anyone driving a van or diesel car here, two motorways and the A5 sit close to town, which suits both local trips and longer runs. The nearest service area is only about 4.1km away.
roadsText: Cannock has three service areas within 6.9km: a truck stop on the A5 at about 4.1km, Norton Canes services on the M6 Toll at 4.7km and Hilton Park services on the M6 at 6.9km. A forecourt in Burntwood (WS7 3XA), about 5.4km away, is listed on OpenStreetMap as selling AdBlue at the pump, though that data is incomplete. The listed roads are the M6 Toll, M6, A460, A34, A5, A4601, A5190 and A5195.

name: Canterbury
intro: A city and UNESCO World Heritage Site, Canterbury lies on the River Stour in Kent, not far from its mouth on the Strait of Dover. It had 55,087 inhabitants in 2021, including a substantial number of students. Its economy relies heavily on tourism, alongside higher education and retail, and the city has a wall founded in Roman times and rebuilt in the 14th century. Postcode districts are CT1 and CT2. The listed roads are all A roads, led by the A2 and A28, with the A290, A257, A291 and A2050 also included. Whitstable is 8.7 km away, Herne 8.9 km and Herne Bay 10.9 km, with Faversham at 14 km. There is no listed service area close to the city for a driver with an AdBlue warning; the nearest is 18 km away.
roadsText: Six A roads make up Canterbury's road list: the A28, A2, A2050, A290, A257 and A291. The three nearest listed service areas are all between 18 and 21.1 km away: Minster Services on the A299 at 18 km, Folkestone Services on the M20 at 20.6 km and Ashford International Truckstop on the A2070 at 21.1 km. None is close, so it is worth knowing which direction you are heading before an AdBlue warning becomes urgent.

name: Canvey Island
intro: Separated from the south Essex mainland by a network of creeks and connected to it by bridges, Canvey Island is a town, civil parish and island in the Thames Estuary, part of Castle Point district. Any journey off the island with an AdBlue warning showing means crossing one of those bridges. The island covers 7.12 square miles (18.44 km2), lies below sea level and is protected by 2 miles (3.2 km) of concrete sea walls. It was mainly agricultural land until the 20th century, then grew rapidly as a seaside resort, and is also known for its relationship to the petrochemical industry. The built-up area had 38,010 people in 2021. The A130 and A13 are the main roads listed, with the A129 and A1014. Thundersley and South Benfleet is 4.7 km away, Rayleigh 8.1 km and Southend-on-Sea 9 km. The postcode district is SS8.
roadsText: The A130 and A13 are the main roads listed, with the A129 and A1014. Orsett Cock Services on the A13 is 12.4 km away, Tollgate Services on the A2 18.9 km and Medway Services on the M2 20.1 km. A station in Strood (ME2 2NY), 16.4 km away, is listed on OpenStreetMap as selling AdBlue at the pump; OpenStreetMap's AdBlue records are not complete.

name: Cardiff
intro: Wales's capital and largest city is also its main commercial centre. Cardiff had a population of 381,516 in 2025 and sits in the south-east of the country, within a Cardiff Capital Region of 1.5 million people. It was a small town until the early 19th century, when its role as a port for coal helped it expand; it became a city in 1905 and was proclaimed capital of Wales in 1955. The urban area reaches beyond the county boundary to include Dinas Powys and Penarth. Postcode districts across the city include CF3, CF5, CF10, CF11, CF14, CF15, CF23 and CF24. Penarth is 6.4 km away and Caerphilly 9 km, with Barry, Church Village, Risca and Pontypridd between 11.4 km and 15.4 km. For a van or diesel car, that means a mix of city driving and trips out to the surrounding towns.
roadsText: Cardiff's main roads include the M4, A470, A48, A469, A4119, A4161, A4160 and A4054. Two service areas sit on the M4 close to the city: Cardiff Gate, 6 km away, and Cardiff West, 8.3 km away. Magor services, also on the M4, is 26.2 km away, which makes the first two the practical stops.

name: Carlisle
intro: Eight miles south of the Anglo-Scottish border, Carlisle is the largest settlement and only city in Cumbria, and its nickname, the 'Great Border City', comes from that closeness to Scotland. It had 77,730 people in 2021 and was founded as a Roman settlement called Luguvalium to serve forts along Hadrian's Wall. For drivers, the distances between towns here are long. The nearest town in the data, Penrith, is 28.1 km away, and Dumfries, Workington, Hexham, Whitehaven and Hawick are all between 46.9 and 60 km off, with Dumfries and Hawick across the border in Scotland. The M6 is on the road list, along with the A595, A7, A6, A69 and A689. Postcode districts CA1, CA2 and CA3 cover the city. Three M6 service areas are within 11.4 km of the city.
roadsText: Carlisle's main roads are the M6, A595, A7, A6, A69 and A689. Three M6 service areas are close: Golden Fleece at 5.9 km, Todhills at 6.9 km and Southwaite at 11.4 km. In OpenStreetMap, a station at the Todhills rest area (CA6, about 7 km away) is listed as selling AdBlue at the pump. Its data is incomplete, but with the next towns so far off, it is a useful point to know.

name: Carlton
intro: Lying east of Nottingham, Carlton is a town in the Borough of Gedling. The figure of 53,555 residents covers the wards of the former urban district: Carlton Hill, Carlton, Cavendish, Colwick, Gedling, Netherfield, Phoenix and Porchester. Carlton, Gedling and Netherfield form one contiguous urban area with Nottingham and the surrounding boroughs, so the town runs straight into the wider built-up area. Postcode districts listed are NG3 and NG4. Arnold is about 4.3 km away and West Bridgford 6 km, with Nottingham itself around 6.8 km and Bingham 8.3 km. Main roads include the A52, A60, A612 and A6011, along with the A6019, A6211, A6514 and A6520. For a van or diesel car with an AdBlue fault, the useful point is that service areas on the A52 and A6011 are only a few kilometres away.
roadsText: Carlton's main roads are the A52, A60, A612, A6011, A6019, A6211, A6514 and A6520. Pierrepont on the A52 is the nearest service area, about 4 km away, followed by Trent Bridge Services on the A6011 at 5.4 km and Trowell Services on the M1 at 12.7 km. A Tesco station about 18.7 km away is listed in OpenStreetMap as selling AdBlue at the pump; the list is not complete.

name: Carluke
intro: Largely a commuter town, Carluke lies in the heart of the Lanarkshire countryside in South Lanarkshire, 4¾ miles (7.5 kilometres) north-west of Lanark and 4¼ mi (7 km) south-east of Wishaw. It has small stores and supermarkets at its centre and serves the surrounding villages of Braidwood, Forth, Kilncadzow and Law. The population is 13,810 and the postcode district is ML8. Larkhall is about 8.6 km away in a straight line and Motherwell 11.7 km, with Hamilton and Bellshill both around 15 km off. For an AdBlue warning, the nearest stop is the M74 Truck Stop, about 10.1 km away, with Hamilton Services on the M74 at 14.1 km and Heart of Scotland Services on the M8 at 15.3 km.
roadsText: The M74 Truck Stop is the nearest service area to Carluke, about 10.1 km away in a straight line. Hamilton Services, also on the M74, is about 14.1 km away and Heart of Scotland Services on the M8 about 15.3 km. With options on two motorways, drivers in the ML8 district can choose based on the direction they are already heading.

name: Carmarthen
intro: Built on the site of a Roman town, Carmarthen has a claim to be the oldest town in Wales. Today it is the county town of Carmarthenshire, a market town on the River Towy 8 miles (13 km) north of its estuary in Carmarthen Bay. At the 2021 census the built-up area had 16,455 residents, and the SA31 postcode district covers it. In the Middle Ages it was two settlements, Old Carmarthen around Carmarthen Priory and New Carmarthen around Carmarthen Castle, merged into one borough in 1546. Its nearest neighbours on the list are some way off: Llanelli is 22.3 km away, Gorseinon 28 km and Swansea 35.3 km. A driver with an AdBlue warning should know that the nearest listed service area is Pont Abraham Services on the M4, 20.8 km away in a straight line.
roadsText: Pont Abraham Services on the M4 is the closest service area to Carmarthen, 20.8 km away in a straight line. Moto Swansea West Services, also on the M4, is 29.4 km away, and Glanusk Services on the A40 is 51.3 km. Road distances will be longer than these figures, so if an AdBlue warning comes on in SA31 it is worth deciding early which way to go.

name: Carnoustie
intro: At the mouth of the Barry Burn on the North Sea coast, Carnoustie is a seaside town and former police burgh in Angus. Its 2022 population of 11,359 made it the fourth-largest town in Angus, and it falls within the DD7 postcode district. The town is best known for the Carnoustie Golf Links course. It can be considered a dormitory town for Dundee, its nearest city, which lies to the west. The nearest major road is the A92, which passes north of the town. Arbroath is the closest neighbouring town at 10.5 km, with Dundee at 15.2 km and Forfar at 18.7 km. Drivers with an AdBlue warning should note that the nearest listed service area is on the A90, around 19 km away in a straight line.
roadsText: The A92, north of Carnoustie, is the town's nearest major road. The closest listed service areas are both on the A90: Forfar Services at 19.2 km and Stracathro Services at 30.8 km, measured in a straight line. Kinross Services on the M90 is 55 km away. With the nearest services almost 20 km off, it is worth acting on an AdBlue warning early rather than waiting.

name: Carrickfergus
intro: County Antrim's oldest town, Carrickfergus sits on the north shore of Belfast Lough, 18 km from Belfast, and forms part of the Belfast Metropolitan Area. It is also one of the oldest towns in Ireland as a whole. Its population was 28,141 at the 2021 census, and since 2015 it has come under Mid and East Antrim Borough Council. The BT38 postcode district covers the town. The A2 is the only main road on the local list. Newtownabbey is 9.1 km away and Ballyclare 13 km, with Larne at 14.9 km. For a diesel driver, the nearest motorway services are 13.8 km off, so an AdBlue warning is best dealt with early rather than left until a longer trip.
roadsText: The A2 is the main road recorded around Carrickfergus. The nearest service area is Temple Patrick Services Northbound on the M2, about 13.8 km away, with Lisburn Services on the M1 at 24.7 km and Cohannon Services on the M1 at 59.9 km. OpenStreetMap lists stations in Bangor (10.8 km) and Newtownabbey (12.4 km), and one at BT6 0LT (17.2 km), as selling AdBlue at the pump. That map data is incomplete, so treat it as a starting point.

name: Carterton
intro: Census figures for 2011 recorded 15,769 people in the parish of Carterton, a town in the West Oxfordshire district of Oxfordshire, south-west of Witney, and a more recent estimate puts the population at around 18,691. Addresses in the town fall within the OX18 postcode district. Witney, 7.7 km away in a straight line, is the nearest town. The next nearest, Wantage, Kidlington, Stratton St Margaret and Oxford, are all between 21.5 and 22.4 km off, and Abingdon-on-Thames is 23 km away. That spacing matters if an AdBlue warning comes on, because the nearest listed service area, Peartree Services on the A44, is 21.2 km away, and the closest listed motorway services are on the M4 at 30.6 km. For a van or diesel car based here, it pays to deal with a low AdBlue level before a longer trip.
roadsText: The nearest listed service areas to Carterton are Peartree Services on the A44 at 21.2 km, a truckstop at Swindon J15 on the A420 at 22.4 km and Membury Services on the M4 at 30.6 km, all measured in a straight line from the town centre. None is close, so a low AdBlue level is best topped up before heading out.

name: Castleford
intro: North of the town centre, the River Calder joins the River Aire and the Aire and Calder Navigation. Castleford, the site of a Roman settlement, is the largest town in the City of Wakefield district after Wakefield itself, with a population estimate of 45,106 in 2021. It lies north-east of Wakefield, north of Pontefract and south-east of Leeds. Its suburbs include Airedale, Cutsyke, Ferry Fryston, Fryston Village, Glasshoughton, Half Acres, Hightown, Lock Lane, Wheldale and Whitwood, so a driver may give one of those names rather than Castleford. The postcode district is WF10. With an AdBlue warning, the motorway access is what counts: the M62 and A1(M) are among the main roads listed, and two motorway service areas lie within 5.4 km. Pontefract is 3.8 km away in a straight line and Featherstone 4.9 km.
roadsText: Main roads around Castleford include the M62 and A1(M), plus the A639, A645, A162, A628, A63 and A656. Whitwood services on the M62 is 4.3 km away in a straight line and Ferrybridge services, also on the M62, is 5.4 km; Skelton Lake Service Station on the M1 is 10.5 km. OpenStreetMap lists stations with a Pontefract address (8.6 km) and a Leeds address (10.5 km) as selling AdBlue at the pump. Mapping of AdBlue sales is incomplete, so there may be others.

name: Castlereagh
intro: Castlereagh falls within the Lisburn and Castlereagh council area in Northern Ireland and lies just 3.7 km from Belfast, with a population of 58,763. The postcode districts covering it are BT2, BT4, BT5, BT6, BT7 and BT8. Holywood is 8.2 km away, Newtownabbey 9.7 km and Lisburn 11.2 km. With the M1, M2 and M3 all on the local road list, a driver here is rarely far from a motorway when an AdBlue warning appears.
roadsText: Roads recorded around Castlereagh include the M1, M2, M3, A55, A24, A20, A2 and A12. Lisburn Services on the M1 is the nearest service area at 9.3 km, with Temple Patrick Services Northbound on the M2 at 15.9 km and Cohannon Services on the M1 at 50.6 km. A station at BT6 0LT, 1.1 km away, is listed on OpenStreetMap as selling AdBlue at the pump, as are sites in Newtownabbey (12.6 km) and Bangor (15.2 km). The list is incomplete.

name: Caterham
intro: Caterham is divided administratively in two. Caterham Valley holds the main town centre in the middle of a dry valley, while Caterham on the Hill sits above the valley to the west. The town is in the Tandridge district of Surrey, in an upper valley cut into the dip slope of the North Downs, south of Croydon and 21 miles from Guildford. It lies close to the A22. Around 22,757 people live here, in the CR3 postcode district. Croydon is 7 km away in a straight line, with Oxted at 7.6 km, Redhill at 8.7 km and Reigate at 9.7 km. For a van or diesel car with an AdBlue warning, the nearest listed service area is Clacket Lane Services on the M25, 9.1 km away.
roadsText: Caterham lies close to the A22. The nearest listed service area is Clacket Lane Services on the M25, 9.1 km away in a straight line, with Cobham Services, also on the M25, at 22.2 km and Pease Pottage Services on the M23 at 23.9 km. A station 18.4 km away is listed in OpenStreetMap as selling AdBlue at the pump. That data is incomplete, so treat it as one known option rather than the only one.

name: Catshill
intro: About 3 miles north of Bromsgrove and 10 miles south-west of Birmingham, Catshill is a village in the civil parish of Catshill and North Marlbrook, in the Bromsgrove district of Worcestershire. The parish was formed in 1844 around the Turnpike Road, the A38, and in 2021 Catshill and North Marlbrook had 6,974 residents. The B61 postcode district covers the village. Motorway services are close for a van or diesel car that flags an AdBlue warning: Hopwood Park Services on the M42 is 6.9 km from the centre and Frankley Services on the M5 is 7.8 km away, both in a straight line. Bromsgrove is the nearest town. Halesowen is 10.4 km away and Redditch 10.5 km, while Stourbridge, Cradley Heath and Droitwich Spa lie between 11.9 km and 13.2 km off.
roadsText: The parish of Catshill was formed around the Turnpike Road (A38) in 1844. Hopwood Park Services on the M42, 6.9 km away in a straight line, and Frankley Services on the M5, 7.8 km away, are the nearest service areas; Warwick North (Budbrooke) Services on the A46 is 31 km off. OpenStreetMap lists a station at DY10 1JS, 13.4 km away, and one in Warley, 16 km away, as selling AdBlue at the pump, though that data is incomplete.

name: Catterick Garrison
intro: The largest British Army garrison in the world, Catterick Garrison is a major garrison and military town 3 miles (5 km) south of Richmond in North Yorkshire. It had a population of around 14,000 in 2021 and covers over 2,400 acres, about 10 square kilometres. The town is in the Richmondshire district and the DL9 postcode district. For drivers, the important road is the A1(M): all three of the nearest listed service areas are on it, at 7.3 km, 8.6 km and 11 km from the centre in a straight line. The surrounding towns are further off. Northallerton is 18.6 km away and Darlington 20.2 km, while Ripon, Egglescliffe and Newton Aycliffe lie between 28.4 km and 28.9 km away and Ingleby Barwick is 30.5 km. That makes the A1(M) the nearest reference point for a van or diesel car with an AdBlue warning.
roadsText: All three of the nearest service areas to Catterick Garrison are on the A1(M): High Brough Moor Services at 7.3 km, Scotch Corner Services at 8.6 km and Barton Truckstop at 11 km, measured in a straight line. OpenStreetMap lists two stations as selling AdBlue at the pump, one with a Richmond address (DL10 6PB) 7.3 km away and one with a Northallerton address (DL7 9EG) 11.7 km away. That list is not complete.

name: Caversham
intro: Directly north of Reading town centre, across the River Thames, Caversham is a suburb that rises from the river's flood plain onto the lowest reaches of the Chiltern Hills. Two road bridges, Caversham Bridge and Reading Bridge, connect it to the rest of Reading. Named areas include Emmer Green, Lower Caversham, Caversham Heights and Caversham Park Village, and the postcode districts listed are RG4 and RG1. Main roads include the A4155, A4074 and A329, with the A33, A4, A327, A3290 and A3032 also on the list. Reading is 4km away, Woodley 5.3km and Henley-on-Thames 7.2km, so many journeys are short trips across the river and into neighbouring towns, while the nearest motorway service area is 7.6km away.
roadsText: The A33, A4155, A4074, A329, A327, A3290, A4 and A3032 are the main roads listed around Caversham. Reading Services on the M4 is the nearest service area at 7.6km; Fleet Services on the M3 (21.6km) and Chieveley Services on the M4 (24km) are further out. A station on the Swallowfield By-pass near Reading (RG7 1LZ), about 9km away, is listed as selling AdBlue at the pump. OpenStreetMap data is incomplete.

name: Chadderton
intro: In the foothills of the Pennines, Chadderton lies just 1 mile west of Oldham, 5 miles south of Rochdale and 6 miles north-east of Manchester. The town stands on the River Irk and the Rochdale Canal and is part of the borough of Oldham. Once a manorial township of farms and hand-loom weavers, it became a major mill town in the late 19th century, with more than 50 cotton mills built by 1914. Today it is covered by the OL9, OL8, M35, M24 and OL1 postcode districts and sits near the A627(M). Failsworth, Middleton and Oldham are each less than 4 km away. If an AdBlue warning comes on, it is worth knowing that one station only 1.9 km away is listed on OpenStreetMap as selling AdBlue at the pump.
roadsText: Chadderton is near the A627(M), and the M60 and M62 are also listed for the area, with the A663, A6104, A62, A627 and A664. Birch Services on the M62 is the nearest service area at 6.2 km; the next, Rivington Services on the M61 and Blackburn with Darwen Services on the M65, are 28.5 km and 29.1 km away. OpenStreetMap lists a station 1.9 km away and another in Manchester (M25 3AJ), 8.8 km away, as selling AdBlue at the pump, though the map is incomplete.

name: Chadwell St Mary
intro: Part of the Thurrock unitary authority in Essex, Chadwell St Mary lies 3 km east of the centre of Grays, which is its post town, and 1.6 km north of Tilbury. It was once an ancient parish that also covered the land to the south where the port town of Tilbury grew up from the 19th century. The parish became the Tilbury Urban District in 1912; that district was abolished in 1936 on the creation of the larger Thurrock Urban District, which became the borough of Thurrock in 1974. The built-up area had 10,685 residents at the 2021 census, across the RM16 and RM18 postcode districts. Neighbouring places are very close, so many local journeys are short: Tilbury is 2.3 km away and Grays 2.7 km, with Northfleet, Gravesend, Swanscombe and Chafford Hundred and West Thurrock all between 5.4 km and 6.1 km.
roadsText: Three service areas are within 7.3 km of Chadwell St Mary. Orsett Cock on the A13 is the closest at 3.7 km, Thurrock services on the M25 is 7 km away, and Tollgate on the A2 is 7.3 km. One station, at Temple Farm in Strood, 13.2 km from the town, is listed in OpenStreetMap as selling AdBlue at the pump. That map data is incomplete, so it is worth checking closer forecourts as well.

name: Chafford Hundred and West Thurrock
intro: North-west of Grays town centre lies Chafford Hundred, a housing development and suburb of Grays in the borough of Thurrock, Essex, built on parts of the old parishes of Stifford and West Thurrock. The area covered here also takes in West Thurrock, home of Lakeside Shopping Centre, which the local railway station serves. Together the area has 23,589 residents and falls in the RM20 postcode district. Main roads listed around the area include the M25, A282, A13, A1089, A2, A126, A1090 and A1306. For a driver dealing with an AdBlue warning, the nearest listed service area is just 1.4 km away on the M25. Grays is 3.3 km from the centre and South Ockendon 3.5 km, with Swanscombe, Dartford, Tilbury and Chadwell St Mary all within 6 km.
roadsText: Listed roads include the M25, A282, A13, A1089, A2, A126, A1090 and A1306. Thurrock Services on the M25 is the nearest service area at 1.4 km in a straight line, then Orsett Cock Services on the A13 at 8.5 km and Tollgate Services on the A2 at 9 km. A station 15.8 km away and a forecourt in Strood (ME2 2NY), 17.4 km off, are listed in OpenStreetMap as selling AdBlue at the pump. That mapping is incomplete.

name: Chalfont St Peter
intro: One of a group of villages known as The Chalfonts, alongside Chalfont St Giles and Little Chalfont, Chalfont St Peter is a large village and civil parish in south-eastern Buckinghamshire, between High Wycombe and Rickmansworth. It has nearly 13,000 residents, and together with Gerrards Cross it forms an urban area of 19,622 people. The postcode district is SL9. The village lies 19.8 miles (31.9 km) west-north-west of Charing Cross and is close to the motorway network, including the M25 and M40. Chorleywood is 6.2 km away and Beaconsfield 6.3 km, with Rickmansworth at 7.5 km and Amersham at 8.7 km. If an AdBlue warning appears, Beaconsfield Services on the M40 is the nearest listed service area at 5.1 km in a straight line, closer than any of the neighbouring towns.
roadsText: Chalfont St Peter is close to both the M25 and the M40. On the M40, Beaconsfield Services is 5.1 km away in a straight line, the nearest listed service area. Bourne End Services on the A41 is 15.3 km off and Heston Services on the M4 is 17.3 km. Road distances will be longer than these figures, which is worth remembering if an AdBlue warning has come on.

name: Chandler's Ford
intro: Chandler's Ford lies on the old road between Winchester and Southampton, and the 'Ford' in its name is thought to refer to a ford, possibly over Monks Brook on the Hursley Road. Today it is a largely residential area and civil parish in the Borough of Eastleigh, Hampshire, covered by the SO53 and SO50 postcode districts. The M3 and M27 are both listed around the area, along with the A27, A33, A35, A335 and A3090. Eastleigh is 3.8km away, Romsey 6.4km and Southampton 7.6km, with Winchester at 9.4km. Local journeys are short, with two motorways on the road list for longer trips and a service area 5.7km away.
roadsText: Around Chandler's Ford, the main roads listed are the M3, M27, A335, A3090, A27, A33 and A35. Rownhams Services on the M27 is the nearest service area at 5.7km. West Wellow Services on the A36 is 11.2km away and Winchester Services on the M3 is 17km. Rownhams is the clear nearest of the three.

name: Chapeltown and High Green
intro: This page covers Chapeltown together with High Green, an area with a population of 22,187. Chapeltown is a small South Yorkshire town in the civil parish of Ecclesfield, half way between Barnsley and Sheffield and approximately 7 miles from each. Historically within the West Riding of Yorkshire, Chapeltown was part of the Wortley Rural District until 1 April 1974, when it became part of the new county of South Yorkshire and the Sheffield City Council area. For drivers, its position between those two centres is the main thing to understand. Hoyland is the nearest town at 4.8 km in a straight line, with Wombwell at 8.1 km, Rawmarsh at 8.9 km, Rotherham at 9.3 km and Sheffield at 10.1 km. The postcode district is S35. The nearest service areas, on the A6102 and the M1, are both around 11 km away, so if an AdBlue warning appears none is close at hand.
roadsText: Measured in a straight line from the town, the nearest service areas are Sheffield Service Area on the A6102 at 10.9 km, Rotherham Services on the M1 at 11.2 km and Woolley Edge services, also on the M1, at 18 km. Road distances will be longer than these figures, so if an AdBlue warning comes on it is worth planning a stop early rather than relying on finding one close to home.

name: Chard
intro: At 121 metres (397 ft) above sea level, Chard is one of the highest towns in Somerset as well as its southernmost. It lies on the A30 road near the Devon and Dorset borders, 15 miles (24 km) south-west of Yeovil, and the parish has a population of approximately 14,000. The TA20 postcode district covers the town. Its history runs back at least to 1065, when it was recorded as Cerden, and its first charter came from King John in 1234. For a driver, the A30 is the road the town sits on, while the nearest listed service area is on the M5, 17.3 km away in a straight line. Neighbouring towns are all some distance off: Taunton at 18.7 km, Honiton at 18.9 km, Bridport at 21.3 km, Wellington at 22 km and Yeovil at 22.8 km. An AdBlue warning that appears in Chard will usually mean a run out of town to reach services.
roadsText: Chard lies on the A30 road. None of the listed service areas is close to the town: the nearest are all on the M5, with RoadChef Taunton Deane Services at 17.3 km in a straight line, Moto Bridgwater Services at 25.6 km and Moto Tiverton Services at 28.1 km. Road distances will be longer than these figures, so it is worth deciding on a route before setting off with a warning showing.

name: Chatham
intro: Built around a Royal Naval Dockyard established in 1567, Chatham lost that dockyard in 1984 after more than four centuries of operation. Part of the old site is now a commercial port, with other parts redeveloped for business and residential use. The town is the administrative headquarters of Medway Council and the principal retail centre of the Medway area, and it had a population of 80,596 in 2020. It forms a conurbation with Gillingham, Rochester, Strood and Rainham. Postcode districts are ME1, ME4, ME5 and ME7. The M2 and A2 are among the listed roads, along with the A228, A229 and A289. Gillingham is 3.4 km away and Rochester 4.6 km. Should an AdBlue warning come on, the nearest listed service area is 5.6 km away on the M2.
roadsText: Main roads listed for Chatham take in the M2, A229, A228, A230, A2, A231, A289 and A278. Medway Services on the M2 is the closest listed service area at 5.6 km, with Maidstone Services on the M20 at 12 km and Tollgate Services on the A2 at 13.5 km. A station in Strood (ME2 2NY), about 4.6 km away, is listed as selling AdBlue at the pump in OpenStreetMap; the data is incomplete, so other stations may sell it too.

name: Chatteris
intro: Out in the Fens of Cambridgeshire, Chatteris is a market town in the Fenland district, between Huntingdon, March and Ely. For much of its history it was a raised island in the low-lying wetland, and the parish is still a large one, covering 6,099 hectares. Since the Fens were drained, the local economy has been based on agriculture and related industry, and being within reach of Cambridge, Huntingdon and Peterborough has also made it a commuter town. That gives two quite different kinds of diesel driving: farm-related work around the PE16 postcode district, and regular commuting runs out of it. The 2021 census counted 11,011 residents. March is the closest neighbouring town at 11.3 km, with Ely 15.6 km away, St Ives 15.9 km and Whittlesey 16.1 km, and Huntingdon 20.2 km. Distances between places here are long enough that a warning light can easily come on well away from home.
roadsText: The nearest service areas to Chatteris are all a little over 20 km away. Cambridge services on the A14 is 21 km from the town, and there are two service areas at Sawtry on the A1(M), at 21.7 km and 21.8 km. On a run towards either of those roads, they are the obvious places to stop and check a dashboard warning before going any further.

name: Cheadle
intro: Cheadle Hulme, Gatley, Heald Green and Cheadle Heath all border Cheadle, along with East Didsbury in Manchester, so it is surrounded by neighbouring communities. Cheadle itself is a suburban village in the Metropolitan Borough of Stockport, within the boundaries of the historic county of Cheshire, and it had 14,698 residents in 2011. The SK8 postcode district covers it. Cheadle Hulme is about 2.3 km away, Stockport 4 km and Bramhall 4.1 km, with Wythenshawe at 4.4 km. Hazel Grove and Reddish are a little further at 6.2 km and 6.8 km. Journeys between these neighbours are short. For a van or diesel car with an AdBlue warning, the nearest motorway service areas are on the M6, starting at about 16.1 km away.
roadsText: Knutsford Services on the M6 is the nearest service area to Cheadle, about 16.1 km away, with Tabley Hill Service Station, also on the M6, at around 16.4 km. Lymm Services on the M6 is roughly 19.9 km off. OpenStreetMap has a site about 15 km away and one under Manchester at 17.4 km listed as selling AdBlue at the pump. Those records are incomplete.

name: Cheadle
intro: Dating back to Anglo-Saxon times, Cheadle is a market town and civil parish in the Staffordshire Moorlands District, within the historic Staffordshire Hundred of Totmonslow. It lies between Uttoxeter, Leek, Ashbourne and Stoke-on-Trent. The parish had 12,165 people in 2011, and the postcode district is ST10. Stoke-on-Trent is 10.6 km away, Uttoxeter 12.5 km, Leek 13.5 km and Stone 14.1 km, with Newcastle-under-Lyme at 17.4 km and Biddulph at 18.5 km. A van or diesel car with an AdBlue warning has no service area close by: the nearest listed is on the A50, 12.6 km away in a straight line, and the nearest on the M6 is 15.4 km off. OpenStreetMap lists one station, in Newcastle-under-Lyme, as selling AdBlue at the pump, though its records are incomplete.
roadsText: The nearest service area to Cheadle is Uttoxeter Services on the A50, 12.6 km away in a straight line. Stone Services on the A34 is 14.1 km off and Swift Services on the M6 is 15.4 km. A station in Newcastle-under-Lyme (ST5 4DH), the same 15.4 km away, is listed in OpenStreetMap as selling AdBlue at the pump. That data is incomplete, so it may not be the nearest.

name: Cheadle Hulme
intro: A suburb in the Metropolitan Borough of Stockport, Cheadle Hulme lies 3.2 km south-west of Stockport and 12.9 km south-east of Manchester, in the historic county of Cheshire. Rather than growing around a church, it formed from several hamlets, and many of their names survive as neighbourhoods within the suburb. The 2011 population was 26,479, and the area falls in the SK8 postcode district. Transport links are good: it has its own railway station and is close to Manchester Airport, the M60 motorway and the A34. Neighbouring places are very close, with Bramhall 2.1 km away, Cheadle 2.3 km, Stockport 4.9 km and Hazel Grove 5 km, and Poynton and Wilmslow both 5.5 km. A van or diesel car here is likely to swap between short suburban trips and motorway driving on the M60 or M56.
roadsText: Main roads around Cheadle Hulme include the M60, M56, A34, A555, A560, A523, A6 and A5145. The nearest service areas are on the M6: Knutsford at 15.9 km, Tabley Hill at 16.4 km and Lymm at 20.8 km. Two stations are listed in OpenStreetMap as selling AdBlue at the pump, one 16.7 km away and one in Manchester (M25 3AJ) at 19.6 km. The map data is incomplete.

name: Chelmsford
intro: Essex's county town, Chelmsford is one of three cities in the county, along with Colchester and Southend-on-Sea. It lies 31 miles (50 km) north-east of Charing Cross and 22 miles (35 km) south-west of Colchester, and its built-up area had 110,625 people at the 2021 census. The wider Chelmsford district covers an extensive surrounding area, so a driver dealing with an AdBlue fault under a Chelmsford address may be well outside the city itself. The settlement began to grow after a bridge was built across the River Can around 1100, gained a market charter in 1196 and had become the county town by 1219. Main roads listed for the city include the A12, A414, A131 and A130. Witham is 12.8 km away and Billericay 12.9 km, with South Woodham Ferrers, Maldon, Wickford and Braintree all between 13.7 and 16.7 km. The city's postcode districts are CM1 and CM2.
roadsText: Main roads listed for Chelmsford are the A12, A414, A131, A130, A1099, A1016, A138 and A1060. Boreham Services on the A131 is only 3.1 km away. Lorry pumps in Chelmsford (CM2 5PY), also 3.1 km away, are listed on OpenStreetMap as selling AdBlue at the pump, but they are marked HGV-only. Further out, Birchanger Green Services on the M11 is 24.6 km away and Orsett Cock Services on the A13 26.1 km. OpenStreetMap's AdBlue data is incomplete, so other outlets may exist.

name: Cheltenham
intro: After mineral springs were discovered in 1716, Cheltenham became known as a health and holiday spa resort, and it claims to be the most complete Regency town in Britain. The historic spa town and borough lies directly north-east of Gloucester, next to the Cotswolds, and has a population of 115,941. The town hosts a long list of cultural festivals, from literature and jazz to science, music and food, and the Cheltenham Festival of steeplechase racing is held every March. Postcode districts covering the town are GL50, GL51, GL52 and GL53. Bishop's Cleeve is 5.7 km away, Brockworth and Churchdown both 7.7 km, Gloucester 10.7 km and Tewkesbury 11.3 km, so many local journeys run between these neighbouring towns. The M5 is also among the main roads near the town, which gives van and diesel-car drivers a straightforward link onto the motorway.
roadsText: The main roads around Cheltenham are the M5, A40, A46, A4019, A436, A417, A4015 and A435. The nearest service area is Gloucester services on the M5, 13 km away, followed by Strensham on the M5 at 19 km and Ross Spur on the M50 at 33.5 km. With two of the three on the M5, that motorway is the obvious route for a planned stop.

name: Chepstow
intro: The easternmost settlement in Wales, Chepstow (Cas-gwent) is a town in Monmouthshire on the tidal River Wye, about 2 miles (3 km) above its confluence with the River Severn. It adjoins both the border with Gloucestershire, England, and the western end of the Severn Bridge. The town is 16 miles (26 km) east of Newport, 28 miles (45 km) east-northeast of Cardiff and 18 miles (29 km) northwest of Bristol. Its clifftop castle above the Wye is often cited as the oldest surviving stone castle in Britain. NP16 is the postcode district. Thornbury is 12 km away, Patchway 13.9 km, Bradley Stoke 15.2 km and Filton 15.7 km. Motorway services are close for a driver with an AdBlue warning, with the nearest listed 5.8 km away on the M48 in a straight line.
roadsText: Chepstow adjoins the western end of the Severn Bridge, and the nearest service area is Severn View Services on the M48, 5.8 km away in a straight line. Magor Services on the M4 is 12.1 km away and Avon Lodge on the A4 is 15 km. Road distances will be longer than these straight-line figures, but Severn View is close enough to be the first place to consider stopping if an AdBlue warning comes on.

name: Chertsey
intro: Inside the M25 and reached from junction 11, Chertsey is a town in Surrey's Borough of Runnymede, 18 miles (29 km) south-west of central London. It grew up around Chertsey Abbey, founded in AD 666, and a bridge across the River Thames first appeared here in the early 15th century. The River Bourne runs through the town and meets the Thames at Weybridge. Chertsey has a population of 15,967 and its postcode district is KT16.
