Several towns are close by: Addlestone is 2.4 km away, Staines-upon-Thames 4.2 km, New Haw, West Byfleet and Sheerwater 4.3 km and Weybridge 4.6 km. Although the town is accessible from the M25 at junction 11, the nearest listed service area for an AdBlue warning is Wisley Services on the A3, 10.5 km away in a straight line, with Cobham Services on the M25 at 11.7 km.
roadsText: Chertsey is within the M25 and accessible via junction 11. The nearest listed service area is Wisley Services on the A3, 10.5 km away in a straight line, with Cobham Services on the M25 at 11.7 km and Heston Services on the M4 at 14.2 km. These are straight-line figures, so expect the drive to each to be longer, which matters with an AdBlue warning already on the dash.

name: Chesham
intro: Set in the Chess Valley and surrounded by farmland, Chesham is a Buckinghamshire market town about 11 miles south-east of Aylesbury and 26 miles north-west of central London, within the London commuter belt. It was known for its four Bs, boots, beer, brushes and Baptists, and today local employment comes mainly from small businesses in light industry, technology and professional services. The town has about 23,691 residents and is covered by the HP5 postcode district. Amersham is 4.3 km away and Berkhamsted 5.8 km, with Hazlemere, Tring, Chorleywood and Hemel Hempstead all around 10 km off. The main roads listed around Chesham are all A roads, including the A41, A413 and A355, and for a van or diesel car with an AdBlue warning, the nearest listed service area, Bourne End Services on the A41, is only 6.3 km away in a straight line.
roadsText: Main roads listed around Chesham are the A41, A413, A355, A416, A4154, A404 and A4251. Bourne End Services on the A41 is the closest listed service area at 6.3 km. Beaconsfield Services on the M40 is 14.1 km away and London Gateway Services on the M1 is 25.5 km away. All are straight-line distances from the town centre, so the drive will be longer.

name: Cheshunt
intro: About 13 miles (21 km) north of Central London, Cheshunt is a commuter-belt town in the Borough of Broxbourne, on the River Lea and Lee Navigation and bordering the Lee Valley Park. It was recorded as Cestrehunt in the Domesday Book. The original centre was around St Mary's Church, near the Roman road of Ermine Street, but it later moved east to the High Street and Turners Hill, which together form a main road running roughly parallel to the River Lea. The old parish also covered Waltham Cross, Turnford and Goffs Oak. The built-up area had 43,680 people at the 2021 census. Waltham Cross is only 2.4 km away, Waltham Abbey 4.1 km and Hoddesdon 6.1 km, with Enfield at 7.5 km. The M25 and A10 are the main roads listed, along with the A1170, A121, A1010, A1055 and A112. Postcode districts are EN7, EN8 and EN10.
roadsText: The M25 and A10 are the main roads listed, with the A1170, A121, A1010, A1055 and A112. South Mimms Services on the A1(M) is 12.6 km away, London Gateway Services on the M1 17.4 km, and Birchanger Green Services on the M11 24.5 km. A station 20 km from Cheshunt is listed on OpenStreetMap as selling AdBlue at the pump, but OpenStreetMap's coverage of this is incomplete.

name: Chester
intro: Very close to the border with Wales, Chester is a cathedral city on the River Dee and the historic county town of Cheshire. Its built-up area had 92,760 people in 2021, making it the largest settlement in Cheshire West and Chester and second only to Warrington in the county. The city walls are almost complete apart from a 100-metre section. That border position shows in the list of nearby towns: Hawarden (8.3 km), Connah's Quay (11.7 km), Buckley (12.4 km) and Wrexham (16.7 km) are all in Wales, while Ellesmere Port (9.5 km) and Neston (16.1 km) are on the English side. Postcode districts CH1 and CH2 cover the city. The M53 is the motorway on the road list, with the A5268, A5116, A483, A56, A51, A5115 and A41. Three service areas, on three different roads, are within about 15 km.
roadsText: Chester's main roads are the M53, A5268, A5116, A483, A56, A51, A5115 and A41. The nearest service areas are Chester Services on the M56 at 10.6 km, Chester West Services on the A55 at 12.4 km and Holt Road Services on the A5156 at 15.2 km. That gives drivers in CH1 and CH2 a choice of three service areas on three different roads within a short drive.

name: Chester-le-Street
intro: Between Durham and Newcastle upon Tyne, Chester-le-Street is a market town in County Durham, about 10 km north of Durham and 14 km south of Newcastle. Markets are held on Saturdays, and the 2021 census put the population at 23,555. The town is split across the DH2 and DH3 postcode districts. It has other towns all around it at close range, which shapes everyday driving: Birtley is 4.8 km away, Shiney Row and Penshaw 6 km, Washington 6.7 km, Houghton-le-Spring 6.8 km and Stanley 7.4 km, with Durham 8.1 km away. The A1(M) is close as well, with Washington services only 3.9 km from the town, so short local trips and motorway runs are both a normal part of driving here. A warning light on a van or diesel car could appear on either kind of journey.
roadsText: Washington services on the A1(M) is just 3.9 km from Chester-le-Street, making it the nearest place to stop. Durham services, also on the A1(M), is 14.6 km away, and Easington on the A19 is 15.2 km. A station with a Durham postcode (DH6 3LJ), 16.8 km from the town, is listed in OpenStreetMap as selling AdBlue at the pump, though that data is incomplete and closer forecourts may stock it.

name: Chesterfield
intro: Where the Rivers Rother and Hipper meet, Chesterfield is a market and industrial town in Derbyshire, 11 miles (18 km) south of Sheffield and 24 miles (39 km) north of Derby. The town itself had 76,402 residents in 2021, within a wider borough of 103,569, and it sits on an old coalfield. Its postcode districts are S40 and S41, and the main roads listed for it are all A roads: the A61, A617, A619 and A632. Surrounding places are close by. Brimington is about 3.2 km away, Staveley 5.5 km and Dronfield 7.2 km, with Bolsover at 9.6 km and Matlock at 13.2 km. Because the nearest service areas are all more than 13 km out, a driver who sees an AdBlue warning in town is better off knowing the local roads than counting on a quick motorway stop.
roadsText: Main roads around Chesterfield are the A61, A617, A619 and A632. The nearest service areas are all more than 13 km away: Welcome Break Woodall Services on the M1 at about 13.3 km, Tibshelf Services, also on the M1, at 13.5 km, and Sheffield Service Area on the A6102 at around 14.9 km.

name: Chichester
intro: West Sussex has only one city, and Chichester is it: a cathedral city, civil parish and the county town. It was a Roman and Anglo-Saxon settlement and has been a major market town ever since. It is also the seat of the Church of England Diocese of Chichester, with a 12th-century cathedral. The city has two main watercourses, the Chichester Canal and the River Lavant. The 2021 census counted 29,407 people in the parish, and the PO19 and PO18 postcode districts cover the city and its surroundings. On the roads, the A27 and A259 are joined by the A286 and A285, and there is no motorway on the list. Bognor Regis is 8.2km away, Barnham 9km, Emsworth 11.6km and Selsey 11.8km. For a van or diesel car, local driving means A roads between the city and nearby towns.
roadsText: Chichester's listed main roads are the A259, A27, A286 and A285. Fontwell Services on the A27 is the nearest service area, about 9.1km away. Farlington Services, also on the A27, is 18.6km and Petersfield Services on the A3 is 22.5km. The two closest stops are both on the A27, which is where a driver with an AdBlue warning will find the nearest listed service areas.

name: Chigwell
intro: Next to the northern boundary of Greater London, Chigwell is a town and civil parish in the Epping Forest District of Essex, served by the Central line of the London Underground. The built-up area had 12,250 residents at the 2021 census, and the town is covered by the IG6 and IG7 postcode districts. Its neighbours are close: Buckhurst Hill is 2.9 km away, Redbridge 3.5 km and Loughton 4 km, with Waltham Forest, Barking and Dagenham and Epping between 7.4 km and 9 km. The nearest service areas are further out, starting with Thurrock Services on the M25 at 19.2 km in a straight line. Closer in, a station 7.9 km away is listed in OpenStreetMap as selling AdBlue at the pump, which may help if an AdBlue warning comes on.
roadsText: The nearest service areas to Chigwell are Thurrock Services on the M25, 19.2 km away in a straight line, South Mimms Services on the A1(M) at 22.3 km and London Gateway Services on the M1 at 23.8 km. OpenStreetMap lists a station 7.9 km away and another 19.8 km away as selling AdBlue at the pump. Those listings are incomplete, so other forecourts around IG6 and IG7 may also sell AdBlue.

name: Chippenham
intro: Under Alfred the Great, Chippenham was a royal vill. The market town was established on a crossing of the River Avon in north-west Wiltshire, 21 km north-east of Bath and 138 km west of London, near the Cotswolds Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty, and it continued to grow when the Great Western Railway arrived in 1841. Its parish had 36,548 people in 2021. The SN15 postcode district covers the town. Corsham is 5.6 km away, Melksham 9.2 km and Calne 9.4 km, with Devizes at 15.3 km and Trowbridge at 15.7 km. The A4, A350, A420 and A342 are the main roads near the town, and the M4 is close enough that two motorway service areas sit 6.2 km and 6.3 km away. For a diesel van or car, that means local work and motorway runs are both easy to reach from here.
roadsText: The main roads around Chippenham are the A4, A350, A420 and A342. Chippenham Pit Stop on the M4 is 6.2 km away and Leigh Delamere services on the M4 is 6.3 km, so there are two motorway stops very close to town. Warminster services on the A350 is further out at 27.3 km.

name: Chorley
intro: Several other towns and cities lie within 20 miles of Chorley: it is 12 miles south of Preston, 8 miles north of Wigan, 11 miles from both Blackburn and Bolton, and 20 miles north-west of Manchester. It is the administrative centre of the Borough of Chorley in Lancashire and had a population of 36,682 in 2020. The town's wealth came mainly from cotton, and while most of the factory chimneys that filled the skyline in the 1970s have gone, mill buildings and streets of terraced houses built for mill workers remain. The M61 and M6 are both listed among the roads around the town, and the PR7 and PR6 postcode districts cover it. Euxton is just 3.1 km away and Leyland 6.4 km. Drivers here have two service areas within 7 km of the town, which is useful to know if an AdBlue warning appears mid-journey.
roadsText: Around Chorley, the listed roads are the M61 and M6 plus the A581, A6, A674, A5106, A49 and A673. Service areas are close: Charnock Richard Services on the M6 is 4.6 km away and Rivington Services on the M61 is 7 km. Blackburn with Darwen Services on the M65, at 12.3 km, is the next nearest. After Euxton, Leyland (6.4 km) and Standish (7.5 km) are the closest towns.

name: Chorleywood
intro: Sitting on the border with Buckinghamshire, about 20 miles (32 km) north-west of Charing Cross, Chorleywood is a village in the Three Rivers District of Hertfordshire. It is part of the London commuter belt and lies next to the Chiltern Hills Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty. Historically it was part of the parish of Rickmansworth, and Rickmansworth itself is just 3.2 km away. The population is 12,632, and the village is covered by the WD3 postcode district. Chalfont St Peter is 6.2 km off, with Watford and Amersham both a little over 7 km away. Two service areas lie at similar distances for anyone with an AdBlue warning: Bourne End Services on the A41 at 10.2 km and Beaconsfield Services on the M40 at 10.7 km, both measured in a straight line.
roadsText: Chorleywood has two service areas at roughly the same distance: Bourne End Services on the A41, 10.2 km away in a straight line, and Beaconsfield Services on the M40 at 10.7 km. London Gateway Services on the M1 is further at 16.9 km. Which is nearer by road will depend on where in WD3 the journey starts and which way it is heading.

name: Christchurch
intro: Where the rivers Avon and Stour meet and flow into Christchurch Harbour, Christchurch sits on the south coast of Dorset, with Bournemouth to the west and the New Forest to the east. The civil parish had 31,372 residents in 2021, and the wider area has a population of 48,973. Historically part of Hampshire, it has been in the Bournemouth, Christchurch and Poole unitary authority since 2019. The town was founded in the 7th century and grew into an important trading port. The BH23 postcode district covers the town. New Milton is 6.3 km away and Bournemouth 9.1 km, while Ringwood, Ferndown, West Moors and Lymington are all between 12.4 km and 13.6 km. For a van or diesel car, that puts Christchurch between Bournemouth on one side and the New Forest on the other, with the nearest service area 12.6 km out.
roadsText: The main roads around Christchurch are the A338, A35, A337 and A3060. The nearest service area is Picket Post on the A31, 12.6 km away, followed by Rufus Stone on the A31 at 20.2 km and West Wellow on the A36 at 27.9 km. A forecourt at Creekmoor in Poole (BH17 7FR), 17.6 km away, is listed as selling AdBlue at the pump in OpenStreetMap data. The map is incomplete, so there may be closer options.

name: Church Village
intro: Centrally placed between the local principal towns of Llantrisant, to the south-west, and Pontypridd, to the north, Church Village (Pentre'r Eglwys) is a large village in the historic parish and community of Llantwit Fardre. It belongs to the Taff Ely district of the County Borough of Rhondda Cynon Taf and lies approximately 8 miles north-west of Cardiff city centre. The CF38 postcode district covers the village. Neighbouring towns are close by: Pontypridd is 4.7 km away, Caerphilly 6.9 km, Tonyrefail 7.6 km and Porth 7.9 km, with Ystrad Mynach at 11 km and Tonypandy at 11.1 km. With an AdBlue warning, the useful detail is that the M4 is not far off, with the nearest listed service area 6.3 km away in a straight line.
roadsText: All three of the nearest service areas to Church Village are on the M4. Cardiff West Services is the closest, 6.3 km away in a straight line, followed by Cardiff Gate Services at 13.7 km and Sarn Park Services at 17.8 km. Distances by road will be longer than these straight-line figures. Cardiff West is the one to bear in mind if a warning comes on and you need somewhere to pull in.

name: Churchdown
intro: Between Gloucester and Cheltenham, in the south of Tewkesbury Borough, Churchdown is a large village with two centres. The older one, known as Brookfield or the village centre, is on Church Road near St Andrew's Church, while the more suburban centre is on St John's Avenue near St John's Church. The village covers about 16.5 km2 and had 10,990 residents at the 2011 census. It sits in the GL3 postcode district. With Gloucester only 4.3 km away and Cheltenham 7.7 km, Churchdown is within easy reach of both, and Brockworth is 5.2 km off, with Quedgeley and Hardwicke at 9.7 km. Bishop's Cleeve and Tewkesbury are 11 km and 11.8 km away. If an AdBlue warning comes on, the nearest listed service area is Westmorland Gloucester Services on the M5, 8 km away in a straight line.
roadsText: Westmorland Gloucester Services on the M5 is the closest service area to Churchdown, 8 km from the village in a straight line. RoadChef Strensham Services, also on the M5, is 19.5 km away, and Ross Spur Services on the M50 is 26 km away. Road distances to each will be longer than these straight-line figures, which is worth allowing for with a warning on the dashboard.

name: Cirencester
intro: The largest town in the Cotswolds, Cirencester is a market town on the River Churn, a tributary of the Thames, in the Cotswold District of Gloucestershire. It had 20,229 residents in 2021 and is home to the Royal Agricultural University, founded in 1840. Known to the Romans as Corinium, the town lies 18 miles (29 km) from both Swindon and Gloucester, 37 miles (60 km) west of Oxford and 39 miles (63 km) north-east of Bristol. It is covered by the GL7 postcode district. None of the neighbouring towns listed is close: Stroud is the nearest at 18.2 km. That distance carries over to services. For a driver with an AdBlue warning, the nearest listed service area is Gloucester Services on the M5, 21.5 km away in a straight line.
roadsText: Cirencester's nearest listed service areas are all more than 21 km away in a straight line: Gloucester Services on the M5 at 21.5 km, the Swindon J15 truckstop on the A420 at 22.2 km and Chippenham Pit Stop on the M4 at 24 km. Two stations in Swindon (SN6 6JR), at 12.5 km and 12.7 km, are listed on OpenStreetMap as selling AdBlue at the pump. That data is incomplete, so other sites may sell it too.

name: City of Westminster
intro: Much of central London falls inside the City of Westminster, including most of the West End, the shopping streets around Oxford Street, Regent Street, Piccadilly and Bond Street, and the entertainment district of Soho. It is also the site of the Houses of Parliament and much of the British government. Away from the centre, the borough takes in inner suburbs such as St John's Wood, Maida Vale, Bayswater, Belgravia and Pimlico, along with Hyde Park and most of Regent's Park. It had 204,300 residents at the 2021 census. Driving here is central London driving: the main roads listed are the A4, A5, A40, A41, A302, A501, A4202 and A4380, and postcode districts include W1B, W1C, W1G, W1H, W1J, W1K, W1S and W1U. Kensington and Chelsea is 2.5km away and Camden 4km, so a van with an AdBlue warning may be only a short distance from another borough.
roadsText: Main roads in Westminster include the A4202, A40, A4380, A5, A41, A501, A4 and A302. The nearest listed service areas are all at least 15km away: London Gateway Services on the M1 (15.3km), Heston Services on the M4 (16.5km) and South Mimms Services on the A1(M) (20.1km). A station at Catford, 12.8km away, and one 16.6km away are listed as selling AdBlue at the pump in OpenStreetMap, whose coverage is incomplete.

name: Clacton-on-Sea
intro: On the Tendring Peninsula, Clacton-on-Sea, often just called Clacton, is the largest settlement in Tendring District, with a population of 53,200 in 2021. It is around 77 miles (124 km) north-east of London, 16 miles (26 km) south-east of Colchester and 16 miles (26 km) south of Harwich. The seaside resort was developed from the 1870s and named Clacton-on-Sea to set it apart from the older village of Great Clacton, about 1 mile (1.6 km) inland. The two were administered together and gradually merged into a single urban area during the 20th century. This is a peninsula town, and the driving reflects it: the main road listed is the A133, and the nearest neighbours are Harwich at 16.6 km, Colchester at 19.6 km and Felixstowe at 21.7 km. Postcode districts are CO15 and CO16.
roadsText: The A133 is the main road listed for Clacton. The nearest service area is Ardleigh South Services on the A120, 16.3 km away. Beyond that, a service area on the A14 is 29.5 km off and Beacon Hill Services on the A140 is 39 km away, so a driver heading inland will cover some distance before reaching services.

name: Cleckheaton
intro: Once the major town of the former borough of Spenborough, Cleckheaton sits at the centre of the Spen Valley in Kirklees, West Yorkshire. It lies south of Bradford, east of Brighouse, west of Batley and south-west of Leeds, and was historically part of the West Riding. A former mill town, it forms part of the Heavy Woollen District. Postcodes fall in BD19 and WF15. Liversedge is about 2.2 km away, Heckmondwike 3.3 km, Gomersal and Birkenshaw 3.5 km and Brighouse 5.1 km. The nearest service area is very close: Hartshead Moor Services on the M62 is about 2.3 km away in a straight line, so a driver with an AdBlue warning has motorway services almost on the doorstep.
roadsText: Hartshead Moor Services on the M62 is about 2.3 km from Cleckheaton in a straight line, the nearest service area by some distance. Woolley Edge Services on the M1 is about 16 km away and Skelton Lake Service Station, also on the M1, about 17 km. OpenStreetMap lists a station in Leeds (LS9 0AS), around 17.1 km away, as selling AdBlue at the pump; its coverage is incomplete.

name: Cleethorpes
intro: Standing on the estuary of the Humber, Cleethorpes is a seaside town in North East Lincolnshire with 29,670 residents in 2021. Fishing was its original industry before it developed into a resort in the 19th century, and it was formed from three small villages, Itterby, Oole and Thrunscoe. The town lies on the prime meridian. Its near neighbours are very near and the rest are a long way off: Humberston and New Waltham is 2.2 km away in a straight line and Grimsby 4.3 km, but Louth is 20.4 km and Barton-upon-Humber 30.5 km. That matters if an AdBlue warning appears, as a run to anywhere beyond Grimsby is a long one. Postcode districts are DN35 and DN32. The main roads listed are the A46, A180, A16, A1098, A1031, A1136 and A1243, with no motorway among them.
roadsText: Main roads around Cleethorpes are the A46, A180, A16, A1098, A1031, A1136 and A1243. The nearest service area is Ulceby Truckstop on the A160, 18.2 km away in a straight line, with Showground Services on the A15 at 44.3 km and Thorpe on the Hill Services on the A46 at 57 km. OpenStreetMap lists a station with a Louth address, 18.6 km away, as selling AdBlue at the pump. It is not a full list.

name: Clevedon
intro: Along the Severn Estuary in North Somerset, Clevedon is a seaside town and civil parish set among a series of small hills, including Church Hill, Dial Hill, Strawberry Hill and Wain's Hill, which is topped by the remains of an Iron Age hillfort. The town is mentioned in the Domesday Book of 1086 and grew in the Victorian period as a seaside resort, and it had 21,398 residents at the 2021 census. It is covered by the BS21 postcode district. Nailsea is 6.5 km away, Portishead 8.3 km and Weston-super-Mare 12 km, with Bristol 18.7 km off. For a van or diesel car with an AdBlue warning, the nearest listed service area is Gordano Services on the M5, 11.5 km away in a straight line, with Avon Lodge on the A4 at 14.2 km.
roadsText: The nearest listed service areas to Clevedon, measured in a straight line, are Gordano Services on the M5 at 11.5 km, Avon Lodge on the A4 at 14.2 km and Magor Services on the M4 at 17.5 km. A filling station at Lower Weare (BS26 2JE), 16.7 km away, is listed on OpenStreetMap as selling AdBlue at the pump. That map data is incomplete, so it should not be read as a full list.

name: Cleveleys
intro: Part of the Blackpool Urban Area, Cleveleys is a town on the coast of the Fylde peninsula, about 4 miles (6 km) north of Blackpool and 2 miles (3 km) south of Fleetwood. It sits in the Borough of Wyre, and with its neighbour Thornton it was part of the former urban district of Thornton-Cleveleys. In 2011 the Cleveleys built-up area sub division had 10,754 residents. The FY5 postcode district covers the town. Thornton is about 2.3 km away, Fleetwood 3.4 km and Poulton-le-Fylde 5.1 km, with Blackpool at 9.6 km and Lytham St Anne's at 14.8 km. For a van or diesel car with an AdBlue warning, the nearest service area is Lancaster Services on the M6, about 20.1 km off, and the next ones on that motorway are more than 35 km away.
roadsText: Lancaster Services on the M6 is the nearest service area to Cleveleys, about 20.1 km away. Charnock Richard Services, also on the M6, is around 35.9 km off, and Burton-in-Kendal Services on the M6 about 38.3 km. Reaching any of them from the FY5 district means a drive of more than 20 km, which is worth knowing before a warning becomes urgent.

name: Clifton
intro: Split into the Clifton West and Clifton East council wards, Clifton is an urban area within the city of Nottingham with 22,936 residents at the 2021 census. It takes in Clifton Village and Clifton Grove, a residential area beside the River Trent, as well as the Nottingham Trent University Clifton Campus. The postcode district is NG11. For drivers, Clifton is part of the wider Nottingham road network rather than a stand-alone town: Beeston is 4.2 km away, West Bridgford 4.7 km, Stapleford 6.6 km, Long Eaton 7.1 km and Nottingham itself 7.2 km. If an AdBlue warning comes on while you are moving between these places in a van or diesel car, the nearest roadside services are Trent Bridge Services, 5.2 km from Clifton.
roadsText: The nearest service areas to Clifton are Trent Bridge Services on the A6011, 5.2 km away, Pierrepont on the A52 at 8 km, and Trowell Services on the M1 at 8.7 km. All three lie within 9 km of Clifton, and Trowell is the only one of them on a motorway, which is worth knowing if you are planning to join the M1.

name: Clifton
intro: In the north of the City of Salford, Clifton runs along the edge of the Irwell Valley as a suburb of Swinton. Historically in Lancashire, it was a centre for coal mining and once formed part of the Municipal Borough of Swinton and Pendlebury. It has about 17,748 residents, and the M27 postcode district covers the area. Swinton itself is only around 2 km away. Prestwich is about 3.3 km off, Salford 3.8 km and Whitefield 4 km, with Kearsley at 4.3 km and Worsley at 4.5 km. All six of those neighbouring places are within 4.5 km, so Clifton has plenty of close neighbours. For a driver with an AdBlue warning, the nearest motorway service area is Birch Services on the M62, about 8.1 km from Clifton.
roadsText: Birch Services on the M62 is the closest service area to Clifton, about 8.1 km away. Rivington Services on the M61 is around 18.9 km off, and Lymm Services on the M6 about 21.5 km. OpenStreetMap has a station under Manchester, roughly 3.1 km away, listed as selling AdBlue at the pump, as well as a site at 11.8 km and one under Warrington at 17.5 km. Its records are incomplete.

name: Clitheroe
intro: Near the Forest of Bowland and often used as a base for tourists visiting the area, Clitheroe is a town and civil parish in the Borough of Ribble Valley, Lancashire, about 34 miles (55 km) north-west of Manchester. It is the most populous settlement in the Ribble Valley, with an estimated 16,279 people in the built-up area in 2018. Several manufacturing companies have sites in the town, and Clitheroe Castle is its most notable building. The BB7 postcode district covers Clitheroe. Neighbouring towns are some distance away: Great Harwood is about 9.4 km off and Padiham 9.5 km, with Brierfield, Nelson, Burnley and Accrington between 11.9 km and 13.6 km. For a driver with an AdBlue warning, that spacing matters, as the closest neighbouring towns are more than 9 km away and the M65 is the nearest motorway with services.
roadsText: Hollin Bank Service Station on the M65 is the nearest service area to Clitheroe, about 11.6 km away. Blackburn with Darwen Services, also on the M65, is around 18.4 km off, and Lancaster Services on the M6 about 26.1 km. Any trip to motorway services from Clitheroe and the BB7 district is therefore at least 11.6 km, which is worth bearing in mind when a warning first appears.

name: Clydebank
intro: Founded as a police burgh in 1886, Clydebank is a West Dunbartonshire town on the north bank of the River Clyde and part of the wider Greater Glasgow urban area: the Yoker and Drumchapel areas of the city lie immediately to the east, and the village of Old Kilpatrick, with Bowling and Milton beyond, lies to the west. To the north are Duntocher, Faifley and Hardgate, depending on where the boundary is drawn, with the Kilpatrick Hills beyond. Locals are known as Bankies. Postcode districts G81, G15, G60, PA4 and PA8 all appear for the town, and its population is listed at 25,620. The M8 and M898 are on the road list along with the A8, A82, A810, A814, A898 and A8014. Erskine is 2.8 km away and Renfrew 4.2 km, with Bearsden at 4.8 km and Dumbarton at 10.5 km.
roadsText: The M898, M8, A82, A898, A8014, A814, A810 and A8 are the main roads recorded around Clydebank. The nearest service areas are some distance away: Bothwell Services on the M74 at 24.1 km, Hamilton Services on the M74 at 26.9 km and Stirling Services on the M9 at 35.5 km. OpenStreetMap lists a station in Glasgow (7.5 km) and another site 10.9 km away as selling AdBlue at the pump; that data is incomplete.

name: Coalville
intro: Sitting on the A511 between Leicester and Burton upon Trent, Coalville is a town in the North West Leicestershire district of Leicestershire. It had a population of 34,575 in 2011 and shares the LE67 postcode district with Whitwick, which is just 1.6 km away. Other neighbours are a short drive off, with Shepshed at 6.6 km, Ashby-de-la-Zouch at 7.3 km and Loughborough at 10.7 km, while Swadlincote is 14.3 km away. There is no motorway stop on the doorstep: the nearest service area is Moto Donington Park Services on the M1, 11.4 km from the town. That means it pays to plan a stop if a van or diesel car shows an AdBlue warning in town. A station in Swadlincote is also listed as selling AdBlue at the pump.
roadsText: Coalville sits on the A511. The nearest service areas are Moto Donington Park Services on the M1, 11.4 km away, Welcome Break Derby South Services on the A50 at 15.8 km, and Leicester Forest East Services on the M1 at 16.2 km. A station in Swadlincote (DE12 8AA), 12.8 km away, is listed on OpenStreetMap as selling AdBlue at the pump. That data is incomplete, so treat it as one known option rather than the only one.

name: Coatbridge
intro: Once described as the 'Iron Burgh', Coatbridge is a North Lanarkshire town in the central Lowlands, about 14 km east of Glasgow city centre, with 42,264 people in 2022. Together with neighbouring Airdrie it forms the Monklands, an area of approximately 90,000 people that is often considered part of the Greater Glasgow urban area. In the 19th century it was a major Scottish centre for iron works and coal mining. Today the ML5 postcode district covers the town. Four motorways appear on its road list, the M8, M73, M74 and A8(M), along with the A8, A89, A725 and A8010. Viewpark is 3.6 km away, Airdrie 3.9 km and Bellshill 4.4 km, so the town sits in a close cluster of communities, and a motorway service area is just over 5 km away.
roadsText: Main roads recorded around Coatbridge are the M8, M73, M74, A8(M), A89, A725, A8 and A8010. Bothwell Services on the M74 is only 5.1 km away, with Hamilton Services, also on the M74, at 7.6 km and Heart of Scotland Services on the M8 at 17 km. OpenStreetMap lists a station in Glasgow (17.6 km) as selling AdBlue at the pump; that is incomplete map data, not a full list.

name: Cobham
intro: Elmbridge's Cobham is a large Surrey village on the River Mole, about 17 miles south-west of London and 10 miles north-east of Guildford. It has a commercial and services High Street, a significant number of primary and private schools, and Painshill Park, an 18th-century landscape garden. Around 17,505 people live in the area, which uses the KT11 postcode district. Hersham is 3.9 km away and Byfleet 5.1 km, with Great Bookham and Fetcham, Walton-on-Thames, West Molesey and Ashtead all between 5.8 and 6.3 km. For a driver with an AdBlue warning, Cobham has motorway services almost on its doorstep: Cobham Services on the M25 is just 3.5 km from the village centre in a straight line, and Wisley Services on the A3 is 8.5 km away.
roadsText: Cobham Services on the M25 is the nearest listed service area, 3.5 km from the centre of Cobham in a straight line. Wisley Services on the A3 is 8.5 km away, and Heston Services on the M4 is further out at 17.2 km. With two listed service areas inside about nine kilometres, drivers here have nearby options on both the M25 and the A3.

name: Codsall
intro: Only a small amount of green belt still separates Codsall from Wolverhampton, 5 miles to the south-east, and the two are almost contiguous. Codsall is a village and civil parish in the South Staffordshire district and, along with Perton, forms part of the Staffordshire and West Midlands county boundary. Telford is 13 miles to the west-north-west. The postcode district is WV8. Other nearby towns include Wombourne at 10.3 km, Bilston at 10.7 km and Willenhall at 10.8 km, with Great Wyrley and Cheslyn Hay and Sedgley both at 11.9 km. For a driver with an AdBlue warning, the nearest listed service area is on the M6, 9.3 km away in a straight line, with another on the A5 at 10.5 km and a third on the M54 at 15.2 km.
roadsText: Hilton Park Services on the M6 is the nearest service area to Codsall, 9.3 km away in a straight line. The Trucker's Rest on the A5 is 10.5 km off and Telford Services on the M54 is 15.2 km. OpenStreetMap lists stations in Warley (17.3 km) and Burntwood (WS7 3XA, 18.2 km) as selling AdBlue at the pump. Those records are incomplete, so stations closer to Codsall may also sell it.

name: Colchester
intro: In north-eastern Essex, on the River Colne 50 miles (80 km) north-east of London, Colchester is a city connected to London by the A12. Its built-up area had 130,245 residents at the 2021 census, making it the second-largest settlement in Essex after Southend-on-Sea, and it is 20 miles (30 km) from the port of Harwich. Postcode districts are CO1, CO2, CO3 and CO4, and the main roads include the A12, A120 and A133, along with the A134, A137, A1124, A1232 and A1341. Neighbouring towns are a fair distance away: Halstead is about 19.2 km, Clacton-on-Sea 19.6 km, Sudbury 19.9 km and Witham 20.9 km. Ardleigh South Services on the A120, about 5.1 km out, is the one service area close to the city; the next nearest are more than 23 km away.
roadsText: Colchester's main roads are the A12, A120, A133, A134, A137, A1124, A1232 and A1341. Ardleigh South Services on the A120 is the nearest service area, about 5.1 km away. The next are some distance off: EG Sprougton Road Services on the A14 at around 23.7 km and Boreham Services on the A131 at 30.6 km.

name: Coleraine
intro: Near the mouth of the River Bann, Coleraine is a market town and the county town of County Londonderry, with 24,483 residents at the 2021 census. Belfast is 55 miles (89 km) to the south-east and Derry 30 miles (48 km) to the west, and both are linked to the town by major roads and railway connections. The town serves a large catchment area within the Causeway Coast and Glens district and is designated a major growth area in the Northern Ireland Development Strategy. Its postcode district is BT52, and the A26, A29, A37, A2 and A54 are among its main roads. Ballymoney is about 12.1 km away and Limavady 20.3 km, but Ballymena, Antrim and Cookstown are between 39 km and 54.8 km off. Service areas are distant too, the closest about 32.1 km away, which matters when an AdBlue warning comes on.
roadsText: Main roads listed for Coleraine are the A26, A29, A37, A2 and A54. Service areas are some distance away: Glenshane Tourist Services on the A6 is the nearest at about 32.1 km in a straight line, Temple Patrick Services Northbound on the M2 is about 64 km away and Cohannon Services on the M1 about 70.3 km. With gaps that long, it is worth dealing with an AdBlue warning before a longer run.

name: Colne
intro: The M65 ends just west of Colne, and from there two main roads carry traffic on towards Yorkshire: the A56 to Skipton and the A6068 to Keighley. That puts this Pendle market town at a handover point between motorway and A-road, close to the southern entrance to the Aire Gap, the lowest crossing of the Pennine watershed. Colne is 3 miles (5 km) northeast of Nelson, 6 miles (10 km) northeast of Burnley and 25 miles (40 km) east of Preston, and it adjoins Foulridge, Laneshaw Bridge, Trawden Forest, Nelson, Barrowford and Blacko. The BB8 postcode district covers the town, which had about 18,914 residents. Brierfield is around 5.4 km away and Barnoldswick 6.8 km. If an AdBlue warning comes on, it helps to know if you are still near the M65 or already on the A-roads beyond its end.
roadsText: The M65 terminates west of Colne, with the A56 continuing towards Skipton and the A6068 towards Keighley. Hollin Bank Service Station on the M65 is the closest service area, about 4.9 km away. Beyond that the options are much further off: Blackburn with Darwen Services, also on the M65, at around 25.8 km, and Hartshead Moor services on the M62 at roughly 32.2 km.

name: Colwyn Bay
intro: Overlooking the Irish Sea from the north coast of Wales, Colwyn Bay is a town and seaside resort in Conwy County Borough. Historically it lay within Denbighshire. The 2021 census gave the built-up area a population of 29,275, and postcodes here fall into LL28 and LL29. Its road list is short: the A55, A470, A547 and A546. Conwy is about 5.5km away and Llandudno 6.3km, while Rhyl is 17.8km and Prestatyn 22.5km. Many local journeys will be short, given how close the nearest neighbours are, but anything further afield means a longer run. If an AdBlue warning comes up, the two nearest service areas are both on the A55, at about 10.7km and 15.1km from the town.
roadsText: The roads listed around Colwyn Bay are the A55, A470, A547 and A546. The nearest service areas are Orme View services on the A55 at about 10.7km, Kinmel Park services, also on the A55, at 15.1km, and Bangor services on the A5 at 26.4km. OpenStreetMap lists two forecourts as selling AdBlue at the pump: one at Penmaenmawr (LL34 6UN), about 10.6km away, and one at Rhyl (LL18 5XE), about 15.1km away. That data is incomplete, so others may exist.

name: Congleton
intro: Manchester is 21 miles to the north and Stoke on Trent 13 miles to the south of Congleton, a market town on the River Dane in Cheshire East. At the 2021 census its built-up area had 30,005 residents, and its postcode district is CW12. Neighbouring towns are spread out rather than packed together: Biddulph is 6.7 km away, Kidsgrove 9.1 km, Alsager 9.7 km, Sandbach 10.5 km and Macclesfield 11.8 km, with Leek at 13.9 km. The roads listed for Congleton are all A roads, among them the A54, A34 and A534. If an AdBlue warning comes on, the closest service area is Sandbach Services on the M6, 8.8 km away, and the other options are set out below.
roadsText: The roads listed around Congleton are the A54, A34, A5365, A534, A536 and A527. All three of the nearest service areas are on the M6: Sandbach Services at 8.8 km, Crewe Services at 13.6 km and Knutsford Services at 19.5 km. Biddulph, 6.7 km away, is the closest neighbouring town.

name: Conisbrough
intro: Roughly midway between Doncaster and Rotherham, Conisbrough is a town within the City of Doncaster, built alongside the River Don. The Conisbrough and Denaby ward has a population of 14,333, and the town uses the DN12 postcode district. Warmsworth is about 2.7 km away, Mexborough 4.1 km and Swinton 5.5 km, with Maltby and Wickersley and Bramley each about 7.1 km and Wath upon Dearne 7.5 km. For a van or diesel car with an AdBlue warning, a station in Doncaster listed as selling AdBlue at the pump is about 4.4 km away. Service areas are further. Rotherham Services on the M1 is about 12.4 km in a straight line, Blyth Services on the A1(M) about 15.4 km and Barnsdale Bar on the A1 about 16.1 km.
roadsText: In a straight line, the closest service areas to Conisbrough are Rotherham Services on the M1 (12.4 km), Blyth Services on the A1(M) (15.4 km) and Barnsdale Bar Services on the A1 (16.1 km). OpenStreetMap lists a station in Doncaster (DN4 0TP), about 4.4 km away, and another in Pontefract (WF7 7HX), about 19.4 km away, as selling AdBlue at the pump. The map data is incomplete.

name: Connah's Quay
intro: Known locally as The Quay, and formerly as Wepre, Connah's Quay (Cei Connah) is the largest town in Flintshire, with 16,771 residents. It stands on the River Dee next to the border with England, 6 miles (9.7 km) west of Chester, and is part of the wider Deeside conurbation, running continuously into Shotton, Flint and Buckley. The CH5 postcode district covers the town. Wepre Woods, an ancient woodland that includes Ewloe Castle, dating from the 13th century, lies within it. For a driver whose van or diesel car shows an AdBlue warning, one advantage stands out: Chester West Services on the A55 is listed just 3.5 km from the centre in a straight line. Hawarden is 4.1 km away, Flint 5.5 km and Buckley 5.9 km, with Chester and Ellesmere Port both 11.7 km off.
roadsText: Chester West Services on the A55 is the nearest service area to Connah's Quay, just 3.5 km from the centre in a straight line. The next two are much further away: Singing Kettle Services, also on the A55, at 17.1 km, and RoadChef Chester Services on the M56 at 18.1 km. For most drivers in CH5 with an AdBlue warning, the A55 site is the natural first stop.

name: Consett
intro: About 14 miles south-west of Newcastle upon Tyne, Consett is a County Durham town in the DH8 postcode district. The main roads listed for it are all A-roads: the A692, A691, A68, A693 and A694, with no motorway among them. That is worth knowing if an AdBlue warning comes on, because the closest motorway services in the data are on the A1(M) at Washington, 18.6 km away. Stanley is the nearest neighbouring town at 9.7 km, with Prudhoe at 12.2 km and Whickham and Blaydon both around 15 km off. Chester-le-Street (16.8 km) and Birtley (17.6 km) complete the local picture. For a van or diesel car based in DH8, most trips out of town will begin on one of those five A-roads before reaching anything bigger.
roadsText: The main roads listed around Consett are the A692, A691, A68, A693 and A694. The nearest service areas are Washington Services on the A1(M) at 18.6 km, Durham Services, also on the A1(M), at 24.5 km, and Seaton Burn Services on the A19 at 27.4 km. All three are a fair drive from DH8, so a low AdBlue reading is better dealt with before a longer run.

name: Conwy
intro: A walled market town on the west bank of the River Conwy, facing Deganwy across the water, Conwy is the administrative centre of Conwy County Borough in North Wales and was previously known in English as Conway. The community also takes in Deganwy and Llandudno Junction, and had 14,753 residents at the 2011 census, though postal addresses do not follow those boundaries: Deganwy is part of the Conwy post town while Llandudno Junction is a separate one. The LL31 postcode district covers the town. Llandudno is just 3.3 km away and Colwyn Bay 5.5 km, with Bangor at 22.5 km. If an AdBlue warning appears, the nearest listed service area, Orme View Services on the A55, is only 5.2 km away in a straight line, and a station listed as selling AdBlue at the pump is a similar distance off.
roadsText: Orme View Services on the A55 is the nearest service area to Conwy, 5.2 km from the town in a straight line. Kinmel Park Services, also on the A55, is 20.4 km away and Bangor Services on the A5 is 21.2 km. An Esso station at Penmaenmawr (LL34 6UN), 5.1 km away, is listed in OpenStreetMap as selling AdBlue at the pump. That mapping is incomplete, so other stations may stock it too.

name: Cookstown
intro: Said to have the longest main street in Ireland, running in a straight line for 1.25 miles (2 km), Cookstown is a market town in County Tyrone and the fourth-largest in the county, with 12,546 residents at the 2021 census. Along with Magherafelt and Dungannon it is one of the main towns in Mid Ulster. It was founded in the early 17th century during the Plantation of Ulster, rebuilt in the late 18th century, and was a centre of the linen industry west of the River Bann until 1956. The town sits in the BT80 postcode district. Dungannon is about 15.6 km away, while Craigavon, Armagh, Antrim and Omagh are between 31.8 km and 36 km off. A driver with an AdBlue warning has two service areas within 22.7 km, and a station listed as selling AdBlue at the pump is in the town itself.
roadsText: Cohannon Services on the M1 is about 16.8 km from Cookstown in a straight line and Glenshane Tourist Services on the A6 about 22.7 km, with Temple Patrick Services Northbound on the M2 at about 47.2 km. OpenStreetMap lists a station in the town (BT80 8QB), about 0.3 km away, as selling AdBlue at the pump. OpenStreetMap's AdBlue data is incomplete, so other local forecourts may stock it as well.

name: Corby
intro: About 23 miles (37 km) north-east of Northampton, Corby is a town and civil parish in North Northamptonshire whose wider built-up area had 68,160 residents in 2021. It was once known as 'Little Scotland' because of the many Scottish workers who came to its steelworks, and it has since been through regeneration, including the opening of Corby railway station in 2009. The town is served by A roads rather than motorways, with the A43, A427, A4300, A6003, A6014, A6086 and A6116 all listed. Postcode districts are NN17 and NN18. Desborough is about 10.4 km away and Kettering 10.6 km, while Market Harborough is around 15.9 km and Oakham 20.3 km. The nearest service areas are close to 12 km out, so it helps to know where to stop before an AdBlue warning becomes pressing.
roadsText: Every main road listed for Corby is an A road: the A43, A427, A4300, A6003, A6014, A6086 and A6116. Two service areas are about 11.8 km away, Rothwell Truck Stop on the A14 and Morcott Services on the A47, with Thrapston Services on the A45 at about 15.7 km. An Esso station near Peterborough (PE8 6TZ), about 18 km away, is listed in OpenStreetMap as selling AdBlue at the pump; that list is incomplete.

name: Corfe Mullen
intro: Although its parish council adopted Town Council status in December 2019, Corfe Mullen remains in most respects a large village, on the north-western urban fringe of the South East Dorset conurbation. The parish had 10,374 residents at the 2021 census and spans two postcode districts, BH21 and BH18. Its name comes from the Old English corf, a cutting or pass, and the Old French molin, a mill, after the old water mill on the River Stour where the village originally stood. It lies within the Dorset Heaths and is surrounded by green belt despite being close to the urban area. Wimborne Minster is 6 km away and Poole 6.4 km. With an AdBlue warning showing, a Poole forecourt listed as selling AdBlue at the pump is much closer than the nearest service area, which is 22.8 km away on the A31.
roadsText: Corfe Mullen is some distance from listed service areas: Picket Post Services on the A31 is the nearest at 22.8 km in a straight line, Rufus Stone, also on the A31, is 32 km and West Wellow Services on the A36 is 40.2 km. Much closer, MFG Creekmoor, a Shell site in Poole (BH17 7FR) just 3.6 km away, is listed in OpenStreetMap as selling AdBlue at the pump. That mapping is incomplete.

name: Corsham
intro: Just off the A4, at the south-western edge of the Cotswolds, Corsham is a historic market town in west Wiltshire, 4 miles (6 km) south-west of Chippenham and 8 miles (13 km) north-east of Bath. The parish also includes the villages of Gastard and Neston. Corsham has a population of 10,887 and sits in the SN13 postcode district. Historically a centre for agriculture and later the wool industry, it remains a focus for quarrying Bath Stone, and during the Second World War and the Cold War it became a major administrative and manufacturing centre for the Ministry of Defence. Chippenham is 5.6 km away, Melksham 7.3 km and Trowbridge 11.7 km. With an AdBlue warning showing, the M4 is the nearest option, with two listed service areas on it within 10.8 km in a straight line.
roadsText: Corsham sits just off the A4. The two nearest service areas are both on the M4: Moto Leigh Delamere Services, 9.2 km away in a straight line, and Chippenham Pit Stop at 10.8 km. Warminster Services on the A350 is further out at 23.7 km. For most drivers in SN13 with an AdBlue warning, the M4 sites will be the first to consider, though road distances will be longer.

name: Coseley
intro: Described as a village, Coseley is in the Dudley district of the West Midlands, three miles (five kilometres) north of Dudley and on the border with Wolverhampton and Sandwell. It falls within the Tipton and Wednesbury parliamentary constituency and has a population of 25,206. Because it borders both Wolverhampton and Sandwell, a short drive from Coseley can take you into another borough: Sedgley is 2.5 km away on a direct line, Tipton 2.7 km, Bilston 3.4 km and Dudley 3.5 km. The postcode districts reflect that mix, reaching across DY1, DY3, DY4 and WV14. The main road network here is made up of A roads, including the A4123, A463, A461 and A41, with no motorway among them. For a van or car with an AdBlue warning, that means reaching a motorway service area involves a run of more than 12 km.
roadsText: Main roads around Coseley include the A4123, A463, A461, A41, A4444, A4036, A449 and A454. On a direct line, the nearest service areas are Hilton Park on the M6 (12.3 km), Frankley on the M5 (13 km) and The Trucker's Rest on the A5 (16.3 km). OpenStreetMap lists a station with a Warley address, 5.4 km away, and one with a Burntwood address, 19.2 km away, as selling AdBlue at the pump. Other stations missing from its records may sell it too.

name: Cottingham
intro: Hallgate and King Street, Cottingham's two main shopping streets, cross near the Church of Saint Mary the Virgin, and the village also has a market square called Market Green. The village lies 4 miles (6 km) north-west of central Kingston upon Hull and 6 miles (10 km) south-east of Beverley, on the eastern edge of the Yorkshire Wolds in the East Riding. With 17,164 residents in 2011, it is one of the villages that claim to be the largest in England. It uses the HU16 postcode district. Willerby and Anlaby is about 4.1 km away, Hull 5.7 km and Beverley 6.5 km. If an AdBlue warning comes on, note that service areas are some distance away: Ulceby Truckstop on the A160 is around 20 km in a straight line, and the nearest motorway services is more than 43 km off.
roadsText: The closest service area to Cottingham is Ulceby Truckstop on the A160, about 20 km in a straight line. Doncaster (North) Services on the M180 is about 43.6 km away and Bilbrough Top Service Area on the A64 about 52.4 km. That gap means the nearest motorway services is a long run from the village, and road distances will be longer still.

name: Coventry
intro: A cathedral city on the River Sherbourne, Coventry is the second largest city in the West Midlands region, with 345,324 residents at the 2021 census. It lies 19 miles (31km) east-south-east of Birmingham, separated from it by the green belt of the Meriden Gap, and 10 miles north of Warwick. The city is part of the Coventry and Bedworth Urban Area, home to 389,603 people in 2021. Postcode districts run from CV1 to CV8. Listed roads include the M6, A4053, A4114, A4600, A428, A444, A45 and A46. Bedworth is about 7.3km from the centre, Kenilworth 8.2km and Leamington Spa 13km. Driving here therefore mixes city traffic, short runs to neighbouring towns and motorway trips on the M6. A motorway service area sits only about 7.3km out, which is a useful fallback if an AdBlue warning appears.
roadsText: The nearest service area to Coventry is Corley services on the M6, about 7.3km away. Next come Warwick North (Budbrooke) services on the A46 at 16km and Rugby services on the M6 at 17.9km. Listed roads around the city are the M6, A4053, A4114, A4600, A428, A444, A45 and A46. One forecourt about 5.6km away is listed on OpenStreetMap as selling AdBlue at the pump. That data is incomplete, so it is not a full picture of where AdBlue is sold.

name: Cowdenbeath and Lumphinnans
intro: This page covers Cowdenbeath, a town and burgh in west Fife, together with Lumphinnans, an area of about 12,030 people in the KY4 postcode district. Cowdenbeath grew up around the extensive coalfields of the area and became a police burgh in 1890. It sits north-east of Dunfermline and 18 miles north of Edinburgh, and the wider civil parish of Beath had 17,351 residents in 2011. Dunfermline is 6.5 km from the centre in a straight line, Rosyth 9.1 km and Kirkcaldy and Dysart 11.6 km, with South Queensferry at 13.8 km and Glenrothes at 14.7 km. If an AdBlue warning appears on a van or diesel car here, the nearest listed motorway services are Kinross Services on the M90, 12.5 km away in a straight line, while the next two listed sites are more than 24 km off.
roadsText: Kinross Services on the M90 is the closest listed service area to Cowdenbeath, at 12.5 km in a straight line. The next two are Dreghorn Services on the A720 at 24.2 km and Musselburgh Services on the A1 at 27.1 km. Straight-line figures understate the drive, so allow extra distance if the AdBlue gauge is already low.

name: Cowes
intro: A seaport town on the west bank of the River Medina estuary, Cowes faces the smaller town of East Cowes across the water on the Isle of Wight. The two are linked by the Cowes Floating Bridge, a chain ferry. The 2021 census put the population at 14,370, and the town is covered by the PO31 and PO32 postcode districts. Cowes has long been a home for international yacht racing, and Cowes Week is held in the first week of August each year. Newport is the nearest town at 5.6 km, and Ryde is 11.2 km away. For a van or diesel car with an AdBlue warning, the key point is distance: the nearest listed service area, Farlington Services on the A27, is 21.3 km away in a straight line, and the other two listed are further still. It is worth planning a stop well ahead.
roadsText: Cowes has no listed service area close by. The nearest are Farlington Services on the A27 at 21.3 km, Rownhams Services on the M27 at 24.8 km and West Wellow Services on the A36 at 27.5 km, all measured in a straight line from the town. As Cowes is on the Isle of Wight, the actual journey to any of them will be longer than these figures suggest.

name: Cradley Heath
intro: Known in the first half of the twentieth century for the manufacture of chains, Cradley Heath is a town in the Metropolitan Borough of Sandwell, in the Black Country, 8 miles (13 km) west of Birmingham. Its postcode districts are B64, B65 and B63. The neighbouring towns are all close: Halesowen is 2.1 km away, Rowley Regis 2.6 km, Brierley Hill 3.7 km, Dudley 4 km and Oldbury 4.3 km, with Stourbridge at 5.7 km. For a van or diesel car with an AdBlue warning, the M5 is the nearest motorway with services, and the listed service area on it is 5.8 km away in a straight line. The next nearest, on the M42 and the M6, are 14.5 km and 19 km off. OpenStreetMap also lists a station in Warley, 4.2 km away, as selling AdBlue at the pump, though its records are incomplete.
roadsText: Frankley Services on the M5 is the nearest service area to Cradley Heath, 5.8 km away in a straight line. Hopwood Park Services on the M42 is 14.5 km off and Hilton Park Services on the M6 is 19 km. OpenStreetMap lists a station in Warley (4.2 km) and one at DY10 1JS (16.6 km) as selling AdBlue at the pump, plus an HGV-only site in Birmingham (B25 8DW) at 15.3 km. Its coverage is incomplete.

name: Craigavon
intro: Begun in 1965 as a planned settlement in north County Armagh, Craigavon has an unusual layout for drivers: in most of the town, motor vehicles are completely separated from pedestrians, roundabouts are used extensively, and its town centre has no traditional streets. It was meant to be the heart of a new linear city taking in Lurgan and Portadown, a plan that was mostly abandoned, and locally the name refers to the urban area between those two towns. The town is built beside a pair of artificial lakes and is made up of Brownlow, a large residential area, the smaller Mandeville, and Highfield, the central area with a shopping centre, courthouse and council headquarters. The BT64, BT65 and BT66 postcode districts cover it, and the M12 and M1 are listed among its roads. With an AdBlue warning, the nearest service area is Cohannon Services on the M1, 18.5 km away.
roadsText: Craigavon's listed roads are the M12 and M1 plus the A3, A27, A50, A76, A26 and A4. Cohannon Services on the M1 is the nearest service area at 18.5 km, with Lisburn Services on the M1 at 26.3 km and the northbound services at Temple Patrick on the M2 at 36.4 km. Banbridge, 12.7 km away, is the closest neighbouring town.

name: Cramlington
intro: Six miles north of Newcastle upon Tyne, Cramlington sits right on the border between Northumberland and North Tyneside. The traffic interchange at Moor Farm, Annitsford links the two areas. East Cramlington lies east of the A189, on the B1326 road that connects the town to Seaton Delaval. NE23 is the postcode district listed, and the town had 28,843 residents at the 2021 census. Its road list is varied for a town of this size, taking in the A1 and A19 as well as the A189, A1171, A1172, A1068, A192 and A1061. Bedlington (5.1 km), Killingworth (5.5 km) and Blyth (5.7 km) are all close by, with Longbenton (7.4 km), Whitley Bay (9.2 km) and Ashington (10.2 km) a little further out. Seaton Burn Services is just 3.5 km away on the A19.
roadsText: Cramlington's main roads include the A189, A19 and A1, plus the A1171, A1172, A1068, A192 and A1061. Seaton Burn Services on the A19 is only 3.5 km away. Beyond that, Washington Services on the A1(M) is 22.1 km off and Easington Services on the A19 is 34.9 km. In OpenStreetMap, whose records are incomplete, one station in Newcastle upon Tyne, about 5.3 km away, is listed as selling AdBlue at the pump.

name: Cranleigh
intro: Guildford lies 8 miles (13 km) north-west of Cranleigh, a village and civil parish in the Borough of Waverley, Surrey, set on a minor road east of the A281, which links Guildford with Horsham. Horsham is 14.2 km away. The village lies in the north-west corner of the Weald, with Winterfold Forest directly to the north-west on the northern Greensand Ridge, and it had a population of just over 11,000 in 2011. Cranleigh is covered by the GU6 postcode district. Its nearest neighbouring towns are all more than 10 km off: Godalming at 10.5 km, Farncombe at 11.3 km and Dorking at 14.4 km. For a driver with an AdBlue warning, none of the listed service areas is close by. The nearest is Wisley Services on the A3, 16.7 km away in a straight line.
roadsText: The A281, linking Guildford with Horsham, runs to the west of Cranleigh. The nearest listed service areas are all at least 16.7 km away in a straight line: Wisley Services on the A3 at 16.7 km, Cobham Services on the M25 at 18.8 km and Buck Barn on the A24 at 19.5 km. Road distances from GU6 will be longer, so it pays to deal with an AdBlue warning before setting off on a longer trip.

name: Crawley
intro: In the medieval period, Crawley grew thanks to its location on the main road from London to the port of Shoreham, and later the passing trade to Brighton brought coaching inns. Today it is a town and borough in West Sussex, 28 miles (45 km) south of London and 18 miles (29 km) north of Brighton and Hove, with a population of 118,493 at the 2021 Census. Southern parts of the borough lie immediately next to the High Weald National Landscape. Postcode districts are RH6, RH10 and RH11. The M23 and A23 head the list of main roads, along with the A264 and A217. Horley is 6.6 km away, Horsham 11.1 km and East Grinstead 11.7 km. Crawley is well placed for anyone dealing with an AdBlue warning, with the nearest listed services 3.8 km away.
roadsText: The M23, A23, A264, A2220, A2004, A2219, A2011 and A217 are the main roads listed for Crawley. Pease Pottage Services on the M23 is the closest listed service area, 3.8 km away, and Handcross on the A23 is 6.8 km. Ricebridge Services (Hickstead), also on the A23, is 16.5 km away. With two listed stops this close, drivers have options near town.

name: Crewe
intro: Best known as a large railway junction, Crewe is a railway town and civil parish in Cheshire East, 28 miles south of Manchester city centre and 31 miles south-east of Liverpool city centre. Its built-up area had 76,437 people at the 2021 census. The roads listed for the town are all A-roads, namely the A534, A5020, A530, A500, A51, A5078, A5019 and A532, but the M6 is not far off: two M6 service areas are within about 9 km. Postcode districts CW1 and CW2 cover the town. Nantwich is the nearest neighbour at 5.5 km, followed by Sandbach (7.8 km), Alsager (10.1 km), Middlewich (10.6 km), Winsford (11.7 km) and Kidsgrove (13.8 km). For a van or diesel car with an AdBlue warning, reaching the M6 services means a run on the local A-roads first.
roadsText: The main roads around Crewe are the A534, A5020, A530, A500, A51, A5078, A5019 and A532. Crewe Services on the M6 is 8 km away, Sandbach Services, also on the M6, 9.1 km, and Keele Services on the M6 15.5 km. A station in Newcastle-under-Lyme (ST5), 19.7 km away, is listed as selling AdBlue at the pump in OpenStreetMap; its data is incomplete, so nearer options may exist.

name: Crosby
intro: Crosby is a coastal town in Sefton, about 6 miles north of Liverpool, with Bootle to the south, Southport and Formby to the north and Netherton to the east. Blundellsands borders it on the north side and Waterloo on the south, and an address here could fall in any of the listed postcode districts L21, L22, L23, L29 or L30. Litherland is the nearest town at 2.4 km, with Bootle at 4 km and Maghull at 6.1 km; Formby and Wallasey are both 8.2 km away, and Kirkby 9.5 km. The road list includes two motorways, the M57 and M58, along with the A565, A5758, A5036, A59, A506 and A5058. The town has a population of 50,218. For a van or diesel car with an AdBlue warning, Old Meadow Services on the M58 is the closest service area in the data at 8 km.
roadsText: Crosby's main roads include the M57 and M58, plus the A565, A5758, A5036, A59, A506 and A5058. Old Meadow Services on the M58 is 8 km away, Earlsfield Services on the M57 14.6 km and Burtonwood Services on the M62 26.6 km. A station at Old Meadow, also 8 km off, is listed as selling AdBlue at the pump in OpenStreetMap; an L5 site 6.7 km away is marked HGV-only. The map data is incomplete.

name: Crowborough
intro: High in the Weald, at the edge of Ashdown Forest, Crowborough is the highest town in the High Weald Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty, reaching 242 metres above sea level at its highest point. It is a town and civil parish in East Sussex, about 33 miles south of London, and with 21,688 residents at the 2021 Census it is the second largest town in inland East Sussex after Hailsham. It is covered by the TN6 postcode district. Uckfield is 10.4 km away and Royal Tunbridge Wells 11.5 km, with East Grinstead at 14.9 km and Tonbridge at 17.9 km. For drivers, the useful point is that Crowborough is some way from the listed service areas: the three nearest listed ones are all around 25 km away in a straight line. A station closer to town is listed as selling AdBlue at the pump.
roadsText: Crowborough's three nearest listed service areas are all about 25 km away in a straight line: Polegate Services on the A22 at 25.3 km, Handcross on the A23 at 25.5 km and Pease Pottage Services on the M23 at 25.6 km. A station 16.1 km away is listed in OpenStreetMap as selling AdBlue at the pump. OpenStreetMap does not record every site that sells AdBlue.

name: Crowthorne
intro: Wellington College, a large school that opened in 1859, is in Crowthorne, a village and civil parish in the Bracknell Forest district of south-eastern Berkshire, and Broadmoor Hospital lies on the eastern edge of the village. The parish had 7,806 residents at the 2021 census, and its postcode district is RG45. Several towns are very close: Sandhurst is 2.9 km away, Wokingham 4.5 km, Bracknell 4.6 km, Yateley 5 km and Camberley 6 km, with Frimley at 7.6 km. For a van or diesel car with an AdBlue warning, the nearest listed service area is Fleet Services on the M3, 9.7 km away in a straight line, and Reading Services on the M4 is 17.7 km. A station on the Swallowfield By-pass near Reading, 13.6 km off, is listed in OpenStreetMap as selling AdBlue at the pump.
roadsText: Fleet Services on the M3 is the nearest service area to Crowthorne at 9.7 km in a straight line. Reading Services on the M4 is 17.7 km away, and Wisley Services on the A3 is 22.9 km. OpenStreetMap lists a station on the Swallowfield By-pass near Reading (RG7 1LZ), 13.6 km away, as selling AdBlue at the pump. That data is incomplete, so it may not be the closest option.

name: Croydon
intro: The London Borough of Croydon covers 87 km2 of Outer London and had 397,741 residents in mid-2023, making it one of London's two most populated boroughs. At its centre is the historic town of Croydon, and its other urban centres include Thornton Heath, Coulsdon, Purley, South Norwood, Norbury, New Addington and Selsdon, so a Croydon address could be in any of several distinct districts. The borough was formed in 1965 by merging the County Borough of Croydon with Coulsdon and Purley Urban District, which had been in Surrey. Main roads listed are the A23, A22, A232, A235, A212, A2022, A236 and A222. Sutton is 6.5 km away, Caterham 7 km, Bromley 9.4 km and Lambeth 9.7 km, with Merton at 10.7 km. Postcode districts listed include CR0, CR2 and CR8.
roadsText: Listed roads are the A23, A232, A22, A235, A212, A2022, A236 and A222. The nearest service area is Clacket Lane Services on the M25, 12.2 km away, followed by Cobham Services on the M25 at 23.1 km and Heston Services on the M4 at 26.3 km. A station at Catford, 11.7 km away, is listed on OpenStreetMap as selling AdBlue at the pump; that data is incomplete.

name: Cudworth and Shafton
intro: Barnsley lies about 4.5 km from Cudworth, a village in the Metropolitan Borough of Barnsley that had 10,977 residents in 2011; with Shafton, the combined area has 12,472. Cudworth has two historic centres, Upper or Over Cudworth and Low or Nether Cudworth, and much of its housing dates from the inter-war and post-war periods. Open space still surrounds the village, including green belt, former colliery land and farmland on the south and south-east sides. Postcodes fall in S72. Royston is about 3 km away, Darton 6.7 km and Wombwell 7 km. For an AdBlue warning, a station in Pontefract listed as selling AdBlue at the pump is about 8.4 km away, and Woolley Edge Services on the M1 is about 9.7 km in a straight line.
roadsText: The nearest service areas to Cudworth and Shafton in a straight line are Woolley Edge Services on the M1 (9.7 km), Barnsdale Bar Services on the A1 (12.6 km) and Exelby Services Whitwood on the M62 (14.2 km). OpenStreetMap lists a station in Pontefract (WF7 7HX), about 8.4 km away, and another in Doncaster (DN4 0TP), about 18.7 km away, as selling AdBlue at the pump. That record is incomplete.

name: Cumbernauld
intro: Positioned in the centre of Scotland's Central Belt, Cumbernauld is the most populated town in North Lanarkshire and the tenth most-populous locality in Scotland. It sits on the Scottish watershed between the Forth and the Clyde, though it leans culturally towards Glasgow: the New Town's planners aimed to fill 80% of its houses with people from the city. For a period, the town was chiefly populated around what is now called The Village. Postcode districts G67 and G68 cover Cumbernauld. The M80 and M73 both appear on its road list, with the A80, A73, A803 and A8011. Kilsyth is 4.9 km away, Kirkintilloch 9 km and Airdrie 9.4 km, while Larbert is 13.7 km and Falkirk 13.9 km. Service areas on three different motorways lie between 14.8 km and 17.6 km from the town.
roadsText: Main roads recorded around Cumbernauld are the M80, M73, A8011, A73, A803 and A80. The nearest service areas are spread across three motorways: Stirling Services on the M9 at 14.8 km, Bothwell Services on the M74 at 15.6 km and Heart of Scotland Services on the M8 at 17.6 km. None is right on the doorstep, so an AdBlue warning is best dealt with before a longer trip.

name: Cwmbrân
intro: New employment opportunities in the south-eastern portion of the South Wales Coalfield were the aim when Cwmbrân was designated as a new town in 1949. It is in the county borough of Torfaen in south Wales, within the historic boundaries of Monmouthshire, and now has a population of 47,075. The NP44 postcode district covers the town. Neighbouring towns are close by: Pontypool is 4.7 km away, Risca 7.5 km and Newport 7.6 km, while Blackwood, Abertillery and Ystrad Mynach are between 12 km and 14.5 km. The M4 is among the main roads listed around the town, along with the A4042, A4051, A472 and A4043. For a van or diesel car, that means driving here mixes short trips to neighbouring towns with runs onto the motorway, where the nearest service areas are 14.1 km and 14.9 km away.
roadsText: The main roads around Cwmbrân are the M4, A4042, A4051, A472 and A4043. The nearest service areas are Cardiff Gate on the M4, 14.1 km away, and Magor on the M4 at 14.9 km. Monmouth A40 Services on the A40 is 20.2 km away, giving a third option for anyone heading that way.

name: Dalkeith
intro: Midlothian's main administrative centre, Dalkeith is a historic market town on the River Esk with a population of 15,146 in 2022. It splits into four distinct areas: Dalkeith proper with its town centre and historic core, Eskbank to the west, Woodburn to the east and the semi-rural village of Newbattle to the south. That mix means a short drive can take you from town-centre streets to a more rural edge. The town sits in the EH22 postcode district, and its neighbours are close: Mayfield is 2.4 km away, Bonnyrigg 3.7 km and Musselburgh 5.4 km, with Edinburgh 10.9 km off. For a driver dealing with an AdBlue warning around Dalkeith, the nearest listed service area is just 3.8 km away, and two more are within 12.9 km.
roadsText: Musselburgh Services on the A1 is the closest service area listed for Dalkeith, about 3.8 km away. Dreghorn Services on the A720 is 10.8 km away and MacMerry, also on the A1, is 12.9 km. Having two A1 stops and one on the A720 within that range gives drivers in Dalkeith, Eskbank, Woodburn or Newbattle more than one listed option when an AdBlue warning comes on.

name: Darlaston
intro: Historically part of Staffordshire, Darlaston is now an industrial town in the Metropolitan Borough of Walsall, in the West Midlands. It is located near Bilston, Walsall, Wednesbury, Willenhall and Tipton, and those neighbours are very close: Wednesbury is just 2 km away, Willenhall 2.5 km, Bilston 2.8 km, Tipton 3.8 km and Walsall 4.1 km, with Bloxwich at 5.2 km. The postcode districts for the town are WS10 and WV13. For a driver with an AdBlue warning, the nearest listed motorway service area is on the M6, 8.3 km away in a straight line, with another on the M6 Toll at 11.4 km and a third on the A5 at 12.5 km. OpenStreetMap also lists a station in Warley, 7.3 km off, as selling AdBlue at the pump, though that data is incomplete.
roadsText: The nearest service areas to Darlaston are Hilton Park Services on the M6, 8.3 km away in a straight line, Norton Canes Services on the M6 Toll at 11.4 km and The Trucker's Rest on the A5 at 12.5 km. OpenStreetMap lists stations in Warley (7.3 km) and Burntwood (WS7 3XA, 13.9 km) as selling AdBlue at the pump, plus an HGV-only refuelling site in Birmingham (B25 8DW) at 17.9 km that is meant for lorries. The map data is incomplete.

name: Darlington
intro: A market town in County Durham, Darlington lies on the River Skerne 13 miles (21 km) west of Middlesbrough and 17 miles (27 km) south of Durham. It had 107,800 people at the 2021 Census, making it one of the largest settlements in North East England. The town is linked to London, Leeds, York, Newcastle and Edinburgh by the East Coast Main Line and by the A1(M), and that motorway matters to anyone driving a diesel van or car here. The A1(M) and A66(M) both appear in the main road list, along with the A66, A67, A68, A167 and A1150, and all three of the nearest listed service areas are on the A1(M). Postcode districts include DL1, DL2 and DL3. Newton Aycliffe is 10.3km away and Egglescliffe 12.8km, with Stockton-on-Tees and Ingleby Barwick both at 15.5km.
roadsText: Two motorways, the A66(M) and A1(M), appear on Darlington's road list with the A68, A66, A167, A67 and A1150. The nearest listed service areas are all on the A1(M): Forest Park Services at 6.4km, Barton Truckstop at 9.8km and Scotch Corner Services at 11.8km. A station at Richmond (DL10 6PB), 13km away, is listed as selling AdBlue at the pump in OpenStreetMap, but that data is incomplete and other stations may stock it.

name: Dartford
intro: Where the old road from London to Dover crossed the River Darent, Dartford's town centre sits in the valley; today the main through-road by-passes the town itself. The principal town in the Borough of Dartford lies 18 miles (29 km) south-east of Central London, next to the London Borough of Bexley, with Thurrock in Essex across the Thames Estuary to the north, reached via the Dartford Crossing. It is principally a commuter town for Greater London and an important rail hub. Postcode districts are DA1, DA2 and DA9. The M25, A282, A2 and A13 are among the listed roads. Swanscombe is 4.6 km away and Bexley 6.6 km. For a driver with an AdBlue warning, the nearest listed service area is just 5.7 km off on the M25.
roadsText: Dartford's road list takes in the M25, A282, A2, A13, A226, A296, A206 and A225. Thurrock Services on the M25 is the nearest listed service area at 5.7 km, with Tollgate Services on the A2 at 9.2 km and Orsett Cock Services on the A13 at 13.3 km. In OpenStreetMap, three stations are listed as selling AdBlue at the pump: one about 15.5 km away, another at 16.9 km and one in Strood (ME2 2NY, 18.3 km). That data is incomplete.

name: Darton
intro: A large village on the border between South and West Yorkshire, Darton belongs to the Metropolitan Borough of Barnsley. It had 14,927 residents at the 2001 census, and the two Darton wards (East and West) together recorded 21,345 in 2011. Postcodes fall within S75. Royston is about 4.3 km away, Barnsley 4.6 km and Cudworth and Shafton 6.7 km, with Wombwell, Wakefield and Hoyland all between 10.4 km and 10.8 km. For drivers, the most useful fact about Darton is how close the M1 services are. Woolley Edge Services is about 4.2 km away in a straight line, making it the obvious first stop for a van or diesel car showing an AdBlue warning. The next service area, Exelby Services Whitwood on the M62, is around 15.7 km off.
roadsText: Woolley Edge Services on the M1 is the nearest service area to Darton, roughly 4.2 km in a straight line. Exelby Services Whitwood on the M62 (15.7 km) and Barnsdale Bar Services on the A1 (18.9 km) are further out. OpenStreetMap lists a station in Pontefract (WF7 7HX), about 13.5 km away, as selling AdBlue at the pump. Its records are incomplete, so other sellers may be closer.

name: Darwen
intro: The A666 passes through Darwen on its way between Blackburn to the north and Bolton to the south, continuing to Pendlebury, where it joins the A6. Darwen itself is a market town and civil parish in the Blackburn with Darwen borough of Lancashire, about 18 miles north-west of Manchester, and had 28,046 residents at the 2011 census. The River Darwen flows south to north through the town and can be seen in the town centre parks, and residents are known as Darreners. Its postcode district is BB3. Blackburn is 5.6 km away and Oswaldtwistle 6.6 km. The M65 is the motorway listed for the area. For drivers with an AdBlue warning, the standout fact is that Blackburn with Darwen Services on the M65 is just 1.9 km from the town.
roadsText: Around Darwen, the listed roads are the M65 and A666, with the A6077, A6078, A678, A6062, A675 and A674. Blackburn with Darwen Services on the M65 is 1.9 km away. Rivington Services on the M61 is 12.9 km off and Charnock Richard Services on the M6 is 16.6 km. Accrington is 9.1 km away and Haslingden 9.3 km.

name: Davenham
intro: With 2,745 residents at the 2011 census, Davenham is a village in the centre of the Cheshire Plain, close to both the River Dane and the River Weaver. It belongs to the Borough of Cheshire West and Chester. Its postcode district is CW9. Northwich is only 2.7 km away and Winsford 5.3 km off, so both are a short drive. Middlewich is 7.2 km away, Knutsford 12.1 km and Sandbach 14.3 km. For a driver with an AdBlue warning, there are three service areas between 8.1 km and 10.4 km away: Whitley Services on the A49, and Knutsford Services and Tabley Hill Service Station, both on the M6.
roadsText: Whitley Services on the A49 is the nearest service area to Davenham at 8.1 km. Knutsford Services and Tabley Hill Service Station, both on the M6, are each 10.4 km away, so all three options sit within a similar distance of the village. Northwich (2.7 km), Winsford (5.3 km) and Middlewich (7.2 km) are the closest towns.

name: Daventry
intro: Close to Northamptonshire's border with Warwickshire, Daventry is a market town in West Northamptonshire. Its 2021 census population of 28,123 makes it the sixth-largest town in the county, and its postcode district is NN11. Main roads include the M1, A5, A45, A361, A425 and A4256. The town is some distance from its neighbours: Rugby is about 13.7 km away, Northampton 18.7 km and Towcester 19.4 km, while Lutterworth, Royal Leamington Spa and Banbury are all more than 22 km away. Watford Gap Services on the M1 is the nearest service area at about 5.8 km, and two truck stops on the M1 and A5 are within about 13.3 km. For a van or diesel car with an AdBlue warning, that spread means a service area is often closer than the next town.
roadsText: Daventry's main roads are the M1, A5, A45, A361, A425 and A4256. Watford Gap Services on the M1 is the nearest service area, about 5.8 km away. Red Lion Truckstop on the M1 is around 11.6 km away, and Rugby Truck Stop on the A5 about 13.3 km.

name: Dawlish
intro: Once a small fishing port, Dawlish grew into a seaside resort in the 18th century, and its near neighbour Teignmouth, 4.3 km away, followed the same path in the 19th. The town is on the south coast of Devon in the Teignbridge district, 12 miles (19 km) south of Exeter and a similar distance from Torquay. It grew quickly between the last two censuses: the 2021 count recorded 15,257 people, 16% more than the 13,161 counted in 2011. The EX7 postcode district covers it. Kingsteignton is 10 km away, Torquay 12.1 km and Newton Abbot 12.6 km. For a van or diesel car with an AdBlue warning, the nearest listed service area is Moto Exeter Services on the M5, 14 km away in a straight line, and the next listed sites are more than twice as far.
roadsText: Moto Exeter Services on the M5 is the closest service area to Dawlish, 14 km away in a straight line. The other two listed are much further: ExtraMSA Cullompton Services at 31 km and Moto Tiverton Services at 37.2 km, both on the M5. Road distances from the coast will be longer than these figures, so plan the route before heading off with a warning showing.

name: Deal
intro: Where the North Sea meets the English Channel, Deal is a coastal town in Kent, 8 miles north-east of Dover and 8 miles south of Ramsgate. It is a former fishing, mining and garrison town that became a limb port of the Cinque Ports in 1278 and grew into the busiest port in England. Today it is a seaside resort, with Walmer close by, and its postcode district is CT14. Only two roads appear on the list, the A256 and A258. Dover is 11.4km away and Ramsgate 13.8km, with Canterbury at 22.5km and Folkestone at 22.9km.
