With no motorway on the road list and the nearest service area 8.9km away, driving from Deal is mostly A-road work to neighbouring towns.
roadsText: Just two main roads are listed around Deal, the A256 and A258. The nearest service area is Whitfield Services on the A2, about 8.9km away. Minster Services on the A299 is 15km and Folkestone Services on the M20 is 27.5km. For a driver with an AdBlue warning, Whitfield is the closest of the three to town.

name: Denton
intro: East of Gorton and 5 miles from Manchester city centre, Denton is a town in Tameside, Greater Manchester. It was historically part of Lancashire and had a population of 36,591 at the 2011 Census. Its postcode districts are M34, SK5, SK16 and M18. Neighbours are packed in close: Audenshaw is 2.6 km away, Reddish 2.8 km, Bredbury and Woodley 3 km, Hyde 3.1 km and Dukinfield 3.3 km, with Droylsden at 4.2 km. The M67 and M60 are both listed among the roads around Denton, along with the A57, A6017 and A635. For a driver with an AdBlue warning, note that the service areas are much further out than the neighbouring towns; the nearest is 14.9 km away.
roadsText: The M67 and M60 are listed for Denton, along with the A6017, A57, A627, A6140, A560 and A635. Service areas are further away: Birch Services on the M62 is 14.9 km off, and Knutsford Services and Tabley Hill Service Station, both on the M6, are 25.2 km and 25.3 km. OpenStreetMap lists one station 7.7 km away and one in Manchester (M25 3AJ), 14.8 km away, as selling AdBlue at the pump. That list will not be complete.

name: Derby
intro: On the River Derwent in Derbyshire, Derby is a city and unitary authority with a population of 275,344 in 2025. It began as a market town, grew rapidly in the industrial era and became a centre of the British rail industry after the railways arrived in the 19th century, though city status only came in 1977. Main roads here include the A38, A50, A52, A6, A61 and A516, and postcode districts include DE1, DE3, DE21, DE22, DE23 and DE24, with DE72 and DE73 also on the list. The nearest towns are all at least 12 km away: Ilkeston at about 12 km, Long Eaton 12.2 km, Belper 12.6 km and Heanor 14.1 km. The two closest service areas, both on the A50, are a little over 8 km out.
roadsText: Main roads around Derby are the A6, A38, A50, A52, A61, A514, A516 and A5111. The two closest service areas are both on the A50: Welcome Break Derby South Services at about 8.2 km and ExtraMSA Derby with Burton Services at 8.4 km. Trowell Services on the M1 is the next nearest, around 14.4 km away.

name: Dereham
intro: Historically known as East Dereham, this Breckland town lies on the A47 about 15 miles (24 km) west of Norwich and 25 miles (40 km) east of King's Lynn. It is the administrative centre for Breckland District Council, has a population of 20,788 and is covered by the NR19 postcode district. It should not be confused with the village of West Dereham, some 25 miles away. Service areas are a long way off: the nearest listed is Thickthorn Services on the A11, 20.5 km away in a straight line, and the next is 38.5 km away on the A47. A driver with an AdBlue warning should keep that gap in mind. Watton is the nearest town at 14.1 km, followed by Wymondham at 16.5 km, Taverham and Drayton at 18.1 km and Attleborough at 18.9 km.
roadsText: Dereham sits on the A47. The nearest service areas are Thickthorn Services on the A11, 20.5 km away in a straight line, Freebridge Park on the A47 at 38.5 km, and Beacon Hill Services on the A140 at 59.5 km. With that much distance involved, plan any stop for an AdBlue problem rather than assuming a services is close by.

name: Derry
intro: Derry, officially Londonderry, covers both banks of the River Foyle. Cityside and the old walled city are on the west bank and Waterside is on the east, linked by two road bridges and a footbridge. With 85,279 people at the 2021 census, it is the second-largest city in Northern Ireland after Belfast. The wider district includes Londonderry Port and City of Derry Airport, and the city sits close to the border with County Donegal. Postcode districts BT47 and BT48 cover Derry. Other towns are some way off: Strabane is 21.9 km away and Limavady 23.6 km, with Coleraine at 43.6 km. That distance matters with an AdBlue warning, because the nearest listed service area is 41.2 km away on the A6.
roadsText: Roads listed for Derry are the A2, A6, A5, A514, A515 and A40. The nearest service area is Glenshane Tourist Services on the A6, 41.2 km away. Beyond that, Cohannon Services on the M1 is 69.3 km off and the northbound services at Temple Patrick on the M2 are 89.3 km away, so it is worth planning a stop well before a long run.

name: Desborough
intro: In the Ise Valley between Market Harborough and Kettering, Desborough is a North Northamptonshire town with a population of 11,899. It was an industrial centre for weaving and shoe-making in the 19th century and had a long association with the Co-operative movement. The postcode district is NN14. Its two nearest neighbours are almost equally close, with Market Harborough 7.9 km away and Kettering 8.4 km, while Corby is 10.4 km off and Burton Latimer 13 km. For drivers, the A14 is close at hand: Rothwell Truck Stop, on the A14, is just 3.4 km from Desborough. That gives van and diesel car drivers a nearby place to stop if an AdBlue warning appears.
roadsText: Rothwell Truck Stop on the A14 is 3.4 km from Desborough, the nearest stop by some distance. Welford Truck Stop, also on the A14, is 15.1 km away, and Morcott Services on the A47 is 20.6 km away. Both of the A14 sites are truck stops rather than motorway service areas, and Rothwell is the only listed stop within 15 km of the town.

name: Devizes
intro: An 11th-century Norman castle was the starting point for Devizes, which grew up around it and received a charter in 1141. A market town and civil parish in Wiltshire, it later became known for textiles, and by the early 18th century it held the largest corn market in the West Country, building its Corn Exchange in 1857. Today it has a population of 19,491 and is covered by the SN10 postcode district. Calne is 9.6 km away and Melksham 10.5 km, with Trowbridge, Chippenham, Corsham and Westbury all between 15.1 km and 17.3 km. Devizes is some way from the listed service areas, which matters if an AdBlue warning appears. The nearest, Chippenham Pit Stop on the M4 and Warminster Services on the A350, are 20 km and 21 km away in a straight line.
roadsText: Listed service areas are not close to Devizes. The nearest listed sites are all about 20 km away in a straight line: Chippenham Pit Stop on the M4 at 20 km, Warminster Services on the A350 at 21 km and Leigh Delamere Services, also on the M4, at 21.4 km. With options on both the M4 and the A350, a driver in SN10 can choose by direction of travel, but road distances will be longer than these figures.

name: Dewsbury
intro: Batley is 3.8 km from Dewsbury on a direct line, Heckmondwike and Ossett are 3.9 km each, Mirfield 4.3 km and Liversedge 5.1 km, so other towns are very close. Dewsbury itself is the largest town in the Heavy Woollen District and lies on the River Calder in the Kirklees borough of West Yorkshire, west of Wakefield, east of Huddersfield and south of Leeds. It saw major growth as a mill town in the 19th century before a period of decline, and its built-up area had 63,722 residents at the 2021 Census. The postcode districts run across WF5, WF12, WF13, WF16 and WF17. Both the M1 and the M62 appear among the main roads, so a vehicle with an AdBlue warning here is close to two motorways, with a service area on each within 9 km.
roadsText: Main roads around Dewsbury include the M1 and M62, with the A638, A644, A642, A637, A653 and A652. Hartshead Moor services on the M62 is 8 km away on a direct line and Woolley Edge services on the M1 is 9 km, while Skelton Lake Service Station on the M1 is 14.5 km. OpenStreetMap lists a station with a Leeds address, 14.6 km away, as selling AdBlue at the pump, though its data is incomplete.

name: Didcot
intro: Didcot is a railway town in South Oxfordshire, 15 miles south of Oxford, 10 miles east of Wantage and 15 miles north-west of Reading. Historically part of Berkshire, it is noted for its railway heritage, with Didcot station opening as a junction on the Great Western Main Line in 1844. Today it is known as the gateway to the Science Vale, with large science and technology centres in the nearby villages of Milton, Culham and Harwell. The town falls in the OX11 postcode district, and 34,600 people live there. Main roads listed are the A34, A4130, A417, A4185 and A415. Abingdon-on-Thames is 7.7km away and Wantage 12.5km. With no motorway on the road list, most driving here is on the A34 and other A roads, and the nearest service area is 17.5km out.
roadsText: The A34, A4130, A417, A4185 and A415 are the main roads listed around Didcot. None of the nearest service areas is especially close: Oxford Services on the M40 is 17.5km away, Chieveley Services on the M4 is 18.5km and Peartree Services on the A44 is 20.6km. For a driver with an AdBlue warning, that is a fair distance to cover on A roads before reaching one.

name: Dinnington
intro: At about 330 feet (101 m) above sea level, Dinnington is a town in the civil parish of Dinnington St John's, in the Metropolitan Borough of Rotherham, South Yorkshire. Historically part of the West Riding of Yorkshire, it is the principal settlement in a parish that also includes the small hamlets of Throapham and St John's. The wider St John's ward, which adds Laughton-en-le-Morthen, Firbeck, Letwell and Gildingwells, had 12,517 people at the 2011 Census. The town is covered by the S25 postcode district and lies near Worksop and Rotherham and the cities of Sheffield and Doncaster. Maltby is the closest town at 6 km, Worksop is 9 km away and Rotherham 11.3 km. Drivers with an AdBlue warning have two motorways within reach: the M1 has service areas at 7.8 km and 9.8 km, and the A1(M) has one at 10.2 km.
roadsText: Two M1 service areas are closest to Dinnington: Woodall Services at 7.8 km and Rotherham Services at 9.8 km, both measured in a straight line. Blyth Services on the A1(M) is 10.2 km away. A station in Doncaster (DN4 0TP), 14.6 km from the town, is listed in OpenStreetMap as selling AdBlue at the pump, but that mapping is incomplete and closer stations may also sell it.

name: Doncaster
intro: Named after the River Don, Doncaster sits in the Don Valley on the western edge of the Humberhead Levels, east of the Pennines. It was granted city status under the Platinum Jubilee Civic Honours, with a ceremony in November 2022, and is the second largest settlement in South Yorkshire, with 87,455 people at the 2021 census, 160,220 in its built-up area and 308,100 across the wider borough. It is linked by road and rail to Barnsley, Wakefield, Pontefract, Selby, Goole, Scunthorpe, Gainsborough, Retford, Worksop and Rotherham. For a van with an AdBlue problem, the motorway connections stand out: the M18 and A1(M) are listed among the main roads. The DN1, DN2 and DN4 postcode districts apply, and neighbouring places come quickly, with Bentley 3.8 km away on a direct line, Armthorpe 4.6 km and New Rossington and Rossington 5.2 km.
roadsText: Main roads around Doncaster include the M18 and A1(M), along with the A638, A18, A6182, A630, A19 and A635. On a direct line, the nearest service areas are Doncaster North on the M180 (11.5 km), Blyth on the A1(M) (14.4 km) and Barnsdale Bar on the A1 (15.2 km). OpenStreetMap lists a station with a Doncaster address, 4.5 km from the centre, as selling AdBlue at the pump. That data is incomplete, so other forecourts may also stock it.

name: Dorchester
intro: Dorset's county town sits on the A35 trunk route between Poole and Bridport. Dorchester is a historic market town on the banks of the River Frome, south of the Dorset Downs and north of the South Dorset Ridgeway, which separates it from Weymouth. The civil parish, which includes Poundbury and the suburb of Fordington, had 21,358 residents in 2021, and the town falls in the DT1 postcode district. Weymouth is the nearest neighbouring town at 8.6 km, while Bridport is 22.2 km away and Blandford Forum 26 km. The Romans knew the settlement as Durnovaria. Listed service areas are a long way from here. The nearest listed one, Picket Post Services on the A31, is 52.7 km away in a straight line, so an AdBlue warning on a van or diesel car is better dealt with early than driven in search of services.
roadsText: Dorchester sits on the A35 trunk route between Poole and Bridport. The nearest listed service areas are all at least 52.7 km away in a straight line: Picket Post Services on the A31 at 52.7 km, Taunton Deane Services on the M5 at 57.6 km and Bridgwater Services, also on the M5, at 58.5 km. One station about 12 km away is listed on OpenStreetMap as selling AdBlue at the pump; that data is incomplete, so others may exist.

name: Dorking
intro: About 21 miles (34 km) south-west of London, Dorking is a Surrey market town in Mole Valley District, with the council headquarters to the east of the centre. Its High Street runs roughly east to west, parallel to the Pipp Brook, and the town is bordered on three sides by the Surrey Hills National Landscape, with Box Hill and Leith Hill close by. A market is thought to have been held here at least weekly since early medieval times. The town has a population of 17,463 and sits in the RH4 postcode district. Motorway services are not on the doorstep: if a van or diesel car shows an AdBlue warning, the nearest listed service area is Cobham Services on the M25, 10.1 km away in a straight line. Leatherhead (6.5 km), Great Bookham and Fetcham (6.7 km) and Reigate (8.8 km) are the closest neighbouring towns, with Ashtead and Redhill a little further out.
roadsText: Three service areas lie within reach of Dorking. Cobham Services on the M25 is the nearest, 10.1 km away in a straight line, with Wisley Services on the A3 at 13.2 km. Pease Pottage Services on the M23 is further out at 18.5 km. Road distances to each will be longer than these figures, which is worth allowing for when an AdBlue warning has already appeared.

name: Dover
intro: Facing France across the Strait of Dover, the narrowest part of the English Channel, Dover is a major ferry port and the administrative centre of the Dover District in Kent. The Port of Dover provides much of the town's employment, alongside tourism. The town takes its name from the River Dour, which flows through it, and lies south-east of Canterbury and east of Maidstone. Its postcode districts are CT16 and CT17. Main roads listed for Dover are the A2, A20, A256 and A258, with no motorway in the list. Deal is 11.4km away and Folkestone 12.8km, with Canterbury at 22.8km. For drivers around the port or heading out of town, that means A roads, with the nearest service area very close to town.
roadsText: Around Dover, the main roads listed are the A256, A20, A2 and A258. Whitfield Services on the A2 is only 2.6km away, making it the nearest place to stop. Folkestone Services on the M20 is 18.5km and Minster Services on the A299 is 24km. For anyone leaving town on the A2 with an AdBlue warning, Whitfield is the closest option by a wide margin.

name: Downham Market
intro: Sometimes simply called Downham, this market town sits on the edge of the Fens and on the River Great Ouse. It grew as an agricultural centre and a market for Fenland produce, with a bridge across the river. The town lies about 11 miles (18 km) south of King's Lynn, 30 miles (48 km) north of Cambridge and 39 miles (63 km) west of Norwich, in the King's Lynn and West Norfolk district. It has a population of 11,349 and is covered by the PE38 postcode district. Wisbech is 16.2 km away and King's Lynn 17.7 km. If an AdBlue warning appears, Freebridge Park on the A47 is the nearest listed service area at 15.4 km in a straight line; the next two are both more than 40 km off.
roadsText: Freebridge Park on the A47 is the nearest service area to Downham Market, 15.4 km away in a straight line. The next two are much further: Springfield Services on the A151 at 40.1 km and Lincs Gateway Services on the A16 at 40.2 km. For drivers in PE38, the A47 site is the only one of the three within about 20 km.

name: Downpatrick
intro: Downpatrick stands on the Lecale peninsula, about 21 mi (34 km) south of Belfast, and is the county town of Down and joint headquarters of Newry, Mourne and Down District Council. It had 11,545 residents at the 2021 census. The town's history runs deep: in the Middle Ages it was the capital of the Dál Fiatach, and its cathedral is said to be the burial place of Saint Patrick. For driving, the main point is that Downpatrick sits some way from other towns. Castlereagh and Newtownards are each about 29.4 km away in a straight line, and Lisburn is 30 km, with Holywood and Banbridge more than 35 km off. Postcode district BT30 covers the town. The nearest service area is about 28.8 km away on the M1, so an AdBlue warning here means a drive before reaching one.
roadsText: Lisburn Services on the M1 is the nearest service area to Downpatrick, about 28.8 km away in a straight line. Temple Patrick Services Northbound on the M2 is about 45.2 km away and Cohannon Services on the M1 about 64 km. From the Lecale peninsula, all three involve a fair drive, and the road distance will be longer than these figures.

name: Driffield
intro: Known as the Capital of the Wolds because it lies near the centre of the Yorkshire Wolds, Driffield (also called Great Driffield) is a market town in the East Riding of Yorkshire. The civil parish covers the town and the village of Little Driffield and had 13,457 residents at the 2021 census. By road it is 23 miles (37 km) north of Hull, 29 miles (47 km) east of York and 53 miles (85 km) north-east of Leeds. The town uses the YO25 postcode district. Bridlington is about 17.8 km away, Beverley 18.2 km and Pocklington 24.1 km. For a driver with an AdBlue warning, service areas are distant: the nearest listed, Ulceby Truckstop on the A160, is about 43.8 km in a straight line, with Bilbrough Top on the A64 at 50.3 km.
roadsText: Service areas are a long way from Driffield. The nearest listed are Ulceby Truckstop on the A160 at about 43.8 km in a straight line, Bilbrough Top Service Area on the A64 at 50.3 km and Doncaster (North) Services on the M180 at 58.8 km. With every option more than 43 km off, and road distances longer still, it pays to know these figures before a long run.

name: Droitwich Spa
intro: Often shortened to Droitwich, this historic spa town on the River Salwarpe lies in the Wychavon district of northern Worcestershire, approximately 7 miles (11 km) north-east of Worcester and 22 miles (35 km) south-west of Birmingham. The parish had 25,027 residents in 2021. It sits on massive deposits of salt that have been extracted since ancient times, and the town was called Salinae in the Roman period. The M5 is among the main roads around Droitwich, along with the A38 and A449, so motorway driving is close at hand. Even so, none of the nearest service areas is especially close, with the first one 18.1 km away in a straight line, which is worth knowing before an AdBlue warning turns into a bigger problem. Worcester is the nearest neighbouring town at 8.2 km, with Bromsgrove at 10.1 km and Stourport-on-Severn at 12.4 km. The postcode district is WR9.
roadsText: Main roads around Droitwich Spa include the M5, A38, A4538, A449, A4133, A442, A4536 and A4440. Although the M5 is close, the nearest service areas are Hopwood Park on the M42 (18.1 km in a straight line), Frankley on the M5 (20.7 km) and Strensham on the M5 (22.3 km). OpenStreetMap lists one station 13.6 km away as selling AdBlue at the pump; coverage in that data is incomplete, so it may not be the only option.

name: Dronfield
intro: Between Chesterfield and Sheffield, in the valley of the River Drone, Dronfield is a North East Derbyshire town that also takes in Dronfield Woodhouse and Coal Aston. Its population was 21,261 at the 2011 census and its postcode district is S18. Both of its larger neighbours are close, with Chesterfield 7.2 km away and Sheffield 7.9 km, while Brimington is 7 km away and Staveley 8.3 km. The Peak District National Park lies three miles to the west. Manufacturing firms still operate in the town, which has a history of coal mining, steel and engineering. For a van or diesel car with an AdBlue warning, the nearest listed service area is Sheffield Service Area, 8.7 km away, with two M1 services a little further out.
roadsText: The nearest service area to Dronfield is Sheffield Service Area on the A6102, 8.7 km away. The M1 has two options a little further out: Welcome Break Woodall Services at 12.4 km and Rotherham Services at 13 km. All three are within 13 km of the town, which gives a choice of stops on the A6102 and the motorway if a warning light comes on.

name: Droylsden
intro: Just 6.4 km east of Manchester city centre, Droylsden is a town in Tameside that grew as a mill town on the Ashton canal in the mid-19th century. From the early 1930s its population expanded quickly as it became a housing overflow area for Manchester, and the 2011 census recorded 22,689 people. The Fairfield area has been home to a Moravian Church since 1785. Droylsden covers the M43 and M11 postcode districts. It is tightly surrounded by other places: Audenshaw is 1.8 km away, Failsworth 2.4 km, Ashton-under-Lyne and Manchester both 4.1 km, Denton 4.2 km and Dukinfield 4.4 km. The road network around it includes the M60 and M67 motorways, the A57(M) and the A635, A6140, A6017, A62 and A663. That makes for a lot of short urban journeys, with motorways close at hand.
roadsText: Around Droylsden the main roads are the M60, M67 and A57(M), plus the A635, A6140, A6017, A62 and A663. Birch services on the M62 is 10.8 km away; the next, Tabley Hill and Knutsford on the M6, are both about 26 km out. A station 3.9 km away and one in Manchester at 10.9 km are listed in OpenStreetMap as selling AdBlue at the pump. That data is incomplete.

name: Dudley
intro: Long known informally as the capital of the Black Country, a title the borough council adopted in a 2014 slogan, Dudley is a market town 6 miles (9.7km) south-east of Wolverhampton and 8 miles north-west of Birmingham. It is the administrative centre of the Metropolitan Borough of Dudley and had 79,379 residents at the 2011 census. Historically in Worcestershire, it was one of the birthplaces of the Industrial Revolution. Tourist attractions include Dudley Zoo and Castle and the Black Country Living Museum. Postcodes include DY1 to DY5 and B64. Listed roads are the M5, A461, A4036, A4123, A463, A458, A41 and A491. Rowley Regis, Coseley, Sedgley, Brierley Hill and Cradley Heath are all within about 4km, so local driving is a tight network of short urban trips. The nearest motorway services are about 9.8km away.
roadsText: OpenStreetMap lists a forecourt in Warley, about 3.9km from Dudley, as selling AdBlue at the pump. It also lists an HGV-only site in Birmingham (17.7km) and a forecourt at DY10 1JS (18.2km), though the data is incomplete. For service areas, Frankley on the M5 is about 9.8km away, Hilton Park on the M6 15.6km and Hopwood Park on the M42 18.5km. Listed roads are the M5, A461, A4036, A4123, A463, A458, A41 and A491.

name: Dukinfield
intro: On the south bank of the river Tame, opposite Ashton-under-Lyne, Dukinfield is a Tameside town about 6.3 miles (10.1 km) east of Manchester. It sat within the historic county boundaries of Cheshire until it became part of Greater Manchester in 1974, and it grew during the Industrial Revolution as a site of coal mining and cotton manufacturing. The 2021 census counted 21,155 people in the built-up area. Postcode districts SK16, OL6 and OL7 all cover parts of the town. The neighbouring towns are tightly packed: Ashton-under-Lyne is only about 2.4 km away, Hyde 2.6 km, Audenshaw 2.9 km and Stalybridge 3.2 km, with Denton at 3.3 km and Droylsden at 4.4 km. For a van or diesel car showing an AdBlue warning, trips between these Tameside towns are short, while the nearest motorway services are a much longer drive away.
roadsText: The nearest motorway service area to Dukinfield is Birch Services on the M62, about 14.1 km away. Knutsford Services and Tabley Hill Service Station, both on the M6, are much further at around 28.5 km and 28.6 km. OpenStreetMap has a site roughly 6.3 km away listed as selling AdBlue at the pump, plus another under Manchester at about 15.1 km. Its records are incomplete, so other local stations may stock it too.

name: Dumbarton
intro: Where the River Leven flows into the Clyde estuary, on the north bank of the River Clyde, Dumbarton is a West Dunbartonshire town with an estimated 19,990 people in 2006. It was the capital of the ancient Kingdom of Strathclyde and later the county town of Dunbartonshire, and Dumbarton Castle on Dumbarton Rock still dominates the area. Shipbuilding, glassmaking and whisky production have declined, and the town is increasingly a commuter town for Glasgow, 13 miles (21 km) to the east-south-east. Postcode district G82 covers the town. In a straight line, Port Glasgow is about 7.1 km away and Erskine 8.6 km, with Clydebank at 10.5 km and Helensburgh at 12.2 km. A station about 1.1 km away is listed as selling AdBlue at the pump, while the nearest service areas are more than 34 km off.
roadsText: Service areas are a long way from Dumbarton: Bothwell Services on the M74 is about 34.6 km away in a straight line, Hamilton Services on the M74 about 37.4 km and Stirling Services on the M9 about 42.3 km. Much closer, OpenStreetMap lists a station about 1.1 km away, and another in Glasgow (G11 6DN) about 17.9 km away, as selling AdBlue at the pump. That data is incomplete.

name: Dumfries
intro: Near the mouth of the River Nith on the Solway Firth, Dumfries is a market town and former royal burgh about 40 km from the Anglo-Scottish border. It is the county town of the historic county of Dumfriesshire, within Dumfries and Galloway, and is nicknamed the Queen of the South. The DG1 and DG2 postcode districts cover the town, which has a listed population of 33,470. What stands out for drivers is distance: the nearest of the listed towns is Carlisle, 46.9 km away, followed by Workington (48 km) and Whitehaven (59.1 km). Main roads recorded here are the A75, A76, A701, A709, A711, A756, A780 and A781. With distances like these, and every recorded road an A road, an AdBlue warning is worth acting on early.
roadsText: The A701, A76, A75, A780, A781, A709, A756 and A711 are the main roads recorded around Dumfries. The nearest service areas are all on the A74(M): Annandale Water Services at 21 km, The 'fechan Truckstop at 21.1 km and Gretna Green Services at 34.2 km. That puts every listed service area at least 21 km from the town, so plan a stop before a longer journey.

name: Dunbar
intro: A former royal burgh on the North Sea coast of East Lothian, Dunbar lies approximately 30 miles (48 km) east of Edinburgh and the same distance from the English border north of Berwick-upon-Tweed. Its parish takes in the villages of West Barns and Belhaven, and the town had a population of 10,777 in 2022. Dunbar has a harbour dating from 1574 and is the birthplace of John Muir. The town is in the EH42 postcode district. It is some way from other towns: Haddington is the nearest at 17.1 km, Tranent is 27.6 km away and Musselburgh 33.7 km. A driver with an AdBlue warning here has a real distance to cover before reaching any of the listed services, the closest of which is 23.1 km away on the A1.
roadsText: The closest listed service area to Dunbar is MacMerry on the A1, 23.1 km away. Musselburgh Services, also on the A1, is 34.6 km and Dreghorn Services on the A720 is 45.7 km. Those distances make the A1 stops the ones to know about, and they are worth bearing in mind before a longer run with an AdBlue warning showing.

name: Dundee
intro: Dundee, Scotland's fourth-largest city, lies on the north bank of the Firth of Tay in the eastern central Lowlands, with an estimated 148,210 people in 2020. It sits within the historic county of Angus and forms the Dundee City council area, with postcode districts DD1 to DD6. A master plan to regenerate the Waterfront and reconnect it to the city centre began in 2001 and is expected to run over a 30-year period. The A90 is on the local road list, joined by the A92, A85, A923, A929, A930, A972 and A991. Carnoustie is 15.2 km away, St Andrews 18.5 km and Forfar 19.2 km, with Arbroath at 24.9 km and Perth at 31.3 km. The nearest service area is 17.9 km away, which is worth knowing if an AdBlue warning appears on a local run.
roadsText: Main roads recorded around Dundee include the A90, A972, A92, A929, A991, A923, A930 and A85. The nearest service area is Forfar Services on the A90, 17.9 km away. Stracathro Services, also on the A90, is 39.4 km off, and Kinross Services on the M90 is 41.7 km. With no service area inside the city on this list, plan any stop before a longer run on the A90.

name: Dunfermline
intro: Five kilometres from the northern shore of the Firth of Forth, Dunfermline is a city, parish and former royal burgh in Fife. It was the de facto capital of the Kingdom of Scotland between the 11th and 15th centuries and was awarded city status in 2022 as part of the Platinum Jubilee Civic Honours. The KY11 postcode district covers the city, and its population is listed at 54,990. For drivers, the road list is the useful part: the M90 and A823(M) sit alongside the A92, A823, A907, A985, A994 and A9000. Rosyth is just 3.7 km away and Cowdenbeath and Lumphinnans 6.5 km, while South Queensferry is 9.5 km. Bo'ness (12.6 km) and Linlithgow (14.9 km) are further off. The nearest service area is 15.6 km away on the M90.
roadsText: Main roads recorded around Dunfermline are the M90, A823(M), A92, A985, A9000, A907, A823 and A994. Kinross Services on the M90 is the nearest service area at 15.6 km, with Dreghorn Services on the A720 at 22.6 km and Musselburgh Services on the A1 at 28.1 km. Kinross Services sits on the M90, which also appears on Dunfermline's own road list.

name: Dungannon
intro: Second only to Omagh in the historic county of Tyrone, Dungannon had 16,282 residents at the 2021 census and, since 2015, has shared local government with Magherafelt and Cookstown in Mid-Ulster District Council. It was a linen centre in the 19th century and attracted an extensive food processing industry in the late 20th, and a poultry producer is now the town's largest employer. Its postcode district is BT71. Cookstown is about 15.6 km away and Armagh 18.3 km, while Craigavon is 25.4 km off and Banbridge, Omagh and Antrim are between 35.6 km and 43 km away. A driver with an AdBlue warning here is relatively well placed, as Cohannon Services on the M1 is only about 7 km from the town.
roadsText: Cohannon Services on the M1 is about 7 km from Dungannon in a straight line, much closer than the next options: Glenshane Tourist Services on the A6 at about 38.3 km and Lisburn Services on the M1 at about 49.4 km. OpenStreetMap lists a station in Cookstown (BT80 8QB), about 15.3 km away, as selling AdBlue at the pump. That data is incomplete, so other forecourts may sell it too.

name: Dunscroft and Hatfield
intro: Hatfield, covered here together with Dunscroft, is a town and civil parish in the City of Doncaster in South Yorkshire. It lies on the A18 road between Doncaster and Scunthorpe, to the west of the M18 motorway, and shares a railway station with Stainforth. Recorded history in the parish goes back to 730, when Bede wrote of the Northumbrian king Edwin being killed in battle in the area. Hatfield had 17,236 residents at the 2011 Census, and the area falls in the DN7 postcode district. For a van or diesel car with an AdBlue problem, the standout fact is that Doncaster (North) Services on the M180 is just 2.4 km from the centre in a straight line. Kirk Sandall and Edenthorpe is 4.3 km away, Armthorpe 4.8 km and Thorne 5.4 km, with Doncaster itself 9.1 km off.
roadsText: Hatfield lies on the A18 and to the west of the M18. The nearest service area is Doncaster (North) Services on the M180, 2.4 km away in a straight line, followed by Barnsdale Bar Services on the A1 at 16 km and Blyth Services on the A1(M) at 20.9 km. A station in Doncaster (DN4 0TP), 13.4 km away, is listed in OpenStreetMap as selling AdBlue at the pump; that mapping is incomplete.

name: Dunstable
intro: East of the Chiltern Hills and 30 miles (50 kilometres) north of London, Dunstable is a market town and civil parish in Bedfordshire, and the fourth largest town in the county. There are several steep chalk escarpments around the town, most noticeable to a driver approaching Dunstable from the north. Together with Houghton Regis, only 2.5 km away, Dunstable forms the westernmost part of the Luton/Dunstable urban area, and Luton itself is 7.4 km off. The M1 is among the main roads listed, alongside the A5, A505, A5183, A5505, A5065 and A5228, so a van or diesel car with an AdBlue warning has motorway access close by. Leighton Buzzard is 9.8 km away, Tring 13.1 km, Flitwick 13.5 km and Berkhamsted 14 km. Postcode districts are LU5 and LU6, and the population is 34,498.
roadsText: The M1 is listed for Dunstable along with the A5, A505, A5183, A5505, A5065 and A5228. Toddington Services on the M1 is the nearest service area, 7.2 km away. Bourne End Services on the A41 is 16 km off, and Crawley Crossing Truck Stop, also on the M1, is 16.1 km away.

name: Durham
intro: Built on a meander of the River Wear, which surrounds the centre on three sides, Durham is a cathedral city and the county town of County Durham, home to the headquarters of Durham County Council. Its built-up area had 50,510 residents at the 2021 Census. The land around the city is hilly, except along the flood plain of the Wear to the north and south-east. Durham Cathedral and Durham Castle together form a UNESCO World Heritage Site. The city was founded in 995 by Anglo-Saxon monks. The road list for the city takes in the A1(M), A167, A177, A181, A688, A690 and A691, and its postcode districts include DH1. Chester-le-Street is 8.1km away, Spennymoor 8.7km and Houghton-le-Spring 8.9km. A driver whose AdBlue warning comes on near the city has Durham Services on the A1(M) 6.9km away.
roadsText: The A1(M), A691, A690, A167, A688, A181 and A177 are the main roads listed for Durham. Durham Services on the A1(M) is 6.9km away, then Washington Services on the A1(M) at 11.9km and Easington Services on the A19 at 13.9km. A station with the postcode DH6 3LJ, 11.3km away, is listed as selling AdBlue at the pump in OpenStreetMap, whose AdBlue records are incomplete.

name: Ealing
intro: Acton, Ealing, Greenford, Hanwell, Northolt, Perivale and Southall make up the London Borough of Ealing, the third most populous London borough with 385,985 inhabitants in 2024. It covers part of west London and a small part of north-west London, bridging Inner and Outer London, and its administrative centre is Ealing Broadway. Known as the Queen of the Suburbs for its many parks and tree-lined streets, the borough also has 330 hectares designated as Green Belt. Neighbouring boroughs, clockwise from the north, are Harrow, Brent, Hammersmith and Fulham, Hounslow and Hillingdon. Main roads listed for the borough are the M4, A40, A312, A406, A4, A205, A4127 and A4020. The M4 is among them, and for a driver with an AdBlue warning, Heston Services on the M4 is only 5 km away. Postcode districts listed include W5, W7, W13, UB1, UB2, UB5 and UB6.
roadsText: The M4, A40, A312, A406 and A4 are listed for Ealing, along with the A205, A4127 and A4020. Heston Services on the M4 is the closest service area, 5 km away. London Gateway Services on the M1 is 13.3 km off, and South Mimms Services on the A1(M) is 20.2 km away.

name: Earl Shilton
intro: Known locally as 'ill Shilton', Earl Shilton is a market town in Leicestershire's Hinckley and Bosworth district, about 5 miles from Hinckley and about 10 miles from Leicester. It had 10,047 residents at the 2011 census and its postcode district is LE9. Hinckley is the closest town at 5.2 km, with Enderby and Narborough 7.8 km away, Leicester Forest East and Kirby Muxloe 8.7 km and Blaby and Whetstone 10 km. Nuneaton is 10.7 km off and Lutterworth 13.6 km. For a van or diesel car with an AdBlue warning, the nearest service area is Leicester Forest East Services on the M1, 9.2 km from the town, and two stations listed as selling AdBlue at the pump are 17.8 km and 20 km away.
roadsText: Leicester Forest East Services on the M1 is 9.2 km from Earl Shilton and is the closest service area. ExtraMSA Leicester Services on the A6 is 18.4 km away and Rugby Services on the M6 18.7 km. Two stations, one 17.8 km away and one in Swadlincote (DE12 8AA) at 20 km, are listed on OpenStreetMap as selling AdBlue at the pump. OpenStreetMap does not record every station, so closer forecourts may also sell it.

name: East Ardsley
intro: Part of the City of Leeds metropolitan borough, East Ardsley is a West Yorkshire village that forms part of the Heavy Woollen District and sits within the Rhubarb Triangle. It has a population of 15,238 and falls in the WF3 postcode district. Several towns are close by: Morley is 3.8 km away, Rothwell 5 km, Ossett 5.3 km and Wakefield 5.5 km, with Batley at 5.8 km and Dewsbury at 7 km. That puts East Ardsley among a cluster of West Yorkshire towns rather than out on its own. For a driver whose van or diesel car shows an AdBlue warning, the M1 and the M62 each have a service area within 10 km of the centre, measured in a straight line, and a station in Leeds, 7.6 km away, is listed in OpenStreetMap as selling AdBlue at the pump.
roadsText: The three nearest service areas to East Ardsley, measured in a straight line, are Skelton Lake Service Station on the M1 at 7.5 km, the Whitwood service area on the M62 at 10 km and Woolley Edge Services on the M1 at 11.6 km. OpenStreetMap lists a station in Leeds (LS9 0AS), 7.6 km away, and another in Pontefract (WF7 7HX), 16.8 km away, as selling AdBlue at the pump. Coverage in that data is incomplete.

name: East Grinstead
intro: In the north-east corner of West Sussex, close to where the county meets East Sussex, Surrey and Kent, East Grinstead lies 43 km south of London and 34 km north of Brighton. It is part of the Mid Sussex district, though it was in East Sussex until 1974, and it runs straight into the village of Felbridge to the north-west. The whole town falls within the RH19 postcode district, and the 2011 Census counted 26,383 residents. The Weald and Ashdown Forest lie to the south-east. Horley and Crawley, both to the west, are 11.6 km and 11.7 km away, Oxted is 13.2 km, and Crowborough is 14.9 km, with Haywards Heath at 15.2 km. The A22 and A264 are the main roads through the area, and with the nearest motorway services 13.8 km away on the M23, a diesel driver with a warning light is more likely to be dealing with it on A roads than on a motorway.
roadsText: East Grinstead's main roads are the A22 and A264. The nearest service areas listed are Pease Pottage on the M23, 13.8 km away, Handcross on the A23 at 15.3 km, and Clacket Lane on the M25 at 16.5 km. All three are a fair drive from the centre, so they are worth knowing about before setting off on a longer run.

name: East Kilbride
intro: Scotland's first new town, designated in 1947, East Kilbride (often just EK) is now the largest town in South Lanarkshire, with 76,607 people in 2022. It stands on a raised plateau south of the Cathkin Braes, about thirteen kilometres southeast of Glasgow and close to the boundary with East Renfrewshire. The town ends close to the White Cart Water to the west and is bounded by the Rotten Calder Water to the east, while The Village, the part that existed before the post-war expansion, lies just north of the modern town centre. Postcode districts G74 and G75 cover the town. The A725, A726, A727, A730 and A749 are the main roads recorded here. Cambuslang (6.6 km), Blantyre and Rutherglen (both 6.8 km) and Hamilton (8 km) are the nearest neighbours, and two M74 service areas are 9.9 km away.
roadsText: The A726, A725, A749, A727 and A730 are the main roads recorded around East Kilbride. Two service areas on the M74 are each about 9.9 km away, Bothwell Services and Hamilton Services, with the M74 Truck Stop further out at 22.1 km. OpenStreetMap lists a station in Glasgow (G11 6DN), 14.5 km away, as selling AdBlue at the pump. That list is incomplete, so nearer options may exist.

name: Eastbourne
intro: Immediately east of Beachy Head, the highest chalk sea cliff in Great Britain, Eastbourne is a seaside resort and borough in East Sussex, 19 miles (31 km) east of Brighton and 54 miles (87 km) south of London. Its seafront consists mainly of Victorian hotels, a pier and a theatre, and the town derives a large and increasing income from tourism. Postcode districts covering the town are BN20 to BN24. The roads listed for the area are all A roads, led by the A22, A259 and A27, and no motorway is among them. Polegate is 4.2 km away and Hailsham 8.5 km, with Seaford at 12.1 km and Bexhill-on-Sea at 13.1 km. A driver with an AdBlue warning has one listed service area close by, but the next ones are much further off.
roadsText: In and around Eastbourne, the main roads listed are the A22, A259, A27, A2280, A2290, A2021, A2270 and A2040. Polegate Services on the A22 is the nearest listed service area, 5.4 km away. After that the gap is large: Pyecombe Services on the A23 is 34.2 km and Ricebridge Services (Hickstead), also on the A23, is 38.7 km. Polegate is therefore the listed stop most drivers in Eastbourne will reach first.

name: Eastleigh
intro: Between Southampton and Winchester, Eastleigh is the largest town and administrative seat of the Borough of Eastleigh in Hampshire. It lies on the River Itchen and was made up of villages until the 19th century, when it was developed as a railway town by the London and South Western Railway. Two motorways appear on the road list, the M3 and M27, together with the A335, A27, A35, A33 and A3035. Chandler's Ford is just 3.8km away, West End 4.8km, Hedge End 6.4km and Southampton 6.5km. The SO50 and SO53 postcode districts cover the area. For a van or diesel car with an AdBlue warning, driving here means short hops between neighbouring places, with two motorways on the road list for longer runs.
roadsText: The M3, M27, A335, A27, A35, A33 and A3035 are the main roads listed around Eastleigh. The nearest service area is Rownhams Services on the M27, about 7.8km away. West Wellow Services on the A36 is 13.9km out and Winchester Services on the M3 is 17.3km. Of the three, Rownhams is the closest to town.

name: Eastwood
intro: The Midland Railway was formed in Eastwood, a town and civil parish in Nottinghamshire's Broxtowe district, 9 miles north-west of Nottingham. It appears in the Domesday Book and expanded rapidly during the Industrial Revolution. Today its postcode district is NG16. Other towns are close by: Heanor is only 3.5 km away, Ilkeston 5.8 km and Hucknall 6 km, with Ripley at 7.7 km and Nottingham at 9.3 km. For anyone driving a van or diesel car, the M1 is near, with Trowell Services 6.1 km from the town. That gives a straightforward place to stop if an AdBlue warning comes on while you are heading for the motorway.
roadsText: Trowell Services on the M1 is the nearest service area to Eastwood, at 6.1 km. Trent Bridge Services on the A6011 is 13.2 km away and Tibshelf Services, also on the M1, is 13.8 km away. A station 16.1 km from Eastwood is listed on OpenStreetMap as selling AdBlue at the pump. Map coverage of AdBlue pumps is patchy, so there may be nearer forecourts that sell it.

name: Ebbw Vale
intro: At the head of the valley formed by the Ebbw Fawr, a tributary of the Ebbw River, Ebbw Vale (Glynebwy) is the largest town in Blaenau Gwent and the county borough's administrative centre. The town has a population of 19,635, while the wider Ebbw Vale and Brynmawr conurbation has roughly 33,000 people, and it falls in the NP23 postcode district. It has direct access to the dualled A465 Heads of the Valleys trunk road and borders the Brecon Beacons National Park. Tredegar is only 2.6 km away, with Abertillery at 8.2 km, Merthyr Tydfil at 12.1 km and Abergavenny at 13.9 km. For a van or diesel car with an AdBlue warning, the distances matter: the nearest listed service area is 27.7 km away in a straight line, and the other two are 28.9 km and 30 km off.
roadsText: Ebbw Vale has direct access to the dualled A465 Heads of the Valleys road. The nearest listed service areas are all some way off: Monmouth A40 Services on the A40 at 27.7 km in a straight line, Welcome Break Cardiff Gate Services on the M4 at 28.9 km and Glanusk Services on the A40 at 30 km. Allow for longer distances by road if an AdBlue warning comes on.

name: Eccles
intro: The M602 motorway splits Eccles, a market town in the City of Salford, which lies 3 miles west of Salford city centre and 4 miles west of Manchester. The Manchester Ship Canal runs along its southern border. Eccles grew around the 13th-century Parish Church of St Mary and stayed mainly agricultural until the Industrial Revolution brought a textile industry; the Liverpool and Manchester Railway then pulled the town outwards along its route. Today the M30, M17, M27 and M41 postcode districts cover the area. Neighbouring places are only a short drive away: Worsley is 2.5 km off, Swinton 2.9 km, Urmston 3.6 km and Walkden 4.5 km. Alongside the M602, the M60, M62 and M61 are listed among the roads nearby. For a driver dealing with an AdBlue warning, that means motorway access is close at hand, and the nearest services and listed pumps are below.
roadsText: The M602 splits Eccles, and the M60, M62, M61, A57, A572, A576 and A575 are also listed nearby. Birch Services on the M62 is the closest service area at 12.7 km, then Lymm Services on the M6 at 16.8 km and Rivington Services on the M61 at 18.9 km. A station in Manchester (M25 3AJ, 7.7 km), one in Warrington (WA3 6RW, 13.1 km) and another at 15 km are listed on OpenStreetMap as selling AdBlue at the pump, though the map is not a complete record.

name: Edinburgh
intro: Between the Firth of Forth to the north and the Pentland Hills to the south, Scotland's capital had 506,520 residents in 2020 and a wider metropolitan population of 912,490. Edinburgh is the second-most-populous city in Scotland, after Glasgow, and the seat of the Scottish Government and the Scottish Parliament. Postcode districts listed for the city are EH1, EH2, EH3, EH7, EH8, EH9, EH10 and EH11. The A720, A8, A90, A7, A70, A71, A702 and A700 are the main roads on the local list, and a service area on the A720 is 4.8 km from the city. Musselburgh and Bonnyrigg are both about 10 km away, with Dalkeith (10.9 km), Penicuik (11.9 km) and South Queensferry (12.6 km) close behind.
roadsText: Main roads recorded around Edinburgh are the A702, A720, A700, A8, A70, A90, A71 and A7. Dreghorn Services on the A720 is the nearest service area at 4.8 km. Musselburgh Services on the A1 is 9.5 km away and MacMerry, also on the A1, is 20.5 km. Having a service area this close to the city is useful if an AdBlue warning appears on a run out of Edinburgh.

name: Egglescliffe
intro: Overlooking Yarm from the opposite bank of the River Tees, Egglescliffe village stands on top of a hill with the river at the bottom. The wider civil parish, in County Durham but administered by the borough of Stockton-on-Tees, takes in Eaglescliffe, Urlay Nook, Sunningdale, Orchard and a development on the former Allens West MOD site. At the 2021 census, the interconnected villages of the parish together with Preston-on-Tees had 10,250 residents. The parish has a light industrial estate and two railway stations, and it is covered by the TS16 postcode district. Ingleby Barwick is 2.7 km away, Thornaby-on-Tees 5.3 km and Stockton-on-Tees 5.9 km, with Middlesbrough 9.6 km, Billingham 10.1 km and Darlington 12.8 km. Local driving is a mix of village roads and short trips into the neighbouring towns.
roadsText: All three of the nearest service areas are between 12.2 km and 13.7 km from Egglescliffe. Wolviston Services on the A689 is 12.2 km away, a service area on the A19 is 12.7 km and Teesside Truck Stop on the A66 is 13.7 km. None of them is close to the village, so if a dashboard warning comes on, the distance to any of them is worth knowing.

name: Egham
intro: Egham lies west of the M25, reached from the motorway at junction 13, about 19 miles west of central London. The town is in the Borough of Runnymede in Surrey, and Runnymede itself, where Magna Carta was sealed in 1215, lies to the north. In the 17th and 18th centuries Egham was a stop on coaching routes between London and places to the west, and its station opened in 1856 on the line from Waterloo to Reading. Postcode districts are TW20 and GU25. Along with the M25, the M3 is listed, as are the A30, A308, A320, A328, A329 and A3113. Staines-upon-Thames is 4.1km away, Chertsey 5.6km and Windsor 7.6km, giving a mix of short local trips and motorway driving.
roadsText: The M25, M3, A30, A308, A3113, A328, A320 and A329 are the main roads listed around Egham. The nearest service areas are Heston Services on the M4 (13.7km), Wisley Services on the A3 (15.7km) and Cobham Services on the M25 (17.3km). Even with the M25 reached at junction 13, the first service area is 13.7km away, so it pays to act on an AdBlue warning early.

name: Elgin
intro: As the administrative and commercial centre for Moray, Elgin is a historic market town and former royal burgh, first documented in the Cartulary of Moray in 1190. The town originated south of the River Lossie, on higher ground above the floodplain. Its population is listed at 25,040 and it falls within the IV30 postcode district. Two main roads are recorded, the A96 and the A941. The listed neighbouring towns are a long way off: Nairn, the nearest of the listed towns, is 34.2 km away, Inverness is 58.2 km and Fraserburgh 76.8 km. For a van or diesel car, that makes an AdBlue warning worth dealing with before heading out of town. A service area on the A96 is 2.9 km from the town.
roadsText: The A96 and A941 are the main roads recorded around Elgin. Elgin Services on the A96 is just 2.9 km away, which is handy given the distances involved elsewhere. The next service areas are Ashgrove Services, also on the A96, at 32.4 km and Skiach Services on the A9 at 59.1 km. Beyond the town, stops are widely spaced, so plan ahead on longer trips.

name: Elland
intro: South of Halifax, Elland is a market town in Calderdale, West Yorkshire, lying by the River Calder and the Calder and Hebble Navigation. It appears in the Domesday Book of 1086 as Elant. The town had 14,554 residents at the 2001 census, and the ward was measured at 11,676 in 2011. Elland uses the HX5 postcode district. Brighouse is about 3.7 km away, Huddersfield 5.2 km and Halifax 5.7 km, with Cleckheaton, Mirfield and Liversedge all around 9 km. For a driver with an AdBlue warning, Hartshead Moor Services on the M62 is the nearest listed service area at around 6.6 km in a straight line. The next, Woolley Edge Services on the M1, is more than 20 km away, so the M62 site is the clear first choice from Elland.
roadsText: Hartshead Moor Services on the M62 is the closest service area to Elland, about 6.6 km in a straight line. Beyond that, Woolley Edge Services on the M1 is about 20.2 km away and Skelton Lake Service Station, also on the M1, about 25.8 km. With the second option around three times as far, Hartshead Moor is the clear nearest choice.

name: Ellesmere Port
intro: Ellesmere Port is on the south-eastern edge of the Wirral Peninsula, six miles north of Chester, though it belongs to Cheshire West and Chester rather than to Wirral or Merseyside. The town was first established on the River Mersey at the entrance to the Ellesmere Canal and stands on the bank of the Manchester Ship Canal. It is an industrial port town that has kept large industries alongside a service sector economy. Its built-up area had 65,430 people at the 2021 census. Two motorways, the M53 and M56, are on the road list, with the A41, A5117, A550, A494, A540 and A5116. Postcode districts CH65 and CH66 cover the town. Bebington (9.2 km) and Chester (9.5 km) are the nearest towns, followed by Neston (10.1 km), Hawarden (11.3 km), Connah's Quay (11.7 km) and Heswall (14.1 km).
roadsText: Ellesmere Port's main roads include the M53 and M56, with the A41, A5117, A550, A494, A540 and A5116. Chester Services on the M56 is the nearest service area at 7.3 km. Chester West Services on the A55 is 14.5 km away and Earlsfield Services on the M57 17.9 km. The nearest site OpenStreetMap has listed as selling AdBlue at the pump, in Liverpool L5 at 18 km, is marked HGV-only, and those records are incomplete.

name: Ellon
intro: Believed to come from the Gaelic Eilean, meaning island, the name Ellon reflects the town's old position at a ford on the River Ythan. This Aberdeenshire town lies approximately 16 miles (26 kilometres) north of Aberdeen in the ancient region of Formartine, and it had a population of 10,126 in 2022. It sits in the AB41 postcode district. Ellon is a similar distance from several larger places: Inverurie is 20.5 km away, Peterhead 22.6 km and Aberdeen 23.9 km. For a driver with an AdBlue warning, the more pressing point is that every service area listed for Ellon is more than 48 km away, so planning a stop matters more here than in towns with services close at hand.
roadsText: Ashgrove Services on the A96 is the nearest service area listed for Ellon, 48.4 km away. Stracathro Services on the A90 is 73.5 km and Elgin Services, also on the A96, is 76.9 km. Much closer, a station at Mintlaw (AB42 5EL), about 18.1 km away, is listed as selling AdBlue at the pump in OpenStreetMap. That data is incomplete, so other stations may sell it as well.

name: Ely
intro: Built on a clay island that rises to 85 feet (26 m), the highest land in the Fens, Ely is a cathedral city in East Cambridgeshire, 14 miles (23 km) north-east of Cambridge and 24 miles (39 km) south-east of Peterborough. The built-up area had 19,185 residents at the 2021 census, and the parish also covers rural settlements such as Chettisham, Prickwillow, Queen Adelaide and Stuntney. The city's postcode district is CB6. The Fens around it were drained from the eighteenth century, leaving fertile farmland. For an AdBlue warning, distance is the main point to know: the nearest listed service area, Cambridge Services on the A14, is 23.3 km away in a straight line. Soham is the nearest town at 9.1 km, with Chatteris at 15.6 km and Newmarket at 19.6 km.
roadsText: The nearest listed service areas are some distance from Ely. Cambridge Services on the A14 is 23.3 km away in a straight line, followed by Four Went Ways Services on the A11 at 30.5 km and Caxton Gibbet Services on the A428 at 31.1 km. Drivers in CB6 facing an AdBlue warning should allow for that distance, which will be longer by road.

name: Emsworth
intro: Halfway between Portsmouth and Chichester, Emsworth is a Hampshire town in the Borough of Havant, right by the border with West Sussex. It lies at the north end of an arm of Chichester Harbour, and its basin for yachts and fishing boats fills at high tide. The town had 10,269 residents at the 2021 Census, and its wider built-up area also takes in Westbourne, Southbourne and Nutbourne, with 18,777 people across the area in 2011. Emsworth falls in the PO10 postcode district. Havant is just 3.4 km away, Waterlooville 7.1 km and South Hayling 7.2 km, with Portsmouth at 10 km and Chichester at 11.6 km. The West Sussex border is close, so short local trips can cross the county line. If an AdBlue warning appears, the nearest listed service area is Farlington Services on the A27, 7.3 km away in a straight line.
roadsText: Farlington Services on the A27 is the nearest listed service area to Emsworth, 7.3 km away in a straight line. Petersfield Services on the A3 is 17.4 km off and Fontwell Services, also on the A27, is 20.4 km. With two of the three on the A27, that is the road worth knowing for a driver in PO10 with an AdBlue warning. Road distances will be longer than the straight-line figures.

name: Enderby and Narborough
intro: Enderby, on the south-west outskirts of Leicester, is a village and civil parish that this page covers together with Narborough. The village sits on the B4114 between Fosse Shopping Park and Narborough, and the M1 separates it from the St John's neighbourhood to the east. The parish also takes in Fosse Shopping Park and Grove Park Commercial Centre, and the course of the Fosse Way Roman road passes through it. The postcode district is LE19, and the combined area has a population of 13,178. Blaby and Whetstone is 3 km away, Leicester Forest East and Kirby Muxloe 4.4 km, Wigston 6.2 km and Leicester 6.8 km. With the M1 running through the parish, Leicester Forest East Services is only 3.7 km away, a handy stop if an AdBlue warning appears.
roadsText: The B4114 runs through Enderby towards Narborough, and the M1 passes between the village and St John's. Leicester Forest East Services on the M1 is the nearest service area, 3.7 km away. ExtraMSA Leicester Services on the A6 is 12.8 km off and Rugby Services on the M6 is 19.7 km away.

name: Enfield
intro: London's northernmost borough, Enfield forms part of North London and borders Hertfordshire to the north and Essex to the northeast. Its main communities are Edmonton, Enfield, Southgate and Palmers Green, and it has an estimated 333,794 residents. Inside London it meets Barnet to the west, Haringey to the south and Waltham Forest to the southeast; beyond the boundary sit Hertsmere, Welwyn Hatfield, Broxbourne and Epping Forest District. The main roads listed for the borough include the M25, A10, A406, A1100, A110 and A105, and its postcode districts include EN1, EN2, N9, N13, N14 and N21. Waltham Cross is 6.5km away, Cheshunt 7.5km and Potters Bar 8.2km. With Hertfordshire and Essex on its borders, a van or diesel car that develops an AdBlue warning on an Enfield round may well be just outside London when it happens.
roadsText: Main roads around Enfield include the M25, A10, A406, A1100, A110, A1005, A105 and A111. The nearest listed service areas are South Mimms Services on the A1(M) at 10km and London Gateway Services on the M1 at 12km, with Heston Services on the M4 much further at 27.2km. A station 16.6km away is listed as selling AdBlue at the pump on OpenStreetMap, but that data is patchy and will not show every forecourt.

name: Enniskillen
intro: In the middle of County Fermanagh, between the Upper and Lower sections of Lough Erne, Enniskillen is the county's largest town and its county town. It had 14,086 residents at the 2021 census and was the seat of the former Fermanagh District Council. Enniskillen Castle dates from the 15th century, built as a Maguire stronghold, and the town was expanded during the Plantation of Ulster. For drivers, the striking fact is distance. Omagh, the nearest neighbouring town, is about 35.8 km away, and Strabane, Dungannon, Armagh and Cookstown are all between 54.3 km and 66.6 km off. Postcode district BT74 covers the town. The closest service area is about 65.9 km away on the M1, so anyone with an AdBlue warning in or around Enniskillen should plan before heading out on a long run.
roadsText: Service areas are a long way from Enniskillen. The nearest is Cohannon Services on the M1, about 65.9 km away in a straight line, followed by Glenshane Tourist Services on the A6 at about 81.3 km and Lisburn Services on the M1 at about 107.8 km. Road distances will be longer than those straight-line figures, which matters when a warning light is already on.

name: Epping
intro: Sitting on a ridge between the valleys of the River Roding and the River Lea, Epping is a market town in the Epping Forest District of Essex, 27 km north-east of Charing Cross. The northern end of Epping Forest surrounds it, and the town lies just outside the M25, firmly within the London commuter belt. As well as the town itself, the parish takes in Coopersale and Fiddlers Hamlet, and the 2021 census gave the built-up area a population of 10,695. The town's postcode district is CM16. Neighbouring towns are close together here: Loughton is 5.3 km away, Waltham Abbey 7.1 km and Harlow 8.2 km, while Buckhurst Hill, Chigwell and Waltham Cross are all within 9.4 km. For a van or diesel car, that means plenty of short hops between these places, with the M25 close at hand for longer runs.
roadsText: Even with the M25 just beyond the town, the nearest service areas are some distance off: Birchanger Green on the M11 is 20.5 km away, South Mimms on the A1(M) 22.9 km and Thurrock on the M25 25.2 km. Two stations are listed in OpenStreetMap as selling AdBlue at the pump, one 16.8 km away and one at Thorley in Bishop's Stortford, 18.9 km out. That map data is incomplete, so nearer forecourts may stock it too.

name: Epsom
intro: First recorded as Ebesham in the 10th century, Epsom is a Surrey town in the borough of Epsom and Ewell, about 14 miles south of central London. It sits on the spring line where the chalk of the North Downs meets London Clay, and a spring on Epsom Common had mineral waters found to be rich in Epsom salts. Its High Street is dominated by a clock tower built in 1847-8, and its postcode districts are KT17, KT18, KT19 and KT21. For drivers, this is a closely packed area: Ewell is 2.5km away, Ashtead 3.3km and Tadworth and Epsom Downs 3.6km, with Leatherhead at 5.8km. The M25 heads a long road list that also includes the A24, A240, A232, A243, A217, A3 and A309.
roadsText: The M25, A24, A240, A232, A243, A217, A3 and A309 are the main roads listed around Epsom. Cobham Services on the M25 is the closest service area at 9.9km. Wisley Services on the A3 is 15.7km away and Heston Services on the M4 is 19.3km. For a driver with an AdBlue warning on the A3, Wisley is the stop on that road.

name: Erskine
intro: The Erskine Bridge gives this Renfrewshire town the lowest crossing to the north bank of the River Clyde, linking it with Old Kilpatrick in West Dunbartonshire. Erskine itself sits on the southern bank as a commuter town at the western extent of the Greater Glasgow conurbation. It borders Bishopton to the west, with Renfrew, Inchinnan, Paisley and Glasgow Airport to the south. Originally a small village, it has expanded since the 1960s as an overspill town, and its population is now over 15,000. Postcode districts PA8 and G60 cover the area. Clydebank is about 2.8 km away in a straight line, Renfrew 4.9 km and Paisley 7.2 km. A driver with an AdBlue warning has two stations within about 9.4 km listed as selling AdBlue at the pump, but the nearest service area is about 26.1 km away.
roadsText: Bothwell Services on the M74 is the nearest service area to Erskine, about 26.1 km away in a straight line, followed by Hamilton Services on the M74 at about 28.9 km and Stirling Services on the M9 at about 38.2 km. OpenStreetMap lists a station about 9.3 km away and another in Glasgow (G11 6DN), about 9.4 km away, as selling AdBlue at the pump. That data is incomplete.

name: Eston
intro: Greater Eston covers more than the old town itself: Grangetown, Normanby, South Bank, Teesville and part of Ormesby all fall within it, so an Eston address can mean any of those places. Eston is a former industrial town in the Redcar and Cleveland unitary area of North Yorkshire, and its postcode districts are TS6 and TS3. Neighbouring towns are close. Middlesbrough is only 4.3 km away, Redcar 6.7 km and Guisborough 7.3 km, so a short local run can easily cross into another town. The road list is long for a place of 29,625 people, with the A66, A174, A1053, A171, A1043, A172, A1085 and A1042 all appearing. With no motorway among them, local driving here is A-road driving. Billingham (8.4 km), Thornaby-on-Tees (9 km) and Stockton-on-Tees (11.2 km) are the other nearby towns.
roadsText: Main roads listed around Eston are the A66, A174, A1053, A171, A1043, A172, A1085 and A1042. The closest service area is Teesside Truck Stop on the A66, just 2.2 km away. Wolviston Services on the A689 is 12.1 km off, and a southbound service area on the A19 is 13.8 km away. That gives drivers in TS6 and TS3 three options, each on a different road.

name: Euxton
intro: Housing developments, including at Buckshaw, have pushed Euxton's population from 9,993 at the 2011 census to an estimated 14,000 or so. It is still a village and civil parish, in the Borough of Chorley, just west of Chorley itself and south of Clayton-le-Woods, covering about 2.5 miles from east to west. The village takes in several areas, among them Runshaw Moor, Balshaw, Shaw Green, Buckshaw, Pincock and Primrose Hill. To the north, Shaw Brook marks the border with Leyland, and on the east side the boundary now broadly follows West Way. PR7 is the postcode district. Chorley is 3.1 km away and Leyland 3.4 km, and if an AdBlue warning comes on mid-journey, Charnock Richard Services on the M6 is just 5.2 km away.
roadsText: Charnock Richard Services on the M6 is the closest service area to Euxton at 5.2 km. Rivington Services on the M61 is 10.1 km away and Blackburn with Darwen Services on the M65 is 12.9 km. Chorley (3.1 km) and Leyland (3.4 km) are the nearest towns, with Bamber Bridge at 6.3 km.

name: Evesham
intro: Roughly equidistant between Worcester, Cheltenham and Stratford-upon-Avon, Evesham is a market town in the Wychavon district of Worcestershire with a 2021 census population of 27,684. It lies in the Vale of Evesham, the flood plain of the River Avon, an area known for market gardening. The town centre sits within a meander of the river and is regularly subject to flooding; the 2007 floods were the most severe in its history. Flooding is worth bearing in mind when planning a route with a vehicle already showing an AdBlue warning. Neighbouring towns are some way off: Tewkesbury is 17.3 km away measured directly, Bishop's Cleeve 17.5 km and Stratford-upon-Avon 19.4 km. The postcode district is WR11, and the A46, A44 and A4184 are the main roads listed nearby.
roadsText: The main roads listed around Evesham are the A46, A44 and A4184, with no motorway among them. Service areas are some distance away: Strensham on the M5 is the nearest at 14.1 km measured directly, then Hopwood Park on the M42 at 30.9 km and Warwick North (Budbrooke) on the A46 at 31.3 km. With an AdBlue warning showing, it helps to know that the nearest motorway stop is not on the doorstep.

name: Ewell
intro: Twelve miles south of central London and two miles north-east of Epsom, Ewell is a Surrey town that is contiguous with the Greater London suburbs. It began as a spring line settlement where the chalk of the North Downs meets London Clay, and the Hogsmill River still rises at a spring close to Bourne Hall in the village centre. Recorded in the Domesday Book as Etwelle, it was granted a market charter in 1618. Postcode districts listed for the area are wide-ranging: KT17, KT19, KT4, KT18, SM2, SM3 and SM7. The road list is all A roads, including the A3, A24, A217, A232, A240, A243, A297 and A309. Epsom is 2.5km away, Worcester Park and Stoneleigh 2.9km and Sutton 4.9km, so most driving here is suburban.
roadsText: The A232, A24, A240, A217, A3, A243, A309 and A297 are the main roads listed around Ewell. The nearest service area is Cobham Services on the M25, about 12.3km away, followed by Wisley Services on the A3 (18km) and Heston Services on the M4 (18.9km). One station about 19.7km away is listed as selling AdBlue at the pump. OpenStreetMap's data is incomplete, so closer forecourts may also stock it.

name: Exeter
intro: Devon's county town stands on the River Exe, 58 km north-east of Plymouth and 105 km south-west of Bristol. Exeter is a cathedral city with a population of 137,894 in 2024, the second largest settlement in the county. Its history runs from a civilian settlement associated with the Roman fort of Isca Dumnoniorum to its time as an affluent centre for the wool trade, and much of the city centre was rebuilt after the Second World War. Under local government plans it will become the Exeter unitary authority from 2028, taking in parishes from East Devon, Teignbridge and Mid Devon. The EX1, EX2, EX3 and EX4 postcode districts cover the city. Exmouth is 13 km away, Dawlish 14.6 km, Teignmouth 17.9 km and Sidmouth 19.4 km, with Tiverton at 20.8 km. With the M5 on the city's doorstep, diesel journeys here often mix city streets and motorway miles.
roadsText: Exeter is well placed for motorway driving: the M5 is among the main roads, along with the A30, A38, A377, A376, A3015, A379 and A396. Exeter services on the M5 is just 3.4 km from the centre, Cullompton services on the M5 is 18.5 km and Tiverton services on the M5 is 24.7 km, so there are three stops on the same motorway within 24.7 km.

name: Exmouth
intro: Exmouth is a port town and seaside resort on the east bank of the River Exe at its mouth, about 18 km south-east of Exeter in the East Devon district. With 35,488 people at the 2021 census, it is the fifth largest settlement in Devon, and it also serves as a commuter town for nearby Exeter. It is noted for its long sandy beaches, its marina and its watersports. The EX8 postcode district covers the town. Exeter is 13 km away and Sidmouth 13.1 km, with Kingsteignton at 16.5 km and Torquay at 18.2 km. Only two main roads, the A376 and A379, are listed around Exmouth, so most journeys in and out use one of them. For a van or diesel car, the run towards Exeter is a familiar one, and the nearest motorway services are 11 km away on the M5.
roadsText: The A376 and A379 are the main roads around Exmouth. The nearest service area is Exeter services on the M5, 11 km away, followed by Cullompton services on the M5 at 26.2 km and Tiverton services on the M5 at 32.3 km. With the other two more than 26 km out, Exeter services is the most practical of the three.

name: Failsworth
intro: Between Manchester and Oldham, Failsworth is a town in the Metropolitan Borough of Oldham, 4 miles (6.4 km) north-east of Manchester and 3 miles (4.8 km) south-west of Oldham. The M60 ring-road motorway skirts it to the east, so the ring road runs along the town's eastern edge. The 2011 census counted 20,680 residents. Historically in Lancashire, Failsworth grew from a farming township into a mill town with redbrick cotton mills, and Daisy Nook country park sits on its southern edge. Postcode districts M35, M40 and M43 all reach into the area. Droylsden is about 2.4 km away and Chadderton 3.3 km, with Audenshaw, Ashton-under-Lyne and Manchester between 4 km and 4.8 km. A van or diesel car that picks up an AdBlue warning here is never far from the M60.
roadsText: The M60 ring road skirts Failsworth to the east. The nearest service area is Birch Services on the M62, about 8.5 km away, while Tabley Hill Service Station and Knutsford Services, both on the M6, are around 27.6 km and 27.7 km off. OpenStreetMap has a site about 1.9 km away listed as selling AdBlue at the pump, and another under Manchester at roughly 9.3 km. OpenStreetMap's records are incomplete, so others may exist.

name: Falkirk
intro: In the Forth Valley, 33 km northeast of Glasgow and 38 km northwest of Edinburgh, Falkirk is the main town and administrative centre of the Falkirk council area. The town had 34,627 people in 2022, while the wider council area of 156,800 takes in Grangemouth, Bo'ness, Denny, Bonnybridge, Camelon, Larbert, Stenhousemuir and the Braes villages. Falkirk sits at the junction of the Forth and Clyde and Union canals, a location that helped it grow as a centre of heavy industry during the Industrial Revolution. Postcode districts FK1, FK2 and FK5 cover the area. The M9 and M876 appear on the road list alongside the A9, A88, A803, A883, A904 and A905. Larbert is 3.5 km away and Grangemouth 4.6 km, with Bo'ness at 11.8 km and Linlithgow at 12.3 km.
roadsText: Main roads recorded around Falkirk are the M9, M876, A9, A803, A904, A905, A883 and A88. Stirling Services on the M9 is the nearest service area, 11.3 km away, followed by Heart of Scotland Services on the M8 at 15.8 km and Balhaldie Services on the A9 at 25.7 km. The M9 appears on Falkirk's own road list, so Stirling Services is the nearest stop on a road that serves the town.

name: Falmouth
intro: A port on the River Fal and the Carrick Roads harbour, Falmouth sits on the south coast of Cornwall and had 24,032 residents at the 2021 census. The town was founded in 1613 by the Killigrew family near Pendennis Castle, and its port came to overshadow neighbouring Penryn, now just 3 km away. Tourism grew after the railways arrived in the 19th century, and the town is home to a campus of Falmouth University and the National Maritime Museum Cornwall. Falmouth is covered by the TR11 postcode district. Truro is 12.8 km away, Redruth 13.8 km and Helston 14.5 km. Main roads listed around the town are the A39, A394, A3078 and A393. For anyone with an AdBlue warning, the nearest listed service area is a long way off: Cornwall Services on the A30, 36 km in a straight line.
roadsText: The main roads listed around Falmouth are the A39, A394, A3078 and A393. Service areas are distant from here. The nearest is Cornwall Services on the A30, 36 km away in a straight line, followed by Saltash Services on the A388 at 67.1 km and Roundswell Service Area on the A39 at 123.5 km. Drivers in TR11 are better off dealing with an AdBlue warning before a long run, as road distances will be longer still.

name: Fareham
intro: At the north-west tip of Portsmouth Harbour, Fareham is a market town between the cities of Portsmouth and Southampton in south-east Hampshire, and gives its name to the Borough of Fareham. It was once an important maker of bricks and a grower of strawberries and other seasonal fruit. The 2021 census put the population at 42,640, and the town spans the PO14, PO15 and PO16 postcode districts. The M27 is the motorway on the road list, with the A27, A32, A334, A3051 and A3222 as the other main roads. Lee-on-the-Solent is 3.6km away, Locks Heath 5.6km and Gosport 6.6km, while Portsmouth is 9.1km. Driving here mixes short trips between neighbouring towns with motorway runs on the M27, though none of the nearest service areas is especially close.
roadsText: The M27, A27, A32, A3222, A334 and A3051 are the main roads listed around Fareham. The nearest service area is Farlington Services on the A27, about 11.1km away. Rownhams Services on the M27 is 21.2km out and Petersfield Services on the A3 is 24.6km. Even the closest of the three is 11.1km from town, so plan a stop early if an AdBlue warning appears.

name: Farnborough
intro: An important centre of aviation, engineering and technology, Farnborough is a town in the Rushmoor district of Hampshire, with a population of around 60,652 at the 2021 census. It is probably best known for its links with aviation, including Farnborough Airport and the Farnborough International Airshow. The town is covered by the GU14 postcode district. It sits in a tight cluster of neighbouring towns: Frimley is 4.1 km away, Aldershot 4.2 km, Fleet 4.9 km and Ash and Ash Vale 5 km, with Camberley at 6.3 km. The road list includes the M3 and A331, along with the A325, A327 and A30. If an AdBlue warning comes on in or around Farnborough, the nearest listed services are at Fleet, 6.3 km away on the M3, and the next two are at least 19.5 km off.
roadsText: Near Farnborough, the main roads listed are the M3, A331, A327, A325, A3011, A323, A3013 and A30. Fleet Services on the M3 is the nearest listed service area at 6.3 km, with Wisley Services on the A3 at 19.5 km and Liphook Services, also on the A3, at 22.7 km. The Swallowfield By-pass station (RG7 1LZ), 19.5 km away, is listed as selling AdBlue at the pump in OpenStreetMap; that source is incomplete.

name: Farncombe
intro: Separated from Godalming by common land known as the Lammas Lands, Farncombe, historically Fernecome, is a village and peripheral settlement of Godalming in Waverley, Surrey, about 0.8 miles (1.3 km) north-east of the Godalming centre. The village of Compton lies 1.8 miles (3 km) to the north-west and Bramley 2 miles (3 km) to the east. Farncombe has a population of 13,247 and its postcode district is GU7. Godalming is 2 km away and Guildford 6.1 km, while Ash and Ash Vale, Aldershot, Cranleigh and Farnham are all between 9.4 km and 12.3 km. For a van or diesel car with an AdBlue warning, the nearest listed service area is Wisley Services on the A3, 13.8 km away in a straight line, so services are a fair distance out. Cobham Services on the M25 and Liphook Services on the A3 are 18.8 km and 19 km off.
roadsText: Wisley Services on the A3 is the nearest listed service area to Farncombe, 13.8 km away in a straight line. Cobham Services on the M25 is 18.8 km off and Liphook Services, also on the A3, is 19 km. Road distances will be longer than these figures, so a driver with an AdBlue warning should not count on services being close.

name: Farnham
intro: At the western end of the North Downs, on the north branch of the River Wey, Farnham is a market town about 36 miles south-west of London and close to Surrey's border with Hampshire. It is in the Borough of Waverley, and its civil parish takes in the villages of Badshot Lea, Hale and Wrecclesham, with 39,488 residents across the parish in 2011. The town uses the GU9 and GU10 postcode districts. Its castle was built in 1138 as a residence for Bishop Henry de Blois. Weybourne is just 2.7 km away and Aldershot 5.1 km, with Ash and Ash Vale at 6.8 km, Fleet at 8.1 km and Farnborough at 8.7 km. For a van or diesel car with an AdBlue warning, Fleet Services on the M3 is the nearest listed service area, 10.7 km away in a straight line, with an A3 site at 14 km.
roadsText: The nearest listed service area to Farnham is Fleet Services on the M3, 10.7 km away in a straight line. Liphook Services on the A3 is 14 km away and Wisley Services, also on the A3, is 23.2 km. These are straight-line distances, so the journey by road to any of them will be longer.

name: Farnworth
intro: Lying on the River Irwell and River Croal, Farnworth is a town in the borough of Bolton, 2 miles south-east of Bolton, 4 miles south-west of Bury and 8 miles north-west of Manchester. It is historically part of Lancashire and had 26,939 residents at the 2011 Census. Four postcode districts reach the town: BL4, M38, BL3 and M28. Farnworth is one of a tight group of places in this part of Greater Manchester, with Kearsley 2 km away, Little Hulton 2.4 km, Little Lever 2.8 km and Walkden 3.2 km. For longer journeys, the M61 and M60 are listed among the nearby roads, along with the A6, A666 and A580. If an AdBlue warning appears, the nearest services, and stations listed on OpenStreetMap as selling AdBlue at the pump, are set out below.
roadsText: The M61 and M60 are listed around Farnworth, plus the A575, A666, A6, A579, A58 and A580. The nearest service areas are Birch Services on the M62 at 11.6 km, Rivington Services on the M61 at 12.6 km and Blackburn with Darwen Services on the M65 at 18.9 km. OpenStreetMap lists stations in Manchester (M25 3AJ, 7.7 km) and Warrington (WA3 6RW, 16.6 km), and one more at 17.4 km, as selling AdBlue at the pump. It is not a full list.

name: Faversham
