intro: Beside the Swale, the strip of sea separating mainland Kent from the Isle of Sheppey in the Thames Estuary, Faversham is a Kent market town 48 miles from London. It lies close to the A2, which follows the ancient British trackway now known as Watling Street, used by the Romans and the Anglo-Saxons. There has been a settlement here since before Roman times, and the town appears in Domesday Book of 1086 as Favreshant. About 20,941 people live in Faversham, in the ME13 postcode district. Sittingbourne is 10.9 km away and Whitstable 11 km, with Minster at 13.4 km, Canterbury at 14 km and Sheerness at 16.4 km. For a van or diesel car with an AdBlue warning, the nearest listed service areas are just under 20 km away on the M20 and M2, so a stop needs some planning.
roadsText: Faversham lies close to the A2. Its two nearest listed service areas are the same straight-line distance away, 19.7 km: Maidstone Services on the M20 and Medway Services on the M2. Ashford International Truckstop on the A2070 is 21 km away. Which is closest by road will depend on the route taken, since these are straight-line figures.

name: Featherstone
intro: Historically part of the West Riding, Featherstone is a town and civil parish in the City of Wakefield, two miles south-west of Pontefract. It had 15,244 residents in 2011, and Featherstone railway station is on the Pontefract Line. The town uses the WF7 postcode district. Pontefract is about 3.6 km away, Normanton 4.3 km, Castleford 4.9 km and Wakefield 9.5 km. Services are close by: Exelby Services Whitwood on the M62 is about 4.5 km away in a straight line and Ferrybridge Services, also on the M62, about 6.5 km. For a van or diesel car with an AdBlue warning, a station in Pontefract listed as selling AdBlue at the pump is about 4.3 km from the town centre.
roadsText: Featherstone has two M62 service areas nearby: Exelby Services Whitwood at about 4.5 km in a straight line and Ferrybridge Services at about 6.5 km. Barnsdale Bar Services on the A1 is about 10 km away. OpenStreetMap lists a station in Pontefract (WF7 7HX), about 4.3 km away, and another in Leeds (LS9 0AS), about 12.7 km away, as selling AdBlue at the pump. It is not a complete record.

name: Felixstowe
intro: Home to the Port of Felixstowe, the largest container port in the United Kingdom, this East Suffolk port town has a population of 24,218 and sits roughly 72 miles (116 km) north-east of London. Its postcode district is IP11. The main roads listed around the town are the A14, A120, A136, A154 and A1021. If an AdBlue warning appears on a van or diesel car here, it helps to know that the nearest listed service area is 18.6 km away on the A14, so a services stop is not on the edge of town. Harwich is the closest neighbouring town at 5.4 km, followed by Kesgrave at 12.8 km, Woodbridge at 14.9 km and Ipswich at 16.2 km, with Clacton-on-Sea and Colchester further out at 21.7 km and 29.7 km.
roadsText: The main roads listed around Felixstowe are the A14, A120, A136, A154 and A1021. The nearest service areas, measured in a straight line, are Sprougton Road Services on the A14 at 18.6 km, Ardleigh South Services on the A120 at 24.7 km and Beacon Hill Services on the A140 at 26.7 km. Road distances will be longer than these figures, so allow for that if an AdBlue warning comes on.

name: Ferndown
intro: Immediately north of Bournemouth and Poole, and about 4 miles (6 km) east of Wimborne Minster, Ferndown is a Dorset town whose parish was called Hampreston until 1986. As well as the town itself, the parish includes Ameysford, Hampreston, Longham, Stapehill and Trickett's Cross, and at the 2021 census it had 17,501 residents. The BH22 postcode district covers the town. Its position on the edge of the Bournemouth and Poole area means neighbouring towns are close: West Moors is 2.7 km away, Wimborne Minster 4.6 km, Bournemouth 7.2 km, Verwood 8.4 km and Poole 9.5 km. Service areas are further off. If an AdBlue warning appears, the nearest listed is Picket Post Services on the A31, 13.1 km away in a straight line, while a forecourt in Poole listed as selling AdBlue at the pump is a little closer.
roadsText: The nearest service area to Ferndown is Picket Post Services on the A31, 13.1 km from the centre in a straight line. Rufus Stone, also on the A31, is 22.4 km away and West Wellow Services on the A36 is 30.5 km. Nearer than any of these, MFG Creekmoor, a Shell site in Poole (BH17 7FR) 10.1 km away, is listed in OpenStreetMap as selling AdBlue at the pump. The mapping is incomplete, so other forecourts may sell it too.

name: Filton
intro: Together with Patchway, Stoke Gifford and Bradley Stoke, Filton forms the North Fringe of Bristol, part of the Bristol urban area that has become an overflow settlement for the city. The South Gloucestershire town lies 6 miles (10 km) north of Bristol, and its economy is linked to the aerospace industry and the former Filton Airport, which closed in 2012 and is now a regeneration site. Filton has a population of 10,955 and spans two postcode districts, BS34 and BS10. Its neighbours are very close: Patchway is 2 km away, Stoke Gifford 2.4 km and Bradley Stoke 2.6 km, so driving here is mostly through built-up streets. If an AdBlue warning appears, three service areas are listed between 7.9 km and 10.4 km away in a straight line, the nearest being Avon Lodge on the A4.
roadsText: Avon Lodge on the A4 is the nearest service area to Filton, 7.9 km away in a straight line. Welcome Break Gordano Services on the M5 is 10 km away and Moto Severn View Services on the M48 is 10.4 km, giving drivers in BS34 and BS10 three options at a similar distance. Road distances through the built-up area will be longer than these figures.

name: Flackwell Heath and Wooburn Green
intro: Sitting at about 150 metres (490 ft) in the Chiltern Hills, Flackwell Heath is a village in the civil parish of Chepping Wycombe on the outskirts of High Wycombe. Together with Wooburn Green, it forms an area of 12,438 people in Buckinghamshire, covered by the HP10 postcode district. Flackwell Heath itself has around 6000 residents. Beaconsfield is 3.8 km away and High Wycombe 4 km, with Hazlemere at 5.4 km and Marlow at 5.8 km, and Maidenhead (9.6 km) and Chalfont St Peter (10 km) a little further. For a van or diesel car with an AdBlue warning, the nearest listed service area is Beaconsfield Services on the M40, 5.5 km away in a straight line. The other two listed, Bourne End Services on the A41 and Heston Services on the M4, are both more than 19 km away, so the M40 site is the clear first choice.
roadsText: Beaconsfield Services on the M40 is the nearest listed service area to Flackwell Heath and Wooburn Green, 5.5 km away in a straight line. The next options are much further: Bourne End Services on the A41 at 19.5 km and Heston Services on the M4 at 25 km. Driving distances will be longer than these figures, so it makes sense to head for the M40 site first.

name: Fleet
intro: The motorway services on the M3 take their name from this Hampshire town, which makes them a handy reference point for any driver. Fleet is the largest town in the Hart District, 38 miles south-west of London and 13 miles east of Basingstoke, and its built-up area runs continuously into Church Crookham and Crookham Village, which is why it is sometimes called Fleet and Crookham. The GU51 and GU52 postcode districts cover the town, and the Basingstoke Canal runs through it. Alongside the M3, the A30, A323, A325, A327, A287, A3013 and A3016 are listed. Farnborough is 4.9km away and Aldershot 6.6km, with Yateley at 6.8km, Farnham at 8.1km and Frimley at 8.5km. Journeys here combine short trips between neighbouring towns with easy access to the motorway.
roadsText: The M3, A323, A3013, A327, A287, A3016, A325 and A30 are the main roads listed around Fleet. Fleet Services on the M3 is just 2.6km away; the next nearest are Reading Services on the M4 and Liphook Services on the A3, both 21.4km out. A station on the Swallowfield By-pass near Reading (RG7 1LZ), about 16.9km away, is listed as selling AdBlue at the pump, though OpenStreetMap's data is incomplete.

name: Fleetwood
intro: At the north-west corner of the Fylde, Fleetwood is a coastal town in the Borough of Wyre with 26,232 people at the 2021 census. It took its modern shape in the 1830s, when landowner Peter Hesketh-Fleetwood planned a seaport and railway spur and commissioned civic buildings, including two lighthouses, from the architect Decimus Burton. The town later grew into a deep-sea fishing port, and fish processing is still a major activity. FY7 is its postcode district. Cleveleys (3.4 km) and Thornton (4.4 km) are the closest neighbours, with Poulton-le-Fylde at 7.7 km and Blackpool at 12.9 km. The roads listed for Fleetwood are all A roads: the A585, A587, A588 and A584. For a driver with an AdBlue warning, the key fact is distance, as the nearest service area is 18.5 km away.
roadsText: The roads listed for Fleetwood are the A585, A587, A588 and A584. Lancaster Services on the M6, 18.5 km away, is the nearest service area by some margin; Burton-in-Kendal Services (35.3 km) and Charnock Richard Services (38.4 km), both on the M6, are much further. Blackpool is 12.9 km away.

name: Flint
intro: The former county town of Flintshire, Flint (Y Fflint) is a town and community on the estuary of the River Dee. The community grew from 12,953 people at the 2011 Census to 13,732 in 2021, and the wider urban area, which includes Holywell and Bagillt, had 26,442. The town is covered by the CH6 postcode district. Neighbouring towns are within easy reach: Connah's Quay is 5.5 km away, Neston 7.6 km, Buckley 9.2 km, Hawarden 9.5 km and Heswall 10.3 km, with Bebington at 14 km. For a driver with an AdBlue warning, the A55 is the road to know, because the two nearest listed service areas are both on it, at 7 km and 11.7 km in a straight line. A third, on the M56, is 22.3 km away.
roadsText: The two nearest service areas to Flint are both on the A55: Chester West Services, 7 km away in a straight line, and Singing Kettle Services at 11.7 km. The third, Chester Services on the M56, is 22.3 km off. Road distances will be longer than these figures. Chester West is the closest listed place to stop if an AdBlue warning comes on around the CH6 area.

name: Flitwick
intro: Recorded in the Domesday Book of 1086 as a hamlet on the River Flitt, Flitwick is now a Central Bedfordshire town with a population of 13,668. The River Flit runs through Flitwick Moor nearby, a nature reserve and Site of Special Scientific Interest. The MK45 postcode district covers the town. For drivers, the M1 is close by: two service areas on that motorway are within 8 km, Toddington Services at 6.4 km and Crawley Crossing Truck Stop at 7.6 km, both measured in a straight line. That gives a van or diesel car with an AdBlue warning a couple of nearby places to stop. Houghton Regis is 11 km away and Kempston 12.2 km, with Luton, Dunstable, Leighton Buzzard and Bedford all between 13 km and 15.2 km.
roadsText: Two M1 sites are the nearest service areas to Flitwick: Toddington Services at 6.4 km and Crawley Crossing Truck Stop at 7.6 km, both straight-line distances from the town centre. Bedford Services on the A421 is 11.4 km away. All three are within about 11 km of MK45, giving drivers a choice of stops on the M1 and the A421.

name: Folkestone
intro: On the English Channel coast of Kent, Folkestone lies on the southern edge of the North Downs, in a valley between two cliffs. It was an important harbour, shipping port and fashionable coastal resort for most of the 19th and mid-20th centuries. Today it has a population of 51,987, and its postcode districts are CT20, CT19 and CT18. For a driver dealing with an AdBlue warning, the useful picture is a town with the M20 and A20 on its road list, plus the A259, A260, A261, A2033 and A2034 for local links. Hythe is only 4.4km away and Dover 12.8km, with Ashford at 19.1km and Canterbury at 21.8km. Journeys here range from short hops between neighbouring towns to longer runs on the M20, and the nearest service area is 6.3km from town.
roadsText: The M20, A20, A259, A2034, A2033, A260 and A261 are the main roads listed around Folkestone. Folkestone Services on the M20 is the nearest service area at 6.3km, followed by Whitfield Services on the A2 (15.2km) and Ashford International Truckstop on the A2070 (16.5km). A station in New Romney (TN28 8AZ), about 17.3km away, is listed as selling AdBlue at the pump. OpenStreetMap data is incomplete, so other forecourts may stock it too.

name: Forest Town
intro: Once a village in its own right, Forest Town has become a suburb within Mansfield, Nottinghamshire, after continuous development joined it to the town. The area has a population of 19,015 and is covered by the NG19 postcode district. For drivers, that means Forest Town is part of the Mansfield road network: Mansfield Woodhouse is 2.9 km away and Mansfield 3.5 km, with Shirebrook 6.7 km and Sutton in Ashfield 7.7 km off. Kirkby-in-Ashfield is 9.1 km away and New Ollerton and Ollerton 10.8 km. Anyone with a van or diesel car showing an AdBlue warning here has one practical advantage, because a station listed as selling AdBlue at the pump is about 2.5 km away. Motorway services are further off, at more than 12 km.
roadsText: A station about 2.5 km from Forest Town is listed on OpenStreetMap as selling AdBlue at the pump. The data behind that is incomplete, so other forecourts may also stock it. For roadside services, the nearest are Tibshelf Services on the M1 at 12.1 km, Markham Moor Services on the A1 at 18.8 km and Welcome Break Woodall Services on the M1 at 19.8 km.

name: Forfar
intro: Just off the main A90 road between Perth and Aberdeen, Forfar is the county town of Angus and the administrative centre for Angus Council. It is a market town and historic royal burgh in Strathmore, with a population of 13,801 in 2022, and Dundee, the nearest city, is 13 miles (21 km) away. Linen and jute manufacturing once mattered here; today the main activities are agriculture and tourism around Strathmore. The DD8 postcode district covers the town. Carnoustie is about 18.7 km away in a straight line and Arbroath 20.2 km, with Montrose at 27 km and Perth at 44.1 km. Forfar has a service area right on its doorstep for a driver with an AdBlue warning: Forfar Services on the A90 is only about 2.2 km away.
roadsText: The main A90 road runs just by Forfar, and Forfar Services on it is only about 2.2 km away in a straight line. Stracathro Services, also on the A90, is about 22.1 km away. The next option, Kinross Services on the M90, is much further at about 59 km, so for the DD8 district the two A90 stops are the ones that matter.

name: Formby
intro: Formby grew up on the plain beside the Irish Sea coast and is now a town and civil parish in the Metropolitan Borough of Sefton, Merseyside. It works as a commuter town for Liverpool, and it also draws day trippers to its beaches, sand dunes and wildlife, including the endangered red squirrel and natterjack toad, in an area conserved by the National Trust. Cockle raking and shrimp fishing carried on here into the 19th century. The town has a population of 22,892 and sits in the L37 postcode district. Its nearest neighbours are Crosby at 8.2 km, Maghull at 9.6 km and Southport at 9.8 km, with Litherland, Ormskirk and Bootle between 10.3 km and 12.1 km. For a van or diesel car based in Formby, regular journeys are likely to include commuting runs towards Liverpool as well as local trips.
roadsText: Old Meadow services on the M58 is the closest service area to Formby, 11.2 km away, and a station at Old Meadow, at the same distance, is listed in OpenStreetMap as selling AdBlue at the pump. Earlsfield services on the M57 is 21.3 km away and Charnock Richard on the M6 25.8 km. HGV refuelling pumps in Liverpool (L5 9XN), 14.9 km away, are also listed, but are marked for lorries only. The map data is incomplete.

name: Frampton Cotterell and Winterbourne
intro: Winterbourne to the south-west and Coalpit Heath to the east run directly into Frampton Cotterell, a village on the River Frome in South Gloucestershire about 8 miles (13 kilometres) north-east of Bristol. Together, Frampton Cotterell and Winterbourne had 14,694 residents in 2011. The parish borders Iron Acton to the north and Westerleigh to the south-east. The area is covered by the BS36 postcode district and has several close neighbours: Bradley Stoke and Yate are both 4.5 km away, Stoke Gifford 4.8 km, Kingswood and Fishponds 6 km, and Patchway and Filton 6.6 km. Drivers with an AdBlue warning have three listed service areas between 12.6 km and 14.8 km away in a straight line, on the M48, A4 and M5.
roadsText: Three listed service areas sit at similar distances from Frampton Cotterell and Winterbourne: Severn View Services on the M48 at 12.6 km in a straight line, Avon Lodge on the A4 at 14.5 km and Michaelwood Services on the M5 at 14.8 km. As each is on a different road, the best choice from BS36 depends on direction of travel. Actual road distances will be greater.

name: Fraserburgh
intro: Known locally as the Broch, Fraserburgh sits in Buchan in the north-eastern corner of Aberdeenshire, about 40 miles (64 km) north of Aberdeen and 17 miles (27 km) north of Peterhead. It is the biggest shellfish port in Scotland and a major port for white and pelagic fish, and the 2022 census recorded a population of 12,921. The town is in the AB43 postcode district. Distances here are long. Peterhead is 23.9 km away, Ellon 35.7 km and Aberdeen 59.6 km, and the nearest service area listed for the town is 54.7 km off. A van or diesel car that shows an AdBlue warning in Fraserburgh is therefore a long way from the nearest listed services, and knowing the options before a longer run makes a real difference.
roadsText: The nearest service areas listed for Fraserburgh are Ashgrove Services on the A96 at 54.7 km, Elgin Services, also on the A96, at 74 km, and Stracathro Services on the A90 at 107.6 km. Nearer at hand, a station at Mintlaw (AB42 5EL), about 18 km away, is listed as selling AdBlue at the pump in OpenStreetMap. That source is incomplete, so other local stations may sell it too.

name: Frimley
intro: Of Saxon origin, though not listed in the Domesday Book of 1086, Frimley is a town in the borough of Surrey Heath, around 30 miles (48 km) south-west of central London. It has a population of 15,101 and spans the GU16 and GU15 postcode districts. Frimley sits among closely spaced towns. Camberley is just 2.4 km away, Farnborough 4.1 km and Sandhurst 4.9 km, with Ash and Ash Vale, Yateley and Aldershot all between 7.2 km and 7.5 km out. A driver dealing with an AdBlue warning here has Fleet Services on the M3 as the nearest listed service area, 8.8 km away in a straight line. The next two, Wisley Services on the A3 and Cobham Services on the M25, are both more than 17 km off, so the M3 site is the closer choice by some distance.
roadsText: From Frimley, the nearest service area is Fleet Services on the M3, 8.8 km in a straight line. Wisley Services on the A3 is at 17.2 km and Cobham Services on the M25 at 22.7 km. A station on the Swallowfield By-pass near Reading (RG7 1LZ), 19.7 km away, is listed in OpenStreetMap as selling AdBlue at the pump. It is a long way out, and the map is incomplete, so nearer stations may also stock it.

name: Frome
intro: Wool and cloth first made Frome grow, before the town diversified into metal-working and printing. It sits at the eastern end of the Mendip Hills on the River Frome, 21 km south of Bath, and had 28,567 people at the 2021 census. Most of its centre now falls within a conservation area with a large number of listed buildings. It has road and rail transport links and acts as an economic, sporting and cultural centre for the surrounding area. The BA11 postcode district covers the town. Westbury is 9.6 km away and Warminster 10.6 km, with Midsomer Norton at 12.9 km and Trowbridge at 13.4 km. There is no motorway among the roads near the town; the A361, A36, A362, A3098 and A359 carry both local trips and longer journeys for vans and diesel cars.
roadsText: Frome's main roads are the A361, A36, A362, A3098 and A359. The nearest service area is Warminster services on the A350, 8.5 km away. Motorway services are much further, with Leigh Delamere on the M4 at 33 km and Chippenham Pit Stop on the M4 at 34.6 km, so Warminster is the closest stop by a wide margin.

name: Fulwood
intro: Fulwood is a suburb in the northern half of the City of Preston district, made up of five wards and home to 28,535 people in 2011. It grew from the second half of the 19th century and was governed separately from Preston until 1974. It has kept a distinct identity, with most of the settlement inside the Fulwood Conservation Area. Preston itself is just 2.4 km away, and the PR2 and PR1 postcode districts cover the suburb. For drivers, the useful point is that the M55 and M6 are both listed among the roads around Fulwood, along with the A6, A59 and A583. Penwortham is 5 km away and Bamber Bridge 7.3 km. If an AdBlue warning comes on, bear in mind that the three nearest service areas are all between 17.6 km and 19.4 km away.
roadsText: Listed roads around Fulwood are the M55 and M6, plus the A6, A5085, A5072, A583, A59 and A582. The three nearest service areas are similar distances out: Charnock Richard Services on the M6 at 17.6 km, Blackburn with Darwen Services on the M65 at 18.2 km and Lancaster Services on the M6 at 19.4 km.

name: Gainsborough
intro: Sometimes claimed to be England's furthest-inland port, Gainsborough is a market town on the east bank of the River Trent in Lincolnshire's West Lindsey district. It lies 18 miles (29 km) north-west of Lincoln, 16 miles (26 km) south-west of Scunthorpe, 20 miles south-east of Doncaster and 39 miles (63 km) east of Sheffield. The population was estimated at 23,243 in 2019, and the postcode district is DN21. The nearest neighbouring town is Retford, about 14.7 km away, with Scunthorpe around 21.7 km and Lincoln 24.4 km. That distance from other towns carries over to service areas: the three nearest, on the A15, A1 and A1(M), are each between about 18.9 km and 19.9 km away, so a driver with an AdBlue warning in Gainsborough has a fair way to go to reach one.
roadsText: The nearest service areas to Gainsborough are all close to 20 km away: Showground Services on the A15 at about 18.9 km, Markham Moor Services on the A1 at around 19.2 km and Moto Blyth Services on the A1(M) at about 19.9 km. With no service area listed closer to the town, it makes sense to plan a stop before setting out on a longer run.

name: Galashiels
intro: Colloquially known as Gala, Galashiels is a major commercial centre for the Scottish Borders region, with an extensive history in the textile industry. It is the location of Heriot-Watt University's School of Textiles and Design. The town had 10,075 residents in 2022 and is covered by the TD1 postcode district. Hawick is 21.3 km away in a straight line, while Mayfield, Bonnyrigg, Dalkeith and Penicuik are each between 32.1 and 35.4 km off, and Tranent is 37.2 km away. That spacing shapes what an AdBlue warning means for a driver here. The nearest listed service areas, on the A1 and A720, are all more than 37 km from the town centre. Much closer, a station in Galashiels, 4 km from the centre, is listed in OpenStreetMap as selling AdBlue at the pump, which is useful to know before setting off on a longer drive.
roadsText: A station in Galashiels, 4 km from the town centre, is listed in OpenStreetMap as selling AdBlue at the pump. OpenStreetMap's AdBlue data is incomplete, so others may exist. The nearest listed service areas are much further away: MacMerry on the A1 at 37.6 km, Musselburgh Services on the A1 at 37.9 km and Dreghorn Services on the A720 at 41.2 km, all straight-line distances.

name: Garforth
intro: Six and a half miles (10.5 km) east of central Leeds, Garforth is a town in the City of Leeds metropolitan borough, sitting in the Garforth and Swillington ward. It is 16 miles (26 km) south-west of York and 10 miles (16 km) north of Wakefield, and it had 14,957 residents in 2011. Most of it is unparished, like much of Greater Leeds. The LS25 postcode district covers the town. Kippax is about 2.6 km away, Castleford 8.3 km, Rothwell 8.4 km and Normanton 9.9 km. Garforth has services fairly close by. Skelton Lake Service Station on the M1 is about 6.3 km away in a straight line, and a station in Leeds listed on OpenStreetMap as selling AdBlue at the pump is a similar distance, about 6.2 km, which helps if an AdBlue warning comes on.
roadsText: The nearest service areas to Garforth, in a straight line, are Skelton Lake Service Station on the M1 (6.3 km), Exelby Services Whitwood on the M62 (8.9 km) and Ferrybridge Services on the M62 (12.9 km). OpenStreetMap lists a station in Leeds (LS9 0AS), about 6.2 km away, and another in Pontefract (WF7 7HX), about 16.6 km away, as selling AdBlue at the pump. The map data is incomplete, so it will not show every outlet.

name: Gateshead
intro: Across the River Tyne from Newcastle upon Tyne, Gateshead sits on the southern bank and shares the Millennium Bridge, the Tyne Bridge and several other bridges with its neighbour. The town is in the Gateshead Metropolitan Borough of Tyne and Wear, and at the 2021 census the population was 196,151. It was historically part of County Durham and became a county borough under the Local Government Act 1888. The Angel of the North stands on the town's southern outskirts. The A1(M), A194(M) and A167(M) all feature in the main road list, along with the A1, A167, A184, A692 and A1231. Postcode districts include NE1, NE6, NE8, NE9, NE10, NE11, NE31 and NE37. Birtley is 4.6km away, with Hebburn and Washington both at 5.6km. For a van with an AdBlue warning, Washington Services is only 5.8km away.
roadsText: Listed main routes in Gateshead are the A194(M), A167(M), A1(M), A167, A184, A1, A692 and A1231. Washington Services on the A1(M) is the nearest listed service area at 5.8km, followed by Seaton Burn Services on the A19 at 14.4km and Easington Services on the A19 at 20.7km. A station in Newcastle upon Tyne, 11.2km away, is listed as selling AdBlue at the pump in OpenStreetMap, which does not include every station.

name: Giffnock
intro: The administrative centre of East Renfrewshire, Giffnock sits at the south-west edge of the Greater Glasgow conurbation in Scotland's Central Lowlands. Together with neighbouring Newton Mearns and Clarkston it forms part of one of Glasgow's wealthiest outer suburban areas. The town began as a scattered agricultural settlement, and its development took off in the 19th century with sandstone quarrying and the first railway link to Glasgow. About 12,250 people live here today, across the G46 and G43 postcode districts. Newton Mearns is 3.7 km away, Rutherglen 5.6 km, Barrhead 6.1 km and Glasgow 6.4 km, with East Kilbride and Cambuslang both under 9 km. If an AdBlue warning comes on, the nearest listed motorway services are on the M74, 14.5 km and 16.2 km from the town centre in a straight line, while one station in Glasgow is listed as selling AdBlue at the pump.
roadsText: The two closest listed service areas to Giffnock are both on the M74: Bothwell Services at 14.5 km and Hamilton Services at 16.2 km, measured in a straight line. The M74 Truck Stop is further out at 30.4 km. A station in Glasgow (G11 6DN), 7.4 km away, is listed in OpenStreetMap as selling AdBlue at the pump. OpenStreetMap's AdBlue records are incomplete, so it may not be the only local option.

name: Gillingham
intro: The largest town in the borough of Medway, Gillingham had a population of 111,033 in 2022. It forms a conurbation with neighbouring Chatham, Rochester, Strood and Rainham, so driving here means moving through one continuous built-up area rather than between separate, spaced-out towns. Chatham is only 3.4 km away and Rochester 7.2 km, with Sittingbourne at 11 km and Maidstone at 11.2 km. Postcode districts listed for Gillingham are ME1, ME4, ME5, ME7 and ME8. The M2 is the motorway listed nearby, alongside the A2, A278, A289, A231, A230 and A229. Its biggest advantage for a driver with an AdBlue warning is a listed service area less than 3 km away on the M2.
roadsText: The M2 is listed for Gillingham along with the A278, A2, A289, A231, A230 and A229. Medway Services on the M2 is the closest listed service area, 2.9 km away. Maidstone Services on the M20 is 11 km, and Tollgate Services on the A2 is 16.6 km. A station in Strood (ME2 2NY), about 7.5 km away, is listed as selling AdBlue at the pump in OpenStreetMap, which is an incomplete source.

name: Gillingham
intro: Dorset's most northerly town, Gillingham lies in the Blackmore Vale on the B3095 and B3081 roads, about four miles (six kilometres) south of the A303 trunk road and five miles (eight kilometres) north-west of Shaftesbury. Unlike its namesake in Kent, it is pronounced with a hard g. The civil parish had 11,505 residents at the 2021 census and includes the hamlets of Eccliffe, Huntingford, Madjeston and Milton on Stour, while Peacemarsh, Bay and Wyke have become part of the town as it has expanded. The SP8 postcode district covers it. Neighbouring towns are fairly distant, with Sherborne at 19.5 km, Warminster at 19.8 km and Blandford Forum at 21.4 km, and the nearest listed service area is 20.7 km away in a straight line.
roadsText: Gillingham is on the B3095 and B3081, with the A303 about four miles to the north. The nearest listed service area is Warminster Services on the A350, 20.7 km away in a straight line; Picket Post Services and Rufus Stone, both on the A31, are 43.5 km and 48.1 km away. Closer to home, Gillingham Service Station, a Shell site 1.8 km from the centre, is listed in OpenStreetMap as selling AdBlue at the pump, though that data is incomplete.

name: Glasgow
intro: Scotland's most populous city spreads along the banks of the River Clyde in west central Scotland, with an estimated 632,350 people in 2020 and more than a million across the Greater Glasgow urban area. At 3,562 people per square kilometre, Glasgow is densely built, and the postcode districts listed for it run from G1 to G5, plus G40, G41 and G42. The M8, M74, M77 and M80 all appear on the local road list too, along with the A8, A77, A804 and A814. The city is made up of 23 wards. Rutherglen (5.6 km), Bishopbriggs (6.3 km) and Giffnock (6.4 km) are the closest neighbouring towns, with Renfrew (7.9 km), Bearsden (8.1 km) and Cambuslang (8.3 km) just beyond.
roadsText: Glasgow's recorded main roads are the M8, M74, M77 and M80 motorways, plus the A814, A804, A77 and A8. The nearest service areas are both on the M74: Bothwell Services at 13.6 km and Hamilton Services at 16.4 km, with Heart of Scotland Services on the M8 at 31.6 km. OpenStreetMap lists a station in Glasgow (G11 6DN), 3.1 km away, as selling AdBlue at the pump. The map data is incomplete, so it is not a full list for the city.

name: Glenrothes
intro: Planned shortly after the Second World War as Scotland's second new town, Glenrothes lies in a river valley in the heart of Fife. It is now the administrative capital of Fife, home to the headquarters of Fife Council and a major service and employment centre for the area. The 2022 census counted 37,468 residents, making it Fife's third-largest settlement. KY6 and KY7 are the postcode districts, and the recorded main roads are the A92, A911, A912 and A914. Kirkcaldy and Dysart is 8 km away and Methil 9.5 km, with Cowdenbeath and Lumphinnans at 14.7 km and Dunfermline at 21.2 km. The nearest motorway service area is 16.4 km from the town, so it helps to know your options before an AdBlue warning turns serious.
roadsText: The A92, A911, A912 and A914 are the main roads recorded around Glenrothes. Kinross Services on the M90 is the nearest service area at 16.4 km. Beyond that, Musselburgh Services on the A1 is 30.8 km away and MacMerry, also on the A1, is 32.7 km. None of these is in the town itself, so it is worth acting on a warning before a long run.

name: Glossop
intro: Thirteen miles east of Manchester, Glossop is a High Peak market town set between 150 and 300 metres above sea level and bounded by the Peak District National Park to the south, east and north. It lies near Derbyshire's borders with Cheshire, Greater Manchester, South Yorkshire and West Yorkshire, and had 17,825 residents in 2021. The area now known as Glossop roughly matches the villages once called Glossopdale, and it became a mill town whose fortunes were tied to the cotton industry. Its postcode district is SK13, shared with Hadfield, 3.2 km away. The other nearest towns listed are Stalybridge at 8 km, Hyde at 8.4 km and Romiley at 9.4 km. With the national park on three sides and the nearest motorway services more than 23 km away, an AdBlue warning here is best dealt with before a longer trip.
roadsText: The nearest service areas to Glossop are some distance away: Moto Birch Services on the M62 is 23.4 km off, with Welcome Break Hartshead Moor on the M62 and Moto Woolley Edge Services on the M1 both at 32.9 km. A station 15.6 km from the town is listed on OpenStreetMap as selling AdBlue at the pump. That listing is unlikely to be complete, so it is worth checking forecourts nearer home too.

name: Gloucester
intro: Counting its suburbs, Gloucester has a population of around 132,000. The county town of Gloucestershire is a cathedral city on the River Severn, between the Cotswolds to the east and the Forest of Dean to the west. It is 11 km from Cheltenham, 53 km from Bristol and 27 km east of the border between England and Wales. The city is also a port, linked to the Severn Estuary by the Gloucester and Sharpness Canal, and its roots go back to a Roman colony founded in AD 97. The GL1, GL2, GL3 and GL4 postcode districts cover the city. Churchdown is 4.3 km away, Brockworth 4.4 km and Quedgeley and Hardwicke 5.5 km, with Stroud at 12.4 km and Bishop's Cleeve at 15 km. With the M5 among the main roads close to the city, plenty of diesel journeys here mix city streets with motorway miles.
roadsText: Gloucester's main roads are the M5, A38, A417, A40, A48, A4302, A430 and A4301. Gloucester services on the M5 is only 4 km from the centre. Further afield, Strensham services on the M5 is 23.6 km away and Ross Spur services on the M50 is 25 km away. That gives a good choice of places to stop if a warning appears on a motorway journey.

name: Godalming
intro: Godalming has long benefited from its place on the main route from London to Portsmouth Dockyard. The market town lies in south-west Surrey, around 30 miles (49 km) south-west of central London, where the Rivers Wey and Ock meet. Its civil parish, in the Borough of Waverley, takes in Farncombe, Binscombe and Aaron's Hill, and the area sits in the GU7 postcode district. The modern town is believed to date from the 6th or early 7th century, and Bargate stone was quarried locally until the Second World War. Guildford is 7.9 km away, Cranleigh 10.5 km and Haslemere 12.4 km. Drivers dealing with an AdBlue warning should note that the two closest listed service areas are both on the A3, at Wisley (15.5 km in a straight line) and Liphook (17.6 km), so neither is right on the doorstep.
roadsText: Both of the nearest listed service areas to Godalming are on the A3: Wisley Services, 15.5 km away in a straight line, and Liphook Services at 17.6 km. Cobham Services on the M25 is next at 20.2 km. None of them is especially close to GU7, so a low AdBlue level is best dealt with before a longer run. Road distances will be longer than these figures.

name: Golborne
intro: Golborne sits across the A580 East Lancashire Road in the borough of Wigan, 5 miles south-south-east of Wigan, 6 miles north-east of Warrington and 14 miles west of Manchester. Together with neighbouring Lowton it recorded a population of 24,041. Mining and textile manufacturing drove its historic growth, though both have since declined, and farming has also mattered, with many farms still belonging to the families who originally owned them. The town's postcode district is WA3. Leigh and Newton-le-Willows are each 4.2 km away and Ashton-in-Makerfield 4.6 km. Alongside the A580, the M6 and M62 are listed among the roads nearby. For a driver with an AdBlue warning, a station in Warrington (WA3 6RW), 6.9 km away, is listed on OpenStreetMap as selling AdBlue at the pump.
roadsText: Golborne's listed roads are the M6 and M62, plus the A580, A579, A49, A58, A577 and A572. Burtonwood Services on the M62 is the nearest service area at 7.5 km, with Lymm Services on the M6 at 13.8 km and Rivington Services on the M61 at 14 km. Two Warrington sites, WA3 6RW at 6.9 km and WA5 3TP at 9 km, are listed on OpenStreetMap as selling AdBlue at the pump, though the map will not show every station.

name: Gomersal and Birkenshaw
intro: South of Bradford and south-west of Leeds, Gomersal is a Kirklees village in West Yorkshire, lying east of Cleckheaton and north of Heckmondwike. It is close to the River Spen and forms part of the Heavy Woollen District. Together with Birkenshaw it has a population of 13,948, and the area falls in the BD11 postcode district. Six towns lie within 6.3 km of the centre: Cleckheaton is 3.5 km away, Heckmondwike 4.9 km, Liversedge 5.2 km, Batley 5.3 km, Pudsey 5.6 km and Bradford 6.3 km. For a van or diesel car with an AdBlue warning, Hartshead Moor on the M62 is the closest listed service area, 5.6 km from the centre in a straight line, while the next two are both on the M1, at 14.8 km and 17.5 km.
roadsText: The Hartshead Moor service area on the M62 is 5.6 km from Gomersal and Birkenshaw in a straight line, making it the nearest service area. Skelton Lake Service Station on the M1 is 14.8 km away and Woolley Edge Services, also on the M1, is 17.5 km. OpenStreetMap lists a station in Leeds (LS9 0AS), 14.9 km away, as selling AdBlue at the pump. That source is incomplete, so it may not be the nearest option.

name: Goole
intro: Nearly 2 million tonnes of cargo a year can be handled at Goole, home to the United Kingdom's furthest inland port, on the River Ouse about 50 miles (80 km) from the North Sea. The town is in the East Riding of Yorkshire, though its historic county is the West Riding, and the parish had 21,246 residents at the 2021 census. Doncaster is 16 miles (26 km) to the south-west, York 19 miles (31 km) to the north and Hull 29 miles (47 km) to the east. Closer in, Thorne is about 11.7 km away, Selby 15.1 km and Dunscroft and Hatfield 17 km. Goole falls in the DN14 postcode district. For a van or diesel car showing an AdBlue warning here, the nearest listed service area is Doncaster (North) Services on the M180, around 14.6 km away in a straight line, so it is worth knowing the route before the warning becomes pressing.
roadsText: The nearest service areas to Goole, measured in a straight line from the town centre, are Doncaster (North) Services on the M180 at about 14.6 km, Barnsdale Bar Services on the A1 at 25.2 km and Ferrybridge Services on the M62 at 25.5 km. The M180 site is clearly the closest of the three, with the other two both more than 25 km away. Road distances will be longer than these figures.

name: Gorleston-on-Sea
intro: Across the mouth of the River Yare from Great Yarmouth, Gorleston-on-Sea is a seaside town in the borough of Great Yarmouth, Norfolk, with a population of 24,474. It was historically in Suffolk and was a port at the time of the Domesday Book, later becoming a centre for herring fishing before turning into a seaside resort. The postcode district is NR31. Bradwell is 1.9 km away and Great Yarmouth 3.4 km, with Lowestoft 10.8 km off, but beyond these the distances grow quickly: Norwich is 30.7 km away. Main roads around the town include the A47, A143 and A149. For a van or diesel car with an AdBlue warning, the key point is distance, as the nearest service area is more than 30 km away.
roadsText: Main roads around Gorleston include the A47, A143, A1243, A1154 and A149. Service areas are a long way off: the nearest is Thickthorn Services on the A11, 33.9 km away, followed by Beacon Hill Services on the A140 at 63.9 km and EG Sprougton Road Services on the A14 at 69.9 km. If a warning appears, it is worth planning a stop well before a longer journey.

name: Gorseinon
intro: Gorseinon was a small village until the late 19th century, when it grew around the coal mining and tinplate industries. Today it is a town within the City and County of Swansea, near the Loughor estuary, around 6 miles (10 km) north west of Swansea City Centre, with its own elected town council. The town council area had 8,693 people in 2011, but the wider Gorseinon Urban Area, which also takes in Loughor, Garden Village and Penllergaer, had 20,581. The SA4 postcode district covers the town. Llanelli is 7.2 km away and Swansea 8.2 km, with Neath at 15.8 km, Baglan at 15.9 km and Port Talbot at 19.3 km. The M4 is close as well: the nearest listed service area is only 3.5 km away in a straight line, which is worth knowing if an AdBlue warning appears on a local run.
roadsText: Gorseinon is well placed for the M4. Two of the three nearest service areas are on it and close to the town: Swansea West Services is 3.5 km away in a straight line and Pont Abraham Services is 9 km. The third, Sarn Park Services, also on the M4, is much further at 35.3 km. Road distances will be longer than these figures, but either of the first two is a reasonable place to stop if an AdBlue warning comes on.

name: Gosport
intro: On a peninsula on the western side of Portsmouth Harbour, Gosport faces the city of Portsmouth, to which it is linked by the Gosport Ferry. At the 2021 Census the town had 70,131 residents and the wider district 81,952. Until the last quarter of the 20th century it was a major naval town, and it is still home to HMS Sultan. Postcode districts are PO12 and PO13. Lee-on-the-Solent is 5.1 km away, Portsmouth 5.9 km and Fareham 6.6 km. The road list includes the A32, A27 and A3, along with the M275. For a van or diesel car with an AdBlue warning, the nearest listed service area is 8.7 km away at Farlington, and the next two are both more than 27 km off, so the Farlington stop is the one to remember.
roadsText: The M275 is the only motorway in Gosport's road list, which also includes the A32, A3, A288, A2030, A2047 and A27. Farlington Services on the A27 is the nearest listed service area, 8.7 km away. The next two are much further out and almost level with each other: Petersfield Services on the A3 at 27.2 km and Rownhams Services on the M27 at 27.3 km.

name: Gourock
intro: Ferry services across the Clyde and a railway terminus serve Gourock, a mainly residential town that extends contiguously from Greenock along the east shore of the upper Firth of Clyde. It lies in the Inverclyde council area and was once a seaside resort and a burgh of the County of Renfrew. About 10,210 people live here, in the PA19 and PA16 postcode districts. Greenock is 3.4 km from the centre and Port Glasgow 10.2 km, while Helensburgh is 8.5 km away in a straight line. Dumbarton (16.5 km) and Largs (17.5 km) are further out. For a van or diesel car with an AdBlue warning, the main thing to know is that the nearest listed motorway services are more than 50 km away in a straight line, so the problem is best handled before setting off on a longer journey.
roadsText: The nearest listed service areas to Gourock are some distance away: Bothwell Services on the M74 at 50.2 km, Hamilton Services on the M74 at 52.7 km and Stirling Services on the M9 at 57.9 km, all in a straight line. A station 16.5 km away is listed in OpenStreetMap as selling AdBlue at the pump. OpenStreetMap's AdBlue records are incomplete, so it may not be the only option.

name: Grangemouth
intro: Grangemouth lies in the Forth Valley on the banks of the Firth of Forth, in the Falkirk council area, and was historically part of Stirlingshire. It is three miles (five kilometres) east of Falkirk, five miles (eight kilometres) west of Bo'ness and 13 miles (21 km) south-east of Stirling. The population was 16,016 in 2022, down from 17,373 in 2011. The town first grew as a port, helped by the Forth and Clyde Canal, and its economy is now focused mainly on the area's large petrochemical industry, including an oil refinery. Postcode districts FK3 and FK2 cover the area. Larbert is about 7.1 km away in a straight line and Linlithgow 8.1 km. A driver with an AdBlue warning will find the nearest service areas on the M9 and M8, about 14.6 km and 16.4 km away.
roadsText: Stirling Services on the M9 is the closest service area to Grangemouth, about 14.6 km away in a straight line. Heart of Scotland Services on the M8 is about 16.4 km away and Balhaldie Services on the A9 about 26.9 km. Road distances from the FK3 and FK2 districts will be longer than these straight-line figures, so allow extra when a warning light is on.

name: Grantham
intro: On the banks of the River Witham, Grantham is a market town and the administrative centre of Lincolnshire's South Kesteven district. The A1 bounds the town to the west, and Grantham lies 23 miles (37 km) south of Lincoln and 22 miles (35 km) east of Nottingham. The population was 44,580 in 2016, and the villages of Manthorpe, Great Gonerby, Barrowby, Londonthorpe and Harlaxton form outlying suburbs. The postcode district is NG31, and the main roads are the A1, A52 and A607. Fittingly for anyone with diesel trouble, the UK's first running diesel engine was made here in 1892. Other towns are some way off: Sleaford is about 18.1 km away, Newark-on-Trent 21.4 km and Melton Mowbray 22.9 km, so the A1 and its services matter for anyone with an AdBlue problem here.
roadsText: Grantham's main roads are the A1, A52 and A607. Moto Grantham North Services on the A1 is about 5 km away, and Colsterworth Services and Colsterworth Truck Stop, both on the A1, are around 12.2 km away. BP Colsterworth Service Station, about 11.7 km away, is listed in OpenStreetMap as selling AdBlue at the pump; the data is incomplete, so treat it as a starting point.

name: Gravesend
intro: Marking the eastern limit of the Greater London Built-up Area, Gravesend lies on the south bank of the River Thames, opposite Tilbury in Essex, 21 miles (35 km) east-south-east of Charing Cross. It is the administrative centre of the borough of Gravesham and had a population of roughly 60,250 in 2021. A Thames Gateway commuter town, it keeps strong links with the river. Postcode districts are DA11 and DA12. Listed roads include the A2 and M2, with the A226, A227 and A2260 among the rest. Northfleet is 3.2 km away and Swanscombe 6 km, while Tilbury, across the river, is 4 km. For a driver with an AdBlue warning, Gravesend is well placed, with a listed service area just 2 km away on the A2.
roadsText: Gravesend's road list includes the M2 and A2, plus the A1089, A226, A227, A126, A2260 and A289. Tollgate Services on the A2 is the closest listed service area, just 2 km away. Orsett Cock Services on the A13 is 9.2 km and Thurrock Services on the M25 is 10.5 km. A station in Strood (ME2 2NY), 8.3 km away, is listed as selling AdBlue at the pump in OpenStreetMap, which is not a complete record.

name: Grays
intro: Historically also known as Grays Thurrock, Grays is the largest town in the borough of Thurrock and its administrative headquarters. It sits on the north bank of the River Thames, about 20 miles (32 km) east of central London and two miles (three kilometres) east of the M25. Its economy is linked to Port of London industries, its own offices and retail, including the shopping centre at West Thurrock. The built-up area had 44,345 people in 2021, a figure that leaves out the adjoining Chafford Hundred. Neighbouring places are very close: Chadwell St Mary is 2.7 km away, Tilbury 3.1 km, Chafford Hundred and West Thurrock 3.3 km and South Ockendon 4.2 km, with Swanscombe and Northfleet around 5 km off. Service areas are close as well, which helps if a van or diesel car flags an AdBlue fault. Postcode districts are RM16, RM17, RM18 and RM20.
roadsText: Listed roads around Grays include the M25, A282, A13, A1089 and A2, plus the A1013, A126 and A1012. Three service areas are within 8 km: Thurrock Services on the M25 at 4.3 km, Orsett Cock Services on the A13 at 5.5 km and Tollgate Services on the A2 at 7.7 km. A station in Strood (ME2 2NY), 15 km away, and another 18.8 km away are listed on OpenStreetMap as selling AdBlue at the pump; that data is incomplete.

name: Great Bookham and Fetcham
intro: Six semi-urban spring line settlements lie between Leatherhead and Guildford, and Great Bookham is one of them. This page covers it together with Fetcham, in the Mole Valley district of Surrey, an area of about 21,655 people. With Little Bookham, Great Bookham forms part of the Saxon settlement of Bocham. The Bookhams sit astride the A246, the direct route between Leatherhead and Guildford, and are surrounded by common land, with residential roads linking them so they feel like one large village. Bookham railway station on Church Road serves both. The area's listed postcode district is KT23. Leatherhead is 4.3 km away, Cobham 5.8 km, Ashtead 6 km and Dorking 6.7 km. For a driver with an AdBlue warning, the motorway is close at hand: Cobham Services on the M25 is just 3.4 km away in a straight line.
roadsText: The A246 runs through the Bookhams as the direct route between Leatherhead and Guildford. Cobham Services on the M25 is the nearest listed service area at 3.4 km in a straight line, with Wisley Services on the A3 at 7.9 km. Heston Services on the M4 is much further at 23 km. That puts two listed service areas within about eight kilometres of the area.

name: Great Dunmow
intro: Also known simply as Dunmow, this historic market town in the Uttlesford district of Essex lies just north of the A120, roughly midway between Bishop's Stortford and Braintree. It stands on the site of a Roman settlement on Stane Street, in the upper valley of the River Chelmer, and is 8 km east of London Stansted Airport. At the 2021 census the built-up area had 10,395 residents and the wider parish 10,630, all within the CM6 postcode district. Neighbouring towns are a moderate drive away rather than on the doorstep: Bishop's Stortford is 13.3 km, Braintree 13.7 km, Sawbridgeworth 16 km, Chelmsford 17.4 km and Saffron Walden 17.8 km. For a van or diesel car based here, most trips to those towns involve a proper run out of Dunmow, and with the town lying just north of the A120, that road is the obvious one to know.
roadsText: Great Dunmow lies just north of the A120. The nearest service area is Birchanger Green on the M11, 11 km away, followed by Boreham on the A131 at 17.4 km and Four Went Ways on the A11 at 29.4 km. In OpenStreetMap, a station at Thorley in Bishop's Stortford, 13.2 km away, is listed as selling AdBlue at the pump, and lorry pumps in Chelmsford, 17.5 km away, are listed too but marked for HGVs only. The map data is incomplete.

name: Great Harwood
intro: Together with Clayton-le-Moors and Rishton, Great Harwood makes up the "Three Towns" conurbation in the Hyndburn district of Lancashire. The town lies 5 miles (8.0 km) north east of Blackburn and is adjacent to the Ribble Valley. Its population was 11,220 in 2001 and 10,800 at the 2011 census. The BB6 postcode district covers Great Harwood. Oswaldtwistle is about 5 km away and Accrington 5.1 km, with Padiham at 6.4 km and Blackburn at 6.8 km. Clitheroe is around 9.4 km off and Darwen 10.7 km, so four of the six nearest towns are within 6.8 km. For a driver with an AdBlue warning, the two nearest service areas are both on the M65, at about 9.4 km and 12.7 km away, so that motorway is the one to know.
roadsText: Blackburn with Darwen Services on the M65 is the nearest service area to Great Harwood, about 9.4 km away. Hollin Bank Service Station, also on the M65, is around 12.7 km off, and Rivington Services on the M61 about 23.5 km. Both M65 stops are within 12.7 km, so the M65 is the closest motorway with services for drivers in the BB6 district.

name: Great Malvern
intro: At the foot of the Malvern Hills, on the eastern flanks of the Worcestershire Beacon and North Hill, Great Malvern is the historic centre of Malvern and holds its town centre. It lies in the Malvern Hills district of Worcestershire. The town grew in the 19th century as a centre for hydrotherapy and spread to take in Barnards Green, Malvern Link with Link Top, Malvern Wells, North Malvern and West Malvern; together with the hills they surround and several villages, these places are known as The Malverns. For anyone driving here with an AdBlue fault, that means an urban area spread around high ground rather than one compact centre. The WR14 and WR13 postcode districts cover the area. Worcester, the nearest town on the list, is 12.1 km away as the crow flies, with Tewkesbury at 18.1 km. No motorway appears among the main local roads, which are the A449, A4103 and A4104.
roadsText: Around Great Malvern the main roads listed are the A449, A4103 and A4104. With no motorway among them, reaching a service area means a longer run: the nearest is Strensham on the M5, 13 km away as the crow flies, followed by Ross Spur on the M50 at 26.6 km and Gloucester on the M5 at 33.2 km. Distances by road will be longer than these straight-line figures.

name: Great Wyrley and Cheslyn Hay
intro: Great Wyrley is a village and civil parish in South Staffordshire that forms one built-up area with Cheslyn Hay, Churchbridge, Landywood and Little Wyrley. It lies 6 miles (9.7 km) north of Walsall and a similar distance from Wolverhampton, and Cannock, 4.5 km away, is directly to the north. Great Wyrley had 11,060 people at the 2011 census, and the area falls within the WS6 postcode district. Pelsall is 4.7 km away, Bloxwich 5.6 km and Brownhills 6.3 km, with Burntwood at 7.1 km and Rushall and Shelfield at 7.2 km. Service areas are very close here: Hilton Park Services on the M6 is 2.8 km away in a straight line, and two more sites are under 4 km away, which gives a van or diesel car with an AdBlue warning several places to pull in.
roadsText: Three service areas are close to Great Wyrley and Cheslyn Hay: Hilton Park Services on the M6, 2.8 km away in a straight line, The Trucker's Rest on the A5 at 3.7 km and Norton Canes Services on the M6 Toll at 3.8 km. OpenStreetMap lists a station in Burntwood (WS7 3XA), 6.3 km away, as selling AdBlue at the pump, and one in Warley at 17.2 km. Those records are incomplete.

name: Great Yarmouth
intro: Straddling the River Yare 20 miles (32 km) east of Norwich, Great Yarmouth, often called Yarmouth, is a seaside town that gives its name to the wider borough. It has been a resort since 1760 and a gateway from the Norfolk Broads to the North Sea. Its herring fishing shrank after the mid-20th century and has all but ended; North Sea oil from the 1960s brought an industry servicing offshore gas rigs, followed more recently by offshore wind and other renewable energy work. The built-up area had 28,985 people in 2021. Bradwell is 3.1 km away and Gorleston-on-Sea 3.4 km, but beyond those Lowestoft is 14.2 km off and Norwich 30.3 km. The A47 and A143 are the main roads listed, alongside the A1243, A1154 and A149. Postcode districts are NR30 and NR31.
roadsText: The A47, A143, A1243, A1154 and A149 are listed for Great Yarmouth. Service areas are distant: Thickthorn Services on the A11 is 34 km away, Beacon Hill Services on the A140 66.7 km and a service area on the A14 72.9 km. A driver with an AdBlue warning should not count on reaching services quickly from here.

name: Greenock
intro: At the 'Tail of the Bank', where the River Clyde deepens into the Firth of Clyde, Greenock sits on the south bank of the river in Scotland's west central Lowlands. It is the administrative centre of Inverclyde Council and forms a contiguous urban area with Gourock to the west and Port Glasgow to the east. The 2022 census recorded 42,870 people, down from 44,248 in 2011. Postcode districts PA15, PA16 and PA19 cover the area, and the main roads recorded are the A8, A78, A770 and A771. Gourock is 3.4 km away and Port Glasgow 6.8 km, with Largs at 17.4 km and Johnstone at 20.6 km. Motorway services are a long way from Greenock, 46.8 km at the nearest, so an AdBlue warning is best not left until a long run.
roadsText: The A78, A8, A770 and A771 are the main roads recorded around Greenock. The nearest service areas are distant: Bothwell Services on the M74 at 46.8 km, Hamilton Services on the M74 at 49.3 km and Stirling Services on the M9 at 54.9 km. OpenStreetMap lists a site 13.3 km away as selling AdBlue at the pump. That map data is incomplete, so check closer to home as well.

name: Greenwich
intro: Covering almost 50 km² of southeast Greater London, the Royal Borough of Greenwich mixes historic, suburban and rapidly redeveloping districts. Greenwich Town and Park, Woolwich, Eltham, Greenwich Peninsula, Shooter's Hill and parts of Abbey Wood and Thamesmead all fall within it, and the council meets in Woolwich Town Hall. The borough was formed in 1965 from the former Metropolitan Borough of Greenwich and most of the Metropolitan Borough of Woolwich. The population is around 288,117. Main roads listed include the A2, A20, A102, A117, A205, A210, A2204 and A2213, and the postcode districts include SE3, SE7, SE9, SE10, SE12 and SE18. Lewisham is 5.6km away, Newham 6.1km and Bexley 7km. With that mix of districts, naming the area, such as Woolwich or Eltham, helps when describing where a vehicle with an AdBlue warning has stopped.
roadsText: Listed main roads for Greenwich are the A205, A2, A102, A2213, A2204, A210, A20 and A117. The closest listed service area is Thurrock Services on the M25 at 15.6km, then Clacket Lane Services on the M25 at 22.5km and Tollgate Services on the A2 at 22.7km. OpenStreetMap has a station at Catford (5km) and another 8.1km away listed as selling AdBlue at the pump, though its coverage is incomplete.

name: Grimsby
intro: Near the mouth of the Humber, on its south bank, Grimsby is a port town of 86,138 people (2021) and the administrative centre of North East Lincolnshire. It joins directly onto Cleethorpes to the south-east, and the two form one conurbation, so the built-up area a driver moves through is bigger than the town alone. Distances to other centres are long: Grimsby is 45 miles (72 km) north-east of Lincoln, 50 miles (80 km) east of Doncaster and 33 miles (53 km) from Hull by way of the Humber Bridge. Beyond Cleethorpes (4.3 km in a straight line) and Humberston and New Waltham (5.7 km), the next nearest town is Louth at 22.7 km. That is worth weighing up when the dashboard flags an AdBlue fault. Postcode districts are DN31, DN32, DN33, DN34 and DN37, and the main roads listed are all A roads, including the A180, A46, A16 and A1136.
roadsText: Main roads around Grimsby include the A16, A46, A180, A1136, A1243, A1031 and A1098; there is no motorway in the list. The nearest service area is Ulceby Truckstop on the A160, 14 km away in a straight line. After that the gap is wide: Showground Services on the A15 is 42.3 km away and Thorpe on the Hill Services on the A46 is 55.5 km.

name: Guildford
intro: Thought to take its name from a crossing of the River Wey, which flows through the town centre, Guildford is a town in west Surrey around 27 miles (43 km) south-west of central London. The town had about 77,000 people at the 2011 census and is the seat of the wider Borough of Guildford, which had around 152,148 inhabitants in 2025. Postcode districts are GU1, GU2 and GU4. The listed roads are all A roads, with the A3 and A31 joined by the A320, A25 and A281 among others. Farncombe is 6.1 km away, Woking 7.3 km and Godalming 7.9 km, so the surrounding towns are all close by. Anyone in Guildford with an AdBlue warning has a listed service area 7.8 km away on the A3.
roadsText: Around Guildford, the listed main roads are the A3, A31, A320, A25, A322, A246, A3100 and A281. Wisley Services on the A3 is the nearest listed service area, 7.8 km away. Cobham Services on the M25 is 13.1 km and Fleet Services on the M3 is 20.8 km. Wisley is the closest listed stop and sits on the A3, which also appears in the town's own road list.

name: Guisborough
intro: North of the North York Moors National Park, Guisborough is a market town and civil parish in the borough of Redcar and Cleveland. Roseberry Topping, a landmark in the national park, stands midway between the town and Great Ayton. The parish also covers Upleatham, Dunsdale and Newton under Roseberry, and at the 2011 census it had 17,777 residents, 16,979 of them in the town's built-up area. Guisborough is in the TS14 postcode district. Its nearest neighbours are Eston at 7.3 km and Redcar at 8.4 km, with Middlesbrough 10.4 km away and Thornaby-on-Tees, Billingham and Ingleby Barwick between 15.3 km and 16.8 km. For a van or diesel car, driving here ranges from local roads around the town to longer runs into neighbouring towns such as Middlesbrough.
roadsText: Teesside Truck Stop on the A66 is the closest service area to Guisborough, at 9.3 km. The next two are a good deal further: Wolviston Services on the A689 is 19.3 km away, and a southbound service area on the A19 is 20.9 km. Beyond that first stop, there is a fair distance to cover before the next services on a longer route.

name: Guiseley
intro: The A65 Otley Road passes through Guiseley and serves as its main shopping street. This small town in the City of Leeds, historically in the West Riding, sits south of Otley and Menston and is now a north-western suburb of Leeds, within the Guiseley and Rawdon ward. Guiseley with Rawdon had 22,347 residents at the 2011 census. The town uses the LS20 postcode district. Yeadon is about 3 km away, Otley 3.7 km, Baildon 5.2 km and Shipley 6.1 km. Guiseley railway station has regular services to Leeds, Bradford and Ilkley. For a driver with an AdBlue warning, the nearest listed service area is Hartshead Moor Services on the M62, around 18.1 km in a straight line, with Skelton Lake on the M1 about 19.5 km away.
roadsText: Guiseley is on the A65, which runs through the town as Otley Road. In a straight line, the nearest service areas are Hartshead Moor Services on the M62 (18.1 km), Skelton Lake Service Station on the M1 (19.5 km) and Wetherby Services on the A1(M) (23.7 km). A station in Leeds (LS9 0AS), about 19.5 km away, is listed on OpenStreetMap as selling AdBlue at the pump; the map's coverage is incomplete.

name: Hackney
intro: Mare Street is the historical and administrative heart of Hackney, an Inner London borough named after its principal district. The modern borough was formed in 1965 by merging the Metropolitan Borough of Hackney with the smaller Metropolitan Boroughs of Stoke Newington and Shoreditch. Its southern and eastern parts are popularly treated as east London, while the northwest belongs to north London. Hackney is bounded by Islington to the west, Haringey to the north, Waltham Forest to the north-east, Newham to the east, Tower Hamlets to the south-east and the City of London to the south-west. Around 258,464 people live here. Main roads listed include the A1, A10, A12, A102, A104, A106, A107 and A1205, and postcode districts include E2, E5, E8, E9, N1, N5, N16 and EC2A. With Islington just 2.7km away, a van on a Hackney round is rarely far from a borough boundary.
roadsText: Main roads in and around Hackney include the A104, A107, A10, A102, A106, A1205, A12 and A1. Listed service areas are London Gateway Services on the M1 at 16.6km, South Mimms Services on the A1(M) at 18.8km and Heston Services on the M4 at 23.6km. OpenStreetMap has a station 9.9km away and one at Catford, 12.4km away, listed as selling AdBlue at the pump; it is not a full list.

name: Haddington
intro: Lying about 17 miles (27 kilometres) east of Edinburgh, this East Lothian market town was one of the earliest settlements in Scotland to receive burgh status, under David I, and in the High Middle Ages it was the fourth-biggest town in Scotland. The Town House, completed in 1745, stands in the centre of the town, and other notable buildings include the Corn Exchange and the County Courthouse. Today Haddington has a population of around 10,360 and sits in the EH41 postcode district. The nearest towns are not right on the doorstep: Tranent is 10.5 km away, Prestonpans 12.1 km, Musselburgh 16.7 km and Dunbar 17.1 km. What matters most for a driver with an AdBlue warning is that the closest listed service area is only 6.1 km away, on the A1.
roadsText: MacMerry on the A1 is the closest service area listed for Haddington, 6.1 km away. Musselburgh Services, also on the A1, is 17.6 km away, and Dreghorn Services on the A720 is 28.6 km. With two of the three on the A1, that road is where most of the listed stopping options are for drivers in and around Haddington.

name: Hadfield
intro: Hadfield lies on the south side of the River Etherow, near the border with Greater Manchester and at the western edge of the Peak District. It is a High Peak town with 6,763 residents at the 2021 census, and it shares the SK13 postcode district with Glossop, which is just 3.2 km away. Several other towns are close by: Stalybridge is 4.9 km away, Hyde 5.6 km, Dukinfield 6.8 km, and Mossley and Romiley both 7.7 km. The nearest motorway services, by contrast, are more than 20 km away on the M62. For a van or diesel car that shows an AdBlue warning in Hadfield, it is more practical to plan a stop in advance than to rely on reaching a motorway service area.
roadsText: Moto Birch Services on the M62 is the closest service area to Hadfield, 20.3 km away. Knutsford Services on the M6 is 32.5 km off and Welcome Break Hartshead Moor on the M62 is 32.6 km away. A station about 12.5 km from Hadfield is listed on OpenStreetMap as selling AdBlue at the pump; because the map data is incomplete, closer forecourts may sell it as well.

name: Hailsham
intro: Near the Cuckmere River, Hailsham is a town, civil parish and the administrative centre of the Wealden district of East Sussex. It lies north of Eastbourne, 17 miles east of Brighton and 14 miles west of Hastings, and had 23,114 residents at the 2021 census. The town appears in Domesday Book and has a history of industry and agriculture. Addresses here fall in the BN27 postcode district. Polegate is 5.1 km away and Eastbourne 8.5 km, with Bexhill-on-Sea, Seaford and Uckfield between 13.5 and 16 km off. For a driver with an AdBlue warning, Hailsham is well placed for a nearby stop: Polegate Services on the A22 is only 4.3 km from the town centre in a straight line. Beyond that, the next listed service areas are more than 30 km away.
roadsText: Polegate Services on the A22 is the nearest listed service area to Hailsham, 4.3 km from the town centre in a straight line. The next two are both on the A23 and much further away: Pyecombe Services at 30.3 km and Ricebridge Services (Hickstead) at 33.4 km. In practice the A22 site is the realistic nearby option for a quick stop.

name: Hale
intro: South-east of Altrincham and 9 miles (14 km) south-west of Manchester, Hale is a village and electoral ward in the Metropolitan Borough of Trafford. It lies within the historic county boundaries of Cheshire, and its population at the 2021 census was 16,715. Postcode districts WA15 and M90 cover the area. Wythenshawe is about 4.4 km away and Altrincham 4.8 km, while Wilmslow is 6.3 km off and Sale 6.9 km. Cheadle is around 7.2 km away and Knutsford 7.6 km. All six of those places are within 7.6 km of Hale. For drivers dealing with an AdBlue warning, the useful detail is that the M6 service areas at Knutsford and Tabley Hill are both little more than 9 km away.
roadsText: Knutsford Services on the M6 is the nearest service area to Hale, about 9.1 km away, with Tabley Hill Service Station, also on the M6, at around 9.3 km. Lymm Services on the M6 is roughly 13.2 km off. OpenStreetMap has a station under Warrington, about 16.1 km away, and one under Manchester at 19.8 km listed as selling AdBlue at the pump. That data is incomplete.

name: Halesowen
intro: Once an exclave of Shropshire and part of Worcestershire from 1844, Halesowen is now a market town in the Metropolitan Borough of Dudley. It sits around 7 miles (11km) from Birmingham city centre and 6 miles from Dudley town centre, and the built-up area had 60,110 residents at the 2021 census. Postcodes include B62, B63, B64 and B65. The M5 heads the road list, alongside the A458, A456, A4036, A461, A491, A4123 and A459. Cradley Heath is only about 2.1km away, with Brierley Hill, Rowley Regis and Stourbridge all within 5km. For a diesel driver that means a lot of short, urban trips, but the M5 is close as well. The nearest service area is under 5km away, which helps if an AdBlue warning appears.
roadsText: Frankley services on the M5 is about 4.5km from Halesowen, the nearest service area by some way. Hopwood Park services on the M42 is 13km off and Hilton Park services on the M6 21.1km. OpenStreetMap lists a forecourt in Warley (6.1km), one at DY10 1JS (15.1km) and an HGV-only site in Birmingham (15.6km) as selling AdBlue at the pump, a list that is incomplete. Roads listed for the town are the M5, A458, A456, A4036, A461, A491, A4123 and A459.

name: Halifax
intro: Calderdale's administrative centre, Halifax sits in the eastern foothills of the Pennines in West Yorkshire and had 88,134 residents at the 2021 census. In the 15th century it became an economic hub of the old West Riding of Yorkshire, mainly through woollen manufacture, and the large Piece Hall square was later built in the town centre for trading wool. It was a mill town during the Industrial Revolution, and the Dean Clough Mill buildings survive as a landmark. Getting around is a matter of A roads. The main roads listed are the A629, A58, A646, A6026, A6036, A647, A6142 and A6139, with no motorway among them, so with the AdBlue light on, the nearest motorway service area is a run of more than 9 km. The HX1, HX2 and HX3 postcode districts cover the town. Elland is 5.7 km away as the crow flies and Brighouse 7 km, with Bradford at 10.8 km and Huddersfield at 10.9 km.
roadsText: All the main roads listed around Halifax are A roads: the A629, A58, A646, A6026, A6036, A647, A6142 and A6139. The nearest service area is Hartshead Moor on the M62, 9.3 km away as the crow flies. The next two are much further: Woolley Edge on the M1 and Hollin Bank Service Station on the M65 are each 25.2 km away.

name: Halstead
intro: In the Braintree district of Essex, Halstead lies on the River Colne, 6 miles (10 km) north-east of Braintree and 12 miles (19 km) north-west of Colchester. The town has a population of 13,902 and is covered by the CO9 postcode district. Braintree is the nearest of the neighbouring towns at 8.9 km, followed by Sudbury at 12.6 km and Witham at 15.6 km, while Colchester, Haverhill and Great Dunmow are all between 19 km and 21 km away. Service areas are not close: the nearest listed are Boreham Services on the A131, 22.5 km away in a straight line, and Ardleigh South Services on the A120 at 23.7 km. A driver whose van or diesel car shows an AdBlue warning in Halstead should factor in that distance before heading for one.
roadsText: The nearest service areas to Halstead are Boreham Services on the A131, 22.5 km away in a straight line, Ardleigh South Services on the A120 at 23.7 km, and Birchanger Green Services on the M11 at 31.4 km. All three are more than 20 km off, and road distances will be longer, so a services stop is a fair drive from CO9.

name: Hamilton
intro: Where the Avon Water meets the River Clyde, on the Clyde's south bank, Hamilton serves as the main administrative centre of South Lanarkshire and is the county town of the historic county of Lanarkshire. It lies 16 km southeast of Glasgow, 60 km southwest of Edinburgh and 120 km north of Carlisle. The town had 55,157 people in 2022 and anchors a wider settlement of 84,000 that includes Blantyre, Bothwell and Uddingston. ML3 is the postcode district. The M74 is the motorway on Hamilton's road list, alongside the A72, A721, A723, A724, A725, A749 and A7071, and two service areas on it are 2.5 km and 4.9 km from the town, which is convenient if a warning light comes on. Blantyre is 3.5 km away, Motherwell 4.7 km and Bellshill 5.8 km, with Larkhall at 6.8 km.
roadsText: The M74, A725, A7071, A724, A72, A723, A721 and A749 are the main roads recorded around Hamilton. Hamilton Services on the M74 is just 2.5 km away and Bothwell Services, also on the M74, is 4.9 km. The M74 Truck Stop is further at 17.1 km. OpenStreetMap lists a station in Glasgow (G11 6DN), 19.2 km away, as selling AdBlue at the pump, but that map data is incomplete.

name: Hammersmith and Fulham
intro: Two major east to west routes cross the London Borough of Hammersmith and Fulham: the A4 Great West Road and the A40 Westway. This West London borough forms part of Inner London. It was formed in 1965 as the London Borough of Hammersmith and took its current name in 1979. It borders Brent to the north, Kensington and Chelsea to the east, Wandsworth to the south, Richmond upon Thames to the south west, and Hounslow and Ealing to the west. Its population is around 182,187. The M4 is also among the main roads listed, with the A205, A217, A306, A316 and A3220, and postcode districts include W4, W6, W8, W11, W12, W14, SW5 and SW13. With the A4, A40 and M4 all in the road list, a diesel van here may be on a major through route rather than a side street when an AdBlue warning appears.
roadsText: Main roads around Hammersmith and Fulham include the M4, A306, A4, A3220, A316, A40, A217 and A205. Heston Services on the M4 is the nearest listed service area at 11.6km, followed by London Gateway Services on the M1 at 15.3km and South Mimms Services on the A1(M) at 21.3km. A station at Catford, 16.1km away, is listed as selling AdBlue at the pump in OpenStreetMap, though that data is incomplete.

name: Haringey
intro: Contrasts define the London Borough of Haringey, both in character and in the lie of the land. From the wooded high ground around Highgate and Muswell Hill, at 130 metres, the land falls sharply to the flat, low-lying land beside the River Lea in the east. Highgate, Muswell Hill and Crouch End are in the west of the borough, and Tottenham and Wood Green in the east. Covering more than 11 square miles, Haringey shares borders with Enfield, Waltham Forest, Hackney, Islington, Camden and Barnet. It has around 264,069 residents. A van's round here can take in steep climbs as well as flat roads, all within the same borough. Main roads listed include the A1, A10, A406, A503, A107, A1100, A104 and A400, and postcode districts include N4, N8, N10, N15, N17, N19 and N22.
roadsText: The A503, A107, A10, A406, A1, A400, A1100 and A104 are the main roads listed for Haringey. London Gateway Services on the M1 is 12.4km away, with South Mimms Services on the A1(M) at 14.1km and Heston Services on the M4 at 22.8km. A station 13.3km away and one at Catford, 17km away, are listed as selling AdBlue at the pump in OpenStreetMap, which is not a complete record.

name: Harlow
intro: Designated a new town in 1947, Harlow in west Essex was a small town until the mid-20th century. Housing estates, industrial areas and a new town centre followed, mostly to the west and south of the original settlement, which became known as Old Harlow. That is worth knowing when describing a location, since Old Harlow and the newer districts are distinct parts of town. Harlow lies on the south bank of the River Stort, which forms the county boundary with Hertfordshire, and the M11 motorway passes to the east. The built-up area had 93,580 people at the 2021 census. Sawbridgeworth is 5.2 km away, Epping 8.2 km and Hoddesdon 8.8 km, with Ware, Bishop's Stortford and Waltham Abbey all just under 12 km. Postcode districts are CM17, CM18, CM19 and CM20.
roadsText: The M11 passes the town, and the A414, A1025, A1169, A1019 and A1184 are also listed. Birchanger Green Services on the M11 is the closest service area at 12.6 km, with South Mimms Services on the A1(M) at 25.1 km and Boreham Services on the A131 at 27.7 km. A station in Bishop's Stortford (CM23 3LA), 10.8 km away, is listed on OpenStreetMap as selling AdBlue at the pump; that data is incomplete, so there may be others.

name: Harpenden
intro: A commuter town with a direct rail connection to Central London, Harpenden is a town and civil parish in the City and District of St Albans, Hertfordshire. Its built-up area had 30,674 people at the 2021 census, and the civil parish 31,128. Three main roads are listed for the town: the M1, A1081 and A5183, giving a driver motorway access as well as local A-roads. St Albans is 7 km away, Hatfield 9.8 km and Luton 10.3 km, with Hemel Hempstead and Welwyn Garden City both 10.7 km off, and Abbots Langley and Kings Langley 13.4 km. The postcode district is AL5. The nearest listed service areas are all more than 14 km away, so with an AdBlue warning on, it pays to know which of those neighbouring towns lies along your route.
roadsText: The M1, A1081 and A5183 are the roads listed for Harpenden, and none of the nearest services is on the doorstep. The closest service area is Bourne End Services on the A41, 14.9 km away, followed by South Mimms Services on the A1(M) at 16.5 km and Toddington Services on the M1 at 18.1 km.

name: Harrogate
intro: Historically part of the West Riding, Harrogate is a spa town in North Yorkshire that grew in the 17th century out of two smaller settlements, High Harrogate and Low Harrogate, and became known as 'The English Spa' in the Georgian era. Its population is put at 75,522. The Yorkshire Dales National Park and Nidderdale AONB are 13 miles (21 km) from the town centre, and Leeds Bradford Airport is 10 miles (16 km) to the south-west. No motorway appears among the main roads, which are the A61, A59, A661, A658, A6040 and A6055, so local driving with an AdBlue warning is on A roads. The HG1 and HG2 postcode districts cover it. Measured directly, Knaresborough is 5.3 km away, Wetherby 11.8 km and Otley 13.7 km, with Ripon at 16.8 km.
roadsText: Harrogate's main roads are the A61, A59, A661, A658, A6040 and A6055. The nearest service area is Wetherby on the A1(M), 12.3 km away measured directly. The next two are roughly twice as far: Skelton Lake Service Station on the M1 at 24.6 km and Bilbrough Top Service Area on the A64 at 25.1 km. Actual driving distances will be greater.

name: Harrow
intro: Three towns make up the London Borough of Harrow: Harrow, Pinner and Stanmore, with western parts of Edgware and Sudbury also inside it. The borough lies in west and north-west London and forms part of Outer London. It borders Barnet to the east of ancient Watling Street, now the A5 road, Brent to the southeast, Ealing to the south and Hillingdon to the west, with the Hertfordshire districts of Three Rivers and Hertsmere to the north. Its population is roughly 260,534. The M1 is among the main roads listed, along with the A41, A409, A404, A410, A4005, A4090 and A312, and the postcode districts include HA1, HA2, HA3, HA5 and HA7. Brent is 6km away, Bushey 6.5km and Watford 7.3km. With Hertfordshire districts along the northern edge, a van with an AdBlue warning in Harrow may be close to the county boundary.
roadsText: Main roads around Harrow include the M1, A41, A409, A4005, A404, A4090, A410 and A312.
