The nearest listed service area is London Gateway Services on the M1 at 6.8km, close enough to matter for a vehicle on that motorway. Heston Services on the M4 is 12.2km away and South Mimms Services on the A1(M) is 13.4km.

name: Hartlepool
intro: Part of the devolved Tees Valley area, Hartlepool is an industrial port town in County Durham, about 8 miles (13 km) north of Middlesbrough and 17 miles (27 km) south of Sunderland. Its built-up area had 87,984 residents at the 2021 Census. The old town was founded in the 7th century on a headland, around the monastery of Hartlepool Abbey, while West Hartlepool was created in 1835 after a new port and railway links were built. The two towns were merged into a single borough in 1967. The A19 and A689 are among the town's main roads, with the A178, A179, A1048, A1049 and A1086 also listed, and its postcode districts include TS24, TS25 and TS26. Billingham is 10.2km away, Peterlee 11.9km and Redcar 12.5km, so trips beyond the town cover some distance. For a van with an AdBlue warning, the nearest listed services are on the A19, 6.4km away.
roadsText: Hartlepool's main roads include the A689, A179, A19, A178, A1048, A1049 and A1086. Southbound services on the A19 are the closest listed at 6.4km, followed by Wolviston Services on the A689 at 8.5km and Teesside Truck Stop on the A66 at 11.6km. A station near Durham (DH6 3LJ), 14.1km away, is listed as selling AdBlue at the pump in OpenStreetMap; the data has gaps, so it may not be the closest option.

name: Harwich
intro: The northernmost coastal town in Essex, Harwich is one of the Haven ports on the North Sea coast, positioned on the estuaries of the Stour and Orwell. Its historic core stands at the end of a peninsula, and the built-up area now runs westwards to take in Dovercourt. The town has a population of 20,219 and is in the Tendring district and the CO12 postcode district. For a van or diesel car with an AdBlue warning, the nearest service areas are some way off: 18 km to Sprougton Road Services on the A14 and 19.8 km to Ardleigh South Services on the A120, both measured in a straight line. Felixstowe is only 5.4 km away, while Ipswich and Clacton-on-Sea are about 16 km away and Colchester 24.8 km.
roadsText: The closest service areas to Harwich are Sprougton Road Services on the A14, 18 km away in a straight line, and Ardleigh South Services on the A120 at 19.8 km. Beacon Hill Services on the A140 is 27.1 km away. Road distances will be longer than these straight-line figures, so build that into plans if an AdBlue warning appears in CO12.

name: Haslemere
intro: Many local roads around Haslemere are narrow and steep, and the urban areas of Haslemere and Shottermill are concentrated along the valleys of the young River Wey and its tributaries. That is worth knowing for anyone driving a van here. Haslemere is in south-west Surrey, around 38 miles (62 km) south-west of London, and forms a civil parish in the Borough of Waverley together with Shottermill, Grayswood, Hindhead and Beacon Hill. The county boundaries of Surrey, Hampshire and West Sussex meet at the west end of Shottermill, with the Surrey Hills National Landscape to the north of the town and the South Downs National Park to the south. Its population is 11,897 and its postcode district is GU27. If an AdBlue warning appears, the nearest listed service area is Liphook Services on the A3 at 7.1 km in a straight line. Godalming, the nearest town, is 12.4 km away.
roadsText: Liphook Services on the A3 is the closest listed service area to Haslemere, 7.1 km away in a straight line. Petersfield Services, also on the A3, is 18.5 km away and Fleet Services on the M3 is 25.1 km. Many of the roads in and around the town are narrow and steep, so the drive out to any of these may take longer than the distance suggests.

name: Haslingden
intro: High moorland surrounds Haslingden, reaching 370 metres (1,210 ft) to the north, Cribden at 396 metres (1,299 ft) to the east and Bull Hill at 418 metres (1,371 ft) to the south. The town is in the borough of Rossendale, Lancashire, 16 miles (26 km) north of Manchester, and at the 2021 census it had 15,969 residents including Helmshore. The BB4 postcode district covers the area. Rawtenstall is the nearest neighbouring town at about 3.7 km, with Ramsbottom at 6.5 km and Accrington at 6.8 km. Oswaldtwistle, Bacup and Darwen are all between 7.4 km and 9.3 km away. For a van or diesel car with an AdBlue warning, the nearest motorway service area is around 10.2 km away, at Blackburn with Darwen on the M65.
roadsText: Blackburn with Darwen Services on the M65 is the nearest service area to Haslingden, about 10.2 km away. Birch Services on the M62 is around 15.2 km off, and Hollin Bank Service Station on the M65 about 16.7 km. OpenStreetMap has a station under Manchester, roughly 17.4 km away, listed as selling AdBlue at the pump. Its records are incomplete, so somewhere closer may also sell it.

name: Hassocks and Hurstpierpoint
intro: Tufts of grass in the surrounding fields are thought to have given Hassocks its name. The village and civil parish is in the Mid Sussex District of West Sussex, about 7 miles (11 km) north of Brighton, and together with Hurstpierpoint it forms an area of 14,216 people in the BN6 postcode district. Until the 19th century Hassocks was just a collection of small houses and a coaching house; it grew once work started on the London to Brighton railway. Burgess Hill is the nearest town at 3.4 km, with Haywards Heath at 8.7 km and Brighton and Hove at 11.3 km. For an AdBlue warning, the A23 is the road to know: Ricebridge Services (Hickstead) is 4 km away in a straight line and Pyecombe Services 4.1 km. A station 11.3 km off is listed in OpenStreetMap as selling AdBlue at the pump.
roadsText: Hassocks and Hurstpierpoint have two service areas on the A23 within easy reach: Ricebridge Services (Hickstead) at 4 km and Pyecombe Services at 4.1 km, both straight-line distances. A third A23 site, Handcross, is 13.6 km away. OpenStreetMap lists a station 11.3 km from the area as selling AdBlue at the pump. The map is incomplete, so other forecourts nearer by may stock it too.

name: Hastings
intro: Hastings gave its name to the Battle of Hastings, fought 8 miles (13 km) to the north-west in 1066, and later became one of the medieval Cinque Ports. This seaside town and borough lies on the south coast of East Sussex, 53 miles (85 km) south-east of London and 24 miles (39 km) east of Lewes. It remains a popular seaside resort and a fishing port, with the UK's largest beach-based fishing fleet, and had an estimated population of 90,855 in 2025. Postcode districts are TN34, TN35, TN37 and TN38. Bexhill-on-Sea is 8.7 km away, but the next towns, Hailsham at 21.5 km and Eastbourne at 21.7 km, are much further. For a van or diesel car with an AdBlue warning, the nearest listed service area is 23.5 km away, so planning ahead matters.
roadsText: No motorway features in the road list for Hastings, which runs to the A21, A259, A2101, A2102, A2690, A2100, A28 and A2036. None of the listed service areas is close. Polegate Services on the A22 is the nearest at 23.5 km, Ashford International Truckstop on the A2070 is 36.7 km, and Folkestone Services on the M20 is 41.6 km. That makes it worth planning ahead when an AdBlue warning appears.

name: Hatfield
intro: Beside the A1(M), 20 miles (30 kilometres) north of London, Hatfield is a town and civil parish in the borough of Welwyn Hatfield with 41,265 people at the 2021 census. The settlement is of Saxon origin, and Hatfield House forms the nucleus of the old town. It was one of the post-war New Towns built around London and has much modernist architecture from that period. From the 1930s until the 1990s, aircraft design and manufacture employed more people there than any other industry, and the University of Hertfordshire is now based in the town. Direct trains run to London, and the number of commuters moving in has risen strongly. Alongside the A1(M), the A1001, A414, A1057, A1000, A6129 and A1081 are listed. Welwyn Garden City is 5 km away, St Albans 6.2 km and Potters Bar 8.1 km. Postcode districts are AL9 and AL10.
roadsText: The A1(M) runs beside Hatfield, and the A1001, A414, A1057, A1000, A6129 and A1081 are also listed. South Mimms Services on the A1(M) is the nearest service area, 8.5 km away. London Gateway Services on the M1 is 14.8 km off, and Bourne End Services on the A41 is 20.7 km away.

name: Havant
intro: In the south-east corner of Hampshire, Havant has Portsmouth to its south-west, Waterlooville to the north, Chichester to the east and Hayling Island to the south. Housing and population more than doubled in the 20 years after World War II, and the town is usually considered economically part of the Portsmouth conurbation. The town itself falls in the PO9 postcode district. For drivers, the road network is a big part of the picture: the M27 and A3(M) are both listed, along with the A27, A3, A259, A2030, A3023 and A397. Emsworth is 3.4km away, Waterlooville 3.8km and Portsmouth 7.3km, so much of the local driving is short runs within the conurbation, with motorway routes close at hand for longer trips.
roadsText: Havant has a long road list: the M27, A3(M), A27, A2030, A3023, A259, A3 and A397. Farlington Services on the A27 is the nearest service area, about 4.5km away. Further out are Petersfield Services on the A3 (16.8km) and Fontwell Services on the A27 (23.8km). A driver on the A27 with an AdBlue warning has a stop within a few kilometres of town at Farlington.

name: Haverfordwest
intro: As the county town of Pembrokeshire, Haverfordwest (Hwlffordd) is the county's most populous urban area, with 14,596 people in 2011, while the community itself had 12,042. It stands at the lowest bridging point of the Western Cleddau. Its suburbs include the former parish of Prendergast, Albert Town and Withybush, which takes in housing, retail parks, a hospital, an airport and a showground. The postcode district is SA61. Milford Haven is 12.2 km away, but beyond that the distances open up: Carmarthen is 45.7 km off, Llanelli 58.7 km and Swansea 74 km. That matters with an AdBlue warning, because the nearest listed service areas are on the M4, the closest 62.7 km away in a straight line, so there is no motorway stop anywhere near the town.
roadsText: Service areas are a long way from Haverfordwest. The nearest two are on the M4: Pont Abraham Services, 62.7 km away in a straight line, and Swansea West Services at 68.8 km. Glanusk Services on the A40 is the third, at 97 km. Road distances will be longer than all of these, so if an AdBlue warning comes on around SA61 it is better to act on it early than to plan around reaching a motorway stop.

name: Haverhill
intro: Next to the borders of Essex and Cambridgeshire, Haverhill is a market town and civil parish in the West Suffolk district of Suffolk. It lies about 14 miles (23 km) south-east of Cambridge and 47 miles (76 km) north-east of central London, and had a population of 27,500 in 2022. Main roads listed for the town are the A143, A1307, A1017 and A1092. Neighbouring towns are some distance away: Saffron Walden is 15.2 km off, Newmarket 18.5 km, Halstead 20.3 km and Sudbury 20.6 km, with Braintree at 23.6 km and Great Dunmow at 23.9 km. The postcode district is CB9. Those distances, and the distance to the nearest services set out below, are the main things to plan around when a van or diesel car flags an AdBlue problem.
roadsText: The A143, A1307, A1017 and A1092 are listed for Haverhill. The nearest service area is Four Went Ways Services on the A11, 15.8 km away. Birchanger Green Services on the M11 is 29.1 km off and Boreham Services on the A131 is 36.8 km away, so none of the three is close to the town.

name: Havering
intro: Romford is the principal town of Havering, the easternmost London borough, and other communities include Hornchurch, Upminster, Collier Row and Rainham. The borough is mainly suburban, with large areas of protected open space that include parts of the Metropolitan Green Belt. It has 259,552 residents and extends south into the London Riverside redevelopment area of the Thames Gateway. Its neighbours are Bexley across the River Thames, Barking and Dagenham, Redbridge, the Essex districts of Epping Forest and Brentwood, and Thurrock. The M25 is among the main roads listed, with the A127, A12, A118, A124, A125, A1251 and A1112, and postcode districts include RM1, RM2, RM3, RM7, RM11 and RM12. Brentwood is 7.8km away and South Ockendon 8.9km, so a van with an AdBlue warning in Havering is often only a short distance from Essex.
roadsText: Havering's listed roads are the M25, A127, A12, A118, A124, A1251, A125 and A1112. Thurrock Services on the M25 is 10.2km away, Orsett Cock Services on the A13 14.6km and Tollgate Services on the A2 20.4km. A station 10.2km away is listed as selling AdBlue at the pump in OpenStreetMap, though that source does not cover every forecourt.

name: Hawarden
intro: Home to Hawarden Castle, Hawarden (Penarlâg in Welsh) is a Flintshire village and community in the Deeside conurbation on the border between Wales and England, about 7 miles (11 km) from Chester. The community also takes in Ewloe, Mancot and Aston, and at the 2011 census it had 13,920 residents, while the Hawarden ward alone had 1,887. It is in the CH5 postcode district. The wooded Hawarden Park adjoins the village to the south, and the western part of the main street, called The Highway, begins at a crossroads with a fountain. Beyond Shotton, Queensferry and the Dee, Hawarden Bridge is an area of distribution and industrial premises. For a van or diesel car with an AdBlue warning, Chester West Services on the A55 is only 4.1 km away in a straight line, and Connah's Quay and Buckley are both within 4.9 km.
roadsText: Chester West Services on the A55 is the nearest service area to Hawarden, 4.1 km from the village in a straight line. Further out are Holt Road Services on the A5156 at 15.7 km and RoadChef Chester Services on the M56 at 16.5 km. With the A55 site so close, it is the obvious first stop for drivers around CH5 if an AdBlue message appears.

name: Hawick
intro: Deep in Teviotdale, where the Slitrig Water meets the River Teviot, Hawick is one of the furthest towns from the sea in Scotland. It is a market town in the Scottish Borders and the biggest town in the historic county of Roxburghshire, with a population of 13,512 in 2022. Jedburgh is 10 miles to the north-east and Selkirk 8.9 miles to the north-north-west. The town grew as a centre for textiles and remains an important regional centre for shopping, tourism and services. It is covered by the TD9 postcode district. Driving here involves real distances: beyond Jedburgh and Selkirk, Galashiels is 21.3 km away, while Mayfield and Penicuik are both more than 50 km off. The nearest listed motorway services are on the A74(M), over 45 km away in a straight line, so an AdBlue warning needs planning.
roadsText: Hawick is a long way from the nearest listed service areas, all on the A74(M): Annandale Water Services at 45.5 km, Gretna Green Services at 50 km and The 'fechan Truckstop at 50.7 km, measured in a straight line. Closer to home, a station in Galashiels, 19.8 km away, is listed in OpenStreetMap as selling AdBlue at the pump. OpenStreetMap does not record every site that sells AdBlue.

name: Haxby
intro: Just outside the York Outer Ring Road (A1237), Haxby is a town and civil parish in the City of York, near the New Earswick and Huntington areas to the south. It shares a continuous built-up area with Wigginton to the west, while open farmland runs north towards Sutton-on-the-Forest and Strensall. The parish had 8,428 residents at the 2011 census. Its centre, known as 'The Village', has been a conservation area since 1976. Postcodes here use YO32. Huntington is about 2.8 km away and York 6.4 km, with Pocklington about 21.4 km off. For an AdBlue warning, the nearest listed service area is Bilbrough Top on the A64, about 14.1 km in a straight line, with Wetherby Services on the A1(M) at about 20.8 km.
roadsText: Haxby sits just outside the A1237 York Outer Ring Road. The nearest service areas in a straight line are Bilbrough Top Service Area on the A64 (about 14.1 km), Wetherby Services on the A1(M) (20.8 km) and Ferrybridge Services on the M62 (37.3 km). The third is much further out than the first two, and road distances will be longer than these figures.

name: Haydock
intro: Since the 1930s the A580 East Lancashire Road, a dual carriageway connecting Liverpool and Manchester, has cut across the north side of Haydock, with several junctions serving St Helens and Haydock. Most of the village's residential estates and commercial property sit either side of the A599. To the south of the East Lancs road is large post-war housing, while the area to the north saw large-scale industrialisation. Haydock is a village in the Metropolitan Borough of St Helens, Merseyside, north-east of St Helens itself, and it had 11,416 residents at the 2011 Census. The WA11 postcode district covers it. Newton-le-Willows and Ashton-in-Makerfield are both about 3.3 km away, and St Helens 5 km. For a driver with an AdBlue warning, Burtonwood Services on the M62 is only about 6.2 km off.
roadsText: The A580 East Lancashire Road crosses the north side of Haydock, and the A599 runs through it. Burtonwood Services on the M62 is the nearest service area, about 6.2 km away, with Earlsfield Services on the M57 at 11.3 km and Rivington Services on the M61 at 15.8 km. OpenStreetMap has stations under Warrington at about 6.6 km and 11.1 km, and one named Old Meadow at 16.6 km, listed as selling AdBlue at the pump. Its records are incomplete.

name: Haywards Heath
intro: Commuting shapes Haywards Heath. With a fairly small number of jobs in the immediate area, many residents work remotely or travel daily by road or rail to London, Brighton, Crawley or Gatwick Airport. The town sits in West Sussex, 36 miles south of London, 14 miles north of Brighton and 13 miles south of Gatwick Airport, with Burgess Hill to the south-west and East Grinstead to the north-east. Its postcode districts are RH16 and RH17. The roads listed for the town are the A272, A273 and A2300, while the nearest service areas are on the A23 and M23. Burgess Hill is 5.5km away and Hassocks and Hurstpierpoint 8.7km, with Crawley at 14.1km. For a commuter's diesel car or a van with an AdBlue warning, the nearest roadside stops mean a run out of town to the A23 or M23.
roadsText: The A272, A273 and A2300 are the main roads listed around Haywards Heath. The nearest service areas are Ricebridge Services (Hickstead) on the A23 at 7.8km, Handcross on the A23 at 9.7km and Pease Pottage Services on the M23 at 11.8km. One station about 18.3km away is listed as selling AdBlue at the pump. OpenStreetMap data is incomplete, so other forecourts may stock it too.

name: Hazel Grove
intro: Although described as a village, Hazel Grove had a built-up area population of 20,170 at the 2021 census, as defined by the Office for National Statistics. It belongs to the Metropolitan Borough of Stockport and lies within the historic county boundaries of Cheshire, having become part of Greater Manchester in 1974. Postcode districts SK7 and SK2 cover the area. Several neighbouring places are very close: Poynton is about 3 km away, Bramhall 3.1 km and Marple 3.8 km, while Stockport is around 4.8 km and Cheadle Hulme 5 km. Romiley is about 5.2 km away. One point worth knowing if an AdBlue warning appears is that the nearest motorway service areas are all more than 20 km away, so they are not a quick detour from here.
roadsText: The closest motorway service areas are on the M6: Knutsford Services, about 20.6 km from Hazel Grove, and Tabley Hill Service Station, about 21.2 km. Birch Services on the M62 is around 22.7 km off. OpenStreetMap has a site roughly 16 km away listed as selling AdBlue at the pump. Its records are incomplete, so stations nearer Hazel Grove may also stock it, and it is worth checking locally before a long detour.

name: Hazlemere
intro: Sitting on the A404 between High Wycombe and Amersham, Hazlemere is a Buckinghamshire village and civil parish north-east of High Wycombe. The B474 meets the A404 at Hazlemere. To the north is the hamlet of Holmer Green, which falls in the civil parish of Little Missenden. The area covered here has about 20,006 residents and uses the HP15 postcode district. High Wycombe is 3.6 km away, Flackwell Heath and Wooburn Green 5.4 km and Beaconsfield 6.2 km, with Amersham at 7.4 km, Chesham at 9.5 km and Marlow at 10 km. For a van or diesel car with an AdBlue warning, the nearest listed motorway services are Beaconsfield Services on the M40, 8.7 km away in a straight line. The other two listed sites are on A roads and further off, at 15.6 km and 22.3 km.
roadsText: Hazlemere is on the A404, which meets the B474 in the village. The nearest listed service area is Beaconsfield Services on the M40, 8.7 km away in a straight line. Bourne End Services on the A41 is 15.6 km away and Thame Services on the A418 is 22.3 km. Expect road distances to be longer than these figures.

name: Heanor
intro: Eight miles north-east of Derby, Heanor is a town in the Amber Valley district of Derbyshire. With the adjacent village of Loscoe it forms the civil parish of Heanor and Loscoe, which had 17,251 residents at the 2011 census, and the town is covered by the DE75 postcode district. What stands out for drivers is how tightly it sits among its neighbours: Eastwood is 3.5 km away, Ripley 4.7 km, Ilkeston 6.1 km and Somercotes and Swanwick 7.2 km, with Belper at 8.7 km and Hucknall at 9.3 km. Main roads recorded around the town include the A610, A608 and A6007. When an AdBlue warning comes on, the nearest listed service area is Trowell Services on the M1, 7.8 km from the town.
roadsText: Main roads through and around Heanor include the A610, A608, A6007, A609 and A6096. The nearest service areas are Trowell Services on the M1 at 7.8 km, Tibshelf Services, also on the M1, at 13.6 km, and Trent Bridge Services on the A6011 at 16 km. One station about 18.3 km from the town is listed on OpenStreetMap as selling AdBlue at the pump. That data is incomplete, so it may not show every outlet nearer to Heanor.

name: Hebburn
intro: Facing Wallsend and Walker across the River Tyne, Hebburn sits on the south bank between Gateshead and Jarrow, in the South Tyneside borough of Tyne and Wear. It was historically part of County Durham and became part of Tyne and Wear in 1974. The built-up area had 21,345 residents at the 2021 census, and the town is split between the NE31 and NE32 postcode districts. The neighbouring towns are close: Jarrow is 2.4 km away, Wallsend 3 km, Tynemouth 5.4 km, Gateshead 5.6 km, South Shields 5.8 km and Longbenton 6.5 km. That keeps many journeys from Hebburn short, the kind of local use a van or diesel car sees day to day, with the nearest service area, Washington on the A1(M), 9.9 km away.
roadsText: The closest service area to Hebburn is Washington on the A1(M), 9.9 km away. Seaton Burn on the A19 is 12.7 km, and Easington, also on the A19, is 21.4 km. A station in Newcastle upon Tyne, 9 km from the town, is listed in OpenStreetMap as selling AdBlue at the pump. OpenStreetMap coverage is incomplete, so treat this as a starting point rather than a full picture.

name: Heckmondwike
intro: Nine miles (14 km) south-west of Leeds, Heckmondwike is a Kirklees town that forms part of the Heavy Woollen District and sits in the Spen Valley parliamentary constituency. It was historically in the West Riding, and its population rose from an estimated 16,986 in 2011 to 18,149 at the 2021 census. Postcodes in the town fall in WF16, WF15 and WF17. Neighbouring towns are very close: Liversedge is about 2 km away, Batley 2.3 km, Cleckheaton 3.3 km, Dewsbury 3.9 km and Mirfield 4 km. For an AdBlue warning, the nearest listed service area is Hartshead Moor Services on the M62, about 4.9 km away in a straight line, which puts motorway services within a short drive.
roadsText: Hartshead Moor Services on the M62 is the nearest service area to Heckmondwike, about 4.9 km in a straight line. Woolley Edge Services on the M1 is about 12.9 km away and Skelton Lake Service Station, also on the M1, about 14.8 km. OpenStreetMap lists a station in Leeds (LS9 0AS), about 14.9 km away, as selling AdBlue at the pump, though the map does not capture every station that sells it.

name: Hedge End
intro: East of the City of Southampton, Hedge End is a Hampshire town and civil parish in the Borough of Eastleigh, and part of the Southampton Urban Area. It adjoins West End and Botley, and grew from a hamlet that developed on Botley Common after 1250, when the land was granted to the men of Botley as common pasture. Today the town has around 23,195 residents in the SO30 postcode district. West End is 2.5 km from the centre, Southampton 6.1 km and Eastleigh 6.4 km, with Locks Heath at 6.8 km and Chandler's Ford and Hythe and Dibden Purlieu both 9.9 km away. For a van or diesel car with an AdBlue warning, the nearest listed motorway service area is Rownhams Services on the M27, 11.2 km away in a straight line.
roadsText: Rownhams Services on the M27 is the nearest listed service area to Hedge End, 11.2 km away measured in a straight line. West Wellow Services on the A36 is 17 km away and Farlington Services on the A27 is 20.4 km away. The road distance to each will be longer than these figures, which is worth bearing in mind if an AdBlue warning has already come on.

name: Helensburgh
intro: Positioned on the north side of the Firth of Clyde at the mouth of the Gareloch, Helensburgh is a town and former burgh with 14,127 residents in 2022. It was historically in Dunbartonshire and became part of Argyll and Bute following the local government reorganisation of 1996. The postcode district is G84. Distances need care here. Greenock is about 7.4 km away in a straight line, Gourock 8.5 km, Port Glasgow 9.5 km and Dumbarton 12.2 km, with Erskine and Clydebank more than 20 km off, and straight-line figures can understate a journey by road. For a van or diesel car with an AdBlue warning, motorway service areas are distant: the nearest is about 46.7 km away on the M74, and the next two, on the M74 and M9, are about 49.5 km and 50.6 km out. A station about 11.7 km away is listed as selling AdBlue at the pump.
roadsText: Helensburgh is a long way from a motorway service area. Bothwell Services on the M74 is about 46.7 km away in a straight line, Hamilton Services on the M74 about 49.5 km and Stirling Services on the M9 about 50.6 km. A station about 11.7 km away is listed in OpenStreetMap as selling AdBlue at the pump, but that data is incomplete, so treat it as one known option.

name: Helston
intro: The most southerly town on the island of Great Britain, Helston stands at the northern end of the Lizard Peninsula in Cornwall, about 12 miles (19.3 km) east of Penzance and 9 miles (14.5 km) south-west of Falmouth. The built-up area had 11,360 residents at the 2021 census, and the town is covered by the TR13 postcode district. A former stannary and cattle market town, it is best known for the annual Furry Dance, also called the Flora Dance. For anyone driving a van or diesel car here, remoteness is the point to note: the nearest listed service area, Cornwall Services on the A30, is 48.4 km away in a straight line. Camborne, Penryn and Falmouth are all within 14.5 km, with Redruth at 15.1 km and Truro at 23.8 km.
roadsText: Helston is a long way from any listed service area. The nearest is Cornwall Services on the A30, 48.4 km from the town in a straight line. Saltash Services on the A388 is 81.5 km away and Roundswell Service Area on the A39 is 135.8 km. With services that far off, an AdBlue warning on the Lizard is best planned for rather than left to chance.

name: Hemel Hempstead
intro: Watford, St Albans and Berkhamsted are among the towns near Hemel Hempstead, which lies in the Dacorum district of Hertfordshire, 24 miles (39 km) north-west of London. It has existed since at least the 8th century and received its town charter from Henry VIII in 1539, and it has expanded and developed in recent decades since being designated a New Town after the Second World War. The population was 95,961 at the 2021 census. Two motorways, the M1 and M25, appear among the main roads listed for the town, along with the A414 and A41, so motorway driving is close at hand for anyone with a diesel van or car here. Abbots Langley and Kings Langley are 5.2 km away, Berkhamsted 7.5 km and St Albans 9.9 km, with Harpenden, Chesham and Chorleywood all within 11.6 km. Hemel Hempstead's postcode districts are HP1, HP2 and HP3.
roadsText: The M1 and M25 are the motorways listed for Hemel Hempstead, together with the A414, A41, A4146, A4251 and A4147. Bourne End Services on the A41 is the nearest service area, 4.7 km away. South Mimms Services on the A1(M) is 18 km off and London Gateway Services on the M1 is 19 km away.

name: Henley-on-Thames
intro: On the River Thames, close to where Oxfordshire, Berkshire and Buckinghamshire meet, Henley-on-Thames is a town and civil parish in the South Oxfordshire district. It had 12,186 residents at the 2021 census and is covered by the RG9 postcode district. Reading lies 9 miles (14 km) to the south-west and Maidenhead 7 miles (11 km) to the east, while Oxford is 23 miles (37 km) away and London 37 miles (60 km) by road. Closer neighbours include Caversham at 7.2 km, Woodley at 9 km and Marlow at 10.4 km. Because the town sits so near the meeting point of three counties, a short drive from Henley can take you into Berkshire or Buckinghamshire. For a van or diesel car showing an AdBlue warning, the nearest listed service area is on the M4 near Reading, 14.8 km away in a straight line, so services are not on the doorstep.
roadsText: No listed service area is especially close to Henley-on-Thames. The nearest listed sites, measured in a straight line, are Reading Services on the M4 at 14.8 km, Beaconsfield Services on the M40 at 20.5 km and Thame Services on the A418 at 25.4 km. A station at Swallowfield near Reading (RG7 1LZ), 15.9 km away, is listed on OpenStreetMap as selling AdBlue at the pump. That map data is incomplete, so other sites may sell it too.

name: Hereford
intro: With about 61,900 residents in 2024, Hereford is the largest settlement in Herefordshire as well as its county town, and it sits on the banks of the River Wye. The city lies 16 miles (26km) east of the Welsh border, 23 miles north-west of Gloucester and 24 miles south-west of Worcester. Its postcode districts include HR1 and HR4. Every road on the local list is an A-road: the A49, A438, A465, A4103, A4193, A4110 and A480. The nearest towns are all some way off, with Ross-on-Wye about 18.3km away, Leominster 19km and Monmouth 27km. For a van or diesel driver, that means longer A-road journeys and more distance between stops, with the nearest service area 17.5km from the city. An AdBlue warning here is worth taking seriously early rather than leaving until the next town.
roadsText: All three of the nearest service areas to Hereford are at least 17.5km away. The closest is Ross Spur services on the M50, followed by Symonds Yat services on the A40 at about 22.9km and Monmouth A40 services at 32.1km. The city's listed roads are the A49, A438, A465, A4103, A4193, A4110 and A480, with no motorway among them. Drivers in HR1 or HR4 with an AdBlue warning should plan where to pull in rather than rely on passing services.

name: Herne
intro: Divided by the Thanet Way from the seaside resort of Herne Bay, 2 km away, Herne is a village in the civil parish of Herne and Broomfield, in Kent's Canterbury district. The former hamlet of Hunters Forstal lies between Herne and Broomfield, and Herne Common is to the south on the A291 road. The area has a population of 14,874 and uses the CT6 postcode district. Whitstable is 6.6 km away and Canterbury 8.9 km, while Faversham, Margate and Ramsgate are all more than 17 km off. Services are not close at hand for a van or diesel car with an AdBlue warning. The nearest listed service area is Minster Services on the A299, 13.3 km away in a straight line, and the next two are both more than 27 km away.
roadsText: The Thanet Way divides Herne from Herne Bay, and Herne Common lies to the south on the A291. The nearest listed service area is Minster Services on the A299, 13.3 km away in a straight line. Whitfield Services on the A2 (27.1 km) and Folkestone Services on the M20 (29.3 km) are a long way further, so the A299 site is the closer choice by some distance.

name: Herne Bay
intro: On the north coast of Kent, Herne Bay is a seaside town north of Canterbury and east of Whitstable. It belongs to the City of Canterbury local government district but remains a separate town, with countryside between it and the city. The town began as a small shipping community receiving goods and passengers from London on their way to Canterbury and Dover, then grew as a seaside resort in the early 19th century. Herne is just 2 km away, with Whitstable at 8 km and Canterbury at 10.9 km, and Margate and Ramsgate are 15.9 km and 18.4 km off. The town is covered by the CT6 postcode district. Main roads listed around it are the A299, A28, A291 and A2990, and for a driver with an AdBlue warning, the nearest listed service area, Minster Services, is on the A299 at 12.3 km.
roadsText: Main roads listed around Herne Bay are the A299, A28, A291 and A2990. The closest listed service area is Minster Services on the A299, 12.3 km away in a straight line, so it sits on one of the town's own main roads. Further out are Whitfield Services on the A2 at 27.9 km and Folkestone Services on the M20 at 31.1 km.

name: Hersham
intro: Joined to Walton-on-Thames, its post town, to the north and north-west, and to Esher on the east, Hersham is a suburban village in Surrey's Elmbridge district. It lies within the M25 and the Greater London Built-up Area, with a mixture of low and high rise housing and four technology and trading estates. Considerable land within its bounds is wooded or farmed, much of it Metropolitan Green Belt. Hersham has a population of 12,622 and its postcode district is KT12. Walton-on-Thames is 2.1 km away, Weybridge 3.5 km and Cobham 3.9 km, with Byfleet, West Molesey and Sunbury-on-Thames all under 5 km. If a van or diesel car shows an AdBlue warning, Cobham Services on the M25 is the nearest listed service area at 6.9 km in a straight line, with Wisley Services on the A3 at 10.2 km.
roadsText: Hersham lies within the M25, and Cobham Services on that motorway is the nearest listed service area at 6.9 km in a straight line. Wisley Services on the A3 is 10.2 km away and Heston Services on the M4 13.5 km. Those are straight-line distances, and the route by road to each will be longer, which is worth factoring in when an AdBlue warning is already showing.

name: Hertford
intro: The county of Hertfordshire takes its name from Hertford, its county town, which grew around a ford on the River Lea near its confluences with the Mimram, Beane and Rib. It lies 20 miles (32 km) north of Charing Cross. Fortified settlements were set up on each side of the ford in 913 AD, and Hertford Castle was built shortly after the Norman Conquest. Both the county council and East Hertfordshire District Council have their main offices here, and two railway lines connect the town to London, which makes it popular with commuters. The built-up area had 28,800 people at the 2021 census. Main roads listed are the A414, A10, A602, A119 and A1170. Ware is only 4.1 km away, Hoddesdon 6.7 km and Welwyn Garden City 7.5 km, with Cheshunt at 10.4 km and Hatfield 10.8 km. Postcode districts are SG13 and SG14.
roadsText: Listed roads are the A414, A10, A602, A119 and A1170. South Mimms Services on the A1(M) is 15.4 km away, Birchanger Green Services on the M11 20.9 km and London Gateway Services on the M1 22.2 km. A station in Bishop's Stortford (CM23 3LA), 18.6 km away, is listed on OpenStreetMap as selling AdBlue at the pump; OpenStreetMap's records of this are incomplete.

name: Hessle
intro: Where the Humber Bridge crosses the estuary, Hessle sits on the north bank, 5 miles (8 km) west of Kingston upon Hull in the East Riding of Yorkshire. It is part of a larger urban area with Hull and several villages but is not part of the city itself. The parish had 15,485 residents at the 2021 census, an increase on the 15,000 recorded in 2011, and the town uses the HU13 postcode district. Willerby and Anlaby is about 3 km away, Barton-upon-Humber 4.5 km, and Cottingham and Brough each about 7 km. Service areas are further away. The nearest listed is Ulceby Truckstop on the A160, about 15.7 km in a straight line, while the closest motorway services, Doncaster (North) Services on the M180, is about 38.9 km away, which matters for anyone with an AdBlue warning.
roadsText: Ulceby Truckstop on the A160 is the nearest service area to Hessle, about 15.7 km away in a straight line. The next two are much further: Doncaster (North) Services on the M180 at 38.9 km and Showground Services on the A15 at 48.7 km. Only one of the listed service areas is within 20 km, and road distances will be longer than these straight-line figures.

name: Heswall
intro: A town on the Wirral Peninsula, Heswall was historically part of Cheshire and became part of the borough of Wirral, in Merseyside, in 1974 when local government was reorganised. At the 2021 census its built-up area had 29,075 residents. The CH60 and CH61 postcode districts cover the town. Its nearest neighbours are Neston at 5.1 km, West Kirby at 5.9 km, Birkenhead at 6.2 km and Bebington at 6.7 km, with Wallasey at 9.5 km and Flint at 10.3 km. The M53 is the motorway listed for the area, with the A540, A551 and A552 among the A roads. If an AdBlue warning shows, it helps to know that the nearest service areas are on the A55, 15.2 km and 16 km away, so a stop needs a little planning.
roadsText: The M53 is listed for Heswall, along with the A552, A540, A551, A5137 and A5027. The two nearest service areas are both on the A55: Singing Kettle Services at 15.2 km and Chester West Services at 16 km. Earlsfield Services on the M57 is 20.9 km away. An HGV-only refuelling site in Liverpool (L5 9XN), 12.6 km away, is listed on OpenStreetMap as selling AdBlue at the pump; the map is not a complete record.

name: Hexham
intro: Close to Hadrian's Wall, Hexham is a market town on the south bank of the River Tyne in Northumberland, near Warden, where the North Tyne and South Tyne join to form the river. It was the administrative centre of the Tynedale district from 1974 to 2009, and the 2011 census recorded 13,097 people. Smaller towns and villages surround it: Corbridge, Riding Mill, Stocksfield and Wylam to the east, Acomb and Bellingham to the north, Allendale to the south, and Haydon Bridge, Bardon Mill and Haltwhistle to the west. Newcastle upon Tyne is 40 km to the east and Carlisle 60 km to the west, while Prudhoe is 16.3 km away and Consett 21.4 km. The town is in the NE46 postcode district, and a van or diesel car based here tends to cover long distances between places.
roadsText: Service areas are a long way from Hexham. The closest, Seaton Burn on the A19, is 31.7 km away, Washington services on the A1(M) is 35.9 km, and Durham services, also on the A1(M), is 45.8 km. With stops that far out, a driver who sees an AdBlue warning on a run around Hexham should not count on reaching a service area quickly.

name: Heysham
intro: Ferries to the Isle of Man and Ireland sail from Heysham, a coastal village in the Lancaster district of Lancashire that overlooks Morecambe Bay. It is also the site of two nuclear power stations. The village's postcode district is LA3. Morecambe is just 2.6 km away and Lancaster 5.5 km, while the next nearest towns, Fleetwood at 18.5 km and Ulverston at 20.2 km, are much further. For a van or diesel car with an AdBlue warning, the nearest service areas are all on the M6, starting with Lancaster Services 13.1 km away. Anyone heading for a ferry with a warning light on may want to deal with it before the crossing rather than after.
roadsText: The nearest service areas to Heysham are all on the M6: Lancaster Services at 13.1 km, Burton-in-Kendal Services at 16.8 km and Killington Lake Services at 33 km. Morecambe (2.6 km) and Lancaster (5.5 km) are the closest towns. With even the nearest of those service areas more than 13 km away, a stop is worth planning before a longer trip.

name: Heywood
intro: Open moorland, the Cheesden Valley and the Pennines lie to the north of Heywood, while Middleton is to the south. The town is in the borough of Rochdale, on the south bank of the River Roch, 2 miles east of Bury, 4 miles south-west of Rochdale and 8 miles north of Manchester. The Anglo-Saxons divided the wooded land into heys, or fenced clearings, and the town later grew into a mill town and coal mining district, becoming a municipal borough in 1881. Today the OL10 and OL11 postcode districts cover Heywood. It is well placed for motorway driving, with the M62, M66, M60 and A627(M) all listed among its roads. That helps if an AdBlue warning appears, since Birch Services on the M62 is only 2.1 km away.
roadsText: Heywood's listed roads include the M62, M66, M60 and A627(M), as well as the A58, A664, A644 and A56. Birch Services on the M62 is just 2.1 km away; the next nearest, Blackburn with Darwen Services on the M65 and Rivington Services on the M61, are 21.8 km and 23.1 km out. A station in Manchester (M25 3AJ) at 6.8 km and another at 9.2 km are listed on OpenStreetMap as selling AdBlue at the pump. That data is incomplete.

name: High Wycombe
intro: Often just called Wycombe, this Buckinghamshire market town lies in the valley of the River Wye, surrounded by the Chiltern Hills. Its built-up area had 83,535 residents at the 2021 census, making it the largest town in the ceremonial county. It is 29 miles (47 km) west-northwest of Charing Cross in London and 8 miles (13 km) north of Maidenhead. Postcode districts include HP10 to HP13 and HP15. The M40 is the motorway listed for the area, alongside the A40, A404 and A4010. Neighbouring places are close: Hazlemere is only 3.6 km away, Marlow 6.6 km and Beaconsfield 6.9 km. A driver with an AdBlue warning in or around High Wycombe will find the nearest listed service area on the M40, 9.1 km away.
roadsText: Alongside the M40, the main roads listed for High Wycombe are the A40, A404, A4010, A4128, A4094 and A4155. Beaconsfield Services on the M40 is the closest listed service area, 9.1 km away. Bourne End Services on the A41 is 19.2 km and Thame Services on the A418 is 21.6 km. For most drivers in the town, the M40 stop is the nearest listed option by a clear margin.

name: Hillingdon
intro: London's westernmost borough, Hillingdon is the second largest of the 32 London boroughs by area and includes Heathrow Airport and Brunel University. Its main towns are Hayes, Ruislip, Northwood, West Drayton and Uxbridge. It is also the third least densely populated London borough, because of rural land in the north, RAF Northolt Aerodrome and Heathrow itself. For drivers, the key point is that three motorways, the M25, M40 and M4, appear in the borough's main road list, alongside the A40, A312, A437, A4020 and A408. A diesel car or van here may be on a motorway rather than a local street when an AdBlue warning appears. Its postcode districts include UB3, UB4, UB7, UB8, UB10 and UB11, and the borough has around 307,089 residents. Ealing is 6.7km away, Hounslow 9km and Slough 10.3km.
roadsText: Hillingdon's road list takes in the M25, M40, M4, A40, A312, A437, A4020 and A408. Heston Services on the M4 is only 6.5km away, followed by Beaconsfield Services on the M40 at 13.9km and London Gateway Services on the M1 at 16.4km. With the M4 and M40 both in the road list, Heston and Beaconsfield are the most likely stopping points for a vehicle already on one of those motorways when a warning appears.

name: Hinckley
intro: Roughly halfway between Leicester and Coventry, on the border with Warwickshire, Hinckley is a market town in south-west Leicestershire. It is the county's third largest settlement after Leicester and Loughborough, with a population of 50,729, and forms an urban area with the large village of Burbage to the south. The town is close to Nuneaton and to Watling Street. Its postcode district is LE10. The M69 is among the main roads, alongside the A5, A47, A447 and A4254. Earl Shilton is about 5.2 km away and Nuneaton 5.7 km, with Bedworth at 10.7 km and Lutterworth at 12.8 km. The nearest service areas are all more than 13 km away, on the M6 and M1, so a driver with an AdBlue warning around Hinckley has some distance to cover to reach one.
roadsText: The main roads listed for Hinckley are the M69, A5, A47, A447 and A4254. The nearest service areas are Corley Services on the M6, about 13.9 km away, Leicester Forest East Services on the M1 at 14.4 km, and Rugby Services on the M6 at 16.9 km. An Asda station around 13 km away is listed in OpenStreetMap as selling AdBlue at the pump, though that data is incomplete.

name: Hindley
intro: Within the wider Greater Manchester Urban Area, Hindley is a town in the Metropolitan Borough of Wigan, 4.8 km east of Wigan itself. It includes Hindley Green and borders Ince-in-Makerfield, Aspull and Westhoughton, as well as Atherton and Westleigh in the former borough of Leigh. The town covers 2,580 acres and had a population of 28,000 at the 2011 census. It is in the WN2 postcode district. Neighbours are very close: Platt Bridge and Abram and Ince-in-Makerfield are both 2.4 km away, Westhoughton 3.7 km, Leigh 4.6 km and Wigan 5.3 km. Main roads around Hindley include the M61 and M6 plus the A58, A577, A49, A6, A6027 and A579, so local driving mixes short trips between joined-up towns with easy access to two motorways.
roadsText: Hindley's main roads include the M61 and M6, with the A58, A577, A49, A6, A6027 and A579. Rivington services on the M61 is 7.2 km away, Charnock Richard on the M6 13.2 km and Burtonwood on the M62 13.8 km. Stations listed in OpenStreetMap as selling AdBlue at the pump include two in Warrington, at 13.3 km and 15 km, and one in Manchester at 18.8 km. The data is incomplete.

name: Hitchin
intro: In the valley of the River Hiz, at the north-eastern end of the Chiltern Hills, Hitchin is a market town in North Hertfordshire dating from at least the 7th century. It is 16 miles (26 km) north-west of the county town of Hertford and 35 miles (56 km) north of London, and had 35,220 people at the 2021 census. The town grew around a market place on the western bank of the Hiz. Its ancient parish covered a large rural area, including hamlets such as Langley, Preston, St Ippolyts and Walsworth that later became separate parishes, and the town historically served as the market for the surrounding farmland. For drivers, the A1(M) is listed along with the A505, A602, A600 and A1072. Letchworth is 4.4 km away, Baldock 6.9 km, and Stotfold and Stevenage both 7.3 km. Postcode districts are SG4 and SG5.
roadsText: Hitchin's listed roads are the A1(M), A505, A602, A600 and A1072. Baldock Services on the A1(M) is the closest service area, 8.3 km away. Toddington Services on the M1 is 15.9 km off, and Bedford Services on the A421 is 22.2 km away, so the A1(M) offers the nearest services to the town.

name: Hockley and Hawkwell
intro: Between Rayleigh and Rochford, and more broadly between Chelmsford and Southend-on-Sea, Hockley has grown until it joins the neighbouring village of Hawkwell. The Office for National Statistics now treats the two as a single built-up area, Hockley and Hawkwell, which had 15,425 residents in 2021. The area is in the Rochford District of Essex and the SS5 postcode district, and Hockley came to prominence when the railway arrived in the 1890s. Neighbouring towns are close together here: Rochford is 3.8 km away, Rayleigh 4.3 km, South Woodham Ferrers 5.4 km and Southend-on-Sea 6.2 km. Service areas are further away, with Boreham Services on the A131 the nearest listed at 19.2 km in a straight line, so a services stop is not a quick option if an AdBlue warning appears.
roadsText: The nearest service areas to Hockley and Hawkwell are Boreham Services on the A131, 19.2 km away in a straight line, Orsett Cock Services on the A13 at 20.6 km and Tollgate Services on the A2 at 29.2 km. OpenStreetMap lists lorry pumps at a site in Chelmsford (CM2 5PY), 19.1 km off, as selling AdBlue at the pump; they are mapped as HGV-only. That data is incomplete, so other forecourts may also sell AdBlue.

name: Hoddesdon
intro: Although it is in Hertfordshire, Hoddesdon lies entirely within the Greater London Urban Area. A town in the Borough of Broxbourne, it sits on the River Lea and the Lee Navigation, along with the New River, and borders Ware to the north, Nazeing in Essex to the east and Broxbourne to the south. The Prime Meridian passes just east of the town. Rye House railway station serves it, as does nearby Broxbourne station. It was the second most populated town in Broxbourne at the 2011 census. Neighbouring towns are close by: Cheshunt is 6.1 km away, Ware 6.2 km, Hertford 6.7 km, Waltham Cross 7.8 km, Waltham Abbey 8 km and Harlow 8.8 km. The main roads listed are the A10 and A414, with the A1170, A1169 and A119. Postcode districts are EN10 and EN11.
roadsText: Listed roads are the A10, A414, A1170, A1169 and A119. The nearest service areas are some way off: South Mimms Services on the A1(M) at 16.6 km, Birchanger Green Services on the M11 at 18.9 km and London Gateway Services on the M1 at 22.5 km. A station in Bishop's Stortford (CM23 3LA), 16.6 km away, is listed on OpenStreetMap as selling AdBlue at the pump, though that data is incomplete.

name: Holyhead
intro: Holy Island, bounded by the Irish Sea to the north and separated from Anglesey by the narrow Cymyran Strait, is home to Holyhead (Caergybi), the largest town in the Isle of Anglesey county. The Port of Holyhead is a major Irish Sea port for connections towards Ireland. The A5 and the railway reach the island over a mid-19th-century causeway known locally as the Cobb, and the A55 dual carriageway runs parallel on a modern causeway. The town proper had 12,084 people at the 2021 census and is in the LL65 postcode district. Other towns are a long way off, with Bangor 34 km away and Llandudno 53.2 km. That makes Parc Cybi, a service area on the A55 just 1.6 km away, the one to note if an AdBlue warning comes on.
roadsText: Holyhead is reached by the A5, which crosses to Holy Island on the Cobb, and by the A55 dual carriageway on the modern causeway beside it. The nearest service area is Parc Cybi on the A55, 1.6 km away in a straight line. After that there is a long gap: Bangor Services on the A5 is 36.7 km away and Orme View Services on the A55 is 48.6 km. Road distances will be longer than these figures.

name: Holywood
intro: Lying on the shore of Belfast Lough between Belfast and Bangor, Holywood is a County Down town within the Belfast metropolitan area. It is a civil parish and townland covering 306 hectares (755 acres), and Holywood Exchange and Belfast City Airport are both close by. The BT18 postcode district covers the town, which has a population of 10,757. Because it sits inside the wider Belfast area, neighbouring places are close: in a straight line, Newtownabbey is about 5.9 km away, Belfast 8 km, Castlereagh 8.2 km and Carrickfergus 8.7 km, with Newtownards at 10 km and Bangor at 10.4 km. That leaves a driver with an AdBlue warning with several options. Two service areas are within about 17 km, and three stations within about 11 km are listed as selling AdBlue at the pump.
roadsText: Temple Patrick Services Northbound on the M2 is about 13.9 km from Holywood in a straight line, and Lisburn Services on the M1 about 17 km. Cohannon Services on the M1 is much further at 55.9 km. OpenStreetMap lists a station in Bangor (BT19 1AA) at about 8.9 km, one at BT6 0LT at about 9 km and one in Newtownabbey (BT36 4GX) at about 10.8 km as selling AdBlue at the pump. That data is incomplete.

name: Honiton
intro: Sitting close to the River Otter, 17 miles (27 km) north-east of Exeter, Honiton is a market town and civil parish in East Devon. Its population was estimated at 12,154 on the basis of the 2021 census, and the town is covered by the EX14 postcode district. Sidmouth, 11.8 km away, is the nearest neighbouring town, followed by Chard at 18.9 km and Wellington at 20.6 km, with Exmouth at 23.3 km, Tiverton at 23.6 km and Exeter at 23.8 km. When an AdBlue warning appears on a van or diesel car here, the M5 is the road that matters, because all three of the nearest listed service areas are on it. ExtraMSA Cullompton Services is the closest, 15.2 km away in a straight line, and the other two are 17.5 km and 20.5 km away.
roadsText: All three of the closest service areas to Honiton are on the M5. ExtraMSA Cullompton Services is the nearest at 15.2 km in a straight line, with Moto Tiverton Services at 17.5 km and RoadChef Taunton Deane Services at 20.5 km. Road distances will be longer, so a driver in EX14 with an AdBlue warning should allow for the run to the motorway.

name: Honley
intro: On the banks of the River Holme, Honley is a village in the Holme Valley civil parish in Kirklees, West Yorkshire, close to Holmfirth and Huddersfield. It was historically part of the West Riding of Yorkshire. The 2011 Census put the village population at 6,474, up 577 on 2001, and its postcode district is HD9. The name may come from the Old English Hanalēah, meaning either 'cock wood or clearing' or 'Hana's wood or clearing'. Huddersfield is the nearest neighbouring town, 6.8 km away, with Mirfield, Elland and Brighouse between 11.6 km and 13.1 km off and Liversedge and Dewsbury at 14.3 km and 14.5 km. Drivers here should note that motorway services are not on the doorstep: the nearest listed is 14.3 km away on the M62, with another on the M1 at 15.6 km.
roadsText: Service areas are some way from Honley. Hartshead Moor on the M62 is the nearest, 14.3 km from the village centre in a straight line, followed by Woolley Edge Services on the M1 at 15.6 km and the Whitwood service area on the M62 at 28.5 km. Road distances will be longer, so a driver in HD9 with an AdBlue warning should plan the route rather than assume a services stop is close.

name: Horley
intro: South of Reigate and Redhill, Horley is a Surrey town in the borough of Reigate and Banstead, with the West Sussex border to its south and Crawley and Gatwick Airport close by. Its postcode district is RH6, and the population is 27,067. Alongside a long high street and a shopping centre, its economy includes business parks, and it has good commuter links to London and the surrounding towns. For a van or diesel car, that points to a mix of commuting, business-park runs and short trips to neighbouring centres: Redhill is 6.3 km away, Crawley 6.6 km and Reigate 7.7 km, with East Grinstead, Dorking and Caterham all within 13.5 km. The M23 and A23 are both among the main roads near the town, so an AdBlue warning is as likely to show up on a motorway run as on a local trip across RH6.
roadsText: The main roads around Horley are the M23 and A23, along with the A264, A217, A2044, A2011, A2220 and A2004. The closest service area is Pease Pottage on the M23, 10.4 km away. Handcross on the A23 is 13.4 km out, and Clacket Lane on the M25 is 17.7 km away. Those are the nearest places to pull in and take stock if a warning comes on during a longer journey.

name: Horndean
intro: Horndean, a village and civil parish in the East Hampshire district, lies 8 miles north of Portsmouth and shares the semi-rural character of other places in the district. The nearest railway station is 2.2 miles to the south-east at Rowlands Castle. Horndean's postcode districts are PO8 and PO7, and the wider area this page covers has a population of 34,046. Only two roads appear in the list: the A3(M) and the A3. Waterlooville is just 3.9km away and Havant 6.2km, with Emsworth at 8.5km, Portsmouth at 10.7km and Petersfield at 11.9km. For a diesel driver, that suggests short trips to neighbouring towns as well as longer runs on the A3(M), with service areas 8.6km and 11.7km from the village.
roadsText: The A3(M) and A3 are the only main roads listed around Horndean. Farlington Services on the A27 is the nearest service area, about 8.6km away, followed by Petersfield Services on the A3 at 11.7km. Liphook Services, also on the A3, is 23.6km out. Of the two listed on the A3, Petersfield is the closer to Horndean.

name: Horsham
intro: Horsham sits on the fringe of the Weald, on the upper reaches of the River Arun. It is a market town and the administrative centre of the Horsham district of West Sussex, 31 miles south-south-west of London and 18.5 miles north-west of Brighton, with an estimated 50,934 people in 2018. Its postcode districts are RH12 and RH13, and Crawley lies to the north-east, with Haywards Heath and Burgess Hill to the south-east. The roads listed around the town are all A roads: the A24, A264, A281 and A29. Southwater is only 4.5km away and Crawley 11.1km, while Cranleigh is 14.2km, Horley 16.2km and Dorking 18km. A driver here covers a mix of town streets and A-road runs to neighbouring towns, with the nearest motorway services, on the M23, 8.6km away.
roadsText: The A24, A264, A281 and A29 are the main roads listed around Horsham. Three service areas sit at similar distances from town: Handcross on the A23 (8.3km), Pease Pottage Services on the M23 (8.6km) and Buck Barn on the A24 (8.6km). That gives a driver with an AdBlue warning several places to stop within a short distance of town, on an A road or the motorway.

name: Horwich
intro: The M61 motorway passes close to the south and west of Horwich, a town and civil parish in the Metropolitan Borough of Bolton that sits at the southern edge of the West Pennine Moors. It lies 5.8 miles (9.3 km) northwest of Bolton town centre, 5.3 miles (8.5 km) southeast of Chorley and 15 miles (24 km) northwest of Manchester, within the historic county boundaries of Lancashire. The 2011 Census recorded 20,067 residents, and the BL6 postcode district covers the town. Its older industries, from bleachworks to the railway works that grew the town after 1884, have closed, and regeneration has been led by out-of-town developments, particularly at Middlebrook. Westhoughton is the closest neighbouring town at about 5.7 km, with Hindley, Bolton and Standish between 6.9 km and 7.3 km. A driver with an AdBlue warning here is close to motorway services, with Rivington Services on the M61 about 2.1 km away.
roadsText: With the M61 running close to the south and west of town, Rivington Services on that motorway is only about 2.1 km from Horwich. Charnock Richard Services on the M6 is around 10.6 km away, and Blackburn with Darwen Services on the M65 about 13.9 km. OpenStreetMap has stations under Manchester (about 18 km) and Warrington (about 19.6 km) listed as selling AdBlue at the pump. That data is incomplete, so nearer stations may also sell it.

name: Houghton Regis
intro: Part of the Luton/Dunstable Urban Area, a conurbation of more than 286,000 people, Houghton Regis is a Central Bedfordshire town that adjoins its neighbours Dunstable and Luton. The town has 18,814 residents, and the parish also takes in the hamlets of Bidwell, Thorn and Sewell. It is covered by the LU5 postcode district. The M1 is close by: Toddington Services on that motorway is 4.7 km from the centre in a straight line, which is useful to know if an AdBlue warning appears before a longer trip. Dunstable is just 2.5 km away and Luton 6.9 km, with Leighton Buzzard at 9.7 km and Flitwick at 11 km. Tring and Harpenden are both a little over 15 km away.
roadsText: Toddington Services on the M1 is the nearest service area to Houghton Regis, 4.7 km away in a straight line. Crawley Crossing Truck Stop, also on the M1, is 14 km away, and Bourne End Services on the A41 is 18.5 km. Both of the two nearest sites are on the M1, which makes that motorway the main reference point for drivers in LU5.

name: Houghton-le-Spring
intro: With recorded origins in Norman times, Houghton-le-Spring is a town within Sunderland, historically part of County Durham. Seaham lies 8 km directly east, and the villages and towns of Newbottle, Fencehouses and Hetton-le-Hole are close by. The Houghton-le-Spring postal district also takes in Philadelphia, Penshaw, Shiney Row, Chilton Moor and Woodstone Village, and the town is covered by the DH4 and DH5 postcode districts. That spread of villages means plenty of short local driving, and the larger towns are not far either: Chester-le-Street is 6.8 km away, Washington 7.7 km, Sunderland 8.3 km and Durham 8.9 km. Two different main roads are within reach, with Washington services on the A1(M) 7.7 km away and Easington services on the A19 8.4 km, so a van or diesel car here can be on either road after a short drive.
roadsText: Houghton-le-Spring has service areas on two different main roads within 8.4 km. Washington services on the A1(M) is 7.7 km away and Easington on the A19 is 8.4 km, with Durham services on the A1(M) at 12.7 km. A station with the postcode DH6 3LJ, 11.9 km from the town, is listed in OpenStreetMap as selling AdBlue at the pump. OpenStreetMap is incomplete, so other forecourts may sell it as well.

name: Hounslow
intro: From Chiswick, near Central London, in the east to Feltham and Bedfont on the Surrey border in the west, the London Borough of Hounslow covers five major towns: Chiswick (W4), Brentford (TW8), Isleworth (TW7), Hounslow (TW3, TW4, TW5) and Feltham (TW13, TW14). It borders Richmond upon Thames, Hammersmith and Fulham, Ealing and Hillingdon, as well as the Spelthorne district of Surrey, and London Heathrow Airport lies just outside its boundary. It is home to about 286,591 people. Two motorways, the M4 and M3, appear in its main road list along with the A4, A30, A312, A316, A308 and A3063, so a diesel van here may be on a motorway rather than a town street when an AdBlue warning appears. Richmond upon Thames is 4.4km away, Ealing 6.5km and Sunbury-on-Thames 6.9km.
roadsText: Two motorways head Hounslow's road list, the M4 and M3, followed by the A4, A30, A312, A316, A308 and A3063. Heston Services on the M4 is only 2.5km away, which makes it the closest listed service area by a wide margin. Cobham Services on the M25 is 18.2km away and London Gateway Services on the M1 is 19.8km.

name: Hoyland
intro: From the Old Norse for 'land on a hill spur' comes the name of Hoyland, also known as Nether Hoyland, a town and district in the Metropolitan Borough of Barnsley inside the historic boundaries of the West Riding. The old Hoyland Nether urban district took in the town along with Hoyland Common, Upper Hoyland, Elsecar, Milton, Platts Common and Wentworth. It had 15,497 residents in 2001 and uses the S74 postcode district. Wombwell is about 3.4 km away, Chapeltown and High Green 4.8 km, Barnsley 6.6 km and Wath upon Dearne 6.9 km. For drivers with an AdBlue warning, three service areas lie between about 13 km and 15 km away in a straight line, the nearest being Rotherham Services on the M1.
roadsText: Three service areas are a similar straight-line distance from Hoyland: Rotherham Services on the M1 at about 13 km, Sheffield Service Area on the A6102 at 14.3 km and Woolley Edge Services on the M1 at 15 km. OpenStreetMap lists a station in Pontefract (WF7 7HX), about 17.4 km away, and another in Doncaster (DN4 0TP), about 18 km away, as selling AdBlue at the pump. These may not be the only places selling it, as the map data is incomplete.

name: Hucknall
intro: Part of Nottinghamshire's Ashfield district, the market town of Hucknall lies 7 miles (11 km) north of Nottingham. It is also 7 miles (11 km) south-east of Kirkby-in-Ashfield, 9 miles (14 km) from Mansfield and 10 miles (16 km) south of Sutton-in-Ashfield, which places it between the city and the Ashfield towns. The population is 35,848, and the postcode districts are NG15 and NG6. Main roads include the M1, A60, A610, A611 and A614, plus the A608, A6002 and A6514. Eastwood is about 6 km away and Arnold 6.8 km, with Heanor at 9.3 km and Ilkeston at 10.2 km. The nearest service area is Trowell Services on the M1, around 8.8 km out, which makes it the closest place to pull in if the dashboard flags an AdBlue problem.
roadsText: Hucknall's main roads are the M1, A60, A608, A610, A611, A614, A6002 and A6514. The nearest service area is Trowell Services on the M1, about 8.8 km away, with Trent Bridge Services on the A6011 at around 11.3 km and Pierrepont on the A52 at 13.9 km. A Tesco station about 11.7 km away is listed in OpenStreetMap as selling AdBlue at the pump; that list is incomplete.

name: Huddersfield
intro: Administrative centre of Kirklees and its largest settlement, Huddersfield lies in the foothills of the Pennines in West Yorkshire. Rivers shape the town: the Holme joins the Colne south of the centre, and the Colne flows on into the Calder on the north-eastern outskirts. The soft water they supplied for textile treatment made Huddersfield a prominent mill town in the early Victorian years of the Industrial Revolution. Its population is put at 141,683. If an AdBlue warning lights up here, the M62 is the motorway among the main roads listed, and A roads including the A62, A629, A640 and A642 are also on the list. Postcode districts run from HD1 to HD7 and also include HX5. Measured directly, Elland is 5.2 km away, Brighouse 6.3 km, Honley 6.8 km and Mirfield 7.1 km, with Liversedge at 8.9 km.
roadsText: The M62 is the motorway among the main roads around Huddersfield, with the A640, A62, A629, A642, A644, A616 and A641 also listed. Hartshead Moor services on the M62 is the nearest service area, 7.9 km away measured directly. Woolley Edge services on the M1 is 16.3 km away and Skelton Lake Service Station, also on the M1, is 25.3 km. Driving there takes you further than those numbers suggest.

name: Humberston and New Waltham
intro: Cleethorpes is only about 2.2 km from Humberston, a village and civil parish just to its south. Together with New Waltham, Humberston makes up a community of 14,861 people in North East Lincolnshire, which falls within the Yorkshire and the Humber region. The area shares the DN36 postcode district. Grimsby is about 5.7 km away, but the next nearest towns are much further: Louth is about 18.2 km off and Barton-upon-Humber about 31.9 km. Services follow the same pattern. The nearest listed service area is Ulceby Truckstop on the A160, around 19.5 km in a straight line, and the next, Showground Services on the A15, is about 43 km away. For a van or diesel car with an AdBlue warning, it helps to know these distances before setting out.
roadsText: Ulceby Truckstop on the A160 is the nearest service area to Humberston and New Waltham, about 19.5 km in a straight line. Showground Services on the A15 is about 43.1 km away and Thorpe on the Hill Services on the A46 about 55.7 km. OpenStreetMap lists a station in Louth (LN11 0WA), roughly 16.4 km away, as selling AdBlue at the pump. That source is incomplete, so it is not a full picture.

name: Huntingdon
intro: Given its town charter by King John in 1205, Huntingdon is a market town in the Huntingdonshire district of Cambridgeshire and was the county town of the historic county of Huntingdonshire. Oliver Cromwell was born there in 1599 and became one of its Members of Parliament in 1628. The road listing is the useful part for a diesel driver: the A1(M), A1 and A14 all appear, alongside the A141, A1307, A1123 and A1198. St Ives is 7.3 km away, St Neots 14.1 km and Cambourne 15.6 km, with Chatteris at 20.2 km, Sandy 23.7 km and Raunds 24.5 km. Postcode districts are PE28 and PE29, and the population is 25,603. The closest listed service area is under 5 km from the town, and two more sit on the A1(M) at Sawtry.
roadsText: The A1(M), A1, A14, A141, A1307, A1123 and A1198 are listed. Brampton Hut Services on the A141 is 4.8 km away, and there are two service sites at Sawtry on the A1(M), at 9.5 km and 11.5 km. A station 17.5 km from Huntingdon is listed on OpenStreetMap as selling AdBlue at the pump; OpenStreetMap's AdBlue coverage is incomplete.

name: Huntington
intro: North of York and south of Strensall, Huntington is a village and civil parish on the River Foss, part of the Huntington & New Earswick ward in the City of York. It was in the North Riding until 1974 and in Ryedale district until 1996. The population was 9,277 in 2001 and 12,108 in 2011. The parish is mainly low-lying, with its highest point only 64 feet above sea level, and measures about 4 miles (6 km) north to south and 3 miles (5 km) east to west. Postcodes fall in YO31 and YO32. Haxby is about 2.8 km away and York 4.1 km. For an AdBlue warning, the nearest listed service area is Bilbrough Top on the A64, around 12.4 km in a straight line, with Wetherby Services on the A1(M) about 20.7 km away.
roadsText: Bilbrough Top Service Area on the A64 is the nearest to Huntington, about 12.4 km in a straight line. Wetherby Services on the A1(M) is about 20.7 km away and Ferrybridge Services on the M62 about 35.1 km. For most drivers here, the A64 site will be the first one to consider, with the M62 option much further out.

name: Huyton with Roby
intro: Huyton is a town in the Metropolitan Borough of Knowsley and part of the Liverpool Built-up Area, bordering the Liverpool suburbs of Dovecot, Knotty Ash and Netherley. Historically in Lancashire, it was an ancient parish that once contained Croxteth Park, Knowsley and Tarbock. Liverpool is 4.5 km away and Prescot 4.4 km, with Kirkby at 7.4 km, St Helens at 8.5 km, Widnes at 9.4 km and Bootle at 10.4 km. Seven postcode districts are listed for the area: L12, L14, L16, L27, L28, L34 and L36. The road list includes two motorways, the M57 and M62, plus the A57, A5080, A58, A5058, A5047 and A562. For a driver with an AdBlue warning, the nearest service area in the data is very close, just 2.2 km away on the M57.
roadsText: Huyton's main roads include the M57 and M62, with the A57, A5080, A58, A5058, A5047 and A562. Earlsfield Services on the M57 is just 2.2 km away; Old Meadow Services on the M58 (11.4 km) and Burtonwood Services on the M62 (14.3 km) are further off. Stations at Old Meadow (11.5 km) and in Warrington's WA5 (12.8 km) are listed as selling AdBlue at the pump in OpenStreetMap, along with an HGV-only site in Liverpool L5. Its data is incomplete.

name: Hyde
intro: Historically a Cheshire town, Hyde became part of Greater Manchester in 1974 and now sits in Tameside. Its built-up area had 35,895 residents at the 2021 census. Stockport is 5 miles to the south-west, Glossop 6 miles to the east and Manchester 6.5 miles to the west, which places Hyde between the city and Glossop. Postcode districts SK14, SK16 and M34 cover the town. Closer in, Dukinfield is 2.6 km away, Denton 3.1 km, Romiley 4.1 km and Stalybridge 4.2 km. The M67 and M60 are the motorways listed nearby, and listed A roads include the A57, A560 and A627. If an AdBlue warning appears, note that the nearest service area is 16.6 km away, so the options below are worth checking first.
roadsText: Roads listed around Hyde include the M67 and M60, plus the A627, A57, A560, A6017, A6018 and A635. Birch Services on the M62, at 16.6 km, is the closest service area, with Knutsford Services (27.6 km) and Tabley Hill Service Station (27.9 km) on the M6 further out. A station 8.8 km away and one in Manchester (M25 3AJ), 17.2 km away, are listed on OpenStreetMap as selling AdBlue at the pump; other sites may simply be missing from the map.

name: Hythe
intro: Hythe takes its name from an Old English word meaning haven or landing place. The old market town and civil parish stands on the edge of Romney Marsh in Kent, in the Folkestone and Hythe district, and has a population of 14,613 within the CT21 postcode district. Folkestone is the nearest town at 4.4 km. Beyond it the distances open up, with Ashford at 16 km, Dover at 17.2 km and Canterbury at 23.1 km, and Deal and Faversham both more than 27 km away. For a driver with an AdBlue warning, the nearest services are closer than any neighbouring town: Folkestone Services on the M20 is 3.4 km from Hythe in a straight line. Ashford International Truckstop on the A2070 is 13.2 km off, and a station in New Romney, at the same distance, is listed in OpenStreetMap as selling AdBlue at the pump.
roadsText: Folkestone Services on the M20 is 3.4 km from Hythe in a straight line, the nearest listed service area. Ashford International Truckstop on the A2070 is 13.2 km away and Whitfield Services on the A2 is 19.6 km. OpenStreetMap lists a station in New Romney (TN28 8AZ), also 13.2 km off, as selling AdBlue at the pump. The map data is incomplete, so this should not be read as the only option.

name: Hythe and Dibden Purlieu
intro: Hythe is a Hampshire town on the shore of Southampton Water, and this page covers it together with Dibden Purlieu, an area of about 19,857 people in the SO45 postcode district. The town has a shopping area, a pier and a marina for yachts. A ferry service links Hythe to Southampton, though it is currently closed. Southampton is 6.8 km away in a straight line, with West End at 9.2 km, Locks Heath at 9.3 km, Totton at 9.5 km and Hedge End at 9.9 km. Eastleigh is a little further at 13.2 km. For a van or diesel car with an AdBlue warning, the nearest listed service area is Rownhams Services on the M27, 11 km away, and the other two listed sites, on the A36 and A31, are both within 16 km.
roadsText: The nearest listed service area to Hythe and Dibden Purlieu is Rownhams Services on the M27, 11 km away in a straight line. West Wellow Services on the A36 is 13.7 km away and Rufus Stone on the A31 is 16 km. All three are straight-line distances, and the drive to each will be longer.

name: Ilkeston
intro: Ilkeston sits between the cities of Derby and Nottingham, near the M1 and on the River Erewash, in Derbyshire's Erewash borough. It had 40,953 residents at the 2021 census and is part of the Nottingham Urban Area, with its eastern boundary on the Nottinghamshire border, only two miles from Nottingham's western edge. Coal mining, iron working and lace making were once its major industries but have all but disappeared. The postcode district is DE7. Main roads include the M1, A52, A609 and A610, together with the A608, A6002, A6007 and A6096. Stapleford is about 4.5 km away, Eastwood 5.8 km, Heanor 6.1 km and Beeston 6.8 km. Trowell Services on the M1 is only around 2.9 km out, which makes it an easy reference point if an AdBlue warning appears nearby.
roadsText: Ilkeston's main roads are the M1, A52, A608, A609, A610, A6002, A6007 and A6096. Trowell Services on the M1 is the nearest service area, about 2.9 km away. Welcome Break Derby South Services on the A50 is around 11.4 km out, and Trent Bridge Services on the A6011 about 11.7 km.

name: Ilkley
intro: Mostly on the south bank of the River Wharfe in Wharfedale, Ilkley is a spa town and civil parish in the City of Bradford, about 12 miles (19 km) north of Bradford and 17 miles (27 km) north-west of Leeds. The parish takes in the adjacent village of Ben Rhydding, and Ilkley Moor lies to the south of the town. Tourism is an important local industry, and the town centre has wide streets and Victorian architecture. Ilkley uses the LS29 postcode district and has 14,852 residents. Bingley and Keighley are each a little over 8 km away, Otley 9.2 km and Baildon 9.6 km. Service areas are not close. The nearest listed, Hartshead Moor Services on the M62, is about 24.4 km away in a straight line, so a driver with an AdBlue warning faces a longer run than the local distances suggest.
roadsText: No service area is especially close to Ilkley. In a straight line, the nearest listed are Hartshead Moor Services on the M62 at about 24.4 km, Hollin Bank Service Station on the M65 at 28 km and Skelton Lake Service Station on the M1 at 29.2 km. With all three more than 24 km away, it helps to decide on a route before a warning light becomes pressing.

name: Ince-in-Makerfield
intro: A railway line divides Ince-in-Makerfield into two separate areas, Higher Ince and Lower Ince, which is worth knowing when finding your way around this residential suburb. Also called Ince, it is a town in the Metropolitan Borough of Wigan and is contiguous to Wigan itself, within the boundaries of the historic county of Lancashire. The Ince ward had 13,486 residents at the 2011 census, and adding a southern part of Ince listed under the Abram ward brings the total to 15,664. Postcode districts WN1, WN2 and WN3 cover the area. Platt Bridge and Abram is about 2.2 km away, Hindley 2.4 km and Wigan 2.9 km. For a driver with an AdBlue warning, the nearest motorway service area is Rivington Services on the M61, about 7.4 km off.
roadsText: Rivington Services on the M61 is the nearest service area to Ince-in-Makerfield, about 7.4 km away. Charnock Richard Services on the M6 is around 11.8 km off, and Burtonwood Services on the M62 about 13.4 km. OpenStreetMap has two stations under Warrington, at about 14.2 km and 14.5 km, listed as selling AdBlue at the pump. OpenStreetMap is not a complete record, so nearer stations may also stock it.

name: Ingleby Barwick
intro: Large-scale building on farmland south-west of Thornaby began in the late 1970s, and Ingleby Barwick is now a town and civil parish in the Borough of Stockton-on-Tees. The first development was officially opened in July 1981, and the parish gained town status in 2007. It lies south of the River Tees and north-east of the River Leven. The 2011 census counted 20,378 people in the civil parish, while its two electoral wards, which also take in Hilton, Maltby, High Leven and Low Leven, had 21,045. Its postcode district is TS17. Egglescliffe is just 2.7 km away and Thornaby-on-Tees 4.3 km, with Stockton-on-Tees at 6.3 km and Middlesbrough at 7.5 km, so much of the driving from here is short runs into neighbouring towns. Billingham, at 9.6 km, and Eston, at 11.8 km, are a little further out.
roadsText: Three service areas sit at a similar distance from Ingleby Barwick. A service area on the A19 is 11.8 km away, Teesside Truck Stop on the A66 is 11.9 km, and Wolviston Services on the A689 is 12.5 km. With all three around 12 km out, a driver who sees an AdBlue warning on a local trip will be some way from the nearest stop.

name: Inverness
intro: Long regarded as the de facto capital of the Scottish Highlands, Inverness is the administrative centre of The Highland Council region and a regional hub for services across the wider Highlands and Islands. That hinterland covers some 39,911 km², around 51% of Scotland's total landmass, and around half a million people, which gives a sense of the distances involved for anyone driving here. The city is covered by the IV1, IV2 and IV3 postcode districts and was previously the county town of Inverness-shire. The A9, A82 and A96 are all recorded around the city, along with the A862 and A8082. Nairn, 24.7 km away, is the nearest of the listed towns; Elgin is 58.2 km and Perth 127.8 km. For a van or diesel car, gaps like those mean an AdBlue warning is best sorted before leaving town.
roadsText: The A82, A9, A96, A8082 and A862 are the main roads recorded around Inverness.
