Skiach Services on the A9 is the nearest service area at 23.8 km, with Elgin Services on the A96 at 60.6 km and Ashgrove Services on the A96 at 81.8 km. OpenStreetMap lists a station in Inverness (IV1 1RY), 1.8 km away, as selling AdBlue at the pump. The map data is incomplete, so it may not be the only option in the city.

name: Inverurie
intro: Where the rivers Ury and Don meet, about 16 miles (26 km) north-west of Aberdeen, Inverurie is a market town in Aberdeenshire. Its Gaelic name, Inbhir Uraidh, means the mouth of the River Ury. The town had a population of 15,106 in 2022 and is covered by the AB51 postcode district. For anyone driving a van or diesel car here, the main point is distance. Westhill is 15.7 km away, Ellon 20.5 km and Aberdeen 21.6 km, while Stonehaven, Peterhead and Fraserburgh are all at least 37.1 km off. The service areas listed for the town are also some way off, with the nearest 35.8 km away on the A96. That makes it sensible to plan a stop well before an AdBlue warning becomes urgent.
roadsText: The nearest service areas listed for Inverurie are some distance away: Ashgrove Services on the A96 at 35.8 km, Stracathro Services on the A90 at 58.8 km and Elgin Services, also on the A96, at 65.4 km. Closer to home, Westhill Service Station in Westhill (AB32 6TJ), 16.2 km away, is listed as selling AdBlue at the pump in OpenStreetMap. That data is incomplete, so other stations nearby may also stock it.

name: Ipswich
intro: A port town on the River Orwell, Ipswich is the county town and largest town in Suffolk, 65 miles (105 km) north-east of London. It had 139,457 residents in 2025 and is the third-largest population centre in East Anglia, after Peterborough and Norwich. The town is surrounded by the towns and villages of Kesgrave, Woodbridge, Bramford and Martlesham Heath. Postcode districts are IP1, IP2, IP3, IP4, IP5 and IP8. The A12 and A14 are both among the main roads, along with the A137, A1022, A1071, A1156, A1189 and A1214. Kesgrave is about 6.2 km away, Woodbridge 11.8 km, and Harwich and Felixstowe around 16 km. A service area on the A14 is only about 2.6 km out, the closest place to stop and check an AdBlue warning.
roadsText: Ipswich's main roads are the A12, A14, A137, A1022, A1071, A1156, A1189 and A1214. EG Sprougton Road Services on the A14 is the nearest service area, about 2.6 km away. Beacon Hill Services on the A140 is around 11.1 km out, and Ardleigh South Services on the A120 about 20.8 km.

name: Irlam
intro: Flat ground between the M62 motorway to the north and the Manchester Ship Canal to the south shapes Irlam, a suburb in the City of Salford. It lies 6.7 miles (10.8 km) southwest of Salford, 7.6 miles (12.2 km) southwest of Manchester and 8.3 miles (13.4 km) northeast of Warrington, and it forms a continuous urban area with Cadishead to the southwest. The canal divides it from Flixton and the Metropolitan Borough of Trafford to the southeast. The A57 is the main road through Irlam, linking it to Cadishead and Eccles. In 2011 the population was 19,933, and the M44 postcode district covers the area. Urmston is about 3.4 km away and Eccles 5.7 km, with Worsley and Sale both around 6.9 km. For a driver with an AdBlue warning, the nearest service area is Lymm Services on the M6, about 11.2 km away.
roadsText: The A57 is the main road through Irlam, and the M62 runs along its northern side. Lymm Services on the M6 is the nearest service area at about 11.2 km, followed by Burtonwood Services on the M62 at 14.9 km and Tabley Hill Service Station on the M6 at 15 km. OpenStreetMap has stations under Warrington at about 7.8 km and 16.5 km, and one under Manchester at 13.4 km, listed as selling AdBlue at the pump. Its data is incomplete.

name: Irvine
intro: Designated in 1966 as the fifth and final Scottish new town, Irvine is also a former royal burgh with a long history, set on the coast of the Firth of Clyde. It is the largest settlement in North Ayrshire, with 33,998 people in 2022, and the seat of North Ayrshire Council. KA11 and KA12 are the postcode districts, and the recorded main roads are the A78, A71, A736, A737, A738 and A759. Irvine sits among a group of close neighbours: Kilwinning is 4.9 km away, Troon 8 km, Saltcoats 8.6 km and Kilmarnock 9.9 km, with Ardrossan at 10.2 km. For a driver with an AdBlue warning, the more important point is that the nearest service areas are at least 42.6 km away on the M74, so a motorway stop is not a quick option from here.
roadsText: The A78, A737, A738, A736, A71 and A759 are the main roads recorded around Irvine. The nearest service areas are all on the M74: Bothwell Services at 42.6 km, Hamilton Services at 42.7 km and the M74 Truck Stop at 47.8 km. That is a long way to drive with a warning showing, so it makes sense to deal with it before setting off.

name: Islington
intro: Arsenal and its home ground, the Emirates Stadium, are in Islington, the second smallest borough in London and the third-smallest district in England. This North London borough forms part of Inner London, was formed in 1965 by combining the metropolitan boroughs of Islington and Finsbury, and has an estimated 215,667 residents. In a borough this small, journeys within it are short, and its listed main roads are all A-roads: the A1, A10, A104, A201, A501, A503, A1202 and A5201. Postcode districts include N1, N1C, N5 and N7, along with EC1R, EC1V, WC1H and WC1X. Hackney is 2.7km away, Camden 4.1km, Haringey 4.7km and the City of Westminster 5.1km. For a van or diesel car with an AdBlue warning, that means the problem may surface on a neighbouring borough's streets rather than in Islington itself.
roadsText: The main roads listed for Islington are the A1, A104, A501, A503, A201, A10, A5201 and A1202. The nearest service areas are London Gateway Services on the M1 at 14.9km, South Mimms Services on the A1(M) at 18.1km and Heston Services on the M4 at 20.9km. A station 12.5km away and one at Catford, 12.9km away, are listed as selling AdBlue at the pump in OpenStreetMap, whose records are incomplete.

name: Ivybridge
intro: Ivybridge lies along the A38, the road known as the Devon Expressway, at the southern extremity of Dartmoor and about 13 miles (21 km) east of Plymouth. The South Hams town grew up as an important crossing point over the River Erme on the road from Exeter to Plymouth, and the South Devon Railway reached its northern edge in 1848. Its two electoral wards, Ivybridge East and Ivybridge West, have a combined population of 11,851, and the PL21 postcode district covers the town. Plymouth is the closest town at 14.3 km, with Saltash at 21.5 km and Tavistock at 23.3 km. The A38 runs along the town, but the nearest listed service area is 22.4 km away in a straight line, and the next is more than twice as far, so an AdBlue warning here is best planned for rather than left to a services stop.
roadsText: Ivybridge lies along the A38 Devon Expressway. The nearest listed service area is Saltash Services on the A388, 22.4 km away in a straight line. Moto Exeter Services on the M5 is 48.6 km away and Cornwall Services on the A30 is 63.4 km, so there is a long gap between stops. If an AdBlue warning appears, decide where to go before setting off.

name: Jarrow
intro: On the south bank of the River Tyne, about three miles from the east coast, Jarrow is home to the southern portal of the Tyne Tunnel. The town sits in South Tyneside, was historically part of County Durham, and lies about six miles north of Sunderland. Hebburn (2.4 km) and South Shields (3.6 km) are its closest neighbours, with Wallsend at 4.3 km, Tynemouth at 4.9 km, Gateshead at 7.3 km and Washington at 7.7 km. Six postcode districts cover the area, NE31 through to NE36, and the built-up area had 29,470 people at the 2021 census. The listed roads include the A194(M) and A19 alongside the A194, A1300, A184, A1018, A1058 and A185, so the list mixes a motorway-standard road with a dense set of local A-roads.
roadsText: Around Jarrow the main roads listed are the A194(M), A19, A194, A1300, A184, A1018, A1058 and A185. The nearest service areas are Washington Services on the A1(M) at 10.4 km, Seaton Burn Services on the A19 at 14.6 km and Easington Services, also on the A19, at 20 km. A station in Newcastle upon Tyne, 10.8 km away, is listed as selling AdBlue at the pump in OpenStreetMap; that data is incomplete, so other sites may exist.

name: Johnstone
intro: At the western edge of the Greater Glasgow Urban Area, part of the biggest conurbation in Scotland, Johnstone is a town in Renfrewshire in the west central Lowlands. It lies 3 miles (5 km) west of neighbouring Paisley, 12 miles (19 km) west of central Glasgow and 12 miles (19 km) north-east of Kilwinning. Johnstone has a population of 15,930 and is covered by the PA5 and PA10 postcode districts. In a straight line, Barrhead is about 8.5 km away, Erskine 9 km and Renfrew 9.3 km, with Clydebank at 11.1 km and Newton Mearns at 13.1 km. For a driver with an AdBlue warning, motorway service areas are a fair distance off, the closest about 28.5 km away on the M74, while two stations within about 15 km are listed as selling AdBlue at the pump.
roadsText: Bothwell Services on the M74 is the closest service area to Johnstone, about 28.5 km away in a straight line, with Hamilton Services on the M74 at about 30.4 km and the M74 Truck Stop at about 44 km. OpenStreetMap lists a station in Glasgow (G11 6DN), about 13.5 km away, and another about 14.5 km away as selling AdBlue at the pump. That data is incomplete.

name: Kearsley
intro: Walkden lies to the west of Kearsley, Whitefield to the east, Farnworth to the north and Clifton to the south, so this town in the Bolton borough has neighbours on every side. It sits within the historic county of Lancashire, 7 miles (11 km) northwest of Manchester, 5 miles (8 km) southwest of Bury and 3.5 miles (6 km) south of Bolton. The 2011 census recorded 14,212 residents. Kearsley was a township in the ancient parish of Deane, and Kearsley Urban District existed from 1894 until 1974. The BL4 postcode district covers the town. Farnworth is about 2 km away, Little Lever 2.4 km and Walkden 2.7 km, with Little Hulton, Swinton and Radcliffe all within 4.3 km. For a van or diesel car with an AdBlue warning, Birch Services on the M62 is about 9.9 km off.
roadsText: Birch Services on the M62 is the nearest service area to Kearsley, about 9.9 km away. Rivington Services on the M61 is around 14.6 km off, and Blackburn with Darwen Services on the M65 about 20.2 km. OpenStreetMap has a station under Manchester, roughly 5.7 km away, listed as selling AdBlue at the pump, as well as a site at 15.5 km and one under Warrington at 17 km. Its data is incomplete.

name: Keighley
intro: Between Airedale and Keighley Moors, close to the borders of North Yorkshire and Lancashire, Keighley is the second-largest settlement in the City of Bradford borough after Bradford itself. It is a market town 8 miles (13 km) north-west of Bradford, 11 miles (18 km) north of Halifax and 8 miles (13 km) south-east of Skipton, and had 56,348 residents at the 2011 census. Its main roads, the A629, A650, A6068, A6035, A6033 and A6034, are all A roads. With no motorway among them, the nearest motorway service area is more than 20 km away, so an AdBlue message here is worth acting on early. Bingley is the closest town at 5.7 km measured directly, followed by Ilkley at 8.4 km and Baildon at 9.2 km. Postcode districts are BD21 and BD22.
roadsText: Keighley's main roads are all A roads: the A629, A650, A6068, A6035, A6033 and A6034. Service areas are some distance away. Measured directly, Hartshead Moor on the M62 is 20.3 km, Hollin Bank Service Station on the M65 is 21.1 km and Skelton Lake Service Station on the M1 is 30.8 km. Distances by road will be longer, which is worth weighing up once a warning appears.

name: Kempston
intro: Separated from the Queen's Park area of Bedford by the River Great Ouse, Kempston is a town and civil parish in the Borough of Bedford, around 2 miles (3.2 km) south-west of Bedford town centre. It forms part of the wider Bedford built-up area. The town has a population of 22,779 and falls in the MK42 postcode district. If an AdBlue warning comes on, Kempston's position helps: Bedford Services on the A421 is just 1.5 km from the centre, and two M1 sites follow, Crawley Crossing Truck Stop at 12.7 km and Newport Pagnell Services at 17.8 km, all measured in a straight line. Bedford itself is 3.6 km away, while Flitwick, Sandy, Newport Pagnell and Biggleswade are all between 12 km and 17 km out. St Neots is a little further at 19.6 km.
roadsText: Bedford Services on the A421 is the nearest service area to Kempston, only 1.5 km from the centre in a straight line. Further out, two sites sit on the M1: Crawley Crossing Truck Stop at 12.7 km and Newport Pagnell Services at 17.8 km. Those three give drivers in MK42 a choice of stops on both the A421 and the motorway.

name: Kendal
intro: Just outside the Lake District, Kendal is a market town in the dale of the River Kent, which gives the town its name. It lies 8 miles south-east of Windermere and 19 miles north of Lancaster, and had 29,593 people at the 2021 Census. At the 2011 census it was the second largest town in Westmorland and Furness after Barrow-in-Furness. Kendal became the county town of Westmorland in 1889, the centre of South Lakeland in 1974 and the administrative centre of Westmorland and Furness in 2023. The LA9 and LA8 postcode districts cover the area. Ulverston is 27.2 km away and Lancaster 30.8 km, so other towns are some distance off. All the roads listed for Kendal are A roads, including the A6, A591 and A590, and the nearest service area, Killington Lake Services on the M6, is 7 km away.
roadsText: Kendal's listed roads are the A65, A6, A684, A5284, A591, A590 and A685. The nearest service areas are all on the M6: Killington Lake Services at 7 km, J38 Truckstop at 15.6 km and Tebay Services at 16.2 km. Lancaster lies 19 miles to the south, and Penrith is 37.6 km away.

name: Kenilworth
intro: Situated at the centre of Warwickshire, Kenilworth is a market town and civil parish in the Warwick District, 5.5 miles (9 km) south-west of Coventry and 4.5 miles (7 km) north of both Warwick and Leamington Spa. It lies on Finham Brook, a tributary of the River Sowe, and had 22,538 people at the 2021 Census. The town is home to the ruins of Kenilworth Castle and Kenilworth Abbey. Its postcode district is CV8. Further afield, Knowle and Dorridge is 12.3 km away, Bedworth 15.4 km and Solihull 17.4 km. If an AdBlue warning comes on, the nearest listed service area is on the A46, 7.9 km away in a straight line, and there are motorway services on the M6 and the M40 at 14.1 km and 14.9 km.
roadsText: The nearest service area to Kenilworth is Warwick North (Budbrooke) Services on the A46, 7.9 km away in a straight line. Corley Services on the M6 is 14.1 km off and Warwick Services on the M40 is 14.9 km. One station, 13.2 km from the town, is listed in OpenStreetMap as selling AdBlue at the pump. That map data is incomplete, so other stations nearer Kenilworth may sell it too.

name: Kensington and Chelsea
intro: The smallest borough in London and the second smallest district in England, the Royal Borough of Kensington and Chelsea is also one of the most densely populated administrative areas in the United Kingdom. It includes Notting Hill, Kensington, South Kensington, Chelsea and Knightsbridge. The borough lies immediately west of the City of Westminster, east of Hammersmith and Fulham, south of Brent and north of Wandsworth across the River Thames. Around 143,348 people live here. The borough's road list includes the A4, A202, A217, A302, A3031, A3212, A3220 and A4202, and its postcodes include SW1W, SW1X, SW3, SW5, SW7, SW10, W8 and W14. The City of Westminster is only 2.5km away and Hammersmith and Fulham 3.3km. In a borough this small, a van that develops an AdBlue warning during the day may just as easily be parked in a neighbouring borough when the driver deals with it.
roadsText: The main roads listed for Kensington and Chelsea are the A4, A3220, A3212, A3031, A302, A4202, A202 and A217. Heston Services on the M4 is the nearest listed service area at 14.9km, then London Gateway Services on the M1 at 16.6km and South Mimms Services on the A1(M) at 21.9km. A station at Catford (12.9km) and another 18.5km away are listed as selling AdBlue at the pump in OpenStreetMap, which has gaps.

name: Kesgrave
intro: Close to both Ipswich and Woodbridge, Kesgrave is a town and civil parish in the East Suffolk district, and its developed area was counted as part of the Ipswich Built-up Area at the 2011 Census. It has 14,947 residents, and its postcode district is IP5. Woodbridge is 6 km from the centre and Ipswich 6.2 km. Felixstowe lies 12.8 km away and Harwich 14.7 km, with Stowmarket at 21.4 km and Colchester at 29.6 km. For a van or diesel car with an AdBlue warning, the closest listed service area is Sprougton Road Services on the A14, 8.7 km away in a straight line, followed by Beacon Hill Services on the A140 at 14.3 km. Ardleigh South Services on the A120 is further out at 25.2 km.
roadsText: Sprougton Road Services on the A14 is the nearest service area to Kesgrave, 8.7 km away in a straight line. Beacon Hill Services on the A140 is 14.3 km away and Ardleigh South Services on the A120 is 25.2 km. From IP5, the A14 site is the closest of the three, and road distances to each will be longer than these figures.

name: Kettering
intro: The 2021 census counted 63,150 people in Kettering, a market and industrial town in North Northamptonshire that lies west of the River Ise, a tributary of the River Nene. Distances give a sense of where it sits: 15 miles (24 km) north-east of Northampton, 28 miles (45 km) south-east of Leicester and 31 miles (50 km) south-west of Peterborough. The A14 is among the main roads, along with the A6, A43, A509, A4300, A6003, A6013 and A6900. Postcode districts are NN14, NN15 and NN16. Burton Latimer is about 4.7 km away, Desborough 8.4 km, Wellingborough 10.5 km and Corby 10.6 km, so Kettering is one of a group of North Northamptonshire towns within a short drive of each other. Rothwell Truck Stop on the A14 is the closest service area, around 6.2 km out.
roadsText: Main roads around Kettering are the A6, A14, A43, A509, A4300, A6003, A6013 and A6900. Rothwell Truck Stop on the A14 is the nearest service area, about 6.2 km away. Thrapston Services on the A45 is around 13.5 km out, and Welford Truck Stop, also on the A14, is about 20.9 km away.

name: Keynsham
intro: Bristol's south-eastern outskirts are close to Keynsham, a town on the A4 between Bristol and Bath, in the Bath and North East Somerset district. It stands where the River Chew meets the River Avon, and it has a history of serious flooding, including the Chew Stoke flood of 1968, which inundated large parts of the town. Keynsham developed as a medieval market town after its abbey was founded around 1170. The built-up area had 19,255 people at the 2021 census, and the town is covered by the BS31 postcode district. Bristol is 7.8 km away and Bath 9.7 km, with Kingswood and Fishponds at 7.2 km. For a driver with an AdBlue warning, no listed service area is especially close: the nearest is Gordano Services on the M5, 16.3 km away in a straight line.
roadsText: Keynsham is on the A4, the road linking Bristol and Bath. The nearest listed service areas are Gordano Services on the M5, 16.3 km away in a straight line, Avon Lodge on the A4 at 16.9 km, and Severn View Services on the M48 at 23 km. None is close to BS31, so it makes sense to act on an AdBlue warning before a longer run. Distances by road will be longer than these figures.

name: Kidderminster
intro: Kidderminster, in the far north of Worcestershire, is the main administrative centre for the Wyre Forest District, which also takes in Stourport-on-Severn and Bewdley. The town lies north of the River Stour and east of the River Severn, 18 miles (29km) south-west of Birmingham and 15 miles north of Worcester. Its northern suburbs are only 3 to 4 miles from the Staffordshire and Shropshire borders. The 2021 census recorded 57,400 residents, and postcodes are DY10 and DY11. All of the listed roads are A-roads: the A456, A442, A451, A448, A449, A4535, A4420 and A450. Stourport-on-Severn is about 5.2km away and Stourbridge 10.2km. With no motorway on the list and the nearest service area 16.5km out, local driving here is mostly A-road work.
roadsText: A forecourt in DY10, about 1.8km away, is listed on OpenStreetMap as selling AdBlue at the pump, as is one in Warley at 19.6km. That data is incomplete. Service areas are further off: Frankley services on the M5 at about 16.5km, Hopwood Park services on the M42 at 20.8km and Hilton Park services on the M6 at 31.4km. Kidderminster's listed roads are the A456, A442, A451, A448, A449, A4535, A4420 and A450.

name: Kidlington
intro: Until February 2026 Kidlington was officially a village; that month its parish council voted unanimously to change its status to a town. It lies in the Cherwell district of Oxfordshire between the River Cherwell and the Oxford Canal, 5 miles (8 km) north of Oxford and 8 miles (13 km) south-west of Bicester. The 2021 census counted 13,600 residents, and the town's postcode district is OX5. Oxford is 7.7 km away, Bicester 12.6 km and Witney 14 km, with Abingdon-on-Thames at 16.1 km. For a driver whose van or diesel car shows an AdBlue warning, Peartree Services on the A44 is close by at 3.2 km in a straight line. Cherwell Valley Services and Oxford Services, both on the M40, are further out at 15.4 km and 16.2 km.
roadsText: Peartree Services on the A44 is the nearest service area to Kidlington, only 3.2 km away in a straight line. The two other listed options are both on the M40: Cherwell Valley Services at 15.4 km and Oxford Services at 16.2 km. The road distance to each will be longer than these figures, which is worth allowing for once an AdBlue warning appears.

name: Kidsgrove
intro: Kidsgrove sits on the border with Cheshire, in the borough of Newcastle-under-Lyme, Staffordshire, and forms part of the Potteries Urban Area along with Stoke-on-Trent and Newcastle-under-Lyme. A population of 26,276 is given for 2019. Most of the town is in the Kidsgrove ward, with the western part in Ravenscliffe, and it is covered by the ST7 postcode district. Alsager is 3.9 km away, Biddulph 5.5 km, Newcastle-under-Lyme 7.2 km and Congleton 9.1 km, with Sandbach at 10.4 km and Stoke-on-Trent at 12.5 km. A driver with an AdBlue warning has the M6 close by: Crewe Services is 6.6 km away in a straight line, and two more M6 service areas are within 10.8 km. That gives several options for a stop without a long detour.
roadsText: The three nearest service areas to Kidsgrove are all on the M6: Crewe Services, 6.6 km away in a straight line, Sandbach Services at 8.6 km and Keele Services at 10.8 km. A station in Newcastle-under-Lyme (ST5 4DH), 11.9 km away, is listed in OpenStreetMap as selling AdBlue at the pump. OpenStreetMap's coverage of AdBlue is incomplete, so nearer stations may sell it too.

name: Killingworth
intro: Built as a new town in the 1960s, next to the much older Killingworth Village, Killingworth is part of North Tyneside within the historic county of Northumberland. Forest Hall, West Moor and Backworth are among the villages nearby. The town is not on the Tyne and Wear Metro network, with its nearest stations at Palmersville and Benton, and it is linked to the rest of Tyne and Wear by bus routes. Killingworth has a population of 12,180 and sits in the NE12 postcode district. Longbenton is just 1.9 km away, Cramlington and Wallsend are both 5.5 km, Newcastle upon Tyne is 6.3 km, and Whitley Bay and Tynemouth are within 7.5 km. Many trips from Killingworth are therefore short ones, with the A19 close by: Seaton Burn services on that road is only 4.8 km from the town.
roadsText: Seaton Burn services on the A19 is 4.8 km from Killingworth, much closer than the next options: Washington services on the A1(M) is 16.7 km away and Easington, on the A19, 29.6 km. A station in Newcastle upon Tyne, just 1.4 km from the town, is listed in OpenStreetMap as selling AdBlue at the pump. OpenStreetMap data is incomplete, so this is not a full list of local stockists.

name: Kilmarnock
intro: Colloquially called Killie, Kilmarnock is a town and former burgh in East Ayrshire, in southwest Scotland. It has been the administrative centre of East Ayrshire Council since 1996 and is the area's main commercial and industrial centre. The KA1 and KA3 postcode districts cover the town, and its population is listed at 46,970. Both the M77 and A77 are on the road list, along with the A71, A76, A719, A735 and A759. Irvine is the nearest of the listed towns at 9.9 km, with Troon at 11.7 km and Kilwinning at 14.1 km, while Prestwick and Ayr are 14.8 km and 18.8 km away. The nearest service areas are all on the M74, at least 34.9 km away, so drivers in and around the town should not expect a motorway stop close by if an AdBlue warning appears.
roadsText: The M77, A77, A76, A735, A759, A71 and A719 are the main roads recorded around Kilmarnock. The nearest service areas are all on the M74 and some distance away: Hamilton Services at 34.9 km, Bothwell Services at 35.4 km and the M74 Truck Stop at 38.1 km. If a warning appears, it is worth getting it checked before committing to a longer run.

name: Kilsyth
intro: Roughly halfway between Glasgow and Stirling, Kilsyth is a town and civil parish in North Lanarkshire with an estimated population of 10,380. It is known for the Battle of Kilsyth and for religious revivals in the 18th, 19th and 20th centuries. The town has links with Cumbernauld, 4.9 km away; the two once formed Cumbernauld and Kilsyth District Council and still share the same members of parliament at Holyrood and Westminster. Kilsyth is in the G65 postcode district. Kirkintilloch is 6.7 km from the centre, with Bishopbriggs, Airdrie and Coatbridge all between 12.6 and 13.6 km off. For a driver with an AdBlue warning, the nearest listed service area is Stirling Services on the M9, 13.9 km away in a straight line, and the two M74 sites are at 18.2 km and 21.2 km.
roadsText: Stirling Services on the M9 is the nearest listed service area to Kilsyth at 13.9 km. Bothwell Services (18.2 km) and Hamilton Services (21.2 km) are both on the M74. All distances are in a straight line. A station in Glasgow (G11 6DN), 20 km away, is listed in OpenStreetMap as selling AdBlue at the pump, though that source is incomplete.

name: Kilwinning
intro: Known as the Crossroads of Ayrshire, Kilwinning is a North Ayrshire town on the banks of the River Garnock, about 21 miles (34 km) south-west of Glasgow. Its neighbours are the coastal towns of Stevenston to the west and Irvine to the south, with Dalry inland to the north. The 2001 Census recorded 15,908 people, and the 2022 figure is around 16,990. Postcode district KA13 covers the town. Irvine is about 4.9 km away in a straight line, Saltcoats 5.1 km and Ardrossan 6.4 km, with Troon at 12.1 km and Kilmarnock at 14.1 km. The main thing to know about an AdBlue warning here is that service areas are a long way off: the nearest three are all on the M74, between about 44 km and 51.1 km away.
roadsText: Every one of the three nearest service areas to Kilwinning is on the M74, and none is close. Bothwell Services is about 44 km away in a straight line, Hamilton Services about 44.5 km and the M74 Truck Stop about 51.1 km. From the KA13 district the road distance will be longer still, so it is worth planning the route before setting off with a warning.

name: King's Lynn
intro: A port and market town, King's Lynn was known as Bishop's Lynn until 1537 and is colloquially called Lynn. It is in the borough of King's Lynn and West Norfolk, about 5 miles (8 km) inland from The Wash estuary, and had 47,610 people in 2021. Distances to the larger centres are long: the town is 36 miles (58 km) north-east of Peterborough, 44 miles (71 km) north-north-east of Cambridge and 44 miles (71 km) west of Norwich. Closer neighbours are Downham Market at 17.7 km and Wisbech at 20.1 km, while March, Watton, Dereham and Boston are all more than 30 km away. That matters for anyone nursing a diesel with an AdBlue warning. Main roads listed are the A47, A10, A17, A148 and A149, plus the A1076 and A1078. The postcode district is PE30.
roadsText: The A47, A10, A17, A148 and A149 all reach King's Lynn, with the A1076 and A1078 also listed. Freebridge Park, listed as a service area on the A47, is just 3.1 km away. After that the choice thins out: Sutterton Services on the A16 is 36.4 km off and Springfield Services on the A151 is 36.5 km away.

name: Kingsteignton
intro: Only since 1 January 2009 has Kingsteignton been a town: the parish council changed its status because of the threat of it being absorbed into nearby Newton Abbot, which is just 2.9 km away. It lies at the head of the Teign Estuary, to the west of Teignmouth, in the Teignbridge district of south Devon. The town has two electoral wards, east and west, with a combined population of 11,147 at the 2011 census, and it is covered by the TQ12 postcode district. Several roads serve it: the A380 takes traffic around the town, and it also sits on the A383, A381, B3193 and B3195. Teignmouth is 6.7 km away, Torquay 8.1 km and Dawlish 10 km. Despite those road links, the nearest listed service area for a driver with an AdBlue warning is Moto Exeter Services on the M5, 20.6 km away in a straight line.
roadsText: The A380 takes traffic around Kingsteignton, and the town is also on the A383, A381, B3193 and B3195. Even so, the nearest listed service area is Moto Exeter Services on the M5, 20.6 km away in a straight line, with ExtraMSA Cullompton Services at 37.9 km and Moto Tiverton Services at 44.1 km. Road distances will be longer than these figures.

name: Kingston upon Hull
intro: Where the River Hull meets the Humber Estuary, 25 miles (40 km) inland from the North Sea, sits the port city of Kingston upon Hull, usually just called Hull. It is a tightly bounded city that leaves out most of its suburbs: the city population was 273,257 in 2025, while the built-up area holds 436,300. For drivers, that means plenty of the area you might think of as Hull lies outside the city line. Neighbouring places are close, with Cottingham 5.7 km from the centre as the crow flies, Willerby and Anlaby at 7.5 km and Hessle at 8.6 km. Postcode districts include HU1, HU2, HU3, HU5, HU6, HU7, HU8 and HU9. The main roads listed are all A roads, among them the A63, A1033, A1079 and A165, and no motorway appears in that list, which shapes where you can stop if an AdBlue warning comes on.
roadsText: Main roads around Hull include the A63, A1033, A1079, A165, A1165, A1105, A1174 and A1166, none of them motorways. Service areas are thin on the ground. The nearest is Ulceby Truckstop on the A160, 16.1 km away as the crow flies; after that, Doncaster North services on the M180 is 47.4 km and Showground Services on the A15 is 54.5 km. With an AdBlue warning, it pays not to count on a motorway stop.

name: Kingston upon Thames
intro: The oldest of the four royal boroughs in England, the Royal Borough of Kingston upon Thames lies in southwest London. Kingston upon Thames is the main town, and the borough also includes Chessington, Malden Rushett, New Malden, Surbiton and Tolworth. Clockwise from the north, its neighbours are Richmond upon Thames, Wandsworth, Merton and Sutton, followed by the Surrey districts of Epsom and Ewell, Mole Valley and Elmbridge. The borough is home to around 166,333 people. The main roads listed are the A3, A24, A217, A232, A240, A243, A308 and A309, and the postcode districts include KT1, KT2, KT3, KT4, KT5, KT6, KT7 and KT9. Worcester Park and Stoneleigh is 3.2km away, West Molesey 4.4km and Merton 5.7km. With three Surrey districts among its neighbours, an AdBlue warning on a Kingston round can easily turn up just outside London.
roadsText: In Kingston, the main roads listed include the A3, A240, A243, A308, A309, A24, A217 and A232. Heston Services on the M4 is 13km away and Cobham Services on the M25 13.4km. Wisley Services is 18.4km away on the A3, the same road that appears in the borough's own list. A station at Catford, 19.6km away, is listed as selling AdBlue at the pump in OpenStreetMap; that map is not a complete record.

name: Kingswinford
intro: No motorway appears on the road list for Kingswinford, which marks the far western edge of the West Midlands conurbation, 5 miles (8km) west-south-west of Dudley and bordering Staffordshire. Beyond it, a rural area extends past the River Severn. The town is part of the Metropolitan Borough of Dudley, sits at the edge of the Black Country and had a built-up area population of 51,910 in 2021. Postcodes include DY5, DY6 and DY8. The listed roads are the A491, A449, A461, A4036, A458, A4123, A4101 and A4102. Brierley Hill is about 3.3km away, Sedgley 4km, Dudley 4.5km and Stourbridge 4.8km. That gives drivers a mix of short urban trips into the conurbation and journeys out into the rural area beyond. The nearest service area is about 11.9km away.
roadsText: From Kingswinford, the nearest service area is Frankley services on the M5, about 11.9km away. Hilton Park services on the M6 is 17.9km and Hopwood Park services on the M42 20.3km. The town's listed roads are the A491, A449, A461, A4036, A458, A4123, A4101 and A4102. OpenStreetMap lists forecourts in Warley (about 8.3km) and at DY10 1JS (about 15km) as selling AdBlue at the pump, though it does not record every site.

name: Kingswood and Fishponds
intro: Home to 160,280 people, the Kingswood and Fishponds area takes in Kingswood itself, a town and civil parish in South Gloucestershire within the Bristol Built-up Area, 4.8 km east-north-east of Bristol city centre, with a population of 48,474 in 2023. Kingswood stretches roughly from John Cabot Academy in the west to the A4174 ring road in the east, and locals often count Two Mile Hill, St George East and parts of Hanham and Warmley Hill as Kingswood too. The boundary between South Gloucestershire and the City of Bristol falls at the western end of the High Street. Postcode districts across the area include BS15, BS16, BS30 and BS36, along with BS2, BS4, BS5 and BS7. Stoke Gifford is 4.6 km away, Filton and Bristol 6.7 km, and Keynsham 7.2 km, so most diesel driving here is urban, with the ring road and motorways close by.
roadsText: Main roads around the area include the M4 and M32, the A4174 ring road, and the A4, A4032, A4044, A4175 and A4017. The nearest service areas are Avon Lodge on the A4, 13.4 km away, Gordano on the M5 at 14.3 km and Severn View on the M48 at 16.4 km. With the motorways close but services further out, it helps to plan a stop before a longer run.

name: Kippax
intro: Until 1939 Kippax was a separate civil parish in Tadcaster Rural District; that year it was annexed to Garforth, and it regained parish status and a parish council on 1 April 2004. Today it is a town and civil parish in the City of Leeds, West Yorkshire, lying east of the city near Garforth and Great Preston, and its parish had 9,785 residents at the 2011 Census. The Kippax and Methley ward of Leeds City Council is part of the Selby parliamentary constituency. The town's postcode district is LS25. Garforth is only 2.6 km away and Castleford 5.7 km, with Normanton, Rothwell, Pontefract and Featherstone all within 10 km. For a van or diesel car with an AdBlue warning, two service areas are 6.5 km from the centre in a straight line, one on the M62 and one on the M1.
roadsText: Two service areas are 6.5 km from Kippax in a straight line: the Whitwood service area on the M62 and Skelton Lake Service Station on the M1. Ferrybridge Services, also on the M62, is 10.6 km away. OpenStreetMap lists a station in Leeds (LS9 0AS), 6.5 km away, and one in Pontefract (WF7 7HX), 14 km away, as selling AdBlue at the pump. That data is not complete.

name: Kirk Sandall and Edenthorpe
intro: The name Kirk Sandall mixes Old English and Old Norse: Sandall comes from sandhalh, 'sandy nook of land', and Kirk from kirkja, 'church'. This outer suburb of Doncaster lies around 4 miles (6.4 km) north-east of the city centre, in the civil parish of Barnby Dun with Kirk Sandall, South Yorkshire, and is served by Kirk Sandall railway station. This page covers it together with Edenthorpe; the combined area has 13,090 residents and sits in the DN3 postcode district. In 1921 the parish had just 606 people, and on 1 October that year it was abolished to form Barnby Dun with Kirk Sandall. Armthorpe is 2.9 km away and Dunscroft and Hatfield 4.3 km, with Bentley at 5.6 km. If an AdBlue warning comes on, Doncaster (North) Services on the M180 is the nearest listed service area, 6.4 km from the centre.
roadsText: Doncaster (North) Services on the M180 is the closest service area to Kirk Sandall and Edenthorpe, 6.4 km away in a straight line. Barnsdale Bar Services on the A1 is 13.2 km off and Blyth Services on the A1(M) 19.1 km. OpenStreetMap lists a station in Doncaster (DN4 0TP), 9.3 km away, and one in Pontefract (WF7 7HX), 19.8 km away, as selling AdBlue at the pump. Other stations may not be mapped.

name: Kirkby
intro: Until the mid-20th century Kirkby was mainly farmland. Its urban development came in the post-war period, after ROF Kirkby, the largest Royal Ordnance Factory filling munitions, was built there during the Second World War. It lies 6 miles north-east of Liverpool and 5 miles north of Huyton and covers 4,070 acres. Historically in Lancashire, it had 41,495 people in 2016, making it the largest town in Knowsley. Postcode districts L10, L32 and L33 are listed. Two motorways, the M57 and M58, are on the road list, with the A506, A5207, A580, A59, A5758 and A5036. Maghull is the nearest town at 5.2 km, followed by Huyton with Roby (7.4 km), Litherland (7.6 km), Bootle (8.1 km), Liverpool (8.3 km) and Ormskirk (8.9 km). For a driver with an AdBlue warning, Old Meadow Services is just 4.1 km away.
roadsText: Kirkby's main roads include the M57 and M58, with the A506, A5207, A580, A59, A5758 and A5036. Old Meadow Services on the M58 is 4.1 km away and Earlsfield Services on the M57 6.9 km, with Burtonwood Services on the M62 at 17.5 km. A station at Old Meadow (4.2 km) and one in Warrington's WA5 (16.5 km) are listed as selling AdBlue at the pump in OpenStreetMap; an L5 site 9.6 km away is HGV-only. Its records are incomplete.

name: Kirkby-in-Ashfield
intro: Part of the wider Mansfield Urban Area, Kirkby-in-Ashfield is a market town in Nottinghamshire's Ashfield district, with 21,285 residents at the 2021 census. It lies on the eastern edge of the Erewash Valley, which separates Nottinghamshire from Derbyshire, and Ashfield District Council has its head offices on Urban Road in the town centre. The NG17 postcode district covers the town. Neighbouring places are close: Sutton in Ashfield is 3.2 km away, South Normanton and Pinxton 5.4 km and Mansfield 5.8 km, with Hucknall, Mansfield Woodhouse and Somercotes and Swanwick all under 9 km. Drivers here have the M1 within reach, as Tibshelf Services is 6.8 km from the town, and a station listed as selling AdBlue at the pump is only a little further.
roadsText: Tibshelf Services on the M1 is the closest service area to Kirkby-in-Ashfield, at 6.8 km. Beyond that, Trowell Services, also on the M1, is 15.3 km away and Trent Bridge Services on the A6011 is 19.2 km away. A station 7.5 km from the town is listed on OpenStreetMap as selling AdBlue at the pump. Because that map data is incomplete, other forecourts may stock it as well.

name: Kirkcaldy and Dysart
intro: Nicknamed the Lang Toun for its long main street, Kirkcaldy is a former royal burgh in Fife, on the east coast of Scotland, and Fife's second-largest settlement, with 51,117 people in 2022. That street eventually stretched to nearly six kilometres, connecting the burgh to Linktown, Pathhead, Sinclairtown and Gallatown, which became part of the town in 1876; the former burgh of Dysart was absorbed in 1930. The town lies about 19 km north of Edinburgh and 44 km south-southwest of Dundee. KY1 and KY2 are the postcode districts, and the A92, A910, A915, A921 and A955 are the recorded main roads. Glenrothes is 8 km away and Methil 11.4 km, with Dunfermline at 17.5 km. The nearest service area is more than 19 km away, so drivers in Kirkcaldy and Dysart are better off knowing their options before an AdBlue warning appears.
roadsText: The A92, A910, A921, A955 and A915 are the main roads recorded around Kirkcaldy. No service area is especially close: Kinross Services on the M90 is the nearest at 19.3 km, with Musselburgh Services on the A1 at 23 km and Dreghorn Services on the A720 at 25.2 km. Drivers who see an AdBlue warning in town are better off dealing with it early than counting on reaching one of these stops.

name: Kirkintilloch
intro: Set on the Forth and Clyde Canal and the south side of Strathkelvin, Kirkintilloch lies about 8 miles (13 km) north-east of central Glasgow. It is a Burgh of Barony, historically part of Dunbartonshire, and the administrative home of the East Dunbartonshire council area. The population was 19,689 in 2011, and the town uses the G66 postcode district. Bishopbriggs is about 5.9 km away in a straight line and Kilsyth 6.7 km, with Cumbernauld at 9 km, and Coatbridge, Milngavie and Glasgow all between 11.3 km and 11.8 km. That puts several towns within a short drive, but the nearest service areas, on the M74 and M9, are between 14.6 km and 20.5 km away, which is worth knowing if an AdBlue warning appears on a van or diesel car.
roadsText: Bothwell Services on the M74 is the closest service area to Kirkintilloch, about 14.6 km away in a straight line. Hamilton Services, also on the M74, is about 17.9 km away and Stirling Services on the M9 about 20.5 km. In OpenStreetMap, a station in Glasgow (G11 6DN), about 13.2 km away, is listed as selling AdBlue at the pump. That record is incomplete, so others may exist.

name: Knaresborough
intro: Knaresborough, a market and spa town on the River Nidd in North Yorkshire, lies three miles (5 km) east of Harrogate. It was part of the Borough of Harrogate until April 2023. The town has a population of 15,781 and uses the HG5 postcode district. Harrogate is about 5.3 km away in a straight line and Wetherby 9.7 km, while Ripon is around 15.4 km and Otley 18.8 km. For a van or diesel car with an AdBlue warning, the nearest listed service area is Wetherby Services on the A1(M), around 9.4 km away, which puts it roughly as far as Wetherby itself. Beyond that, the next options are Bilbrough Top on the A64 and Skelton Lake on the M1, both more than 20 km off, so the A1(M) site is the closest option by a clear margin.
roadsText: From Knaresborough, the closest service area in a straight line is Wetherby Services on the A1(M), about 9.4 km away. Bilbrough Top Service Area on the A64 is about 21.6 km away and Skelton Lake Service Station on the M1 about 26.2 km. That leaves the A1(M) site well ahead as the nearest option, with the other two more than twice as far.

name: Knowle and Dorridge
intro: Knowle is a large village 3 miles (5 km) east-south-east of Solihull. It lies within the Arden area of historic Warwickshire, and since 1974 it has been part of the Metropolitan Borough of Solihull. Dorridge and Bentley Heath, similar-sized and mainly residential communities, adjoin it to the south, with Copt Heath to the north and Tilehouse Green to the south. Knowle had a recorded population of 10,678 and is 2.5 miles from the Warwickshire border. B93 is the postcode district. Kenilworth is 12.3 km away, Birmingham 13.9 km, Redditch 15.6 km and Coventry 16.3 km. For a driver with an AdBlue warning, the nearest listed service area is on the M42 at 13.7 km in a straight line, with another on the A46 at 14.2 km, so there is no motorway stop right next to the village.
roadsText: The nearest service areas to Knowle and Dorridge are Hopwood Park Services on the M42, 13.7 km away in a straight line, Warwick North (Budbrooke) Services on the A46 at 14.2 km and Corley Services on the M6 at 17.2 km. OpenStreetMap lists an HGV-only refuelling site in Birmingham (B25 8DW), 11.3 km away, as selling AdBlue at the pump, but it is meant for lorries rather than vans or cars. That data is incomplete, so other stations may sell AdBlue.

name: Knutsford
intro: Knutsford Services on the M6 is only about 2.1 km from Knutsford, and Tabley Hill Service Station is 3.2 km away, so this Cheshire East market town has motorway services almost on its doorstep. It lies 14 miles (23 km) south-west of Manchester, 9 miles (14 km) north-west of Macclesfield and 12½ miles (20 km) south-east of Warrington, on the Cheshire Plain. The 2021 census counted 13,259 people in the parish. Princess Street, known locally as Top Street, and King Street lower down, known as Bottom Street, form the hub of the town, and at one end of the narrow King Street is an entrance to Tatton Park. The WA16 postcode district covers Knutsford. Hale is about 7.6 km away and Wilmslow 9.8 km. For a driver dealing with an AdBlue warning, Lymm Services, also on the M6, is a third option at about 10.8 km.
roadsText: Knutsford Services on the M6 is the nearest service area, about 2.1 km from the town, with Tabley Hill Service Station, also on the M6, at around 3.2 km. Lymm Services on the M6 is roughly 10.8 km off. OpenStreetMap has a station under Warrington, about 16.6 km away, listed as selling AdBlue at the pump. OpenStreetMap's coverage is incomplete, so places nearer town may also stock it.

name: Lambeth
intro: Few places are more central: the geographical centre of London is at Frazier Street, near Lambeth North tube station, in this South London borough, although Charing Cross across the Thames is traditionally treated as the centre. Lambeth forms part of Inner London and has a population of around 317,108. Its name was recorded in 1062 as Lambehitha, meaning landing place for lambs. For drivers, the useful facts are its postcode districts, which include SE19, SE21, SE24, SE27, SW2, SW4, SW12 and SW16, and its listed main roads, which are all A-roads: the A23, A24, A3, A205, A214, A203, A217 and A3220. With Wandsworth 4.6km away, Southwark 6.4km and Merton 6.6km, a van working across the borough is never far from a neighbouring one, and an AdBlue warning can surface on either side of the boundary.
roadsText: The main roads listed for Lambeth are the A205, A23, A214, A24, A203, A3, A217 and A3220, with no motorway among them. The nearest service areas are some way out: Heston Services on the M4 at 20km, Clacket Lane Services on the M25 at 21.1km and London Gateway Services on the M1 at 24.3km. Stations listed as selling AdBlue at the pump in OpenStreetMap include one at Catford (7.6km) and one 18.1km away; the map data is not complete.

name: Lancaster
intro: Lancaster is the county town of Lancashire, although the county council has been based in Preston since 1889. The city lies on the River Lune, directly inland from Morecambe Bay, and Morecambe itself is only 3.7 km away, with Heysham at 5.5 km. Beyond those two, the next towns in the data are more than 20 km off: Fleetwood (21.7 km), Thornton (23.7 km), and Cleveleys and Ulverston (both 24.4 km). The city had 52,660 people at the 2021 census and the wider district 142,931. LA1 is the postcode district listed. The M6 heads the road list, together with the A683, A6, A589, A588 and A5105. Glasson Dock, downstream, has long been the area's main shipping facility. For a driver with an AdBlue warning, the nearest service area in the data is on the M6, 10.4 km away.
roadsText: Lancaster's main roads are the M6, A683, A6, A589, A588 and A5105. All three service areas in the data are on the M6: Lancaster Services at 10.4 km, Burton-in-Kendal Services at 14.7 km and Killington Lake Services at 31 km. The first two are the realistic stops for a driver in LA1, with the third much further out.

name: Lancing and Sompting
intro: Lancing sits on the western edge of the Adur Valley in West Sussex, in the narrow central part of the Sussex coastal plain, with Sompting to the west, Shoreham-by-Sea to the east and the parish of Coombes to the north. Together the two places make up the area this page covers, with a population of 27,924. Lancing is a large coastal village in the Adur district, and its economy is usually treated as part of the Brighton, Worthing and Littlehampton conurbation. The area mixes mid-rise coastal homes with farmland and the chalk downs to the north. Postcode districts listed are BN15, BN14 and BN95. The A27 and A259 lead a road list that also includes the A24, A283, A2025, A2031, A2032 and A2037. Shoreham-by-Sea is 4km away and Worthing 5.3km, so many trips are short runs between neighbouring towns.
roadsText: Main roads listed around Lancing and Sompting are the A27, A283, A24, A2025, A259, A2031, A2032 and A2037. The nearest service area is Pyecombe Services on the A23 (13.1km), with Ricebridge Services (Hickstead) on the A23 and Buck Barn on the A24 both 17.7km away. One station about 14.2km away is listed as selling AdBlue at the pump; OpenStreetMap's list is incomplete.

name: Larbert
intro: In the Forth Valley, above the River Carron, Larbert lies north-west of Falkirk and three miles from the shoreline of the Firth of Forth. Stenhousemuir adjoins it directly to the east, and the two settlements are contiguous and share some public amenities. The town grew with the arrival of the Scottish Central Railway in the 1840s and was long underpinned by heavy industry such as boilermaking, casting and manufacturing. Around 12,180 people live here today, in the FK5 postcode district. Falkirk is 3.5 km from the centre, Grangemouth 7.1 km and Alloa 10 km, with Stirling at 11.9 km. A driver dealing with an AdBlue warning has a fairly short trip to motorway services, since Stirling Services on the M9 is 7.8 km from the town centre in a straight line.
roadsText: The nearest listed service area to Larbert is Stirling Services on the M9, 7.8 km away in a straight line. Heart of Scotland Services on the M8 is 18.9 km off and Balhaldie Services on the A9 is 22.4 km away. The M9 site is the obvious first option. All three distances are straight-line figures, and the drive itself will be longer.

name: Largs
intro: A seaside resort with a pier on the Firth of Clyde, Largs is a coastal town in North Ayrshire with a population of 10,917 in 2022. Its Gaelic name means "the slopes", and the town promotes its historic links with the Vikings. In 1263 it was the site of the Battle of Largs between the Norwegian and Scottish armies. Its postcode district is KA30. What stands out for drivers is how spread out the surrounding area is. The closest neighbouring towns are all more than 16 km away: Ardrossan at 16.7 km, Greenock at 17.4 km, Gourock at 17.5 km and Saltcoats at 17.8 km. The nearest listed motorway services are about 50 km away in a straight line, so a van or diesel car with an AdBlue warning here has a long way to go before reaching any.
roadsText: Largs is around 50 km in a straight line from the nearest listed service areas, all on the M74: Bothwell Services at 50.1 km, Hamilton Services at 51.7 km and the M74 Truck Stop at 63 km. The real driving distance will be greater. If an AdBlue warning appears in or around the town, plan for that distance rather than assuming services are close at hand.

name: Larkfield
intro: Strictly a village, Larkfield is the more built-up part of the civil parish of East Malling and Larkfield, in the Kent borough of Tonbridge and Malling. It lies on and north of the A20, and the M20 also passes through, with junction 4 at the centre of Leybourne on the A228. That puts motorway driving very close to home for local vans and diesel cars. The ME20, ME6 and ME19 postcode districts cover the area, which has a population of 26,147. Snodland is 3.4 km away and Maidstone 6.1 km, while Chatham, Rochester and Gillingham are between 9.2 km and 11.8 km. The name is literal: it refers to the large numbers of skylarks found in the fields, and it first appears in Domesday Book as Lavrochesfel. For a driver dealing with an AdBlue warning, the short distances to Maidstone and Chatham matter as much as the motorway junction.
roadsText: Larkfield is well connected: the M20, M2 and M26 are all nearby, along with the A228, A229, A20 and A26. Medway services on the M2 is 12.1 km away, Maidstone services on the M20 is 12.2 km and Tollgate on the A2 is 14.4 km. In OpenStreetMap data, a station at Strood (ME2 2NY), 10 km away, and another 19.4 km away are listed as selling AdBlue at the pump. That map is incomplete, so others may stock it too.

name: Larkhall
intro: Around 14 miles (23 km) south-east of Glasgow, Larkhall sits on high ground between the River Clyde to the east and the Avon Water to the west, on the edge of the Clyde valley. It is a commuter town for Glasgow. The South Lanarkshire town had 15,308 residents in 2022 and is a typical Scottish former industrial town: mining, weaving and textiles were its traditional trades, and most of those industries, including the Lanarkshire ironworks, have closed. Postcode district ML9 covers the town. Wishaw is about 5.4 km away in a straight line, Motherwell 6 km and Hamilton 6.8 km, with Carluke at 8.6 km. Three service areas, all on the M74, lie between about 7 km and 10.9 km away, so a driver with an AdBlue warning has options within reach.
roadsText: All three of the nearest service areas to Larkhall are on the M74. Hamilton Services is about 7 km away in a straight line, Bothwell Services about 10.4 km and the M74 Truck Stop about 10.9 km. Road distances from the ML9 district will be longer than these straight-line figures, but all three are within a short run of the town.

name: Larne
intro: As a major roll-on roll-off port for passengers and freight, Larne sees vehicles arriving and leaving by sea as well as by road. The town sits on the east coast of County Antrim, within the Mid and East Antrim Borough Council area, and had 18,853 residents at the 2021 census. It lies in the historic barony of Glenarm Upper, and its postcode district is BT40. In a straight line, Carrickfergus is about 14.9 km away and Ballyclare 16.1 km, with Newtownabbey at 22 km, Bangor at 23.1 km and Holywood at 23.5 km. Belfast is about 29 km off. Should an AdBlue warning appear, the nearest service area is on the M2 at about 21.6 km and the next is on the M1 at 38 km, so neither is close to the town.
roadsText: Temple Patrick Services Northbound on the M2 is the nearest service area to Larne, about 21.6 km away in a straight line. Lisburn Services on the M1 is about 38 km away and Glenshane Tourist Services on the A6 about 57.9 km. For drivers coming off a ferry with a warning showing, that M2 stop is the closest of the three, and the road distance will be longer than the figure above.

name: Leatherhead
intro: Its name is thought to come from the ford on the River Mole beside which Leatherhead grew up. Now a town in the Mole Valley district of Surrey, it lies about 17 mi (27 km) south of Central London. The arrival of turnpike roads in the mid-18th century and of the railways in the second half of the 19th century brought newcomers to what had long been an agricultural settlement. Today the town is in the KT22 postcode district and has several close neighbours: Ashtead is 2.6 km away, Great Bookham and Fetcham 4.3 km, Epsom 5.8 km, and Dorking and Tadworth and Epsom Downs both 6.5 km. When an AdBlue warning comes on, the nearest listed service area is Cobham Services on the M25, 6.8 km away in a straight line.
roadsText: The nearest service areas to Leatherhead, in a straight line, are Cobham Services on the M25 at 6.8 km, Wisley Services on the A3 at 12.2 km and Heston Services on the M4 at 23 km. Cobham and Wisley are both within 12.2 km, giving drivers in KT22 a choice between an M25 stop and an A3 stop. Driving distances will be greater than these figures.

name: Lee-on-the-Solent
intro: Often shortened to Lee-on-Solent, Lee-on-the-Solent is a seaside district of the borough of Gosport in Hampshire, on the Solent coast west of Portsmouth. It is primarily residential, with a summer upsurge of mostly local visitors, and was formerly home to the Royal Naval Air Station HMS Daedalus. The area covered here has about 24,307 residents and uses the PO14 postcode district. Fareham is the nearest town at 3.6 km, with Gosport at 5.1 km, Locks Heath at 6.1 km and Portsmouth at 9.9 km. Cowes and Ryde are 10.3 km and 11.6 km away in a straight line. Main roads listed around Lee include the M27, A32 and A27, so the motorway is within reach for a van or diesel car, although the nearest listed service area is 12.4 km away on the A27.
roadsText: Main roads listed around Lee-on-the-Solent are the M27, A32 and A27. The nearest listed service area is Farlington Services on the A27, 12.4 km away in a straight line. Rownhams Services on the M27 is 22.3 km off and West Wellow Services on the A36 is 26.9 km away. Driving distances to each will be longer than these straight-line figures.

name: Leeds
intro: As the largest settlement in Yorkshire and the administrative centre of the City of Leeds Metropolitan Borough, Leeds is a big area to cover with an AdBlue warning on the dashboard. The city is built around the River Aire in the eastern foothills of the Pennines. It grew from a market town into a mill town during the Industrial Revolution, and after gaining city status in 1893 it formed a populous urban centre that absorbed the villages around it. Its population is now put at 536,262. Motorways feature strongly: the M621 and M1 are listed among the main roads, as are the A58(M) and A64(M), along with the A58, A61, A64 and A660. Postcode districts include LS1, LS2, LS3, LS4, LS6, LS7, LS9 and LS12. Rothwell is 7.3 km from the centre as the crow flies, Morley 7.5 km and Pudsey 8 km.
roadsText: Main roads around Leeds include the M621, M1, A58(M) and A64(M), plus the A660, A58, A61 and A64. The nearest service areas as the crow flies are Skelton Lake Service Station on the M1 (6.5 km), Whitwood on the M62 (14.5 km) and Hartshead Moor on the M62 (16.3 km). OpenStreetMap lists a station with a Leeds address, 6.6 km from the centre, as selling AdBlue at the pump. That data is incomplete, so other forecourts may sell it too.

name: Leek
intro: On the River Churnet, 10 miles (16 km) north east of Stoke-on-Trent, Leek is a market town and the administrative centre for the Staffordshire Moorlands District. It is an ancient borough, granted its royal charter in 1214, and in 1207 King John granted the right to hold a weekly Wednesday market there. The 2021 population was 19,385, and the town is covered by the ST13 postcode district. Biddulph is 9.2 km away, followed by Cheadle at 13.5 km, Congleton at 13.9 km and Kidsgrove at 14.1 km, with Newcastle-under-Lyme 16.8 km away. For a diesel driver, the main point is that the three nearest listed service areas are all on the M6, the closest 18.6 km away in a straight line, so there is no motorway stop close to the town.
roadsText: All three of the nearest service areas to Leek are on the M6: Swift Services, 18.6 km away in a straight line, and Crewe Services and Sandbach Services, both at 20.6 km. A station in Newcastle-under-Lyme (ST5 4DH), at the same 18.6 km as Swift Services, is listed in OpenStreetMap as selling AdBlue at the pump. OpenStreetMap data is incomplete, so there may be closer options.

name: Lees
intro: Amongst the Pennines east of the River Medlock, Lees is a town in the Metropolitan Borough of Oldham, 1.8 miles (2.9 km) east of Oldham and 8.2 miles (13.2 km) northeast of Manchester. It began as a group of hamlets where farming was the main industry, and it grew into a mill town in the late 19th century on the back of Oldham's cotton spinning boom, with eleven cotton mills at its peak. It has about 12,641 residents, and the OL4 postcode district covers it. Mossley is about 2.8 km away and Uppermill 3.5 km, with Shaw, Royton and Ashton-under-Lyne between 5.1 km and 5.3 km. For a driver with an AdBlue warning, the nearest motorway service area is Birch Services on the M62, around 11.6 km away.
roadsText: Birch Services on the M62 is the nearest service area to Lees, about 11.6 km away. Hartshead Moor services, also on the M62, is around 28.5 km off, and Blackburn with Darwen Services on the M65 about 33.5 km. OpenStreetMap has a site roughly 5.9 km away listed as selling AdBlue at the pump, plus a station under Manchester at about 14.9 km. Those records are incomplete.

name: Leicester
intro: The largest city in the East Midlands, Leicester is the county town of Leicestershire and sits on the River Soar, about 33 miles (53 km) east-northeast of Birmingham. Nottingham and Derby lie around 21 miles (34 km) to the north and northwest, and Coventry is a similar distance away. The city had 383,116 residents in 2025 and the greater urban area counted 559,017 in 2021, so this is a large built-up area rather than a compact town. Postcode districts in and around it include LE1, LE2, LE3, LE4, LE5, LE6, LE18 and LE19. Wigston, Oadby and Birstall are each only about 5.5 to 5.6 km away, with Blaby and Whetstone at 7.3 km. Two motorways, the M1 and M69, are among the main roads alongside the A6, A47 and A50, and a motorway service area sits under 5 km from the city.
roadsText: Main roads around Leicester include the M1, M69, A6, A47, A50, A563, A607 and A5460. The nearest service area is Leicester Forest East Services on the M1, about 4.7 km away. ExtraMSA Leicester Services on the A6 is around 6.5 km out, and Six Hills Services Northbound on the A46 is about 14.6 km away, giving a third option further out.

name: Leicester Forest East and Kirby Muxloe
intro: Straddling the M1 to the west of Leicester, Leicester Forest East is a large suburban village in the Blaby district that this page covers together with Kirby Muxloe. Housing was built here mainly between 1920 and 1985, first along the Hinckley Road (A47) and to the south-east of the motorway, then to the north-east and west of it in the 1960s, with a further development on the western edge in the 1980s. The area is popular with commuters and falls in the LE3 postcode district. Leicester is 5.6 km away and Enderby and Narborough 4.4 km, with Blaby and Whetstone at 7 km. For a van or diesel car with an AdBlue warning, the service area that shares the village's name is about 1.2 km away.
roadsText: Leicester Forest East Services, on the M1, is about 1.2 km from the area. Much of the village's housing was built along the Hinckley Road (A47) and on either side of the motorway. Beyond the motorway stop, ExtraMSA Leicester Services on the A6 is 9.8 km away and Six Hills Services Northbound on the A46 is 18.1 km away.

name: Leigh
intro: On low-lying land north-west of Chat Moss, Leigh sits about 6 miles south-east of Wigan and 11 miles west of Manchester city centre. It is a town in the Wigan district of Greater Manchester and had a population of 53,000 in 2011. Leigh became the official name in 1875, when the townships of Pennington, Westleigh and Bedford merged, and part of Atherton was added in 1894. Historically in Lancashire, it moved from dairy farming to silk and later cotton. Every road on its list is an A-road: the A579, A577, A580, A58, A6, A578, A572 and A574. Postcode districts WN7 and M46 cover the town. Six towns are within 5 km: Golborne and Atherton (4.2 km), Hindley (4.6 km), Platt Bridge and Abram (4.7 km), Tyldesley (4.9 km) and Westhoughton (5 km). The nearest listed service area is 11.3 km away.
roadsText: Leigh's main roads are the A579, A577, A580, A58, A6, A578, A572 and A574, with no motorway among them. The nearest service areas are Rivington Services on the M61 at 11.3 km, Burtonwood Services on the M62 at 11.6 km and Lymm Services on the M6 at 16 km. Stations in Warrington's WA3 (9.1 km) and WA5 (13.2 km) and in Manchester's M25 postcode district (16.7 km) are listed as selling AdBlue at the pump in OpenStreetMap, which does not record every site.

name: Leighton Buzzard
intro: Close to the Buckinghamshire border, in the south-west of Bedfordshire, Leighton Buzzard is a market town in the civil parish of Leighton-Linslade. It lies between Aylesbury, Tring, Luton/Dunstable and Milton Keynes, near the Chiltern Hills, and is 36 miles (58 km) north-west of Central London. The built-up area extends on either side of the River Ouzel and includes Linslade, historically a separate place, with both now run by Leighton-Linslade Town Council. Main roads listed are the A5, A505, A418, A4146 and A4012, and the nearest listed services are all on the M1, so a van with an AdBlue fault has some driving to do to reach them. Bletchley is 9.5 km away, Houghton Regis 9.7 km and Dunstable 9.8 km, while Tring is 13.6 km off and Flitwick and Milton Keynes both 14.7 km. The postcode district is LU7, and the population is 42,736.
roadsText: Listed roads are the A5, A505, A418, A4146 and A4012. The nearest service areas are all on the M1: Toddington Services at 11.4 km, Crawley Crossing Truck Stop at 12.1 km and Newport Pagnell Services at 19 km. Reaching any of these listed service areas from Leighton Buzzard therefore means a drive out to the M1.

name: Leominster
intro: Where the River Kenwater flows into the River Lugg, Leominster is a Herefordshire market town 12 miles (19 km) north of Hereford and 7 miles (11 km) south of Ludlow in Shropshire. With a population of almost 12,000, it is the largest of the county's five towns; the others are Ross-on-Wye, Ledbury, Bromyard and Kington. From 1974 to 1996 it was the administrative centre of the former Leominster district, and today it sits in the HR6 postcode district. For anyone driving a van or diesel car here, distance is the thing to plan around if an AdBlue warning appears. The nearest listed service area is 35.2 km away in a straight line, on the M50. Ludlow and Hereford are the closest neighbouring towns. Great Malvern, Stourport-on-Severn, Ross-on-Wye and Worcester are all more than 30 km off.
roadsText: Leominster is a long way from the nearest service areas. Measured in a straight line from the town centre, Ross Spur Services on the M50 is 35.2 km away, Symonds Yat Services on the A40 is 41.9 km and Strensham Services on the M5 is 44.6 km. Distances by road will be longer, so a driver in HR6 dealing with an AdBlue warning should plan any stop with that in mind.

name: Letchworth
intro: The first garden city, Letchworth Garden City, usually just called Letchworth, is a town in North Hertfordshire with 33,990 people in its built-up area at the 2021 census. It appears in the Domesday Book but stayed a small rural village until 1903, when land in Letchworth and the neighbouring parishes of Willian and Norton was bought to build a garden city following Ebenezer Howard's principles. The aim was a settlement with jobs, services and good housing that kept the quality of the countryside. Raymond Unwin and Barry Parker designed the initial layout, which includes the United Kingdom's first roundabout, Sollershott Circus, built around 1909. The A1(M) and A1 are listed, along with the A505, A507, A600 and A602. Baldock is just 2.7 km away, Stotfold 4 km and Hitchin 4.4 km, with Stevenage 8.1 km and Biggleswade 11.8 km. Postcode districts are SG5 and SG6.
roadsText: The A1(M) and A1 are listed for Letchworth, along with the A505, A507, A600 and A602. Baldock Services on the A1(M) is close, at 4.2 km. Toddington Services on the M1 is 19.3 km away, and Bedford Services on the A421 is 22.4 km away, so Baldock is by far the nearest of the three.

name: Lewes
intro: The county town of East Sussex, Lewes is also the administrative centre of the district that shares its name. It lies on the River Ouse at the point where the river cuts through the South Downs, about 7 miles (11 km) north-east of Brighton and 11 miles (18 km) north-west of Eastbourne. Lewes has long been a market town and a centre of communications, and the 2021 census put the parish population at 16,723. Its postcode district is BN7. A driver with an AdBlue warning in or around Lewes has Brighton and Hove 8.5 km away, Peacehaven 8.6 km and Newhaven 9.9 km, with Uckfield, Burgess Hill and Seaford all between 12.5 km and 13.5 km. The nearest listed service area is Pyecombe Services on the A23 at 12.6 km in a straight line, and a station 9.8 km away is listed in OpenStreetMap as selling AdBlue at the pump.
roadsText: Two of the three closest service areas to Lewes are on the A23: Pyecombe Services at 12.6 km and Ricebridge Services (Hickstead) at 17.1 km, both measured in a straight line. Polegate Services on the A22 is a similar distance at 17.2 km. OpenStreetMap lists a station 9.8 km from the town as selling AdBlue at the pump, though that map data is incomplete and other forecourts may stock it.

name: Lewisham
intro: In south-east London, the borough of Lewisham forms part of Inner London, with the town of Lewisham as its principal settlement and the council based in Catford. The Prime Meridian passes through the borough, and Blackheath, Goldsmiths, University of London and Millwall F.C. are all inside it. Its population is about 300,764. The main roads listed are the A2, A20, A21, A102, A202, A205, A210 and A2213, and the borough's postcodes cover SE4, SE6, SE12, SE13, SE14, SE22, SE23 and SE26. Southwark (5.5km), Greenwich (5.6km) and Lambeth (6.7km) are the nearest neighbouring areas, with Bromley at 8.8km. With no motorway in the road list and the nearest listed service area 20km away, a van with an AdBlue warning here is more likely to be on the borough's own A-roads than on a motorway.
roadsText: For Lewisham, the listed main roads are the A21, A205, A20, A2, A202, A2213, A210 and A102. Service areas listed are Clacket Lane Services on the M25 (20km), Thurrock Services on the M25 (20.9km) and Heston Services on the M4 (26km). Closer to home, a station at Catford, just 1km away, is listed as selling AdBlue at the pump in OpenStreetMap, as is one 12.7km away. That data is incomplete, so other stations may sell it too.

name: Leyland
intro: Preston is 6 miles to the north of Leyland, a town in the South Ribble district of Lancashire that had a population of 35,578 at the 2011 Census. Its postcode districts are PR25 and PR26. Several neighbours are close by: Euxton is 3.4 km away, Bamber Bridge 4.4 km, Penwortham 5.7 km, Longton 6.2 km and Chorley 6.4 km. For longer trips, the M6, M65 and M61 are all listed among the roads around Leyland, alongside A roads including the A582, A6, A59 and A49. If an AdBlue warning comes on, the nearest service area is Charnock Richard Services on the M6, 7.1 km away, with Rivington Services on the M61 at 13.4 km and Blackburn with Darwen Services on the M65 at 14.8 km.
roadsText: Leyland's listed roads are the M6, M65 and M61, plus the A582, A6, A59, A49 and A5083. The nearest service area is Charnock Richard Services on the M6, 7.1 km away. Rivington Services on the M61 is 13.4 km off and Blackburn with Darwen Services on the M65 is 14.8 km. Preston lies 8.5 km away.

name: Lichfield
intro: A cathedral city in Staffordshire, Lichfield lies 14 miles (22.5 km) north of Birmingham, 9 miles (14 km) north-east of Walsall, 8 miles (13 km) north-west of Tamworth and 18 miles (29 km) south-east of Stafford. The 2021 census recorded 34,738 people in the city and 106,400 across Lichfield District. Its centre still follows the ladder-shaped street pattern laid out in the 12th century under Roger de Clinton. For a diesel driver with a warning light on, the city's position matters more than its history: it sits within reach of several other centres, and the M6 Toll and the A38 are among the main roads nearby. Postcode districts are WS13 and WS14. Measured directly, the closest neighbouring towns are Burntwood at 6.6 km, Brownhills at 8.3 km and Aldridge at 10.8 km, with Rugeley 11.7 km away.
roadsText: Main roads around Lichfield include the M6 Toll and the A38, along with the A51, A461, A5206, A5192, A5127 and A5148. The nearest service areas, measured directly, are Norton Canes on the M6 Toll (9.8 km), Tamworth on the M42 (15.1 km) and The Trucker's Rest on the A5 (16.1 km). OpenStreetMap lists a station with a Burntwood address, 7.4 km away, and one with a Swadlincote address, 18.8 km away, as selling AdBlue at the pump. Its coverage is incomplete, so others may sell it too.

name: Limavady
intro: With Binevenagh as its backdrop, Limavady is a market town in County Londonderry, lying 17 miles (27 km) east of Derry and 14 miles (23 km) south-west of Coleraine. Its population was 11,279 at the 2021 Census, having nearly doubled in the 40 years between 1971 and 2011. Between 1988 and 2004 a total of 1,332 dwellings were built in the town, mainly at Bovally along its south-eastern edge, and a large industrial estate at Aghanloo lies 2 miles (3 km) to the north. The town is part of Causeway Coast and Glens Borough and uses the BT49 postcode district. Ballymoney is about 28.2 km away in a straight line, with Strabane at 41.6 km. If a van or diesel car flags low AdBlue here, the nearest service area is about 27 km away on the A6.
roadsText: The closest service area to Limavady is Glenshane Tourist Services on the A6, about 27 km away in a straight line. The others are much further: Cohannon Services on the M1 at about 63.9 km and Temple Patrick Services Northbound on the M2 at about 71.6 km. From the BT49 district, the A6 stop is therefore the practical choice, and the road distance will be longer than the figure here.

name: Lincoln
intro: A cathedral city and the county town of Lincolnshire, Lincoln stands on the River Witham and is the largest settlement in the county. Its district had 103,813 residents at the 2021 census, while the wider urban area, which includes Bracebridge Heath, North Hykeham, South Hykeham and Waddington, recorded 127,540. North Hykeham is only about 2.9 km away, but beyond the urban area the distances open up: Newark-on-Trent is around 21.4 km away, Gainsborough 24.4 km and Sleaford 25.8 km. Every main road listed for Lincoln is an A road, chiefly the A46, A15, A57 and A607, plus the A1192 and A1434. Postcode districts covering the city are LN1, LN2, LN5 and LN6. For a driver with an AdBlue warning, that means planning around A roads and the gaps between towns rather than a motorway.
roadsText: The main roads listed for Lincoln are the A15, A46, A57, A607, A1192 and A1434. The nearest service area is Thorpe on the Hill Services on the A46, about 5.2 km away. Showground Services on the A15 is around 9 km out, and Cromwell Services on the A1 is about 17.4 km away.

name: Linlithgow
intro: On the historic route between Edinburgh and Falkirk, beside Linlithgow Loch, this former county town of West Lothian lies approximately 20 miles (32 km) west of Edinburgh in Scotland's Central Belt. It had a population of 12,517 in 2022. The town grew around Linlithgow Palace, later developed quickly with the Union Canal and the railway, and today its town centre economy is focused on hospitality, heritage and tourism. Linlithgow is covered by the EH49 postcode district. Neighbouring towns are close by: Bo'ness is 3.8 km away, Grangemouth 8.1 km, Broxburn 8.7 km and Bathgate 8.8 km, with Livingston, where the council is now based, at 10.4 km. For a diesel van or car with an AdBlue warning, it is worth knowing that the closest listed service area is 15.7 km away, further than any of those towns.
roadsText: Heart of Scotland Services on the M8 is the nearest service area listed for Linlithgow, 15.7 km away. Stirling Services on the M9 is 22.7 km off, and Dreghorn Services on the A720 is 24.6 km. That puts all three listed stops a fair distance from the town, so it pays to know which of them suits your route before an AdBlue warning turns into a problem.

name: Lisburn
intro: Thirteen kilometres southwest of Belfast city centre, Lisburn stands on the River Lagan, which forms the boundary between County Antrim and County Down. The 2021 census counted 51,447 people, making it the third-largest city in Northern Ireland, and since the 2016 local government reform it has been joined with most of Castlereagh in the Lisburn and Castlereagh council area. Postcode districts BT27, BT28 and BT17 cover the city. For drivers, the M1 is the key road on the local list, with Lisburn Services on it just 2.1 km away, and the A1, A3, A30, A49, A101, A512 and A519 are also recorded. Belfast is 10.8 km away and Castlereagh 11.2 km, while Craigavon lies 24.3 km off. With a motorway service area this close, Lisburn drivers have an easy first stop if an AdBlue warning appears.
roadsText: The M1, A1, A512, A3, A101, A30, A49 and A519 are the main roads recorded around Lisburn. Lisburn Services on the M1 is only 2.1 km away, which makes it the obvious stop. Further out are Temple Patrick Services Northbound on the M2 (19.1 km) and Cohannon Services on the M1 (40.3 km). OpenStreetMap lists a station at BT6 0LT (10.1 km) and one in Newtownabbey (16.8 km) as selling AdBlue at the pump; that list is not complete.

name: Liskeard
intro: Bodmin Moor lies to the north-west of Liskeard (Lyskerrys in Cornish), an ancient stannary and market town in south-east Cornwall. It is about 20 miles (32 km) west of Plymouth, 14 miles (23 km) west of the Devon border and 12 miles (20 km) east of Bodmin. The parish had 10,902 residents at the 2021 census, and the PL14 postcode district covers the town. Neighbouring towns are spread out: Saltash is 17.5 km away, Bodmin 18 km, and Tavistock and Plymouth both 24.7 km, with St Austell at 25.9 km. That spacing carries over to service areas. If a van or diesel car shows an AdBlue warning in or around Liskeard, the nearest listed service area is Saltash Services on the A388, 16.4 km away in a straight line, with Cornwall Services on the A30 at 25.3 km.
roadsText: Saltash Services on the A388 is the nearest service area to Liskeard, 16.4 km from the town in a straight line, and Cornwall Services on the A30 is 25.3 km away. Beyond those two the gap is large, with Roundswell Service Area on the A39 at 72.7 km. Road distances will be longer than these figures, so it pays to know which way to head before setting off.

name: Litherland
intro: Approximately 5 miles (8.0 km) north of Liverpool city centre, Litherland is a town in the Metropolitan Borough of Sefton, Merseyside. Waterloo borders it to the north, Seaforth to the west and Bootle to the south. Until 1974 it was within the historic county of Lancashire, and its former urban district took in Seaforth and Ford. Four postcode districts, L20, L21, L22 and L30, reach into the area, and the town has about 18,752 residents. Bootle is only around 2 km away and Crosby 2.4 km, with Maghull at 5.5 km and Wallasey and Kirkby both about 7.6 km. That leaves Litherland with close neighbours on three sides. For a driver with an AdBlue warning, the nearest motorway services are at Old Meadow on the M58, roughly 7.1 km away, with the M57 also within reach.
roadsText: Old Meadow Services on the M58 is the nearest service area to Litherland, about 7.1 km away, and Earlsfield Services on the M57 is around 12.3 km. Burtonwood Services on the M62 is further at roughly 24.4 km. On OpenStreetMap, a station named Old Meadow at the same 7.1 km is listed as selling AdBlue at the pump, as is an HGV-only refuelling site in Liverpool about 5 km away. Those records are not complete.
