name: Little Hulton
intro: Bordered by Farnworth to the north, Walkden to the east and Tyldesley to the south, Little Hulton is a suburb in the City of Salford. It lies 3.4 miles south of Bolton, 7 miles north-west of Salford and 9 miles north-west of Manchester, within the historic county of Lancashire, and had a population of 13,469 in 2014. The M38, M28, BL4 and M29 postcode districts cover the area. Walkden is only 1.9 km away, Farnworth 2.4 km, Kearsley 3.2 km and Worsley 3.6 km, with Atherton at 4.6 km. Four motorways are listed among the roads nearby: the M61, M60, M602 and M62, along with the A6 and A580. If an AdBlue warning appears, the service areas and stations below are the closest listed options.
roadsText: Little Hulton has the M61, M60, M602 and M62 listed nearby, plus the A6, A575, A577 and A580. Rivington Services on the M61 (13 km) and Birch Services on the M62 (13.1 km) are almost equally close, with Burtonwood Services on the M62 at 19.1 km. OpenStreetMap lists stations in Manchester (M25 3AJ, 8.6 km) and Warrington (WA3 6RW, 14.2 km), plus one at 18.1 km, as selling AdBlue at the pump. Expect gaps in that data.

name: Little Lever
intro: Two miles (3.2 km) southeast of Bolton and the same distance west of Radcliffe, Little Lever is a village in the Metropolitan Borough of Bolton, about 4 miles (6.4 km) southwest of Bury. It lies within the historic county of Lancashire. In the 19th century local people worked in cotton mills, paper mills, bleach works, terracotta works, a rope works and numerous collieries. The village has about 12,524 residents, and postcode districts BL3 and M26 cover the area. Kearsley is the nearest neighbour at about 2.4 km, with Farnworth at 2.8 km and Radcliffe at 3.2 km. Little Hulton, Bolton and Walkden are each about 5 km away. For a van or diesel car with an AdBlue warning, the closest motorway service area is Birch Services on the M62, about 9.2 km off.
roadsText: Birch Services on the M62 is the closest service area to Little Lever, about 9.2 km away. Rivington Services on the M61 is around 14 km off, and Blackburn with Darwen Services on the M65 about 18.1 km. OpenStreetMap has a station under Manchester, roughly 6.1 km away, listed as selling AdBlue at the pump, as well as a site at 15.7 km and one under Warrington at 19.2 km. Its records are incomplete.

name: Littleborough
intro: With Milnrow and the M62 motorway to the south and the rural uplands of Blackstone Edge to the east, Littleborough sits in the upper Roch Valley by the foothills of the South Pennines. The town is in the Metropolitan Borough of Rochdale, 3 miles (4.8 km) northeast of Rochdale and 13 miles (20.9 km) northeast of Manchester. In the 2001 census, Littleborough and its suburbs of Calderbrook, Shore and Smithy Bridge had 13,807 residents. In the Middle Ages it was a hamlet focused on the junction of two ancient routes over the Pennines. The OL15 postcode district covers the town. Shaw is about 7 km away and Todmorden 7.6 km, with Royton at 8.6 km and Bacup at 8.7 km. For a driver with an AdBlue warning, the M62 lies to the south, and Birch Services on that motorway is about 12 km off.
roadsText: The M62 runs to the south of Littleborough, and Birch Services on that motorway is the nearest service area, about 12 km away. Hollin Bank Service Station on the M65 is around 22.4 km off, and Hartshead Moor services on the M62 about 24.7 km. OpenStreetMap has a site roughly 14.2 km away and a station under Manchester at 17.1 km listed as selling AdBlue at the pump. Its data is incomplete.

name: Littlehampton
intro: With roughly 55,000 people in its suburban area, Littlehampton is a seaside resort, town and civil parish in the Arun District of West Sussex, on the eastern bank of the mouth of the River Arun. It is the westernmost settlement of the Brighton, Worthing and Littlehampton conurbation, and the town's conurbation also takes in Wick to the north-west, Lyminster to the north and Rustington to the east. Wick and Toddington, which has a large business park, became part of the town in 1901. The town is covered by the BN17 postcode district. Wick is 1.5 km from the centre and Rustington 3.9 km, with Worthing at 9.4 km and Bognor Regis at 11 km. The South Downs National Park begins 3 miles to the north, and roads link the town to Amberley and Arundel. For a driver with an AdBlue warning, the nearest listed service area is Fontwell Services on the A27, 9.5 km away in a straight line.
roadsText: Fontwell Services on the A27 is the nearest listed service area to Littlehampton, 9.5 km away in a straight line. The next two are much further: Buck Barn on the A24 at 24.1 km and Pyecombe Services on the A23 at 27.1 km. So the A27 site is the nearest listed option by some margin, and road distances will be longer than the straight-line figures.

name: Liverpool
intro: On the eastern side of the Mersey Estuary, close to the Irish Sea, Liverpool is a port city and metropolitan borough with an estimated 507,915 residents in 2025. It is within the larger Liverpool City Region, a combined authority area of over 1.5 million people, and its neighbouring towns are close: Huyton with Roby is 4.5 km away, Bootle 7.1 km, Kirkby 8.3 km, Litherland 8.7 km, Prescot 8.9 km and Wallasey 9.1 km. The postcode districts in the data include L6, L7, L12, L13, L14, L15, L16 and L18. Two motorways appear on the road list, the M62 and M57, with A-roads including the A5047, A5080, A57, A5058, A5049 and A562. For a van or diesel car with an AdBlue warning, the nearest service area in the data is on the M57, 6.6 km away. The city was moved from Lancashire to the new county of Merseyside in 1974.
roadsText: Liverpool's main roads include the M62 and M57, plus the A5047, A5080, A57, A5058, A5049 and A562. The nearest service areas are Earlsfield Services on the M57 at 6.6 km, Old Meadow Services on the M58 at 11.5 km and Chester Services on the M56 at 17.6 km. In OpenStreetMap, a station at Old Meadow (11.6 km) and one in Warrington's WA5 district (17.2 km) are listed as selling AdBlue at the pump; a closer site in Liverpool L5 is marked HGV-only. The data is incomplete.

name: Liversedge
intro: An industrial town in the Kirklees district of West Yorkshire, Liversedge lies between Cleckheaton and Heckmondwike and was historically part of the West Riding of Yorkshire and of the parish of Birstall. Spen Beck runs through it, and it forms part of the Heavy Woollen District. The Kirklees ward, now called Liversedge and Gomersal, had 19,420 people at the 2011 Census. Three postcode districts cover the town: WF15, WF16 and BD19. Neighbouring towns are very close: Heckmondwike is 2 km away, Cleckheaton 2.2 km, Mirfield 3.1 km, Batley 4.3 km and Dewsbury 5.1 km. For a van or diesel car with an AdBlue warning, the most useful fact is that the Hartshead Moor service area on the M62 is only 3 km from the centre in a straight line.
roadsText: Hartshead Moor on the M62 is the closest service area to Liversedge, 3 km from the centre in a straight line. On the M1, Woolley Edge Services is 13.9 km away and Skelton Lake Service Station 16.8 km. OpenStreetMap lists a station in Leeds (LS9 0AS), 16.9 km away, as selling AdBlue at the pump. That listing is incomplete, so stations nearer to WF15, WF16 or BD19 may also sell it.

name: Livingston
intro: The largest town in West Lothian, Livingston was designated in 1962 as Scotland's fourth post-war new town and lies some 24 km west of Edinburgh and 48 km east of Glasgow. It was developed along the River Almond around older villages such as Livingston Village and Bellsquarry. Residential areas include Craigshill, Howden, Ladywell, Knightsridge, Deans, Dedridge, Murieston, Almondvale, Eliburn, Kirkton and Adambrae, and the town has several large industrial estates, among them Houston and Brucefield. The M8 is on the local road list, along with the A71, A89, A705, A779, A899 and A7066. Postcode districts EH53 and EH54 cover the town. Broxburn (4.9 km) and Bathgate (7.1 km) are the nearest neighbours, with Linlithgow at 10.4 km.
roadsText: The M8, A705, A899, A71, A779, A89 and A7066 are the main roads recorded around Livingston. Heart of Scotland Services on the M8 is the nearest service area at 15.1 km, followed by Dreghorn Services on the A720 at 18.2 km and Musselburgh Services on the A1 at 29 km. Heart of Scotland Services sits on the M8, which is also on Livingston's own road list.

name: Llandudno
intro: As early as 1861 Llandudno was being called 'the Queen of the Welsh Watering Places', and it is still a major seaside resort. The town sits on the Creuddyn peninsula, which protrudes into the Irish Sea, in Conwy County Borough. Its community, which also includes Gogarth, Penrhyn Bay, Craigside, Glanwydden, Penrhynside and Bryn Pydew, had around 19,700 people at the 2021 census, and the LL30 postcode district covers the town. The name means Church of Saint Tudno. Historically part of Caernarfonshire, it was in the Aberconwy district within Gwynedd until 1996. Conwy and Colwyn Bay are the nearest towns, at 3.3 km and 6.3 km; after them, the next on the list, Rhyl, is 23.4 km away. If an AdBlue warning comes on, the nearest listed service area is Orme View Services on the A55, 6.5 km away in a straight line.
roadsText: Orme View Services on the A55 is the closest service area to Llandudno, 6.5 km away in a straight line. Kinmel Park Services, also on the A55, is 21.3 km away and Bangor Services on the A5 22.6 km. OpenStreetMap lists an Esso station at Penmaenmawr (LL34 6UN), 6.4 km away, as selling AdBlue at the pump. That data is incomplete, so treat it as one known option rather than the only one.

name: Llanelli
intro: St Elli's Parish is the meaning of the Welsh name Llanelli, and the market town on the estuary of the River Loughor is the largest in Carmarthenshire, 18 km north-west of Swansea and 19 km south-east of Carmarthen. The built-up area had 42,155 people at the 2021 census, while the community itself had 25,366. It has been under Carmarthenshire County Council since 1996, having previously had Llanelli Borough Council as its local authority while the county of Dyfed existed. The SA15 postcode district covers the town. Gorseinon is the nearest neighbour at 7.2 km, with Swansea at 15.4 km and Carmarthen at 22.3 km, and Neath at 22.9 km. All the main roads listed near the town are A roads, so for a van or diesel car the motorway is a short drive away rather than on the doorstep, with the nearest M4 service area 8.8 km out.
roadsText: The main roads around Llanelli are the A4138, A484, A4214, A476 and A4240, with no motorway among them. The nearest service areas are both on the M4: Pont Abraham at 8.8 km and Swansea West at 10.2 km. Sarn Park, also on the M4, is much further at 42.4 km.

name: Locks Heath
intro: A residential suburb of Fareham in the south of Hampshire, Locks Heath is ringed by villages: Sarisbury to the west, Swanwick, Park Gate and Whiteley to the north, Warsash to the south-west and Titchfield to the south-east. At its heart is a shopping village with a community centre. The 2021 population was 35,757, and the area spans the SO31 and PO15 postcode districts. Roads listed nearby include the M27 and A27, along with the A3051, A3025, A3024 and A334. Fareham is 5.6km away, Lee-on-the-Solent 6.1km and Hedge End 6.8km, with Southampton at 10.4km. Most driving connects suburban streets to these neighbouring towns and the motorway. The nearest service areas are 16.2km or more away, which is worth knowing if a warning light appears.
roadsText: Listed main roads around Locks Heath are the M27, A27, A3051, A3025, A3024 and A334. Service areas are not especially close: Rownhams Services on the M27 is 16.2km away, Farlington Services on the A27 is 16.7km and West Wellow Services on the A36 is 21km. A driver with an AdBlue warning should not count on a quick roadside stop from here.

name: Long Eaton
intro: Just north of the River Trent, Long Eaton is a town in Derbyshire's Erewash district, about 6 miles (9.7 km) south-west of Nottingham and 9 miles (14 km) south-east of Derby. The 2011 census recorded 37,760 people, and the town has been part of Erewash borough since 1974, when Long Eaton Urban District was disbanded. Its postcode district is NG10. The M1, A50 and A52 are all among the main roads, together with the A453, A6002, A6005 and A6007. Stapleford is about 4.6 km away, Beeston 5 km and Clifton 7.1 km, with Ilkeston at 8.2 km. Three service areas, on the A50 and the M1, are all within about 8 km, so a driver with an AdBlue warning near Long Eaton has several places to pull in without a long detour.
roadsText: The main roads listed for Long Eaton are the M1, A50, A52, A453, A6002, A6005 and A6007. Welcome Break Derby South Services on the A50 is the nearest service area, about 6 km away. Trowell Services on the M1 is around 7.9 km away, and Moto Donington Park Services, also on the M1, about 8 km.

name: Longbenton
intro: Longbenton is a district of North Tyneside, in Tyne and Wear, rather than a stand-alone town. Much of it is an extensive estate first built as municipal housing by Newcastle City Council in the 1930s and extended in the 1950s. Places around it include Killingworth, Forest Hall, Four Lane Ends, West Moor, Heaton and South Gosforth. Killingworth is just 1.9 km away, Wallsend 4.2 km and Newcastle upon Tyne 5.2 km, with Hebburn, Tynemouth and Whitley Bay all within about 7 km. Postcode districts NE12, NE7 and NE27 cover the area. The road list is strong for a district of this kind: the A1, A19 and A167(M) all appear, alongside the A189, A1058, A167, A188 and A191. That gives a driver here a wide choice of roads in and out.
roadsText: The main roads around Longbenton include the A167(M), A1 and A19, along with the A189, A1058, A167, A188 and A191. Seaton Burn Services on the A19 is 6.2 km away, Washington Services on the A1(M) 14.8 km and Easington Services on the A19 27.9 km. In OpenStreetMap, which is not a complete record, a station in Newcastle upon Tyne just 2.5 km away is listed as selling AdBlue at the pump.

name: Longfield, New Ash Green and Hartley
intro: This area brings together three Kent settlements, Longfield, New Ash Green and Hartley, with a combined population of 16,077 and a single postcode district, DA3. Longfield itself is a village in the Borough of Dartford, 6 miles south-east of Dartford and the same distance south-west of Gravesend. For drivers, the useful point is that Tollgate Services on the A2 is only 4.5 km away in a straight line, which makes it the nearest listed service area if an AdBlue warning comes on. Thurrock Services on the M25 is the next closest at 11.9 km. Northfleet (5.8 km), Gravesend (6.5 km) and Swanscombe (6.6 km) are the nearest towns, with Dartford, Tilbury and Swanley between 8.4 km and 10.1 km away. OpenStreetMap also lists a station in Strood, 11.6 km off, as selling AdBlue at the pump.
roadsText: Tollgate Services on the A2 is the nearest service area to Longfield, New Ash Green and Hartley, 4.5 km away in a straight line. Thurrock Services on the M25 is 11.9 km off and Orsett Cock Services on the A13 is 14.8 km. A station at Temple Farm, Strood (ME2 2NY), 11.6 km away, is listed in OpenStreetMap as selling AdBlue at the pump. That listing is not complete, so other stations nearby may also sell it.

name: Longton
intro: About 4 miles south-west of Preston, Longton is a village and civil parish in the west of South Ribble, Lancashire. The parish also takes in the village of New Longton, and its population has risen from 5,500 in 2001 to 7,652 in 2011 and 7,752 at the 2021 Census. The area is covered by the PR4 postcode district. Several neighbouring towns are close: Penwortham is about 4.9 km away in a straight line, Leyland 6.2 km, Bamber Bridge 7.9 km and Preston 8.5 km, with Fulwood and Euxton both just over 9 km off. When a van or diesel car shows an AdBlue warning around Longton, the nearest motorway service area is on the M6 at about 11.3 km, and two more lie on the M61 and M65 at about 19 km and 20.4 km.
roadsText: In a straight line, Charnock Richard Services on the M6 is the nearest service area to Longton at about 11.3 km. Rivington Services on the M61 is about 19 km away and Blackburn with Darwen Services on the M65 about 20.4 km. All three are motorway sites, and the drive from the PR4 district to any of them will be longer than the straight-line distance.

name: Loughborough
intro: Second only to Leicester in size within the county, Loughborough is a market town and the administrative centre of Charnwood borough. Its built-up area had 64,884 residents at the 2021 census. The town lies close to the Nottinghamshire border and near Leicester, Nottingham and Derby, so three cities are within reach. Main roads include the M1, A6, A60, A512, A6004 and A6006, and the postcode districts are LE11 and LE12. Shepshed is only about 4.6 km away and Mountsorrel 7.4 km, with Whitwick at 9.4 km, Coalville at 10.7 km and Birstall at 11.7 km, which means several neighbouring towns are a short drive apart. Three service areas, on the M1, A6 and A46, are all between about 8 km and 11 km from the town, so there is more than one option if an AdBlue warning appears.
roadsText: Loughborough's main roads include the M1, A6, A60, A512, A6004 and A6006. Moto Donington Park Services on the M1 is the nearest service area, about 8.2 km away. ExtraMSA Leicester Services on the A6 is around 10.8 km away, and Six Hills Services Northbound on the A46 is about 11.2 km.

name: Loughton
intro: Inside the M25 but just outside the boundary of Greater London, Loughton is a town and civil parish in Epping Forest District, 13 miles (21 km) north-east of Charing Cross. The parish includes part of the ancient woodland of Epping Forest and has two stations on the Central line, Loughton and Debden. Its population was 33,346 at the 2021 census. Neighbouring parishes are Waltham Abbey, Theydon Bois, Chigwell and Buckhurst Hill, and the parish also borders the London Borough of Waltham Forest near Chingford. Two motorways, the M11 and M25, are listed among the main roads, together with the A1168, A121, A113, A1112, A104 and A1069. Buckhurst Hill is 3.4 km away, Chigwell 4 km and Epping 5.3 km, with Waltham Abbey 6.1 km off. Postcode districts are IG9 and IG10.
roadsText: The M11 and M25 are listed, together with the A1168, A121, A113, A1112, A104 and A1069. The listed service areas are all over 20 km away: South Mimms Services on the A1(M) at 20.9 km, Thurrock Services on the M25 at 22.4 km and London Gateway Services on the M1 at 23.6 km. A station 11.9 km away is listed on OpenStreetMap as selling AdBlue at the pump; that data is incomplete, so there may be others nearer.

name: Louth
intro: Serving a large rural area of eastern Lincolnshire, Louth is a market town in the East Lindsey district with a population of 17,415 and the LN11 postcode district. It still has Lincolnshire's last remaining cattle market. For a driver, the main fact here is distance. The nearest listed places are Humberston and New Waltham, about 18.2 km away, Cleethorpes at 20.4 km and Grimsby at 22.7 km, while Skegness is 32.7 km, Lincoln 41.9 km and Boston around 43.8 km. The nearest service areas are further still, at more than 34 km, so a station close to town matters: one in Louth, about 2 km away, is listed in OpenStreetMap as selling AdBlue at the pump, though that data is incomplete.
roadsText: The nearest service areas to Louth are a long way off: Ulceby Truckstop on the A160 at about 34.1 km, Showground Services on the A15 at around 37.2 km, and Thorpe on the Hill Services on the A46 at 46.8 km. A BP station in Louth (LN11 0WA), about 2 km away, is listed in OpenStreetMap as selling AdBlue at the pump; the data is incomplete.

name: Lowestoft
intro: As the most easterly settlement in the UK, Lowestoft is a coastal town and civil parish in East Suffolk and the main town in its district. It is 38 miles (61 km) north-east of Ipswich and 22 miles (35 km) south-east of Norwich. The town grew with the fishing industry and as a seaside resort with wide sandy beaches, and as fishing declined, North Sea oil and gas work took over from the 1960s. The built-up area had 71,327 people in 2021. Being on the coast shapes the driving: Gorleston-on-Sea is 10.8 km away, Bradwell 11.9 km and Great Yarmouth 14.2 km, but Norwich is 35.2 km off and the next towns are further still. The A12, A47 and A146 are the main roads, with the A1117, A1144 and A1145 also listed. Postcode districts are NR32 and NR33.
roadsText: The A12, A47 and A146 are the main routes, along with the A1117, A1144 and A1145. Service areas are a long way from Lowestoft. The closest listed is Thickthorn Services on the A11, 36.8 km away, followed by Beacon Hill Services on the A140 at 56.6 km and a service area on the A14 at 61.7 km. With an AdBlue warning showing, that distance is worth bearing in mind before setting off.

name: Ludlow
intro: A medieval walled town, founded in the late 11th century, forms the oldest part of Ludlow, a market town and civil parish in south Shropshire. That core is centred on a small hill on the eastern bank of a bend in the River Teme, with streets sloping down to the rivers Corve and Teme to the north and south. The town has nearly 500 listed buildings and lies beneath Mortimer Forest and the Clee Hills. Ludlow is 28 miles (45 km) south of Shrewsbury and 23 miles (37 km) north of Hereford, on the A49, which passes around the town rather than through it. Its postcode district is SY8. A driver with an AdBlue warning should know that the nearest listed service area is 40.1 km away in a straight line. Leominster, 16.2 km off, is the closest town.
roadsText: The A49 runs past Ludlow, but service areas are a long way from the town. The nearest are Telford Services on the M54, 40.1 km away in a straight line, Nesscliffe Services on the A5 at 46.9 km and Frankley Services on the M5 at 47.5 km. Road distances will be longer, so a driver in SY8 with an AdBlue warning should allow for a long trip to reach any of them.

name: Luton
intro: Founded in the sixth century as a Saxon settlement on the River Lea, Luton is now a Bedfordshire town and borough about 32 miles (50 km) north-west of London, with 225,262 residents at the 2021 census. It became a centre of the British motor industry from 1905, and commercial vehicle manufacturing there came to an end in 2025. London Luton Airport opened in 1938, and the town also has three railway stations. Postcode districts are LU1, LU2, LU3, LU4 and LU5. The M1 is among the main roads, together with the A5, A6, A505 and A1081. Houghton Regis is about 6.9 km away and Dunstable 7.4 km, with Harpenden at 10.3 km and Hitchin at 12.4 km. Toddington Services on the M1, around 7.9 km out, is the nearest service area, and the next ones are more than 18 km away.
roadsText: Main roads around Luton include the M1, A5, A6, A505, A1081, A5065, A5228 and A5505. Toddington Services on the M1 is the nearest service area, about 7.9 km away. Bourne End Services on the A41 is around 18.5 km out, and Crawley Crossing Truck Stop on the M1 about 18.9 km.

name: Lutterworth
intro: In southern Leicestershire, close to the borders with Warwickshire and Northamptonshire, Lutterworth is a historic market town in the Harborough district with 10,833 residents at the 2021 census. It lies 6.5 miles north of Rugby and 12 miles south of Leicester, and its postcode district is LE17. Rugby is the nearest town at 9.3 km, while Hinckley, Blaby and Whetstone, and Earl Shilton are all between 12 and 14 km away. Enderby and Narborough is 14.2 km off. For a van or diesel car with an AdBlue warning, Lutterworth is well placed for motorway services: Rugby Services on the M6 is 5.6 km away, and two truck stops, on the A5 and the A14, are within 16 km.
roadsText: Rugby Services on the M6 is the nearest service area to Lutterworth, 5.6 km away. Rugby Truck Stop on the A5 is 9.4 km off and Welford Truck Stop on the A14 is 15.7 km away. A station 13.7 km away is listed on OpenStreetMap as selling AdBlue at the pump; because OpenStreetMap's records are incomplete, other forecourts may sell it as well.

name: Lymington
intro: A port town on the west bank of the Lymington River, on the Solent, Lymington faces Yarmouth on the Isle of Wight, and a car ferry service runs between the two. It lies in the New Forest district of Hampshire, within the civil parish of Lymington and Pennington, and had 14,858 residents in 2021. Its postcode district is SO41. The town has a large tourist industry based on its harbour and nearness to the New Forest, and it is a major yachting centre with three marinas. For a driver with an AdBlue warning, the main point is distance. The nearest listed service areas, Picket Post Services and Rufus Stone, are both on the A31, at 16.2 km and 16.9 km in a straight line. New Milton is the closest town at 7.3 km, with Christchurch at 13.6 km and Hythe and Dibden Purlieu at 15.3 km.
roadsText: The two nearest service areas to Lymington are both on the A31: Picket Post Services at 16.2 km and Rufus Stone at 16.9 km, measured in a straight line. West Wellow Services on the A36 is 21.7 km away. Road distances will be longer than these figures, which matters for a driver already seeing an AdBlue warning in a town this far from any listed services.

name: Lymm
intro: Just over a mile south of the Manchester Ship Canal and the River Mersey, Lymm is a village and civil parish in Cheshire, now in the Borough of Warrington. It takes in several hamlets, including Booths Hill, Broomedge, Heatley, Oughtrington, Rush Green and Statham, so the parish spreads well beyond the village centre. At the 2021 census the parish had 12,660 residents and the built-up area 11,545. Warburton, Thelwall and High Legh are its neighbouring villages. Warrington is the nearest town, 6 miles (9.7 km) to the west, with Altrincham 7 miles (11 km) due east and Knutsford 9 miles (14 km) south east. The WA13 postcode district covers Lymm. For a van or diesel car with an AdBlue warning, Lymm Services on the M6 is only about 2.6 km away.
roadsText: Lymm Services on the M6 is the nearest service area, about 2.6 km from the village. Tabley Hill Service Station, also on the M6, is around 8.7 km off, and Knutsford Services on the M6 about 10.1 km. OpenStreetMap has two stations under Warrington, at about 5.5 km and 12.4 km, listed as selling AdBlue at the pump. OpenStreetMap's records are incomplete, so others may exist.

name: Lytham St Anne's
intro: On the Fylde coast, directly south of Blackpool and facing the Ribble Estuary, Lytham St Annes is a seaside town in the Borough of Fylde, Lancashire. Its built-up area had 42,695 residents at the 2021 census. The town is made up of four areas: Lytham, the oldest settlement, plus Ansdell, Fairhaven and St Annes-on-the-Sea, which began as a new resort in the 1870s. They were reunited under the compound name in 1922, and the whole area now sits in the FY8 postcode district. Blackpool is only 5.3 km away, with Poulton-le-Fylde at 11.1 km and Southport at 12.8 km. The M55 is the motorway listed for the area. If an AdBlue warning comes on, bear in mind that the nearest service areas are all more than 24 km away, so it pays to plan the stop rather than hope one turns up.
roadsText: Roads listed for the Lytham St Annes area are the M55, A583, A5073, A584 and A5230. The three nearest service areas are all some way off: Charnock Richard Services on the M6 at 24.2 km, Old Meadow Services on the M58 at 27 km and Lancaster Services on the M6 at 28.2 km. Blackpool, 5.3 km away, is the closest neighbouring town.

name: Macclesfield
intro: On the River Bollin, at the edge of the Cheshire Plain, Macclesfield has Macclesfield Forest to its east and lies 16 miles south of Manchester and 38 miles east of Chester. It is a market town and civil parish in Cheshire East, and the medieval town grew up on a hilltop around what is now St Michael's Church. From the mid-18th century it became a major silk-manufacturing centre. The road list is short and has no motorway: the A537, A523, A536 and A538. Postcode districts SK10 and SK11 cover the town. Wilmslow and Poynton are both 9.7 km away, Bramhall 11.7 km and Congleton 11.8 km, with Hazel Grove and Cheadle Hulme at 12.8 km. The nearest service areas in the data are all on the M6, between 18.4 and 19.7 km away.
roadsText: Macclesfield's main roads are the A537, A523, A536 and A538. The nearest service areas are all on the M6: Knutsford Services at 18.4 km, Sandbach Services at 19.2 km and Tabley Hill at 19.7 km. With no motorway on the town's own road list, reaching any of them from SK10 or SK11 means an A-road run first, so a low AdBlue reading is worth acting on early.

name: Maesteg
intro: Since the coal industry declined, with the last pit closing in 1985, the Llynfi Valley has become a residential area for people travelling to work in Port Talbot, Bridgend and Cardiff. Maesteg sits at its northernmost end, in Bridgend County Borough and close to the border with Neath Port Talbot. The town had 20,612 residents in 2011, and the CF34 postcode district covers it. It officially became a town in 1826 and grew with the opening of ironworks in the 1820s and 1830s; the name translates as 'fair field'. For drivers making those journeys, the nearest listed service area is Welcome Break Sarn Park Services on the M4, 9.9 km away in a straight line. Sarn is 8.6 km from the town, Pyle 9.2 km, Port Talbot 9.6 km and Bridgend 12.8 km.
roadsText: Welcome Break Sarn Park Services on the M4 is the closest service area to Maesteg, 9.9 km away in a straight line. The other two nearest sites are also on the M4 but much further: Moto Swansea West Services at 24.8 km and Moto Cardiff West Services at 26.5 km. Distances by road will be longer than these figures.

name: Maghull
intro: North of Liverpool and west of Kirkby, Maghull is a town and civil parish in Sefton, Merseyside, covered by the L31 postcode district. The 2011 Census put its population at 20,444. Housing here is almost entirely a 20th-century settlement of semi-detached and detached homes, though remains of the original town do exist. Ashworth Hospital is also located in the town. Kirkby is about 5.2 km away and Litherland 5.5 km, while Crosby, Ormskirk and Bootle lie between 6.1 km and 7.1 km off, and Formby is around 9.6 km. For anyone dealing with an AdBlue warning, the most useful local detail is that Old Meadow Services on the M58 is only about 2 km from Maghull, so a motorway service area is close at hand.
roadsText: Old Meadow Services on the M58 is the closest service area, about 2 km away. Earlsfield Services on the M57 is around 11.9 km off, and Charnock Richard Services on the M6 about 21.1 km. A station named Old Meadow, also about 2 km away, is listed as selling AdBlue at the pump on OpenStreetMap, as is an HGV-only refuelling site in Liverpool around 9.8 km away. OpenStreetMap's records are incomplete, so other stations may also sell it.

name: Maidenhead
intro: On the south-western bank of the River Thames, which here forms the border with Buckinghamshire, Maidenhead is a market town in the Royal Borough of Windsor and Maidenhead. Its built-up area had a population of 67,375 at the 2021 Census, and it lies 27 miles (43 km) west of Charing Cross and 13 miles (21 km) east-north-east of Reading. Its postcode district is SL6. Three motorways appear in its road list, the M4, A404(M) and A308(M), alongside the A404, A308, A4, A4094 and A330, so motorway links are part of the local picture. Marlow is 6.9 km away, Windsor 7.6 km and Slough 9.4 km. If a van or diesel car flags an AdBlue warning here, the nearest listed service area is 10.5 km away on the M40.
roadsText: Listed main roads for Maidenhead are the M4, A404(M), A308(M), A404, A308, A4, A4094 and A330. The nearest listed service area is Beaconsfield Services on the M40, 10.5 km away. The two M4 options are much further and almost equal: Heston Services at 23.5 km and Reading Services at 23.7 km. Neither M4 stop is close to town.

name: Maidstone
intro: Kent's county town and its largest town, Maidstone lies 32 miles (51 km) east-south-east of London, with the River Medway running through its centre and linking it to Rochester and the Thames Estuary. The town had an approximate population of 100,000 in 2019, and since World War II its economy has shifted from heavy industry towards light industry and services. Postcode districts include ME14, ME15, ME16 and ME20. The M20 is the motorway listed for the area, along with the A229, A249, A20, A26 and A274. Larkfield is 6.1 km away and Snodland 8.6 km, with Chatham at 10.2 km and Gillingham at 11.2 km. If an AdBlue warning comes on in or around Maidstone, the nearest listed service area is 6.5 km away on the M20, and a second is 9.9 km away on the M2.
roadsText: The M20 heads the list of main roads around Maidstone, which also includes the A229, A249, A20, A26 and A274. Maidstone Services on the M20 is the nearest listed service area at 6.5 km, followed by Medway Services on the M2 at 9.9 km and Tollgate Services on the A2 at 19.8 km. In OpenStreetMap, a station in Strood (ME2 2NY), 13.2 km away, and another about 19.1 km away are listed as selling AdBlue at the pump. That data is incomplete.

name: Maldon
intro: Seat of the Maldon District, this Essex town on the Blackwater Estuary is the starting point of the Chelmer and Blackwater Navigation. Its built-up area stretches north to include Heybridge, giving a population of 23,380 at the 2021 census. The CM9 postcode district covers the town. For a driver whose van or diesel car flags an AdBlue fault, the nearest listed service area is Boreham Services on the A131, 12.2 km away in a straight line, and the next is more than twice that distance. Witham is the closest neighbouring town at 8.7 km, followed by South Woodham Ferrers at 11.6 km and Chelmsford at 14.5 km. Hockley and Hawkwell, Rochford and Rayleigh lie between 14.6 km and 17.1 km away.
roadsText: Boreham Services on the A131 is the closest service area to Maldon, 12.2 km from the centre in a straight line. Ardleigh South Services on the A120 is 26.9 km away and Orsett Cock Services on the A13 is 32.1 km. OpenStreetMap lists lorry pumps at a site in Chelmsford (CM2 5PY), 12.2 km away, as selling AdBlue at the pump, but they are mapped as HGV-only, so they may not suit a van or car. The map data is incomplete, so other forecourts may sell AdBlue too.

name: Maltby
intro: The M18 motorway separates Maltby, and neighbouring Hellaby with which it forms a continuous urban area, from the rest of Rotherham. The town is 6 miles (10 km) east of Rotherham and 10 miles (16 km) north-east of Sheffield, in the Metropolitan Borough of Rotherham, and was historically in the West Riding. It had 16,688 residents at the 2011 census and uses the S66 postcode district. Wickersley and Bramley is about 5.9 km away, Dinnington 6 km, Warmsworth 6.3 km and Conisbrough 7.1 km, with New Rossington and Rossington around 9 km. For a driver whose van or car shows an AdBlue warning, the nearest listed service area is Blyth Services on the A1(M), roughly 9.5 km away in a straight line, with Rotherham Services on the M1 a little further at 11.1 km.
roadsText: The M18 runs between Maltby and the rest of Rotherham. In a straight line, the closest service areas are Blyth Services on the A1(M) at about 9.5 km, Rotherham Services on the M1 at 11.1 km and Woodall Services on the M1 at 13.5 km. OpenStreetMap lists a station in Doncaster (DN4 0TP), roughly 8.6 km away, as selling AdBlue at the pump, though its AdBlue coverage is incomplete.

name: Manchester
intro: At the centre of Greater Manchester, the city is bordered by the Cheshire Plain to the south, the Pennines to the north and east and the city of Salford to the west. It had over 589,000 residents in 2024, and with Salford and the surrounding towns it forms the Greater Manchester Built-up Area, home to 2.87 million people. Several neighbouring places are within a few kilometres: Droylsden (4.1 km), Failsworth (4.8 km), Reddish (5.1 km) and Salford (5.2 km), with Audenshaw at 5.4 km and Denton at 6.7 km. Postcode districts in the data are M1, M2, M3, M4, M11, M12, M13 and M15. Half the road list is motorway-standard, taking in the M60, M602 and M67 and the A57(M), together with the A635, A665, A57 and A6. The city grew from a settlement near the confluence of the rivers Medlock and Irwell.
roadsText: Manchester's listed roads are the M602, M60, M67 and A57(M), plus the A635, A665, A57 and A6. The nearest service area is Birch Services on the M62, 10.4 km away, while Tabley Hill (22.8 km) and Knutsford (23 km) are both on the M6. A station about 6.6 km away and another in the city's M25 postcode district at 8.6 km are listed as selling AdBlue at the pump in OpenStreetMap. Its records are incomplete.

name: Mansfield
intro: In the Maun Valley, 12 miles (19 km) north of Nottingham, Mansfield is a market town and the administrative centre of Mansfield District. It is the second largest settlement in Nottinghamshire after Nottingham, and the district had 110,500 residents at the 2021 census. Historically it was the leading town of Sherwood Forest. Postcode districts covering the town are NG18 and NG19. Several towns lie close by: Mansfield Woodhouse is about 3.1 km away, Forest Town 3.5 km, Sutton in Ashfield 4.2 km and Kirkby-in-Ashfield 5.8 km. The main roads here are A roads, among them the A38, A60, A611, A617 and A6009, along with the A6075, A6117 and A6191. The M1 is not among them, but Tibshelf Services on the M1, about 8.9 km away, is the nearest service area to the town.
roadsText: Mansfield's main roads are the A38, A60, A611, A617, A6009, A6075, A6117 and A6191. The nearest service area is Tibshelf Services on the M1, about 8.9 km away; Welcome Break Woodall Services and Trowell Services, both on the M1, are each just over 20 km out. A Tesco station about 3 km away is listed in OpenStreetMap as selling AdBlue at the pump, though that data is incomplete.

name: Mansfield Woodhouse
intro: A wide, low valley between the Rivers Maun and Meden is the setting for Mansfield Woodhouse, which lies about a mile north of Mansfield on the A60. It was once separate, but continuous development has made it part of the Mansfield Urban Area, and since 1974 it has been within the Mansfield district of Nottinghamshire. The town has a stone-built centre and is covered by the NG19 postcode district. Forest Town is 2.9 km away, Mansfield 3.1 km and Shirebrook 4.2 km, with Sutton in Ashfield 6.3 km off. For a van or diesel car driver with an AdBlue warning, the useful point is that a station listed as selling AdBlue at the pump is 4.5 km away, while the nearest motorway services are 10 km off on the M1.
roadsText: The A60 links Mansfield Woodhouse with Mansfield, about a mile to the south. The nearest service areas are Tibshelf Services on the M1 at 10 km, Welcome Break Woodall Services, also on the M1, at 17.5 km, and Markham Moor Services on the A1 at 20.2 km. A station 4.5 km away is listed on OpenStreetMap as selling AdBlue at the pump; the map data is incomplete, so other stations may also sell it.

name: March
intro: Once an island in the marshes of the Great Level, March is now a Fenland market town in the Isle of Ely area of Cambridgeshire and the administrative centre of Fenland District Council. It grew as a railway centre and was the county town of the Isle of Ely, a separate administrative county from 1889 to 1965. The town has a population of 21,345, sits on the old course of the River Nene and is covered by the PE15 postcode district. Drivers here should note how far the service areas are: the three nearest listed are all between 27.7 km and 28.3 km away in a straight line, two of them on the A1(M). Closer to home, Chatteris is 11.3 km away, Wisbech 13.5 km and Whittlesey 14 km, while Downham Market, Ely and Peterborough are each more than 20 km off.
roadsText: Service areas are some distance from March. Peterborough Services on the A1(M) is 27.7 km away in a straight line, the Sawtry service area, also on the A1(M), is 28 km, and Lincs Gateway Services on the A16 is 28.3 km. Road distances will be longer, so a driver in PE15 with an AdBlue warning should not count on a services stop being close by.

name: Margate
intro: Along Kent's north coast in the Thanet District, Margate takes in Cliftonville, Garlinge, Palm Bay and Westbrook, and lies 16 miles (26 kilometres) north-east of Canterbury. It has been a maritime port since the Middle Ages and became a popular place for holidaymakers in the 18th century; in 2011 the population was 61,223. Postcode districts are CT8, CT9, CT10 and CT12. All the listed roads are A roads, including the A28, A299 and A256. Broadstairs is 3.6 km away and Ramsgate 4.6 km, but beyond those the next towns are much further, with Herne Bay at 15.9 km and Canterbury at 23.1 km. A van or diesel car with an AdBlue warning in Margate has one listed service area close by, at 5.3 km, while the others are a long way off.
roadsText: Margate's road list is made up of the A28, A256, A299, A254 and A255. Minster Services on the A299 is the nearest listed service area, 5.3 km away. The next two are much further: Whitfield Services on the A2 at 25.8 km and Folkestone Services on the M20 at 38.8 km. With such a gap after Minster, it is the stop to know about for drivers in and around Thanet.

name: Market Drayton
intro: Market Drayton is a market town and civil parish on the banks of the River Tern in Shropshire, close to the Cheshire and Staffordshire borders. It lies between Whitchurch, Wem, Nantwich, Newcastle-under-Lyme, Newport and the city of Stoke on Trent, and sits on the Shropshire Union Canal. The A53 road skirts the town rather than running through it. The postcode district is TF9. Other towns are some distance off: Newport is 17.1 km away, Nantwich 17.8 km, Newcastle-under-Lyme 20.6 km and Crewe 21 km. For an AdBlue warning, the closest listed service area is on the A41, 4.2 km away in a straight line, while the M6 services are further away at 16.4 km and 19.5 km.
roadsText: Adastra Services on the A41 is the nearest service area to Market Drayton, 4.2 km away in a straight line, and the A53 runs round the town. Further out, Keele Services on the M6 is 16.4 km off and Swift Services, also on the M6, is 19.5 km. A station in Newcastle-under-Lyme (ST5 4DH), at the same 19.5 km, is listed in OpenStreetMap as selling AdBlue at the pump. That data is incomplete.

name: Market Harborough
intro: Close to the Northamptonshire border, Market Harborough is the administrative headquarters of the Harborough district of Leicestershire and had 24,779 residents at the 2021 census. The town was at a crossroads for both road and rail, but the A6 now bypasses it to the east and the A14 to the south. The LE16 postcode district covers the town. Desborough is the closest neighbouring town at 7.9 km, with Corby 15.9 km away, Kettering 16.2 km and Oadby 17 km. The nearest roadside stops are both on the A14, more than 10 km from the town, so a van or diesel car that shows an AdBlue warning may have some way to go before it can pull in. It is worth knowing where those stops are before setting out on the A6 or the A14.
roadsText: Main roads around Market Harborough include the A6, A4304, A508 and A427, with the A14 passing to the south of the town. The closest roadside stops are Rothwell Truck Stop on the A14, 10.5 km away, and Welford Truck Stop, also on the A14, at 11.4 km. Further out, Rugby Truck Stop on the A5 is 20.8 km from Market Harborough.

name: Marlow
intro: Set on the River Thames in Buckinghamshire, Marlow is a town and civil parish 4 miles (6 km) south-west of High Wycombe, 5 miles (8 km) north-west of Maidenhead and 33 miles (53 km) west of central London. It has a population of 14,641, and its postcode district is SL7. The closest neighbouring places are Flackwell Heath and Wooburn Green at 5.8 km, High Wycombe at 6.6 km and Maidenhead at 6.9 km, with Beaconsfield, Hazlemere and Henley-on-Thames between 9.4 km and 10.4 km away. A driver with an AdBlue warning should know that only one listed service area is reasonably near. Beaconsfield Services on the M40 is 10.2 km away in a straight line, and the next two, on the M4 and the A418, are both more than 24 km off. Several neighbouring towns are therefore closer than any services.
roadsText: Marlow's closest listed service area is Beaconsfield Services on the M40, 10.2 km away in a straight line. After that the gap is large: Reading Services on the M4 is 24.5 km off and Thame Services on the A418 is 24.8 km. Road distances will be longer than these straight-line figures, so it is worth heading for the M40 site early if an AdBlue warning appears.

name: Marple
intro: Nine miles (14 km) south-east of Manchester and 4 miles (6 km) south-east of Stockport, Marple sits on the River Goyt in the Metropolitan Borough of Stockport, also 9 miles (14 km) north of Macclesfield. It lies within the historic county boundaries of Cheshire, though its district Marple Bridge was historically partly in Derbyshire, and it became part of Greater Manchester in 1974. The built-up area had 12,970 residents at the 2021 census. The town lies along the Peak Forest Canal, and two railway stations, Marple and Rose Hill Marple, serve it. The SK6 postcode district covers the area. Romiley is about 2.4 km away, Hazel Grove 3.8 km and Bredbury and Woodley 4.3 km. For a driver with an AdBlue warning, the nearest motorway services are a long way off, at more than 21 km.
roadsText: Birch Services on the M62 is the nearest service area to Marple, about 21.9 km away. Knutsford Services and Tabley Hill Service Station, both on the M6, are around 24.4 km and 24.9 km off. OpenStreetMap has a site roughly 14.6 km away listed as selling AdBlue at the pump. Its records are incomplete, so somewhere nearer may also stock it.

name: Matlock
intro: Derbyshire's county town and the headquarters of Derbyshire County Council, Matlock sits in the south-eastern part of the Peak District, with the National Park directly to the west. The spa resort of Matlock Bath lies immediately to the south, and Cromford further south again. The civil parish had 10,000 residents in 2021, and the postcode district is DE4. Matlock is 9 miles south-west of Chesterfield, with Derby 19 miles away, Sheffield 20 miles and Nottingham 29 miles. Of the towns around it, Chesterfield is 13.2 km away, Somercotes and Swanwick 13.7 km and Belper 13.9 km. For a van or diesel car with an AdBlue warning, the nearest motorway services are 14.6 km away on the M1, so it is worth planning ahead rather than setting off on a long run with the warning lit.
roadsText: Tibshelf Services on the M1 is the nearest service area to Matlock, at 14.6 km. Welcome Break Woodall Services, also on the M1, is 26.2 km away and Sheffield Service Area on the A6102 is 27.3 km away. With every listed service area more than 14 km from the town, it is worth knowing which way you will head before a warning becomes urgent.

name: Mayfield
intro: Just south of Dalkeith, between the A68 and the A7 south, Mayfield is a Midlothian community near Edinburgh with an estimated 13,690 residents in 2020. It was built in the 1950s as overspill housing for colliery workers from nearby Newtongrange and Easthouses, along with other essential workers and the workforce of a small industrial estate. The collieries closed after the coal industry declined in the 1980s, and the old mining village of Easthouses has been largely absorbed into Mayfield, which today has a population similar to a small town. Postcode district EH22 covers the area. Dalkeith is about 2.4 km away in a straight line, Bonnyrigg 3.6 km and Musselburgh 7.6 km. Musselburgh Services on the A1, about 6.2 km away, is the closest stop for anyone dealing with an AdBlue warning.
roadsText: The A68 and the A7 run either side of Mayfield. The nearest service area is Musselburgh Services on the A1, about 6.2 km away in a straight line, followed by Dreghorn Services on the A720 at about 11.8 km and MacMerry, also on the A1, at about 13.8 km. That gives drivers in the EH22 district three stops within 13.8 km.

name: Melksham
intro: Trowbridge is about 4.5 miles (7 km) south-west of Melksham, and Chippenham 6 miles (10 km) to the north. The town and civil parish sits on the River Avon in Wiltshire, had 18,113 residents at the 2021 census and is covered by the SN12 postcode district. Several other towns are close at hand. Corsham is 7.3 km away, Devizes 10.5 km and Calne 11.7 km, with Westbury at 13.2 km. None of the listed service areas is in or next to the town, which is worth knowing before an AdBlue warning comes on. The nearest are two on the M4, Leigh Delamere Services at 15.1 km in a straight line and Chippenham Pit Stop at 15.3 km, with Warminster Services on the A350 at 18.3 km. All three are a similar distance away, so the best choice depends on which way you are heading.
roadsText: Two of the three nearest listed service areas to Melksham are on the M4: Leigh Delamere Services at 15.1 km in a straight line and Chippenham Pit Stop at 15.3 km. Warminster Services on the A350 is 18.3 km away. With all three at 15 km or more, drivers in SN12 face a similar run to services whichever way they head, and road distances will be longer.

name: Melton Mowbray
intro: Melton Mowbray is a Leicestershire market town on the River Eye, which is known as the Wreake below the town. It lies 19 miles (31 km) north-east of Leicester and 20 miles (32 km) south-east of Nottingham, and had 27,670 residents in 2019. Sometimes promoted as Britain's 'Rural Capital of Food', it is the home of the Melton Mowbray pork pie. Postcode districts are LE13 and LE14, and the main roads are the A606, A607 and A6006. Neighbouring towns are spread out: Syston is about 15 km away and Oakham 15.1 km, with Mountsorrel at 18.1 km and Loughborough at 22.8 km. The nearest service areas are also some way off, at about 11.8 km on the A46 and 13.2 km on the A606, so a driver with an AdBlue warning should expect a drive to reach either.
roadsText: Melton Mowbray's main roads are the A606, A607 and A6006. Six Hills Services Northbound on the A46 is the nearest service area at about 11.8 km, followed by Welcome Break Hickling on the A606 at 13.2 km and ExtraMSA Leicester Services on the A6 at 18.5 km. BP Colsterworth Service Station, around 18.8 km away, is listed in OpenStreetMap as selling AdBlue at the pump; that list is incomplete.

name: Merthyr Tydfil
intro: Often called just Merthyr, Merthyr Tydfil is the main town in the county borough of the same name, about 23 miles (37km) north of Cardiff. In the early 19th century it was known as the 'Iron Capital of the World', and the world's first steam-powered railway journey ran here in 1804. Today the town covers the CF47 and CF48 postcode districts. Its road list is all A-roads: the A470, A465, A4060, A4102, A4054 and A469, with no motorway among them. Neighbouring towns are close, including Aberdare at 6.7km, Mountain Ash at 7.7km, Tredegar at 9.7km and Ebbw Vale at 12.1km. For a diesel driver that means most local journeys stay on A-roads, and the nearest motorway services, Cardiff West on the M4, are about 27.7km away. An AdBlue warning here is worth acting on early rather than assuming a service area is close by.
roadsText: Merthyr's listed roads are the A470, A465, A4060, A4102, A4054 and A469. None of the nearest service areas is in the town: Glanusk services on the A40 is about 25.1km away, Cardiff West services on the M4 about 27.7km and Sarn Park services, also on the M4, about 27.9km. With even the closest at 25.1km, a driver who gets an AdBlue warning in CF47 or CF48 should plan the stop rather than count on passing one.

name: Merton
intro: Host of the Wimbledon tournament, one of tennis's Grand Slam competitions, the London Borough of Merton has Mitcham, Morden and Wimbledon as its main commercial centres, with Wimbledon the largest. Smaller centres include Raynes Park, Colliers Wood, South Wimbledon and Wimbledon Park. The borough was formed in 1965 from the Municipal Borough of Mitcham, the Municipal Borough of Wimbledon and the Merton and Morden Urban District, all formerly in Surrey, and its council is based in Morden. About 214,931 people live here. Main roads listed include the A3, A23, A24, A205, A214, A217, A297 and A306, and postcode districts include SW17, SW19, SW20, SM4 and CR4. Wandsworth is 4.8km away, Worcester Park and Stoneleigh 5.6km and Kingston upon Thames 5.7km. With no motorway in its road list, a van with an AdBlue warning in Merton is more likely to be on an A-road or a local street than on a motorway.
roadsText: Merton has the A24, A297, A217, A3, A214, A306, A205 and A23 among its main roads. Heston Services on the M4 is the closest listed service area at 15.7km, followed by Cobham Services on the M25 at 18.5km and Clacket Lane Services on the M25 at 22.8km. A station at Catford, 14km away, is listed as selling AdBlue at the pump in OpenStreetMap; that data is incomplete, so other stations may sell it too.

name: Methil
intro: Levenmouth is the name given to the continuous urban area that includes Methil, on the north shore of the Firth of Forth between Largo Bay to the east and Wemyss Bay to the west. The River Leven separates the town from its neighbours, and the Fife Coastal Path runs through it. Once Scotland's greatest coal port, Methil is now turning towards a green energy future, and its 2022 population was 10,890. Addresses here fall in the KY8 postcode district. Glenrothes is 9.5 km away and Kirkcaldy and Dysart 11.4 km, with St Andrews at 21.3 km. For a driver with an AdBlue warning, this coastal town is some distance from the nearest listed services: Kinross Services on the M90 is 25.9 km away in a straight line, and the other two listed sites are further still.
roadsText: The nearest listed service area to Methil is Kinross Services on the M90, 25.9 km away in a straight line. The other two, MacMerry and Musselburgh Services, are both on the A1, at 27.6 km and 29.1 km. Those are straight-line figures from the town centre and the drive to each will be longer, so a low AdBlue reading is best dealt with before a long trip.

name: Mexborough
intro: Between Manvers and Denaby Main in the City of Doncaster district, Mexborough lies on the River Don close to where it meets the River Dearne, and on the A6023 road. It runs continuously into Swinton to the south-west and Conisbrough to the east, and had 15,244 residents at the 2011 census. Historically it was part of the West Riding of Yorkshire. Like Swinton, it uses the S64 postcode district. Swinton is about 2.3 km away, Wath upon Dearne 3.5 km, Conisbrough 4.1 km and Rawmarsh 5.5 km. For a van or diesel car with an AdBlue warning, a station in Doncaster listed as selling AdBlue at the pump is about 7.6 km away, while the nearest service area, Rotherham Services on the M1, is about 11.9 km in a straight line.
roadsText: Mexborough is on the A6023. The nearest service areas, in a straight line, are Rotherham Services on the M1 (11.9 km), Barnsdale Bar Services on the A1 (14.7 km) and Sheffield Service Area on the A6102 (16.1 km). OpenStreetMap lists a station in Doncaster (DN4 0TP), about 7.6 km away, and another in Pontefract (WF7 7HX), about 16.7 km away, as selling AdBlue at the pump. Its AdBlue records are incomplete.

name: Middlesbrough
intro: On the southern bank of the River Tees, Middlesbrough is a port town and unitary authority that forms part of the Teesside built-up area and the Tees Valley. It had 148,215 residents in 2021. There was no urban settlement here until Joseph Pease selected the site for the Stockton and Darlington Railway in 1829, after which it grew rapidly into a major centre of iron production. Those older industries have declined since World War II, but Teesport and the Wilton International industrial site remain major employers. Its listed main roads include the A19, A66, A171, A172, A174, A1043, A1053 and A1085, and the postcode districts include TS1 to TS8. Eston is 4.3km away, Thornaby-on-Tees 5km and Billingham 6.6km, so a van working across Teesside can pass through several towns in a short distance, and an AdBlue warning may appear in any of them.
roadsText: The A172, A174, A171, A66, A19, A1043, A1053 and A1085 are all on Middlesbrough's road list. The closest listed stop is Teesside Truck Stop on the A66, 4.7km away. Wolviston Services on the A689 is 10.6km away, and southbound services on the A19 are 13.1km away. With the A66 and A19 both in the town's road list, those are the stops most within reach for drivers already on them.

name: Middleton
intro: Halfway between Rochdale and Manchester, 5 miles from each, Middleton lies on the River Irk in the Metropolitan Borough of Rochdale. Blackley is to the south and Moston to the south-east. For a town of 46,617 people, its road list is unusually heavy on motorways: the M60, M62 and M66 all appear, along with the A627(M), A664, A576, A6104 and A663. Birch Services on the M62 is only 2.7 km away. The postcode districts listed are M24, M9 and OL9, so addresses carry both M and OL prefixes. Chadderton is the nearest town at 3.5 km, with Heywood at 4 km and Royton at 5 km. Prestwich (5.8 km), Failsworth (6.1 km) and Whitefield (6.1 km) are a little further.
roadsText: Middleton's main roads include the M60, M62 and M66, plus the A627(M), A664, A576, A6104 and A663. Birch Services on the M62 is only 2.7 km away. The next two, Rivington on the M61 and Blackburn with Darwen on the M65, are around 25 km off. In OpenStreetMap, a station 5.3 km away and one in Manchester's M25 postcode district at 6.3 km are listed as selling AdBlue at the pump. The data is incomplete.

name: Middlewich
intro: With three major roads, the A533, A54 and A530, and good motorway links to Manchester and Liverpool, Middlewich is a market town and civil parish in Cheshire East. It lies 20 miles (32.2 km) east of Chester, 3 miles (4.8 km) east of Winsford, 5 miles (8.0 km) south-east of Northwich and 5 miles (8.0 km) north-west of Sandbach. Its population at the 2021 census was 14,421, having doubled since 1970. Middlewich sits at the confluence of the rivers Dane, Croco and Wheelock, and the Shropshire Union and Trent & Mersey canals both pass through it. The CW10 postcode district covers the town. Winsford is about 5.6 km away, Sandbach 7.1 km and Davenham 7.2 km. For a driver with an AdBlue warning, the nearest motorway service area is Sandbach Services on the M6, about 8.9 km away.
roadsText: The A533, A54 and A530 are Middlewich's three major roads. The nearest service area is Sandbach Services on the M6, about 8.9 km away. Knutsford Services and Tabley Hill Service Station, both also on the M6, are around 12.7 km and 13.6 km off. All three are motorway stops, so reaching them means joining the M6.

name: Midsomer Norton
intro: Close to the Mendip Hills in Bath and North East Somerset, Midsomer Norton sits 10 miles (16 km) from each of Bath, Wells and Frome, and 16 miles (26 km) south-east of Bristol. The River Somer runs the length of the town centre. At the 2021 census the built-up area, which extends into the neighbouring parish of Westfield, had 13,745 people. The town closely adjoins Radstock, and between 1933 and 2011 the two formed a single area called Norton Radstock. The BA3 postcode district covers it. Midsomer Norton grew into a transport hub with the development of the Somerset coalfield, but service areas are not close today: the nearest listed is 21.2 km away in a straight line, on the A350. Frome is 12.9 km away, Bath 13.5 km, Keynsham 14 km and Wells 14.5 km, so most trips out of town to deal with an AdBlue warning involve some distance.
roadsText: Midsomer Norton has no listed service area close by. The nearest listed is Warminster Services on the A350, 21.2 km away in a straight line, followed by Welcome Break Gordano Services on the M5 at 26.3 km and Avon Lodge on the A4 at 28.2 km. Road distances will be longer than these figures, so an AdBlue warning here is worth acting on before setting off on a longer run.

name: Milford Haven
intro: On the north side of the Milford Haven Waterway, an estuary forming a natural harbour that has been used as a port since the Middle Ages, Milford Haven is the most populous community in Pembrokeshire, with 13,907 people at the 2011 census. The town was founded in 1790 with a grid street pattern. By 2010 its port was the fourth largest in the United Kingdom by tonnage, and oil refineries and one of the world's biggest liquefied natural gas terminals keep it central to the energy sector. The town is covered by the SA73 postcode district. Distance is the thing to plan around with an AdBlue warning here. Haverfordwest is 12.2 km away, but Carmarthen is 52.9 km away, Llanelli 62 km and Swansea 77 km, and the closest listed service areas are on the M4.
roadsText: No listed service area is close to Milford Haven. The two nearest listed are both on the M4: Pont Abraham Services, 67.4 km away in a straight line, and Swansea West Services at 72.2 km. Road distances will be longer than those figures. With motorway services that far off, an AdBlue warning that comes on around the SA73 area is better dealt with early than left until the next motorway stop.

name: Milngavie
intro: On the Allander Water at the north-western edge of Greater Glasgow, Milngavie is an East Dunbartonshire town and a suburb of Glasgow, about ten kilometres from the city centre. Scottish Government figures for 2018 put its population at 13,537 in 6,062 households, and its postcode district is G62. It is also the official starting point of the West Highland Way footpath, marked by a granite obelisk in the town centre. Bearsden is its immediate neighbour, 2.6 km away, with Clydebank at 6.4 km, Bishopbriggs at 7.8 km, Renfrew at 8.7 km and Erskine at 9 km. For a van or diesel car showing an AdBlue warning here, distance to services is the thing to know: the nearest listed motorway service area is more than 20 km away in a straight line, while two stations nearer the town, at 8.3 km and 14.8 km, are listed in OpenStreetMap as selling AdBlue at the pump.
roadsText: Around Milngavie, the nearest listed service areas are Bothwell Services on the M74 at 21.7 km, Hamilton Services on the M74 at 25 km and Stirling Services on the M9 at 29.1 km, all straight-line distances from the town centre. A station in Glasgow (G11 6DN), 8.3 km away, and another 14.8 km away are listed in OpenStreetMap as selling AdBlue at the pump. That mapping is incomplete, so other sites may sell it too.

name: Milton Keynes
intro: Planned as a new town in the 1960s, Milton Keynes took in the existing towns of Bletchley, Fenny Stratford, Wolverton and Stony Stratford, along with fifteen villages and the farmland between them. Today it is a city in Buckinghamshire about 50 miles (80 km) north-west of London, with an urban area population of 264,349 at the 2021 census. By design it is made up of many well-delineated neighbourhoods, and approximately 25% of the urban area is parkland or woodland. Postcode districts include MK4, MK5, MK6, MK8, MK9, MK13, MK14 and MK15. The M1 is the only motorway listed, alongside the A5, A421, A422, A509 and A4146. Bletchley is 5.2 km away and Newport Pagnell 5.6 km. A van or diesel car with an AdBlue warning here is close to a listed service area, with the nearest 5.2 km away on the M1.
roadsText: The M1 is among the main roads listed for Milton Keynes, with the A509, A5, A421, A4146 and A422. Two of the three nearest service areas are on the M1: Newport Pagnell Services at 5.2 km and Crawley Crossing Truck Stop at 11 km. Towcester Services on the A43 is 19.3 km away. For a van with an AdBlue warning, Newport Pagnell is the closest listed stop.

name: Minehead
intro: On the south bank of the Bristol Channel, close to Exmoor National Park, Minehead is a coastal Somerset town 21 miles (34 km) north-west of the county town of Taunton and 12 miles (19 km) from the Devon boundary. The parish takes in Alcombe and Woodcombe, suburban villages that have been absorbed into the town, and had 11,752 residents at the 2021 census. Its postcode district is TA24. There was a small port here by 1380, and the town's fortunes later revived with the growth of sea bathing. For drivers, distance is the main issue: the nearest listed service areas are all on the M5, between 33.3 km and 35.6 km away in a straight line, and Wellington, Taunton and Tiverton are all more than 30 km away.
roadsText: Minehead is a long way from motorway services. The three nearest listed service areas are all on the M5: Moto Tiverton Services at 33.3 km in a straight line, RoadChef Taunton Deane Services at 34.4 km and Moto Bridgwater Services at 35.6 km. Roads to each will be longer than those figures, so an AdBlue warning here is worth dealing with before setting out rather than leaving to a services stop.

name: Minster
intro: On the north coast of the Isle of Sheppey, Minster is a Kent town in the Swale district and sits within the parish of Minster-on-Sea. The 2021 census recorded 17,389 people here, and the town's postcode district is ME12. Sheerness is its nearest neighbour at 3.7 km. Because this is an island town, distances to services matter if a van or diesel car shows an AdBlue warning. The closest listed service area is Medway Services on the M2, 16.3 km away in a straight line, and the next, Maidstone Services on the M20, is 21.7 km off. Sittingbourne is 9.5 km from Minster, followed by Faversham at 13.4 km and Gillingham at 16.6 km, with Southend-on-Sea (16.7 km) and Whitstable (17.7 km) slightly further. With the nearest listed services that far away, it pays to act on a warning early.
roadsText: Minster's nearest listed service area is Medway Services on the M2, 16.3 km away measured in a straight line. Maidstone Services on the M20 is 21.7 km away, and Orsett Cock Services on the A13 is 29.8 km. From a town on the Isle of Sheppey, the real road distance to any of these will be longer, so leave a good margin once an AdBlue warning shows.

name: Mirfield
intro: Sitting on the A644 between Brighouse and Dewsbury, Mirfield is a town and civil parish in Kirklees, West Yorkshire. Historically part of the West Riding, it forms part of the Heavy Woollen District and had 19,563 residents at the 2011 census. Its name comes from the Old English myrgefeld, meaning 'pleasant field'. Mirfield sits in the WF14 postcode district, and its neighbours are close: Liversedge is about 3.1 km away, Heckmondwike 4 km, Dewsbury 4.3 km and Cleckheaton 5.2 km, with Batley and Brighouse a little further at 5.9 km and 6.5 km. For a driver whose van or car shows an AdBlue warning, motorway services are not far. Hartshead Moor Services on the M62 is the nearest listed service area, about 4.9 km away in a straight line, and Woolley Edge Services on the M1 is about 11.8 km.
roadsText: Mirfield is on the A644, the road linking Brighouse and Dewsbury. The nearest service areas in a straight line are Hartshead Moor Services on the M62 (4.9 km), Woolley Edge Services on the M1 (11.8 km) and Skelton Lake Service Station on the M1 (18.2 km). A station in Leeds (LS9 0AS), about 18.3 km away, is listed on OpenStreetMap as selling AdBlue at the pump. That map data is incomplete, so it is not a full list of places selling AdBlue.

name: Monmouth
intro: Where the River Monnow joins the River Wye, two miles (three kilometres) from the border between Wales and England, stands Monmouth (Trefynwy), a market town and community in Monmouthshire. It was the county town of historic Monmouthshire, although Abergavenny is the largest settlement. The town grew up after the Normans built Monmouth Castle around 1067, and its medieval stone gated bridge is the only one of its type remaining in Britain. The population was 10,508 at the 2011 census, up from 8,877 in 2001, and the postcode district is NP25. Ross-on-Wye is 14.9 km away, Chepstow 19.5 km, Abergavenny 20.9 km and Hereford 27 km. For a driver with an AdBlue warning, the A40 is the useful road, with two listed service areas on it within 8 km of the town.
roadsText: Monmouth's two nearest service areas are both on the A40: Symonds Yat Services, 5.6 km away in a straight line, and Monmouth A40 Services at 8 km. The third is Ross Spur Services on the M50, 16.3 km away. Road distances will be longer than these straight-line figures, but either A40 site is near enough to be a practical place to stop if an AdBlue warning comes on.

name: Montrose
intro: The northernmost coastal town in Angus, Montrose lies between the mouths of the North and South Esk rivers, 28 miles (45 kilometres) north of Dundee and 37 miles (60 kilometres) south of Aberdeen. It had 11,251 residents in 2022, making it the third most-populous settlement in Angus. The town functions as a port, including as a commercial port for the oil and gas industry. It is known for its wide thoroughfare and high street, and it looks out over Montrose Basin, a tidal lagoon. Montrose sits in the DD10 postcode district. Neighbouring towns are spread out: Arbroath is 18.7 km away, Forfar 27 km and Stonehaven 31.4 km. With that much distance between towns, a van or diesel car with an AdBlue warning is better dealt with before a longer run than part way through one.
roadsText: Stracathro Services on the A90 is the closest service area listed, 10.8 km from Montrose. Forfar Services, also on the A90, is 29.2 km away, and the next listed option is Kinross Services on the M90 at 82.3 km. For most drivers that makes the two A90 stops the realistic choices when an AdBlue warning comes on away from town.

name: Morecambe
intro: On the shore of Morecambe Bay, part of the Irish Sea, Morecambe is a seaside town and civil parish in the City of Lancaster district of Lancashire. The parish had a population of 34,590 in 2021. The LA4, LA3 and LA1 postcode districts cover the town. Its closest neighbours are very close indeed: Heysham is 2.6 km away and Lancaster 3.7 km. Beyond those two, Ulverston and Fleetwood are both more than 20 km away. The M6 and A6 are listed among the roads around the town, along with the A589, A683, A5105 and A588. If an AdBlue warning comes on, the nearest service areas are all on the M6, starting 13.1 km away.
roadsText: Roads listed around Morecambe are the M6 and A6, along with the A589, A683, A5105 and A588. All three of the nearest service areas are on the M6: Lancaster Services at 13.1 km, Burton-in-Kendal Services at 14.4 km and Killington Lake Services at 30.7 km. Lancaster, 3.7 km away, is the closest neighbour after Heysham.

name: Morley
intro: Built on seven hills, Scatcherd, Dawson, Daisy, Chapel, Hunger, Troy and Banks, Morley is a market town about 5 miles (8 km) south-west of Leeds city centre and the largest town in the City of Leeds borough after Leeds itself. It forms part of the Heavy Woollen District and includes the New Brighton area. In 2011 the town had 44,440 residents. For a driver with an AdBlue fault, the striking thing is motorway access: three motorways, the M62, M621 and M1, appear among the main roads listed, with the A643, A650, A653, A62 and A6110. The postcode district is LS27. Measured directly, East Ardsley is 3.8 km away and Batley 3.9 km, with Dewsbury at 7 km and Rothwell at 7.2 km. The town is split between the Morley North and Morley South wards of Leeds City Council.
roadsText: Morley has three motorways among its main roads, the M62, M621 and M1, along with the A643, A650, A653, A62 and A6110. Measured directly, Skelton Lake Service Station on the M1 is 8.9 km away, Hartshead Moor on the M62 is 10.3 km and Whitwood on the M62 is 13.5 km. OpenStreetMap lists a station with a Leeds address, 9 km away, as selling AdBlue at the pump, but its coverage is incomplete.

name: Morpeth
intro: Morpeth's name may refer to its position on the road to Scotland and a murder that happened on that road, though the meaning is uncertain. This historic market town lies on the River Wansbeck in Northumberland, close to Ashington and Bedlington. It was granted a market charter in 1200 and by the mid-1700s was one of the main markets in England, before the opening of the railways in the 1800s led to its decline. The 2011 census gave a population of 14,017, and the town is in the NE61 postcode district. Bedlington is 7.1 km away and Ashington 8.6 km, with Cramlington at 10.7 km, Blyth at 11.7 km and Ponteland at 14.5 km. Service areas are thin on the ground nearby: the closest is 11.7 km away and the next is 31.9 km off, so a warning light on a longer trip out of Morpeth can leave some distance to cover.
roadsText: The nearest service area to Morpeth is Seaton Burn on the A19, 11.7 km away. After that there is a long gap: Washington services on the A1(M) is 31.9 km away and Adderstone on the A1 is 44.8 km. In OpenStreetMap, a station in Newcastle upon Tyne, 15.2 km from the town, is listed as selling AdBlue at the pump. That data is incomplete, so other forecourts may stock it.

name: Mossley
intro: Before it was placed entirely in Lancashire in 1889, Mossley grew up straddling three historic counties: Lancashire, Cheshire and Yorkshire. It became part of Greater Manchester in 1974 and is now a town and civil parish in Tameside, in the upper Tame Valley and the foothills of the Pennines, 3 miles (4.8 km) south-east of Oldham and 9 miles (14.5 km) east of Manchester. At the 2021 census the built-up area had 11,410 residents and the parish 11,557. The OL5 postcode district covers the town. Lees is about 2.8 km away, Uppermill 3.3 km and Stalybridge 3.7 km, with Ashton-under-Lyne at 4.6 km and Dukinfield at 6 km. For a driver with an AdBlue warning, the nearest motorway service area is Birch Services on the M62, about 13.9 km off.
roadsText: Birch Services on the M62 is the closest service area to Mossley, about 13.9 km away. Hartshead Moor services, also on the M62, is around 28.8 km off, and Woolley Edge Services on the M1 about 34.2 km. OpenStreetMap has a site roughly 7.1 km away listed as selling AdBlue at the pump, plus a station under Manchester at about 16.8 km. Its records are incomplete, so other stations may also sell it.

name: Motherwell
intro: Home to the headquarters of North Lanarkshire Council, Motherwell is a town and former burgh around 19 km southeast of Glasgow. It has a population of around 32,120 and is geographically attached to Wishaw, the two towns forming a large urban area. Rivers mark its edges: the River Clyde separates it from Hamilton to the west, while the South Calder Water divides it from Carfin to the north-east and from New Stevenston and Bellshill to the north. ML1 and ML4 are the postcode districts. The M74 and M8 both appear on the road list, together with the A8, A72, A721, A723, A725 and A7071. Bellshill is 3.6 km away, Wishaw 4.5 km and Hamilton 4.7 km. With two motorway service areas within 5.2 km, there are options close at hand if an AdBlue warning comes up.
roadsText: Main roads recorded around Motherwell are the M74, M8, A725, A7071, A8, A721, A723 and A72. Hamilton Services on the M74 is only 2.7 km away and Bothwell Services on the M74 is 5.2 km. The M74 Truck Stop is further at 16.8 km. For drivers in Motherwell, that puts a service area a short distance from the town.

name: Mountain Ash
intro: In the Cynon Valley, Mountain Ash (Aberpennar in Welsh) is a town in Rhondda Cynon Taf with 11,230 people at the 2011 Census and an estimated 11,339 in 2019. It is split into two communities: West, covering the town centre, Miskin, Darranlas, Fernhill and Glenboi, and East, covering Cefnpennar, Cwmpennar, Caegarw and Newtown. Penrhiwceiber lies a mile to the south-east and Cardiff 19 miles (31 km) to the south-east. The CF45 postcode district covers the town. Aberdare is 4.7 km away, followed by Rhondda at 7.5 km, Merthyr Tydfil at 7.7 km, Porth at 8.1 km and Pontypridd at 9.6 km. Motorway services are some distance away, with the nearest listed site 20.4 km off in a straight line, so an AdBlue warning here is best handled before setting out on a longer run.
roadsText: All three of the nearest service areas to Mountain Ash are on the M4: Cardiff West Services at 20.4 km in a straight line, Sarn Park Services at 21.2 km and Cardiff Gate Services at 24.1 km. Those are straight-line distances, so the drive to any of them will be longer. With no service area close to the town, an AdBlue warning in the Cynon Valley is worth acting on sooner rather than later.

name: Mountsorrel
intro: Just south of Loughborough on the River Soar, Mountsorrel is a large Leicestershire village that has grown quickly. Its population was 6,662 in 2001, 8,223 in 2011 and 12,885 in 2021, nearly doubling in twenty years. The village is in the Charnwood district and falls within the LE12 postcode district. Birstall is 4.7 km away and Syston 5.5 km, with Loughborough 7.4 km off and Leicester 10.1 km. Shepshed is 11.1 km away. For anyone driving a van or diesel car, two roadside service areas are close by, on the A6 and the A46, both within 7 km of the village. That means a stop is close at hand if an AdBlue warning comes on during a local trip.
roadsText: Mountsorrel has two service areas within 7 km: ExtraMSA Leicester Services on the A6 at 3.7 km and Six Hills Services Northbound on the A46 at 6.6 km. For the motorway, Leicester Forest East Services on the M1 is 12.3 km away. Those three give a choice of stops on the A6, the A46 and the M1.

name: Musselburgh
intro: Known as the 'Honest Toun' and believed to be the oldest existing town in Scotland, Musselburgh sits at the mouth of the River Esk on the shore of the Firth of Forth, about 8 km east of Edinburgh. It is the largest settlement in East Lothian, with 21,479 people in 2022, and is home to Queen Margaret University. The EH21 postcode district covers the town. Close neighbours include Prestonpans (4.8 km), Dalkeith (5.4 km) and Tranent (6.2 km), with Mayfield at 7.6 km and Bonnyrigg at 8.3 km. For drivers, the A1 is close at hand: a service area on it is 1.7 km from the town, which is useful to know if an AdBlue warning appears.
roadsText: The nearest service area is Musselburgh Services on the A1, only 1.7 km away. MacMerry, also on the A1, is 10.6 km off, and Dreghorn Services on the A720 is 12.1 km. Having three service areas within 12.1 km, on two different roads, gives drivers in and around Musselburgh a choice of stops if a warning appears.

name: Nailsea
intro: Bristol is 8 miles (13 km) north-east of Nailsea and Weston-super-Mare 11 miles (18 km) to the south-west. The North Somerset town is close to the M5 and Bristol Airport, and the village of Backwell lies to the south, on the other side of the Bristol to Exeter railway line. Nailsea was once an industrial centre based on coal mining and glass manufacture, which have since been replaced by service industries, and it had 15,539 residents at the 2021 census. The town is surrounded by the North Somerset Levels and sits in the BS48 postcode district. Portishead is 5.9 km away and Clevedon 6.5 km. For a van or diesel car with an AdBlue warning, the nearest listed service area is Gordano Services on the M5, 6.5 km away in a straight line.
roadsText: Nailsea is close to the M5, and the nearest listed service area is Gordano Services on that motorway, 6.5 km away in a straight line. Avon Lodge on the A4 is 9.7 km off and Magor Services on the M4 is 18.3 km. A filling station at Lower Weare (BS26 2JE), 17.5 km away, is listed on OpenStreetMap as selling AdBlue at the pump.
