That data is incomplete, so other sites may sell it too.

name: Nairn
intro: Where the River Nairn enters the Moray Firth, east of Inverness, Nairn is an ancient fishing port and market town and the traditional county town of Nairnshire. It is a former royal burgh in the Highland Council area, and with 9,582 residents at the 2022 census it is the third-largest settlement in Highland after Inverness and Fort William. The town is best known as a seaside resort, with two golf courses and beaches. It is covered by the IV12 postcode district. This is a part of Scotland where distances are long: Inverness is 24.7 km away in a straight line and Elgin 34.2 km, while the next nearest town, Inverurie, is 94.7 km off. For a van or diesel car with an AdBlue warning, the nearest listed service area is 27.7 km away on the A9.
roadsText: The nearest listed service area to Nairn is Skiach Services on the A9, 27.7 km away in a straight line. Elgin Services on the A96 is 36.8 km away and Ashgrove Services, also on the A96, is 61.4 km away. With every listed service area at least 27.7 km from the town centre, a driver seeing an AdBlue warning here should not leave it until the gauge is nearly empty.

name: Nantwich
intro: Crewe is the nearest neighbouring town to Nantwich, only about 5.5 km away, and every other nearby town is more than 13 km off. This market town and civil parish in Cheshire East, covered by the CW5 postcode district, had 18,740 people in its built-up area at the 2021 census, with 14,045 in the parish itself. It has among the highest concentrations of listed buildings in England, with notably good examples of Tudor and Georgian architecture. Sandbach is around 13.3 km away, Winsford 13.7 km and Middlewich 14.6 km, while Alsager is about 15 km and Market Drayton 17.8 km. For a driver with an AdBlue warning, that spread matters: once you are outside Nantwich and Crewe, the next towns and the M6 service areas are all a fair drive away.
roadsText: All three of the nearest service areas are on the M6. Crewe Services is about 12.1 km from Nantwich, Sandbach Services around 14.6 km and Keele Services roughly 17.2 km. None of them is close to the town, so a van or diesel car with an AdBlue warning faces a drive of at least 12.1 km to reach motorway services from here.

name: Neath
intro: Known in Welsh as Castell-nedd, Neath is a market town in Neath Port Talbot County Borough, on the River Neath about seven miles (eleven kilometres) east-north-east of Swansea. It was historically part of Glamorgan, and the town had a population of 50,658 in 2011. Its postcode districts are SA10 and SA11. The local road list covers a lot of ground for a van or diesel car: the M4, A465, A483, A474, A4230, A4109, A48 and A4241 all appear around the town. Neighbouring places are close together, with Baglan about 3.6km away, Port Talbot 8km, Swansea 8.3km and Maesteg 12.5km. Driving here can mix short trips between those towns with longer runs on the M4, and an AdBlue warning can come up on either. Knowing which services are within reach before setting off makes that easier to deal with.
roadsText: Roads listed around Neath include the M4, A465, A483, A474, A4230, A4109, A48 and A4241. All three of the nearest service areas are on the M4: Swansea West services at about 12.7km, Pont Abraham services at 19.7km and Sarn Park services at 21.7km. That puts the closest motorway stop a short drive from the town, which is worth knowing if a warning appears before a longer run.

name: Nelson
intro: Nelson developed as a mill town during the Industrial Revolution and is now a town and civil parish in the Borough of Pendle, Lancashire, with 33,617 residents in 2021. It sits 3 miles north of Burnley and 2 miles south-west of Colne, and the BB9 and BB8 postcode districts cover the area. Brierfield is only 2 km away and Colne 3.4 km, so Nelson is part of a close group of towns, with Padiham at 8 km and Barnoldswick at 9.3 km a little further out. The M65 is the motorway listed for Nelson, with the A56, A682 and A6068 among the A roads. One useful detail for anyone with an AdBlue warning: Hollin Bank Service Station on the M65 is just 1.5 km away, while the next nearest service area is more than 22 km off.
roadsText: The M65 is the motorway listed around Nelson, along with the A56, A682, A6068, A6114, A671 and A679. Hollin Bank Service Station on the M65 is 1.5 km away. After that, the next service areas are much further: Blackburn with Darwen Services on the M65 at 22.5 km and Birch Services on the M62 at 29.9 km. Burnley is 5.1 km away.

name: Neston
intro: On the Wirral Peninsula, Neston is a market town and civil parish within Cheshire West and Chester. Its built-up area takes in the nearby villages of Parkgate to the north-west and Little Neston and Ness to the south, so the town covers more ground than its centre alone. At the 2021 census the parish had 15,392 residents and the immediate built-up area 14,960. The CH64 postcode district covers Neston. Heswall is the nearest neighbouring town at about 5.1 km, with Bebington at 6.4 km and Flint at 7.6 km. Connah's Quay is around 8.3 km away, Birkenhead 9.8 km and Ellesmere Port 10.1 km. For a driver with an AdBlue warning, the nearest service areas are on the A55 rather than a motorway, the closest about 11.7 km away.
roadsText: The nearest service area to Neston is Chester West Services on the A55, about 11.7 km away. Singing Kettle Services, also on the A55, is around 16.5 km off, and Chester Services on the M56 about 17.4 km. OpenStreetMap has a refuelling site in Liverpool, roughly 15.5 km away, listed as selling AdBlue at the pump, but it is marked as HGV-only. Its data is incomplete, so other stations may sell it.

name: New Haw, West Byfleet and Sheerwater
intro: This area of Surrey takes in New Haw, West Byfleet and Sheerwater, and has a population of 33,035. New Haw itself is a village in the Borough of Runnymede, about 1 mile south of Addlestone and 20 miles south-west of London. The postcode districts listed for the area are KT14, KT15 and KT16. Two motorways are on the road list, the M25 and M3, along with the A3, A245, A317, A318, A319 and A320. Addlestone is 3.3km away, Byfleet 4.1km, Chertsey 4.3km and Weybridge 5.3km, with Woking at 6.6km. That mix of closely spaced towns and nearby motorways means a diesel van or car here can cover a lot of short local trips as well as longer motorway runs, with service areas 6.3km and 8.8km away.
roadsText: Main roads listed around New Haw, West Byfleet and Sheerwater are the M25, M3, A3, A245, A320, A318, A319 and A317. Wisley Services on the A3 is the closest service area at 6.3km, and Cobham Services on the M25 is 8.8km away. Heston Services on the M4 is further out at 17.8km. Those first two give a driver with an AdBlue warning nearby options on the A3 and M25.

name: New Milton
intro: To the north of New Milton lies the New Forest, and to the south the coast at Barton on Sea. This market town and civil parish is in the New Forest district of south-west Hampshire, and its parish takes in Old Milton, Barton on Sea, Ashley, Bashley and Wootton. The 2021 census recorded 25,546 people in the parish, 11,870 of them in New Milton itself, and the postcode district is BH25. The town sits between Lymington and Christchurch: Christchurch is 6.3 km away and Lymington 7.3 km, with Ringwood at 13.6 km and Bournemouth at 15.3 km. Services are some way off for a driver with an AdBlue warning. The nearest listed service area is Picket Post Services on the A31, 12.1 km away in a straight line, and Rufus Stone, also on the A31, is 16.9 km.
roadsText: Both of the nearest listed service areas to New Milton are on the A31: Picket Post Services at 12.1 km and Rufus Stone at 16.9 km, measured in a straight line. West Wellow Services on the A36 is 23.8 km away. By road, each will be further than these figures, so plan a stop early if an AdBlue warning comes on while driving out of the town.

name: New Ollerton and Ollerton
intro: On the edge of Sherwood Forest, New Ollerton is a town in the parish of Ollerton and Boughton within Nottinghamshire's Newark and Sherwood district. It sits close to the villages of Ollerton and Boughton, and the parish had 9,840 residents at the 2011 census. The postcode district is NG22. Other towns are all more than 10 km away: Forest Town is 10.8 km off, Mansfield Woodhouse 12.6 km, Shirebrook 13.9 km, and Retford, Worksop and Mansfield all around 14 km. For a van or diesel car with an AdBlue warning, the A1 is where the nearest services are, with Markham Moor Services 8.2 km away, and it is worth planning ahead given the distances involved.
roadsText: All three nearest service areas to New Ollerton and Ollerton are on the A1: Markham Moor Services at 8.2 km, Cromwell Services at 15.1 km and North Muskham at 15.4 km. A station 12.3 km away is listed on OpenStreetMap as selling AdBlue at the pump. Its AdBlue data is incomplete, so treat this as one option rather than a full list.

name: New Rossington and Rossington
intro: Countryside surrounds Rossington, a civil parish and former mining village in the City of Doncaster, South Yorkshire, with the market towns of Bawtry and Tickhill around it. Together with New Rossington, it has a population of 13,911, and the area uses the DN11 postcode district. Doncaster is the nearest large place, about 5.2 km away, with Warmsworth at 7.4 km, Armthorpe 7.7 km, Bentley 8.8 km and Maltby 9 km. For a van or diesel car showing an AdBlue warning, a station in Doncaster listed as selling AdBlue at the pump is about 6.9 km away. The closest service area is Blyth Services on the A1(M), around 9.3 km in a straight line, followed by Doncaster (North) Services on the M180 at about 14.7 km.
roadsText: Blyth Services on the A1(M) is about 9.3 km from Rossington in a straight line, Doncaster (North) Services on the M180 about 14.7 km and Rotherham Services on the M1 about 19.8 km. OpenStreetMap lists a station in Doncaster (DN4 0TP), roughly 6.9 km away, as selling AdBlue at the pump. Coverage on the map is incomplete, so other stations may also stock it.

name: Newark-on-Trent
intro: Known simply as Newark, Newark-on-Trent is a market town in Nottinghamshire's Newark and Sherwood district. It lies on the River Trent and was historically a major inland port. For drivers, the key fact is the A1, which bypasses the town on the line of the ancient Great North Road; the spire of St Mary Magdalene church can be seen when bypassing it. The parish had 30,345 residents at the 2021 census, and the postcode district is NG24. Alongside the A1, the main roads include the A46, A17, A612, A616, A617 and A1133. Balderton is only about 2.7 km away, but most other towns are further: Bingham is around 17.2 km, North Hykeham 18.6 km, and Grantham and Lincoln both 21.4 km. Three service areas lie within 6 km of the town, on the A46 and A1.
roadsText: Newark-on-Trent's main roads are the A1, A17, A46, A612, A616, A617 and A1133. Newark Services on the A46 is about 2.5 km away and Welcome Break Newark on the A1 around 3.5 km. North Muskham, also on the A1, is about 6 km out, giving three service areas close to the town.

name: Newbury
intro: Set in the valley of the River Kennet, Newbury is a West Berkshire market town 20 miles west of Reading and 26 miles south of Oxford, and the headquarters of West Berkshire Council. It lies on the edge of the Berkshire Downs, 3 miles north of the Hampshire border. Together with the adjoining town of Thatcham, 4.7km away, it forms the principal part of an urban area of approximately 70,000 people, and the local postcode districts are RG14 and RG20. The local economy is linked to the eastern M4 corridor, and the M4 and A34 are both on the road list along with the A4, A339 and A343. Tadley is 13km away, Basingstoke 21.5km and Wantage 22km. Driving from here often means a run on the M4 or A34 as well as local trips to Thatcham.
roadsText: Newbury's main listed roads are the M4, A339, A34, A4 and A343. Chieveley Services on the M4 is the nearest service area at 5.1km, with Tot Hill Services on the A34 at 6.3km. Membury Services, also on the M4, is 18.6km away. Two service areas this close to town give drivers on either the M4 or the A34 a nearby place to stop if an AdBlue warning comes on.

name: Newcastle upon Tyne
intro: Newcastle upon Tyne developed around a Roman settlement called Pons Aelius and is now England's northernmost city, on the northern bank of the River Tyne opposite Gateshead. It is a city and metropolitan borough in Tyne and Wear and the most populous settlement in both the Tyneside conurbation and North East England, with the metropolitan borough estimated at 320,838 people in 2025. Historically part of Northumberland, the city became part of the new metropolitan county of Tyne and Wear in 1974. The A1 and A69 are among the main roads listed, with the A167(M), A167, A184, A191, A696 and A1058, and postcode districts include NE1, NE2, NE3, NE4, NE5, NE7, NE8 and NE13. Longbenton is 5.2km away, Blaydon 5.9km, Killingworth 6.3km and Gateshead 7.6km. For a van or diesel car with an AdBlue warning, a city of this size means anything from short runs in the centre to journeys on the A1 or A69.
roadsText: Roads listed for Newcastle are the A167(M), A167, A1, A696, A1058, A69, A184 and A191. Seaton Burn Services on the A19 is 7.5km away, followed by Washington Services on the A1(M) at 13.2km and Easington Services on the A19 at 28.2km. A station in Newcastle upon Tyne, 5.5km away, is listed as selling AdBlue at the pump in OpenStreetMap; other stations may not be recorded.

name: Newcastle-under-Lyme
intro: Next door to Stoke-on-Trent, Newcastle-under-Lyme is a market town and the administrative centre of its own borough in Staffordshire. It grew up in the twelfth century around the castle that gave it its name and received its first charter in 1173. Early industries included millinery, silk weaving and coal mining, though it never developed a ceramics trade despite being so close to the Potteries. The 2021 census counted 75,082 residents, and the town's postcode district is ST5. The road list is long: the M6, A34, A52, A527, A53, A519, A500 and A50. Kidsgrove is about 7.2km away, Stoke-on-Trent 7.3km and Alsager 9km. With the M6 so close, driving from here can combine town traffic with motorway runs, and three M6 service areas sit within 8.1km.
roadsText: Keele services on the M6 is about 4.3km from Newcastle-under-Lyme, with Swift services, also on the M6, at 4.8km and Crewe services on the same motorway at 8.1km. A forecourt at ST5 4DH, about 4.8km away, is listed on OpenStreetMap as selling AdBlue at the pump. That information is incomplete, so it should not be treated as the only local source. Listed roads are the M6, A34, A52, A527, A53, A519, A500 and A50.

name: Newham
intro: Five miles (8 km) east of the City of London and north of the River Thames, the London Borough of Newham is bounded by the River Lea to the west and the North Circular Road to the east. Its major districts are East Ham, West Ham, Stratford, Plaistow, Forest Gate, Manor Park, Beckton and Canning Town, and it holds London City Airport and most of the 2012 Olympic Park. With 387,576 residents it has the third highest population of the London boroughs. The Woolwich Ferry, the Woolwich foot tunnel and the Silvertown tunnel provide crossings to the south. For a van or diesel car that shows an AdBlue warning here, the postcode districts to know include E6, E7, E12, E13, E15, E16, E20 and IG11, and the main roads include the M11, A13 and A406. Tower Hamlets (5.3km), Greenwich (6.1km) and Barking and Dagenham (6.4km) are the closest neighbouring areas.
roadsText: Roads listed for Newham are the M11, A13, A117, A1020, A406, A123, A1026 and A1261. The closest service areas listed are Thurrock Services on the M25 (16.7km), London Gateway Services on the M1 (24km) and Orsett Cock Services on the A13 (25km). A station 3.3km away and another at Catford, 9.8km away, are listed as selling AdBlue at the pump in OpenStreetMap. Its records are incomplete, so other forecourts may stock it too.

name: Newhaven
intro: Ferries and freight still pass through Newhaven, a port town at the mouth of the River Ouse in the Lewes district of East Sussex. It developed in the Middle Ages as the nearby port of Seaford began drying up, gained a sheltered harbour in the mid-16th century and grew in importance after the railway arrived in 1847, along with cross-Channel ferry services to Dieppe. Those services have been reduced, but the town still runs regular ferries and is an important freight terminal. The parish had 12,854 residents in 2021, and the postcode district is BN9. Peacehaven is 3 km away and Seaford 4.9 km, with Lewes at 9.9 km. If an AdBlue warning appears, the nearest listed service area is Polegate Services on the A22, 13.8 km away in a straight line, and a station 13.3 km off is listed in OpenStreetMap as selling AdBlue at the pump.
roadsText: Polegate Services on the A22 is the nearest listed service area to Newhaven, 13.8 km away in a straight line. Pyecombe Services on the A23 is 19.6 km off and Ricebridge Services (Hickstead), also on the A23, is 25.9 km. OpenStreetMap lists a station 13.3 km from the town as selling AdBlue at the pump. Because that data is incomplete, there may be other stations nearer by.

name: Newmarket
intro: Best known as a centre for breeding, training and racing thoroughbred horses, Newmarket is a West Suffolk market town 14 miles (22.5 km) from both Bury St Edmunds and Cambridge. Its two racecourses hold races on 39 days a year, and the town has about 70 training yards and more than 60 stud farms. In Tudor times it served travellers on the London to Norwich road. The population was 16,772 in 2021, and the town is covered by the CB8 postcode district. A driver dealing with an AdBlue warning here should know that the nearest listed service area is Four Went Ways Services on the A11, 18.5 km away in a straight line. Soham is the closest town at 10.6 km, with Haverhill, Cambridge, Ely and Bury St Edmunds all between 18.5 km and 20.7 km away.
roadsText: Four Went Ways Services on the A11 is the nearest service area to Newmarket, 18.5 km from the town centre in a straight line. Cambridge Services on the A14 is 28.5 km away and Caxton Gibbet Services on the A428 is 34.8 km. For a van or diesel car in CB8 with an AdBlue warning, the A11 site is the closest of the three by a clear margin.

name: Newport
intro: Population growth in Newport between the 2011 and 2021 censuses, from 145,700 to 159,587, was the largest of any unitary authority in Wales. The city and county borough lies on the River Usk near its confluence with the Severn Estuary, roughly 19 km north-east of Cardiff, and forms part of the Cardiff-Newport metropolitan area and the Cardiff Capital Region. A port since the Middle Ages, it was for a time the largest coal-exporting port in Wales, and the earlier Roman settlement of Caerleon is now part of the city. Postcode districts include NP10, NP18, NP19 and NP20. Cwmbrân is 7.6 km away, Risca 9.3 km and Pontypool 12.2 km, with Caerphilly at 15.5 km and Cardiff at 15.8 km. With the M4 and A48(M) among the main roads, motorway driving is never far away for vans and diesel cars here.
roadsText: Newport's main roads include the M4 and A48(M), along with the A4042, A449, A48, A4051, A467 and A468. Cardiff Gate services on the M4 is 10 km away and Magor services on the M4 is 11.5 km, with Cardiff West services on the M4 further out at 22.7 km. With the M4 so close, those are the natural stopping points on a longer drive.

name: Newport
intro: As the county town of the Isle of Wight, Newport sits slightly north of the centre of the island, in the civil parish of Newport and Carisbrooke. It has a quay at the head of the navigable stretch of the River Medina, which flows north to Cowes and the Solent. The 2021 census recorded 25,407 people, and the town is covered by the PO30 postcode district. From that central position, Cowes is 5.6 km away, Ryde 10 km and Sandown 10.5 km. The nearest listed service area is 23.5 km away, so for a van or diesel car based here it pays to deal with an AdBlue warning close to home.
roadsText: The main roads around Newport are the A3020, A3054, A3056 and A3021. The nearest listed service areas are all more than 23 km away: Farlington on the A27 at 23.5 km, Rownhams on the M27 at 30.3 km and Rufus Stone on the A31 at 32.3 km. None of them is close, so it is worth acting on a warning rather than counting on a service-area stop.

name: Newport
intro: Near the Shropshire-Staffordshire border, this Newport is a market town and civil parish in the borough of Telford and Wrekin in Shropshire, 7 miles (11 km) north-east of Telford and 12 miles (19 km) west of Stafford. The parish had 10,814 people at the 2001 census and 11,387 by 2011. Its postcode district is TF10. Other nearby towns are spread out: Market Drayton is 17.1 km away, Codsall 19.9 km, Stone 21.1 km and Cannock 25.7 km. Vans and diesel cars showing an AdBlue warning have no listed service area close to the town. The nearest listed is on the M54, 10.2 km away in a straight line, with another on the A41 at 16.5 km and one on the M6 at 18.6 km.
roadsText: The nearest service area to Newport is Telford Services on the M54, 10.2 km away in a straight line. Adastra Services on the A41 is 16.5 km off and Stafford Services on the M6 is 18.6 km. Road distances will be longer than these straight-line figures. None of the three is close to the town, so if an AdBlue warning comes on it is worth deciding early where to stop.

name: Newport Pagnell
intro: Although the Office for National Statistics counts it as part of the Milton Keynes urban area, Newport Pagnell is separated from the rest of it by the M1 motorway. The town and civil parish sits within the City of Milton Keynes in Buckinghamshire, has a population of 15,250 and is covered by the MK16 and MK20 postcode districts. Its name is attached to Newport Pagnell services, the UK's second ever motorway service station, which is just 1.5 km from the town in a straight line. That puts motorway services very close at hand if an AdBlue warning comes on in a van or diesel car. Milton Keynes itself is 5.6 km away and Bletchley 10 km, while Kempston, Flitwick, Towcester and Leighton Buzzard are all between 16.3 km and 18.5 km. The next listed service area after Newport Pagnell is Crawley Crossing Truck Stop, also on the M1, at 10.7 km.
roadsText: Newport Pagnell Services on the M1 is only 1.5 km from the town in a straight line. The next nearest is Crawley Crossing Truck Stop, also listed on the M1, at 10.7 km, followed by Bedford Services on the A421 at 17.2 km. The M1 itself divides the town from the rest of the Milton Keynes urban area. Distances by road will be longer than these figures.

name: Newquay
intro: On Cornwall's north coast, Newquay is a seaside resort and fishing port facing the North Atlantic, and its airport and spaceport make it a regional centre for aerospace. The River Gannel and its salt marsh bound the town to the south, the Porth Valley to the north-east, and Fistral Bay marks its western edge. Since the second half of the nineteenth century the town has been expanding inland, to the south. The built-up area had 24,545 people at the 2021 census, across the TR7 and TR8 postcode districts. Truro lies about 12 miles (19 km) to the south and Bodmin 20 miles (32 km) to the east. The main roads listed around the town are all A roads, including the A392, A3058 and A3059. For an AdBlue warning, the nearest listed service area is Cornwall Services on the A30, 17.3 km away in a straight line.
roadsText: The main roads listed around Newquay are the A392, A3058, A3059, A3075 and A3076, with no motorway among them. The nearest service area is Cornwall Services on the A30, 17.3 km away in a straight line. The next listed options are much further: Saltash Services on the A388 at 58.3 km and Roundswell Service Area on the A39 at 99.7 km. In practice, the A30 site is the realistic stop for drivers in TR7 and TR8.

name: Newry
intro: Standing on the Clanrye River in counties Armagh and Down, Newry is a cathedral city close to the border with the Republic of Ireland. It lies on the main routes between Belfast, 55 km away, and Dublin, 108 km away. The population was 27,913 in 2021, and Newry was granted city status in 2002 along with Lisburn. It grew as a market town and garrison and became a port when the Newry Canal opened in 1742. The BT35 postcode district covers the city. Recorded roads include the A1, A2, A25, A27 and A28. Banbridge is the nearest of the listed towns at 19.4 km, followed by Armagh (28.7 km) and Craigavon (30 km). With Belfast and Dublin both some distance away, journeys on those routes are long ones, and the nearest motorway services are 41.5 km from the city.
roadsText: The A1, A2, A27, A28 and A25 are the main roads recorded around Newry. Services are some distance away: Cohannon Services on the M1 is the nearest at 41.5 km, with Lisburn Services on the M1 at 44.3 km and Temple Patrick Services Northbound on the M2 at 61 km. If an AdBlue warning appears, it is worth dealing with it before setting off on a longer journey rather than hoping to reach a service area.

name: Newton Abbot
intro: Rapid growth came to Newton Abbot in the Victorian era, as the home of the South Devon Railway locomotive works, a site that now houses the Brunel industrial estate. The market town sits on the River Teign in Devon's Teignbridge district, about 21 km south-west of Exeter and 42 km from Plymouth. The town had 26,746 residents at the 2021 census and is covered by the TQ12 postcode district. It also has a race course nearby, the most westerly in England, and a country park at Decoy. Kingsteignton is only 2.9 km away, and Torquay, Teignmouth and Paignton are all within 11.6 km, so the town sits at the centre of a cluster of short local journeys. Six main roads are listed around it, with the A38 and A380 among them, which gives diesel vans and cars a choice of routes in and out of town.
roadsText: The main roads around Newton Abbot are the A380, A38, A381, A382, A383 and A3022. The nearest service area is Exeter services on the M5, 23.6 km away. Cullompton services on the M5 is 40.8 km and Saltash services on the A388 is 45.5 km, so there is nothing close to town and a longer run is needed to reach a service area.

name: Newton Aycliffe
intro: Founded in 1947 under the New Towns Act, Newton Aycliffe is the oldest new town in the north of England. It lies 5 miles north of Darlington and 10 miles south of Durham, and together with Aycliffe Village to the south and the northern part of School Aycliffe to the west it forms the civil parish of Great Aycliffe. The town is covered by the DL5 postcode district and had 26,415 residents at the 2021 census. For drivers, the key fact is that the A1(M) is on the road list, alongside the A167, A689, A68 and A6072, and two A1(M) service areas are within 6 km of town. Bishop Auckland (8 km) and Spennymoor (9.6 km) are the closest towns, with Darlington 10.3 km away and Stockton-on-Tees, Egglescliffe and Durham all around 17 to 18 km off.
roadsText: Newton Aycliffe's listed roads are the A1(M), A167, A689, A68 and A6072. Service areas are close: Forest Park Services on the A1(M) is 4 km away and Bradbury Services, also on the A1(M), 5.7 km. Sedgefield Services on the A689 is 9.5 km off. A station near Durham, in DH6 and 16.9 km away, is listed as selling AdBlue at the pump in OpenStreetMap, though the data is incomplete and nearer sites may not be mapped.

name: Newton Mearns
intro: Eleven kilometres southwest of Glasgow city centre, Newton Mearns lies on what was historically the main road to Ayrshire and is now the largest settlement in East Renfrewshire. It sits 125 m above sea level and is part of the Greater Glasgow conurbation, with a population of approximately 26,993. The town stretches from Whitecraigs and Kirkhill in the north-east to Maidenhill in the south-east, and from Westacres and Greenlaw in the west to Capelrig and Patterton in the north-west, covered by postcode districts G77, G46 and G76. The M77 and A77 are both on the road list, together with the A726, A727 and A736. Giffnock is 3.7 km away and Barrhead 4.6 km, with Paisley and East Kilbride each 9.2 km off.
roadsText: Main roads recorded around Newton Mearns are the M77, A726, A77, A727 and A736. The nearest service areas are on the M74: Bothwell Services at 17.3 km, Hamilton Services at 18.5 km and the M74 Truck Stop at 30.9 km. OpenStreetMap lists a station in Glasgow (G11 6DN), 10.3 km away, as selling AdBlue at the pump, though that map data is incomplete and other stations may stock it.

name: Newton-le-Willows
intro: Often just called Newton, this market town sits on the eastern edge of St Helens in Merseyside, south of Wigan, north of Warrington and the same distance from Liverpool as from Manchester. Its urban growth in the early 19th century came with the building of the Liverpool and Manchester Railway, and Earlestown, which developed around the industrial works near the Sankey Viaduct, became the town's administrative and commercial centre. The 2021 census counted 24,642 residents, and the town is in the WA12 postcode district. Main roads around the town include the M6 and M62 as well as the A49, A580, A58, A572, A573 and A599. Haydock is 3.3 km away, Golborne 4.2 km and Ashton-in-Makerfield 4.5 km, with St Helens and Warrington a little over 7 km. A diesel van here can easily mix motorway miles with short runs between neighbouring towns.
roadsText: Newton-le-Willows has the M6 and M62 close by, along with the A49, A580, A58, A572, A573 and A599. Burtonwood services on the M62 is only 4 km away, with Earlsfield on the M57 at 13.3 km and Lymm on the M6 at 13.4 km. Stations in Warrington, 5.1 km and 7.7 km away, and one at Old Meadow, 19.8 km away, are listed in OpenStreetMap as selling AdBlue at the pump. That data is incomplete.

name: Newtown
intro: The largest town in Powys and in Mid Wales, Newtown (Y Drenewydd) lies on the River Severn within the historic boundaries of Montgomeryshire, in the community of Newtown and Llanllwchaiarn. It was designated a new town in 1967 and grew as firms settled there, which changed its market town character. The population went from 10,780 in 2001 to 11,357 in 2011 and 11,362 in 2021. SY16 is the postcode district. Distances to other towns are long: Oswestry is 42.8 km away, Ludlow 44.1 km and Shrewsbury 44.5 km, with Aberystwyth at 51.9 km. For a driver with an AdBlue warning, those distances are the main thing to plan around, because the nearest listed service area is 39.7 km off in a straight line.
roadsText: Service areas are a long way from Newtown. The nearest is Nesscliffe Services on the A5, 39.7 km away in a straight line, followed by Mile End Services on the A483 at 42.7 km and Ruabon Park Services, also on the A483, at 56 km. Road distances will be longer than these figures. With no services close to the town, an AdBlue warning here is best acted on early rather than left until the next stop.

name: Newtownabbey
intro: North of Belfast city centre, Newtownabbey is a large County Antrim settlement that still forms part of the Belfast metropolitan area, even though Cavehill and Fortwilliam golf course separate it from the rest of the city. It grew from the merging of several small villages, including Whiteabbey, Glengormley and Carnmoney, and wraps around Carnmoney Hill. At the 2021 census it had 67,599 people, making it the third largest settlement in Northern Ireland, and it falls under Antrim and Newtownabbey Borough Council. For a driver with an AdBlue warning, that means a settlement covering the BT36 and BT37 postcode districts, with the M2, M5 and A8(M) all on the local road list. Belfast is 7.1 km away, and Holywood (5.9 km), Carrickfergus (9.1 km) and Ballyclare (11.7 km) are among the other nearby towns.
roadsText: Roads recorded around Newtownabbey include the M2, M5, M3, A8(M), A2, A6, A55 and A8. The nearest service area is Temple Patrick Services Northbound on the M2, about 8 km away, followed by Lisburn Services on the M1 at 16.1 km and Cohannon Services on the M1 at 51.4 km. OpenStreetMap lists a station in Newtownabbey (BT36 4GX), 5 km away, as selling AdBlue at the pump, along with sites at BT6 0LT (9.9 km) and in Bangor (14.3 km). That map data is incomplete.

name: Newtownards
intro: Referred to simply as Ards, Newtownards is a County Down town at the most northern tip of Strangford Lough, on the Ards Peninsula and 16 km east of Belfast. It had 29,677 residents at the 2021 census and sits within the Ards and North Down Borough, under the BT23 postcode district. Six A roads are recorded around the town: the A2, A20, A21, A22, A48 and A221. Bangor is 7.8 km away and Holywood 10 km, with Castlereagh at 12.7 km and Belfast at 15.1 km. The nearest motorway service areas are more than 20 km away, so a driver who sees an AdBlue warning here is better off knowing the closer options in advance. The nearest station listed as selling AdBlue at the pump is in Bangor, 6.2 km away.
roadsText: The main roads recorded around Newtownards are the A20, A21, A22, A2, A48 and A221. The nearest service areas are Lisburn Services on the M1 (21.5 km) and Temple Patrick Services Northbound on the M2 (23.9 km), with Cohannon Services on the M1 much further at 63.2 km. Closer to home, OpenStreetMap lists a station in Bangor (6.2 km) and one at BT6 0LT (13.8 km) as selling AdBlue at the pump. That data is incomplete, so check locally as well.

name: Normanton
intro: Only 1.1 km, as the crow flies, separates Normanton from Whitwood services on the M62, which is the most useful detail for a driver with an AdBlue warning. The town lies north-east of Wakefield and south-west of Castleford, in the civil parish of Normanton and Altofts within the City of Wakefield district of West Yorkshire. The parish reaches west and north to the River Calder and takes in the large village of Altofts; it had 20,872 residents in 2011. The Normanton council ward is drawn differently, leaving out Altofts but including Warmfield cum Heath to the south-west. Neighbouring towns are close too: Featherstone is 4.3 km away, Castleford 5.3 km, Wakefield 6.6 km and Pontefract 6.9 km. The postcode district is WF6.
roadsText: Whitwood services on the M62 is the nearest service area to Normanton, only 1.1 km away as the crow flies. Skelton Lake Service Station on the M1 is 8.6 km away and Ferrybridge services on the M62 is 9.6 km. OpenStreetMap lists stations with a Pontefract address (8.3 km) and a Leeds address (8.7 km) as selling AdBlue at the pump, though its records are incomplete.

name: North Hykeham
intro: Directly south of Lincoln, North Hykeham is a town and civil parish in Lincolnshire's North Kesteven district. It forms the southern part of the Lincoln Urban Area along with Waddington, Bracebridge Heath, Canwick and South Hykeham, and the parish had about 16,844 residents at the 2021 census. The postcode district is LN6. Lincoln is about 2.9 km away, while Newark-on-Trent is 18.6 km, Balderton 19.4 km and Sleaford 24.3 km. The closest service area, Thorpe on the Hill Services on the A46, is only about 2.5 km away, which is useful if an AdBlue warning comes on around the southern edge of Lincoln. Showground Services on the A15 and Cromwell Services on the A1 are further out, at about 11.8 km and 15.1 km.
roadsText: North Hykeham's nearest service area is Thorpe on the Hill Services on the A46, about 2.5 km away. Showground Services on the A15 is around 11.8 km away, and Cromwell Services on the A1 about 15.1 km. Lincoln, the nearest town, is about 2.9 km to the north, and Newark-on-Trent around 18.6 km.

name: North Walsham
intro: Eight miles (13 km) south of Cromer, with Norwich 15 miles (24 km) to the south, North Walsham is a market town in the North Norfolk district. The town has 12,829 residents and sits in the NR28 postcode district. In local dialect the name is pronounced "Nor Walsham". Distance shapes what a driver needs to know here: the nearest listed service area, Thickthorn Services on the A11, is 26.8 km away in a straight line, and the next is more than 68 km away. Closer to home, a station 7.8 km away is listed in OpenStreetMap as selling AdBlue at the pump, which may help if an AdBlue warning comes on. Taverham and Drayton is the nearest town in the list at 19.4 km, with Norwich at 21.2 km and Great Yarmouth at 33.6 km.
roadsText: Service areas are a long way from North Walsham. Thickthorn Services on the A11 is the nearest at 26.8 km in a straight line, with Freebridge Park on the A47 at 68.1 km and Beacon Hill Services on the A140 at 77.7 km. Nearer at hand, a station with a Norwich address (NR11 7HA), 7.8 km away, appears in OpenStreetMap as selling AdBlue at the pump. That data is incomplete, so other forecourts may sell it too.

name: Northallerton
intro: Coaches travelling between Edinburgh and London once stopped at Northallerton, a market town near the River Wiske in the Vale of Mowbray, North Yorkshire, until the railway arrived. It had 16,832 residents in 2011 and today is an administrative centre for North Yorkshire Council and the York and North Yorkshire Combined Authority. The town uses the DL6 postcode district. Neighbouring towns are a fair distance away: Catterick Garrison is about 18.6 km off, Egglescliffe 20.5 km, Ingleby Barwick 20.7 km and Darlington 21.9 km. Services are closer. Three service areas lie about 10 km away in a straight line, Coneygarth and Leeming Bar Services on the A1(M) and Exelby Services on the A19, and a station with a Northallerton address is listed as selling AdBlue at the pump.
roadsText: Three service areas are around 10 km from Northallerton in a straight line: Coneygarth Services on the A1(M) (9.5 km), Leeming Bar Services on the A1(M) (10 km) and Exelby Services on the A19 (10.4 km). OpenStreetMap lists two stations as selling AdBlue at the pump, one with a Northallerton address (DL7 9EG) about 9.5 km from the centre and one in Richmond (DL10 6PB) about 18.1 km away. The map's AdBlue data is incomplete.

name: Northampton
intro: Sitting on the River Nene, Northampton is the county town of Northamptonshire and the administrative centre of West Northamptonshire. It lies 60 miles (97 km) north-west of London and 50 miles (80 km) south-east of Birmingham, and the 2021 census recorded 249,093 people across its urban area, making it one of the largest towns in England. For drivers, the M1 is the obvious reference point, and the other main roads include the A43, A45, A428, A508 and A5123. Postcode districts here are NN1, NN2, NN3, NN4, NN5 and NN7. The surrounding towns are separate places rather than suburbs: Towcester is about 13.7 km away, Wellingborough 15.1 km, Daventry 18.7 km and Rushden 21.1 km. With a motorway service area under 5 km from the town, there is somewhere close to pull in when the AdBlue light shows.
roadsText: Northampton's main roads are the M1, A43, A45, A428, A508, A4500, A5076 and A5123. Northampton Services on the M1 is about 4.6 km away, and Red Lion Truckstop, also on the M1, is around 7.5 km out. Jacks Hill Cafe & Truck Stop on the A5 is the third nearest, at roughly 12.7 km.

name: Northfleet
intro: Immediately west of Gravesend, Northfleet is a town in the borough of Gravesham in Kent, sitting on the border with the Borough of Dartford. The 2021 census put its population at 29,900 (rounded to the nearest 100), and the DA11, DA10 and DA12 postcode districts cover the area. It has its own station on the North Kent Line, just east of Ebbsfleet International on the High Speed 1 line. For drivers, the A2 heads the road list, with the A1089, A126, A206, A226, A227, A296 and A2260 also around the town. Swanscombe is 2.8km away and Gravesend 3.2km, and the Longfield, New Ash Green and Hartley area is 5.8km. For a diesel van, the nearest service area is only 2.8km from town, on the A2.
roadsText: The A2, A1089, A226, A2260, A227, A126, A296 and A206 are the main roads listed around Northfleet. Tollgate Services on the A2 is only 2.8km away, with Thurrock Services on the M25 at 7.6km and Orsett Cock Services on the A13 at 9km. A station in Strood (ME2 2NY), about 11.4km away, is listed as selling AdBlue at the pump, though OpenStreetMap's records are incomplete.

name: Northwich
intro: Northwich stands on the Cheshire Plain where the rivers Weaver and Dane meet. The market town, in Cheshire West and Chester, lies 15 miles south of Warrington, 18 miles east of Chester, 19 miles south of Manchester and 22 miles south-east of Liverpool, and its parish had 22,726 residents at the 2021 census. The Romans worked salt pans here when the settlement was called Condate, and salt mining later caused serious subsidence; mine stabilisation work was completed in 2007. CW8 and CW9 are the town's postcode districts. Davenham is just 2.7 km away and Winsford 7.9 km. For a driver with an AdBlue warning, Northwich is reasonably placed: Whitley Services on the A49 is 5.8 km away, and two M6 service areas are within 9.3 km.
roadsText: Northwich has three service areas within 9.3 km: Whitley Services on the A49 at 5.8 km, Tabley Hill Service Station on the M6 at 9 km and Knutsford Services on the M6 at 9.3 km. Two Warrington sites, WA3 6RW at 17.7 km and WA5 3TP at 19.1 km, are listed on OpenStreetMap as selling AdBlue at the pump; closer stations may exist but not be mapped.

name: Norwich
intro: Norfolk's county town, Norwich is a cathedral city by the River Wensum and the largest settlement in East Anglia. It lies about 100 miles (160 km) north-east of London, 40 miles (64 km) north of Ipswich and 65 miles (105 km) east of Peterborough. The city council area had an estimated 144,000 residents in 2021, and the wider built-up area recorded 213,166 in 2011. Postcode districts run from NR1 to NR8. Main roads include the A11, A47, A140 and A146, along with the A1042, A1067, A1074 and A1270. Taverham and Drayton is about 6.6 km away, but other towns are further out: Wymondham at 13.7 km, North Walsham 21.2 km and Dereham 23.1 km. Service areas follow the same pattern. Thickthorn Services on the A11 is about 6 km away, and the next nearest are more than 56 km away, so it is the obvious stop for a driver with an AdBlue message on the dash.
roadsText: The main roads listed for Norwich are the A11, A47, A140, A146, A1042, A1067, A1074 and A1270. Thickthorn Services on the A11 is about 6 km away. Beyond that, the nearest listed service areas are a long way out: Beacon Hill Services on the A140 at around 56.6 km and Freebridge Park on the A47 at 61.6 km.

name: Nottingham
intro: County town of Nottinghamshire and a unitary authority in its own right, Nottingham lies 42 miles (68 km) south-east of Sheffield and 54 miles (87 km) north-east of Birmingham. The 2021 census put the city's population at 323,632, while the wider conurbation, which takes in suburbs including Arnold and Carlton, reached 768,638. It is the largest urban area in the East Midlands, so a van or diesel car based here can spend much of its time on built-up roads. Postcode districts covering the city include NG1, NG2, NG3, NG5, NG6, NG7, NG8 and NG9. Neighbouring towns are close: Arnold is about 5.3 km away, West Bridgford 5.8 km, Beeston 6.1 km and Carlton 6.8 km, with Clifton and Stapleford both at 7.2 km. Roads serving the city include the M1, A52, A60, A610 and A453.
roadsText: The main roads listed for Nottingham are the M1, A52, A60, A453, A610, A6011, A6130 and A6514. Trent Bridge Services on the A6011 is the nearest service area, about 3.9 km away, followed by Trowell Services on the M1 at 5.9 km and Pierrepont on the A52 at 7.6 km. One Tesco station about 18.6 km away is listed in OpenStreetMap as selling AdBlue at the pump; that data is incomplete, so it should not be read as a full list.

name: Nuneaton
intro: A medieval nunnery gave Nuneaton its name, and ribbon weaving and coal mining later made it an important industrial town. It is now the largest town in Warwickshire, with 88,813 residents at the 2021 census, and its wider urban area, including Bulkington and Hartshill, reached 99,372. It sits in the Nuneaton and Bedworth district in the north of the county, close to the border with Leicestershire. Postcodes here fall into CV10 and CV11. The M69 is on the road list, along with the A47, A444, A5 and A4254. Hinckley is about 5.7km away and Bedworth 6.1km, with Coventry at 13.4km. Driving here can mix short runs to Hinckley and Bedworth with longer trips on the M69 or towards Coventry. The nearest service area is about 8.5km away on the M6, a useful stop if an AdBlue warning comes on.
roadsText: Corley services on the M6 is the closest service area to Nuneaton, about 8.5km away. Tamworth services on the M42 is 15.4km off and Rugby services on the M6 19km. The town's road list is the M69, A47, A444, A5 and A4254. OpenStreetMap lists one forecourt about 10.6km away and another at Swadlincote (DE12 8AA), about 19.2km away, as selling AdBlue at the pump. Those records are incomplete, so other places may stock it.

name: Oadby
intro: Made up of five wards, like its neighbour Wigston, Oadby is a town in the borough of Oadby and Wigston, 4 miles south-east of Leicester on the A6. It had 23,849 residents in 2011, and Leicester Racecourse sits on its border with Stoneygate. Its postcode district is LE2. The town sits close to the city and its neighbours: Wigston is just 3.1 km away and Leicester 5.6 km, with Blaby and Whetstone at 7.3 km, Enderby and Narborough at 8.9 km and Birstall at 9.7 km. Routes recorded around the town include the A6, A563, A6030 and A47. If an AdBlue warning appears, the nearest listed service area is Leicester Forest East Services on the M1, 9 km away.
roadsText: Main roads around Oadby include the A6, A563, A6030, A47, A5199, A426, A594 and A5460. The nearest service areas are Leicester Forest East Services on the M1, 9 km away, and ExtraMSA Leicester Services on the A6 at 10.6 km. Six Hills Services Northbound, on the A46, is further out at 17.2 km.

name: Oakham
intro: As the county town of Rutland, Oakham is a market town of 12,149 people (2021 census) to the west of Rutland Water, in the Vale of Catmose. It is 25 miles east of Leicester, 28 miles south-east of Nottingham and 23 miles north-west of Peterborough, and stands between 325 and 400 feet above sea level. The postcode district is LE15. Neighbouring towns are spread out: Melton Mowbray is 15.1 km away, Stamford 16.9 km and Corby 20.3 km, with Market Harborough 25.3 km off. The nearest service area, Morcott Services on the A47, is 10.5 km away, so a van or diesel car with an AdBlue warning is best dealt with before setting off on a longer trip.
roadsText: Morcott Services on the A47 is the closest service area to Oakham, 10.5 km away. On the A1, Colsterworth Services is 16.6 km off and Colsterworth Truck Stop 16.7 km. A station with a Grantham address (NG33 5JJ), 16.9 km away, is listed on OpenStreetMap as selling AdBlue at the pump. OpenStreetMap is not a complete record, so other stations may stock it as well.

name: Old Trafford
intro: Bordering both Manchester and Salford, Old Trafford is an area of Trafford, 3.2 km south-west of Manchester city centre. It is roughly marked out by two old toll gates, Brooks' Bar and Trafford Bar, to the east and west, and it forms the north-eastern tip of the Stretford and Urmston parliamentary constituency. The area is home to Old Trafford Cricket Ground and the Old Trafford football stadium. Its population is 21,442, spread across the M5, M17, M32 and M50 postcode districts. Neighbouring places are very close: Stretford is 1.7 km away, Salford 3.4 km, Eccles and Urmston 4 km, Sale 4.9 km and Swinton 5.4 km. Many local journeys from here are short urban ones, while the nearest motorway service area, Birch on the M62, is 12.6 km away.
roadsText: The nearest service area to Old Trafford is Birch on the M62, 12.6 km away, with Lymm and Tabley Hill on the M6 at 17.4 km and 18.6 km. Stations listed in OpenStreetMap as selling AdBlue at the pump include one in Manchester at 8.2 km, one 12.6 km away and one in Warrington at 15.1 km. The map data is incomplete, so nearer forecourts may also stock it.

name: Oldbury
intro: Sandwell's administrative centre is Oldbury, a market town in the West Midlands county. Sandwell council defines Oldbury Town as the wards of Bristnall, Langley, Oldbury and Old Warley, which together had 50,641 residents in 2011. Postcode districts listed for the town are B65, B66, B67, B68, B69 and B70. The M5 is on the road list, along with the A4123, A4031, A41, A461, A458, A456 and A4041. Neighbouring towns are close: Rowley Regis is about 2.1km away, Smethwick 3km, West Bromwich 4.1km and Cradley Heath 4.3km. For a diesel driver that means short urban trips between closely spaced places, with the M5 close at hand for longer runs. Frankley services is about 7.5km away, the nearest planned stop if an AdBlue warning comes on.
roadsText: Oldbury is only about 1.6km from a forecourt in Warley that OpenStreetMap lists as selling AdBlue at the pump. It also lists an HGV-only site in Birmingham (B25 8DW) at 12.5km, though its records are incomplete. Frankley services on the M5, about 7.5km away, is the nearest service area, followed by Hopwood Park on the M42 at 15.5km and Hilton Park on the M6 at 16.6km. The listed roads are the M5, A4123, A4031, A41, A461, A458, A456 and A4041.

name: Oldham
intro: Seven miles north-east of Manchester city centre and 5 miles south-east of Rochdale, Oldham stands on elevated ground amongst the Pennines, between the rivers Irk and Medlock. It is the administrative centre of the Metropolitan Borough of Oldham, which had 242,003 people in 2021. The town rose to prominence in the 19th century as a centre of textile manufacture, and its last mill closed in 1998. Neighbouring places are very close: Lees is 2.6 km away, Royton 3.4 km and Chadderton 3.6 km, with Shaw, Mossley and Ashton-under-Lyne all within 5 km. The postcode districts listed are OL1, OL2, OL4, OL5, OL6, OL8, OL9 and M35. The road list includes the M60 and the A627(M), along with the A62, A627, A6104, A663, A670 and A635. With so many towns this close together, a short drive here can easily cross several of them.
roadsText: Oldham's main roads are the M60 and A627(M), with the A62, A627, A6104, A663, A670 and A635. Birch Services on the M62 is 9.1 km away. The next service areas in the data are much further: Hartshead Moor on the M62 at 30.4 km and Blackburn with Darwen on the M65 at 31.3 km. In OpenStreetMap, which may be missing others, a station just 3.7 km away and one in Manchester's M25 postcode district at 12.3 km are listed as selling AdBlue at the pump.

name: Omagh Town
intro: County Tyrone's county town, Omagh stands where the Drumragh and Camowen rivers meet to form the Strule. It had 20,458 residents at the 2021 census, and the former district council was the largest in the county, with 51,356 people in 2011. The Northern Ireland Roads Service has offices at the Tyrone County Hall in the town. Distances here are long. Belfast is 68 miles (109.5 km) to the east and Derry 34 miles (55 km) to the north, and the nearest neighbouring towns, Strabane, Enniskillen, Cookstown and Dungannon, are between 27.1 km and 36 km away. The BT78 postcode district covers the town. With an AdBlue warning showing, the closest service area is about 42.8 km away on the M1, so it is worth acting on a warning before setting out on a longer run.
roadsText: The nearest service area to Omagh is Cohannon Services on the M1, about 42.8 km away in a straight line. Glenshane Tourist Services on the A6 is about 46.2 km away, and Temple Patrick Services Northbound on the M2 is about 83.2 km. Those distances are long for a driver in the BT78 district with a warning light, so check the road distance before setting off.

name: Ormskirk
intro: Ormskirk's market dates back to 1286, and the town is also known for Ormskirk gingerbread. This West Lancashire market town lies about 13 miles north-east of Liverpool and forms part of the wider Liverpool urban and commuting area, with rail services to Liverpool Central and to Preston. The L39 postcode district covers it. Maghull and Skelmersdale are both 6.7 km away, Kirkby 8.9 km and Southport 10.9 km. The M58 is the motorway listed for the area, alongside the A570, A59 and A577. If an AdBlue warning comes on, Old Meadow Services on the M58 is the closest stop at 5.6 km, and its fuel station is listed on OpenStreetMap as selling AdBlue at the pump.
roadsText: The M58 is listed around Ormskirk, with the A570, A59, A5209, A577, A506 and A5147. Old Meadow Services on the M58 is 5.6 km away; Charnock Richard Services on the M6 (14.8 km) and Earlsfield Services on the M57 (15.3 km) are next. The fuel station at Old Meadow is listed on OpenStreetMap as selling AdBlue at the pump, as is an HGV-only site in Liverpool. OpenStreetMap is not a complete record.

name: Orrell
intro: A suburb of Wigan, Orrell lies 3 miles west of Wigan town centre and is contiguous with Pemberton. The electoral ward also takes in parts of Billinge and Winstanley, and had a population of 11,513 at the 2011 Census. Orrell was historically in Lancashire and was once a centre of the coal mining industry, though no evidence of that industrial past remains today. The postcode district is WN5. Wigan is 4.4 km away, Skelmersdale 4.9 km, Ashton-in-Makerfield 6.8 km and Standish 7.1 km. For a driver with an AdBlue warning, three service areas lie between 10.9 km and 13.1 km away, on the M6, the M61 and the M58, and the fuel station at Old Meadow Services on the M58 is listed on OpenStreetMap as selling AdBlue at the pump.
roadsText: Around Orrell, the nearest service areas are Charnock Richard Services on the M6 at 10.9 km, Rivington Services on the M61 at 11.8 km and Old Meadow Services on the M58 at 13.1 km. The fuel station at Old Meadow is listed on OpenStreetMap as selling AdBlue at the pump, as are two Warrington sites (WA5 3TP at 14.2 km and WA3 6RW at 17.8 km); the map is not a complete record.

name: Ossett
intro: A market and residential town in the Wakefield district, Ossett sits between Dewsbury, Horbury and Wakefield and forms part of the Heavy Woollen District of West Yorkshire. It was historically in the West Riding of Yorkshire, and the 2021 census recorded 21,861 people living there. Its neighbours are close: Dewsbury is 3.9 km away on a direct line, Wakefield 4.6 km and East Ardsley 5.3 km, with Batley at 6.1 km. Everyday driving in and around Ossett can easily cross into other towns, and a vehicle that develops an AdBlue warning on a local run may be in Dewsbury or Wakefield by the time it needs attention. The town's postcode district is WF5. The nearest motorway service area is Woolley Edge on the M1, 6.7 km away.
roadsText: The nearest service area to Ossett is Woolley Edge on the M1, 6.7 km away on a direct line. Hartshead Moor on the M62 is 11.9 km away and Whitwood, also on the M62, is 12 km. OpenStreetMap lists stations with a Leeds address (12.5 km) and a Pontefract address (16.2 km) as selling AdBlue at the pump. Coverage in that source is incomplete.

name: Oswaldtwistle
intro: Oswaldtwistle, pronounced "ozzle twizzle", is a town in the Hyndburn borough of Lancashire, 3 miles south-east of Blackburn, and it is contiguous with Accrington. It had 10,815 residents in 2021. The town has a strong industrial heritage: it was home to James Hargreaves, inventor of the spinning jenny, and the Leeds and Liverpool Canal, which passes through the town, carried much of the area's cotton produce. Its postcode district is BB5, and Accrington is 2.7 km away. Great Harwood is 5 km off, Blackburn 5.5 km and Darwen 6.6 km. For an AdBlue warning, Blackburn with Darwen Services on the M65 is 6 km away, the closest of the listed service areas.
roadsText: Blackburn with Darwen Services on the M65 is the nearest service area to Oswaldtwistle at 6 km. Hollin Bank Service Station, also on the M65, is 15 km away, and Rivington Services on the M61 is 19.5 km. Accrington (2.7 km) and Blackburn (5.5 km) are the nearest neighbours, with Haslingden at 7.4 km.

name: Oswestry
intro: At the junction of the A5, A483 and A495, Oswestry (Croesoswallt) is an ancient market town, civil parish and historic railway town in Shropshire, five miles (8.0 km) from the Welsh border, with a mixed English and Welsh heritage. It was the administrative headquarters of the Borough of Oswestry until that was abolished in 2009, had 17,509 people at the 2021 Census, and is the largest settlement in the Oswestry Uplands natural area. SY11 is the postcode district. Nearby towns are some distance off: Rhosllannerchrugog is 16.7 km away, Wrexham 22.1 km and Shrewsbury 25.6 km. For a van or diesel car with an AdBlue warning, the A483 helps, with Mile End Services on it just 1.6 km away in a straight line.
roadsText: Oswestry is at the junction of the A5, A483 and A495. Mile End Services on the A483 is the nearest service area, only 1.6 km away in a straight line. Nesscliffe Services on the A5 is 12.6 km off and Ruabon Park Services, also on the A483, is 14.2 km. Road distances will be longer than these figures, but Mile End is close enough to be the natural place to pull in if an AdBlue warning comes on.

name: Otley
intro: The A660 connects Otley to Leeds, and this market town lies in lower Wharfedale at a bridging point on the River Wharfe. Otley is in the City of Leeds metropolitan borough and had 13,668 residents at the 2011 census. The town comes in two parts: historic Otley south of the river, and Newall, once a separate township, to the north. It sits in the Otley and Yeadon ward and uses the LS21 postcode district. Guiseley is about 3.7 km away, Yeadon 4.7 km, Baildon 8.5 km and Ilkley 9.2 km. For an AdBlue warning, the three nearest listed service areas are all between about 20.9 km and 21.8 km away in a straight line, on the M1, the A1(M) and the M62, so none of them is a short hop from the town.
roadsText: Otley is on the A660, the road that connects it to Leeds. The nearest service areas are at a similar straight-line distance: Skelton Lake Service Station on the M1 at about 20.9 km, with Wetherby Services on the A1(M) and Hartshead Moor Services on the M62 both at about 21.8 km. Which is quickest will depend on where in or around the town you start.

name: Oxford
intro: Set where the Thames, known locally as the Isis, meets the Cherwell, Oxford is a cathedral city and the county town of Oxfordshire. It had a population of 165,940 in 2025 and lies 56 miles (90 km) north-west of London and 64 miles (103 km) south-east of Birmingham. Alongside the university, its industries include motor manufacturing, publishing, science and information technologies. The city is covered by the OX1, OX2, OX3 and OX4 postcode districts. Every road listed for Oxford is an A road, including the A34, A40, A44 and A420, and the nearest listed motorway services are on the M40. Kidlington is 7.7 km away and Abingdon-on-Thames 8.8 km. For a driver with an AdBlue warning on the way in or out of the city, the closest listed service area is 4.6 km away.
roadsText: No motorway appears in the main road list for Oxford, which is made up of the A420, A34, A40, A423, A44, A4142, A4144 and A4165. Peartree Services on the A44 is the nearest listed service area, 4.6 km away. Oxford Services on the M40 is 11.3 km, and Thame Services on the A418 is 19.3 km. Peartree is the closest listed stop for a driver dealing with an AdBlue warning around the city.

name: Oxted
intro: Croydon, Sevenoaks and East Grinstead are each 9 miles (14 km) from Oxted, a commuter town at the foot of the North Downs in the Tandridge district of Surrey. Its main built-up area runs into the village of Limpsfield, and to the south the largely residential settlements of Hurst Green and Holland lie within the same civil parish. The headwaters of the River Eden meet in the town. Oxted is covered by the RH8 postcode district. Caterham is the nearest neighbouring town at 7.6 km, with Redhill at 12.1 km. Oxted is well placed for a driver facing an AdBlue warning: Clacket Lane Services on the M25 is only 4 km away in a straight line, much closer than the next options on the M23 and A23, which are both more than 22 km off.
roadsText: Clacket Lane Services on the M25, 4 km from Oxted in a straight line, is by far the nearest listed service area. The next two are much further: Pease Pottage Services on the M23 at 22.7 km and Handcross on the A23 at 25.3 km. For most drivers in RH8 the M25 site will be the obvious stop if an AdBlue warning comes on, though road distances will be longer than these figures.

name: Padiham
intro: On the River Calder in the Borough of Burnley, Padiham is a Lancashire market town with the foothills of Pendle Hill along its north-west and north-east edges. The parish counted 10,098 people at the 2011 census and an estimated 10,138 in 2019, and the town uses the BB12 postcode district. Burnley lies to the south-east, about 5.1 km away in a straight line, while Clayton le Moors and Great Harwood are to the south-west. Several towns sit within a short distance: Brierfield at 6 km, Great Harwood at 6.4 km, Accrington at 6.5 km, Nelson at 8 km and Oswaldtwistle at 8.7 km. If a van or diesel car flags an AdBlue warning here, the nearest service area is on the M65, about 6.4 km away, and a second on the same motorway is about 14.6 km out.
roadsText: Two of the three nearest service areas to Padiham are on the M65. Hollin Bank Service Station is about 6.4 km away in a straight line and Blackburn with Darwen Services about 14.6 km. The third, Birch Services on the M62, is about 26.3 km away. Straight-line figures understate the drive, so allow for a longer journey by road from the BB12 district.

name: Paignton
intro: Together with Torquay and Brixham, the seaside town of Paignton on Tor Bay makes up the Devon borough of Torbay, a holiday destination known as the English Riviera. The town grew from a small fishing village, gained a new harbour in 1847 and a passenger railway in 1859, and as its population increased it merged with the villages of Goodrington and Preston. It is around 40 km north-east of Plymouth and 32 km south of Exeter, and has a population of 67,509 across the TQ3 and TQ4 postcode districts. Brixham is 5 km away and Torquay 7.5 km, with Newton Abbot at 11.6 km and Teignmouth at 15.4 km. That makes most driving here a matter of short runs around the bay, with a longer trip needed to reach a motorway if an AdBlue warning appears on the way out.
roadsText: The main roads around Paignton are the A380, A385, A3022 and A379. There is no motorway close by: the nearest service area is Exeter services on the M5, 33.1 km away, with Saltash on the A388 at 47 km and Cullompton on the M5 at 50.4 km. Those distances are worth knowing before heading out of Torbay with a warning light on.

name: Paisley
intro: Often cited as Scotland's largest town, Paisley lies immediately west of Glasgow and north of the Gleniffer Braes, straddling the White Cart Water, a tributary of the River Clyde. It is the administrative centre for Renfrewshire and had 79,369 people in 2022, making it the fifth-largest settlement in Scotland. The PA1, PA2 and PA3 postcode districts cover the town. The M8 and M77 are both on the road list, along with the A8, A726, A736, A737, A741 and A761, so drivers have motorway and A-road options close by. Neighbours are close too: Renfrew is 4.5 km away, Barrhead 4.8 km and Johnstone 5.7 km, with Erskine at 7.2 km and Clydebank at 8 km. The nearest motorway service area is 23 km away, so the stations listed as selling AdBlue at the pump are worth knowing.
roadsText: Main roads recorded around Paisley are the M8, M77, A726, A737, A761, A741, A736 and A8. The nearest service areas are on the M74: Bothwell Services at 23 km and Hamilton Services at 25.1 km, with the M74 Truck Stop at 39.6 km. OpenStreetMap lists a station in Glasgow (7.9 km) and another site 15.7 km away as selling AdBlue at the pump, though that data is incomplete.

name: Patchway
intro: An overflow settlement for Bristol, Patchway is a town and civil parish in South Gloucestershire about 6 mi (9.7 km) north-north-west of the city centre. Like the nearby towns of Filton and Bradley Stoke, only 2 km and 2.1 km away, it is contiguous with Bristol's urban area. Patchway became a civil parish in its own right in 1953, separating from nearby Almondsbury. Two postcode districts cover it, BS34 and BS32. Stoke Gifford is 3.6 km off, and Frampton Cotterell and Winterbourne 6.6 km. If an AdBlue warning appears, three listed service areas lie within 10.8 km in a straight line, the closest being Avon Lodge on the A4 at 8.3 km and Severn View Services on the M48 at 8.5 km.
roadsText: Three listed service areas sit within 10.8 km of Patchway in a straight line, each on a different road: Avon Lodge on the A4 at 8.3 km, Severn View Services on the M48 at 8.5 km and Gordano Services on the M5 at 10.8 km. That gives drivers in BS34 and BS32 a choice depending on which way they are heading. Road distances will be longer than these figures.

name: Peacehaven
intro: Set above the chalk cliffs of the South Downs, Peacehaven is a town in the Lewes district of East Sussex, about 6 miles (10 km) east of Brighton city centre. It sits on the A259 road, and Telscombe Cliffs, a later western extension with its own parish and town council, adjoins it. The Greenwich meridian crosses the English south coast here. The town has a population of 15,705 and uses the BN10 postcode district. Newhaven is 3 km away, Seaford 7.9 km, Lewes 8.6 km and Brighton and Hove 9.4 km. For a diesel car or van with an AdBlue warning, the nearest listed service area is Polegate Services on the A22, 16.5 km away in a straight line, so services are not close by. Pyecombe Services on the A23 is a similar distance at 16.9 km. A station 10.3 km away is listed in OpenStreetMap as selling AdBlue at the pump.
roadsText: Peacehaven sits on the A259. The nearest service areas are Polegate Services on the A22 at 16.5 km in a straight line, Pyecombe Services on the A23 at 16.9 km and Ricebridge Services (Hickstead), also on the A23, at 23.5 km. A station 10.3 km away is listed in OpenStreetMap as selling AdBlue at the pump. The map is incomplete, so treat it as one option rather than the only one.

name: Pelsall
intro: Three miles (4.8 km) north of Walsall, Pelsall is a village in the Metropolitan Borough of Walsall and forms part of the borough's border with Staffordshire. It lies midway between Bloxwich and Brownhills, and in the 19th century it became a centre for coal mining and the site of an iron works. Today it is known for its commons, and the Wyrley and Essington Canal is nearby. The area has a population of 10,455 and is covered by the WS3 postcode district. For a van or diesel car with an AdBlue warning, Pelsall is well placed: three service areas lie within 8.4 km, on the M6 Toll, the M6 and the A5. Rushall and Shelfield is 2.6 km away, Bloxwich 2.8 km and Brownhills 3.1 km, with Aldridge at 4.2 km and Great Wyrley and Cheslyn Hay at 4.7 km.
roadsText: Norton Canes Services on the M6 Toll is the nearest service area to Pelsall, 3.8 km from the centre in a straight line. Hilton Park Services on the M6 is 5.9 km away and The Trucker's Rest on the A5 is 8.4 km. OpenStreetMap lists a station in Burntwood (WS7 3XA), 5.9 km away, and one in Warley, 14.7 km away, as selling AdBlue at the pump. That map data is incomplete, so other forecourts may stock it too.

name: Penarth
intro: About three miles (five kilometres) south of Cardiff city centre, Penarth sits on the west shore of the Severn Estuary at the southern end of Cardiff Bay. It is a seaside resort within the Cardiff Urban Area and the second largest town in the Vale of Glamorgan after Barry. These days it is mainly a dormitory town for Cardiff commuters, with a substantial retired population. Postcodes include CF64, CF11 and CF10. The road list is long for a town this size: the A48, A4160, A4055, A4232, A4119, A470, A4234 and A4161. Cardiff is about 6.4km away and Barry 6.7km. For a diesel car or van, much of the driving here is likely to be commuter traffic into and around Cardiff, and the two nearest motorway services are 11.2km and 11.4km out.
roadsText: Roads listed around Penarth are the A48, A4160, A4055, A4232, A4119, A470, A4234 and A4161, with no motorway among them. The two nearest service areas are almost the same distance away, both on the M4: Cardiff West services at about 11.2km and Cardiff Gate services at 11.4km. For a driver in CF64 with an AdBlue warning, either is a sensible place to aim for once it is safe to carry on.

name: Penicuik
intro: Penicuik is a Midlothian town and former burgh on the west bank of the River North Esk, east of the Pentland Hills. It lies on the A701, midway between Edinburgh and Peebles, so that road connects it to both. Its population is listed at 16,150 and it falls within the EH26 postcode district. Bonnyrigg is the nearest of the listed towns at 8.1 km, followed by Mayfield (11.3 km), Dalkeith (11.8 km) and Edinburgh (11.9 km), with Musselburgh at 15.7 km. For a van or diesel car with an AdBlue warning, the nearest service area is 7.3 km away, which makes a stop reasonably easy to reach from the town. Beyond that, the next service areas are on the A1.
roadsText: Penicuik lies on the A701, between Edinburgh and Peebles. The nearest service area is Dreghorn Services on the A720, 7.3 km away. Musselburgh Services on the A1 is 14.2 km off, and MacMerry, also on the A1, is 24.8 km. With the next stop 14.2 km away, that A720 stop is the one most drivers here will want to know.

name: Penrith
intro: Penrith's history was defined primarily by its strategic position on north-south and east-west communications routes. The market town lies less than 3 miles (5 km) outside the Lake District National Park and about 17 miles (27 km) south of Carlisle, between the Rivers Petteril and Eamont and just north of the River Lowther. It is a civil parish in the Westmorland and Furness unitary authority area of Cumbria, historically part of Cumberland, with 16,987 residents at the 2021 census. The CA11 postcode district covers the town. Other towns are a long way off: Kendal is about 37.6 km away and Workington 51.5 km. For a van or diesel car with an AdBlue warning, that distance is the key point, since the next town is not a short hop.
roadsText: The nearest service areas to Penrith are all on the M6. Southwaite Services is about 16.6 km away, Golden Fleece Service Station around 22.7 km and Tebay Services roughly 25.6 km. With the next towns also far away, drivers around Penrith and the CA11 district should expect a drive of at least 16.6 km to reach motorway services.

name: Penryn
intro: Beside the Penryn River, close to Falmouth, sits the west Cornwall town of Penryn, whose name comes from the Cornish Pennrynn, meaning promontory. At the 2021 census the parish had 8,489 residents and the wider built-up area, which extends beyond the parish boundary, had 11,195. The town is in the TR10 postcode district. Now overshadowed by its larger neighbour, Penryn was once an important harbour in its own right, shipping granite and tin in the medieval period. Falmouth is just 3 km away, Redruth 10.8 km, Truro 11.4 km and Helston 13.4 km. Service areas are far off: the nearest listed, Cornwall Services on the A30, is 35.5 km away in a straight line, which is worth knowing before a long run with an AdBlue warning lit.
roadsText: Cornwall Services on the A30 is the nearest service area to Penryn, 35.5 km away in a straight line. The next listed sites are much further: Saltash Services on the A388 at 68.2 km and Roundswell Service Area on the A39 at 123.1 km. Road distances will be longer again, so a driver in TR10 with an AdBlue warning should not count on passing services nearby.

name: Penwortham
intro: Penwortham faces the city of Preston from the south bank of the River Ribble. It is a town and civil parish in South Ribble, Lancashire, with 22,570 residents at the 2021 Census. The town stands at the most westerly crossing point of the river, where major road and rail links cross towards Preston. Its postcode district is PR1. Preston is 3.7 km away, Bamber Bridge 4.1 km, Longton 4.9 km, Fulwood 5 km and Leyland 5.7 km. If an AdBlue warning appears, the closest service area is Charnock Richard Services on the M6, 12.7 km away, with Blackburn with Darwen Services on the M65 at 16.9 km and Rivington Services on the M61 at 18.9 km.
roadsText: The nearest service areas to Penwortham are Charnock Richard Services on the M6 at 12.7 km, Blackburn with Darwen Services on the M65 at 16.9 km and Rivington Services on the M61 at 18.9 km. Major road links cross the Ribble at Penwortham, and Preston is 3.7 km away, with Euxton at 8.8 km.

name: Penzance
intro: Land's End is only 9 miles (14 km) west of Penzance, a town and port in the shelter of Mount's Bay, facing south-east onto the English Channel. It is 255 miles (410 km) west-south-west of London and 64 miles (103 km) west-south-west of Plymouth, and its railway station is the terminus of the Cornish Main Line. The parish also takes in the fishing port of Newlyn and the villages of Mousehole, Paul, Gulval and Heamoor, and had 20,734 residents at the 2021 census. Penzance is covered by the TR18 postcode district. Helston is the nearest listed town at 19.7 km, with Camborne at 20.6 km and Redruth at 26 km. An AdBlue warning here needs some thought, because the listed service areas are very distant: the nearest, Cornwall Services on the A30, is 61.9 km away in a straight line.
roadsText: Listed service areas are a long way from Penzance. The nearest listed one is Cornwall Services on the A30, 61.9 km away in a straight line, followed by Saltash Services on the A388 at 98.7 km and Roundswell Service Area on the A39 at 147 km. For drivers in TR18, a services stop is not a quick answer to an AdBlue warning, so it is worth acting on one early.

name: Perth
intro: Raised slightly above the flood plain of the River Tay on a natural mound, Perth is a central Scottish city and the administrative centre of Perth and Kinross. It is also the historic county town of Perthshire and had 47,893 people in 2022. The PH1 and PH2 postcode districts cover the city. For drivers, Perth's road list stands out: the M90, A9, A90, A85, A93 and A94 all feature, along with the A912 and A989. The nearest listed towns are some way off. Glenrothes is 28.3 km away and Dundee 31.3 km, with Kirkcaldy and Dysart at 35.3 km and Dunfermline at 36.6 km. That spacing makes it worth knowing where the nearest services are before an AdBlue warning becomes urgent.
roadsText: Main roads recorded around Perth are the M90, A85, A9, A90, A93, A912, A989 and A94. Kinross Services on the M90 is the nearest service area at 21 km. Balhaldie Services on the A9 is 34.4 km away and Forfar Services on the A90 is 41.9 km. All three sit on roads that also appear on Perth's own road list.

name: Peterborough
intro: Designated a new town in the 1960s, Peterborough is a cathedral city on the River Nene in the ceremonial county of Cambridgeshire, 74 miles (119 km) north of London. Its urban area had 192,178 residents at the 2021 census, and financial services and distribution are now its main economic sectors. For drivers, the A1 and A1(M) are the key references: both are among the main roads, along with the A15, A16, A47, A605, A1139 and A1260. Postcode districts include PE1 to PE5 and PE7. Whittlesey is about 9.5 km away and Stamford 17.9 km, while Bourne, March, Spalding and Chatteris are all between about 23 km and 25 km. Three service areas on the A1 and A1(M) are within about 9.3 km, so a driver with a low-AdBlue message has several places to pull in.
roadsText: Main roads around Peterborough include the A1, A1(M), A15, A16, A47, A605, A1139 and A1260. The nearest service areas are Welcome Break Kate's Cabin on the A1, about 5.7 km away, Peterborough Services on the A1(M) at 6.1 km, and Stibbington Diner Lorry Park on the A1 at 9.3 km. OpenStreetMap lists a Shell at about 6.2 km, an Esso (PE8 6TZ) at 13.4 km and a BP near Bourne at 18.6 km as selling AdBlue at the pump; that list is incomplete.

name: Peterhead
intro: At the easternmost point of mainland Scotland, Peterhead is the largest settlement in Aberdeenshire, with 19,791 people at the 2022 Census. It is the busiest fishing port in the United Kingdom for total landings by UK vessels, according to a 2019 survey, and is often referred to as the Blue Toun. The AB42 postcode district covers the town. Distance is the main thing a driver here needs to keep in mind: Ellon is 22.6 km away and Fraserburgh 23.9 km, while Inverurie is 42.6 km and Aberdeen 43.8 km. The nearest service area is 63.1 km off, so an AdBlue warning is best dealt with early rather than left for a long run. On OpenStreetMap, the closest station listed as selling AdBlue at the pump is in Mintlaw, 12 km away.
roadsText: The nearest service areas are a long way from Peterhead: Ashgrove Services on the A96 is 63.1 km away, Elgin Services on the A96 is 88.3 km and Stracathro Services on the A90 is 95 km. Closer to town, OpenStreetMap lists a station in Mintlaw (AB42 5EL), 12 km away, as selling AdBlue at the pump. That map data is incomplete, so check locally too.

name: Peterlee
intro: Town status came to Peterlee in 1948 under the New Towns Act 1946, the same legislation that created nearby Newton Aycliffe and Washington. It lies in County Durham, west of the Durham Coast and east of Durham, with Sunderland to the north and Hartlepool to the south. The town has a population of 19,750 and sits in the SR8 postcode district. Seaham is the nearest neighbouring town at 8.5 km, followed by Hartlepool at 11.9 km and Houghton-le-Spring at 12 km, with Durham 14.6 km away and Sunderland 16.5 km. Those distances mean many journeys from Peterlee are runs between towns rather than short hops. The A19 is close by, with Easington services on it just 4.9 km away, so for a van or diesel car the A19 is likely to feature in plenty of trips.
roadsText: Easington services on the A19 is 4.9 km from Peterlee, and a southbound service area on the same road is 12 km away. Durham services on the A1(M) is 11.7 km. One station with a Durham postcode (DH6 3LJ), 4.8 km from the town, is listed in OpenStreetMap as selling AdBlue at the pump. Map data like this is incomplete, so other local forecourts may also sell it.

name: Petersfield
intro: Petersfield grew as a coach stop on the Portsmouth to London route, at the crossroads of a north to south road and an east to west one. The north to south route was formerly the A3, which now passes around the town, and the east to west route is today the A272. This East Hampshire market town lies 15 miles (24 km) north of Portsmouth, below the northern slopes of the South Downs and wholly within the South Downs National Park. It has a population of 14,994 and covers the GU32 and GU31 postcode districts. For a driver with an AdBlue warning, Petersfield Services on the A3 is just 1.2 km from the town in a straight line. Neighbouring towns are more spread out: Horndean is 11.9 km away, Waterlooville 15.7 km, and Alton and Havant both 16.7 km.
roadsText: Petersfield Services on the A3 sits 1.2 km from the town in a straight line, the closest listed service area by a wide margin.
