Liphook Services, also on the A3, is 11.8 km away, and Farlington Services on the A27 is 20.3 km. The A3 once ran through Petersfield but now passes around it, while the A272 carries the east to west route.

name: Platt Bridge and Abram
intro: This part of the Metropolitan Borough of Wigan covers Platt Bridge and neighbouring Abram, with a population of 10,587. Platt Bridge lies 2 miles (3.2 km) south of Wigan town centre along the spine of the A573 road. It was historically part of the Hindley Urban District in Lancashire and is now a residential suburb of Wigan. It borders Abram, Bamfurlong, Hindley and Ince-in-Makerfield, and a brook running under the A58 marks its boundary with Bamfurlong. The West Coast Main Line passes through. The postcode district is WN2. In a straight line, Ince-in-Makerfield is about 2.2 km away and Hindley 2.4 km, with Ashton-in-Makerfield at 4 km, Leigh and Wigan at 4.7 km each and Golborne at 5.2 km. For an AdBlue warning, three motorway service areas lie between about 9.1 km and 13.9 km away, on the M61, M62 and M6.
roadsText: The A573 runs through Platt Bridge, and the A58 crosses its boundary with Bamfurlong. Rivington Services on the M61 is the nearest service area, about 9.1 km away in a straight line, with Burtonwood Services on the M62 at 11.6 km and Charnock Richard Services on the M6 at 13.9 km. OpenStreetMap lists two sites in Warrington, one at WA3 6RW about 12 km away and one at WA5 3TP about 12.8 km away, as selling AdBlue at the pump. The mapping is incomplete, so there may be others.

name: Plymouth
intro: Between the rivers Plym and Tamar on Devon's south coast, Plymouth is the most populous settlement in the county and a port city with a long naval history; a dockyard for the Royal Navy was established on the Tamar in 1690. It lies 58 km south-west of Exeter and 311 km south-west of London, and it absorbed nearby settlements in 1914 before gaining city status in 1928. Postcode districts across the city include PL1, PL2, PL3, PL4, PL5, PL6, PL7 and PL9, and the population is 266,970. Saltash is 7.2 km away, Ivybridge 14.3 km and Tavistock 16.6 km, with Liskeard at 24.7 km. Distance matters for drivers here: the nearest motorway service area is 58.7 km away near Exeter, so a diesel van or car with an AdBlue warning is usually dealing with it on the city's A roads rather than close to a motorway.
roadsText: The main roads around Plymouth are the A38, A386, A3822, A374, A3860, A3064 and A379. Saltash services on the A388 is the closest service area at 8.3 km. Beyond that, Cornwall services on the A30 is 49.1 km away and Exeter services on the M5 is 58.7 km, so it pays to deal with a warning before setting off on a long run.

name: Pocklington
intro: All Saints' parish church has a 15th-century tower that marks the skyline of Pocklington, a market town and civil parish at the foot of the Yorkshire Wolds in the East Riding of Yorkshire. It lies 13 miles (21 km) east of York and 22 miles (35 km) north-west of Hull, and had 10,123 residents at the 2021 census. The town uses the YO42 postcode district. Its nearest neighbours are some way off: Huntington is about 19.5 km away, York 20.4 km, Haxby 21.4 km and Driffield 24.1 km. That distance applies to services too. The nearest listed service area is Bilbrough Top on the A64, about 26.7 km in a straight line, so a driver with an AdBlue warning should not expect a short trip.
roadsText: Service areas are some distance from Pocklington. In a straight line, the nearest listed are Bilbrough Top Service Area on the A64 at about 26.7 km, Wetherby Services on the A1(M) at 38.6 km and Doncaster (North) Services on the M180 at 40 km. Road distances will be longer than these straight-line figures, so it is worth planning which to use.

name: Polegate
intro: In 2011 the census put the population of Polegate's civil parish at 8,586, with 41.2% of residents aged 65 and over. The town, in the Wealden District of East Sussex, is part of the greater Eastbourne area and falls in the BN26 postcode district. Eastbourne is 4.2 km away and Hailsham 5.1 km, while Seaford, Newhaven and Bexhill-on-Sea are all between 10.5 km and 14.5 km off, and Peacehaven is 17 km. For anyone driving a van or diesel car here, the town has a service area almost on its doorstep: Polegate Services on the A22 is 1.2 km away in a straight line. That is worth knowing, because the next listed service areas, both on the A23, are more than 30 km away.
roadsText: Polegate Services on the A22 is the nearest listed service area to Polegate, just 1.2 km away in a straight line. After that the options are a long way off: Pyecombe Services on the A23 at 30.6 km and Ricebridge Services at Hickstead, also on the A23, at 34.8 km. For drivers in BN26 with an AdBlue warning, the A22 site is the practical stop.

name: Pontefract
intro: East of Wakefield and south of Castleford, the historic market town of Pontefract is part of the City of Wakefield district in West Yorkshire and had 30,881 residents at the 2011 Census. Its Latin motto refers to the town's Royalist sympathies in the English Civil War. For drivers, what stands out is how many major routes run close by. The M62, A1(M) and A1 are all among the main roads listed, alongside the A645, A639, A628, A162 and A638, and three service areas lie within 8.7 km as the crow flies, which helps if an AdBlue warning appears. The town's postcode district is WF8. Featherstone is 3.6 km away and Castleford 3.8 km, with Normanton at 6.9 km, so local trips quickly cross into neighbouring towns. Small villages and settlements in the immediate area include Stapleton.
roadsText: Main roads around Pontefract include the M62, A1(M) and A1, plus the A645, A639, A628, A162 and A638. Ferrybridge services on the M62 is 2.9 km away as the crow flies, Whitwood services on the M62 is 6.4 km and Barnsdale Bar on the A1 is 8.7 km. OpenStreetMap lists a station with a Pontefract address, 5.5 km away, and one with a Leeds address, 14 km away, as selling AdBlue at the pump. That source does not cover every forecourt.

name: Ponteland
intro: Just outside Newcastle upon Tyne and near the airport, Ponteland is a Northumberland town and civil parish on the edge of rural countryside, 13 km north-west of the city. It was built on marshland near St Mary's Church and the old bridge, and most of that marshland has since been drained for housing. The settlement grew with the development of Darras Hall, and the parish now covers the old village of Ponteland, the Darras Hall estate and the villages of Kirkley, Medburn, Milbourne and Prestwick. Ponteland is in the NE20 postcode district and has a population of 10,149. Newcastle upon Tyne is 8.9 km away, Blaydon 9.8 km and Prudhoe 10.7 km, with Cramlington, Killingworth and Whickham all within 11.9 km. Driving here mixes the surrounding countryside with runs towards Newcastle.
roadsText: Seaton Burn on the A19 is the closest service area to Ponteland, 8.5 km away. The next nearest are much further: Washington services on the A1(M) at 21.2 km and Easington on the A19 at 36.8 km. A station in Newcastle upon Tyne, 10.4 km from the town, is listed in OpenStreetMap as selling AdBlue at the pump. OpenStreetMap is incomplete, so other forecourts may sell it.

name: Pontypool
intro: In 2021, 29,062 people lived in Pontypool, the administrative centre of the county borough of Torfaen, within the historic boundaries of Monmouthshire in South Wales. The town uses the NP4 postcode district. The roads listed around it are all A-roads: the A4042, A472, A4043 and A4051. Cwmbrân is the closest neighbour at about 4.7km, followed by Abertillery at 9.2km, Risca at 10.6km and Newport at 12.2km, with Blackwood and Abergavenny a little further. For a diesel driver, local journeys here will often be short hops between those towns. No service area is close: the nearest three are all between 17.2km and 18.4km away, split between the A40 and the M4, so an AdBlue warning is best dealt with by planning the stop rather than hoping one turns up.
roadsText: No motorway appears on Pontypool's road list, which is made up of the A4042, A472, A4043 and A4051. The three nearest service areas are at similar distances: Monmouth A40 services at about 17.2km, Magor services on the M4 at 17.4km and Cardiff Gate services, also on the M4, at 18.4km. From NP4, any of the three is a realistic target if an AdBlue warning needs a planned stop.

name: Pontypridd
intro: Church Village is only about 4.7km from Pontypridd, with Porth at 5.1km, Tonyrefail at 7.3km, and Caerphilly and Ystrad Mynach around 8km. Often called Ponty, the town and community in Rhondda Cynon Taf lies roughly 10 miles (16km) north-west of Cardiff city centre. It has a population of 31,895, and its postcode district is CF37. It has a long list of A-roads around it: the A470, A4054, A4223, A4058, A473, A4233, A4059 and A472 all appear, but no motorway. With neighbours that close, Pontypridd is a place of short connecting journeys for most van and diesel car drivers. The nearest motorway services are a little over 10km away, close enough to plan for if an AdBlue warning comes up on the way out of town.
roadsText: Listed roads around Pontypridd are the A470, A4054, A4223, A4058, A473, A4233, A4059 and A472. The three closest service areas are all on the M4: Cardiff West services at about 10.9km, Cardiff Gate services at 15.9km and Sarn Park services at 18.6km. For a driver in CF37, Cardiff West is the nearest planned stop if an AdBlue warning appears.

name: Poole
intro: Visitors come to Poole for its large natural harbour and Blue Flag beaches, and the south-coast seaport began to emerge as an important port in the 12th century. It adjoins Bournemouth to the east and lies 34 km east of Dorchester. With an estimated 143,418 people in 2024, it is the second-largest town in the ceremonial county of Dorset, and together with Bournemouth and Christchurch it forms a conurbation of 400,196. Postcode districts include BH11, BH12, BH13, BH14, BH15, BH17 and BH18, along with BH4. Corfe Mullen is 6.4 km away, Wimborne Minster 8.8 km and Ferndown 9.5 km, with Christchurch the furthest of the nearby towns at 14.8 km. For a diesel van or car, the neighbouring towns are all within 15 km, but the nearest service areas are more than 20 km out.
roadsText: Poole's main roads include the A35, A350, A3049, A338, A348, A3040, A349 and A347. The nearest service areas are some distance away: Picket Post on the A31 at 21.3 km, Rufus Stone on the A31 at 30.6 km and West Wellow on the A36 at 38.9 km. Closer to home, a forecourt at Creekmoor (BH17 7FR), 3.1 km away, is listed as selling AdBlue at the pump in OpenStreetMap data. The map data is incomplete, so it may not be the only one.

name: Port Glasgow
intro: Founded in 1668 as a remote port for Glasgow, because large ships could not navigate the shallow and meandering River Clyde to the city centre, Port Glasgow is now the second-largest town in the Inverclyde council area. It sits immediately east of Greenock and was formerly a burgh in Renfrewshire. The population has fallen over recent decades, from 19,426 in 1991 to 16,617 in 2001 and 15,414 in 2011. The town grew outwards from its historic centre and up the steep hills inland, where areas such as Park Farm, Boglestone, Slaemuir, Devol and Oronsay were built, so local driving involves some steep climbs. The postcode district is PA14. Dumbarton is about 7.1 km away in a straight line and Helensburgh 9.5 km. A station about 7.6 km away is listed as selling AdBlue at the pump, but the nearest service area is about 40 km off.
roadsText: Port Glasgow is a long way from a motorway service area. Bothwell Services on the M74 is about 40 km away in a straight line, Hamilton Services on the M74 about 42.6 km and Stirling Services on the M9 about 49.4 km. OpenStreetMap lists a station about 7.6 km away as selling AdBlue at the pump, though that data is incomplete and other forecourts may stock it.

name: Port Talbot
intro: A large steelworks dominates the south east of Port Talbot, an industrial port town in the county borough of Neath Port Talbot. It sits on the east side of Swansea Bay, about 8 miles (13km) from Swansea, and its population was 31,550 in 2021. The SA12 and SA13 postcode districts cover it. The M4 is on the local road list, along with the A483, A4241, A48, A4107 and A474. Baglan is about 4.7km away, Neath 8km, Maesteg 9.6km and Pyle 10.2km, with Swansea at 11.2km and Porthcawl 13.6km. Driving here can range from short runs around an industrial town to longer journeys on the M4. If an AdBlue warning comes on, the nearest motorway services are between 16km and 25.6km away, so it is worth knowing which one to aim for.
roadsText: For Port Talbot, the listed roads are the M4, A483, A4241, A48, A4107 and A474. Its three nearest service areas are all on the M4: Sarn Park services at about 16km, Swansea West services at 17.1km and Pont Abraham services at 25.6km. Sarn Park and Swansea West are close to the same distance, so either is a realistic stop for a driver in SA12 or SA13.

name: Porth
intro: The Welsh word "porth" means "gate", and the name fits: Porth sits in the Rhondda Valley where the Rhondda Fawr and Rhondda Fach valleys meet, and it is regarded as the gateway connecting the two. It is a town and community in the county borough of Rhondda Cynon Taf, within the historic county boundaries of Glamorgan. Neighbouring villages include Trealaw, Trebanog, Trehafod and Ynyshir, and the town falls in the CF39 postcode district. Nearby towns are closely spaced: Tonypandy is 3.5 km away, Tonyrefail 4 km, Pontypridd 5.1 km and Rhondda 5.8 km, with Church Village at 7.9 km and Mountain Ash at 8.1 km. The motorway is further off. The nearest listed service area is 13.4 km away in a straight line on the M4, so there is no motorway stop close at hand if an AdBlue warning comes on in the valley.
roadsText: The three nearest service areas to Porth are all on the M4. Cardiff West Services is 13.4 km away in a straight line, Sarn Park Services 14.6 km and Cardiff Gate Services 20.8 km. Road distances will be longer than these figures. With none of them close to the town, it is worth planning a stop before an AdBlue warning becomes urgent rather than relying on reaching the motorway.

name: Porthcawl
intro: Set on a low limestone headland overlooking the Bristol Channel, Porthcawl is a coastal town in Bridgend County Borough, 25 miles (40 km) west of Cardiff and 19 miles (31 km) south-east of Swansea. It developed as a coal port in the 19th century before that trade moved to more rapidly developing ports such as Barry. North-west of the town, in the dunes of Kenfig Burrows, are the remains of Kenfig Castle. The town has a population of 15,797 and is covered by the CF36 postcode district. Pyle is the nearest town at 5 km, with Bridgend at 9.3 km, Sarn at 9.9 km and Port Talbot at 13.6 km. If a van or diesel car shows an AdBlue warning, Welcome Break Sarn Park Services on the M4 is the closest listed service area, 9.8 km away in a straight line.
roadsText: Welcome Break Sarn Park Services on the M4 is the nearest service area to Porthcawl, 9.8 km from the town in a straight line. The other two listed are also on the M4 but much further away: Moto Cardiff West Services at 26.9 km and Moto Swansea West Services at 29.9 km. For drivers in CF36, the Sarn Park site is the realistic first stop.

name: Portishead
intro: Facing Cardiff and Newport across the Severn Estuary, Portishead is a North Somerset town 13 km west of Bristol with a population of 26,366 at the 2021 Census. It has a long history as a fishing port and expanded rapidly around its docks during the early 19th century. A power station and chemical works were added in the 20th century, but the dock and industrial facilities have since closed and been redeveloped into a marina and residential areas. The BS20 postcode district covers the town. Nailsea is 5.9 km away and Clevedon 8.3 km, while Bristol, Filton and Patchway are between 13 km and 14.3 km. The M5 is among the main roads near the town, along with the A403, A4 and A369, so motorway driving is close to hand for vans and diesel cars based here.
roadsText: Portishead's main roads are the M5, A403, A4 and A369. Gordano services on the M5 is the nearest service area at 4.3 km, and Avon Lodge on the A4 is 6.1 km away. Having two stops this close makes it easy to pull in if a warning appears at the start of a longer trip.

name: Portsmouth
intro: Most of Portsmouth sits on Portsea Island in the Solent, which makes it the only city in England not located primarily on the mainland. It is also the most densely populated city in the United Kingdom, with a population last recorded at 208,100, and it has been home to a significant Royal Navy dockyard and base for centuries. Postcode districts include PO1 to PO6, with PO12 and PO16 also listed. Roads listed for the area include the M275, M27, A3(M) and A27, and the city sits 22 miles (35 km) south-east of Southampton. Gosport is 5.9 km away, Waterlooville 6.9 km and Havant 7.3 km. If an AdBlue warning comes on, a listed service area just 2.8 km away is about as close as it gets.
roadsText: Three motorways are listed for Portsmouth, the M275, M27 and A3(M), along with the A27, A3, A2030, A2047 and A288. Farlington Services on the A27 is the nearest listed service area, just 2.8 km away. Petersfield Services on the A3 is 22.4 km and Rownhams Services on the M27 is 30.1 km. With Farlington so close, it is the obvious first stop to check.

name: Potters Bar
intro: Thirteen miles (21 km) north of central London, Potters Bar is a Hertfordshire town in the Hertsmere district and part of the London commuter belt. It was in Middlesex until 1965 and stayed a small, mainly agricultural settlement until the Great Northern Railway arrived in 1850. In 2022 the population was around 23,325. The town is made up of four wards, Bentley Heath & The Royds, Furzefield, Oakmere and Parkfield, and the first of these takes in outlying hamlets such as Bentley Heath and Ganwick Corner. Its postcode district is EN6. For anyone whose van or diesel car shows an AdBlue warning, the useful fact is that South Mimms Services on the A1(M) is only 3 km from the centre, with London Gateway Services on the M1 at 9.3 km. Borehamwood, Hatfield, Enfield and Barnet are all within 9.4 km.
roadsText: The nearest service area to Potters Bar is South Mimms Services on the A1(M), 3 km from the town centre in a straight line. London Gateway Services on the M1 is 9.3 km away and Bourne End Services on the A41 is 24.4 km away. With South Mimms so close, the A1(M) site is the obvious reference point for drivers in EN6 looking for somewhere to stop.

name: Poulton-le-Fylde
intro: Poulton-le-Fylde, usually shortened to Poulton, is a market town on the Fylde coastal plain and the administrative centre of the Borough of Wyre. It had 18,115 residents at the 2021 census and is part of the Blackpool Urban Area, roughly 5 miles from Blackpool town centre. The town has deep roots: the church of St Chad was recorded in 1094, and in the post-medieval period Poulton was an important commercial centre, trading through two harbours on the River Wyre, until its importance waned as Fleetwood and Blackpool developed. FY6 is its postcode district. Thornton is 3.3 km away and Cleveleys 5.1 km, with Fleetwood at 7.7 km. Motorway services are a longer trip: if an AdBlue warning comes on, the nearest listed service area is 19 km away.
roadsText: Service areas are some distance from Poulton-le-Fylde. Lancaster Services on the M6 is the nearest at 19 km, followed by Charnock Richard Services on the M6 at 30.8 km and Blackburn with Darwen Services on the M65 at 36.3 km. Thornton (3.3 km), Blackpool (6.4 km) and Fleetwood (7.7 km) are the closest towns.

name: Poynton
intro: Eleven miles (18 km) south-east of Manchester, on the easternmost fringe of the Cheshire Plain, Poynton is a town in the civil parish of Poynton-with-Worth, in Cheshire East. It is also 7 miles (11 km) north of Macclesfield and 5 miles (8 km) south of Stockport. Coal was mined here from the 16th century, and in the late 20th century Poynton became a commuter town for Manchester, with the population reaching 14,260 by 2011. The SK12 postcode district covers the town. Hazel Grove is the closest neighbour at about 3 km, with Bramhall at 3.4 km and Cheadle Hulme at 5.5 km. Marple is around 6.1 km away, and Stockport and Cheadle both 7.5 km. For a van or diesel car with an AdBlue warning, the nearest motorway service areas are on the M6, about 19.5 km away.
roadsText: Knutsford Services on the M6 is the nearest service area to Poynton, about 19.5 km away, with Tabley Hill Service Station, also on the M6, at around 20.3 km. Birch Services on the M62 is roughly 25.5 km off. OpenStreetMap has a site about 19 km away listed as selling AdBlue at the pump. Those records are incomplete, so stations closer to Poynton may also sell it.

name: Prescot
intro: Prescot marks the start of the A58, which runs all the way from this Knowsley town to Wetherby, near Leeds in West Yorkshire. A town and civil parish in Merseyside, it lies about 8 miles east of Liverpool city centre. The town is served by Prescot railway station and by Eccleston Park station in neighbouring Eccleston. It falls within the L35, L34 and L36 postcode districts and has close neighbours, including Huyton with Roby at 4.4 km, St Helens at 4.7 km and Widnes at 6.3 km. The M62 and M57 are both listed among the roads nearby, plus the A57, A580 and A5300. That matters when an AdBlue warning shows up, because the closest service area, Earlsfield Services on the M57, is only 2.8 km away.
roadsText: The M62 and M57 are the motorways listed for Prescot, along with the A57, A58, A570, A557, A5300 and A580. Earlsfield Services on the M57 is 2.8 km away, Burtonwood Services on the M62 9.9 km and Old Meadow Services on the M58 13.4 km. OpenStreetMap lists the station at Old Meadow and a site in Warrington (WA5 3TP), 8.4 km away, as selling AdBlue at the pump; an HGV-only refuelling site in Liverpool (L5 9XN) is also listed. The map data is not exhaustive.

name: Prestatyn
intro: Historically part of Flintshire, Prestatyn is now a seaside town and community in Denbighshire, on the Irish Sea coast to the east of Rhyl. It has a population of 19,085, and the town is covered by the LL19 postcode district. Rhyl is the nearest town at 4.8 km, while Flint is 20.5 km away and Colwyn Bay 22.5 km. For a van or diesel car with an AdBlue warning, the A55 is the road that matters here: all three of the nearest listed service areas are on it. Singing Kettle Services is 9.4 km away in a straight line and Kinmel Park Services 10.1 km, so two options lie at a similar distance, while the third, Chester West Services, is 26.8 km off. A station in Rhyl is also listed as selling AdBlue at the pump, at 10 km.
roadsText: Every listed service area near Prestatyn is on the A55. Singing Kettle Services is the closest at 9.4 km in a straight line, followed by Kinmel Park Services at 10.1 km and Chester West Services at 26.8 km. OpenStreetMap lists an Esso station in Rhyl (LL18 5XE), 10 km away, as selling AdBlue at the pump. The map data is incomplete, so other forecourts may also stock it.

name: Preston
intro: As the administrative centre of Lancashire, Preston sits on the north bank of the River Ribble and gained city status in 2002. The south bank of the Ribble is part of the Preston urban area but forms the separate South Ribble borough, so an address just across the river may fall under a different council. The city had 147,835 people at the 2021 census, and the wider Preston Built-up Area 313,322. Three motorways appear on the road list, the M6, M55 and M61, with the A6, A5085, A59, A583 and A5072. Postcode districts PR1 and PR2 are listed. Fulwood is just 2.4 km away, Penwortham 3.7 km and Bamber Bridge 5 km, with Longton and Leyland both at 8.5 km and Euxton at 11.1 km. For a van with an AdBlue warning, it helps to know that the nearest listed service area is 15.6 km away, on the M6.
roadsText: Preston's main roads include the M6, M55 and M61, plus the A6, A5085, A59, A583 and A5072. The nearest service areas listed are Charnock Richard Services on the M6 at 15.6 km, Blackburn with Darwen Services on the M65 at 16 km and Rivington Services on the M61 at 20.8 km. All three are on motorways, so reaching any of them from PR1 or PR2 means a motorway run.

name: Prestonpans
intro: About eight miles east of Edinburgh, Prestonpans is a mining town in East Lothian, known in Scots as The Pans and famous for murals depicting local history. Its population was 10,460 in 2020, and it lies near the site of the 1745 Battle of Prestonpans. The town is in the EH32 postcode district. Distances between towns are short here: Tranent is just 2.4 km away and Musselburgh 4.8 km, with Dalkeith at 8.8 km and Haddington at 12.1 km. That closeness carries over to the listed service areas. Two of them sit at the same 6.1 km distance from the town, both on the A1, which gives a driver with an AdBlue warning more than one nearby option rather than a single long run to the nearest stop.
roadsText: Two service areas on the A1 are listed at the same distance from Prestonpans, 6.1 km: MacMerry and Musselburgh Services. Dreghorn Services on the A720 is further out at 17 km. With both A1 stops so close, a driver who sees an AdBlue warning around Prestonpans has two listed options within a short drive.

name: Prestwich
intro: Three miles north of both Manchester and Salford, and five miles south of Bury, Prestwich has grown in popularity as a commuter town for Manchester. It is in the borough of Bury and historically sat within Lancashire, as the seat of the ancient parish of Prestwich-cum-Oldham. The oldest part of the town, around Bury New Road, is known as Prestwich Village. Postcode districts M25, M45, M7 and M8 cover the area, and Whitefield is only 2.4 km away, with Clifton at 3.3 km and Salford at 4.2 km. Five motorways are listed among the roads nearby: the M60, M62, M66, M602 and M61. For a driver with an AdBlue warning, the most useful fact is close to home, since a station 1.3 km away, at M25 3AJ, is listed on OpenStreetMap as selling AdBlue at the pump.
roadsText: Prestwich has the M60, M62, M66, M602 and M61 listed nearby, plus the A56, A665 and A576. Birch Services on the M62 is the nearest service area at 5.2 km; Rivington Services on the M61 (21.3 km) and Lymm Services on the M6 (24.3 km) are further out. On OpenStreetMap, a station at M25 3AJ, 1.3 km away, is listed as selling AdBlue at the pump, as is another 8.7 km away. The map is not a complete record, so check before relying on it.

name: Prestwick
intro: Glasgow Prestwick Airport sits on the outskirts of Prestwick, handling passenger flights and international cargo flights. The town itself is a former royal burgh on the Firth of Clyde coast in South Ayrshire, adjoining the larger town of Ayr, whose centre is about two miles (three kilometres) to the south, with the small village of Monkton to the north. It had 14,570 residents in 2022 and was the first home of the Open Golf Championship, played on the Prestwick Old Course from 1860 to 1872. The KA9 and KA8 postcode districts cover the town. Troon is about 7 km away in a straight line, and Irvine and Kilmarnock are both about 14.8 km off. Motorway service areas are distant, the closest about 48.1 km away on the M74, which matters if an AdBlue warning comes on.
roadsText: The nearest service areas to Prestwick are all on the M74 and a long way off: the M74 Truck Stop is about 48.1 km away in a straight line, Hamilton Services about 48.5 km and Bothwell Services about 49.4 km. Road distances from the KA9 and KA8 districts will be longer, so a warning light here is best dealt with before a long trip.

name: Prudhoe
intro: The second largest town in the Tyne Valley after Hexham, Prudhoe sits on a steep, north-facing hill on the south bank of the River Tyne in the south of Northumberland. It is 18 km west of Newcastle upon Tyne and had a population of 11,675 at the 2011 census. Villages around it include Ovingham, Ovington, Wylam, Stocksfield, Hedley on the Hill and Mickley, and the town is covered by the NE42 postcode district. Blaydon is 9.2 km away, Ponteland 10.7 km, Whickham 10.8 km and Consett 12.2 km, with Newcastle upon Tyne at 13.8 km and Stanley at 14.5 km. Trips from Prudhoe to neighbouring towns are therefore at least a few kilometres long, and the nearest service area is 18.1 km away.
roadsText: Prudhoe's nearest service area is Seaton Burn on the A19, 18.1 km away, with Washington services on the A1(M) at 20.1 km and Durham services at 33.1 km. A station in Newcastle upon Tyne, 18.4 km from the town, is listed in OpenStreetMap as selling AdBlue at the pump. That map data is incomplete, so there may be closer places to buy it.

name: Pudsey
intro: Midway between Bradford city centre and Leeds city centre, Pudsey is a market town within the City of Leeds and historically part of the West Riding of Yorkshire. Its population is given as 25,393. That halfway position is the main thing to know when driving here. Bradford is 5.9 km away measured directly and Leeds 8 km, and the postcode districts reflect the split, with LS28 and LS13 alongside BD3. Other nearby places include Gomersal and Birkenshaw at 5.6 km, Shipley at 6.7 km and Yeadon at 7.3 km. Every main road listed around the town is an A road, among them the A647, A6120, A6110 and A6177, and no motorway appears in that list. For a van or diesel car showing an AdBlue fault, that means the nearest motorway service area is 11 km away rather than on the doorstep.
roadsText: Main roads around Pudsey include the A647, A6120, A6110, A6177, A658, A650, A657 and A6176. The nearest service area is Hartshead Moor on the M62, 11 km away measured directly, followed by Skelton Lake Service Station on the M1 at 13.8 km and Whitwood on the M62 at 20.7 km. OpenStreetMap lists a station with a Leeds address, 13.9 km away, as selling AdBlue at the pump. Plenty of stations may be missing from that source.

name: Pyle
intro: Less than one mile from Junction 37 of the M4, Pyle (Y Pîl) is a large village and community in Bridgend county borough, served by the A48 road and only about a half-hour journey from Cardiff. Kenfig Hill adjoins it to the north-east and North Cornelly also adjoins Pyle; the built-up area had 13,701 people in 2011. The CF33 postcode district covers the area. Porthcawl, the nearest town and a seaside resort, is 5 km away, with Sarn at 6.8 km, Bridgend at 8.4 km and Maesteg at 9.2 km. Port Talbot lies 10.2 km off and Baglan 14.7 km. For a van or diesel car with an AdBlue warning, the main practical point is that the motorway is close: Junction 37 is nearby and the nearest listed services are 7.3 km away in a straight line.
roadsText: Pyle is served by the A48 and lies less than one mile from Junction 37 of the M4. The three nearest service areas are all on the M4: Sarn Park Services is 7.3 km away in a straight line, Cardiff West Services 26.1 km and Swansea West Services 27.2 km. Road distances will be longer than these figures. Sarn Park is the closest of the listed services if an AdBlue warning comes on.

name: Quedgeley and Hardwicke
intro: Since the 1980s Quedgeley has become increasingly contiguous with both Gloucester and Hardwicke, which lies in Stroud District. It is the only town within the city of Gloucester, its civil parish having been transferred to the Gloucester district in 1991. In the west, a thin strip of land runs between the Severn and the Gloucester Ship Canal, while the south-eastern part of the town is Kingsway Village, with Tuffley directly to its north. The parish had 17,519 people in 2011 and covers 576 hectares. The area falls in the GL2 postcode district. Gloucester is 5.5 km away, Brockworth 8.8 km and Stroud 9.4 km. Diesel drivers with an AdBlue warning have the M5 close by: Gloucester Services is only 3.8 km away in a straight line.
roadsText: Gloucester Services on the M5 is the nearest listed service area to Quedgeley and Hardwicke, just 3.8 km away in a straight line. Michaelwood Services, also on the M5, is 20.8 km off, and Ross Spur Services on the M50 is 23.1 km. For drivers in GL2, the M5 holds two of the three options, and the nearest is close enough for a short trip if an AdBlue warning comes on.

name: Radcliffe
intro: Radcliffe is a market town in the Irwell Valley, part of the borough of Bury, lying 7 miles north-west of Manchester and 3 miles south-west of Bury. To the south it is contiguous with Whitefield, and the disused Manchester Bolton & Bury Canal cuts through the town. Evidence of Mesolithic, Roman and Norman activity has been found locally, and a Roman road passes along the border with Bury. By the mid-19th century Radcliffe was an important mill town with its own road, canal and railway network; today it is mainly residential, with 29,950 people at the 2011 Census. The M26, M45 and BL9 postcode districts cover it. For drivers, the neighbours are close (Little Lever is 3.2 km away and Bury 3.9 km), and four motorways are listed nearby: the M66, M60, M62 and M61. With an AdBlue warning, the nearest service area is Birch Services on the M62, 6 km away.
roadsText: Listed roads around Radcliffe are the M66, M60, M62 and M61, plus the A56, A58, A666 and A6053. Birch Services on the M62 is 6 km away, Rivington Services on the M61 17.1 km and Blackburn with Darwen Services on the M65 19.4 km. OpenStreetMap lists a station in Manchester (M25 3AJ), 3.7 km away, as selling AdBlue at the pump, and another at 12.8 km; there may be others the map does not show.

name: Ramsbottom
intro: Lying on the River Irwell in the West Pennine Moors, Ramsbottom is a market town in the Metropolitan Borough of Bury, 3.9 miles (6.3 km) north-west of Bury and 12 miles (19 km) from Manchester. It was historically in Lancashire, and the 2011 census put its population at 17,872. Victorian architecture, Pennine landscape and industrial heritage, including the East Lancashire Railway, support heritage tourism in the town. The BL0 postcode district covers it. Haslingden is about 6.5 km away and Radcliffe 7.7 km, while Little Lever, Heywood and Rawtenstall are all between 8.3 km and 8.6 km off. For a driver with an AdBlue warning in the BL0 area, the nearest motorway service area, Birch Services on the M62, is about 9.7 km away.
roadsText: Birch Services on the M62 is the nearest service area to Ramsbottom, about 9.7 km away. Blackburn with Darwen Services on the M65 is around 13.3 km off, and Rivington Services on the M61 about 16.7 km. OpenStreetMap has a station under Manchester, roughly 11 km away, listed as selling AdBlue at the pump, plus a site at about 17.6 km. Its data is incomplete, so other stations may stock it.

name: Ramsgate
intro: Ramsgate, one of the great English seaside towns of the 19th century, is a port town and civil parish in the Thanet district of eastern Kent. Its 2021 population was 42,027, and its postcode districts are CT11, CT12 and CT10. The town has one of the largest marinas on the English south coast, and the Port of Ramsgate provided cross-channel ferries for many years. Broadstairs is only 3km away and Margate 4.6km, so the Thanet towns sit close together, while Deal is 13.8km and Canterbury 23.6km. The A299, A256, A28, A255 and A254 make up the main road list, with no motorway among them. For a diesel driver, that means short runs between neighbouring towns and A-road journeys further afield, with Minster Services 6.1km away as the one nearby stop.
roadsText: Only A roads are listed around Ramsgate: the A299, A256, A28, A255 and A254. Minster Services on the A299 is the nearest service area, about 6.1km away. After that the distances grow: Whitfield Services on the A2 is 22.2km and Folkestone Services on the M20 is 37km. If an AdBlue warning appears, Minster is by far the closest service area to town.

name: Raunds
intro: A market town in North Northamptonshire, Raunds had 9,379 residents at the 2021 census and falls within the NN9 postcode district. Its nearest neighbour is Rushden, 7.2 km away, followed by Burton Latimer at 9.7 km and Wellingborough at 11.6 km. Kettering is 13.7 km off and Corby 19.2 km. For anyone driving a van or diesel car around Raunds, the most useful nearby stop is Thrapston Services on the A45, 5.5 km from the town. Beyond that, the next service areas are almost 20 km away, so if an AdBlue warning appears, the A45 stop is the one to remember. A station listed as selling AdBlue at the pump is also close to 20 km away.
roadsText: Thrapston Services on the A45 is 5.5 km from Raunds and is by far the closest service area. Rothwell Truck Stop on the A14 and Brampton Hut Services on the A141 are both 19.8 km away. A station with a Peterborough address (PE8 6TZ), 19.7 km from the town, is listed on OpenStreetMap as selling AdBlue at the pump. That data is incomplete, so nearer stations may well stock it.

name: Rawmarsh
intro: Part of the Sheffield Urban Area, Rawmarsh is a village in the Metropolitan Borough of Rotherham, 2 miles (3 km) north-north-east of Rotherham town centre. It lay within the West Riding of Yorkshire historically. Counting output areas from neighbouring wards, its population was 18,535 in 2014, and it uses the S62 postcode district. The places around it are close together: Swinton is about 3.2 km away, Rotherham 3.5 km, Wath upon Dearne 4.4 km, Mexborough 5.5 km and Wickersley and Bramley 6 km, with Wombwell at 7.8 km. For a van or diesel car with an AdBlue warning, the nearest listed service area is Rotherham Services on the M1, around 7.1 km away in a straight line. Sheffield Service Area on the A6102 is the next closest, at about 10.8 km.
roadsText: Rotherham Services on the M1 is the nearest service area to Rawmarsh, about 7.1 km in a straight line, followed by Sheffield Service Area on the A6102 at 10.8 km and Woodall Services on the M1 at 16.8 km. OpenStreetMap lists a station in Doncaster (DN4 0TP), roughly 12.2 km away, as selling AdBlue at the pump. That source is far from complete, so treat it as one known option rather than the only one.

name: Rawtenstall
intro: At the centre of the Rossendale Valley, Rawtenstall is a town in the borough of Rossendale, Lancashire, 24 km north of Manchester, 35 km east of Preston and 70 km south-east of Lancaster. Its population was about 23,000 in 2022, and it is in the BB4 postcode district. The M66 is among the main roads around the town, along with the A56, A681, A682, A680, A6066, A671 and A676. Neighbouring towns are close: Haslingden is 3.7 km away, Bacup 5 km and Accrington 7.6 km, with Ramsbottom at 8.6 km, Oswaldtwistle at 9.3 km and Burnley at 10.3 km. For a van or diesel car based here, that means a mix of short runs between neighbouring towns and longer trips, such as the 24 km run to Manchester, with the nearest service areas all more than 13 km away.
roadsText: Main roads around Rawtenstall include the M66, A56, A681, A682, A680, A6066, A671 and A676. The nearest service areas are Blackburn with Darwen on the M65 at 13.4 km, Hollin Bank, also on the M65, at 14.4 km and Birch on the M62 at 15.4 km. A station in Manchester, 18.6 km away, is listed in OpenStreetMap as selling AdBlue at the pump; the map data is incomplete, so nearer forecourts may also sell it.

name: Rayleigh
intro: Between Chelmsford and Southend-on-Sea, Rayleigh is a market town and civil parish in the Rochford District of Essex, 32 miles (51 km) east of central London. At the 2021 census the parish had 32,248 people and the built-up area 32,380. Its neighbours are packed in close: Thundersley and South Benfleet is 3.7 km away, Hockley and Hawkwell 4.3 km, South Woodham Ferrers and Wickford both 5.8 km, Rochford 7.3 km and Southend-on-Sea 8 km. Several main roads are listed for the town, including the A127, A130 and A13, along with the A1245, A129, A1015 and A132. For a van or diesel car with an AdBlue warning, that means plenty of route choices, but the listed service areas are all more than 16 km away, as set out below. Postcode districts are SS5, SS6 and SS7.
roadsText: Listed roads are the A127, A1245, A130, A13, A129, A1015 and A132. Orsett Cock Services on the A13 is 16.4 km away, Boreham Services on the A131 18.9 km and Thurrock Services on the M25 25.1 km. Lorry pumps in Chelmsford (CM2 5PY), 18.8 km away, are listed on OpenStreetMap as selling AdBlue at the pump, but they are marked HGV-only; the data is incomplete.

name: Reading
intro: Berkshire's county town and largest town, Reading lies in the Thames Valley where the Thames and Kennet meet. Its built-up area had 203,795 people in 2021, and some of the outer suburbs fall within neighbouring local authority areas. It is a major commercial centre and a regional retail centre serving a large area of the Thames Valley. Postcode districts include RG1, RG2, RG4, RG5, RG6, RG30 and RG31. The M4 and the A329(M) are the motorways listed for the area, with the A33, A4 and A329 among the A roads. Caversham is 4 km away, Woodley 4.4 km and Wokingham 9.6 km. From an AdBlue point of view, Reading is well placed, with a listed service area 5.3 km away on the M4.
roadsText: Two motorways, the M4 and A329(M), appear among the main roads listed for Reading, along with the A33, A327, A4, A329, A4155 and A3290. Reading Services on the M4 is the closest listed service area, 5.3 km away; Fleet Services on the M3 is 17.8 km and Chieveley Services on the M4 is 24.1 km. The Swallowfield By-pass station (RG7 1LZ), about 5.1 km away, is listed as selling AdBlue at the pump in OpenStreetMap. That record is incomplete, so other stations may sell it too.

name: Redbridge
intro: Established in 1965, the London Borough of Redbridge has Ilford, Wanstead and Woodford as its principal settlements. The borough shares boundaries with Epping Forest District in Essex to the north, Waltham Forest to the west, Havering to the east, Barking and Dagenham to the south east and Newham to the south west. It has a population of around 309,509. The M11 is among its main roads, along with the A12, A406, A123, A113, A118, A1400 and A1083, so a warning could come on in town or out on a major route. Postcode districts include IG1 to IG7 and E18. Chigwell is 3.5km away, Buckhurst Hill 5.4km and Barking and Dagenham 5.9km, and with Essex on the northern boundary, a van on a Redbridge round may be just outside the borough when an AdBlue warning appears.
roadsText: Main routes listed here are the M11, A123, A12, A1400, A406, A113, A118 and A1083. Listed service areas are Thurrock Services on the M25 (17km), South Mimms Services on the A1(M) (23.7km) and Orsett Cock Services on the A13 (23.8km). A station 4.4km away is listed as selling AdBlue at the pump in OpenStreetMap, as is one at Catford, 16.5km off. Coverage in that data is incomplete, so treat it as a starting point.

name: Redcar
intro: Seven miles (11 km) east of Middlesbrough, Redcar is a seaside town on the Yorkshire Coast in the Redcar and Cleveland district, within the ceremonial county of North Yorkshire. The town is made up of Coatham, Dormanstown, Kirkleatham, Newcomen, West Dyke, Wheatlands and Zetland, and the Redcar subdivision of the Teesside built-up area had 37,073 residents at the 2011 census. It gained a town charter in 1922 and was governed by the municipal borough of Redcar until 1968. Main roads listed are the A66, A174, A1042, A1053 and A1085, and the postcode districts include TS10 and TS11. Eston is 6.7km away, Guisborough 8.4km and Middlesbrough 10.9km. If an AdBlue warning comes on near Redcar, Teesside Truck Stop on the A66 is the closest listed stop at 6.6km, with other services 15km or more away.
roadsText: Redcar's listed main roads are the A174, A1053, A66, A1042 and A1085. The closest listed stop is Teesside Truck Stop on the A66, 6.6km away, which is also one of the town's own main roads. Wolviston Services on the A689 is 15km away and southbound services on the A19 are 15.5km away.

name: Reddish
intro: Houldsworth Mill, a former textile mill, is one of the landmarks Reddish still has from its rapid growth during the Industrial Revolution. Historically part of Lancashire, it is now an area of the Metropolitan Borough of Stockport, 7.4 km south-east of Manchester city centre, and Reddish Vale is a country park. The 2021 census counted 22,203 people, spread across the SK5 and M18 postcode districts. It is closely surrounded by other places: Denton is 2.8 km away, Stockport and Bredbury and Woodley are both 3.6 km, Audenshaw is 3.9 km, Droylsden 4.6 km and Manchester 5.1 km. For a van or diesel car, that adds up to plenty of short urban journeys between neighbouring towns, with the nearest motorway service area 14.8 km away at Birch on the M62.
roadsText: The closest service area to Reddish is Birch on the M62, 14.8 km away, with Knutsford and Tabley Hill, both on the M6, at 22.6 km and 22.7 km. Two stations are listed in OpenStreetMap as selling AdBlue at the pump: one 8.5 km from Reddish and one in Manchester at 13.7 km. As the map data is incomplete, closer forecourts may also sell it.

name: Redditch
intro: In the 1800s, Redditch became a centre for the needle and fishing tackle industry, and in the 1960s it joined the new town planning movement, expanding into the villages and hamlets around it. It is now the second largest settlement in Worcestershire after Worcester, with 81,637 people in the town at the 2021 census. Postcodes are B97 and B98. The roads listed for Redditch are all A-roads: the A441, A448, A4189, A435 and A4023. Bromsgrove is about 9.1km away and Catshill 10.5km, while Solihull, Droitwich Spa and Stratford-upon-Avon are between 15.1km and 18.7km off. Much local driving stays on those A-roads, with motorway services about 7.4km away on the M42. That is the most practical stop if an AdBlue warning appears.
roadsText: Listed roads around Redditch are the A441, A448, A4189, A435 and A4023. The nearest service area is Hopwood Park services on the M42, about 7.4km away. Frankley services on the M5 is about 15.7km and Warwick North (Budbrooke) services on the A46 about 22.1km. OpenStreetMap lists an HGV-only refuelling site in Birmingham (B25 8DW), about 19.3km away, as selling AdBlue at the pump. That data is incomplete.

name: Redhill
intro: Two main roads cross at Redhill: the north-south A23 between London and Brighton, and the east-west A25 running from Guildford to Sevenoaks. The town sits in the borough of Reigate and Banstead in Surrey, adjoining Reigate to the west and due south of Croydon, and is part of the London commuter belt. It is also the post town and commercial area for Earlswood, Merstham and Whitebushes, and for the villages of Bletchingley and Nutfield to the east. Postcode districts are RH1 and RH2. The M25 and M23 are both on the road list, with the A217, A242 and A2044 too. Reigate is 2.3km away and Horley 6.3km, so a driver here mixes short local runs with access to two motorways.
roadsText: The M25, M23, A23, A217, A25, A2044 and A242 are the main roads listed around Redhill. The nearest service areas are Clacket Lane Services on the M25 (15.6km), Pease Pottage Services on the M23 (16.3km) and Cobham Services on the M25 (18.3km). Although both motorways are on the road list, the closest of these stops is 15.6km away, which is worth knowing if an AdBlue warning appears.

name: Redruth
intro: Redruth takes its name from the Cornish Resrudh, meaning red ford. The town lies about 9 miles (14 km) west of Truro, 11 miles (18 km) north-west of Falmouth, 12 miles (19 km) east of St Ives and 18 miles (29 km) north-east of Penzance. At the 2021 census its built-up area had 15,455 residents, and the parish 15,626. Two postcode districts cover the town, TR15 and TR16. Camborne is just 5.5 km away, with Penryn at 10.8 km, Helston at 15.1 km and Newquay at 23 km. Service areas are a long way off for a driver with an AdBlue warning. The nearest listed one is Cornwall Services on the A30, 35.9 km away in a straight line, and the next, Saltash Services on the A388, is 73.1 km.
roadsText: Every listed service area is more than 35 km from Redruth. The nearest is Cornwall Services on the A30, 35.9 km away in a straight line, while Saltash Services on the A388 is 73.1 km off and Roundswell Service Area on the A39 is 122.3 km. That makes it worth acting on an AdBlue warning in TR15 or TR16 promptly rather than planning around a services stop.

name: Reigate
intro: Around 19 miles south of central London, Reigate is a Surrey town recorded in Domesday Book in 1086 as Cherchefelle. For most of its history it was an agricultural settlement, with a weekly market held from no later than 1279 until 1895. Today it has about 23,774 residents and sits in the RH2 postcode district, right next to Redhill, which is just 2.3 km away. Horley is 7.7 km off, and Tadworth and Epsom Downs, Dorking, Leatherhead and Caterham are all within 10 km. Two motorways, the M25 and M23, appear among the main roads listed around the town, along with the A217, A23, A25, A242 and A2044. For a driver with an AdBlue warning, the nearest listed service areas are on those motorways, between 16 km and 17.3 km away in a straight line.
roadsText: Main roads listed around Reigate are the M25, M23, A217, A23, A25, A242 and A2044. The three nearest listed service areas are close together in distance: Cobham Services on the M25 at 16 km, Pease Pottage Services on the M23 at 17.2 km and Clacket Lane Services on the M25 at 17.3 km, all straight-line. Which one is most practical depends on the direction of travel.

name: Renfrew
intro: Six miles (10 km) west of Glasgow, Renfrew is a town and royal burgh in Renfrewshire and the historic county town, although local government gradually shifted to its larger neighbour Paisley. It gained royal burgh status in 1397 and is called the Cradle of the Royal Stewarts. The town had 23,809 residents in 2022 and uses the PA4 postcode district. Neighbouring towns are close together here. In a straight line, Clydebank is about 4.2 km away, Paisley 4.5 km and Erskine 4.9 km, with Bearsden at 6.3 km and Barrhead at 8.2 km. Two motorways, the M8 and M77, are among the main roads, along with the A8, A726, A737 and A741. A driver with an AdBlue warning has a station listed as selling AdBlue at the pump within about 5 km, while the nearest service area is over 20 km away.
roadsText: Main roads listed for Renfrew are the M8, M77, A726, A737, A741, A8, A877 and A736. The nearest service areas are on the M74: Bothwell Services at about 21.5 km in a straight line and Hamilton Services at about 24.1 km, with Stirling Services on the M9 at 36.8 km. OpenStreetMap lists a station in Glasgow (G11 6DN), about 4.9 km away, and another about 14.2 km away as selling AdBlue at the pump; that list is incomplete.

name: Retford
intro: Also known as East Retford, this market town in the Bassetlaw district of Nottinghamshire lies on the River Idle and the Chesterfield Canal. It had 23,740 residents at the 2021 census and is covered by the DN22 postcode district. The cities around it are some distance away: Lincoln is 23 miles to the east, Sheffield 26 miles to the west and Nottingham 31 miles to the south-west. The A1 bypasses the town, and the three nearest service areas are all on the A1 or the A1(M). Neighbouring towns are spaced out too, with Worksop 11.8 km away, New Ollerton and Ollerton 14.2 km and Gainsborough 14.7 km. For a driver whose van or diesel car shows an AdBlue warning around Retford, knowing the A1 stops is the most useful starting point.
roadsText: Main roads around Retford are the A1, A620, A638 and A634. The nearest service areas all sit on the A1 corridor: Markham Moor Services on the A1 at 7.6 km, Moto Blyth Services on the A1(M) at 10.6 km, and Cromwell Services on the A1 at 22.1 km. Markham Moor is the closest of the three, at under 8 km from the town.

name: Rhondda
intro: Two valleys make up the Rhondda: the larger Rhondda Fawr and the smaller Rhondda Fach, both taking their name from the River Rhondda and both part of the South Wales Valleys. A former coalmining area in the historic county of Glamorgan, its mining peaked between 1840 and 1925. From 1897 until 1996 Rhondda was a local government district, and its 16 communities have been part of Rhondda Cynon Taf County Borough since 1996. The area still forms a Senedd and a Westminster constituency, with an estimated 69,506 people in 2020. The postcode districts here are CF41 and CF43. Neighbouring towns are close: Tonypandy is 2.7 km away, Porth 5.8 km, Mountain Ash 7.5 km, and Aberdare and Tonyrefail 7.7 km each. Motorway services are further, with the nearest listed site 14 km off on the M4 in a straight line.
roadsText: The nearest service areas to Rhondda are all on the M4. Sarn Park Services is 14 km away in a straight line, Cardiff West Services 18.9 km and Cardiff Gate Services 26.5 km. Those are straight-line figures, and road distances will be longer. If an AdBlue warning appears, it makes sense to plan a stop rather than expect services close by.

name: Rhosllannerchrugog
intro: Rhos is the simple short form of Rhosllannerchrugog, also spelled Rhosllanerchrugog, a village and community in Wrexham County Borough within the historic county of Denbighshire. Its built-up area, which also takes in Penycae, Ruabon and Cefn Mawr, had a population of 25,362, and LL14 is the postcode district. Wrexham is 6.7 km away. Oswestry is 16.7 km away, Buckley 18.3 km and Chester 23.1 km, with Hawarden and Connah's Quay at 21.2 km and 24 km. For drivers, the A483 stands out in the data: two service areas on it are both within 3 km of the village, at 2.6 km and 2.8 km in a straight line, so a van or diesel car with an AdBlue warning does not have far to go to find somewhere to pull in. A third site, on the A5156, is 8.7 km away.
roadsText: Two service areas on the A483 are very close to Rhosllannerchrugog: Ruabon Park Services, 2.6 km away in a straight line, and Rhostyllen Services at 2.8 km. Holt Road Services on the A5156 is the third nearest, at 8.7 km. Road distances will be longer than these figures, but both A483 sites are near enough to be practical places to stop if an AdBlue warning comes on.

name: Rhyl
intro: At the mouth of the River Clwyd on the north coast of Wales, Rhyl is a seaside town in Denbighshire with a 2021 population of 27,325. Kinmel Bay and Towyn lie to the west, Prestatyn to the east, and Rhuddlan and St Asaph to the south-east. Together with Prestatyn, Rhyl forms a built-up area of 45,250 people, the most populous non-city in North Wales. The town's postcode district is LL18. Listed roads are the A55, A525, A548, A547 and A5151. Prestatyn is only 4.8km away, but other nearby towns, including Colwyn Bay, Conwy and Llandudno, are all 17.8km or more away. Trips around Rhyl and Prestatyn tend to be short, while reaching other towns means a longer run. The nearest service area is about 5.9km away on the A55, which is useful to know if an AdBlue warning appears.
roadsText: All three service areas nearest to Rhyl are on the A55: Kinmel Park services at about 5.9km, Singing Kettle services at 12.2km and Orme View services at 28.4km. The town's listed roads are the A55, A525, A548, A547 and A5151. One forecourt in Rhyl (LL18 5XE), about 5.8km away, is listed on OpenStreetMap as selling AdBlue at the pump. That listing is not complete, so there may be others nearby.

name: Richmond upon Thames
intro: The only London borough to straddle the River Thames, Richmond upon Thames was formed in 1965 from the boroughs of Richmond and Barnes, south of the river and formerly in Surrey, and Twickenham on the northern, Middlesex bank. Its major communities are Barnes, East Sheen, Mortlake, Kew, Richmond, Twickenham, Teddington and Hampton, and it has 198,019 residents. Richmond Park, the largest park in London, is inside the borough, as are Kew Gardens and Hampton Court Palace. Because the borough straddles the river, a journey from one community to another can mean crossing it. The M3 appears in the main road list along with the A3, A4, A30, A205, A308, A309 and A316, and postcode districts include TW1, TW2, TW10, TW11, TW12 and KT2. Hounslow is 4.4km away and Sunbury-on-Thames 5.7km, while Heston Services is 7km from the borough.
roadsText: Richmond upon Thames has the M3, A309, A316, A308, A4, A205, A3 and A30 among its main roads. Heston Services on the M4 is the closest listed service area at 7km. Cobham Services on the M25 is 15.2km away, and Wisley Services, on the A3, is 18.8km; the A3 is also one of the borough's own main roads.

name: Rickmansworth
intro: South-west Hertfordshire's Rickmansworth sits inside the perimeter of the M25, about 17 miles (27 km) north-west of central London and 5 miles (8 km) south-west of Watford. It is the administrative seat of Three Rivers District, named after the confluence of the Chess and the Gade with the Colne in the town. Most of the town lies north of the Grand Union Canal and the River Colne. It is served by the London Underground and by National Rail trains between London Marylebone and Aylesbury. Main roads listed include the M25 and A41, with the A412, A404, A4145, A4180, A4125 and A4178. Chorleywood is 3.2 km away and Watford 4.2 km, while Bushey and Chalfont St Peter are both 7.5 km off. Postcode districts are WD3 and WD18, and the population is 26,290.
roadsText: Listed roads are the M25, A41, A412, A404, A4145, A4180, A4125 and A4178. Three service areas are between 12 and 14 km away: Bourne End Services on the A41 at 12.2 km, Beaconsfield Services on the M40 at 12.5 km and London Gateway Services on the M1 at 13.8 km.

name: Ringwood
intro: Founded by the Anglo-Saxons and home to a weekly market since the Middle Ages, Ringwood is a market town on the River Avon in the New Forest district of south-west Hampshire. It lies close to the New Forest, north-east of Bournemouth and south-west of Southampton. In 2021 the parish had 14,618 residents and the built-up area of the town 12,785, and its postcode district is BH24. For a driver with an AdBlue warning, the nearest listed service area is Picket Post Services on the A31, just 3.4 km from the town in a straight line, and Rufus Stone, also on the A31, is 12.3 km away. Verwood is 7.7 km away and West Moors 7.8 km, with Ferndown at 10 km, Christchurch at 12.4 km and New Milton at 13.6 km. Bournemouth is 14 km off.
roadsText: Picket Post Services on the A31 is 3.4 km from Ringwood in a straight line, making it the closest listed service area. Rufus Stone, also on the A31, is 12.3 km away and West Wellow Services on the A36 is 20.5 km. OpenStreetMap lists a station at Creekmoor in Poole (BH17 7FR), 19.9 km off, as selling AdBlue at the pump, but the map data is incomplete.

name: Ripley
intro: North-east of Derby and south-west of Alfreton, Ripley is a market town and civil parish in Derbyshire's Amber Valley district. It is contiguous with Heanor, Eastwood and Ilkeston and forms part of the wider Nottingham Urban Area, so one place runs into the next. The postcode district is DE5. Somercotes and Swanwick is 4.1 km away, Heanor 4.7 km and Belper 5.5 km, with Eastwood and South Normanton and Pinxton both 7.7 km off. If your work keeps you moving between these towns, bear in mind that the nearest M1 service area is more than 11 km away. That matters if a van or diesel car shows an AdBlue warning on a local run.
roadsText: Tibshelf Services on the M1 is the nearest service area to Ripley, at 11.5 km, with Trowell Services, also on the M1, at 12.5 km. Welcome Break Derby South Services on the A50 is 19.5 km away. A station 19.1 km from Ripley is listed on OpenStreetMap as selling AdBlue at the pump. OpenStreetMap's coverage is incomplete, so a closer forecourt may sell it too.

name: Ripon
intro: Ripon, a cathedral city and civil parish in North Yorkshire, stands at the confluence of the Laver and the Skell, two tributaries of the River Ure. It was once known as Inhrypum, and its history includes an early monastery, a period under Viking control and a later wool and cloth industry. The city uses the HG4 postcode district and has a population of 16,593. Its neighbours are spread out: Knaresborough is about 15.4 km away, Harrogate 16.8 km, Northallerton 23.4 km and Wetherby 24.9 km. Services are some distance off too. The nearest listed service areas are on the A1(M), with Leeming Bar Services about 17.7 km away in a straight line and Coneygarth about 19.1 km, so a driver with an AdBlue warning should expect a drive of some length to reach one.
roadsText: Three service areas on the A1(M) are the nearest to Ripon: Leeming Bar Services at about 17.7 km in a straight line, Coneygarth Services at 19.1 km and Wetherby Services at 24.1 km. A station with a Northallerton address (DL7 9EG), about 19.2 km away, is listed on OpenStreetMap as selling AdBlue at the pump. OpenStreetMap does not record every forecourt that sells it, so there may be closer options.

name: Risca
intro: Wooded hills rise to the east and west of Risca, including Mynydd Machen at 362 m and Twmbarlwm at 419 m, giving this Caerphilly County Borough town a rural aspect. It lies at the south-eastern edge of the South Wales Coalfield, within the historic boundaries of Monmouthshire, and has been shaped by mining and other heavy industries for many centuries. The town has a population of 11,228 and is covered by the NP11 postcode district. It includes Ty-Sign, a large housing estate built in the early 1960s, and has a station on the Ebbw Valley Railway, reopened in February 2008. Cwmbrân is 7.5 km away, Blackwood 7.6 km, Caerphilly 8.4 km and Newport 9.3 km. For a van or diesel car with an AdBlue warning, the nearest listed service area is on the M4, 8.8 km away in a straight line.
roadsText: Welcome Break Cardiff Gate Services on the M4 is the closest service area to Risca, 8.8 km away in a straight line. Moto Cardiff West Services is 17.6 km away and Roadchef Magor Services 20.2 km, both also on the M4. With all three on the same motorway, the M4 is the road to head for if an AdBlue warning comes on in NP11.

name: Rochdale
intro: In the dale of the River Roch, in the foothills of the South Pennines, Rochdale lies 5 miles north-west of Oldham and 10 miles north-east of Manchester. It is the administrative centre of the Metropolitan Borough of Rochdale and had 111,261 residents at the 2021 Census, against 223,773 for the wider borough. Historically in Lancashire, it became a mill town and centre for textile manufacture during the Industrial Revolution. For drivers, the M62 and the A627(M) are both on the road list, together with the A58, A640, A664, A644, A6193 and A6033. Postcode districts in the data are OL2, OL10, OL11, OL12, OL15 and OL16. Heywood (5.1 km) and Littleborough (5.2 km) are the nearest towns, Royton and Shaw are both 5.8 km away, and Middleton (7.1 km) and Bury (8.9 km) are not much further.
roadsText: Rochdale's main roads are the M62 and A627(M), plus the A58, A640, A664, A644, A6193 and A6033. Birch Services on the M62 is the nearest service area at 6.8 km; the next two, Blackburn with Darwen Services (23.4 km) and Hollin Bank (24.4 km), are both on the M65. A station 10.7 km away and one in Manchester's M25 postcode district (11.9 km) are listed as selling AdBlue at the pump in OpenStreetMap. Those records are incomplete.

name: Rochester
intro: At the lowest bridging point of the River Medway, about 30 miles (50 km) east-south-east of London, Rochester is a port town in the Medway unitary authority. It forms a conurbation with Chatham, Rainham, Strood and Gillingham, and it was a city until 1998, when it lost that status after Medway was formed. The 2011 population was 62,982. Postcode districts are ME1, ME2 and ME4. The road list includes the M2 and A2, with the A228, A229 and A289 among the others. Chatham is 4.6 km away and Gillingham 7.2 km, with Gravesend at 8.6 km. For a driver with an AdBlue warning, the two nearest listed service areas are both a little under 10 km away, one on the A2 and one on the M2.
roadsText: The main roads listed for Rochester include the M2, A228, A2, A2017, A226, A229, A289 and A231. Tollgate Services on the A2 is 9.5 km away and Medway Services on the M2 is 9.9 km, so the two are almost level; Orsett Cock Services on the A13 is 14.6 km. Much closer, a station in Strood (ME2 2NY), about 1 km away, is listed as selling AdBlue at the pump in OpenStreetMap, which does not cover every station.

name: Rochford
intro: The town that gives its name to the wider Rochford District lies 3 miles (4.8 km) north of Southend-on-Sea, 21 miles (34 km) from Chelmsford and 43 miles (69 km) from London. Rochford's built-up area had 12,615 residents at the 2021 census, and its postcode district is SS4. Southend-on-Sea and Hockley and Hawkwell are both under 4 km away, with Rayleigh at 7.3 km, South Woodham Ferrers at 9.1 km, Thundersley and South Benfleet at 9.3 km and Canvey Island at 11.3 km. Service areas are some way off: Boreham Services on the A131 and Orsett Cock Services on the A13 are both 22.6 km away in a straight line. For a van or diesel car with an AdBlue warning, that is a fair distance to cover.
roadsText: Boreham Services on the A131 and Orsett Cock Services on the A13 are equally close to Rochford, each 22.6 km away in a straight line. Medway Services on the M2 is 28.1 km away, and road distances to all three will be longer. Drivers in SS4 should allow for that if an AdBlue warning comes on.

name: Romiley
intro: Part of the Metropolitan Borough of Stockport, Romiley is a Greater Manchester village that was historically in Cheshire. It borders Marple, Bredbury and Woodley, and at the 2021 census its built-up area had 10,900 residents. Romiley falls within SK6. Neighbouring places are packed closely together here: Bredbury and Woodley is about 2.2 km away in a straight line, Marple 2.4 km, Hyde 4.1 km and Denton 4.6 km, while Hazel Grove and Stockport are both just over 5 km off. Motorway service areas are further away. The nearest, on the M62, is about 19.6 km from Romiley and the two on the M6 are around 25 km out, so for a driver with an AdBlue warning it helps that two stations within about 20 km are listed as selling AdBlue at the pump.
roadsText: The closest motorway service area to Romiley is Birch Services on the M62, about 19.6 km away in a straight line. Knutsford Services and Tabley Hill Service Station, both on the M6, are about 24.9 km and 25.3 km away. OpenStreetMap lists a station about 12.1 km away and another in Manchester (M25 3AJ), about 19.3 km away, as selling AdBlue at the pump. That data is incomplete, so other forecourts may stock it too.

name: Romsey
intro: Romsey Abbey, the largest parish church in Hampshire, dominates the centre of Romsey, a town and civil parish on the River Test in the Test Valley district, at the outskirts of the New Forest. It lies north-west of Southampton, 11 miles south-west of Winchester and 17 miles south-east of Salisbury. In 2019 the town centre was substantially remodelled, removing the roundabout around the statue of Lord Palmerston and creating a pedestrianised area. The town is in the SO51 postcode district. Chandler's Ford is 6.4 km away and Totton 8.5 km, with Eastleigh at 9.9 km and Southampton at 10.3 km. For drivers with an AdBlue warning, Romsey is close to two service areas: Rownhams Services on the M27 at 4.6 km and West Wellow Services on the A36 at 6 km, both straight-line figures.
roadsText: Romsey has two listed service areas close by: Rownhams Services on the M27, 4.6 km away in a straight line, and West Wellow Services on the A36 at 6 km. Rufus Stone on the A31 is further out at 14.3 km. That gives a driver with an AdBlue warning a choice of a motorway stop or an A-road stop within a short distance of the town.

name: Ross-on-Wye
intro: Close to the border with Wales, Ross-on-Wye is a market town and civil parish in the south-east of Herefordshire. It stands on the River Wye at the northern edge of the Forest of Dean, and its population was estimated at 10,978 in 2021. Its postcode district is HR9. What helps a driver here is how near the town is to the M50: Ross Spur Services is only 1.5 km from the centre, and Symonds Yat Services on the A40 is 9.2 km away, so a van or diesel car showing an AdBlue warning has two listed stops within about 10 km. Monmouth is the nearest town at 14.9 km and Hereford is 18.3 km away. Quedgeley and Hardwicke, Gloucester, Churchdown and Great Malvern all lie between 23 km and 28 km from Ross.
roadsText: Ross Spur Services on the M50 is the nearest service area to Ross-on-Wye, just 1.5 km from the town centre in a straight line. Symonds Yat Services on the A40 is 9.2 km away, and Monmouth A40 Services, also on the A40, is 22.6 km away. That gives drivers in HR9 a choice of stops on both the M50 and the A40 if an AdBlue warning comes on.

name: Rosyth
intro: Scotland's first Garden City, Rosyth is a Fife town on the coast of the Firth of Forth and part of the Greater Dunfermline Area. It lies 3 miles south of Dunfermline city centre and 10 miles north-west of Edinburgh city centre, with Limekilns to the west and Inverkeithing to the east. The town was founded alongside Rosyth Dockyard, completed in March 1916 as a naval base, and the site was later redeveloped to maintain submarines and to serve as a port and business park. Rosyth is near the narrowest crossing point of the Firth of Forth and is today a suburban commuter town for both Edinburgh and Dunfermline. The postcode district is KY11. South Queensferry is about 5.9 km away in a straight line. The nearest service areas are all more than 19 km away.
roadsText: Kinross Services on the M90 is the nearest service area to Rosyth, about 19.2 km away in a straight line, with Dreghorn Services on the A720 almost the same distance at about 19.4 km. Musselburgh Services on the A1 is about 25.8 km away. Road distances from the KY11 district will be longer than these straight-line figures.

name: Rotherham
intro: Two rivers meet at Rotherham: the Rother, which gives the town its name, and the Don. It is the largest settlement in its metropolitan borough. It became known for coal mining and later steel in the late 18th and 19th centuries, and it was part of the West Riding of Yorkshire before becoming part of South Yorkshire after 1974. The 2021 census recorded 129,897 people. For a driver, the M1 is the obvious reference point: it is among the main roads listed, and Rotherham Services on the M1 is only 3.6 km from the town in a straight line, which is useful to know if an AdBlue warning comes on. The A630, A631, A6102, A6021, A6178, A618 and A633 make up the rest of the list. Postcode districts are S60, S61, S62 and S65. Rawmarsh is 3.5 km away, Wickersley and Bramley 4.8 km and Swinton 6.5 km.
roadsText: The M1 is the motorway among Rotherham's main roads, with the A630, A631, A6102, A6021, A6178, A618 and A633 also listed. Rotherham Services on the M1 is 3.6 km away in a straight line, Sheffield Service Area on the A6102 is 7.5 km and Woodall services on the M1 is 13.6 km. OpenStreetMap lists a station with a Doncaster address, 14.2 km away, as selling AdBlue at the pump; its coverage is incomplete.

name: Rothwell
intro: In the south-east of the City of Leeds borough, between Leeds city centre and Wakefield, Rothwell is a town of 20,600 people (2021 census) and part of the West Yorkshire Urban Area. It is close to the A1/M1 link road and the Stourton park and ride, and its nearest railway station is Woodlesford. For a driver dealing with an AdBlue warning, Rothwell is well placed: Skelton Lake Service Station on the M1 is only 2.6 km away in a straight line, and Leeds and Wakefield are 7.3 km and 7.7 km away respectively. East Ardsley is the closest neighbouring town at 5 km, with Morley at 7.2 km and Normanton at 7.5 km. The postcode district is LS26. The town is in the Rothwell ward of Leeds City Council and the Wakefield and Rothwell parliamentary constituency.
roadsText: The town is close to the A1/M1 link road, and the nearest service area is Skelton Lake Service Station on the M1, 2.6 km away in a straight line. Whitwood services on the M62 is 7.4 km and Woolley Edge on the M1 is 15.1 km. OpenStreetMap lists a station with a Leeds address, 2.7 km away, and one with a Pontefract address, 15.8 km away, as selling AdBlue at the pump. OpenStreetMap does not record every forecourt that sells it.

name: Rowley Regis
intro: Four Sandwell council wards make up Rowley Regis, taking in the towns of Blackheath and Cradley Heath as well as Old Hill, Rowley and Tividale. Those wards had a combined population of 50,257 at the 2011 census. Historically in Staffordshire, the town forms part of the Black Country. Postcode districts listed are B64, B65, B68, B69 and DY2. The M5 appears on the road list with the A4123, A461, A458, A4031, A4036, A456 and A41. Oldbury is about 2.1km away and Dudley 3.4km, with Halesowen at 4.5km. That makes for a patchwork of short urban runs between closely packed districts. Frankley services on the M5 is about 7.2km out, the nearest planned stop if an AdBlue warning comes up.
roadsText: For Rowley Regis, the nearest service area is Frankley services on the M5, about 7.2km away. Beyond that, Hopwood Park services on the M42 is 15.7km off and Hilton Park services on the M6 16.9km. The listed roads are the M5, A4123, A461, A458, A4031, A4036, A456 and A41. OpenStreetMap lists a forecourt in Warley (about 1.6km) as selling AdBlue at the pump, along with an HGV-only site in Birmingham (14.3km) and a forecourt at DY10 1JS (19.1km). It does not list every site.

name: Royal Leamington Spa
intro: Named after the River Leam that flows through it, Royal Leamington Spa grew from a small village called Leamington Priors into a spa town in the 18th century, then expanded rapidly in the 19th. It is commonly known as Leamington Spa or simply Leamington. The town is a civil parish in the Warwick district of Warwickshire, and the 2021 census counted 50,923 residents. Today it is a centre for retail and digital industries. Postcode districts are CV31, CV32 and CV34. Listed roads are the M40, A452, A425, A429, A46, A4177, A445 and A4189. Warwick is only about 3.7km away and Kenilworth 6.5km, with Coventry at 13km. Local driving here is a mix of town streets, short runs to Warwick and Kenilworth, and longer trips on the M40 or A46. The nearest service area is about 5.6km away on the A46.
roadsText: Two service areas are close to Leamington: Warwick North (Budbrooke) services on the A46, about 5.6km away, and Warwick services on the M40 at 8.5km. Corley services on the M6 is further out at 19.9km. The listed roads are the M40, A452, A425, A429, A46, A4177, A445 and A4189. OpenStreetMap lists one forecourt, about 16.6km away, as selling AdBlue at the pump, but its data is incomplete and closer sites may exist.

name: Royal Sutton Coldfield
intro: Birmingham City Council handles local government for Sutton Coldfield, though the town and civil parish has its own town council and elects a mayor. It lies within the city of Birmingham, about 7.5 miles north-east of the city centre, and sits 11.5 miles south of Lichfield, 10.1 miles south-west of Tamworth and 9.2 miles east of Walsall. It has a population of 93,392. Historically in Warwickshire, it became part of Birmingham in 1974. Its postcode districts are B72, B73, B74 and B75. The listed roads include the M6 Toll, A453, A452, A4041, A38, A446, A5127 and A454. Streetly is about 4.2km away and Aldridge 7.6km. For a diesel driver, that puts Birmingham, Walsall and Tamworth all within a short drive. The nearest service areas, though, are all 13.4km or more away.
roadsText: Listed roads around Sutton Coldfield are the M6 Toll, A453, A452, A4041, A38, A446, A5127 and A454. The nearest service areas are Tamworth services on the M42 at about 13.4km, Norton Canes services on the M6 Toll at 14.2km and Hilton Park services on the M6 at 17.5km. OpenStreetMap lists an HGV-only site in Birmingham (12.1km), a forecourt in Burntwood (14.2km) and one in Warley (15.7km) as selling AdBlue at the pump. That list is incomplete.

name: Royal Tunbridge Wells
intro: Thirty miles south-east of Central London, Royal Tunbridge Wells lies close to the East Sussex border on the northern edge of the High Weald. It was a spa in the Restoration and a fashionable resort in the mid-1700s, and today it is the administrative centre of Tunbridge Wells Borough. Its postcode districts are TN1, TN2, TN3 and TN4. Every road on the list is an A road: the A26, A21 and A264 lead it, with the A267, A228 and A2014 also listed. That matters if an AdBlue warning comes on, because the nearest service area, Clacket Lane on the M25, is 22.2km away. Tonbridge is 7km up the road and Crowborough 11.5km, with Sevenoaks at 17.1km and East Grinstead at 19.6km, so much local driving is A-road work between neighbouring towns.
roadsText: The A26, A21, A2014, A264, A267 and A228 are the main roads listed around Royal Tunbridge Wells. The closest service areas are Clacket Lane Services on the M25 (22.2km), Maidstone Services on the M20 (28.3km) and Tollgate Services on the A2 (32.2km). One station about 5.9km away is listed as selling AdBlue at the pump. OpenStreetMap data is incomplete, so other forecourts nearby may sell it as well.

name: Royal Wootton Bassett
intro: Formerly plain Wootton Bassett, this north Wiltshire market town was granted royal patronage in March 2011 in recognition of its role in the military funeral repatriations of the early 21st century, which passed through the town. It lies 6 miles (10 km) west of Swindon and 10 miles (16 km) north-east of Calne. The 2021 census counted 13,570 people, and the SN4 postcode district covers Royal Wootton Bassett. Swindon is the nearest town at 7.5 km, with Stratton St Margaret at 11.6 km, Calne at 13.5 km and Chippenham at 18.2 km. If a van or diesel car shows an AdBlue warning here, the nearest listed service area is 12.2 km away in a straight line, on the A420, with two M4 sites a little further out. A station only 3.9 km away is also listed as selling AdBlue at the pump.
roadsText: The nearest service area to Royal Wootton Bassett is the Onroute Truckstops site at Swindon J15, on the A420, 12.2 km away in a straight line. Chippenham Pit Stop on the M4 is 15 km away and Moto Leigh Delamere Services, also on the M4, 18.4 km. OpenStreetMap lists a BP station in Swindon (SN5 8UY), 3.9 km away, as selling AdBlue at the pump, along with BP and Esso entries at SN6 6JR, 11.2 km away. That data is incomplete.

name: Royston
intro: Royston's town centre was once split by a county boundary: the line between Hertfordshire and Cambridgeshire ran east to west along Baldock Street and Melbourn Street until 1896, when it was moved to put the town wholly in Hertfordshire. Today Royston is a North Hertfordshire town of 17,444 people, 12 miles (19 km) south-west of Cambridge and 18 miles (29 km) north of Hertford, and the Greenwich Meridian passes through its eastern part. The SG8 postcode district covers it. The nearest of the neighbouring towns listed is Baldock at 13.4 km, with Stotfold at 15.1 km and Letchworth at 16 km. If an AdBlue warning appears, the closest listed service area is Baldock Services on the A1(M), 13 km away in a straight line.
roadsText: Baldock Services on the A1(M) is the nearest service area to Royston, 13 km away in a straight line.
