Hatfield is 6.2 km away and Harpenden 7 km, while Abbots Langley and Kings Langley, Hemel Hempstead, Welwyn Garden City and Borehamwood are all within 11 km. Postcode districts are AL1 and AL4.
roadsText: Roads listed for St Albans are the M25, M1 and A1(M), plus the A414, A405, A1057, A1081 and A4147. South Mimms Services on the A1(M) is the nearest service area, 9.9 km away. London Gateway Services on the M1 is 14 km off, and Bourne End Services on the A41 is 14.5 km away.

name: St Andrews
intro: Fife's fourth-largest settlement, St Andrews is a coastal university town on the east coast of the county, 10 miles (16 km) south-east of Dundee and 30 miles (50 km) north-east of Edinburgh. It had 16,460 residents in 2022. Named after Saint Andrew the Apostle, it was the ecclesiastical capital of Scotland until the Reformation, and it is known globally as the home of golf, with the Old Course the most frequent venue for the Open Championship. KY16 is the local postcode district. In a straight line, Carnoustie is about 19.3 km away, Methil 21.3 km and Glenrothes 27.7 km, with Arbroath at 28.7 km. Service areas are not close by. The nearest is about 34.1 km away on the A90, which is worth knowing before a long run with an AdBlue warning showing.
roadsText: St Andrews has no service area nearby. The closest is Forfar Services on the A90, about 34.1 km away in a straight line, followed by Kinross Services on the M90 at about 41.6 km and MacMerry on the A1 at about 42.9 km. Road distances from the KY16 district will be longer than those figures, so it pays to check the route first.

name: St Austell
intro: China clay shaped St Austell: the town was the centre of a large quarrying industry, with many clay works and their spoil heaps. It lies 10 miles (16 km) south of Bodmin and 30 miles (48 km) west of the border with Devon, and its built-up area had 24,360 people at the 2021 census. The town is covered by the PL25 postcode district. The main roads listed around it are the A390, A391, A3058 and A3082, all A roads with no motorway in the list. Bodmin, at 14.6 km, is the nearest neighbouring town, with Newquay and Truro both 21.1 km away. For a van or diesel car with an AdBlue warning, the nearest listed service area is Cornwall Services on the A30, 9.5 km away in a straight line, and the next one, at Saltash, is about four times further.
roadsText: Four A roads are listed around St Austell: the A390, A391, A3058 and A3082. The nearest service area is Cornwall Services on the A30, 9.5 km away in a straight line. Saltash Services on the A388 is the next listed option at 39.6 km, and Roundswell Service Area on the A39 is 93.9 km off. For drivers in PL25, the A30 site is by far the closest stop.

name: St Helens
intro: Six miles north of the River Mersey, St Helens began as a small settlement in the township of Windle. By 1838 its traditional boundaries took in Windle together with Eccleston, Parr and Sutton. Today it is the administrative centre of a metropolitan borough that had 183,200 people at the 2021 Census. Postcode districts mix WA and L prefixes: WA9, WA10, WA11 and WA12, plus L34 and L35. Two motorways, the M62 and M57, sit on the road list, along with the A58, A570, A580, A57, A557 and A571. Prescot is the nearest town at 4.7 km, with Haydock at 5 km, Newton-le-Willows at 7.1 km and Ashton-in-Makerfield at 8.2 km. Huyton with Roby and Widnes are both 8.5 km away. Two service areas are within 7.3 km of town, both on motorways.
roadsText: St Helens' main roads include the M62 and M57, with the A58, A570, A580, A57, A557 and A571. Earlsfield Services on the M57 is 6.3 km away and Burtonwood Services on the M62 7.3 km, with Old Meadow Services on the M58 at 13.6 km. Stations in Warrington's WA5 (6.5 km) and WA3 (14.2 km) districts and at Old Meadow (13.6 km) are listed as selling AdBlue at the pump in OpenStreetMap. The data is not exhaustive.

name: St Ives
intro: A medieval market town on the River Great Ouse, St Ives in Cambridgeshire's Huntingdonshire district grew up at a fording point on a route between the north and east of the country and London. It was first known as Slepe, and drovers brought cattle and sheep through the town on their way to southern markets. Its stone bridge dates from 1425. Today the town has a population of 16,818 and is covered by the PE27 postcode district. Huntingdon is the nearest town at 7.3 km, with Cambourne at 12.9 km and Chatteris at 15.9 km. For a driver with an AdBlue warning, the useful fact is that Cambridge Services on the A14 is only 8.4 km away in a straight line, and two more service areas lie within 12 km.
roadsText: Three service areas sit within about 12 km of St Ives in a straight line: Cambridge Services on the A14 at 8.4 km, Caxton Gibbet Services on the A428 at 11.8 km and Brampton Hut Services on the A141 at 12 km. OpenStreetMap lists a station 13.4 km away and another at CB3 0LQ, 16.5 km away, as selling AdBlue at the pump. OpenStreetMap's AdBlue data is incomplete, so there may be others.

name: St Neots
intro: Eighteen miles (29 km) west of Cambridge, St Neots is a town and civil parish in Huntingdonshire, Cambridgeshire. Eynesbury, Eaton Ford, Eaton Socon, Love's Farm and Wintringham all form part of the town. Its centre lies on the bank of the River Great Ouse, close to the A1, which runs north to south, and to the A421 and A428, which link Cambridge to Bedford and Milton Keynes. That puts the town where a north-south route meets east-west ones, so a driver with an AdBlue warning here could be on any of them. The railway station is on the Great Northern route between London and Peterborough. The built-up area had 33,265 people in 2021. Sandy is 9.8 km away, Cambourne 13.5 km and Huntingdon 14.1 km, with Biggleswade 15.6 km and Bedford 16.1 km. The postcode district is PE19.
roadsText: The A428, A1 and A421 are the listed roads. Caxton Gibbet Services on the A428 is 11.3 km away and Brampton Hut Services on the A141 is 12.1 km away, with Cambridge Services on the A14 at 18.4 km. A station about 17.2 km away is listed on OpenStreetMap as selling AdBlue at the pump, though OpenStreetMap's AdBlue records are incomplete.

name: Stafford
intro: Halfway between Stoke-on-Trent and Wolverhampton, about 15 miles (24km) from each, Stafford is the county town of Staffordshire. It was founded in 913, when Æthelflæd, Lady of the Mercians, built a defensive burh, and later grew through shoemaking, engineering and electrical industries. The 2021 census counted 71,673 people in the town. Postcodes are ST16, ST17 and ST18. The M6 heads the road list, followed by the A34, A449, A518, A5187, A513, A5288 and A5013. Stone is about 10.9km away, Rugeley 11.9km and Cannock 13.1km, so most neighbouring towns are a moderate drive rather than next door. Van and car journeys here are a mix of A-road links and M6 runs. The nearest service area is about 9.6km away on the M6.
roadsText: Stafford services on the M6, about 9.6km away, is the nearest service area. A truck stop on the A5 is about 13.6km away and Stone services on the A34 about 13.7km. The town's listed roads are the M6, A34, A449, A518, A5187, A513, A5288 and A5013. One forecourt in Burntwood (WS7 3XA), about 17.7km away, is listed on OpenStreetMap as selling AdBlue at the pump, though OpenStreetMap's data is incomplete.

name: Staines-upon-Thames
intro: Commonly just called Staines, Staines-upon-Thames is a market town in north-west Surrey, about 17 miles west of central London, at the confluence of the Thames and the Colne. It is close to Heathrow Airport, is linked to the national motorway network by the M25 and M3, and forms part of the Greater London Built-up Area. Historically part of Middlesex, the town moved to Surrey in 1965 and sits in the Borough of Spelthorne. The first bridge over the Thames here is thought to have been Roman, and a market is recorded from 1218. About 21,327 people live in the town, in the TW18 postcode district. Ashford is 2.8 km away, with Stanwell, Egham and Chertsey all around 4 km. If an AdBlue warning comes on, the nearest listed service area is Heston Services on the M4, 10.6 km away in a straight line.
roadsText: Staines is linked to the motorway network by the M25 and M3. The nearest listed service area is Heston Services on the M4, 10.6 km away in a straight line, followed by Wisley Services on the A3 at 14.5 km and Cobham Services on the M25 at 14.8 km. Road distances will be longer than these straight-line figures.

name: Stalybridge
intro: A water-powered cotton mill built in 1776 made Stalybridge one of the first centres of textile manufacture in the Industrial Revolution, and 19th-century factory wealth turned scattered farms and homesteads into a self-confident town. Historically divided between Cheshire and Lancashire, it is now a Tameside town of 26,830 people (2021 census), 8 miles east of Manchester and 6 miles north-west of Glossop. It spans five postcode districts: SK15, SK16, OL6, OL5 and SK14. Dukinfield (3.2 km), Ashton-under-Lyne (3.5 km) and Mossley (3.7 km) are all close by, and Hadfield is 4.9 km away. The M67 and M60 are the motorways listed for the area. Drivers with an AdBlue warning should be aware that service areas are not close: the nearest is 15.4 km away.
roadsText: The M67 and M60 are listed for Stalybridge, along with the A635, A6018, A670, A6043, A627 and A57. Birch Services on the M62 is 15.4 km away, while Knutsford Services and Tabley Hill Service Station on the M6 are 31.5 km and 31.7 km. On OpenStreetMap, a station 7.7 km away and one in Manchester (M25 3AJ), 17.3 km away, are listed as selling AdBlue at the pump. That mapping is patchy, so confirm before you go.

name: Stamford
intro: With 17th- and 18th-century stone buildings, older timber-framed buildings and five medieval parish churches, Stamford is a market town in Lincolnshire's South Kesteven district and a frequent film location. Its population was estimated at 20,645 in 2019, and the postcode district is PE9. The nearest towns are spread out: Bourne is about 14.2 km away, Oakham 16.9 km and Peterborough 17.9 km, while Corby is around 23.2 km, Spalding 25.8 km and Whittlesey 26.8 km. That spacing matters if an AdBlue warning comes on, because the nearest service areas are also some distance from town, between about 11 km and 16 km away. Two of the three are on the A1 and the third is on the A47, so the A1 is the road most likely to matter for a stop.
roadsText: Stamford's nearest service areas are Stibbington Diner Lorry Park on the A1, about 11.1 km away, Morcott Services on the A47 at around 13 km, and Welcome Break Kate's Cabin on the A1 at 16.1 km. OpenStreetMap lists three stations as selling AdBlue at the pump: a BP near Bourne at about 11.1 km, an Esso near Peterborough at 17.1 km and a Shell at 17.7 km. That data is incomplete, so there may be others.

name: Standish
intro: Near Junction 27 of the M6 motorway, on the A49 road between Chorley and Wigan, Standish is a village in the Metropolitan Borough of Wigan. It lies within the boundaries of the historic county of Lancashire and had 13,278 residents at the 2011 census. The town formed around a crossroads and has grown as urban expansion between Manchester and Liverpool extends outwards. The WN6 postcode district covers it. Wigan is about 4.4 km away, Ince-in-Makerfield 6.2 km and Orrell 7.1 km, with Horwich, Chorley and Hindley all between 7.3 km and 7.8 km. For a van or diesel car with an AdBlue warning, two service areas, on the M61 and M6, are each only about 5.5 km away.
roadsText: The A49 runs through Standish between Chorley and Wigan, and Junction 27 of the M6 is nearby. Rivington Services on the M61 and Charnock Richard Services on the M6 are both about 5.5 km away. Blackburn with Darwen Services on the M65 is around 18.3 km off. OpenStreetMap has a station named Old Meadow at 18.7 km and one under Warrington at 19.6 km listed as selling AdBlue at the pump. Its data is incomplete.

name: Stanford-le-Hope
intro: Known locally simply as Stanford, Stanford-le-Hope is a town in the borough of Thurrock in Essex, 24 miles (39 km) east of Charing Cross in central London. The Office for National Statistics built-up area includes Corringham and had 29,525 people at the 2021 census. Stanford-le-Hope was an ancient parish, abolished as a civil parish in 1936 when Thurrock Urban District was created; that in turn became the borough of Thurrock in 1974. Its church parish has since been merged with neighbouring Mucking. Main roads listed are the A13, A1014, A1013, A176, A128 and A1321, and the nearest service area is very close, as shown below. Basildon is 5.8 km away, Chadwell St Mary 6.8 km, Tilbury 8.8 km, Canvey Island 8.9 km and Grays 9 km, with Thundersley and South Benfleet 9.9 km off. The postcode district is SS17.
roadsText: The A13 is listed alongside the A1014, A1013, A176, A128 and A1321. Orsett Cock Services on the A13 is just 3.6 km away. Thurrock Services on the M25 is 12.6 km off and Tollgate Services on the A2 is 12.9 km away. A station in Strood (ME2 2NY), 15 km away, is listed on OpenStreetMap as selling AdBlue at the pump; OpenStreetMap data on this is incomplete.

name: Stanley
intro: Centred on a hilltop between Chester-le-Street and Consett, Stanley is a town and civil parish in County Durham, south-west of Gateshead. Its name comes from the Old English for a stony woodland clearing. The town's core grew in the 19th century as the mining villages of East Stanley and West Stanley expanded and merged, and the local economy was once based on coal mining and other heavy industries. With those largely gone, Stanley is now mainly a commuter town, which points to a lot of regular runs out to neighbouring centres. Chester-le-Street is 7.4 km away, Birtley 8.2 km, Whickham 9 km and Consett 9.7 km, with Blaydon at 10.6 km and Gateshead at 11 km. The town is in the DH9 postcode district and has a population of 19,423.
roadsText: For Stanley, the nearest service area is Washington on the A1(M), 9 km away. After that the distances grow: Durham services, also on the A1(M), is 18.6 km, and Easington on the A19 is 22.4 km. For a commuter heading towards the A1(M), Washington is the obvious place to stop if a warning light comes on.

name: Stanwell
intro: Heathrow Airport's cargo-handling area lies to the north of Stanwell, a village in the Spelthorne district of Surrey about 16 miles (26 km) west of central London. It is the northernmost settlement in Surrey and borders both Berkshire and Greater London, with the Staines Reservoirs to the west. Historically part of Middlesex, it has been in Surrey since 1965. The village has been cut back three times, most recently in 1995 after the M25 was completed, when Poyle, beyond Stanwell Moor, was moved to Colnbrook in the Borough of Slough. Stanwell falls in the TW19 postcode district. Ashford is only 2 km away and Staines-upon-Thames 3.9 km, with Sunbury-on-Thames, Egham, Hounslow and Chertsey all within 8 km. For a diesel driver with an AdBlue warning, the nearest listed service area is on the M4 at Heston, 6.9 km away in a straight line.
roadsText: The nearest service areas to Stanwell, measured in a straight line, are Heston Services on the M4 at 6.9 km, Cobham Services on the M25 at 17 km and Wisley Services on the A3 at 17.8 km. Heston is well ahead of the other two, which are both around 17 km off, so for most drivers in TW19 the M4 site is the first one to consider. Road distances will be longer than these figures.

name: Stapleford
intro: Population growth in Stapleford has been steady: the civil parish had 14,991 residents in 2001, 15,241 in 2011 and 15,453 at the 2021 census. The town lies 6 miles west of Nottingham in the Borough of Broxtowe. Its postcode district is NG9. The town is closely surrounded by other places: Beeston is just 2.5 km away, Ilkeston 4.5 km, Long Eaton 4.6 km, Clifton 6.6 km and Nottingham 7.2 km, with Eastwood 9.4 km off. For a van or diesel car, Stapleford's most useful feature is how close it is to the motorway. Trowell Services on the M1 is only 3.4 km away, and two further service areas, on the A6011 and the A50, are 8.8 km and 9.7 km away. If an AdBlue warning appears, a place to stop is not far off.
roadsText: Stapleford is very close to motorway services: Trowell Services on the M1 is 3.4 km from the town. Trent Bridge Services on the A6011 is 8.8 km away and Welcome Break Derby South Services on the A50 is 9.7 km away, so all three are within 9.7 km. That gives drivers a choice of stops on the M1, the A50 and the A6011.

name: Staveley
intro: Staveley is a town and civil parish in the Borough of Chesterfield, Derbyshire, set along the banks of the River Rother, with a population of 15,151. It lies 5 miles north-east of Chesterfield, with Clowne 5 miles to the east, Bolsover 5 miles to the south-east, Worksop 11 miles to the north-east and Sheffield 13 miles to the north-west. The postcode district is S43, which it shares with Brimington, just 2.3 km away. Chesterfield is 5.5 km from Staveley and Bolsover 5.6 km, while Dronfield is 8.3 km off. For a van or diesel car showing an AdBlue warning, the nearest motorway services are 8.1 km away on the M1, and a station listed as selling AdBlue at the pump is 20 km away.
roadsText: Welcome Break Woodall Services on the M1 is the nearest service area to Staveley, at 8.1 km. Sheffield Service Area on the A6102 is 13 km away and Tibshelf Services, also on the M1, is 13.9 km away. A station 20 km from Staveley is listed on OpenStreetMap as selling AdBlue at the pump. OpenStreetMap does not record every forecourt that sells AdBlue, so it is worth checking closer ones first.

name: Stevenage
intro: Designated in 1946 as the United Kingdom's first New Town under the New Towns Act, Stevenage is a town and borough about 28 miles (45 km) north of London. It sits east of junctions 7 and 8 of the A1(M), between Letchworth Garden City to the north and Welwyn Garden City to the south, which puts the motorway along its western side. For a driver with an AdBlue warning, those two junction numbers are a quick way to say where you are. The population was 94,456 in 2021. Besides the A1(M), the roads listed for the town are the A602, A505, A1155, A1072 and A1070. Hitchin is 7.3 km away, Letchworth 8.1 km and Baldock 8.5 km, while Welwyn Garden City is 11.9 km off, Stotfold 12.1 km and Hertford 14.4 km. Postcode districts are SG1 and SG2.
roadsText: Stevenage is served by the A1(M), A602, A505, A1155, A1072 and A1070. The nearest service area listed is Baldock Services on the A1(M), 11.7 km away. Toddington Services on the M1 is 21.8 km off, and South Mimms Services, also on the A1(M), is 24.7 km away, so the A1(M) gives the town two of its three nearest options.

name: Stirling
intro: Stirling's position has long shaped travel: as the lowest bridging point of the River Forth before it broadens towards the Firth of Forth, it became a focal point for journeys north and south, and it earned the name 'Gateway to the Highlands'. The city lies in central Scotland, 42 km northeast of Glasgow and 60 km northwest of Edinburgh, and is the administrative centre for the Stirling council area. Postcode districts FK7, FK8 and FK9 cover it. For a diesel driver, the M9 and M80 are the motorways on the local list, with the A9, A84, A91, A811, A872 and A905 alongside them. Alloa is 8.9 km away and Larbert 11.9 km, with Falkirk at 15.5 km. Service areas are close by too, which helps if an AdBlue warning appears on the way in or out.
roadsText: Main roads recorded around Stirling are the M9, M80, A84, A9, A905, A811, A872 and A91. Stirling Services on the M9 is the nearest service area, 4.7 km away, and Balhaldie Services on the A9 is 12.1 km. Heart of Scotland Services on the M8 is further off at 30.3 km. Having two service areas within 12.1 km gives drivers here a choice of stops.

name: Stockport
intro: Where the rivers Goyt and Tame meet to form the Mersey, Stockport sits 6 miles south-east of Manchester, 7 miles south-west of Ashton-under-Lyne and 12 miles north of Macclesfield. Most of the town lies within historic Cheshire, with the area north of the Mersey in historic Lancashire. The built-up area had 117,935 people at the 2021 census, and the wider metropolitan borough 294,773. The road list leans heavily on motorways, with the M60, M56 and M67 all present, alongside the A6, A560, A5145, A6017 and A34. Postcode districts in the data are SK1, SK2, SK3, SK4, SK5, SK7 and SK8, plus M19. Six neighbouring places are within 5 km: Reddish, Bredbury and Woodley, Cheadle, Hazel Grove, Cheadle Hulme and Bramhall. A short local drive can easily cross from one into the next.
roadsText: Stockport's main roads include the M60, M56 and M67 along with the A6, A560, A5145, A6017 and A34. The nearest service areas are all more than 18 km away: Birch Services on the M62 at 18.1 km, Knutsford Services on the M6 at 20.1 km and Tabley Hill on the M6 at 20.4 km. OpenStreetMap, whose coverage is patchy, has a station 12.1 km away and another in Manchester's M25 postcode district at 16.5 km listed as selling AdBlue at the pump.

name: Stockton-on-Tees
intro: With 84,815 people at the 2021 census, Stockton-on-Tees is a market town in County Durham on the northern bank of the River Tees. It is the largest settlement in the wider Borough of Stockton-on-Tees and part of both Teesside and the Tees Valley. The river was straightened in the early 19th century so that larger ships could reach the town, though the Tees Barrage now means ships can no longer sail in from the sea. The Stockton and Darlington Railway served the port during the early part of the Industrial Revolution. For drivers, the A19 and A66 head the main road list, followed by the A174, A177, A139, A1027, A1046 and A1305. Postcode districts include TS18, TS19 and TS20. Thornaby-on-Tees is just 3.2km away and Billingham 4.6km, so a van with an AdBlue warning in Stockton is close to several other Teesside towns.
roadsText: Listed roads for Stockton are the A19, A66, A174, A1027, A177, A1305, A139 and A1046. Wolviston Services on the A689 is the nearest listed service area at 6.3km, then southbound services on the A19 at 9.3km and Teesside Truck Stop on the A66 at 10.1km. In OpenStreetMap, which does not record every outlet, a station near Durham (DH6 3LJ), 19.2km away, is listed as selling AdBlue at the pump.

name: Stoke Gifford
intro: Part of Bristol's North Fringe, Stoke Gifford is a large village and civil parish in South Gloucestershire that forms part of the Bristol built-up area. The parish includes the neighbourhoods of Little Stoke and Harry Stoke, and it borders Filton to the south-west, Patchway to the north-west, Bradley Stoke to the north, Winterbourne and Hambrook to the east and Cheswick to the south. At the 2021 census the ward had 14,200 residents in 5,788 households and the parish 19,794. It is in the BS34 postcode district. Bristol Parkway railway station serves the area, and to the south it is served by the Bristol Ring Road. Driving here is largely urban, with Filton 2.4 km away, Bradley Stoke 2.6 km and Bristol itself 6.9 km. The nearest listed service area is 10 km away in a straight line.
roadsText: Three service areas lie within 11.9 km of Stoke Gifford in a straight line. Avon Lodge on the A4 is the nearest at 10 km, with Welcome Break Gordano Services on the M5 at 11.8 km and Moto Severn View Services on the M48 at 11.9 km. The Bristol Ring Road serves the area to the south, and road distances to all three sites will be longer than the figures given.

name: Stoke-on-Trent
intro: Six towns federated in 1910 to form Stoke-on-Trent, and the city is still polycentric: Hanley is the main commercial centre, with Burslem, Tunstall, Longton, Fenton and Stoke-upon-Trent making up the rest. Known as The Potteries, it is a city and unitary authority in Staffordshire with an estimated 259,965 people in 2022, the county's largest settlement. It is now a centre for service industries and distribution centres. Alsager, Biddulph, Cheadle, Kidsgrove, Newcastle-under-Lyme and Stone surround it. Postcode districts include ST1 to ST5, along with ST9, ST11 and ST12. Listed roads are the M6, A50, A5007, A500, A52, A520, A34 and A519. With several town centres and distribution sites, driving here can mean plenty of short trips across the city as well as longer motorway runs. The nearest services are about 4.9km away on the M6.
roadsText: Three service areas are close to Stoke-on-Trent: Swift services on the M6 at about 4.9km, Stone services on the A34 at 8km and Keele services on the M6 at 9.3km. A forecourt near Newcastle-under-Lyme (ST5 4DH), also about 4.9km away, is listed on OpenStreetMap as selling AdBlue at the pump, though that data is incomplete. The city's listed roads are the M6, A50, A5007, A500, A52, A520, A34 and A519.

name: Stone
intro: A notable canal town, Stone had its development and local industry shaped by the Trent and Mersey Canal. The market town and civil parish lies in the Borough of Stafford, approximately 7 miles (11 km) from both Stafford to the south and Stoke-on-Trent to the north. Stone became part of the Borough of Stafford in 1974, and its population has grown steadily, from 12,305 in 1991 to 14,555 in 2001 and 16,385 in 2011. The postcode district is ST15. Rugeley is 15 miles (24 km) to the south, Cheadle 14.1 km away and Newcastle-under-Lyme 15.5 km. Drivers with an AdBlue warning are well placed for a stop: Stafford Services on the M6 is 2.5 km away in a straight line, and Stone Services on the A34 is 3.1 km.
roadsText: Two service areas are very close to Stone: Stafford Services on the M6, 2.5 km away in a straight line, and Stone Services on the A34 at 3.1 km. Swift Services, also on the M6, is 10.7 km off. A station in Newcastle-under-Lyme (ST5 4DH), at the same 10.7 km, is listed in OpenStreetMap as selling AdBlue at the pump. That data is incomplete, so other stations may sell it too.

name: Stonehaven
intro: Known in the local Doric as Steenhive and nicknamed Stoney, Stonehaven is a coastal town on the north-east coast of Scotland, 15 miles (24 km) south of Aberdeen. It was once the county town of Kincardineshire and is now administered as part of Aberdeenshire. The 2022 Census put its population at 11,177, and it falls within the AB39 postcode district. Towns are fairly well spaced out around here. Westhill is 21.5 km away and Aberdeen 21.6 km, while Montrose is 31.4 km and Inverurie 37.1 km. The service areas listed for the town start at 32.1 km, so a van or diesel car showing an AdBlue warning is worth dealing with before setting off on a longer trip in either direction.
roadsText: The nearest service area listed is Stracathro Services on the A90, 32.1 km from Stonehaven. Forfar Services, also on the A90, is 56.3 km away, and Ashgrove Services on the A96 is 69.2 km. That leaves a sizeable gap between the town and its nearest listed stop, which is worth planning around if an AdBlue warning appears.

name: Stotfold
intro: Although it is in Central Bedfordshire, Stotfold comes under the Hitchin post town for addresses, which placed it in the postal county of Hertfordshire. The River Ivel passes through the town, and its built-up area, which includes the adjoining Fairfield Park development, had 12,310 residents at the 2021 census. The SG5 and SG15 postcode districts cover it. Letchworth is just 4 km away and Baldock 4.5 km, with Hitchin at 7.3 km and Biggleswade at 7.8 km. For a driver with an AdBlue warning, Stotfold is close to a motorway service area: Baldock Services on the A1(M) is only 2.2 km from the centre in a straight line. The next nearest are almost 20 km away, on the A421 and the M1.
roadsText: Baldock Services on the A1(M) is the nearest service area to Stotfold, just 2.2 km from the town centre in a straight line. After that the distances jump: Bedford Services on the A421 is 19.5 km away and Toddington Services on the M1 is 19.8 km. For drivers in SG5 and SG15, the A1(M) site is the obvious first stop.

name: Stourbridge
intro: During the Industrial Revolution, Stourbridge was the centre of British glass making. Historically part of Worcestershire, the market town is now in the Metropolitan Borough of Dudley, on the River Stour at the south-western edge of the West Midlands conurbation, around 11 miles (18km) west of Birmingham. The 2021 census recorded 56,950 residents. Postcode districts include DY5, DY8 and DY9. Every listed road is an A-road: the A491, A458, A4036, A461, A456, A449, A451 and A4102. Brierley Hill is about 3km away, Kingswinford 4.8km and Halesowen 5km. Driving here tends to mean short trips between closely spaced towns, with no motorway on the local list. The nearest motorway services are about 8.8km away, which is worth knowing if an AdBlue warning comes on.
roadsText: Frankley services on the M5, about 8.8km away, is the nearest service area to Stourbridge, though no motorway appears among the town's own listed roads: the A491, A458, A4036, A461, A456, A449, A451 and A4102. Hopwood Park services on the M42 is 16.5km away and Hilton Park services on the M6 22.1km. Forecourts in Warley (about 9.4km) and at DY10 1JS (about 11.4km) are listed on OpenStreetMap as selling AdBlue at the pump, from data that is incomplete.

name: Stourport-on-Severn
intro: Often shortened to Stourport, Stourport-on-Severn is a town and civil parish in the Wyre Forest District of North Worcestershire, 4 miles to the south of Kidderminster and downstream from Bewdley on the River Severn. It had 20,653 people at the 2021 census and is covered by the DY13 postcode district. Droitwich Spa is 12.4 km away, Stourbridge and Bromsgrove both 15.2 km, Catshill 15.8 km and Worcester 17 km. The thing a driver with an AdBlue warning should know is that motorway services are not close: the nearest listed, on the M5, is 20.1 km away in a straight line, and the next, on the M42, is 22.6 km. Closer to town, one station 3.8 km away is listed in OpenStreetMap as selling AdBlue at the pump, though the map's records are incomplete.
roadsText: Motorway services are some way from Stourport-on-Severn. The nearest is Frankley Services on the M5, 20.1 km away in a straight line, with Hopwood Park Services on the M42 at 22.6 km and Strensham Services on the M5 at 32.6 km. Closer to home, a station at DY10 1JS, 3.8 km away, is listed in OpenStreetMap as selling AdBlue at the pump. That data is incomplete, so it may not be the only option.

name: Stowmarket
intro: Set on the A14 trunk road between Bury St Edmunds to the west and Ipswich to the south-east, Stowmarket is the largest town in the Mid Suffolk district. Its population has grown from around 6,000 in 1981 to around 21,000 in 2021, and further development is planned for the town and surrounding villages. The town lies on the River Gipping, which is joined by the River Rat to the south, and it falls in the IP14 postcode district. For anyone with an AdBlue warning, a station in Stowmarket itself is listed in OpenStreetMap as selling AdBlue at the pump, and Beacon Hill Services on the A140 is 7.1 km from the centre. Ipswich is 17.7 km away and Bury St Edmunds 20.6 km, with Kesgrave, Woodbridge and Sudbury all between 21 km and 24 km.
roadsText: The A14 trunk road passes Stowmarket on its way between Bury St Edmunds and Ipswich. The nearest service areas are Beacon Hill Services on the A140 at 7.1 km in a straight line, Sprougton Road Services on the A14 at 15.6 km and Ardleigh South Services on the A120 at 31.6 km. A station in Stowmarket (IP14 3QQ), 2.4 km from the centre, is listed in OpenStreetMap as selling AdBlue at the pump. That mapping is incomplete, so it may not be the only option.

name: Strabane
intro: On the east bank of the River Foyle, Strabane is a County Tyrone town of 13,507 people (2021 census) right on the border, since the Foyle divides Northern Ireland from the Republic of Ireland. Across Lifford Bridge is the smaller town of Lifford, the county town of Donegal. The River Mourne runs through the centre of Strabane and meets the Finn to form the Foyle, and the hill of Knockavoe, where the Sperrin Mountains begin, rises behind the town. Strabane lies roughly midway between Omagh, Derry and Letterkenny. Derry is about 21.9 km away and Omagh 27.1 km, with Limavady, Cookstown, Enniskillen and Dungannon between 41.6 km and 57.5 km off. Postcode district BT82 covers the town. The nearest service area is about 48 km away on the A6, a long way to go with an AdBlue warning showing.
roadsText: The nearest service area to Strabane is Glenshane Tourist Services on the A6, about 48 km away in a straight line. Cohannon Services on the M1 is about 63.3 km away and Temple Patrick Services Northbound on the M2 about 94.2 km. None of these is close, so check the actual road distance from the BT82 district before setting out with a warning showing.

name: Stranraer
intro: On Loch Ryan, at the northern side of the isthmus that joins the Rhins of Galloway to the mainland, Stranraer is the second-largest town in Dumfries and Galloway, with 9,751 people in 2022. It is the administrative centre for the Wigtownshire area. The town was formerly a ferry port with sailings to Belfast and Larne in Northern Ireland, until the service moved to nearby Cairnryan in 2011. Distances from here are long. Glasgow is 87 miles to the north-east, Ayr 52 miles and Dumfries 72 miles to the east. The town is in the DG9 postcode district. For a van or diesel car with an AdBlue warning, the remoteness is the main consideration: the nearest listed motorway service area is 107.6 km away in a straight line, so planning ahead matters.
roadsText: Stranraer is a long way from any listed service area. The three nearest are Cairn Lodge on the M74 at 107.6 km, Abington Services on the M74 at 108 km and Annandale Water Services on the A74(M) at 109 km, all measured in a straight line. By road each is further still, so a driver with an AdBlue warning in or around the town should treat it as urgent rather than count on reaching services.

name: Stratford-upon-Avon
intro: On the River Avon, 22 miles (35 km) south-east of Birmingham and 8 miles (13 km) south-west of Warwick, Stratford-upon-Avon is a Warwickshire market town in the Stratford-on-Avon District. It marks the southernmost point of the Arden area, at the northern extremity of the Cotswolds, and had 30,495 residents at the 2021 census. As the birthplace and burial place of William Shakespeare it receives approximately 2.7 million visitors a year, so local driving can mean sharing the town with large numbers of visitors. The postcode district is CV37. The main roads listed around it are the A46, A422, A4390, A3400, A4131 and A439, and no motorway is among them. Warwick is the nearest other town at 13.4 km point to point, followed by Royal Leamington Spa at 17 km and Redditch at 18.7 km, which gives a sense of how far you may travel if a warning light comes on outside the town.
roadsText: Main roads around Stratford-upon-Avon include the A46, A422, A4390, A3400, A4131 and A439. The nearest service area is Warwick North (Budbrooke) on the A46, 12.1 km away point to point. Warwick services on the M40 is 15.1 km away, and Hopwood Park on the M42 is 24.5 km. Those straight-line figures understate the distance by road, so it is worth planning a stop before an AdBlue warning becomes urgent.

name: Stratton St Margaret
intro: Swindon's north-eastern suburbs make up Stratton St Margaret, a civil parish in the Borough of Swindon, Wiltshire. As well as Stratton St Margaret itself, it takes in Upper Stratton, Lower Stratton and Kingsdown, and it has a population of 20,689. The parish is in the SN3 postcode district, with Swindon 4 km away. Beyond Swindon the nearest towns are further out: Royal Wootton Bassett at 11.6 km, Cirencester at 20.7 km, and Carterton, Wantage and Calne all at 22 km or more. The area is well placed for a driver with an AdBlue warning. A truckstop on the A420 is listed just 1.5 km away in a straight line, and three stations in Swindon, between 7.9 km and 8.3 km away, are listed on OpenStreetMap as selling AdBlue at the pump.
roadsText: The nearest listed service area to Stratton St Margaret is the Swindon J15 truckstop on the A420, only 1.5 km away in a straight line. Membury Services on the M4 is 17.4 km off and Chippenham Pit Stop, also on the M4, is 26.4 km. Three stations in Swindon (SN5 8UY and SN6 6JR), at 7.9 km, 8.1 km and 8.3 km, are listed on OpenStreetMap as selling AdBlue at the pump. That data is incomplete, so other sites may sell it too.

name: Street
intro: Street stands on a dry spot in the Somerset Levels at the end of the Polden Hills, 2 miles (3 km) south-west of Glastonbury. It is a large village and civil parish, with 12,712 residents at the 2021 census, and is covered by the BA16 postcode district. There is evidence of Roman occupation, and much of the village's history is tied to nearby Glastonbury Abbey: in the 12th century a causeway was built from Street to the abbey to carry local Blue Lias stone. Beyond Glastonbury, the nearest towns are Wells at 11.3 km, Bridgwater at 18.4 km and Yeovil at 21.2 km, with Burnham-on-Sea at 21.9 km. A driver whose van or diesel car flags an AdBlue fault here has no listed service area close at hand: the nearest is on the M5, 17.9 km away in a straight line.
roadsText: Street's nearest service area is Moto Bridgwater Services on the M5, 17.9 km away in a straight line, with Sedgemoor Services, also on the M5, at 20.5 km and RoadChef Taunton Deane Services at 32.7 km. Lunns Filling Station, a BP site at Lower Weare (BS26 2JE) 19.1 km away, is listed in OpenStreetMap as selling AdBlue at the pump. That mapping is not complete, so other stations may stock it.

name: Streetly
intro: Streetly's position is unusual: this area of the West Midlands lies within the borders of three district authorities, Birmingham, Lichfield and Walsall, around 7 miles (11 km) north of Birmingham City Centre. It is adjacent to New Oscott, Great Barr, Four Oaks, Little Aston and Aldridge, yet it is semi-rural, close to farms and separated from Walsall by open fields and the North Birmingham green belt. The local area includes Sutton Park, where Streetly has its own dedicated gate. Bus services link the area to Birmingham, Walsall and Sutton Coldfield, and Streetly railway station closed in 1965. The postcode district is B74. Aldridge is 3.7 km away and Royal Sutton Coldfield 4.2 km. For an AdBlue warning, the nearest listed service area is on the M6 Toll, 10.8 km off in a straight line.
roadsText: The nearest service areas to Streetly are Norton Canes Services on the M6 Toll, 10.8 km away in a straight line, Hilton Park Services on the M6 at 13.4 km and The Trucker's Rest on the A5 at 16.4 km. OpenStreetMap lists stations in Burntwood (WS7 3XA, 11.5 km) and Warley (13 km) as selling AdBlue at the pump, and an HGV-only site in Birmingham (B25 8DW, 13.7 km) meant for lorries. Its records are incomplete.

name: Stretford
intro: Stretford sits on flat ground between the River Mersey and the Manchester Ship Canal, with the Bridgewater Canal cutting through the town. This Trafford market town is 4 miles south of central Manchester, 3 miles south of Salford and 4 miles north-east of Altrincham. Neighbours border it on most sides: Chorlton-cum-Hardy to the east, Hulme to the north-east, Urmston to the west, Salford to the north and Sale to the south. Once an agricultural village known locally as Porkhampton, it saw industrialisation speed up after the Ship Canal arrived in 1894 and the Trafford Park industrial estate was developed. Eight postcode districts touch the area, from M32 and M17 to M33 and M5. For a driver with an AdBlue warning, the M60 and M602 are the motorways listed close by, and the nearest service area is 14.1 km away on the M62.
roadsText: Stretford's listed roads include the M60, M602 and A57(M), with the A5181, A5145, A56, A6010 and A5081. Birch Services on the M62 (14.1 km), Lymm Services on the M6 (16.4 km) and Tabley Hill Service Station on the M6 (17.1 km) are the closest service areas. OpenStreetMap lists a station in Manchester (M25 3AJ, 9.9 km), another at 13.4 km and one in Warrington (WA3 6RW, 14.8 km) as selling AdBlue at the pump; others may not be mapped.

name: Stroud
intro: Below the western escarpment of the Cotswold Hills, where the Five Valleys meet, Stroud is a market town noted for its steep streets. For anyone in a loaded van or diesel car, those steep streets are part of local driving. It is the main town in Stroud District and is surrounded by the Cotswold Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty. The town itself had 13,500 people in 2021, and the contiguous civil parishes of Rodborough and Cainscross form part of its urban area, with a population of 26,073 across the wider area. Stroud is 16 km south of Gloucester and 23 km from Cheltenham, and the GL5 and GL6 postcode districts cover it. Quedgeley and Hardwicke is 9.4 km away, Brockworth 12.3 km and Cirencester 18.2 km.
roadsText: Stroud's main roads are the A419, A46, A4171 and A4173. The nearest service area is Gloucester services on the M5, 8.5 km away. Michaelwood services on the M5 is 17 km and Leigh Delamere services on the M4 is 26.3 km, so the M5 is the nearest motorway for a planned stop.

name: Sudbury
intro: On the River Stour in the south-west of Suffolk, close to the Essex border, Sudbury is the largest town in the Babergh district and a market town with roots in the Anglo-Saxon period. Its built-up area had 23,912 people in 2021, and the CO10 postcode district covers it. The main roads listed around the town are all A roads: the A131, A134, A1092 and A1071. That matters if an AdBlue warning comes up, because the closest listed service area is 22.4 km away in a straight line. Halstead, 12.6 km off, is the nearest neighbouring town, with Colchester at 19.9 km, Haverhill at 20.6 km and Braintree at 21.4 km. Bury St Edmunds and Stowmarket are both within about 24 km, and London is 60 miles (97 km) to the south-west.
roadsText: The main roads listed around Sudbury are four A roads: the A131, A134, A1092 and A1071. No motorway appears in that list. The nearest service areas are Ardleigh South Services on the A120, 22.4 km away in a straight line, Sprougton Road Services on the A14 at 25.6 km, and Beacon Hill Services on the A140 at 26.4 km. Road distances to each will be longer.

name: Sunbury-on-Thames
intro: The London end of the M3 motorway is in Sunbury Common, known locally as Sunbury Cross, the more urban northern part of Sunbury-on-Thames. The town sits on the north bank of the River Thames in the Borough of Spelthorne, Surrey, about 13 miles south-west of central London. Its other focal point, Lower Sunbury or Sunbury Village, lies beside the river and holds most of the parks, pubs and listed buildings. Sunbury adjoins Feltham to the north, Hampton to the east, Ashford to the north-west and Shepperton to the south-west, with Walton-on-Thames on the opposite bank, 2.7 km away. About 21,476 people live in the town, which is covered by the TW16 postcode district. For a driver with an AdBlue warning, the M3 is on the doorstep, though the nearest listed service area is Heston Services on the M4, 8.9 km away in a straight line.
roadsText: The London end of the M3 is at Sunbury Common, also called Sunbury Cross, in the north of the town. The nearest listed service areas are Heston Services on the M4 at 8.9 km, Cobham Services on the M25 at 11.6 km and Wisley Services on the A3 at 14 km, all measured in a straight line from the town centre, so actual driving distances will be longer.

name: Sunderland
intro: A port city at the mouth of the River Wear on the North Sea, Sunderland lies approximately 10 miles (16 km) south-east of Newcastle upon Tyne. It is the most populous settlement in the Wearside conurbation and the administrative centre of the wider Metropolitan Borough of Sunderland. The modern city centre combines three Anglo-Saxon settlements: Monkwearmouth on the north bank of the Wear, and Sunderland and Bishopwearmouth on the south bank. Its population is about 168,323. Main roads listed include the A19, A183, A184, A690, A1018, A1231 and A1290, and postcode districts include SR1, SR2, SR3, SR4, SR5 and SR6, along with NE35 and NE36. Shiney Row and Penshaw is 6.4km away, Washington 6.8km and Houghton-le-Spring 8.3km. With the city split by the Wear, saying which bank a vehicle is on, as well as the postcode district, helps when describing where an AdBlue fault has struck.
roadsText: The city's road list covers the A183, A690, A1231, A1018, A19, A184 and A1290. Washington Services on the A1(M) is the nearest listed service area at 9.7km, then Easington Services on the A19 at 11.6km and Durham Services on the A1(M) at 20.8km. In OpenStreetMap's incomplete data, a station near Durham (DH6 3LJ), 18.4km away, and one in Newcastle upon Tyne, 19.3km away, are listed as selling AdBlue at the pump.

name: Sutton
intro: Covering 43 km2 (17 sq mi) of south London, the London Borough of Sutton is an Outer London borough whose principal town shares its name. It borders Croydon to the east, Merton to the north and Kingston upon Thames to the north-west, with the Surrey boroughs of Epsom and Ewell to the west and Reigate and Banstead to the south. The borough's population is about 208,858. All of the main roads listed are A-roads: the A217, A232, A297, A24, A23, A22, A240 and A237. Postcode districts include SM1, SM2, SM3, SM5 and SM6. Ewell is 4.9km away, Worcester Park and Stoneleigh 5.6km, Merton 6.1km and Croydon 6.5km. With Surrey on two sides of the borough, a van or diesel car that picks up an AdBlue warning on a Sutton job may well be over the county boundary by the time the driver pulls over.
roadsText: Sutton's listed roads are the A232, A217, A297, A24, A23, A22, A240 and A237. Cobham Services on the M25 is the nearest listed service area at 17.2km, with Clacket Lane Services on the M25 at 17.7km and Heston Services on the M4 at 20.8km. A station at Catford, 15.1km away, is listed as selling AdBlue at the pump in OpenStreetMap, but that data is incomplete.

name: Sutton in Ashfield
intro: With 36,404 residents in 2021, Sutton in Ashfield is the largest town in Nottinghamshire's Ashfield district. The market town lies 4 miles (6 km) west of Mansfield, 12 miles (19 km) north of Nottingham and 2 miles (3 km) from the Derbyshire boundary. Its postcode district is NG17. Main roads include the M1, A38, A60 and A617, plus the A611, A6009, A6075 and A6191. Neighbouring towns are close: Kirkby-in-Ashfield is about 3.2 km away and Mansfield 4.2 km, with South Normanton and Pinxton at 5.9 km, Mansfield Woodhouse at 6.3 km and Shirebrook at 8.6 km. Tibshelf Services on the M1 is about 5.1 km away, so a motorway service area is close at hand if an AdBlue warning comes on.
roadsText: Sutton in Ashfield's main roads are the M1, A38, A60, A611, A617, A6009, A6075 and A6191. Tibshelf Services on the M1 is the nearest service area at about 5.1 km; Trowell Services and Welcome Break Woodall Services, also on the M1, are about 18.4 km and 20.9 km away. A Tesco station around 6.9 km away is listed in OpenStreetMap as selling AdBlue at the pump; the data is incomplete.

name: Swadlincote
intro: Within The National Forest area, Swadlincote is a historic mining town in South Derbyshire that borders the counties of Leicestershire and Staffordshire. It lies 5 miles (8 km) south-east of Burton upon Trent and 12 miles (19 km) south-west of Derby, north-west of Ashby-de-la-Zouch. The town covers the suburban areas of Church Gresley, Goseley, Midway, Newhall, Oversetts and Woodville, and had 34,576 residents in 2021. Postcode districts are DE11 and DE15. Its main roads are all A roads: the A444, A511, A514 and A5189. Burton upon Trent is about 6.3 km away and Ashby-de-la-Zouch 7 km, while Coalville is around 14.3 km. The nearest service area is ExtraMSA Derby with Burton Services on the A50, about 9.8 km out, so a driver with an AdBlue warning should expect a short drive to reach it.
roadsText: Swadlincote's main roads are the A444, A511, A514 and A5189. The nearest service area is ExtraMSA Derby with Burton Services on the A50, about 9.8 km away, followed by Welcome Break Derby South Services on the A50 at 16.7 km and Moto Donington Park Services on the M1 at 18 km. A Shell station with a Swadlincote address (DE12 8AA), about 9.8 km away, is listed in OpenStreetMap as selling AdBlue at the pump; that data is incomplete.

name: Swallownest and Aston
intro: White's directory of 1833 gives Swallow Nest as the name of a toll bar and public house. Today Swallownest is a village in the civil parish of Aston cum Aughton, in the Metropolitan Borough of Rotherham, 4 miles (6.4 km) south of Rotherham and 7 miles (11 km) from Sheffield. It borders the Sheffield suburb of Woodhouse to the west and Beighton to the south-west, with the small village of Aston to the east and Aughton to the north. Woodhouse railway station serves it. The combined area has a population of 14,912 and is covered by the S26 postcode district. For a van or diesel car with an AdBlue warning, two M1 service areas are close: Rotherham Services is 4.4 km from the centre and Woodall Services 5.9 km. Dinnington is 7.1 km away and Wickersley and Bramley 7.3 km.
roadsText: Swallownest and Aston has three service areas within 7 km in a straight line: Rotherham Services on the M1 at 4.4 km, Woodall Services on the M1 at 5.9 km and Sheffield Service Area on the A6102 at 6.6 km. OpenStreetMap lists a station in Doncaster (DN4 0TP), 17.9 km away, as selling AdBlue at the pump. That data is incomplete, so forecourts nearer to S26 may sell it as well.

name: Swanley
intro: Within the M25 and next to the Greater London boundary, Swanley is a town in the Sevenoaks District of Kent, 16 miles (26 km) south-east of central London. The 2021 census counted 17,826 people in the town and civil parish, and its postcode district is BR8. Dartford is 7 km away, Bexley 8 km and Bromley 9 km, while Longfield, New Ash Green and Hartley, Swanscombe and Greenwich all lie between 10 km and 12 km out. For a van or diesel car with an AdBlue warning, it helps to know that the nearest listed service area, Thurrock Services on the M25, is 12.5 km away in a straight line, and Tollgate Services on the A2 is 13.4 km. A station at Catford, 13.4 km away, and another 17.5 km off are listed in OpenStreetMap as selling AdBlue at the pump.
roadsText: Swanley is inside the M25, and two of the three nearest listed service areas are on that motorway: Thurrock Services at 12.5 km and Clacket Lane Services at 16.7 km, both straight-line distances. Tollgate Services on the A2 is 13.4 km away. OpenStreetMap lists a station at Catford, 13.4 km off, and another station at 17.5 km as selling AdBlue at the pump. That data is incomplete, so other forecourts may stock it too.

name: Swanscombe
intro: Part of the civil parish of Swanscombe and Greenhithe, Swanscombe is a town in the Borough of Dartford in Kent, 4.4 miles west of Gravesend and 4.8 miles east of Dartford. Two postcode districts, DA10 and DA9, cover the area, which has a population of 15,462. Neighbouring towns are packed closely around it. Northfleet is 2.8 km away, Chafford Hundred and West Thurrock 4 km, Tilbury 4.4 km, Grays 4.5 km and Dartford 4.6 km, with Gravesend at 6 km. For a van or diesel car with an AdBlue warning, Swanscombe is well placed for services: Tollgate Services on the A2 is 5.3 km away in a straight line and Thurrock Services on the M25 is 5.4 km. Orsett Cock Services on the A13 is the third option at 9.7 km. OpenStreetMap also lists a station at Temple Farm in Strood, 14.2 km away, as selling AdBlue at the pump.
roadsText: Two service areas are within 5.4 km of Swanscombe in a straight line: Tollgate Services on the A2 at 5.3 km and Thurrock Services on the M25 at 5.4 km. Orsett Cock Services on the A13 is 9.7 km away. OpenStreetMap lists a station at Temple Farm, Strood (ME2 2NY), 14.2 km off, and another station at 18.9 km as selling AdBlue at the pump, but that data is incomplete and other forecourts may sell it.

name: Swansea
intro: Along Swansea Bay in south-west Wales, Swansea is the country's second-largest city, a port whose principal area also covers the Gower Peninsula. The principal area had an estimated 249,429 people in 2025, and together with Neath and Port Talbot the city forms the Swansea urban area. During its 19th-century industrial heyday it was the key centre of the copper-smelting industry, earning the nickname Copperopolis. Postcode districts across the city include SA1, SA2, SA5, SA6 and SA7. Neighbouring places are close: Baglan is 7.8 km away, Gorseinon 8.2 km, Neath 8.3 km and Port Talbot 11.2 km, with Llanelli at 15.4 km. Driving here can range from city streets to the roads of the Gower, and with the M4 among the main roads around the city, longer runs are easy to reach.
roadsText: The M4 is the main motorway near Swansea, with the A483, A465, A4067, A4217, A4118, A48 and A4216 also among the main roads. All three of the nearest service areas are on the M4: Swansea West at 5.9 km, Pont Abraham at 14.8 km and Sarn Park at 27.2 km.

name: Swindon
intro: The Cotswolds lie just to the north of Swindon and the North Wessex Downs just to the south. The town sits on the M4 corridor at the north-eastern edge of the South West, 135 km west of London and 57 km east of Bristol, and with a built-up population of 224,942 in 2021 it is the largest settlement in Wiltshire and the centre of its own unitary authority. It was transformed from a small market town into a railway hub after the Great Western Railway arrived in 1843. Postcode districts include SN1, SN2, SN3, SN4, SN5, SN25 and SN26. Stratton St Margaret is 4 km away and Royal Wootton Bassett 7.5 km, while Cirencester is 19.7 km and Calne 20 km. For a diesel van or car, Swindon combines busy town driving with easy access to the M4, so an AdBlue warning could come up on either.
roadsText: Besides the M4, the main roads near Swindon are the A419, A420, A4311, A4289, A4313, A3102 and A4312. The closest stop is the Swindon J15 truckstop on the A420, 4.7 km away; Membury services on the M4 is 19.2 km and Chippenham Pit Stop on the M4 is 22.4 km. In OpenStreetMap data, three stations are listed as selling AdBlue at the pump: one in SN5, 3.9 km away, and two in SN6 at 7.6 km and 7.8 km. That list is unlikely to be complete.

name: Swinton
intro: The name Swinton comes from the Old English Swynton, meaning swine town. It is a town in the City of Salford, south-west of the River Irwell and 6.4 km north-west of Manchester, adjoining Pendlebury and the suburb of Clifton. Collieries opened here during the Industrial Revolution, with coal fuelling the cotton spinning and brickmaking industries, and the Bridgewater Canal passes Swinton to the south. The population was 22,931 in 2014, and the town is in the M27 postcode district. Neighbouring places are all very near: Clifton is 2 km away, Worsley 2.5 km, Eccles 2.9 km, Walkden 3.2 km, Kearsley 4 km and Salford 4.6 km. For a diesel van or car, that means lots of brief urban trips around Salford and towards Manchester, with Birch services on the M62 the nearest service area at 10.1 km.
roadsText: Birch services on the M62 is the nearest service area to Swinton, 10.1 km away, followed by Rivington on the M61 at 18 km and Lymm on the M6 at 19.7 km. Three stations are listed in OpenStreetMap as selling AdBlue at the pump: one in Manchester 5.1 km away, one 13.5 km away and one in Warrington at 15.5 km. That data is incomplete, so others may sell it too.

name: Swinton
intro: Set on the west bank of the River Don, Swinton is a town in the Metropolitan Borough of Rotherham, five miles north-north-east of Rotherham and south-west of Mexborough. It had 15,559 residents at the 2011 census and falls in the S64 postcode district. Other towns surround it closely: Mexborough is about 2.3 km away, Wath upon Dearne 2.6 km, Rawmarsh 3.2 km and Conisbrough 5.5 km, while Rotherham is about 6.5 km and Wickersley and Bramley 6.9 km. If an AdBlue warning comes on, the nearest listed service area is Rotherham Services on the M1, about 9.9 km away in a straight line, and a station in Doncaster listed as selling AdBlue at the pump is about 9.5 km away.
roadsText: Rotherham Services on the M1 is about 9.9 km from Swinton in a straight line, Sheffield Service Area on the A6102 about 13.9 km and Barnsdale Bar Services on the A1 about 16.7 km. OpenStreetMap lists a station in Doncaster (DN4 0TP), around 9.5 km away, and another in Pontefract (WF7 7HX), around 17.9 km away, as selling AdBlue at the pump. Coverage of AdBlue on the map is incomplete.

name: Syston
intro: Syston is a town and civil parish in Leicestershire's Charnwood district, and its population rose from 11,508 at the 2001 census to 12,804 in 2011. It is covered by the LE7 postcode district. Its nearest neighbours are Birstall, 3.9 km away, and Mountsorrel, 5.5 km away, with Leicester 8.5 km off. Oadby is 10.9 km away, and Wigston and Loughborough are both 12.8 km away. For a driver with a van or diesel car, the useful point is that two roadside service areas lie within 6.3 km of the town, one on the A6 and one on the A46. Either is within easy reach if an AdBlue warning comes on, while the nearest M1 services are further off at 12.5 km.
roadsText: Two service areas are within 6.3 km of Syston: ExtraMSA Leicester Services on the A6 at 3.7 km and Six Hills Services Northbound on the A46 at 6.3 km. The nearest motorway service area is Leicester Forest East Services on the M1, 12.5 km from the town. That gives a choice between the A6 and the A46 for a quick stop, with the M1 as the longer option.

name: Tadley
intro: Between Basingstoke and Reading, Tadley is a Hampshire town and civil parish in the Basingstoke and Deane district, 5.5 miles (8.9 km) north of Basingstoke and 11 miles (17 km) south-west of Reading. Many of its houses were built in the 1950s and 1960s for workers at the Atomic Weapons Research Establishment, which was located in the parish of Aldermaston. The town's postcode district is RG26. Thatcham is the nearest town at 8.6 km, with Basingstoke at 10.8 km, Newbury at 13 km and Reading at 15.7 km. If an AdBlue warning comes on, Reading Services on the M4 is the closest listed service area, 10.6 km away in a straight line, followed by Tot Hill Services on the A34 at 13.6 km. A station on the Swallowfield By-pass near Reading, 12 km off, is listed in OpenStreetMap as selling AdBlue at the pump.
roadsText: Reading Services on the M4 is 10.6 km from Tadley in a straight line, the nearest listed service area. Tot Hill Services on the A34 is 13.6 km away and Chieveley Services, also on the M4, is 15.1 km. OpenStreetMap lists a station on the Swallowfield By-pass near Reading (RG7 1LZ), 12 km away, as selling AdBlue at the pump. That mapping is incomplete, so other stations may sell it too.

name: Tadworth and Epsom Downs
intro: This page covers Tadworth and the Epsom Downs area of Surrey, which has a population of 27,095. Tadworth itself is a large suburban village on the south-east side of the Epsom Downs, which form part of the North Downs, and it sits in the Borough of Reigate and Banstead. Postcode districts listed for the area are KT20, KT17, KT18 and SM7. The M25 heads the road list, with the A217, A240, A24, A232, A23, A2022 and A2043 also around the area. Epsom is 3.6km away and Ewell 3.8km, while Ashtead is 5.1km, Sutton 6.4km and Leatherhead 6.5km. For drivers, that means suburban roads and short trips between neighbouring towns, with the M25 for longer journeys.
roadsText: Main roads listed around Tadworth and Epsom Downs are the M25, A240, A217, A24, A232, A23, A2022 and A2043. The nearest service area is Cobham Services on the M25, about 12.4km away. Wisley Services on the A3 is 18.1km and Clacket Lane Services, also on the M25, is 19.2km. Two of the three nearest stops are on the M25, which helps if an AdBlue warning appears on the motorway.

name: Tamworth
intro: Fourteen miles (23km) north-east of Birmingham, Tamworth is a market town and borough in Staffordshire, named after the River Tame that flows through it. North Warwickshire borders it to the east and south and Lichfield District to the north, south-west and west. The borough had 81,392 residents in 2025. In the 8th and 9th centuries it was the main centre of royal power in the Anglo-Saxon Kingdom of Mercia, and today its industries include logistics and engineering. Postcodes are B77, B78 and B79. The M42 is on the road list with the A5, A453, A51, A513 and A4091. Sutton Coldfield and Lichfield are both about 12km away. If an AdBlue warning appears, the closest service area is only 3km out, while the next two are 19km and 20.3km away.
roadsText: Tamworth services on the M42 is only about 3km from the town. The next options are much further: Corley services on the M6 at 19km and Norton Canes services on the M6 Toll at 20.3km. Listed roads are the M42, A5, A453, A51, A513 and A4091. On OpenStreetMap, forecourts at Swadlincote (DE12 8AA, about 11.1km) and Burntwood (WS7 3XA, about 18.7km) are listed as selling AdBlue at the pump. That data is incomplete.

name: Taunton
intro: Somerset's county town, Taunton is a market town with a thousand-year history, from a 10th-century monastic foundation to the castle the Normans rebuilt on that site in the 12th century. The Grand Western Canal reached it in 1839 and the Bristol and Exeter Railway in 1842. Today it is home to Musgrove Park Hospital, Somerset County Cricket Club and the United Kingdom Hydrographic Office, and its population is 61,667. The TA1 and TA2 postcode districts cover the town. For van and diesel-car drivers, the M5 is among the main roads close by, so motorway runs are an easy part of local journeys. Wellington is 9.8 km away and Bridgwater 13.6 km, while Chard is 18.7 km, Honiton 25.7 km and Burnham-on-Sea 26 km. With three motorway service areas within 21 km, an AdBlue warning on a longer run is rarely far from a place to stop.
roadsText: Taunton's main roads include the M5, A358, A38, A3027, A3038, A3807, A3087 and A3259. Taunton Deane services on the M5 is 5.6 km away, Bridgwater services on the M5 is 12.2 km and Tiverton services on the M5 is 21 km. One station 7.5 km from the town is listed as selling AdBlue at the pump in OpenStreetMap data, though the map is incomplete and others may sell it too.

name: Taverham and Drayton
intro: Taverham sits on the River Wensum about 5 miles (8 km) north-west of Norwich and forms part of the wider Norwich built-up area. Its recent growth has come with the building of Thorpe Marriott, a residential development that straddles the boundary with the neighbouring village of Drayton. Taken together, Taverham and Drayton have 14,989 residents in the Broadland district and the NR8 postcode district. Norwich itself is 6.6 km from the centre and Wymondham 14 km, with Dereham and North Walsham 18.1 km and 19.4 km away. For a driver with an AdBlue warning, Thickthorn Services on the A11 is the nearest listed service area at 9 km in a straight line. The next is more than 56 km away, so the A11 site is by far the closest.
roadsText: Thickthorn Services on the A11 is the nearest service area to Taverham and Drayton, 9 km away in a straight line. The next two are a long way off: Freebridge Park on the A47 at 56.2 km and Beacon Hill Services on the A140 at 60.2 km. A station with a Norwich address (NR11 7HA), 18.6 km away, is listed in OpenStreetMap as selling AdBlue at the pump. That source is incomplete, so treat it as one known option only.

name: Tavistock
intro: An ancient stannary town on the River Tavy, from which it takes its name, Tavistock is a market town in the West Devon district, about 12 miles (19 km) north of Plymouth and 29 miles (47 km) south-west of Exeter. It had 12,675 residents at the 2021 census and is covered by the PL19 postcode district. The ruins of Tavistock Abbey lie in the centre of the town, and Sir Francis Drake is its most famous son. Service areas are thin on the ground from here. The nearest listed is Saltash Services on the A388, 15.5 km away in a straight line, and the next two are around 50 km away. Saltash and Plymouth, at 16.2 km and 16.6 km, are the closest neighbouring towns, with Ivybridge at 23.3 km and Liskeard at 24.7 km, so an AdBlue warning usually means a run of some distance.
roadsText: Saltash Services on the A388 is the only listed service area within 20 km of Tavistock, 15.5 km from the town in a straight line. After that the gap is large: Cornwall Services on the A30 is 49.4 km away and Moto Exeter Services on the M5 is 51.5 km. With an AdBlue warning showing, it makes sense to plan the route before setting off rather than count on passing services.

name: Teignmouth
intro: From the 1800s onwards, Teignmouth grew rapidly from a fishing port associated with the Newfoundland cod industry into a fashionable resort of some note in Georgian times, and it expanded further after the South Devon Railway opened in 1846. The Devon seaside town lies on the north bank of the estuary mouth of the River Teign, about 12 miles (19 km) south of Exeter. Its port still operates, and the town remains a popular seaside and day-trip destination. Teignmouth had 14,932 residents at the 2021 census and is covered by the TQ14 postcode district. Dawlish is 4.3 km away, Kingsteignton 6.7 km, Torquay 7.9 km and Newton Abbot 8.9 km, with Exmouth at 10.8 km. When a van or diesel car shows an AdBlue warning in Teignmouth, the nearest listed service area is Exeter Services on the M5, 17.9 km away in a straight line.
roadsText: All three of the nearest listed service areas to Teignmouth are on the M5. Exeter Services is the closest at 17.9 km in a straight line, followed by Cullompton Services at 35 km and Tiverton Services at 41.3 km. For drivers in TQ14, the M5 near Exeter is the first realistic services stop, and road distances will be longer than these figures.

name: Telford
intro: To the south of Telford lies the Ironbridge Gorge, and The Wrekin hill is close to the town. Telford sits near the River Severn and close to Shropshire's eastern boundary, and is the main administrative centre for Telford and Wrekin Council. At the 2021 census the town had 156,896 residents. The M54, completed in 1983, links Telford with the West Midlands conurbation, with Wolverhampton 19 miles (31km) to the south-east and Birmingham 28 miles away. Other listed roads are the A5, A442, A518, A464, A5223, A4640 and A4169, and postcodes include TF1 to TF5, TF7 and TF8. The nearest towns are some distance off: Newport at about 11.2km, Bridgnorth 17.3km and Shrewsbury 18.9km. Driving here can mean local runs across a large town plus motorway trips towards the West Midlands. Telford services is about 5.1km away, while the next service areas are 21.9km or more away.
roadsText: One service area stands out for Telford: Telford services on the M54, about 5.1km away. After that the gap is large, with Adastra services on the A41 at about 21.9km and a truck stop on the A5 at 27.7km. The M54 and A5 head the listed roads, followed by the A442, A518, A464, A5223, A4640 and A4169. For a driver in the TF postcodes with an AdBlue warning, the M54 stop is the obvious one to aim for.

name: Tewkesbury
intro: Where the River Severn meets the River Avon, in the north of Gloucestershire, stands the market town of Tewkesbury. It grew up after Tewkesbury Abbey was built in the twelfth century and became an important trading point, and it gives its name to the Borough of Tewkesbury. The town has a population of 14,387 and is covered by the GL20 postcode district. The Worcestershire border lies close by, marked largely by the Carrant Brook. Tewkesbury is described as spending the winter months surrounded by water, which is worth remembering when planning a winter route to a service area with an AdBlue warning showing. The nearest listed services are on the M5, 8 km away in a straight line. Bishop's Cleeve is the closest neighbouring town at 7.5 km, with Cheltenham at 11.3 km, Churchdown at 11.8 km, and Gloucester and Brockworth both 16 km away.
roadsText: RoadChef Strensham Services on the M5 is the nearest service area to Tewkesbury, 8 km from the centre in a straight line. Westmorland Gloucester Services, also on the M5, is 19.8 km away, and Ross Spur Services on the M50 is 29.8 km. With two M5 sites inside 20 km, the motorway is the natural direction to head if an AdBlue warning comes on in GL20. Road distances will be longer than these figures.

name: Thame
intro: The River Thame gives this Oxfordshire market town its name, flowing along the north side of Thame and forming part of the county border with Buckinghamshire. The town lies about 13 miles (21 km) east of Oxford, 10 miles (16 km) south-west of Aylesbury and 40 miles (64 km) north-west of London, and its parish includes the hamlet of Moreton just to the south. The 2011 census recorded 11,561 people in the parish, and the town's postcode district is OX9. Other towns are some distance away: Aylesbury is 13.9 km, Oxford 19.4 km, and Bicester and High Wycombe both 20.8 km. For a driver with an AdBlue warning, though, services are close. Thame Services on the A418 is 1.1 km from the town in a straight line, and Oxford Services on the M40 is 8.3 km away.
roadsText: Thame Services on the A418 is just 1.1 km from Thame in a straight line, the closest listed service area. Oxford Services on the M40 is 8.3 km away, while Peartree Services on the A44 is much further at 21.7 km. These are straight-line figures, so the drive to each will be longer.

name: Thatcham
intro: Just 4.8 km east of Newbury, Thatcham is a market town in the valley of the River Kennet in West Berkshire, and together the two form a built-up area of over 70,000 residents. Thatcham itself had a population of 25,464 in 2021. The town lies on the A4 Bath Road, the historic main road between London and Bristol, and is 23 km west of Reading and 87 km west of London. It also has a long history, and is a claimant to the title of oldest continuously inhabited place in Great Britain. The RG19 and RG18 postcode districts cover the town. Local trips tend to be short, with Newbury next door, Tadley 8.6 km away and Basingstoke 18.1 km. Reading is 20.6 km and Didcot 23.6 km, so a diesel van here can easily cover both town streets and longer runs in a working day.
roadsText: The main roads through the area are the A4, A339 and A343. For services, Chieveley on the M4 is the nearest at 6.9 km, Tot Hill on the A34 is 8.4 km and Reading services on the M4 is 15.4 km. A station on the Swallowfield By-pass (RG7 1LZ), 18.6 km away, is listed as selling AdBlue at the pump in OpenStreetMap data. That data is incomplete, so other forecourts may stock it too.

name: Thetford
intro: Sitting on the A11 between Norwich and London, just east of Thetford Forest, Thetford is a market town and civil parish in the Breckland District of Norfolk. There has been a settlement here since the Iron Age, and Thetford Castle was established shortly after the Norman Conquest. After the Second World War Thetford became an overspill town, taking people from London, and its population increased substantially. The civil parish covers 29.55 km2 and had 24,340 people in 2011. The railway station is on the Breckland line. Main roads listed are the A11, A134, A1066, A1075 and A1088. Neighbouring towns are not close: Watton is 18.4 km away, Bury St Edmunds 18.7 km and Attleborough 21.5 km, with Soham, Newmarket and Stowmarket all between 28.9 and 30.6 km. The postcode district is IP24.
roadsText: The A11, A134, A1066, A1075 and A1088 are listed for Thetford. Service areas are distant: Beacon Hill Services on the A140 is 37.4 km away, Thickthorn Services on the A11 38.5 km and Freebridge Park on the A47 44 km. Plan for that distance if an AdBlue warning comes on.

name: Thornaby-on-Tees
intro: Usually known simply as Thornaby, this town on the south bank of the River Tees falls within the Borough of Stockton-on-Tees and the Tees Valley area. Its modern town centre was built on the north-eastern part of the old Thornaby airfield, 3.2 km south-east of Stockton-on-Tees. Thornaby became a municipal borough in 1892, lost that status in 1968 when the County Borough of Teesside was created, and returned as a civil parish in 1996. The 2011 census recorded 24,741 people in the parish, which spans the TS17 and TS18 postcode districts. Distances to neighbouring towns are short: Stockton-on-Tees is 3.2 km away, Ingleby Barwick 4.3 km and Middlesbrough 5 km, with Egglescliffe and Billingham both 5.3 km. For a van or diesel car based in the town, a lot of everyday driving is therefore short hops across the Tees Valley.
roadsText: Two service areas sit 8.5 km from Thornaby: Teesside Truck Stop on the A66 and Wolviston Services on the A689. A southbound service area on the A19 is 11.5 km away. All three are a short drive out of town, which makes them practical places to pull in if a dashboard warning appears on a longer run.

name: Thornbury
intro: Between 2011 and 2021, the population of Thornbury grew from 12,063 to 14,496, according to the census. The market town lies in South Gloucestershire, about 12 miles (19 km) north of Bristol. Its roots go back a long way: a village called Thornbyrig is recorded at the end of the 9th century, and the Domesday Book of 1086 lists a manor of Turneberie. The town is also a Britain in Bloom award winner. Thornbury is covered by the BS35 postcode district. The nearest listed towns are all around 9 km away, with Bradley Stoke at 9.1 km, Frampton Cotterell and Winterbourne at 9.2 km, Yate at 9.5 km and Patchway at 9.6 km. For a van or diesel car with an AdBlue warning, two motorway service areas are close: Severn View Services on the M48 at 7.2 km in a straight line and Michaelwood Services on the M5 at 8 km.
roadsText: Thornbury has two motorway service areas within 8 km in a straight line: Severn View Services on the M48 at 7.2 km and Michaelwood Services on the M5 at 8 km. Avon Lodge on the A4 is further at 16.7 km. With options on both the M48 and the M5, drivers in BS35 can pick whichever suits their route. Road distances will be longer than these figures.

name: Thorne
intro: Doncaster (North) Services on the M180 is only about 3 km from Thorne in a straight line, which is useful to know for any van or diesel car showing an AdBlue warning. Thorne is a market town and civil parish in the City of Doncaster, South Yorkshire, and was part of the West Riding until 1974. Its population was 17,295 at the 2011 census. The town uses the DN8 postcode district. Dunscroft and Hatfield is about 5.4 km away, Kirk Sandall and Edenthorpe 9.3 km, Armthorpe 10.1 km and Goole 11.7 km, while Doncaster itself is about 14.5 km off. Beyond the M180 site, the next service areas are much further out, with Barnsdale Bar on the A1 at 18.1 km and Ferrybridge Services on the M62 at 22 km.
roadsText: The closest service area to Thorne is Doncaster (North) Services on the M180, about 3 km in a straight line. Barnsdale Bar Services on the A1 is about 18.1 km away and Ferrybridge Services on the M62 about 22 km. OpenStreetMap lists a station in Doncaster (DN4 0TP), about 18.6 km away, as selling AdBlue at the pump. Its AdBlue data is incomplete, so other stations may sell it too.

name: Thornton
intro: About 4 miles (6 km) north of Blackpool and 2 miles (3 km) south of Fleetwood, Thornton is a village in the Borough of Wyre. Its civil parish became an urban district in 1900 and was renamed Thornton-Cleveleys in 1927, tying its name to nearby Cleveleys. In 2011 the Thornton built-up area sub division had 18,941 residents. Postcode districts FY5 and FY6 cover the area. Cleveleys is about 2.3 km away and Poulton-le-Fylde 3.3 km, with Fleetwood at 4.4 km and Blackpool at 8.9 km. Lytham St Anne's is around 14 km off. The main thing for a driver dealing with an AdBlue warning to know is the distance to motorway services: the nearest service areas are all on the M6, and the closest of them is about 18.5 km away.
roadsText: Motorway services are some way from Thornton. The nearest service area is Lancaster Services on the M6, about 18.5 km away. Charnock Richard Services, also on the M6, is around 34.1 km off, and Burton-in-Kendal Services roughly 37.9 km. That means reaching a motorway service area involves a drive of at least 18.5 km from Thornton.

name: Thundersley and South Benfleet
intro: This built-up area, as the Office for National Statistics defines it, takes in Thundersley, Hadleigh, Daws Heath and South Benfleet, and had 49,885 people at the 2021 census. It lies in the Borough of Castle Point in south-east Essex, 31 miles (50 km) east of Charing Cross and 23 miles south of the county town of Chelmsford. Thundersley itself is a village and former civil parish that includes the hamlet of Daws Heath. Plenty of main roads are listed for the area: the A13, A130 and A127, along with the A1245, A129, A1015, A132 and A1321. Neighbouring places are close together here. Rayleigh is 3.7 km away, Canvey Island 4.7 km, Wickford 6.4 km, Hockley and Hawkwell 7.4 km, Southend-on-Sea 8.6 km and Rochford 9.3 km. Postcode districts are SS6 and SS7.
roadsText: Roads listed for the area are the A13, A130, A127, A1245, A129, A1015, A132 and A1321. The closest service area is Orsett Cock Services on the A13, 13.4 km away. Boreham Services on the A131 is 21.7 km off, and Tollgate Services on the A2 is 21.9 km away, so only one listed service area is within 15 km.

name: Tidworth
intro: Two villages, North Tidworth and South Tidworth, grew into the modern garrison town of Tidworth, which is now dominated by Tidworth Camp, a large British Army site, with Swinton Barracks in the west of the parish. The town is on the eastern edge of Salisbury Plain in south-east Wiltshire, lying on both sides of the A338 about 3½ miles (5.6 km) north of the A303. Andover is about 8 miles (13 km) to the east and Salisbury 13 miles (21 km) to the south-south-west. The parish had around 10,600 residents at the 2011 census, and the SP9 postcode district covers it. With an AdBlue warning showing, the A303 is the road to know: all three listed service areas are on it, the nearest 9.7 km away in a straight line. Amesbury is the closest neighbouring town at 10.4 km.
roadsText: Tidworth lies on both sides of the A338, about 3½ miles (5.6 km) north of the A303, and every listed service area nearby is on the A303. Weyhill Services is the closest at 9.7 km in a straight line, with The Buck Services at 18.8 km and Barton Stacey Services at 21.3 km. Road distances to each will be longer than these figures.

name: Tilbury
intro: A port town on the north bank of the Thames, Tilbury is in the borough of Thurrock and is part of the Port of London, with a major deep-water port. It adjoins Grays, lies 24 miles (39 km) east of central London and is the southernmost point in Essex. The town was established in the late 19th century, mostly on land from the parish of Chadwell St Mary, and its built-up area had 14,185 people at the 2021 census. Its postcode district is RM18. The Gravesend to Tilbury ferry was an ancient and important crossing point. Chadwell St Mary is 2.3 km away and Grays 3.1 km. For an AdBlue warning, three service areas lie within about 7 km in a straight line, though road distances to each will be longer.
roadsText: Three service areas lie within about 7 km of Tilbury in a straight line: Tollgate Services on the A2 at 5 km, Orsett Cock Services on the A13 at 6 km and Thurrock Services on the M25 at 7.1 km.
