Road distances will be longer, so check the route before setting off. A forecourt in Strood (ME2 2NY), 11.9 km away, is listed in OpenStreetMap as selling AdBlue at the pump; that data is incomplete.

name: Tipton
intro: For a van or diesel car in Tipton, much of the driving is likely to be short urban hops, because the industrial Black Country town is contiguous with Darlaston, Dudley, Wednesbury and Bilston. It lies north-west of Birmingham and south-east of Wolverhampton in the borough of Sandwell, and takes in the villages and suburbs of Tipton Green, Ocker Hill, Dudley Port, Horseley Heath and Great Bridge. The 2011 census recorded 38,777 residents. Postcode districts listed for the town are DY4, WV14, WS10, DY1 and B70. The M6 and M5 are on the road list, alongside the A41, A461, A4123, A4444, A463 and A454. Coseley is about 2.7km away and Bilston 3.1km. The nearest motorway services are 11.7km or more away, so a warning picked up locally is not always near a service area.
roadsText: The nearest service area to Tipton is Hilton Park services on the M6, 11.7km away. Frankley services on the M5 is 12.4km and Norton Canes services on the M6 Toll 15.3km. Much closer, OpenStreetMap lists a forecourt in Warley, about 4km away, as selling AdBlue at the pump, plus an HGV-only site in Birmingham (16.9km) and a forecourt in Burntwood (17.7km). The data is incomplete. Listed roads are the M6, M5, A41, A461, A4123, A4444, A463 and A454.

name: Tiverton
intro: The commercial and administrative centre of the Mid Devon district, Tiverton is a market town on the River Exe, about 12 miles (19 km) north of Exeter and 18 miles (29 km) west-southwest of Taunton. It had 22,291 residents at the 2021 census and is covered by the EX16 postcode district. Neighbouring towns are not especially close: Wellington is 20 km away, Exeter 20.8 km and Honiton 23.6 km, so even the closest listed town is 20 km off. If a van or diesel car shows an AdBlue warning here, the M5 is the key road. All three of the nearest listed service areas are on it, with Cullompton Services at 8.4 km in a straight line, Tiverton Services at 9.3 km and Exeter Services at 20.9 km.
roadsText: All three of the nearest listed service areas to Tiverton are on the M5. Cullompton Services is 8.4 km away in a straight line, Tiverton Services is 9.3 km, and Exeter Services is 20.9 km. With the two closest only 8.4 km and 9.3 km away, a driver in EX16 has a fairly short run to motorway services. Distances by road will be longer.

name: Todmorden
intro: Three steep-sided Pennine valleys meet at Todmorden, a market town in the Upper Calder Valley surrounded by moorland. It lies in Calderdale, West Yorkshire, 17 miles (27 km) north-east of Manchester, 8 miles (13 km) south-east of Burnley and 9 miles (14 km) west of Halifax, and had 15,481 residents in 2011. The River Calder and Walsden Water, which run through the town, once marked the historic boundary between Yorkshire and Lancashire. Postcodes here fall in OL14. Bacup is about 6.6 km away and Littleborough 7.6 km, with Rawtenstall, Rochdale and Burnley all between 11.3 km and 12.5 km. For a driver with an AdBlue warning, the nearest listed service area is Hollin Bank Service Station on the M65, around 15.5 km in a straight line, with Birch Services on the M62 at about 18.1 km.
roadsText: From Todmorden, the closest service areas in a straight line are Hollin Bank Service Station on the M65 (about 15.5 km), Birch Services on the M62 (18.1 km) and Hartshead Moor Services, also on the M62 (23.5 km). Road distances will be longer than these straight-line figures, so allow for that when deciding which to head for.

name: Tonbridge
intro: Tonbridge (historically spelt Tunbridge) is a market town on the River Medway in Kent, in the borough of Tonbridge and Malling, with an estimated 41,293 people in 2019. It lies 4 miles north of Royal Tunbridge Wells, 12 miles south-west of Maidstone and 29 miles south-east of London, and the TN9, TN10 and TN11 postcode districts cover the area. The main roads listed are the A21, A26, A227, A228 and A2014. No motorway appears in that list, and the nearest service area, on the M25, is 19km away. Royal Tunbridge Wells is 7km away and Sevenoaks 11.4km, while Larkfield is 16.2km and Maidstone 18.6km. For a diesel driver, local trips are mostly on A roads between these Kent towns, and a warning light is worth acting on before a long run.
roadsText: Main roads listed around Tonbridge are the A26, A2014, A21, A227 and A228. The nearest service areas are Clacket Lane Services on the M25 (19km), Maidstone Services on the M20 (24.4km) and Tollgate Services on the A2 (25.2km). One station about 8.4km away is listed as selling AdBlue at the pump. OpenStreetMap data is incomplete, so other forecourts may sell it as well.

name: Tonypandy
intro: A former coal mining town in the Rhondda Fawr Valley, Tonypandy was the scene of the 1910 Tonypandy riots. Its community boundary is drawn tightly around the central part of the urban area and held just 3,750 people in 2011, but the Office for National Statistics defines a much larger Tonypandy built-up area, covering much of the Rhondda Fawr valley and the lower Rhondda Fach valley, with 62,545 people, and a smaller sub division with 17,789. The CF40 postcode district covers the town, which is in Rhondda Cynon Taf and is served by a station on the Rhondda Line. Rhondda is 2.7 km away, Porth 3.5 km and Tonyrefail 5 km. With an AdBlue warning showing, the nearest listed service area is on the M4, 12.8 km away in a straight line.
roadsText: All three of the nearest service areas to Tonypandy are on the M4. Welcome Break Sarn Park Services is 12.8 km away in a straight line, Moto Cardiff West Services is 16.2 km and Welcome Break Cardiff Gate Services is 24.3 km. Road distances from the valley will be longer than these figures, so allow for that if a warning comes on.

name: Tonyrefail
intro: From a rural hamlet, Tonyrefail grew into an industrial village in the second half of the 19th century, as coal and steel became synonymous with the South Wales Valleys. The village and community, in Rhondda Cynon Taf County Borough, sits at the head of the River Ely, 4 miles (6.4 km) north-west of Llantrisant, with Trebanog approximately 1.5 miles (2.4 km) away and Williamstown about 2 miles (3.2 km). The 2001 census recorded 11,035 people. The village is in the CF39 postcode district. Porth is 4 km away, Tonypandy 5 km, Pontypridd 7.3 km and Church Village 7.6 km, with Rhondda at 7.7 km. For an AdBlue warning, the M4 is where the nearest services are, with two listed sites at 11.3 km and 11.6 km in a straight line.
roadsText: Tonyrefail's three nearest service areas are on the M4. Sarn Park Services and Cardiff West Services are almost the same distance away, at 11.3 km and 11.6 km in a straight line, and Cardiff Gate Services is 21.3 km. Road distances will be longer than these figures, and which of the first two is quicker to reach will depend on the direction of travel.

name: Torquay
intro: Torquay sits on the north side of Tor Bay, adjoining Paignton to the west and looking across the bay to the fishing port of Brixham. It is part of the Torbay unitary authority area, 29 km south of Exeter and 45 km east-north-east of Plymouth, and the built-up area had 52,037 people at the 2021 census. Its economy was first based on fishing and agriculture before it grew into a fashionable seaside resort in the early 19th century, known for its mild climate. The TQ1 and TQ2 postcode districts cover the town. Several towns sit close by: Newton Abbot is 7.4 km away, Paignton 7.5 km, Teignmouth 7.9 km and Kingsteignton 8.1 km, with Brixham at 10.9 km. With no motorway among the roads near the town, most diesel journeys here are on A roads, and the nearest motorway service area is a 25.7 km run away.
roadsText: Around Torquay the main roads are the A380, A379, A3022 and A381. The nearest service area is Exeter services on the M5, 25.7 km away. Cullompton services on the M5 is 42.9 km and Tiverton services on the M5 is 49.2 km, so every planned stop on a longer trip is some way up the M5 rather than close to town.

name: Totton
intro: Totton is a town within the civil parish of Totton and Eling, in the New Forest district of Hampshire, with 28,094 residents at the 2021 census and a single postcode district, SO40. What stands out for drivers is the road list. Two motorways, the M27 and M271, appear alongside the A36, A35, A31, A33, A326 and A336. Southampton is 8.3km away and Romsey 8.5km, with Hythe and Dibden Purlieu at 9.5km and Chandler's Ford at 11.4km. Service areas are close as well, with the three nearest on the A36, M27 and A31. For a van or diesel car with an AdBlue warning, that combination means short runs to neighbouring towns, motorway access and several nearby places to stop.
roadsText: The M271, M27, A36, A33, A336, A326, A35 and A31 are the main roads listed around Totton. Three service areas are close by: West Wellow Services on the A36 (4.4km), Rownhams Services on the M27 (5.8km) and Rufus Stone on the A31 (8.5km). That gives a driver with an AdBlue warning a nearby stop on the A36, the M27 or the A31.

name: Towcester
intro: Watling Street, today's A5, runs through the history of Towcester: the town was the Roman settlement of Lactodurum on that road and is one of the oldest continuously inhabited settlements in the country. It is a market town in West Northamptonshire and was the administrative centre of the South Northamptonshire district from 1974 to 2021. The town has a population of 11,333 and its postcode district is NN12. Northampton is 13.7 km away, Buckingham 14.6 km and Brackley 15.4 km, with Milton Keynes 18.3 km off. For van and diesel car drivers, the town's position on main routes is the useful fact: two roadside stops are within 2 km of the town, and Northampton Services on the M1 is 9.5 km away.
roadsText: Towcester sits on the A5, the modern line of Watling Street. Towcester Services on the A43 is 1.2 km from the town, Jacks Hill Cafe & Truck Stop on the A5 is 2 km away, and Northampton Services on the M1 is 9.5 km away. That puts three stops within 9.5 km, across the A43, the A5 and the M1.

name: Tower Hamlets
intro: Immediately east of the City of London, on the north bank of the River Thames, Tower Hamlets spans the traditional East End and much of the regenerated London Docklands, including Canary Wharf. The borough was formed in 1965 by merging the former metropolitan boroughs of Stepney, Poplar and Bethnal Green, and its 2019 population was estimated at 324,745. Main roads include the A11, A12, A13, A102, A107, A1203, A1205 and A1261, and its postcodes take in E1, E1W, E2, E3 and E14, along with SE16 and EC3N. Neighbouring boroughs are close: Hackney is 4.1km away, Southwark 4.4km, Newham 5.3km and Islington 5.4km. With neighbours this close, a diesel van can cross several borough boundaries in a day, so knowing the postcode district is the quickest way to say where an AdBlue fault has left the vehicle.
roadsText: Main roads in and around Tower Hamlets include the A1205, A11, A13, A1203, A1261, A107, A12 and A102. The nearest service areas listed are London Gateway Services on the M1 (20.3km), Thurrock Services on the M25 (21.6km) and South Mimms Services on the A1(M) (22.9km). OpenStreetMap, whose AdBlue records are incomplete, has a station at Catford (8.4km) and another 8.5km away listed as selling AdBlue at the pump.

name: Tranent
intro: Once a major mining town, Tranent now works largely as a commuter town for Edinburgh, whose city centre is 9.1 miles away. It is one of the oldest towns in East Lothian, built on a gentle slope about 90 metres above sea level, and has roughly 12,140 residents in the EH33 postcode district. The A1 is the road that matters most here. It runs through the parish to the north of the town, separating Tranent from Meadowmill and the ports of Cockenzie and Port Seton, and it replaced the old post road that once ran straight through the town. Prestonpans is 2.4 km away and Musselburgh 6.2 km, with Dalkeith, Mayfield and Haddington all within about 11 km. For a driver with an AdBlue warning, two listed service areas on the A1 are close by.
roadsText: Two of the three nearest listed service areas sit on the A1, the road that passes north of Tranent: MacMerry at 4.5 km and Musselburgh Services at 7.1 km, both straight-line distances from the town centre. Dreghorn Services on the A720 is further away at 18.1 km. So the A1 is where the closest stops are for a van or diesel car showing an AdBlue warning.

name: Tredegar
intro: One of the early centres of the Industrial Revolution in Wales, Tredegar is a town on the banks of the Sirhowy River in the county borough of Blaenau Gwent, within the historic boundaries of Monmouthshire. At the 2011 census its wards, Tredegar Central and West, Sirhowy and Georgetown, listed a combined population of 15,103. The NP22 postcode district covers the town. Ebbw Vale is the closest neighbour, only 2.6 km away, with Abertillery at 8.8 km and Merthyr Tydfil at 9.7 km, while Blackwood is 12.9 km off. If an AdBlue warning comes on, the key point is that none of the listed service areas is near: the closest, Welcome Break Cardiff Gate Services on the M4, is 27.9 km away in a straight line, and the two A40 sites are 29.1 km and 29.7 km away.
roadsText: None of the listed service areas is close to Tredegar. Welcome Break Cardiff Gate Services on the M4 is the nearest at 27.9 km in a straight line, with Glanusk Services on the A40 at 29.1 km and Monmouth A40 Services at 29.7 km. Road distances will be longer, so plan the route before setting off with an AdBlue warning showing.

name: Tring
intro: Linked to London by the A41, the Grand Union Canal and the West Coast Main Line, Tring is a market town in the Borough of Dacorum, set in a gap through the Chiltern Hills 30 miles (50 km) from central London. It received its market charter in 1315 and is now largely a commuter town. The population was 12,427 in 2021, and the town is covered by the HP23 postcode district. Berkhamsted is 7.3 km away, Chesham 9.8 km and Aylesbury 10.1 km. For a van or diesel car with an AdBlue warning, Bourne End Services on the A41 is the nearest listed service area at 11 km in a straight line, with Toddington Services on the M1 at 19.8 km. Dunstable, Leighton Buzzard and Amersham are all between 13 km and 14 km off.
roadsText: The A41 connects Tring with London, and Bourne End Services on that road is the closest service area, 11 km from the centre in a straight line. Toddington Services on the M1 is 19.8 km away and Thame Services on the A418 is 22.4 km. From HP23, the A41 site is the nearest of the three, and road distances to all of them will be longer.

name: Troon
intro: A seaside town and sea port on the west coast of Ayrshire, Troon lies about eight miles (thirteen kilometres) north of Ayr and three miles (five kilometres) north-west of Glasgow Prestwick Airport. The port has ferry and freight services and a yacht marina, and since March 2024 a ferry service has run to Brodick on the Isle of Arran. The 2022 population, including the Barassie area but not the nearby village of Loans, was 15,261. Postcode district KA10 covers the town. Prestwick is about 7 km away in a straight line and Irvine 8 km, with Kilmarnock at 11.7 km and Kilwinning at 12.1 km. If an AdBlue warning comes on in a van or diesel car, motorway service areas are far off: the nearest three, all on the M74, are between about 46.6 km and 48.8 km away.
roadsText: Troon is a long way from a motorway service area. The nearest three are all on the M74: Hamilton Services at about 46.6 km in a straight line, Bothwell Services at about 47 km and the M74 Truck Stop at about 48.8 km. Drivers in the KA10 district, including those using the port, should allow for a longer journey by road than those figures suggest.

name: Trowbridge
intro: Nicknamed the Manchester of the West, Trowbridge was the foremost centre of woollen cloth production in south-west England in the late 18th and early 19th centuries, helped by the Kennet and Avon canal to the north. Long a market town, it is the county town of Wiltshire, on the River Biss in the west of the county and close to the border with Somerset. It is 13 km south-east of Bath, 32 km from Bristol and 50 km south-west of Swindon, and its parish had 37,169 people in 2021, with 43,753 across the wider area. The parish also takes in Longfield, Lower Studley, Upper Studley, Studley Green and Trowle Common. The BA14 postcode district covers the town. Westbury is 6.9 km away and Melksham 7.4 km, with Corsham, Bath, Frome and Warminster all between 11.7 km and 13.6 km, so a lot of local driving runs between these towns.
roadsText: Trowbridge's main roads are the A361, A350, A363 and A366. The nearest service area is Warminster services on the A350, 12 km away. For motorway services, Leigh Delamere on the M4 is 20.8 km away and Chippenham Pit Stop on the M4 is 21.8 km. With no motorway among the roads near the town, those are the closest places to stop on a longer run.

name: Truro
intro: Cornwall's county town and only city, Truro is the southernmost city in the United Kingdom, lying 232 miles (373 km) west-south-west of London. It is the county's centre for administration, leisure and shopping, and home to Cornwall Council and the county's Courts of Justice. The built-up area had 23,060 people at the 2021 census, including the Gloweth and Treliske areas in the neighbouring parish of Kenwyn. Truro grew as a trading port and as a stannary town for tin mining, and was awarded city status in 1877. It is covered by the TR1 postcode district. Penryn is 11.4 km away, Redruth 12.6 km, Falmouth 12.8 km and Newquay 16.6 km. With an AdBlue warning showing, the nearest listed service area is Cornwall Services on the A30, 24.6 km away in a straight line.
roadsText: The nearest listed service area to Truro is Cornwall Services on the A30, 24.6 km away in a straight line. Saltash Services on the A388 is 60.4 km off and Roundswell Service Area on the A39 is 112.1 km. With the closest option more than 24 km away, drivers in TR1 are better off acting on an AdBlue warning early rather than relying on reaching services.

name: Tyldesley
intro: North of Chat Moss near the foothills of the West Pennine Moors, Tyldesley is a market town in the Metropolitan Borough of Wigan. It is eight miles (13 kilometres) southeast of Wigan and nine miles (14 kilometres) northwest of Manchester, within the boundaries of the historic county of Lancashire. At the 2001 census the built-up area subdivision, excluding Shakerley, had 16,142 residents. A Roman road between Coccium (Wigan) and Mamucium (Manchester) passed through the township, and its remains were evident during the 19th century. The M29 postcode district covers the town. Atherton is only about 2.6 km away and Little Hulton 3.5 km, with Walkden, Leigh, Worsley and Westhoughton all between 4.6 km and 5.6 km. For a driver with an AdBlue warning, the nearest motorway service area is Rivington Services on the M61, around 12.5 km away.
roadsText: Rivington Services on the M61 is the closest service area to Tyldesley, about 12.5 km away. Burtonwood Services on the M62 is around 15.6 km off and Birch Services, also on the M62, about 16.4 km. OpenStreetMap has stations under Warrington at about 11 km and 17.3 km, and one under Manchester at 11.8 km, listed as selling AdBlue at the pump. That data is incomplete.

name: Tynemouth
intro: The medieval Tynemouth Priory and Castle stand on a headland overlooking the mouth of the River Tyne and the North Sea, with the town centre immediately west of it. Tynemouth is a coastal town in North Tyneside, on the north side of the river mouth and eight miles (13 kilometres) east-northeast of Newcastle upon Tyne. Until 1974 the town was a county borough that included North Shields, and the Tynemouth built-up area, which still includes North Shields, had 60,605 people at the 2021 census; Tynemouth itself had 10,256. That matters when describing a location: a van with an AdBlue warning in the Tynemouth area may in fact be in North Shields. Roads listed for the town include the A19, A192, A193, A194, A1018, A1058, A1108 and A1300, and its postcodes include NE27, NE28, NE29, NE30 and NE33. Whitley Bay is 3.6km away and Wallsend 3.7km.
roadsText: Main roads around Tynemouth include the A1058, A19, A194, A1018, A1300, A1108, A193 and A192. Seaton Burn Services on the A19 is the nearest listed service area at 12.2km, with Washington Services on the A1(M) at 15.1km and Easington Services on the A19 at 24.4km. OpenStreetMap is incomplete, but it has a station in Newcastle upon Tyne, 8.8km away, listed as selling AdBlue at the pump.

name: Uckfield
intro: Uckfield stands on the River Uck, one of the tributaries of the River Ouse, on the southern edge of the Weald. It is a town in the Wealden District of East Sussex with a population of 15,037, and its postcode district is TN22. The town is some way from its neighbours: the closest, Crowborough, is 10.4 km away, followed by Lewes at 12.5 km and Haywards Heath at 13.9 km, with Hailsham and Burgess Hill both around 16 km off. That spacing matters for a driver who sees an AdBlue warning. None of the listed service areas is close. The nearest, Polegate Services on the A22, is 18.4 km away in a straight line, and the other two, Ricebridge Services (Hickstead) and Pyecombe Services, are both on the A23 at just over 20 km. Hassocks and Hurstpierpoint lies 18.8 km away.
roadsText: Uckfield is at least 18.4 km from the nearest listed service area, Polegate Services on the A22, measured in a straight line. Ricebridge Services (Hickstead) on the A23 is 20.3 km away and Pyecombe Services, also on the A23, is 20.5 km. With services this far out, the road journey will be longer still, so it helps to plan a stop early if an AdBlue warning comes on.

name: Ulverston
intro: Within the Furness Peninsula, just north-west of Morecambe Bay and a few miles south of the Lake District National Park, Ulverston is a market town and civil parish in Westmorland and Furness, Cumbria. It was historically in Lancashire. Barrow-in-Furness is 10 miles (16 km) to the south-west, Kendal 25 miles (40 km) to the north-east and Lancaster 39 miles (63 km) to the east. The parish population rose from 11,678 at the 2011 census to 11,823 in 2021. The LA12 postcode district covers the town. For a van or diesel car with an AdBlue warning, those distances matter, and motorway services are a long way off too: the nearest is on the M6, about 23 km away.
roadsText: The nearest service area to Ulverston is Burton-in-Kendal Services on the M6, about 23 km away. Killington Lake Services, also on the M6, is around 32.5 km off, and Lancaster Services on the M6 about 33.3 km. With every listed service area more than 20 km from the town, drivers around the LA12 district should allow for a long run to reach motorway services.

name: Uppermill
intro: Historically in the West Riding of Yorkshire, Uppermill is a village in the civil parish of Saddleworth, now in the Metropolitan Borough of Oldham. It lies on the River Tame in a valley amongst the South Pennines, with the Peak District National Park directly to the east, 5 miles (8.0 km) east of Oldham and 11 miles (17.7 km) northeast of Manchester. Uppermill and the neighbouring village of Dobcross have a combined population of 7,500. The OL3 postcode district covers the area. Mossley is about 3.3 km away and Lees 3.5 km, with Oldham at 6.1 km and Shaw and Stalybridge both around 6.9 km. For a driver with an AdBlue warning, the nearest motorway service area is Birch Services on the M62, about 14.8 km off, and the next ones are more than 25 km away.
roadsText: Birch Services on the M62 is the nearest service area to Uppermill, about 14.8 km away. Hartshead Moor services, also on the M62, is around 25.6 km off, and Woolley Edge Services on the M1 about 31.7 km. OpenStreetMap has a site roughly 9.3 km away listed as selling AdBlue at the pump, plus a station under Manchester at about 18.4 km. Those records are incomplete.

name: Urmston
intro: Five miles south-west of Manchester city centre, Urmston is a Trafford town of 41,731 people (2021 census) that was historically part of Lancashire. The River Mersey forms its southern boundary, Stretford lies to the east, Flixton to the west and Davyhulme to the north of the town centre. Until the railway arrived in 1873 it was a small farming community; the line turned it into a residential town for the middle classes. The M41, M17, M30 and M32 postcode districts cover the area today. Irlam is 3.4 km away, Eccles 3.6 km, Stretford 3.8 km and Sale 4.6 km. For longer runs, the M60, M62 and M602 are all listed among the roads around Urmston. If an AdBlue warning appears, the nearest services and listed pumps are set out below.
roadsText: The M60, M62 and M602 are listed around Urmston, with the A5081, A57, A5181, A5145 and A56. The nearest service areas are Lymm Services on the M6 (13.7 km), Birch Services on the M62 (15.8 km) and Tabley Hill Service Station on the M6 (16.1 km). A station in Manchester (M25 3AJ) at 10.9 km, one in Warrington (WA3 6RW) at 11.1 km and a third at 16.6 km are listed on OpenStreetMap as selling AdBlue at the pump. That map data is incomplete.

name: Uttoxeter
intro: Uttoxeter's road links to Burton upon Trent, Stoke-on-Trent and Derby all use the A50. Burton upon Trent is 14 miles (23 km) away via the A50 and the A38, Stoke-on-Trent 18 miles (29 km) via the A50, and Derby 19 miles (31 km) via the A50 and the A38. Stafford is 14 miles (23 km) via the A518, and Rugeley lies 11 miles (18 km) to the south-west via the A518 and the B5013. The market town and civil parish is in the East Staffordshire borough, near the Derbyshire county border. The population was 14,014 at the 2021 Census, and the postcode district is ST14. Cheadle is 12.5 km away. Uttoxeter Services on the A50, just 1.4 km away in a straight line, is the obvious stop for a van or diesel car with an AdBlue warning.
roadsText: Uttoxeter Services on the A50 is the nearest service area, only 1.4 km from the town in a straight line. The A50 also links Uttoxeter with Stoke-on-Trent, Burton upon Trent and Derby, while the A518 runs to Stafford. The next nearest service areas are much further off: Stafford Services on the M6 at 20 km and Stone Services on the A34 at 20.3 km.

name: Verwood
intro: In eastern Dorset, 10 miles (16 km) north of Bournemouth and 13 miles (21 km) north-east of Poole as the crow flies, Verwood is a town on the River Crane, which further on becomes the Moors River. The civil parish also takes in the extended village of Three Legged Cross, and in 2014 it had 15,170 residents according to Dorset County Council. The town is covered by the BH31 postcode district. Its closest neighbouring towns are West Moors at 5.9 km, Ringwood at 7.7 km, Ferndown at 8.4 km and Wimborne Minster at 10.2 km, with Bournemouth 15.3 km away. If a van or diesel car shows an AdBlue warning in or around Verwood, the nearest listed service area is Picket Post Services on the A31, 10.8 km away in a straight line, and the next one along that road is 18.1 km away.
roadsText: Picket Post Services on the A31 is the nearest service area to Verwood, 10.8 km from the centre in a straight line, with Rufus Stone, also on the A31, at 18.1 km and West Wellow Services on the A36 at 25.5 km. MFG Creekmoor, a Shell site in Poole (BH17 7FR) 17.8 km away, is listed in OpenStreetMap as selling AdBlue at the pump. That data is incomplete, so nearer forecourts may also sell it.

name: Viewpark
intro: Just across the M74 motorway from Uddingston, Viewpark is an area of North Lanarkshire lying immediately to Uddingston's north-east and two kilometres (1¼ miles) west of Bellshill. Its 2016 population estimate of 13,916 covers the smaller adjoining neighbourhoods of Birkenshaw, Bellziehill, Calderbraes, Fallside and Tannochside, all within the Thorniewood ward of the local council. Viewpark falls in the G71 postcode district. In a straight line, Coatbridge is about 3.6 km away, Blantyre 4.5 km, Cambuslang 5.8 km, Motherwell 6.4 km and Hamilton 6.6 km, so several neighbouring towns are within a short drive. With the M74 running past, a driver with an AdBlue warning here has Bothwell Services around 1.7 km away, and Hamilton Services on the same motorway at about 5 km.
roadsText: The M74 runs past Viewpark, and Bothwell Services on it is about 1.7 km away in a straight line. Hamilton Services, also on the M74, is about 5 km away and Heart of Scotland Services on the M8 about 19.4 km. OpenStreetMap lists a station in Glasgow (G11 6DN), about 16.1 km away, as selling AdBlue at the pump; its records are incomplete.

name: Wakefield
intro: City status came to Wakefield in 1888 because of its cathedral. The city stands on the River Calder in West Yorkshire, had 109,766 residents at the 2021 census, up from 99,251 in 2011, and is the administrative centre of a metropolitan borough with a 2025 population of 369,450. It grew as a market town and wool centre, using the navigable river to become an inland port. Two motorways, the M1 and M62, appear among the main roads, and for a diesel driver with an AdBlue problem that means a motorway service area on each of them within 8 km. The A650, A642, A638, A61, A636 and A6194 complete the list. The postcode districts are WF1 and WF2. Ossett is 4.6 km away in a straight line, East Ardsley 5.5 km and Normanton 6.6 km, and the city is part of the West Yorkshire Built-up Area, so a short local journey can easily cross into a neighbouring town.
roadsText: The M1 and M62 both appear among the main roads around Wakefield, alongside the A650, A642, A638, A61, A636 and A6194. In a straight line, Woolley Edge services on the M1 is 7.5 km away, Whitwood services on the M62 is 7.6 km and Skelton Lake Service Station on the M1 is 10.2 km. OpenStreetMap lists stations with a Leeds address (10.3 km) and a Pontefract address (12 km) as selling AdBlue at the pump; its records are incomplete.

name: Walkden
intro: As one of seven main town centres in the City of Salford, Walkden now largely functions as a retail centre and commuter suburb of Greater Manchester. It lies six miles (ten kilometres) northwest of central Salford and seven miles (eleven kilometres) from Manchester. Historically part of the township of Worsley in Lancashire, it was a centre for coal mining and textile manufacture. In 2021 the Walkden North, Walkden South and Little Hulton wards had a combined population of 39,761. Postcode districts M28 and M38 cover the area. Neighbours are very close: Little Hulton is about 1.9 km away, Worsley 2 km and Kearsley 2.7 km, with Farnworth and Swinton both at 3.2 km. For a van or diesel car with an AdBlue warning, the six nearest towns are all within 4.5 km, with Eccles the furthest of them.
roadsText: Birch Services on the M62 is the closest service area to Walkden, about 11.9 km away. Rivington Services on the M61 is around 14.8 km off and Lymm Services on the M6 about 19.4 km. OpenStreetMap has a station under Manchester, roughly 7.2 km away, listed as selling AdBlue at the pump, along with one under Warrington at 14.3 km and another site at 16.5 km. Its coverage is incomplete, so nearer stations may also stock it.

name: Wallasey
intro: At the mouth of the River Mersey, on the north-eastern corner of the Wirral Peninsula, Wallasey is a town in the Metropolitan Borough of Wirral. It lay within the historic county boundaries of Cheshire and became part of Merseyside in 1974. At the 2021 Census its built-up area had 85,610 people. Birkenhead is only 3.6 km away. Five postcode districts are listed for Wallasey: CH41, CH43, CH44, CH45 and CH46. Bootle is 6 km away, Litherland 7.6 km and Crosby 8.2 km, while West Kirby and Liverpool are both 9.1 km off. The M53 is the motorway on the road list, joined by the A5139, A554, A552, A5036, A41, A5227 and A565. The nearest service areas in the data are all at least 14.5 km away.
roadsText: Wallasey's main roads are the M53 with the A5139, A554, A552, A5036, A41, A5227 and A565. Old Meadow Services on the M58 is 14.5 km away, Earlsfield Services on the M57 15.3 km and Singing Kettle Services on the A55 22.9 km. In OpenStreetMap, a station at Old Meadow (14.5 km) is listed as selling AdBlue at the pump, while a nearer site in Liverpool L5 is marked HGV-only. The data is incomplete.

name: Wallsend
intro: At the eastern end of Hadrian's Wall, Wallsend is a town in North Tyneside, Tyne and Wear, four miles (6.5 kilometres) east of Newcastle upon Tyne. It has a population of 43,842. Its neighbours are close together: Hebburn is 3km away, Tynemouth 3.7km, Longbenton 4.2km, Jarrow 4.3km, Killingworth 5.5km and Whitley Bay 6km. That means a van working around Wallsend can cross into several other towns in a short drive, and an AdBlue warning may appear in any of them. Main roads listed include the A19, A184, A186, A187, A193, A194, A1058 and A1300, and postcode districts include NE7, NE27, NE28, NE29 and NE31. With the A19 among those roads, Seaton Burn Services on the same road is the nearest listed service area, 10.3km away.
roadsText: Wallsend's road list takes in the A1058, A19, A194, A1300, A184, A193, A187 and A186. Seaton Burn Services on the A19 is 10.3km away, Washington Services on the A1(M) 12.7km and Easington Services on the A19 24.2km. A station in Newcastle upon Tyne, 6.6km away, is listed as selling AdBlue at the pump in OpenStreetMap; the map does not show every station that sells it.

name: Walsall
intro: Six neighbouring towns, from Wednesbury to Willenhall, are all within 4.8km of Walsall, the market town and administrative centre of the Metropolitan Borough of Walsall in the Black Country. It lies 9 miles (14km) north-west of Birmingham, 7 miles east of Wolverhampton and 9 miles south-west of Lichfield. Historically in Staffordshire, it moved into the new West Midlands county in 1974. The 2011 census put the built-up area at 67,594 people. Postcode districts include WS1, WS2, WS4, WS5 and WS10. The M6 and M5 both appear on the road list, with the A4148, A34, A461, A4031, A454 and A4041. Neighbours that close make for a lot of short urban trips, with quick motorway access for longer runs. The nearest service areas are around 9km out.
roadsText: Two service areas are within 9.6km of Walsall: Hilton Park services on the M6 at about 9.1km and Norton Canes services on the M6 Toll at 9.6km, with a truck stop on the A5 at 13km. OpenStreetMap lists forecourts in Warley (9.1km) and Burntwood (11.5km), plus an HGV-only site in Birmingham (15.9km), as selling AdBlue at the pump, and its coverage is incomplete. Listed roads are the M6, M5, A4148, A34, A461, A4031, A454 and A4041.

name: Waltham Abbey
intro: Lying in the Lea Valley between the River Lea and Epping Forest, Waltham Abbey is a suburban town in the Epping Forest District of Essex, 13.5 miles (21.7 km) north-east of Charing Cross. Large parts of it are Metropolitan Green Belt, and besides the main built-up area it covers places such as Sewardstone, High Beach, Holyfield and Upshire. The EN9 postcode district covers the town. Neighbours are close on several sides: Waltham Cross is 2.3 km away, Cheshunt 4.1 km, Loughton 6.1 km and Buckhurst Hill 7 km. Motorway service areas are further out, so a driver with an AdBlue warning should note that South Mimms Services on the A1(M) is the nearest listed, 15.9 km away in a straight line.
roadsText: South Mimms Services on the A1(M) is the closest service area to Waltham Abbey at 15.9 km in a straight line, with London Gateway Services on the M1 at 19.8 km and Birchanger Green Services on the M11 at 24.2 km. A station 16.6 km away is listed in OpenStreetMap as selling AdBlue at the pump. That source is incomplete, so it should not be read as the only place nearby that sells it.

name: Waltham Cross
intro: Named after the Eleanor cross that stands in its centre, Waltham Cross is a Broxbourne town of 11,936 people in the south-eastern corner of Hertfordshire, 12 miles (19 km) north of central London. It borders Cheshunt to the north, Waltham Abbey to the east and Enfield to the south, and the Waltham Cross post town reaches into Cheshunt and a small part of Enfield. The town centre has a pedestrianised High Street and an indoor shopping centre. The EN8 postcode district covers the town. Waltham Abbey is 2.3 km away and Cheshunt 2.4 km. If an AdBlue warning comes on, the closest listed service area is South Mimms Services on the A1(M), 13.5 km away in a straight line.
roadsText: South Mimms Services on the A1(M) is the nearest service area to Waltham Cross, 13.5 km from the centre in a straight line. London Gateway Services on the M1 is 17.6 km away and Birchanger Green Services on the M11 is 25.4 km. A station 17.6 km away is listed in OpenStreetMap as selling AdBlue at the pump. That mapping is incomplete, so it is one option rather than a full list.

name: Waltham Forest
intro: Leyton, Walthamstow and Chingford merged in 1965 to form the London Borough of Waltham Forest, an outer London borough that had 278,428 residents at the 2021 census. It borders Enfield, Haringey, Hackney, Newham and Redbridge, as well as the Epping Forest District of Essex to the north. Epping Forest itself forms the eastern and northern fringe of the borough, while the River Lea, with its marshes, parkland and reservoirs, lies to the west. Main roads listed include the M11, A12, A406, A104, A106, A107, A113 and A503, and the postcode districts include E5, E10, E11, E17, E18 and E20. For a driver dealing with an AdBlue warning, that means anything from streets in Walthamstow or Leyton to bigger routes such as the M11 and A406. Hackney is 4.8km away, Redbridge 6.2km and Haringey 6.2km.
roadsText: The road list for Waltham Forest covers the M11, A104, A503, A106, A12, A406, A113 and A107. Listed service areas are London Gateway Services on the M1 at 18.4km, South Mimms Services on the A1(M) at 18.8km and Thurrock Services on the M25 at 22.1km. A station 7.5km away and another at Catford, 15.1km away, are listed as selling AdBlue at the pump in OpenStreetMap; its data is incomplete.

name: Walton-on-Thames
intro: Known locally as Walton, this market town sits on the south bank of the Thames in north-west Surrey, about 24 km south-west of central London. It is in the Borough of Elmbridge and forms part of the Greater London Built-up Area, so most local driving is on suburban streets around a historic town centre. Along with Weybridge, it is one of the largest towns in Elmbridge, with a population of 27,016 across the KT12, TW17, TW16, KT8 and KT13 postcode districts. Neighbouring places are very close: Hersham is 2.1 km away, Sunbury-on-Thames 2.7 km, Weybridge 3.4 km and West Molesey 4.8 km, with Byfleet and Addlestone a little further out. For a diesel van or car, that means plenty of short hops between suburbs, broken up by runs onto bigger roads such as the M3, the A3 and the A316.
roadsText: Walton's road network includes the M3 and A3, plus the A308, A316, A309, A3050, A244 and A317. For a break on a longer journey, Cobham services on the M25 is 9 km away, Heston services on the M4 is 11.4 km away and Wisley services on the A3 is 11.8 km away. All three sit on major routes, which makes them convenient places to stop if a dashboard warning appears mid-trip.

name: Wandsworth
intro: Battersea, Balham, Putney, Tooting and Wandsworth Town are the main communities in Wandsworth, a South West London borough of around 329,677 people that forms part of Inner London. It borders Lambeth to the east, Merton and Kingston upon Thames to the south and Richmond upon Thames to the west, while Hammersmith and Fulham, Kensington and Chelsea and the City of Westminster lie across the River Thames to the north. Every main road listed for the borough is an A-road: the A3, A24, A205, A214, A217, A3205, A3220 and A3031. There is no motorway in that list, and the closest listed service area is 15.4km away, so a driver whose dashboard shows an AdBlue warning here is more likely to be dealing with it on local streets than on a motorway. Postcode districts include SW4, SW6, SW11, SW12, SW15, SW17, SW18 and SW19. Lambeth (4.6km), Kensington and Chelsea (4.7km) and Merton (4.8km) are all close by.
roadsText: Roads listed for Wandsworth are the A214, A3, A217, A3205, A3220, A205, A24 and A3031. The nearest service areas are Heston Services on the M4 (15.4km), London Gateway Services on the M1 (21.1km) and Cobham Services on the M25 (22.8km). OpenStreetMap, which is incomplete, has a station at Catford listed as selling AdBlue at the pump, 11.8km from the borough.

name: Wantage
intro: At the foot of the Berkshire Downs, Wantage is a historic market town in the Vale of White Horse. It was part of Berkshire until 1974 and has been administered as part of Oxfordshire since then. The town stands on Letcombe Brook, 8 miles (13 km) south-west of Abingdon, 14 miles (23 km) north-west of Newbury and 15 miles (24 km) south-west of Oxford, and it was the birthplace of King Alfred the Great in 849. Its population is 13,100 and its postcode district is OX12. Wantage is some distance from other towns: the nearest, Didcot, is 12.5 km away, and Abingdon-on-Thames is 14.2 km. That distance applies to services too. For a van or diesel car with an AdBlue warning, the nearest listed service area is Membury Services on the M4, 15.1 km away in a straight line.
roadsText: Both of the nearest listed service areas to Wantage are on the M4: Membury Services at 15.1 km and Chieveley Services at 17.6 km, measured in a straight line. A truck stop listed as Swindon J15, on the A420, is 21.1 km away. Road distances will be longer, so with services this far out it pays to act early on an AdBlue warning.

name: Ware
intro: At the 2021 census the parish of Ware had 19,627 residents. The town and civil parish lies just east of Hertford, the county town, in the East Hertfordshire district, and is covered by the SG12 postcode district. Hertford is only 4.1 km away and Hoddesdon 6.2 km, with Welwyn Garden City, Harlow, Cheshunt and Sawbridgeworth all between 11 km and 12.3 km from the centre. For a van or diesel car showing an AdBlue warning, the nearest service areas are not especially close. Birchanger Green Services on the M11 is 16.8 km away in a straight line and South Mimms Services on the A1(M) is 19.1 km, so road distances to either will be longer. A station in Bishop's Stortford, 14.5 km away, is listed in OpenStreetMap as selling AdBlue at the pump.
roadsText: Three service areas are within about 25 km of Ware in a straight line: Birchanger Green Services on the M11 at 16.8 km, South Mimms Services on the A1(M) at 19.1 km and Baldock Services, also on the A1(M), at 25.3 km. A station in Bishop's Stortford (CM23 3LA), 14.5 km away, is listed in OpenStreetMap as selling AdBlue at the pump. OpenStreetMap coverage of AdBlue is incomplete, so other forecourts may also stock it.

name: Warminster
intro: Salisbury Plain's western edge is where Warminster sits, a historic market town in south-west Wiltshire, with 18,173 people in the parish in 2021. Several Army establishments, known together as the Warminster Garrison, sit on the edges of the town, and its High Street and Market Place hold many fine buildings, including the Town Hall and the Athenaeum Centre. The town is covered by the BA12 postcode district. Westbury is 6.7 km away, Frome 10.6 km and Trowbridge 13.6 km. Warminster has a service area right beside it, useful if an AdBlue warning appears: Warminster Services on the A350 is only 2.3 km away in a straight line. That matters, because the next listed options, both on the M4, are more than 34 km away.
roadsText: Warminster Services on the A350 is the nearest listed service area, just 2.3 km from Warminster in a straight line. The next two are both on the M4 and much further off: Leigh Delamere Services at 34.1 km and Chippenham Pit Stop at 34.7 km. For drivers in BA12, the A350 site is the obvious stop if an AdBlue warning appears.

name: Warmsworth
intro: Lying along the A1(M) and the A630, Warmsworth is a village and civil parish in the City of Doncaster, South Yorkshire, 4 miles (6.5 km) from Doncaster itself. The River Don is close to the village, and Sprotbrough, Edlington, Conisbrough, Levitt Hagg and Balby surround it. The village population was estimated at 3,908 in 2019, and its postcode district is DN12. Conisbrough is the closest neighbouring town at 2.7 km, followed by Maltby at 6.3 km and Mexborough at 6.7 km, with Scawthorpe and Cusworth at 6.9 km and Bentley at 7 km. For a van or diesel car with an AdBlue warning, a station in Doncaster (DN4 0TP), just 2.5 km from the centre, is listed in OpenStreetMap as selling AdBlue at the pump. The nearest listed service area is Blyth Services on the A1(M), 13.4 km away in a straight line.
roadsText: Warmsworth lies along the A1(M) and the A630. The nearest service areas, measured in a straight line, are Blyth Services on the A1(M) at 13.4 km, Rotherham Services on the M1 at 14.1 km and Barnsdale Bar Services on the A1 at 16.6 km. A station in Doncaster (DN4 0TP), 2.5 km away, is listed in OpenStreetMap as selling AdBlue at the pump. OpenStreetMap is incomplete, so it may not be the only nearby option.

name: Warrington
intro: Sixteen miles from both Liverpool and Manchester, Warrington sits on the banks of the River Mersey and has long been a crossing point. The Romans founded it at an important crossing place on the river, and by the Middle Ages it was a market town at the lowest bridging point. Three motorways appear on today's road list: the M62, M6 and M56. The town centre and the suburbs north of the river were historically part of Lancashire. With 174,970 people in the built-up area in 2021, it is the largest town in the ceremonial county of Cheshire. Postcode districts WA1, WA2, WA4 and WA5 are listed. Lymm (6.9 km) and Newton-le-Willows (7.6 km) are close by, while Runcorn and Widnes are both around 10 km away. For a van or diesel car with an AdBlue warning, the motorway network is never far off, with Burtonwood Services only 4.8 km away.
roadsText: Warrington's main roads include the M62, M6 and M56, with the A49, A57, A5061, A5060 and A5196. Burtonwood Services on the M62 is 4.8 km away and Lymm Services on the M6 6.4 km, with Whitley Services on the A49 at 10.8 km. In OpenStreetMap, two stations in Warrington are listed as selling AdBlue at the pump, one in WA3 at 5 km and one in WA5 at 5.6 km. The map data is incomplete.

name: Warwick
intro: Warwick, the county town of Warwickshire, stands beside the River Avon 9 miles (14km) south of Coventry and 19 miles south-east of Birmingham. It adjoins Leamington Spa and Whitnash, so the built-up area carries on beyond the town itself. Warwick Castle is the most notable relic of its time as a fortified settlement, and much of the town was rebuilt after the Great Fire of 1694. The 2021 population was estimated at 36,665. Postcodes are CV34 and CV31. The road list includes the M40, A425, A429, A452, A46, A4177, A445 and A4189. Leamington Spa is about 3.7km away, Kenilworth 7.5km and Stratford-upon-Avon 13.4km. For drivers, that puts both the M40 and the A46 close at hand, and a service area sits just 2km out on the A46.
roadsText: Warwick North (Budbrooke) services on the A46 is only about 2km from Warwick, and Warwick services on the M40 is 8.6km away. Corley services on the M6 is much further, at 21.6km. Listed roads are the M40, A425, A429, A452, A46, A4177, A445 and A4189. OpenStreetMap's AdBlue records are incomplete, but they list one forecourt, about 19.6km away, as selling it at the pump.

name: Washington
intro: Designated a new town in 1964, Washington is in the Sunderland district of Tyne and Wear and lies between Chester-le-Street, Gateshead and South Tyneside. It was historically part of County Durham and became part of Tyne and Wear in 1974. The town has expanded dramatically since its designation, with new villages created and areas reassigned from Chester-le-Street, and its population was 67,085 at the 2011 census. Three motorway-standard roads appear in its main road list, the A1(M), A194(M) and A195(M), along with the A1, A19, A167, A184 and A1231, and Washington Services on the A1(M) is just 3.2km away. Postcode districts include NE37 and NE38. Birtley is 4.1km away, Shiney Row and Penshaw 4.7km, Gateshead 5.6km and Chester-le-Street 6.7km. A diesel van here can be on a motorway within a short distance, so an AdBlue warning may first appear on a fast road.
roadsText: Roads recorded for Washington are the A194(M), A1(M), A195(M), A1231, A1, A19, A167 and A184. Washington Services on the A1(M) is 3.2km away, Easington Services on the A19 15.1km and Seaton Burn Services on the A19 19.5km. OpenStreetMap, which is incomplete, has a station in Newcastle upon Tyne (15.9km) and one near Durham (DH6 3LJ, 19.6km) listed as selling AdBlue at the pump.

name: Waterlooville
intro: The old A3 London to Portsmouth road is what Waterlooville grew around. Today it is the largest town in the Borough of Havant, about 6 miles north-east of Portsmouth, with 34,775 people in its built-up area at the 2021 census. It is part of the South Hampshire conurbation and is surrounded by communities including Purbrook, Cowplain, Denmead, Horndean and Widley. Postcode districts are PO7 and PO9. The road list is substantial: the M27, M275 and A3(M) sit alongside the A3, A27, A2030, A397 and A3023. Havant is 3.8km away, Horndean 3.9km and Portsmouth 6.9km, so trips are often short, with motorway access on hand for longer runs. A driver with an AdBlue warning also has a service area 4.8km from town.
roadsText: Main roads listed around Waterlooville are the M27, M275, A3(M), A3, A2030, A27, A397 and A3023. Farlington Services on the A27 is the nearest service area, about 4.8km away. Petersfield Services on the A3 is 15.5km and Fontwell Services on the A27 is 27km. For a driver on the A3 or the A27, there is a service area within reach on either road.

name: Watford
intro: Several companies have based their headquarters in Watford, drawn by its location near London and its transport links. The Hertfordshire town and borough sits on the banks of the River Colne, 15 miles (24 km) north-west of central London, and has a population of 131,336. Both the M1 and the M25 appear among the main roads, along with the A41, A405, A411, A4008, A4145 and A4178. Postcode districts include WD3, WD17, WD18, WD19, WD23, WD24 and WD25, plus HA6. Neighbouring places are close: Bushey is about 3.3 km away, Rickmansworth 4.2 km, Chorleywood 7.1 km and Harrow 7.3 km. For a driver with an AdBlue warning, the nearest service areas are on the M1, A1(M) and A41, between about 9.8 km and 13.5 km away.
roadsText: Main roads around Watford include the M1, M25, A41, A405, A411, A4008, A4145 and A4178. London Gateway Services on the M1 is the nearest service area, about 9.8 km away. South Mimms Services on the A1(M) is around 13.4 km away, and Bourne End Services on the A41 about 13.5 km.

name: Wath upon Dearne
intro: Almost midway between Barnsley and Doncaster, Wath upon Dearne (shortened to Wath) sits south of the River Dearne in the Metropolitan Borough of Rotherham, 5 miles (8 km) north of Rotherham itself. It had 11,816 residents at the 2011 census and is twinned with Saint-Jean-de-Bournay in France. The S63 postcode district covers the town. Several neighbouring towns are close by: Swinton is about 2.6 km away, Mexborough 3.5 km, Rawmarsh 4.4 km and Wombwell 4.9 km, with Hoyland at 6.9 km and Conisbrough 7.5 km. For a van or diesel car with an AdBlue warning, the nearest listed service area is Rotherham Services on the M1, about 11.5 km away in a straight line, and a station in Doncaster listed as selling AdBlue at the pump is a similar distance.
roadsText: Rotherham Services on the M1 is the closest service area to Wath upon Dearne, about 11.5 km away in a straight line. Sheffield Service Area on the A6102 (15 km) and Barnsdale Bar Services on the A1 (15.5 km) follow. Two stations are listed on OpenStreetMap as selling AdBlue at the pump: one in Doncaster (DN4 0TP), about 11.1 km away, and another in Pontefract (WF7 7HX), about 15.9 km away. The map's AdBlue coverage is incomplete.

name: Watton
intro: About 25 miles (40 km) west-south-west of Norwich and 15 miles (24 km) north-east of Thetford, Watton is a Breckland market town with a population of 11,549. Its annual Wayland Agricultural Show is one of the oldest one-day agricultural shows in England. The town is covered by the IP25 postcode district. Dereham and Attleborough are both about 14 km away, Thetford 18.4 km and Wymondham 19.3 km, with Downham Market 30.7 km off. Service areas are a long way from the town: Thickthorn Services on the A11 is the nearest listed, 26.7 km away in a straight line, and Freebridge Park on the A47 is 35.8 km. A driver with an AdBlue warning in Watton should bear that in mind before setting off on a longer run.
roadsText: The nearest service areas to Watton are all more than 25 km away in a straight line: Thickthorn Services on the A11 at 26.7 km, Freebridge Park on the A47 at 35.8 km and Beacon Hill Services on the A140 at 50 km. Road distances will be longer, so a services stop is not a quick option from IP25.

name: Wednesbury
intro: Part of the Black Country and near the source of the River Tame, Wednesbury is a market town in the Sandwell district of the West Midlands county, and was historically in Staffordshire. It lies five miles (eight kilometres) south-east of Wolverhampton, three miles (five kilometres) south-west of Walsall and seven miles (eleven kilometres) north-west of Birmingham. At the 2021 Census the town's built-up area had 20,313 people, and the postcode district is WS10. Neighbouring towns are very close: Darlaston is 2 km away, Tipton and West Bromwich 3.4 km each, Bilston 4 km and Willenhall 4.4 km. For a van or diesel car with an AdBlue warning, the M6, the M6 Toll and the M5 all have listed service areas between 10.1 km and 14.1 km away in a straight line, so none is right on the doorstep.
roadsText: The nearest service areas to Wednesbury are Hilton Park Services on the M6, 10.1 km away in a straight line, Norton Canes Services on the M6 Toll at 12.5 km and Frankley Services on the M5 at 14.1 km. A station in Warley, 5.9 km away, is listed in OpenStreetMap as selling AdBlue at the pump, as is one in Burntwood (WS7 3XA) at 14.7 km. An HGV-only site in Birmingham (B25 8DW) at 15.9 km is meant for lorries. OpenStreetMap's coverage is incomplete.

name: Wellingborough
intro: North of the River Nene, Wellingborough is a market town in North Northamptonshire, 10 miles (16 km) from Northampton and 65 miles (105 km) from London. Its population was 56,564 at the 2021 census. The built-up area takes in suburbs including Hemmingwell, Kingsway, Queensway, Redhill Grange, Wilby, Stanton Cross, Glenvale Park and Waendle View, and the postcode district listed for the town is NN8. Main roads include the A6, A45, A509 and A510, plus the A4500, A5001, A5128 and A5193. Neighbouring towns are close: Burton Latimer is about 6.7 km away, Rushden 7.3 km and Kettering 10.5 km. The nearest service areas, by contrast, are all more than 14 km out, which is worth knowing if an AdBlue warning comes on during a local run.
roadsText: The main roads listed for Wellingborough are the A6, A45, A509, A510, A4500, A5001, A5128 and A5193. The nearest service areas are Rothwell Truck Stop on the A14, about 14.2 km away, Thrapston Services on the A45 at around 15.4 km, and Northampton Services on the M1 at roughly 19.6 km.

name: Wellington
intro: Seven miles (11 km) south-west of Taunton, Wellington is a Somerset market town close to the Devon border, which follows the Blackdown Hills to the south. Besides the main built-up area, the parish takes in the smaller settlements of Rockwell Green, Tone and Tonedale. At the 2021 census the built-up area had 13,815 residents and the parish 16,678, and the town is covered by the TA21 postcode district. Wellington received a royal charter in 1215 and in the Middle Ages grew as a centre for trade on the road from Bristol to Exeter. A driver whose van or diesel car flags an AdBlue fault here is well placed for the M5: the nearest listed service area on it is just 5.6 km away in a straight line, and two more M5 sites lie within 17 km. Taunton is the closest town at 9.8 km, with Tiverton 20 km away and Honiton 20.6 km.
roadsText: RoadChef Taunton Deane Services on the M5 is the nearest service area to Wellington, 5.6 km from the centre in a straight line. Moto Tiverton Services is 11.4 km away and ExtraMSA Cullompton Services 17 km, both also on the M5. Closer still, a Texaco station 2.3 km away is listed in OpenStreetMap as selling AdBlue at the pump. That mapping is incomplete, so other forecourts may stock it too.

name: Wells
intro: Often described as England's smallest city, Wells has held city status since medieval times because of its cathedral, although it is actually the second smallest after the City of London. It stands on the southern edge of the Mendip Hills, 22 miles (35 km) south-west of Bath, 23 miles (37 km) south of Bristol and 24 miles (39 km) north-east of Taunton. The built-up area, which extends into the neighbouring parish of St Cuthbert Out, had 12,105 residents at the 2021 census, and the BA5 postcode district covers the city. Unlike London, Wells is not part of a larger urban area. Street is 11.3 km away and Midsomer Norton 14.5 km, with Frome at 23.4 km. Should an AdBlue warning come on, the nearest listed service area is Sedgemoor Services on the M5, 19.8 km away in a straight line.
roadsText: Sedgemoor Services on the M5 is the closest service area to Wells, 19.8 km away in a straight line. Moto Bridgwater Services is 26.5 km away and Welcome Break Gordano Services 30 km, both also on the M5. Lunns Filling Station, a BP site at Lower Weare (BS26 2JE) 15.6 km away, is listed in OpenStreetMap as selling AdBlue at the pump. The map data is incomplete, so treat it as one example rather than the only option.

name: Welwyn Garden City
intro: England's second garden city, founded in 1920, Welwyn Garden City was also designated one of the first new towns in 1948, which makes it unusual in being both. It exemplifies the planning ideals of the periods in which it was built. The town is in the Welwyn Hatfield district of Hertfordshire, 20 miles (32 km) north of London, and had 51,505 residents in 2021. Anyone heading out with a diesel showing an AdBlue fault has the A1(M), the main road listed, plus the A414, A1000, A6129, A1001 and A1057. Hatfield is just 5 km away and Hertford 7.5 km, while St Albans, Harpenden and Ware are all between 10.3 and 11.2 km, and Potters Bar is 11.6 km off. Postcode districts are AL6, AL7 and AL8.
roadsText: Welwyn Garden City's listed roads are the A1(M), A414, A1000, A6129, A1001 and A1057. The nearest service area is South Mimms Services on the A1(M), 12.8 km away. London Gateway Services on the M1 is 19.5 km off, and Baldock Services, also on the A1(M), is 23.6 km away, so all three listed service areas are on motorways.

name: West Bridgford
intro: As the administrative centre of Rushcliffe borough, West Bridgford is a Nottinghamshire town south of Nottingham city centre, with an estimated population of 37,181 in 2024. It lies east of Wilford, north of Ruddington and west of Radcliffe-on-Trent, with Colwick and Beeston on the opposite bank of the River Trent, and it is part of the Nottingham Urban Area. Postcode districts are NG1 and NG2. Main roads include the A52, A60, A453 and A606, as well as the A612, A6011, A6514 and A6520. Clifton is about 4.7 km away, Nottingham 5.8 km, Carlton 6 km and Beeston 7.3 km. Two service areas are under 4 km from the town, which is handy when an AdBlue message appears on a short local trip.
roadsText: Main roads around West Bridgford are the A52, A60, A453, A606, A612, A6011, A6514 and A6520. Trent Bridge Services on the A6011 is about 1.9 km away and Pierrepont on the A52 about 3.4 km. The next nearest is Trowell Services on the M1, at around 10.3 km.

name: West Bromwich
intro: Commonly known as West Brom, West Bromwich is a market town in the borough of Sandwell, about 5 miles west of Birmingham with the Sandwell Valley in between. It is part of the Black Country and had 103,112 residents at the 2021 census. Historically in Staffordshire, it grew with the Industrial Revolution into a centre for coal mining, brick making and metal trades. Postcode districts include B70, B71, B43, B21, B66, B69, WS10 and DY4. Two motorways, the M5 and M6, appear on the road list along with the A4031, A4041, A41, A461, A4123 and A34. Neighbouring towns are packed close: Wednesbury is about 3.4km away, Oldbury 4.1km, Smethwick 4.4km and Tipton 4.5km. Driving here is likely to involve many short urban journeys between them, with motorway access close by.
roadsText: West Bromwich's road list includes the M5, M6, A4031, A4041, A41, A461, A4123 and A34, yet its nearest service areas are all at least 11.4km away: Frankley on the M5 at about 11.4km, Hilton Park on the M6 at 13.4km and Norton Canes on the M6 Toll at 15km. Closer in, OpenStreetMap lists a forecourt in Warley, about 4.1km away, as selling AdBlue at the pump, plus an HGV-only site in Birmingham (12.7km) and a forecourt in Burntwood (17km). Its data is incomplete.

name: West End
intro: Hampshire County Cricket Club plays at the Utilita Bowl in West End, a parish in the borough of Eastleigh, Hampshire, east of the city of Southampton. The village itself is small and is generally classed as part of the borough's outer suburbs or rural urban fringe, because of the woodland and countryside around it, including Telegraph Woods and Itchen Valley Country Park. Two postcode districts cover the area, SO18 and SO30. Hedge End is the closest neighbour at 2.5 km, with Eastleigh at 4.8 km, Chandler's Ford at 7.7 km and Locks Heath at 8.6 km. For a driver with an AdBlue warning, the nearest listed service area is Rownhams Services on the M27, 8.8 km away in a straight line, with West Wellow Services on the A36 the next option at 14.6 km.
roadsText: Rownhams Services on the M27 is the nearest listed service area to West End, 8.8 km away in a straight line. West Wellow Services on the A36 is 14.6 km off and Rufus Stone on the A31 is 20.7 km. Each is on a different road, so it helps a driver in SO18 or SO30 to know which one suits the route before an AdBlue warning becomes pressing. Road distances will be longer than these figures.

name: West Kirby
intro: At the mouth of the River Dee, in the north west of the Wirral Peninsula, West Kirby is a coastal town in the Metropolitan Borough of Wirral, Merseyside. It is contiguous with Hoylake and lies within the historic county boundaries of Cheshire, having become part of Merseyside in 1974. The built-up area had 13,380 residents at the 2021 census. The CH48 postcode district covers the town. Heswall is about 5.9 km away, Birkenhead 7.5 km and Wallasey 9.1 km, with Neston and Bebington between 10.9 km and 11.7 km. Motorway services are some distance from the town. For a van or diesel car with an AdBlue warning, the nearest service area is on the A55, about 14.1 km away.
roadsText: The nearest service area to West Kirby is Singing Kettle Services on the A55, about 14.1 km away. Chester West Services, also on the A55, is around 20.7 km off, and Old Meadow Services on the M58 about 23.4 km. OpenStreetMap has a refuelling site in Liverpool, roughly 13.2 km away, listed as selling AdBlue at the pump, but it is marked as HGV-only. Its data is incomplete.

name: West Molesey
intro: Molesey, on the south bank of the River Thames, is made up of two large villages, East and West Molesey, in the Borough of Elmbridge, Surrey. The area is within the Greater London Built-up Area. The two villages share a high street, and a second shopping street, Bridge Road, runs close to Hampton Court Palace in the eastern part of the district. Postcode districts listed for the wider area are KT8, KT7, KT10, KT6, KT9 and KT5. The road list is long: the A309, A3, A243, A308, A240, A307, A3009 and A244 all appear. Kingston upon Thames is 4.4km away, Hersham 4.7km and Walton-on-Thames 4.8km, with Richmond upon Thames at 6km and Sunbury-on-Thames at 6.1km. Much of the driving here is suburban, on A roads between closely spaced towns.
roadsText: West Molesey's listed main roads are the A309, A3, A243, A308, A240, A307, A3009 and A244. The nearest service areas are Cobham Services on the M25 (9.7km), Heston Services on the M4 (12.6km) and Wisley Services on the A3 (14.3km). With stops on three different main routes, a driver has more than one option if an AdBlue warning appears mid-journey.

name: West Moors
intro: The railway lines built in the late 19th century brought West Moors to local prominence, and its station was served by a branch line until 4 May 1964. Today the Castleman Trailway footpath follows the old trackbed towards Ringwood to the east and Poole to the west. The Dorset village sits on the northern fringe of the Poole and Bournemouth conurbation, just outside Ferndown and Verwood, and its parish council was renamed West Moors Town Council in 2020. The parish had 7,561 residents at the 2011 census and is in the BH22 postcode district. Ferndown is only 2.7 km away, with Verwood at 5.9 km, Wimborne Minster at 6.3 km and Ringwood at 7.8 km. If an AdBlue warning comes on, the nearest listed service area is Picket Post Services on the A31, 11.1 km away in a straight line.
roadsText: Picket Post Services on the A31 is the nearest service area to West Moors, 11.1 km away in a straight line. Rufus Stone, also on the A31, is 20.1 km away and West Wellow Services on the A36 is 28.2 km. MFG Creekmoor, a Shell site in Poole (BH17 7FR) 12.7 km away, is listed in OpenStreetMap as selling AdBlue at the pump. OpenStreetMap coverage is incomplete, so other stations may sell it.

name: Westbury
intro: The busy A350, which connects the M4 motorway with the south coast, passes through Westbury. The market town lies in west Wiltshire, below the north-western edge of Salisbury Plain, about 4 miles (6 km) south of Trowbridge and a similar distance north of Warminster. Its urban area has spread to include the village of Westbury Leigh and the hamlets of Chalford and Frogmore, and the town has a population of 16,394. Later growth came from its position where two railway lines meet. Westbury is covered by the BA13 postcode district, with Frome 9.6 km away, Melksham 13.2 km and Bath 17.8 km. The A350 is also where a driver with an AdBlue warning will find the nearest listed service area: Warminster Services, 5.1 km away in a straight line.
roadsText: Westbury sits on the A350, the busy road linking the M4 with the south coast. The nearest listed service area is on that same road: Warminster Services, 5.1 km away in a straight line. The next two are both on the M4, Leigh Delamere Services at 27.6 km and Chippenham Pit Stop at 28.4 km. For drivers in BA13 with an AdBlue warning, the A350 is the route to know.

name: Westhill
intro: Seven miles (11 km) west of Aberdeen, Westhill is a suburban town that grew in the second half of the 20th century by taking in villages and farms, Elrick most notably among them. With 11,750 residents in 2022 it is one of the largest towns in Aberdeenshire, and it has its own shopping centre, library and swimming pool. Westhill is in the AB32 postcode district. Aberdeen is 10.1 km away, Inverurie 15.7 km and Stonehaven 21.5 km, so the nearest larger centres are within easy reach. The listed service areas are a different matter, starting at 46.6 km away. For a driver dealing with an AdBlue warning in Westhill, that distance is worth keeping in mind before heading out on a longer run.
roadsText: Westhill Service Station (AB32 6TJ), about 0.6 km from the town centre, is listed as selling AdBlue at the pump in OpenStreetMap; that data is incomplete, so it may not be the only option. The nearest service areas are a long way off: Stracathro Services on the A90 at 46.6 km, Ashgrove Services on the A96 at 49.8 km and Forfar Services, also on the A90, at 69.2 km.

name: Westhoughton
intro: Made up of several former villages and hamlets, including Wingates, Over Hulton, Chequerbent, Daisy Hill, Hart Common and Four Gates, Westhoughton is a town and civil parish in the Metropolitan Borough of Bolton. It lies 6 km south-west of Bolton, 8 km east of Wigan and 21 km north-west of Manchester. Once a centre for coal mining, cotton spinning and textile manufacture, it had 24,974 residents at the 2011 census and is covered by the BL5 postcode district. Atherton is 3 km away and Hindley 3.7 km, with Leigh at 5 km and Tyldesley, Horwich and Platt Bridge and Abram all under 6 km. Getting between the town's different districts and these neighbours means a lot of short local driving, and Rivington services on the M61 is 7 km away for longer runs.
roadsText: Rivington services on the M61 is the nearest service area to Westhoughton, 7 km away, followed by Charnock Richard on the M6 at 14.8 km and Burtonwood on the M62 at 16.2 km. Stations listed in OpenStreetMap as selling AdBlue at the pump include two in Warrington, at 14 km and 17.6 km, and one in Manchester at 15.3 km. That data is incomplete.

name: Weston-super-Mare
intro: Between Worlebury Hill and Bleadon Hill on the Bristol Channel, Weston-super-Mare is a seaside town 32 km south-west of Bristol, with a built-up population of 84,605 at the 2021 census. It was still a small village until the 19th century, when it developed as a seaside resort, and in the second half of the 20th century it was connected to the M5. The number of people holidaying in the town has since declined, but day visitor numbers have risen. The BS22, BS23 and BS24 postcode districts cover the town. Burnham-on-Sea is 11.7 km away and Clevedon 12 km, with Nailsea at 16.6 km and Portishead at 20.2 km. For van and diesel-car drivers, the motorway link makes longer trips straightforward, and Sedgemoor services is the closest stop on it.
roadsText: The M5 is the motorway serving Weston-super-Mare, with the A370, A371 and A3033 as the other main roads. Sedgemoor services on the M5 is the closest, 8.8 km away, and Gordano services on the M5 is 22.8 km away. A filling station at Lower Weare (BS26 2JE), 10.4 km from the town, is listed as selling AdBlue at the pump in OpenStreetMap data. That mapping is incomplete, so other forecourts may stock it too.

name: Wetherby
intro: For centuries Wetherby has been a crossing place and staging post on the Great North Road, midway between London and Edinburgh, and the course of the Old Great North Road still passes through the town. It is a market town on the River Wharfe in the City of Leeds, close to the border with North Yorkshire, about 12 miles (19 km) from both Leeds city centre and York and 8 miles (13 km) from Harrogate. Postcodes here use LS22. Knaresborough is about 9.7 km away and Harrogate 11.8 km, with Garforth at 15.8 km. For a driver with an AdBlue warning, Wetherby is well placed: Wetherby Services on the A1(M) is about 1.8 km from the centre in a straight line.
roadsText: Wetherby Services on the A1(M) is about 1.8 km from Wetherby town centre in a straight line, making it by far the nearest service area. Bilbrough Top Service Area on the A64 is about 13.6 km away and Skelton Lake Service Station on the M1 about 18.6 km. OpenStreetMap lists a station in Leeds (LS9 0AS), roughly 18.5 km away, as selling AdBlue at the pump; the map data is incomplete.

name: Weybourne
intro: Aldershot, across the county line in Hampshire, borders Weybourne, a small village on the outskirts of Farnham in the Waverley district of Surrey. Short local trips from here can cross between the two counties. The village is in the GU9 postcode district, and the towns around it are packed close together: Farnham is 2.7 km away and Aldershot 2.9 km, with Ash and Ash Vale at 5 km, Fleet at 5.9 km and Farnborough at 6 km. Frimley is a little further at 9.9 km. When an AdBlue warning appears on a van or diesel car here, the nearest listed service area is Fleet Services on the M3, 8.5 km away in a straight line. The next options are both on the A3, at Liphook (16.7 km) and Wisley (21.9 km), so the M3 site is clearly the closer choice.
roadsText: Fleet Services on the M3 is the nearest listed service area to Weybourne, 8.5 km away in a straight line. The next two are both on the A3: Liphook Services at 16.7 km and Wisley Services at 21.9 km. For a driver in GU9, the M3 site is the closest option by some way, and road distances will be longer than these straight-line figures.

name: Weybridge
intro: Named after a crossing point of the River Wey, which flows into the Thames to the north of the town centre, Weybridge is a town in the Borough of Elmbridge in Surrey, around 17 miles (27 km) south-west of central London. It had 15,449 residents in 2011 and falls in the KT13 postcode district. The area was held by Chertsey Abbey during the Anglo-Saxon and medieval periods, and in the 1530s Henry VIII built Oatlands Palace to the north of the centre. For drivers, the striking feature is how close the neighbouring towns are: Addlestone is 2.6 km away, Byfleet 3 km, Walton-on-Thames 3.4 km and Hersham 3.5 km, with Chertsey and Sunbury-on-Thames under 5 km. If an AdBlue warning appears, the nearest listed service area is Cobham Services on the M25, 8.3 km away in a straight line, with Wisley Services on the A3 at 9.4 km.
roadsText: Cobham Services on the M25 is the nearest to Weybridge at 8.3 km in a straight line, and Wisley Services on the A3 is close behind at 9.4 km. Heston Services on the M4 is 13.3 km away. All three distances are measured as the crow flies, so the drive will be longer, which is worth bearing in mind if an AdBlue warning has already come on.

name: Weymouth
intro: A sheltered bay at the mouth of the River Wey is the setting for Weymouth, 11 km south of the county town of Dorchester. With 53,416 people in 2021, it is the third-largest settlement in Dorset after Bournemouth and Poole. It is a seaside resort whose economy depends on tourism, with a harbour that is home to a commercial fishing fleet, pleasure boats and private yachts, and it sits roughly halfway along the Jurassic Coast. Nearby Portland Harbour hosted the sailing events of the 2012 Olympic and Paralympic Games. The DT3 and DT4 postcode districts cover the town. Beyond Dorchester, 8.6 km away, the nearest towns are a fair distance off: Bridport is 23.9 km, Blandford Forum 32.8 km and Poole 36.9 km. With only the A354 and A353 listed as main roads near the town, longer journeys on A roads are part of driving here for any van or diesel car.
roadsText: The main roads around Weymouth are the A354 and A353. Service areas are a long way off: Picket Post on the A31 is 56.8 km away, Taunton Deane on the M5 is 61.7 km and Bridgwater on the M5 is 64.7 km. Closer to town, one station 3.6 km from the centre is listed as selling AdBlue at the pump in OpenStreetMap data. That map data is incomplete, so it may not be the only one.

name: Whickham
intro: Set on high ground overlooking the River Tyne, Whickham is in the Borough of Gateshead, 8 km south-west of Newcastle upon Tyne. It is described as a village, though its population is 15,680, and it was historically part of County Durham. Whickham's postcode district is NE16. Blaydon is the closest neighbour at only 2.2 km, Newcastle upon Tyne and Gateshead are both 6.5 km away, and Birtley, Stanley and Prudhoe lie between 8.3 km and 10.8 km. Many journeys from here are therefore short ones in and around Gateshead and Newcastle, the kind of driving a van or diesel car does day in, day out. For anything longer, the nearest motorway service area is Washington on the A1(M), 9.9 km away.
roadsText: From Whickham, the nearest service area is Washington on the A1(M), 9.9 km away. Seaton Burn on the A19 is 13.8 km and Easington, also on the A19, is 25.9 km. A station in Newcastle upon Tyne, 11.9 km from Whickham, is listed in OpenStreetMap as selling AdBlue at the pump. Because that map data is incomplete, nearer forecourts may also sell it.

name: Whitburn
intro: Halfway between Scotland's two largest cities, Whitburn sits on the south bank of the River Almond in West Lothian, about 23 miles (37 kilometres) east of Glasgow and 22 miles (35 kilometres) west of Edinburgh. Bathgate, four miles (six kilometres) away, and Livingston, six miles (ten kilometres) away, are the nearest major towns, and Armadale is closer still at 3.7 km. The town has a population of around 11,490 and is covered by the EH47 postcode district. A van or diesel car based here can head towards either city, and the useful thing to know is that a listed service area on the M8 is only 4.5 km away. If an AdBlue warning appears on a trip out of Whitburn, that stop is the nearest listed place to pull in.
roadsText: Heart of Scotland Services on the M8 is the nearest service area listed for Whitburn, 4.5 km away. Beyond that, the next two listed are both on the M74: Hamilton Services at 23.3 km and Bothwell Services at 24 km. With the M8 stop so close, it is the obvious first check for a driver dealing with an AdBlue warning around Whitburn, Armadale or Bathgate.

name: Whitby
intro: At the mouth of the River Esk, where the North York Moors meet the Yorkshire Coast, Whitby is a seaside town, port and civil parish in North Yorkshire. It has a maritime, mineral and tourist economy, and its history includes herring and whaling fleets and the abbey ruin on the East Cliff. York is 47 miles (76 km) away and Middlesbrough 22 miles (35 km). The town uses the YO21 postcode district and has 12,603 residents. Other towns are some way off: Scarborough is about 28.3 km away, Guisborough 28.8 km and Redcar 32.7 km. For a van or diesel car with an AdBlue warning, a station about 1.3 km from the centre is listed as selling AdBlue at the pump, while the nearest service area is more than 37 km away.
roadsText: A station about 1.3 km from Whitby town centre is listed on OpenStreetMap as selling AdBlue at the pump. That map data is incomplete, so it may not be the only one. Service areas are distant: Teesside Truck Stop on the A66 is about 37.3 km in a straight line, Exelby Services on the A19 about 45.8 km and Wolviston Services on the A689 about 47.2 km.

name: Whitefield
intro: On undulating ground above the Irwell Valley, Whitefield is a town in the Metropolitan Borough of Bury, 4.8 km south-east of Bury and 8 km north-west of Manchester. Prestwich and the M60 motorway lie just to the south. The town was on the path of an ancient Roman road running from Manchester to Ribchester, and its urbanisation largely came with the Industrial Revolution. In 2001 it had 23,283 residents, and today it is covered by the M45 and M25 postcode districts. Prestwich is 2.4 km away and Radcliffe 2.8 km, with Clifton at 4 km, Bury at 5.1 km and Little Lever and Kearsley under 6 km. With the M60 just to the south and Birch services on the M62 4.4 km away, a van or diesel car here moves easily between local streets and motorway driving.
roadsText: Birch services on the M62 is 4.4 km from Whitefield and the closest service area by some distance; Rivington on the M61 is 19.6 km away and Blackburn with Darwen on the M65 22.1 km.
